100239.excerpt_en: The calendar shows August 5 today, and fresh photographs show that the champagne-glass-shaped snow formation on Operafjellet has now broken.
100239.subtitle_en: That means it is finally summer in Longyearbyen.

100251.excerpt_en: At 11:30 on Sunday morning, the Governor was notified that a sailboat was taking on water just south of Dunderbukta. It was a 35-foot German sailboat with a crew of three. “They had called the German rescue service, which then called the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre, which in turn contacted us.”

100325.excerpt_en: On Svalbard, neither the Natural Damage Act nor the mainland provision allowing the state to expropriate land applies. This has caused major problems for people with private homes in landslide-prone areas.
100325.subtitle_en: Now the ministers must keep their promises and show resolve.

100330.excerpt_en: “I’m so happy to see these big machines. It almost moves me,” says operations engineer Einar Olsen of Longyearbyen Local Council (LL).
100330.subtitle_en: New asphalt will be laid in Longyearbyen and at the airport over the next two weeks. The last time this was done was in 2014.

100331.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, Karoline Setten Wingsternes (27) cast her vote just outside her own office on the second floor of the Næringsbygget building. “Was it difficult to decide?” “Yes, it was, but it came down to a few parties on the same side,” says Wingsternes.
100331.subtitle_en: If you are not in your home municipality on election day, September 11, you can vote early in Longyearbyen.

100333.excerpt_en: After the avalanche, Grøndal and Aulibråten were given the choice of rebuilding the house they had lost or accepting compensation for the lost value from their insurance company, Trygg Forsikring. They wanted to have the house rebuilt on another avalanche-safe plot.
100333.subtitle_en: Nora Grøndal and Olav Aulibråten are still waiting for a replacement plot after the pointed-roof house they owned was destroyed in the avalanche on December 19, 2015.

100335.excerpt_en: One private individual and two private companies are left with virtually worthless homes and a highly uncertain situation after the avalanche in Lia in February. They were evacuated from their homes from February until the beginning of June.
100335.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) wants the Ministry of Justice’s Polar Department to help resolve the problems surrounding the replacement of worthless homes in Lia.
100335.title_en: LL Asks Polar Department for Help

100345.excerpt_en: In recent days, posts have appeared in the Facebook group “Ros & Info Longyearbyen” about tourists picking flowers in Longyearbyen and venturing outside town without weapons or a guide. “Not a major problem.” “We receive a few reports about this every year, perhaps especially in summer.”
100345.subtitle_en: Tourists hiking outside Longyearbyen without weapons are sparking debate on Facebook.

100378.excerpt_en: Initiator Kjetil Dahl Knutsen has returned to Longyearbyen with his wife Birgitte to take part in the Peak Hiking Challenge.
100378.subtitle_en: The peak-hiking challenge takes place for the third time on Saturday. Larshiertafjellet is a new peak this year.

100383.excerpt_en: This year, hunting reports and jaw collection are being expanded to include carcass weight. Hunters are also being asked to provide small tissue samples from the animals, which will be used to study both genetics and exposure to environmental toxins.
100383.subtitle_en: For many years, Svalbard hunters have contributed biological data on harvested reindeer through hunting reports.

100388.excerpt_en: At 11:30 on Sunday morning, the Governor was notified that a sailboat was taking on water just south of Dunderbukta. It was a 35-foot German sailboat with a crew of three. “They had called the German rescue service, which then called the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre, which in turn contacted us.”
100388.subtitle_en: “We have conducted interviews and reached a conclusion,” says senior police officer Arnt Rennan of the Governor’s Office.

100390.excerpt_en: Road 300 between Museumsveien and Huset remains closed. Small landslides are occurring in the area, and Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) has closed the road to all traffic until further notice, including pedestrians.
100390.subtitle_en: Loose material is sliding down in several places. In recent days, people have been observed on foot in avalanche-prone areas.
100390.title_en: People Urged to Avoid Landslide Areas

100402.excerpt_en: “It’s great fun. I moved up here this summer, so it’s a little special that I won,” says Terje Scott Syvertsen when Svalbardposten calls to tell him he has won the competition.
100402.subtitle_en: Terje Scott Syvertsen was this year’s winner of Svalbardposten’s annual guessing contest predicting when Stetten would go.

100411.excerpt_en: Every Wednesday, a group gathers at around seven in the morning for a dip before work. “We’ve been doing it since the first Wednesday in July,” says Mona Ada Andersen, who initiated the activity.
100411.subtitle_en: Gray, cold weather did not stop this group from plunging into the icy water outside Longyearbyen.
100411.title_en: A Bracing Start to the Day

100438.excerpt_en: “Project Isfjorden,” led by Svalbard Turn through “Aktiv i Friluft,” has now really got under way. Last weekend, 55 volunteers took part in litter picking at Anserbukta and by Gipshuksletta, where Billefjorden and Sassenfjorden meet.
100438.subtitle_en: “It is a paradox that we travel far and wide to pick up litter on Svalbard when the worst of it is right across Adventfjorden,” says Silje M. Hagen.

100444.excerpt_en: In 2008, Daiane decided to take a break from her law studies because she was unsure whether she wanted to become a lawyer. At the same time, her sister invited her to visit Longyearbyen. “The plan was to stay here for six months.”
100444.subtitle_en: Daiane Freitas (30) from Brazil came to visit her sister in Longyearbyen. Nine years later, she is still here.

100458.excerpt_en: Throughout his adult life, Einar Ianssen was deeply involved in business in general, and especially on Svalbard, particularly in oil and gas. His main base was in Trondheim, but his activities extended far beyond Norway, including to Canada, Alaska and Russia.
100458.subtitle_en: Einar Ianssen died on June 18, aged 93.

100460.excerpt_en: The Governor went to the cemetery in Longyearbyen on Sunday morning to inform tourists that Road 300 was closed because of the risk of landslides. “We met about ten people. Some were at the cemetery, and we met some along the road.”
100460.subtitle_en: The Governor went out to remove tourists from a landslide-prone road.

100489.excerpt_en: School starts again on Monday. The holidays are over, permanent residents are returning, and Longyearbyen is slowly but surely returning to “normal.”
100489.subtitle_en: More visitors also mean more waste and greater pressure on nature.

100500.excerpt_en: Last Wednesday, Svalbard Brewery announced in a post on its Facebook page that the popular events Brewery Bingo and Friday Pints had been cancelled indefinitely.
100500.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council put a stop to Brewery Bingo and Friday Pints at Svalbard Brewery.

100510.excerpt_en: The two new DAB transmitters were installed last September at Skjæringa and Platåberget. Coverage is expected to be better than today’s FM network, particularly in the fjords and farther out into the sea.
100510.subtitle_en: On 13 December, NRK’s FM transmitter network on Svalbard will be switched off. From then on, it will be DAB all the way.
100510.title_en: FM to Be Switched Off in December

100526.excerpt_en: They had found it floating on an ice floe north of Kong Karls Land and contacted the Governor of Svalbard because they wanted to bring it ashore. They were allowed to do so on the condition that it was donated to the museum. “This is a gift that made us very happy.”
100526.subtitle_en: At 9:30 on Sunday morning, Svalbard Museum collected a narwhal tusk from the expedition ship M/S “Malmö.”

100527.excerpt_en: A table covered in plans and three enthusiastic school leaders sit down for an interview. On Tuesday this week, they welcomed all the new employees, and on Wednesday the rest of the teaching staff returned from their holidays.
100527.subtitle_en: The new school leadership at Longyearbyen School are all from Fredrikstad. A friendly group with a sense of humour.
100527.title_en: There Could Be “An Awful Lot of Talking”

100537.excerpt_en: By the end of June, total tax revenue for Svalbard stood at NOK 113 million. At the same time last year, it was NOK 78 million.
100537.subtitle_en: Tax revenues in the first half of the year have risen by 45 percent since last year. Corporate tax is the main driver.

100548.excerpt_en: On Tuesday evening, the parish priest gave a talk together with doctor Bjarne Vig, who worked aboard the Norwegian ship “Siem Pilot,” which has picked up migrants in the Mediterranean. “My job is to communicate with people, give talks and deliver sermons.”
100548.subtitle_en: Parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen of Svalbard Church has strong views on the refugee crisis. This summer, he visited three refugee camps in Serbia.

100563.excerpt_en: We meet Mats Grimsæth aboard the sailboat “Humla,” moored to the floating dock down by Bykaia.
100563.subtitle_en: Mats Grimsæth is “only” 22, but has already led his first sailing expedition around Spitsbergen.

100578.excerpt_en: Last Saturday, the Topptrim Challenge was held for the third time. “I spend too much time in the office and too little time out hiking. The weather is so lovely today, so I thought I’d do half the route with a group,” says Victoria Windstad.
100578.subtitle_en: Wind and a little fog on the mountain peaks did nothing to dampen this year’s Topptrim Challenge.

100592.excerpt_en: I visited Svalbard from 31 July to 3.
100592.subtitle_en: “As a tourist, you must respect that this is a very vulnerable environment,” writes tourist Ragnhild Jonea in this letter to the editor.

100604.excerpt_en: Many people have spoken out about tourism to Svalbard this summer, which I consider a healthy sign. Our industry must also be able to withstand scrutiny and questioning.
100604.subtitle_en: “I feel the need to offer some clarifications and reflections on the development of tourism at 78 degrees north,” writes tourism director Ronny Brunvoll.

100628.excerpt_en: Elisabeth first visited Svalbard in 2011, when a friend was on exchange at UNIS. “I was completely captivated by the place, the nature, the light and the people. Looking out over Hiorthfjellet bathed in golden orange-pink light.”
100628.subtitle_en: Elisabeth Gjelsteen Eines (33) is starting a job as a music teacher in Longyearbyen. But she is already a familiar face to many.

100649.excerpt_en: Sunday’s service at Svalbard Church will be broadcast live on Norway’s largest radio channel, NRK P1. The last time Svalbard Church featured in the radio programme was in 2009.
100649.subtitle_en: “Of course, it’s especially exciting to be able to broadcast from Svalbard, because it is an exotic part of Norway,” says NRK producer Hanne Næss Tremoen.

100659.excerpt_en: Early this morning, Longyearbyen School was bustling with pupils, parents and school staff. Principal Anne Line Pedersen welcomed the pupils back and sent a special greeting to all the school’s new pupils.
100659.subtitle_en: 265 excited pupils met teachers who were at least as excited to begin the 2017/18 school year.
100659.title_en: Mutual Joy on the First Day of School

100705.excerpt_en: Steve Daldorff Torgersen stands outside Lompensenteret and shows where the new entrance facing the car park will be. His pub, Karlsberger, is on one side of the building.
100705.subtitle_en: Steve Daldorff Torgersen is opening a new restaurant at Lompensenteret.

100709.excerpt_en: Lompensenteret is to be renovated and rebuilt. This autumn, they will begin the technical reconstruction in phase two.
100709.subtitle_en: “There won’t be room for everyone,” says Thon property manager Carsten Rimer.
100709.title_en: The Shopping Centre Plan Is Set

100723.excerpt_en: “We quickly became aware that the centre’s owners were going to rebuild, and saw that they had plans for a different type of restaurant from ours in our current location.”
100723.subtitle_en: Taste of Thai wanted to continue at Lompensenteret, but the shopping centre management could not find room for the business.

100753.excerpt_en: On Monday, 265 pupils started the 2017–18 school year.
100753.subtitle_en: “I’ve been looking forward to starting school for a long time. Mum works here, and I love being here,” said first-grader Victoria Risstad (6).
100753.title_en: An Exciting First Day of School for Young and Old

100756.excerpt_en: A total of 460 students are beginning their studies at Unis this autumn. That is a sharp increase from the same period last year, when the figure was 429.
100756.subtitle_en: More degree students than ever are starting this autumn.
100756.title_en: Unis Heading in the Right Direction

100781.excerpt_en: Many people in Longyearbyen will probably have noticed that Jovna Zakharias Dunfjell works as an organist at Svalbard Church. He is a familiar face in the town’s cultural life and conducts the Store Norske Male Choir and the Tundradundrene women’s choir.
100781.subtitle_en: Jovna Zakharias Dunfjell is Longyearbyen’s only national politician. Now he is running for re-election to the Sámi Parliament.

100800.excerpt_en: KSAT has provided services for the S-NPP weather satellite, which NASA used as a test satellite to determine whether new instruments were working properly. The testing phase is now over, and it will enter operational service alongside the JPSS weather satellite.
100800.subtitle_en: Kongsberg Satellite Services (KSAT) has signed a contract with NASA worth NOK 360 million.

100802.excerpt_en: After our latest trip to Svalbard with the whole family, several questions about pollution and littering came up, and we discussed them.
100802.subtitle_en: There is too much littering, the contributor believes.

100804.excerpt_en: In the area around Longyearbyen, there are remains of three German aircraft wrecks from the Second World War. One wreck lies at Hiorthamn, one is by the old airstrip in Adventdalen, and a third is probably buried in mud at the mouth of the Advent River.
100804.subtitle_en: Shot to pieces by British aircraft in June 1942.

100832.excerpt_en: During a 10-year period from the mid-1870s, there was intensive cod fishing around Svalbard, with almost 600,000 cod caught in the peak year of 1879 in Kongsfjorden alone. In 1883, this fishery collapsed completely, and the 18 boats that sailed to Kongsfjorden from mainland Norway that year returned with three cod.
100832.subtitle_en: Stocks have varied over the past 100 years.
100832.title_en: On Snow Crab, Cod and Seafood from the Waters around Svalbard

100845.excerpt_en: The climate is changing. In the Arctic, this is especially clear in Svalbard, where temperatures on land have risen three times faster than on the mainland in recent years, and winters in particular have become warmer.
100845.subtitle_en: The Svalbard course has been held for the 41st consecutive year.
100845.title_en: Challenging Nature and Safety in Svalbard

100849.excerpt_en: A few weeks ago, a news story about a boy who was attacked by sand fleas while swimming in Australia went around the world. It could just as easily have happened here in Svalbard!
100849.title_en: Watch Out for These When You Swim!

100876.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten meets the archaeologist at the Governor of Svalbard’s office at Skjæringa. What must be one of the world’s largest computer screens lights up the room, and the archaeologist needs only a brief question before her enthusiasm practically pours out of her.
100876.subtitle_en: When Lise Loktu (37) is not working as an archaeologist, she is a graphic designer.

100903.excerpt_en: Erling Hisdal represents the Tjalve Athletics Club and works at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences. He holds a master’s degree in physical activity and health from the same institution.
100903.subtitle_en: Erling Hisdal, runner-up in this year’s Norwegian Cup mountain-running series, broke the Svalbard SpacERun course record by more than three minutes.
100903.title_en: A Rout and a New Course Record

100910.excerpt_en: On Wednesday morning, police stood outside Polarflokken kindergarten and stopped drivers for inspection. The inspection had two purposes: checking whether people were driving under the influence and checking the cars’ lights. “We tested 37 cars for alcohol levels, and several more for their lights.”
100910.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard urges people to make sure their car lights are working before the polar night sets in.
100910.title_en: Checked Lights and Blood Alcohol Levels

100914.excerpt_en: The drive under the influence began outside one of the town’s bars at around 2 a.m. on Sunday. The man in his 40s was reportedly visibly intoxicated when he got into a car and drove away.
100914.subtitle_en: A tip from the public enabled police to arrest a drunk driver.

100928.excerpt_en: On Thursday evening, the Governor of Svalbard went out by helicopter to chase a female polar bear and her two cubs away from Revneset. The bears entered the area via Carolinedalen on Thursday morning.
100928.subtitle_en: It is unfortunate that the bear is finding food in the cabin area at Revneset.

100932.excerpt_en: The head of emergency preparedness at Helse Nord brought good news when he visited Longyearbyen this week. Sixteen million kroner for an anaesthetist in Longyearbyen is a quantum leap in the right direction.
100932.subtitle_en: Strengthening expertise and ensuring a permanent presence during the acute phase is an important step forward.
100932.title_en: A major strengthening of emergency preparedness

100941.excerpt_en: Library director Elin Anita Olsrud is pleased that everything is finally in place. Now she is simply looking forward to it. “The last authors were confirmed only two weeks ago.”
100941.subtitle_en: Seven authors, two hosts and a group of volunteers will fill the town with literature for five days.
100941.title_en: Ready for a festival week with visiting authors

100947.excerpt_en: Last Thursday, biologist Helga Bårdsdatter Kristiansen took local council leader Arild Olsen (Ap), Espen Klungseth Rotevatn (MDG), Kjetil Figenschou (H), Trine Krystad from Visit Svalbard and operations engineer Rasmus Bøckman from Longyearbyen Local Council to Hiorthhamn so they could see the waste problem outside town for themselves.
100947.subtitle_en: The politicians got a wake-up call when they saw the rubbish on the other side of Adventfjorden.
100947.title_en: Wading through a sea of rubbish

100977.excerpt_en: Throughout Earth’s history, we have seen a number of mass extinctions. Only a small fraction of the species that once lived on Earth are alive today.
100977.subtitle_en: Around Svalbard’s coast, we find many fascinating marine animals. Few are as peculiar as the two fish you are about to meet here. Perhaps they face an uncertain future?
100977.title_en: Two Odd Acquaintances from Svalbard’s Fjords

100989.excerpt_en: The damage has particularly affected a couple of Jason Roberts Productions AS’s buildings and Totakteren’s hall. Over the past year, the ground on the side of the buildings where the district heating pipes run has subsided by up to 40 centimetres.
100989.subtitle_en: A leak in the district heating network has damaged several buildings in the Sjøområdet area.
100989.tags_en: Longyearbyen Community Council, district heating, news, water leak

101011.excerpt_en: Traffic through Longyearbyen harbour is growing extremely quickly. In 2016, the harbour handled 75,000 passengers.
101011.subtitle_en: By August, the harbour had already handled more passengers than in the whole of last year.

101052.excerpt_en: “We have assessed how to strengthen healthcare preparedness in Svalbard. The main challenge is getting equipment and personnel there quickly.”
101052.subtitle_en: Helse Nord is allocating NOK 16 million for an anaesthesiologist on the Governor of Svalbard’s rescue helicopters. The ambulance jet plan has been put on ice.

101058.excerpt_en: Together with Beter Burrow from Washington, Petter Fjellstad and Odd Harald Hauge, Torgersen has established Svalbard Destillery AS. “The company is well established, and the name is trademark-protected in the United States. Asia is just around the corner, and we are starting the process of establishing ourselves in Longyearbyen,” says Torgersen, who is chair of the board.
101058.subtitle_en: Plans to mix imported vodka with glacier ice and sell it at a premium.

101063.excerpt_en: Marit Karlsen Brandal of Innovation Norway would like to bring a group of entrepreneurs together in a shared office at Store Norske’s administration building.
101063.subtitle_en: Innovation Norway wants to create an incubator for developing ideas in Store Norske’s administration building.

101073.excerpt_en: Professor David Pearce drove around Longyearbyen and Adventdalen and saw all the human remains, the landfill and the remnants of mining. He decided to find out whether microbes could act as a “clean-up crew” and help return nature more quickly at the landfill in Adventdalen. “I’m interested in biology.”
101073.subtitle_en: Bacteria and other microbes could help restore the landscape to how it was before rubbish began changing it.

101075.excerpt_en: A local man in his 40s and his partner, in her late 20s, both took their own lives within a short period of one another. “We have had two tragic deaths in our community over the past two weeks. It has particularly affected those closest to them, but all of us as well.”
101075.subtitle_en: The local community is deeply affected after two deaths. The hospital has a 24-hour helpline.

101081.excerpt_en: It was broken up by channels, with meltwater beneath a porridge of snow. At times, the ice was drifting north, away from their southerly destination.
101081.subtitle_en: At this time 120 years ago, three men struggled to make their way across the ice to Svalbard.

101097.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Meteorological Institute has issued a weather warning for heavy precipitation over Nordenskiöld Land from Saturday evening until Sunday afternoon. Considerable local precipitation is expected, between 10 and 25 millimetres in 24 hours.
101097.subtitle_en: Weather warning issued and roads closed.

101128.excerpt_en: On Saturday, the Norwegian Meteorological Institute issued a weather warning that heavy precipitation could fall over Nordenskiöld Land and further north on Spitsbergen from Saturday evening until Sunday afternoon. Longyearbyen remained relatively dry overnight. “Most of the precipitation has fallen in western Nordenskiöld Land.”
101128.subtitle_en: The weather warning will not be renewed. The travel ban along the closed roads remains in force.

101136.excerpt_en: At around 3:30 p.m. on Sunday, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that a female polar bear with two cubs was moving through Adventdalen. “Some locals who had been out driving reported it. We are out observing now,” says senior police officer Anders Haugerud of the Governor’s Office.
101136.subtitle_en: A female polar bear with two cubs is travelling through Adventdalen.

101140.excerpt_en: The female polar bear and her two cubs are the same bears that reached Revneset via Carolinedalen five days ago. After feeding on a reindeer carcass in the area, the bears were driven back the way they had come.
101140.subtitle_en: On Monday morning, the Governor of Svalbard is heading out to drive a female and two cubs further into Todalen.
101140.title_en: Efforts to drive away three polar bears continue

101163.excerpt_en: Activity levels were high in the makeshift control room and the “studio” at Restaurant Nansen in the Polar Hotel just before the broadcast. Host Hans Olav Brenner welcomed the audience in true Svalbard fashion, in his socks, together with host Jessika Gedin (SVT).
101163.subtitle_en: Hosts Hans Olav Brenner and Jessika Gedin spoke with three authors during NRK’s recording of “Brenner og Babel på Svalbard” on Wednesday evening.

101166.excerpt_en: Over the weekend, a total travel ban was imposed on Road 503 from Skjæringa to Elvesletta south (Melkeveien) and on Road 300, from the old museum to Huset, following the warning that was issued. Physical barriers were also put up.
101166.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is lifting the total travel ban on Roads 503 and 300.

101181.excerpt_en: “We went out by helicopter on Friday morning, but didn’t see the bears. They were last observed east of Janssonhaugen,” says Governor of Svalbard officer Trond Olsen on Friday morning.
101181.subtitle_en: The female polar bear and her two cubs have returned to areas close to town.

101184.excerpt_en: The first time Infinitum looked into whether a return scheme could be established on Svalbard was in 2007. The matter has also been discussed internally since then.
101184.subtitle_en: Infinitum is considering a deposit-return scheme or recycling collection system in Longyearbyen.

101204.excerpt_en: “The first thing I think we need to put in place is more bins in the town centre. They fill up quickly, and both residents and tourists want more of them.”
101204.subtitle_en: Operations engineer Karine Hauan believes many people want better waste services and a cleaner town. In July, she began planning more extensive and improved waste sorting at source.
101204.title_en: Taking it step by step to improve

101221.excerpt_en: “Waste shall be handled in such a way that Longyearbyen appears as a worthy gateway to one of the world’s best-managed wilderness areas.” This is the vision in Longyearbyen Local Council’s current waste management plan. Yet the town is awash with rubbish and a long way from being a worthy gateway.
101221.subtitle_en: When will we get recycling that makes sense and actually works?

101225.excerpt_en: Six companies applied to put out a total of eight so-called temporary field installations for the winter before the deadline. Only one application was rejected because of a high probability of conflict with wildlife.
101225.subtitle_en: “We are very pleased with the processes following the introduction of the new guidelines,” says Eivind Aksnes of Better Moments. The company is one of six granted permission to put up temporary field installations during the coming winter season.
101225.title_en: Six granted permission to erect temporary structures

101257.excerpt_en: “Mum had meniscus surgery on her knee, which didn’t go entirely well. That’s why she hasn’t been up here for the past two years,” she explains.
101257.subtitle_en: For years, Nora Grøndal has kept her mother company on her annual trip north. The past two years have been different.

101276.excerpt_en: The person flying the paraglider had not notified the airport control tower, but was spotted by chance in Adventdalen just before the SAS-Braathens flight was due to land. The alarm was raised, and the tower had to divert the aircraft.
101276.subtitle_en: A scheduled flight had to be diverted on Sunday afternoon before landing because of a paraglider pilot.

101278.excerpt_en: There were 297 applicants for this year’s reindeer hunt, but one of them failed to return the permit by last year’s deadline and was therefore not awarded an animal this year. The applicants included 68 women and 228 men, representing a total of 73 hunting teams.
101278.subtitle_en: A total of 296 people have been awarded reindeer ahead of this year’s hunt. That is roughly the usual number.
101278.title_en: Nearly 300 awarded reindeer ahead of the hunt

101303.excerpt_en: Birger Johan Lund was five years old when he, together with his family and the rest of Longyearbyen’s population, was evacuated to Scotland in the autumn of 1941. Now he has returned to the old site, where all that remains of the barracks he grew up in are the stumps of its foundations.
101303.subtitle_en: Lund Cabin in Adventdalen was his playground—the cabin where the Germans established their first meteorological station on Svalbard during the war.

101305.excerpt_en: For three years, researchers from the University of Copenhagen, working with UNIS, have been carrying out a project at the innermost coal dump in Bjørndalen. They have studied what is inside the dump, what comes out of it and what effect it has on nature.
101305.subtitle_en: A three-year study of a coal dump in Bjørndalen has given researchers the answer to why some plants die.
101305.title_en: Found the Answer to Plant Death

101312.excerpt_en: “I don’t think we should have any great expectations for next year’s national budget. I don’t expect any changes before 2008,” says Lian.
101312.subtitle_en: Local council leader Ellen Lian (Conservative) no longer believes the tax increase will be reversed next year.

101324.excerpt_en: In an identical letter to O&K Service and Selmer Skanska, head of planning and development Vigdis Hole asks for an explanation of the illegally installed site cabins in the Sjøområdet area: “Longyearbyen Local Council has not received any application or notification concerning these cabins.”
101324.subtitle_en: Skanska Norge placed a site cabin complex in the Sjøområdet area without permission. The local council is demanding an explanation.
101324.title_en: Owner of Unauthorised Site Cabins Found

101330.excerpt_en: “This is the most serious case we have seen involving the owner of a listed building. I can hardly recall seeing anything like it on the mainland either,” exclaims Susan Barr, an adviser at the Directorate for Cultural Heritage in Oslo.
101330.subtitle_en: Jason Roberts has been reported by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage for violating the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act after beginning construction on a listed building.

101347.excerpt_en: Thor Siggerud first came to Svalbard in the summer of 1960 as a newly employed geologist with the Norwegian Polar Institute (NP). In those days, Svalbard was still a distant and strange world, and Longyearbyen a somewhat shabby collection of buildings centred on Nybyen and Sverdrupbyen.
101347.subtitle_en: They are both equally fascinated by Svalbard and by what the land is made of: millions of years have brought them together, while 34 years separate them.

101349.excerpt_en: The research project is one of Norway’s three flagship projects under IPY, which runs from 1 March next year to 1.
101349.subtitle_en: One of the largest international research collaborations ever undertaken in the Arctic will take place during the International Polar Year (IPY). The entire Arctic Ocean will be mapped from the seabed to the surface.
101349.title_en: The Entire Arctic Ocean to Be Mapped

101357.excerpt_en: Last week, the Environment and Industry Committee (MNU) recommended granting Asplan Viak permission to build an access road to the new field station for northern lights observatories by Gruve 7 mountain.
101357.subtitle_en: The local council has approved the application to build a road to the new northern lights observatory at Breinosa.

101368.excerpt_en: Museum director Gerd Johanne Valen says she is nevertheless pleased, even though her museum did not come out on top. Svalbard Museum was one of three nominees, after around 20 museums had been assessed.

101393.excerpt_en: The two bicycles were stolen in Longyearbyen on 14 June this year.
101393.subtitle_en: The three youths who stole and vandalised two bicycles in June will not be punished. The case was resolved through the conciliation board.

101396.excerpt_en: “The last time I was here was when the Progress Party formed a local branch. That was in January 2003, and it was bitterly cold and dark.”
101396.subtitle_en: Nearly 50 people turned up at Funken on Wednesday to hear Siv Jensen, leader of the Progress Party.
101396.title_en: Party Leader Siv Jensen on Svalbard

101410.excerpt_en: The gun is an important fetish. It makes the man—and the woman, of course.
101410.subtitle_en: There are frequent gunshots on Svalbard, without anyone paying much attention to them. There can hardly be anywhere else in the world with a higher density of firearms, apart from certain outlaw states in Southeast Asia.

101425.excerpt_en: “This is the biggest thing that has happened during the time I’ve worked here!” Nurse Gerd Gregersen enters the hospital common room, where Monica Buschmann is sitting beside a pram.
101425.subtitle_en: For the first time in 15 years, a child has been born at Longyearbyen Hospital. Little Alva arrived on Sunday afternoon.

101447.excerpt_en: A film crew of around 70 people, with nearly 40 tonnes of equipment, has taken over Isfjorden this week. Filming of the major British production “True North” began on Monday and will continue for four weeks at Bjonapynten, Von Postbreen and Sveabreen.
101447.subtitle_en: Filming of the major motion picture “True North” began in Bjonahamna in Tempelfjorden on Monday. The film crew will be working for four weeks.

101453.excerpt_en: All three bodies point out that seasonal workers will be excluded from the temporary tax scheme proposed by the appointed working group tasked with reviewing Svalbard’s tax system following the increase. “We want to draw the working group’s serious attention to the fact that this will once again particularly affect the tourism industry.”
101453.subtitle_en: The tourism industry, the Governor of Svalbard and the local council all fear that seasonal workers will lose out under the proposed tax scheme.
101453.title_en: Fears Tourism Will Be the Loser

101462.excerpt_en: “We are interested in the fact that Svalbard is a family community, but we have not found any studies of family life here, even though it is not a new phenomenon.”
101462.subtitle_en: Over the coming weeks, two professors and two master’s students will study family life in Longyearbyen.

101475.excerpt_en: According to duty officer Roar Hilde of the Governor of Svalbard’s office, one of the neighbours tried for a long time to get the partygoers to show consideration. “Around 3 a.m., she gave up and called us for help. We went out and told them the party was over,” says Hilde.
101475.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard had to go out early Saturday morning to end a party in Road 222 that was disturbing the neighbours.

101483.excerpt_en: “We were notified of the fight around midnight and went out. By the time we arrived, the fight had broken up on its own, and those involved had left the scene,” says duty officer Roar Hilde of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
101483.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard went out early Sunday morning to break up a fight outside the Karls-berger pub.

101496.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Meteorological Institute is warning of increasing northwesterly gales along Spitsbergen’s west coast on Monday evening, with scattered snow showers and temperatures around zero. Slightly lower temperatures are also expected later in the week.
101496.subtitle_en: On Sunday, people in Longyearbyen woke up to the year’s first snow. Around 10 centimetres of wet, heavy snow fell overnight. Large flocks of geese could be seen flying in formation over Isfjorden.

101500.excerpt_en: Thirty-three-year-old Ronny Gjøse is director of Radisson SAS Polar Hotel, Spitsbergen Hotel and the guesthouse in Nybyen. For the second time, he was nominated for the Young Leader of the Year title alongside eight other candidates from across Norway.
101500.subtitle_en: Hotel director Ronny Gjøse was not named Young Leader of the Year in the travel industry. The award was presented on Tuesday.
101500.title_en: Did Not Win Young Leader of the Year

101517.excerpt_en: Previous research has shown that the glaucous gull is among the most contaminated Arctic seabirds when it comes to chlorinated organic compounds such as PCBs and DDT. But little is known about the effects these compounds have on seabirds and how this pollution is transferred to their offspring.
101517.subtitle_en: A new doctoral study shows that glaucous gulls in the Arctic, particularly on Bjørnøya, are contaminated by brominated flame retardants and fluorinated compounds.
101517.title_en: New Environmental Toxins Found in Glaucous Gulls

101520.excerpt_en: The fire was automatically reported to the fire station at around 4:30 p.m. Fire chief Alf-Morten Pedersen says the cabin would have burned down if the fire service had not arrived so quickly.
101520.subtitle_en: A fire broke out at Russerhytta in Sjøskrenten on Tuesday afternoon. No one was in the cabin, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

101527.excerpt_en: One of the cars left the road on the stretch between Longyearbyen School and Nybyen at around 3:30 p.m. “The car overturned, but fortunately no one was injured.”
101527.subtitle_en: Two cars ran off the road on Tuesday afternoon because of the icy conditions.

101560.excerpt_en: The Directorate for Cultural Heritage and the Directorate for Nature Management have proposed to the Minister of Climate and the Environment that Svalbard, Jan Mayen and Bouvet Island be added to the list of possible new Norwegian World Heritage sites.

101561.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has ordered Jason Roberts to demolish the illegal extension at Taubanelageret. Meanwhile, Økokrim has taken over the further investigation of the criminal case.

101571.subtitle_en: According to Vladimir Makarov, an authorised representative of Trust Arktikugol, the company plans to staff Pyramiden this winter. Several buildings will be renovated and opened to tourists.

101583.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, Rune B. Hansen left Svalbard “for the last time” after nearly three years as assistant governor.
101583.subtitle_en: Assistant Governor Rune B. Hansen believes there should be room for differing views in Svalbard, and understands that some people do not always follow the law.

101606.excerpt_en: See more pictures here! The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the dead whale last Thursday.
101606.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has secured the lower jaw of a sperm whale that washed up in Van Mijenfjorden.

101623.excerpt_en: Police sergeant Synnøve Stette of the Governor of Svalbard’s office says the man was stopped during a drink-driving checkpoint at around 1:30 a.m., and his driving licence was confiscated after a blood sample was taken. The man lives in Longyearbyen.
101623.subtitle_en: A man in his 20s was caught drink-driving in Longyearbyen early Sunday morning.

101625.excerpt_en: The 34-year-old, who is from Tromsø but currently lives in Møre og Romsdal, must now appear before Nord-Troms District Court charged with multimillion-kroner fraud. The fraud allegedly continued for many years, and the man is alleged to have sold highly exclusive Rolex and Breitling watches for more than NOK 6 million.
101625.subtitle_en: A 34-year-old man allegedly sold luxury watches worth several million kroner without preparing annual accounts or paying VAT. He is alleged to have collected several of the watches in Longyearbyen.

101630.excerpt_en: Kjell Mork was unanimously appointed as the new leader, while Heinrich Eggenfellner (Conservative) was elected deputy leader. The change follows former leader Bjørn Fjukstad requesting leave from the position earlier this year because of the criminal case against him following last summer’s fatal accident at Svea Nord.
101630.subtitle_en: Kjell Mork (Labour) has been elected as the new leader of Longyearbyen Community Council.
101630.title_en: Kjell Mork Becomes Community Council Leader

101645.excerpt_en: The service is being introduced as a result of Posten’s agreement with freight carrier West Air Sweden taking effect at the end of October. “We have not previously been able to offer this because the regularity of the postal service has unfortunately not been good enough.”
101645.subtitle_en: From Monday, Posten will deliver packages to private individuals and businesses at their doors in Longyearbyen.
101645.title_en: Posten to Deliver Packages to Your Door

101650.excerpt_en: The incident took place on 8 September this year and was detected by liquor-control inspectors from Alkontroll.

101650.title_en: Served Alcohol to Highly Intoxicated Guest

101665.subtitle_en: Store Norske has failed to reach an agreement with its insurers over compensation following the fire at the Svea Nord mine. Store Norske has therefore filed suit against the companies in Nord-Troms District Court.

101673.excerpt_en: The artwork was supposed to have been in place when Svalbard Research Park was officially opened by the King and Queen on 26 April this year.
101673.subtitle_en: Advanced glass art was to adorn the Research Park in Longyearbyen. Following a bankruptcy in Germany, the project has now been abandoned.

For ten days, he has led a group of 15 students on a study trip to Svalbard.
101689.subtitle_en: In the future, there will be railways to Svea and Colesbukta, while Barentsburg will have been closed. Longyearbyen will also undergo major changes.

101712.excerpt_en: “The fact that I was elected for just one year was a key factor in my decision to accept. It gives me a manageable perspective on whether this is something I enjoy,” says Kjell Mork (Labour).
101712.subtitle_en: Incoming Longyearbyen Community Council leader Kjell Mork considers his election a great vote of confidence. But he will not predict anything about the next election.
101712.title_en: Taking It One Year at a Time

article_keywords_en: Ministry of Climate and the Environment
101719.excerpt_en: A week ago Friday, it became clear that the Directorate for Cultural Heritage and the Directorate for Nature Management want Svalbard and Jan Mayen and Bouvet Island added to Norway’s tentative list for UNESCO’s World Heritage List. The Ministry of Climate and the Environment will now decide whether the tentative list should be updated with the new areas.
101719.subtitle_en: Even if Svalbard is included on Norway’s tentative list, it will be a long time before the archipelago might appear on UNESCO’s World Heritage List.

101730.subtitle_en: A clean-up partnership between Longyearbyen Community Council, the Governor of Svalbard and Store Norske could be in place before the end of the year.
101730.title_en: Seeking Broader Cooperation on Clean-Up Efforts

101739.excerpt_en: “It has been a very good year, and I’m pleased so far,” says gallery manager John W. Olsen.

101739.title_en: A Good Year for Galleri Svalbard

101759.subtitle_en: The sociologists researching family life in Longyearbyen have received considerable interest in their project.

101764.subtitle_en: Could the University of the Arctic become a static elephant, or can it continue as a dynamic network for higher education in polar regions?

101768.subtitle_en: What the Governor of Svalbard suspected was illegal transshipment in Hornsund turned out to be entirely lawful.

101793.subtitle_en: The government will allocate an additional NOK 500,000 to tourism in Svalbard in next year’s national budget.

In the Middle Ages, the Church took a tithe; one of Islam’s Five Pillars is zakat, an annual tax of 2.5 percent; and in mainland Norway, people must pay for a clear conscience for all the sinful things they do.

101821.subtitle_en: The government will allocate NOK 80 million to the International Polar Year, IPY. See the entire Svalbard budget here!

101824.subtitle_en: The Local Council will not give Jason Roberts more time to comment on the illegal extension at Taubanelageret.

101828.subtitle_en: With a packed programme and a healthy dose of self-deprecation, Svalbardbutikken celebrated itself and Coop’s centenary last Saturday.

101830.subtitle_en: Students’ preferences will be mapped as early as the autumn before they start upper secondary school. The scheme is intended to ensure stability in the student body.

101832.subtitle_en: The Environment and Business Committee wants access roads to cabins to be allowed to extend beyond 100 metres.
101832.title_en: Does not want a limit on cabin roads

101870.title_en: Housing development clashes with snowmobile trail

101883.subtitle_en: The Environment and Business Committee supports Stefano Poli’s plans to build an airship museum at Sjøskrenten.

101886.excerpt_en: “This is something several employees have wanted. The biggest advantage is having an internet-based service at home, along with faster internet access—for example, for online banking,” says Kings Bay office manager Kristian Thowsen.
101886.subtitle_en: Interest in Triple Play is high in Ny-Ålesund. Since the service was installed, more than 20 customers have connected.

101888.subtitle_en: Store Norske is suing its insurers in the Nord-Troms District Court.
101888.title_en: Svea Nord fire goes to court

101901.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s Super Puma had to collect a woman in labour from Svea during the night. She was flown onward by air ambulance to Tromsø hospital.

101917.subtitle_en: Neighbours of two planned buildings below Road 228 are protesting against the projects. They are asking the Local Council to find another site.

101951.subtitle_en: The tax increase will remain, and the Local Council will have less money to work with next year. No funding has been allocated for backup power either. See the full Svalbard budget here!

101962.subtitle_en: The Governor’s duty officer had to go out during the night to help an extremely drunk, sleeping pub guest get home.

101970.excerpt_en: The flight was cancelled because of local weather conditions at the airport here in Longyearbyen. All approximately 100 passengers who were due to travel on the flight will be transferred to tomorrow’s flight.
101970.subtitle_en: The flight from Oslo and Tromsø scheduled to land at Svalbard Airport this afternoon has been cancelled.

101985.excerpt_en: The man, who lives in Longyearbyen and is in his late 20s, was very drunk when he started fighting just after midnight, according to duty officer Brynjulf Eide. “No one was injured, but we took the man with us, first to our office and then to his own bed,” Eide says.
101985.subtitle_en: The Governor’s office had to collect a drunk man from Karls-Berger Pub during the night because he was fighting.

101989.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s Super Puma helicopter was dispatched around 2 p.m. Thursday to retrieve an injured person aboard a Norwegian fishing boat.

101998.excerpt_en: This year, the money will go to Doctors Without Borders, an organization that works under extreme conditions around the world and provides medical aid to some of the poorest people on the planet.
101998.subtitle_en: The annual televised fundraising campaign takes place on Sunday. Thousands of volunteers will go door to door throughout Norway collecting money, which will be counted live during prime time on our licence-funded channel.

102004.excerpt_en: See more photos here! Longyearbyen School has been under construction and expansion for a year and a half.

102004.title_en: Royal opening of the assembly hall

102010.subtitle_en: Over the next few weeks, the Governor of Svalbard will visit a number of businesses in Longyearbyen to check that they are not storing PCB illegally.

102049.excerpt_en: See the municipal list here! So far, more than NOK 192 million has been raised nationwide for Doctors Without Borders.

102049.title_en: Svalbard tops the country in giving

102071.title_en: A Dignified Finale for the Telethon

102081.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol Director General Jurij V. Tsivka is unhappy about the shipment of fruit and vegetables to Barentsburg.

102086.excerpt_en: Mine manager Per Nilssen at Svea Nord says the many stoppages have resulted in production being 400,000 tonnes below budget. Nilssen also emphasizes that some of this is because production resumed later than planned after the fire.
102086.subtitle_en: A series of operational problems at Svea Nord has left coal production so far this year well below budget.

102091.excerpt_en: The self-employed 30-year-old was convicted of receiving Rolex and Breitling watches from a watchmaker’s shop in Tromsø and reselling them for payment. The handling took place in Longyearbyen from June 2001 through March 2003.
102091.subtitle_en: A 30-year-old man from Longyearbyen has been sentenced to a suspended 90-day prison term for handling a quantity of luxury watches.

102105.excerpt_en: The company wants to launch the trips next summer, from early August to early September. Strømsholmen Sjøsportsenter was established in Møre og Romsdal and began operating in 1981.
102105.subtitle_en: Strømsholmen Sjøsportsenter wants to offer week-long trips in Svalbard where guests can go diving.
102105.title_en: Wants to Launch Diving Trips in Svalbard

102119.excerpt_en: An art committee—including artistic consultant Solveig Ovanger, who chairs the committee, and airport director Ole Rambech—decided who would decorate the new building.
102119.subtitle_en: Trine Mauritz Eriksen will create the artwork for the new airport terminal. She mainly uses wadmal in her work.

102135.excerpt_en: The research project ended last week, and the four researchers have returned to the mainland. In their luggage are recordings of hour-long interviews with more than 50 people living in Longyearbyen.
102135.subtitle_en: The four family researchers who studied Longyearbyen society conducted in-depth interviews with more than 50 people.

102143.excerpt_en: Carrying 3,387 kilos of mail, the first mail plane landed at Svalbard Airport 33 minutes late after the de-icing machine in Tromsø ended up in a ditch and delayed the departure. “The weather was fine throughout the journey north; we even saw Bear Island.”
102143.subtitle_en: “This is a great joy for all of us on Svalbard,” exclaimed Jan Haugan of Svalbardbutikken when the first mail plane landed at 11:18 a.m. on Monday.

102152.excerpt_en: Rune Bergstrøm, the Governor’s environmental protection chief, had long been concerned that a fire would start inside the large spoil heap just outside Barentsburg. A little over two weeks ago, he was in the Russian mining town to measure the temperature in the heap.
102152.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is asking mainland Norwegian authorities to pressure Trust Arktikugol into extinguishing the smoldering fire in Barentsburg.

102161.excerpt_en: Five days a week, the West Air Sweden plane will depart Tromsø Airport carrying mail and groceries to Longyearbyen. It is all rather dizzying, even though the event did not prompt any major ceremony at the airport.
102161.subtitle_en: At 11:18 a.m. on Monday, the very first mail plane landed at Svalbard Airport. Naturally, many will object that mail planes—or cargo planes, if you prefer—have landed on Svalbard before. And they have, but this is the first aircraft on a regular route.

102172.excerpt_en: The new general rule introduced on Monday is that all forms of liquid are prohibited through security, with a few exceptions. Svalbardposten wrote two weeks ago that duty-free sales could decline when the new security rules take effect.
102172.subtitle_en: From Monday, you will need to think extra carefully about how you pack when flying—and especially what you put in your hand luggage.

102182.excerpt_en: On October 11 this year, the Environment and Industry Committee (MNU) sent a response to Tegne & Byggeservice, the responsible applicant, approving the application for a framework permit without authorizing construction to begin.
102182.subtitle_en: Per Viggo Teigen must halt construction of the new fabric hangar he has erected in the Sjøområdet district.
102182.title_en: Built a Fabric Hangar Without Permission

102197.excerpt_en: “The goods were not sent from our store here in Longyearbyen, but taken from Coop’s central warehouse in Tromsø, and were of top quality. The claim that they were past their sell-by date and unusable is therefore wrong,” says Jan Haugan.
102197.subtitle_en: Jan Haugan, managing director of Svalbardbutikken, says he feels hurt and outraged by the claim that the food sent to Barentsburg was unusable.
102197.title_en: Outraged by Claims of Poor-Quality Food

102200.excerpt_en: The recreation center will give employees the opportunity to pursue their interests when they are not working in Svea. “It is a fact that many of our employees are technically minded.”
102200.subtitle_en: Store Norske wants a recreation center where employees can do carpentry, welding, and work on cars and snowmobiles.
102200.title_en: Wants a Hobby Workshop for the Boys

102203.excerpt_en: “There is grave concern in the Norwegian government because of the fire in the spoil heap,” Knut Storberget said when he met Trust Arktikugol Director General Jurij V. Tsivka in Barentsburg on Friday.
102203.subtitle_en: Justice Minister Knut Storberget expressed deep concern when he visited Barentsburg. “The fire in the enormous spoil heap is extremely serious,” he said.

102219.excerpt_en: We are sitting at Café Busen. Outside, it is half-dark and raw.
102219.subtitle_en: He has kept himself airborne over Svalbard for nearly 30 years. Now he is soon coming in to land.

102226.excerpt_en: “We don’t yet have an overview of how it went, but it probably went beyond all expectations. We sold more tickets than last year, and virtually every event was packed,” says Sneltvedt.
102226.subtitle_en: Gry Sneltvedt, head of the festival committee at Longyearbyen Blues Club, is extremely pleased with this year’s blues festival.

102229.excerpt_en: Several institutions in Longyearbyen must improve their fire-safety procedures after the fire service carried out a series of inspections over the past month. Two of them are the town’s kindergartens.
102229.subtitle_en: Fire safety is inadequate in Longyearbyen’s kindergartens. Significant faults and deficiencies have also been uncovered at Galleri Svalbard.

102249.excerpt_en: None of the passengers flying from Svalbard Airport today had to leave anything behind at security. “There are actually very few people carrying hand luggage at all today.”
102249.subtitle_en: The chaos feared by Avinor and others because of the new rules failed to materialize ahead of the first flight departure after their introduction. Security screening proceeded smoothly.
102249.title_en: Fears of Airport Chaos Fail to Materialize

102254.excerpt_en: The grant funds from Svalbard Science Forum will be distributed among master’s and doctoral students at Norwegian universities. The funds will cover additional expenses connected with projects on Svalbard, the Norwegian Polar Institute writes on its website.
102254.subtitle_en: Svalbard Science Forum is awarding grants to students and researchers with projects on Svalbard in 2007.

102264.excerpt_en: A few hours before the support was due to be erected last Friday, a crack running right across one of the main beams was discovered. No one had seen the damage before; it became apparent during a test lift with a mobile crane, which put the beam under stress.
102264.subtitle_en: The cableway support that was due to be erected at Skjæringa a week ago will remain on the ground for the time being.

102270.excerpt_en: During a liquor-inspection on 8 September, Alkontroll pointed out that an obviously intoxicated person was inside the restaurant at Polarhotellet.
102270.subtitle_en: Polarhotellet will probably receive only a written warning after the restaurant was found to have breached liquor-serving regulations earlier this year.

102273.excerpt_en: See some of Synnøve’s pictures here! Kunstpause is being held on Svalbard for the fifth time, and this year the event is also shaped by Longyearbyen’s centenary, with a stronger local focus than in previous years.
102273.subtitle_en: Kunstpause opened at the Gallery on Thursday evening. Liv Mari Schei presented selections from her forthcoming CD, while Synnøve Haga opened her photo exhibition.

102280.excerpt_en: The issue of building tourist cabins, often referred to as commercial cabins, has dragged on for a long time without a decision. Svalbard Wildlife Service was finally turned down last autumn for its plans for a tourist facility at Elveneset, at the mouth of De Geerdalen.
102280.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has received six applications to build tourist cabins. Only two or three of the projects will be approved.

102290.excerpt_en: A few searches on SAS Braathens’ website show that tickets are no longer as cheap as they used to be, even when booked many months—or up to a year—in advance.
102290.subtitle_en: Airfares between Longyearbyen and Tromsø have shot up since the new postal aircraft began operating.

102295.excerpt_en: The planned snow fences will be placed in an area that Svalbard Villmarkssenter AS uses as a route for its winter dog-sled tours. Correspondence between UNIS, the Governor of Svalbard and Villmarkssenteret shows that the company believes the fences will diminish tourists’ experience of its dog-sled product.
102295.subtitle_en: UNIS plans to erect twelve snow fences in Adventdalen. Svalbard Villmarkssenter AS believes they will spoil the experience of pristine nature.

102312.excerpt_en: The inflatable Mini Anne manikin and an instructional film are among the most important tools now being introduced to prevent deaths from cardiac arrest. Last Thursday, the seventh-grade students received…
102312.subtitle_en: Students in seventh grade at Longyearbyen School can help reduce the number of people who die from cardiac arrest.

102314.excerpt_en: Jason Roberts bought the warehouse from Store Norske and carried out extensive work to convert it into a residence. In February 2003, the exterior of the building was listed, as was Taubanesentralen next door.
102314.subtitle_en: The Directorate for Cultural Heritage has rejected Jason Roberts’ appeal after the Governor of Svalbard halted the illegal expansion of Taubanelageret earlier this autumn.

102333.excerpt_en: The Governor learned how much damage the polar bear had caused during the August inspection tour. “We believe it is the same bear that wrecked four cabins in Agardhbukta, Dunérbukta and Mohnbukta.”
102333.subtitle_en: Several cabins on the east coast have been wrecked by polar bears this summer. Now the Longyearbyen Hunters and Anglers’ Association is repairing one of them.

102340.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Community Council wants to prevent students from travelling to the mainland because the provision at Longyearbyen School is inadequate. The Education Enterprise has now drawn up an action plan for planning the coming school year.
102340.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council wants greater predictability regarding upper secondary education at Longyearbyen School. Its action plan is now ready.
102340.title_en: Early Survey of Students’ Study Preferences

102362.excerpt_en: The Governor responded after receiving a report that a car had driven off the road just above Polarhotellet. When officers arrived, they suspected that the driver was not sober.
102362.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard suspects drunk driving after a car left the road early Friday morning.

102369.excerpt_en: The boat will remain in Tempelfjorden from mid-February to mid-May, but the plan is to put it in place at the end of December or early January. Basecamp wants to position it where it lay in 2005, on the northwestern side of Tempelfjorden between Kapp Murdoch and Bjonapynten.
102369.subtitle_en: Basecamp has been granted permission by the Governor of Svalbard to freeze “Noorderlicht” into the ice in Tempelfjorden for another three years.
102369.title_en: Allowed to Keep Boat in the Ice Until 2010

102384.excerpt_en: Agnes Kvilvang was Store Norske’s chief union representative from 1984 to 1992 and received the award for her efforts during the critical years. “There was always something that was about to be shut down back then.”
102384.subtitle_en: On Saturday, Agnes Kvilvang received Store Norske’s 200,000-kroner anniversary award.
102384.title_en: Store Norske Awarded to Agnes Kvilvang

102390.excerpt_en: The matter stems from her struggle to obtain the pension she is entitled to. Freia Hutzschenreuter was 18 when she came to Norway from West Germany in 1956 and found work at Findus in Hammerfest.
102390.subtitle_en: Freia Hutzschenreuter refuses to accept being registered in German archives as homeless on Svalbard in autumn 1975.

102393.excerpt_en: The exhibition is on display at Galleri Svalbard and opened in connection with Kunstpause last Thursday. Many people found their way to the gallery that evening, which opened with Liv Mari Schei performing some selections from her forthcoming CD, “Soløde”.
102393.subtitle_en: Synnøve Haga’s photo exhibition “The Things Close to Home” shows the beautiful subjects found right outside Longyearbyen residents’ doors.
102393.title_en: Exhibition at the Gallery Focuses on the Things Close to Home

102403.excerpt_en: “A man must accept his fate,” Robin Hood replied when his great love, Lady Marian, asked if he would marry her. The adults in the audience burst out laughing, and the story of Robin Hood also ended happily at Longyearbyen School.
102403.subtitle_en: Students at Longyearbyen School’s lower secondary level presented the results of this year’s project week, making both children and adults laugh.
102403.title_en: An Ironic and Elegant Robin Hood

102433.excerpt_en: See more photos from Kunstpause here! A large part of Longyearbyen’s population, along with many visitors, braved the weather to attend the event in the town square.
102433.subtitle_en: This year’s Kunstpause was the fifth edition, reflecting Longyearbyen’s centenary celebrations. Many local artists were represented.

102453.excerpt_en: “Foreign media have increasingly begun writing reports about Svalbard—about how people can come here and how they can find work here.”
102453.subtitle_en: A Bulgarian couple were expelled from Svalbard on Sunday afternoon. Neither had a job or money to stay.

102456.excerpt_en: Both of Lufttransport's aircraft were grounded last Friday.
102456.subtitle_en: Lufttransport has now repaired one of its two aircraft and will fly to Svea today, weather permitting. This will be Lufttransport's first flight since Friday.

102467.excerpt_en: “We were called by the people who run Grillen at around 2 a.m. because of a brawl.”
102467.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard had to respond early Friday morning because two intoxicated men had got into a fight.

102475.excerpt_en: “Today's flight has been cancelled because there was insufficient braking action on the runway in Longyearbyen,” says Unni Johansen of SAS Ground Services in Longyearbyen. The aircraft has now returned to Tromsø.
102475.subtitle_en: The flight from Oslo to Longyearbyen was cancelled on Tuesday because of runway conditions in Longyearbyen.

102498.excerpt_en: See the full overview here! The decision meant an increase of NOK 49,000 compared with the recommendation from Chief Administrative Officer Sigmund Engdal.
102498.subtitle_en: The Executive Committee approved the final allocation of this year's cork funds on Tuesday.

102503.excerpt_en: “If it had been allowed, I’d probably have been born up here. I’ve been here forever, almost, and took my first steps at the canteen in Svea.”
102503.subtitle_en: She is rail-thin and remarkably sturdily built. True, she did have one arm broken, but it has hardly slowed her down.

102516.excerpt_en: In October, Svalbardposten reported that the Spitsbergen Airship Museum had been allocated a site at Sjøskrenten.
102516.subtitle_en: Stefano Poli has been allocated a site at Sjøskrenten for the airship museum, and is pleased with it. Store Norske believes the site is poorly suited for museum operations.
102516.title_en: Wants to Give Museum a Better Site

102557.excerpt_en: UNIS is already involved in six projects connected with the International Polar Year (IPY), leading one of them. Following a new round of calls and funding allocations by the Research Council of Norway last week, another project has received support.
102557.subtitle_en: A new research project led by UNIS has been included in the IPY, which begins next March.

102576.excerpt_en: A hint of red, greenish white, a shimmer of gold and silver. Gently undulating.
102576.subtitle_en: A frost-clear starry sky. Ribbons of northern lights over the mountains; over Longyeardalen, Sukkertoppen, into Adventdalen, behind Operafjellet.

102603.excerpt_en: “The property must be restored to the condition it was in before the illegal building work began. The requirement applies both to the building itself and to the outdoor areas on the property and neighboring property,” writes Vigdis Hole, head of planning and development at Longyearbyen Local Council, in a letter to Jason Roberts.
102603.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council has decided that Jason Roberts must demolish the extension at Taubanelageret. The deadline is 15 June next year.

102613.excerpt_en: The couple came to Longyearbyen in the autumn with their marriage papers in their luggage, but the Governor refused to marry them after discovering that one party's identity could not be documented. “I contacted the population register on the mainland that had issued the certificate of no impediment, which is intended to clarify whether the statutory conditions for marriage are met.”
102613.subtitle_en: A couple were refused permission to marry on Svalbard because one of the parties did not have valid identity documents.

102618.excerpt_en: “It had become a long, big ice slide that we had been waiting for since last winter. We have always been allowed to keep it, but the new principal melted it,” says Magnus Berg.
102618.subtitle_en: The fifth-graders are furious that the school leadership melted away the ice slide they used to play on.

102632.excerpt_en: After the inspection in Barentsburg, the Russians met with Governor Per Sefland in Longyearbyen on Sunday. In addition to two men from the Russian energy directorate, Consul Vjatsjeslav G.
102632.subtitle_en: Representatives of the Russian energy directorate inspected Barentsburg last week. Extensive measures to extinguish the dump fires are now being announced.

102652.excerpt_en: Passengers could see fuel leaking from one of the wings, and the aircraft had to turn back after 20 minutes in the air. The return and landing at Gardermoen proceeded without problems.
102652.subtitle_en: The SAS Braathens aircraft had to return to Gardermoen on Sunday because of a leak in a fuel tank.
102652.title_en: Had to Turn Back After Fuel Leak

102655.excerpt_en: Geophysicist Yngvar T. Gjessing receives the honour for his contributions to research and teaching.
102655.subtitle_en: His Majesty the King has appointed Professor Yngvar T. Gjessing a Knight, First Class, of the Royal Norwegian Order of St. Olav.

102660.excerpt_en: A snowmobile party from Longyearbyen saw fresh bear tracks outside the cabin at Fredheim on Wednesday evening.
102660.subtitle_en: A polar bear was spotted at Fredheim on Wednesday evening. Harald Soleim at Kapp Wijk has also had a visit from a bear.

102667.excerpt_en: See the full Red List here! Of the 47 Svalbard species classified as threatened, 16 are considered critically endangered, 13 endangered and 18 vulnerable.
102667.subtitle_en: Of the 70 species from Svalbard included on the Red List published this week, 47 are classified as threatened.

102672.excerpt_en: In previous seasons, the crew at Hopen Radio saw as many as 300 bears. In the 2005–06 season, the number had fallen to 53 polar bears.
102672.subtitle_en: There has been a marked decline in polar bear visits to Hopen over the past year. The reason is that there is no ice around the island.

102681.excerpt_en: If you had a crooked hut, a somewhat shabby plank shed, a pile of pallets, a broken snowmobile you could not bear to get rid of—in short, anything that needed to be put somewhere—the Harbour Area was the place. Boats were also laid up here for the winter.
102681.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen has an area that has traditionally been a place for free spirits and cowboys. It is a distinctive, rough-and-ready place filled with odds and ends. A place with its own laws and rules.

102696.excerpt_en: Previously, the Governor of Svalbard had not permitted the use of seawater during firefighting because of the risk of dioxin formation, which is highly hazardous to health. Wants to use seawater In a letter to the Governor, Director General Jurij V.
102696.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard permits limited use of seawater to bring the dump fires in Barentsburg under control.
102696.title_en: Allowed to Use Seawater to Fight Fires

102712.excerpt_en: The Ministry of the Environment’s response took two years to arrive. When it finally came last week, the conclusion was that the Local Council must rectify the fact that several people are living in Sjøområdet without authorization.
102712.subtitle_en: The Local Council must resolve the fact that several people are living illegally in Sjøområdet. The Ministry of the Environment has decided this.

102714.excerpt_en: The Governor’s duty officer, Petter Braaten, was notified that a loose dog had been spotted on the main road in Adventdalen shortly before 11 p.m. on Sunday. He went out and searched for the dog with a light, but found nothing.
102714.subtitle_en: Three dogs escaped from Svalbard Huskies’ kennel near Gruve 6 on Sunday evening. One ended up in a full-blown fight inside the kennel.

102724.excerpt_en: It was the car’s owner who discovered that a man had got into his vehicle and was revving the engine hard after driving a short distance back and forth.
102724.subtitle_en: A man was caught red-handed in a stolen car on Road 222 in Longyearbyen on Tuesday morning. He is suspected of being under the influence.
102724.title_en: Car Theft and Suspected Drunk Driving

102752.excerpt_en: Children and young people from the age of five through their teens impressed greatly at the gymnastics show in the hall last Sunday. Across 16 routines, they demonstrated much of what they could do, including floor exercises, gym-wheel work and acrobatics.
102752.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen’s younger residents showcased agility, balance and a love of gymnastics when they entertained with a gymnastics show in the hall last Sunday.
102752.title_en: Acrobatic Display in the Sports Hall

102767.excerpt_en: Ice-covered fjords put us in a good mood; swelling glaciers, snow blowing white, the intense stabs of cold along the bridge of the nose. Yes, even the season’s first frostbite has something positive about it.
102767.subtitle_en: We do not burrow into our clothes in winter and hunch our shoulders, we who live up here in the north. We are not here by chance, but as the result of natural selection. Like other mammals drawn to cold regions, we live in Svalbard because we thrive in the land as it is.

102775.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has just concluded a major campaign in which all large companies and settlements in Svalbard were inspected, with particular focus on regulations intended to phase out PCB-containing components in buildings. Waste management in general and how businesses handle hazardous waste were also examined.
102775.subtitle_en: The Polish station was the only operation with everything in order during the Governor of Svalbard’s environmental inspection campaign.

102778.excerpt_en: Everything has a beginning: two people meet, a sigh and an amen, and a tiny newborn sees the light of day. It is 38 years since little Stefano first saw the light.
102778.subtitle_en: Italians are not made for polar regions. Stefano Poli is not like most Italians—he is infected by a tiny little bug.

102795.excerpt_en: “Jason Roberts shall remove all traces of physical intervention connected with the illegal measures. This means removing the partially constructed, illegally erected extension to the Taubanelageret building and restoring the building’s façade to its condition before the work began.”
102795.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council gave Jason Roberts until 15 June to demolish the extension at Taubanelageret. The Governor of Svalbard requires it to be done by 15 March.

102802.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, someone brought a puppy to Longyearbyen without either a permit or a rabies vaccination. The puppy was placed in home quarantine and cannot leave its owner’s house until it has been vaccinated and received the necessary documentation confirming that everything is in order.
102802.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard intends to tighten enforcement of the rules governing the import and export of dogs to Svalbard because of the risk of rabies.

102804.excerpt_en: The seven companies have made the following requests for locations: • Svalbard Snøscooterutleie: Wimandalen • Poli Arctici: Diabas • Svalbard Reiser: Slettvika (conversion of private cabin) • Spitsbergen Travel: Brentskardet • Spitsbergen Tours and Spitsbergen Experience AS: Adolfbukta • Svalbard Wildlife Service AS: DeGeer/Skjørlokstupet. Consultation deadline in January. The Governor of Svalbard…
102804.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has published the names of the seven companies that have applied to establish commercial cabins in Svalbard.
102804.title_en: These Companies Applied for Commercial Cabins

102823.excerpt_en: Both of Lufttransport’s aircraft were grounded on Friday. “One aircraft has been on the mainland for major maintenance; the other therefore suffered considerable wear and tear, since it is the only one operating out of Longyearbyen.”
102823.subtitle_en: Lufttransport completed its first flight since Friday on Wednesday evening. The company has now repaired one of its two aircraft and finally made it to Svea.

102830.excerpt_en: UNIS and OSS (Observing Snow Avalanches at Svalbard) are launching the new online service. It will inform people in Svalbard about, among other things, the avalanche danger in and around Adventdalen.
102830.subtitle_en: A new online service providing information about wind and drifting snow has been launched. The service is intended to help people avoid avalanche-prone areas.

102849.excerpt_en: The people who live on the island do not rush about; they stroll around without hurrying. Of course we are ordinary people too, heaven help us—it is simply that the land itself has such a calming effect.
102849.subtitle_en: We are not like most Norwegians, we who cling to life here on the island. Never is it more evident than now, when people down south on the mainland are rushing around trying to stock up on enough supplies to get through the Christmas holidays.

102856.excerpt_en: “I can readily admit that things have happened quickly and that I have gone too far. But I’m only trying to make my surroundings look nice, which is why I take this very personally.”
102856.subtitle_en: When Australian Jason Roberts began carrying out illegal building work on his own house, all hell broke loose. Now he refuses to back down and beg for mercy.

102874.excerpt_en: Following a meeting at the Governor’s office on Wednesday, Store Norske has been granted permission to ship coal from Svea until 15 February next year.
102874.subtitle_en: Despite objections from the Norwegian Coastal Administration, the Governor of Svalbard is allowing Store Norske to ship coal in January and February.
102874.title_en: Allowed to Ship Svea Coal This Winter

102893.excerpt_en: “There have been three incidents involving loose dogs from his kennel between the 10th and the 17th.”
102893.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s Environmental Department is reporting Niklas Gerhardsson, who runs Svalbard Huskies.

102895.excerpt_en: The mail was consequently flown up with SAS Braathens on Wednesday and Thursday. “This meant we had to work into the evening, and the mail was somewhat delayed reaching customers,” says postmaster Arne Holmberg.
102895.subtitle_en: The West Air Sweden cargo plane was damaged at Tromsø Airport on Boxing Day and was therefore out of service for two days during the Christmas holidays.

102907.excerpt_en: Robert Hermansen was put forward as a leadership candidate as early as a year ago, and confirms to NRK Troms that he is still interested. But it is not only TIL’s chairman who is due to be replaced at the annual meeting held on the 28th.
102907.subtitle_en: Store Norske CEO Robert Hermansen is being considered as chairman of Tromsø Idrettslag.
102907.title_en: Robert in the Running to Chair TIL Board?

102927.excerpt_en: The newspaper is no longer blue at the top but red, while the polar bear with the iceberg in the background has disappeared. (Not because of global warming.) For 17 years, the blue masthead, with a few minor adjustments, gave Svalbardposten its distinctive look.
102927.subtitle_en: As you have already noticed, something has happened to Svalbardposten since the previous issue was published just before Christmas.

102938.excerpt_en: Nox Polaris has long wanted to build a cabin in Carolinedalen in connection with fossil collecting at its claim there. “There are no plans to station a permanent crew at the site; instead, the work will be carried out through regular deployments of work teams between June and October.”
102938.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has rejected Nox Polaris’s application to build a cabin in Carolinedalen.

102958.excerpt_en: The two people were returning to Longyearbyen on separate snowmobiles when one of the machines became stuck in Eskerdalen. “We were notified of what had happened at 1:15 p.m. and initially launched a rescue operation.”
102958.subtitle_en: Two people living in Longyearbyen were assisted by the Red Cross on Monday afternoon in getting home from Eskerdalen.

102960.excerpt_en: Both of Lufttransport’s aircraft have periodically been out of service, causing problems for coal production in Svea. Store Norske and the airline have now met to discuss how such situations can be avoided in the future.
102960.subtitle_en: Store Norske is in talks with Lufttransport about new aircraft. They could arrive as early as this autumn.
102960.title_en: Could Get New Aircraft in the Autumn

102969.excerpt_en: See the full programme here! “These are the two ministers who are most important to Svalbard, among other things in relation to the Local Council debate and the discussion on protection. They are two fascinating ministers,” says Inger Lise Næss, an information consultant at the Norwegian Polar Institute (NP).
102969.subtitle_en: Knut Storberget and Helen Bjørnøy will be the headline speakers at this year’s Svalbard Seminar, which begins on 23 January.
102969.title_en: Ministers to Attend the Svalbard Seminar

102980.excerpt_en: Most of the eleven people there fainted on the spot; others managed to get some distance away before collapsing. Frank Wiggo Karlsen, 34, from Borkenes, died.
102980.subtitle_en: On Monday, Nord-Troms District Court begins hearing the criminal case against Bjørn Fjukstad. He was operations engineer at Svea Nord during the fatal breakthrough, when oxygen-depleted air from a previously mined-out area suddenly rushed into the mine heading.

103003.excerpt_en: “I want clarification and to get out of a hopeless deadlock. Apart from that, I will not comment on the case.”
103003.subtitle_en: Proceedings in the criminal case against Bjørn Fjukstad begin at Nord-Troms District Court on Monday. Fjukstad is charged with gross negligence in connection with the fatal accident at Svea Nord in 2005.
103003.title_en: Case Against Bjørn Fjukstad Goes to Court
