103007.excerpt_en: There has been a major need for a new quay in Longyearbyen for several years. Because capacity is stretched and none of the quays meet the requirements of the largest cruise ships, many vessels remain offshore in Adventfjorden instead of coming alongside.
103007.subtitle_en: The solution to the quay problem has been postponed by at least a year. The Governor of Svalbard and the Local Council have squandered the opportunity to secure funding for a quay in next year’s national budget.
103007.title_en: Still a Shortage of Berth Space

103019.excerpt_en: When the trial of Bjørn Fjukstad began in Nord-Troms District Court today, he pleaded not guilty. Instead, he stressed that the area where 34-year-old Frank Wiggo Karlsen died in the summer of 2005 had neither been ventilated nor physically sealed off.
103019.subtitle_en: Operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad believes that changes to the ventilation system caused the fatal accident at the Svea Nord mine in the summer of 2005.

103021.excerpt_en: “Both the wind direction and the high temperatures before the weekend helped increase the likelihood of avalanches. Conditions are more stable now because it has become colder and we have a different type of weather,” says Roar Hilde, the duty officer with the Governor of Svalbard.
103021.subtitle_en: According to the Governor of Svalbard, there is no immediate danger of further avalanches in the areas near Longyearbyen. An avalanche occurred by Gruve 2 on Friday.

103025.excerpt_en: Had Store Norske taken the measurements made by Per Magne Pedersen on 29 June seriously and taken action, the accident at Svea Nord could not have happened.
103025.subtitle_en: Four days before the fatal accident at the Svea Nord mine in 2005, it was established that the main ventilation system was not working properly, without the alarm being triggered.
103025.title_en: Store Norske Failed to Take Measurements Seriously

103044.excerpt_en: The former mine manager, for his part, went so far as to claim that operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad was evading the truth about whether he had read an operating plan.
103044.subtitle_en: The defence lawyer for defendant Bjørn Fjukstad pressed Stig Brunes, mine manager during the fatal accident at Svea Nord in 2005, hard during questioning in Nord-Troms District Court on Wednesday.
103044.title_en: Who Is Telling the Truth in Nord-Troms District Court?

103053.excerpt_en: “I cannot see that Bjørn Fjukstad showed indifference or negligence before the accident in Svea Nord. He accepts that he acted negligently and unlawfully, but the punishment must be proportionate to this,” said defence lawyer Erling O.
103053.subtitle_en: The prosecutor sought 90 days’ unconditional imprisonment when the trial of Bjørn Fjukstad ended in Nord-Troms District Court on Thursday. The defence argued that a fine would be sufficient punishment.

103058.excerpt_en: For Lufttransport AS, this means gaining a strong owner’s backing just before it submits a tender for the nationwide air ambulance service.
103058.subtitle_en: Airlift Holding AS has entered into a conditional agreement with Norsk Helikopter AS to purchase 100 percent of the shares in Lufttransport.

103066.excerpt_en: The human side concerns truth, repression, concealment and poor memory. The technical side concerns the unfathomable paths of airflow through a vast mine complex, and people’s efforts to keep it under control.
103066.subtitle_en: The criminal case against operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad, heard in Nord-Troms District Court this week, has both a technical and a human side.

103101.excerpt_en: On Monday, the Environment and Industry Committee (MNU) once again decided to defer the problems in Sjøområdet. The administration had proposed giving residents of the area until the 15th.
103101.subtitle_en: The Local Council has postponed consideration of Sjøområdet for another year. Those living there illegally have been given until the end of the year to move.

103106.excerpt_en: The Jakobsen shipping company is currently sending the former governor’s vessel, a sealing and expedition ship, south for handover to its new owners in Germany. According to Fiskeribladet, the boat may later be seen in Arctic waters, but carrying out entirely new duties.
103106.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s former vessel, “Polarsyssel,” has been sold. There are now very few suitable sealing vessels left in the Norwegian fleet.

103117.excerpt_en: “We want to create a concept that is different from what already exists in town, but it is a little too early to say what it will be like,” says Albrigtsen.
103117.subtitle_en: A pub could open in the new building by Kroa. It will be called Svalbard Pub, with Roy Albrigsten as general manager.
103117.title_en: Wants New Pub in the Town Centre

103148.excerpt_en: Last November, senior engineer Torfinn Kjærnet of the Mining Inspectorate, with the Chief Mining Inspector for Svalbard, installed two samplers beside the burning and smouldering spoil heaps near Barentsburg. Substances from the yellow-brown smoke were collected over three weeks and have now been fully analysed at UNIS.
103148.subtitle_en: Analyses of smoke from the spoil-heap fires in Barentsburg show the presence of carcinogenic coal tar. Nothing indicates that the fires will be extinguished anytime soon.

103153.excerpt_en: “The reason we are applying to establish a camp is that the ice conditions in Tempelfjorden currently appear likely to be just as unstable as last year.”
103153.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has granted Svalbard Snøscooterutleie (SSU) permission to establish a winter camp for 30 people just south of Fredheim.

103164.excerpt_en: On Monday, the Local Council unanimously decided that Longyearbyen should have its own election day in October for local elections. The council thus rejected the recommendation from the Administration Committee, which had previously called for a joint election day with the mainland, with one dissenting vote from the Cross-Party Joint List (TF).
103164.subtitle_en: The Local Council has unanimously decided that it does not want the same election day as the municipal elections on the mainland.

103172.excerpt_en: If you see a lone woman walking up or down Adventdalen, she is Hilde Fålun Strøm. She simply cannot help herself.
103172.subtitle_en: She is an avid riflewoman, loves nature and brought down the man in her life shortly after arriving in Svalbard twelve years ago.

103188.excerpt_en: See more photos here! This year marks the tenth consecutive year of Polarjazz, which opened with a warm-up at Polarhotellet on Wednesday evening.
103188.subtitle_en: Polarjazz opened on Wednesday evening with a warm-up featuring local performers. The tenth-anniversary festival has held up well and kept the energy going this evening too.
103188.title_en: The music festival is under way

103197.excerpt_en: “It is ten years since some exceptionally bright idiots, longing for sun and warmth, brought Polarjazz into the world. Polarjazz is an institution despite itself, not because of itself.”
103197.subtitle_en: After a somewhat hesitant start, Mari Boine eventually got going and ultimately captivated the audience with her concert.

103237.excerpt_en: Bjørn Fjukstad was the responsible operations engineer at Svea Nord on 3 July 2005 when one man died and ten others fainted after oxygen-deficient air flowed into the mine tunnel.
103237.subtitle_en: Operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad was sentenced on Friday to 90 days’ suspended imprisonment and a NOK 30,000 fine in Nord-Troms District Court for violating the Working Environment Act. The state prosecutor is considering appealing the verdict.
103237.title_en: 90 days’ suspended imprisonment for Bjørn Fjukstad

103257.excerpt_en: “Closing the fjord to trawling, including trawling for shellfish, seaweed and kelp, will help stimulate research activity in Kongsfjorden,” says Justice Minister Knut Storberget. Storberget, who arrived in Longyearbyen on Friday, continued on to Ny-Ålesund on Sunday.
103257.subtitle_en: On Friday, the government adopted regulations banning trawling in Kongsfjorden, following a proposal from the Ministry of Justice.

103261.excerpt_en: The last time he did so was in January the previous year at Huset, in connection with the government’s irrational tax increase. People were furious.
103261.subtitle_en: There was no public meeting after all when Justice Minister Knut Storberget once again placed himself squarely in the line of fire before the public on Monday.

103266.excerpt_en: “We get little understanding from customers who cannot have a glass of wine with their meal during the day. They would rather walk 200 metres farther up the road.”
103266.subtitle_en: Café Busen may have to close during the day because guests cannot be served alcohol then and consequently stay away.

103284.excerpt_en: The mail plane that was ready to depart from Tromsø has now been cancelled. The aircraft is returning to Oslo, so Svalbardposten and other mail are unlikely to reach Longyearbyen before Monday.
103284.subtitle_en: An icy runway and strong crosswinds with blowing snow in Tromsø are causing trouble for the mail plane. Friday’s departure has been cancelled.

103290.excerpt_en: Weather conditions in Tromsø caused major disruptions to air traffic on Friday. The flight to Svalbard could not land in Tromsø and was diverted to Evenes.
103290.subtitle_en: SAS Braathens is expected to land at Svalbard Airport at 4:30 p.m. on Friday. The aircraft, which took off from Evenes, has no passengers from Tromsø. Svalbardposten is also absent for that reason.

103299.excerpt_en: At the public meeting held in UNIS’s Møysalen on Monday evening, Justice Minister Knut Storberget placed great emphasis on wanting close dialogue with the local council. “I think having more consultations is an exciting and constructive idea.”
103299.subtitle_en: Justice Minister Knut Storberget (Labour) is open to closer contact with the local council when decisions about Svalbard are being made.

103310.excerpt_en: “Having to commute to Tromsø is a major burden. I am considering stopping therapy because I do not want it to affect my work,” says Kristine Grimseth.
103310.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen has no dedicated service for adults who need psychological help. Users themselves are calling for one.

103312.excerpt_en: When the case was heard in Nord-Troms District Court in mid-January, prosecutor Torstein Hevnskjel sought 90 days’ unconditional imprisonment. In the judgment handed down last Friday, Bjørn Fjukstad was sentenced to 90 days’ suspended imprisonment and a NOK 30,000 fine.
103312.subtitle_en: The state prosecutor is appealing the sentence against operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad following the fatal accident at Svea Nord in 2005.

103322.excerpt_en: According to mine director Boris I. Nagajuk in Barentsburg, Alexander P.
103322.subtitle_en: The Russian mining company Trust Arktikugol, which operates coal mines in Barentsburg, appointed a new director-general on Wednesday after Jurij V. Tsivka (pictured) was forced to step down.

103355.excerpt_en: Coal mining was faltering, tourism was as unpredictable as the famous sea currents of Berlevåg, and research was conducted by a group of ascetics living on crispbread and porridge. Nothing made any money.
103355.subtitle_en: Once upon a time, people feared that Longyearbyen would shrink to a hard core of just a few hundred inhabitants.
103355.title_en: How many do we want to be?

103361.excerpt_en: She drives a car along the runway in Ny-Ålesund, braking hard at regular intervals and carefully entering figures in columns. Linda Bakken is in charge of the 808-metre runway and the small blue-painted tower beside it.
103361.subtitle_en: Linda Bakken has a tower of her own. From there, she can survey her kingdom. She sees Nora, Dana, Svea, Pretender, Diademet and many, many others. The goal is to climb them all.

103367.excerpt_en: To solve the problem of several boathouses in the Sea Area being used illegally as homes, the local council wants to create regulations that can bring some of this use within the law.
103367.subtitle_en: The local council proposes allowing holiday homes in the Sea Area. The proposal will be considered on Monday.
103367.title_en: Opening up the Sea Area for housing

103378.excerpt_en: The equipment was originally meant to arrive last autumn, but the equipment Trust Arktikugol had been waiting for so long has finally arrived in Barentsburg.
103378.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, a freighter from Murmansk arrived in Barentsburg with heavy equipment to bring the burning spoil heaps under control.
103378.title_en: Boat carrying firefighting equipment arrives in Barentsburg

103380.excerpt_en: “We find almost every day that we do not have enough space for visiting lecturers and researchers who want to come here. We have 20 old SSD apartments that we rent from Bydrift, but they are very run-down and in poor condition,” says Helen Flå, deputy director at UNIS.
103380.subtitle_en: UNIS has such a severe shortage of accommodation for visiting researchers that it wants to build its own hotel with 81 rooms.
103380.title_en: UNIS wants to build a researcher hotel here

103383.excerpt_en: “This is one of the biggest things we have ever done at one time, and it will help secure our operations on Svalbard going forward.”
103383.subtitle_en: KSAT has invested more than NOK 50 million and is building twelve new antennas on Platåberget.

103390.excerpt_en: “We are interested in more permanent trappers, and would like to see some people think more long-term. Our main goal is to keep the trapping culture alive,” says Rune Bergstrøm, head of environmental protection at the Governor’s Office.
103390.subtitle_en: The Governor is not entirely satisfied that people spend only one season at Mushamna and Austfjordnes, and would like to see trappers who stay for several years.

103400.excerpt_en: The general view among businesses in Longyearbyen is that the new mail plane has brought greater stability and shorter freight times. They rarely find that goods are left behind in Tromsø.
103400.subtitle_en: Businesses in Longyearbyen have had good experiences with the new mail plane. Many are nevertheless cautious about the high season.

103405.excerpt_en: “We have not made any price changes because of the mail flight. So the more fresh goods we sell, the more money we lose.”
103405.subtitle_en: Strong customer reactions meant Svalbardbutikken did not raise prices on fresh goods this autumn. Now the store is losing money on the mail flight.
103405.title_en: Losing money on the mail flight

103420.excerpt_en: That was how the new-circus performance presented by Sirkus Svalnardo at Huset on Monday began. A week earlier, 52 children and young people from Longyearbyen had spent several hours each day practicing various circus exercises, and the result was a fantastic performance combining circus, theater and dance.
103420.subtitle_en: A princess is rejected by her father because she is too happy. To win back his heart, she must travel to the heart of the Earth and find a flower.
103420.title_en: To the heart of the Earth

103431.excerpt_en: These days, Statistics Norway (SSB) is sending a questionnaire to 300 households in Longyearbyen.
103431.subtitle_en: Three hundred households in Longyearbyen have been selected to answer what they spend their money on. The responses will be used to map the town’s consumption.

103432.excerpt_en: One change is that the Local Council’s website has been redesigned and made more user-friendly. “We want to communicate information by publishing case documents, minutes and decisions.”
103432.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council has taken the criticism seriously and is trying to be more accessible and less bureaucratic.

103439.excerpt_en: “We were contacted at around 2:30 p.m. by people who had seen fresh bear tracks in Bjørndalen. Shortly afterward, we saw the bear outside Vestpynten, and it was heading steadily toward Revneset,” says Arild Lyssand, the Governor’s duty officer.
103439.subtitle_en: A polar bear was spotted at Vestpynten on Wednesday afternoon before swimming toward Revneset.

103445.excerpt_en: The committee unanimously voted on Monday to put the detailed plan for Sjøområdet out for public review.
103445.subtitle_en: The Environment and Business Committee believes the boathouses in Sjøområdet could be used as holiday homes. The detailed plan is now being made available for public review.
103445.title_en: This is what Sjøområdet could look like

103452.excerpt_en: Just before 11 p.m. on Tuesday, the power went out throughout Longyearbyen. The cause was a leak that caused one of the Energy Works’ many hundreds of pipes to burst, bringing the entire coal facility to a standstill.
103452.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen was plunged into complete darkness when one of the power station’s many pipes burst on Tuesday evening.
103452.title_en: Burst pipe plunged city into darkness

103481.excerpt_en: Niklas Gerhardsson, the owner of Svalbard Huskies, has previously been reported by the Governor of Svalbard for poor dog keeping. Dogs have repeatedly escaped from the kennel.
103481.subtitle_en: On Saturday, the Governor of Svalbard was once again notified of a loose dog near the Svalbard Huskies kennel at the mouth of Todalen.

103484.excerpt_en: “The fire in the rock dump triggered the whole thing. After discussions with the Mining Commissioner and the Governor of Svalbard, we realized that this was a major problem and that little was known about such dumps,” says UNIS researcher Roland Kallenborn.
103484.subtitle_en: UNIS is launching a research project on the burning rock dumps in Barentsburg in cooperation with a Danish company.
103484.title_en: Fire in rock dump becomes science

103518.excerpt_en: “This is the fourth Polar Year in a sequence spanning 125 years, so it is hardly an everyday occasion,” said Local Council leader Kjell Mork after the first official opening had taken place.
103518.subtitle_en: The International Polar Year, IPY, was inaugurated with speeches and the unveiling of a sculpture outside Forskningsparken on Thursday.
103518.title_en: The starting gun has fired for IPY

103526.excerpt_en: “We have mapped the preferences of the 10th grade and upper-secondary students, and will now create a range of subjects that meets them as far as possible,” says Ina Misje, head of the upper-secondary department at Longyearbyen School.
103526.subtitle_en: The overview of the students’ subject preferences is ready. New this year is that Longyearbyen School can offer sports studies from the autumn.

103531.excerpt_en: “This could mean opening later and staying open into the evening. If we are to survive, we have to make some changes; we cannot continue with the concept we have now,” says general manager Silje Marie Våtvik.
103531.subtitle_en: Café Busen is changing its operations after the Local Council refused to extend its serving hours.

103536.excerpt_en: A pint of beer or five, wine, cognac, even gammel dansk—in short, anything that flows and contains alcohol—goes down without resistance. We feel the warmth, of course, and let ourselves be cheered by the social conviviality. Alcohol loosens us up, or rather, dissolves us.
103536.subtitle_en: There is something about us and alcohol that flows together into a higher unity down the valley. It may be the latitude, the cold, the darkness—and the nagging loneliness.

103545.excerpt_en: Catherine Braathen had originally planned to travel to Trondheim on Thursday afternoon to give birth there, but when labor began at around 8 a.m., she went to the hospital in Longyearbyen. “Two hours later, Lydia was born.”
103545.subtitle_en: Little Lydia was born at Longyearbyen Hospital on Thursday morning.

103551.excerpt_en: “This is the earliest opening I can remember,” says Basecamp general manager Brita Knutsen Dahl. The first guests arrived at the icebound vessel “Noorderlicht” in Tempelfjorden last Thursday, and Knutsen Dahl is very pleased.
103551.subtitle_en: Tourists are flocking to the “Noorderlicht” in Tempelfjorden, and several other fjords are now reportedly passable.
103551.title_en: Full speed on the fjord ice

103582.excerpt_en: A total of 137 snowmobile drivers were checked during the Governor’s alcohol inspection on Saturday morning. Four of them were over the legal limit and were therefore prevented from driving on.
103582.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard barred four people from driving snowmobiles on Saturday morning because they were over the alcohol limit.

103605.excerpt_en: The woman was skiing on Larsbreen when she cut her lower leg on the steel edge of one of her skis. The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the accident at 7:45 p.m. and dispatched a Red Cross patrol.
103605.subtitle_en: A woman was brought down from Larsbreen by a Red Cross patrol on Wednesday evening after badly cutting her lower leg.
103605.title_en: Red Cross rescues woman from Larsbreen

103608.excerpt_en: Although the site is zoned for commercial use in the land-use plan, the committee voted to reject the developer Barlindhaug’s detailed plan. “We must take the densification issue into account in the new land-use plan.”
103608.subtitle_en: The Environment and Business Committee does not want the site between Polarhotellet and Road 500 developed, where UNIS wants to build a research hotel.

103613.excerpt_en: In the accident, she suffered a blow to the head that made it difficult for her to function normally. She could not speak to two people in the same room without hearing ringing in her head.
103613.subtitle_en: We all owe Kristine Grimseth a great debt of gratitude for speaking so openly in Svalbardposten last month about her mental health problems following a car accident in autumn 2005.

103625.excerpt_en: Following a direct appeal from Pernille Weis-Fogh of the Cross-Party Common List, Søren Nissen, chief physician at Longyearbyen Hospital, has promised to investigate the possibility of establishing a dedicated psychological service for adults in Longyearbyen.
103625.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Hospital will investigate the possibility of psychologists from Tromsø holding consultations in Longyearbyen

103627.excerpt_en: “I had spoken to Kato Lorentsen at Karls-Berger Pub, who said I could get electricity from him, but it turned out he had no outlet I could use,” says Ariaiwand.
103627.subtitle_en: Kazem Ariaiwand was supposed to open his snack bar last Friday. The opening has been postponed because he has not clarified where he will get electricity from.

103646.excerpt_en: “We treated it as a trip when we went to Von Post—four people and a chainsaw,” says Kyrre Fledsberg, who was tasked with bringing in the ice for the concert. It was important that the ice used for the instruments had as few air bubbles as possible.
103646.subtitle_en: On Wednesday evening, Terje Isungset made music from Von Postbreen and ice formations from Adventdalen.

103676.excerpt_en: Store Norske operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad was sentenced in early February to 90 days’ suspended imprisonment and a NOK 30,000 fine. Fjukstad was the responsible operations engineer at Svea Nord 3.
103676.subtitle_en: The Court of Appeal will hear the appeal case against Bjørn Fjukstad, but has refused to hear the appeal concerning the question of guilt.
103676.title_en: Fjukstad Case Proceeds to Court of Appeal

103691.excerpt_en: The World Wildlife Fund (WWF) is now also among the many seeking to visit polar bears in Svalbard’s protected areas.
103691.subtitle_en: The World Wildlife Fund wants to visit Svalbard with German and French journalists to document polar bear research.
103691.title_en: World Wildlife Fund on Polar Bear Hunt

103698.excerpt_en: “By the time we arrived, things had already calmed down. We drove one of the parties home, while the taxi drove the other,” says Roar Hilde, the Governor’s duty officer.
103698.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard was called early Sunday morning by a taxi driver reporting a fight in his taxi.

103707.excerpt_en: The Czechs had been stranded in tents on the northern side of Inglefieldbukta, on the eastern side of Spitsbergen, for three days. After one of their two tents began to rip apart at the seams in the strong winds, they alerted the Governor of Svalbard at around 2 p.m. Sunday.
103707.subtitle_en: Four Czech skiers were picked up by helicopter in Inglefieldbukta on Sunday after one of their tents was destroyed by strong winds.

103714.excerpt_en: “We received a report of the avalanche at 5:15 p.m. from someone at the ice cave on Longyearbreen. The person feared that someone had been caught in the avalanche because of fresh ski tracks,” says chief inspector Roar Hilde of the Governor’s office.
103714.subtitle_en: Two UNIS students skiing triggered an avalanche on Sunday afternoon on the mountainside west of Longyearbreen. No one was caught in the avalanche.

103718.excerpt_en: “He had to spend the rest of the night in the cells and was fined NOK 4,000 for disorderly conduct,” says Petter Bråten, the Governor’s duty officer.
103718.subtitle_en: A visiting man in his 50s urinated in the stairwell and corridor of one of the accommodation establishments in Nybyen on Monday evening.

103733.excerpt_en: “We were afraid that no one from Svalbard had made it through to the national event this year, since we did not get a result right away. We did last year,” says Pia Boholm.
103733.subtitle_en: The four girls will represent Svalbard at the national gathering of the Youth Cultural Festival this summer. For Pia Boholm, it is the second time in a row.

103744.excerpt_en: Norsk Helikopter AS has owned the Norwegian company Lufttransport AS and the Swedish company Lufttransport AB since June 2005. 17.
103744.subtitle_en: In January, Airlift Holding AS announced that it would acquire Lufttransport AS. The deal will now not go ahead because the two parties disagree over the company’s value.

103752.excerpt_en: After four days of work preparing the cableway support for erection, the work was postponed again on Thursday. The reason was that the rig intended to drill the pile anchors into the ground broke down.
103752.subtitle_en: The erection of the cableway support at Skjæringa has once again been postponed after faults developed in the rig that was to drill the anchors into the ground.

103754.excerpt_en: It was an adventure reserved for a select few, along with a handful of stubborn souls who would not take no for an answer. Interest in the region among the general public was lukewarm.
103754.subtitle_en: Of course, everything was not much better before; it was simply different. Travelling to Svalbard, for example, was a major leap and a journey into the unknown.

103808.excerpt_en: “Could you please resume flights to Svalbard? The situation has changed somewhat since you last flew here.”
103808.subtitle_en: An email campaign was launched last week to bring Norwegian back to Longyearbyen. The airline currently has no plans to return.

103822.excerpt_en: In 2004, vessels had to be secured against attacks when moored, including in Longyearbyen. A new regulation is now out for consultation.
103822.subtitle_en: The EU wants ports to be better protected against “terrorism”. Longyearbyen Local Council believes the quays in Longyearbyen are sufficiently secure.

103845.excerpt_en: The fire was caused by welding drainage pipes in the mine’s main tunnel on 30 July 2005.
103845.subtitle_en: The case against Store Norske following the fire at the Svea Nord mine in 2005 has been dropped by the Governor of Svalbard.

103846.excerpt_en: The man, who is 38 and German, is stranded by bad weather on Nordenskiöldbreen, at an altitude of nearly 1,000 metres close to Ferrierfjellet. The weather is extreme, with very strong winds and heavy, wet snow.
103846.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s Super Puma helicopter landed in Longyearbyen just before 1 p.m. Saturday after an unsuccessful attempt to come to a ski tourist’s aid.

103867.excerpt_en: “The weather still makes it impossible to retrieve the man. I spoke to him on a satellite phone at 6 p.m., and he is not in any danger.”
103867.subtitle_en: The German ski tourist who was picked up by helicopter on Saturday remains stranded by bad weather on Nordenskiöldbreen.
103867.title_en: Still Stranded, but Not in Distress

103878.excerpt_en: “We had no contact with the man on Sunday, but he notified others in Longyearbyen that he had turned back and was heading to Brucebyen,” says duty chief inspector Petter Braaten of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
103878.subtitle_en: The German ski tourist who had been stranded by bad weather at the top of Nordenskiöldbreen walked to Brucebyen on Sunday.

103887.excerpt_en: The snowmobile party, consisting of the guide and two guests, was on a week-long trip and had reached Mohnbukta when the guide’s snowmobile broke through the ice at around 1 p.m. Tuesday. The guide got off without getting wet, but both the rifle and the GPS disappeared with the snowmobile.
103887.subtitle_en: A snowmobile belonging to a guide from Svalbard Snowmobile Rental broke through the ice in Mohnbukta on Tuesday afternoon.
103887.title_en: Guide’s Snowmobile Breaks Through the Ice

103889.excerpt_en: Jon Sandmo, who runs the tour company Svalbard4you, was heading for Kapp Linné with a tour group when the accident happened at around 5:30 p.m. Monday. The group was on the eastern side of Grønfjorden when Sandmo had trouble getting up a steep incline.
103889.subtitle_en: Jon Sandmo nearly plunged 20 metres with his snowmobile, but managed to get off at the last moment.

103905.excerpt_en: The same routine every year: We stroll between the houses with the darkness close and snug around us. We meet, look around, exchange a few words, and often talk about the weather.
103905.subtitle_en: The land lies there, tempting us: the jagged, gleaming-white mountains, the soft snow-covered glaciers. The sparkling light. Oh yes, that eternal pull.

103933.excerpt_en: “It is difficult to find hotel rooms for the guests we have who want ordinary hotel standards.”
103933.subtitle_en: SWS is planning a new hotel on Elvesletta with 80 beds. The hotel is due to be completed by 2009.

103938.excerpt_en: “It will be extremely problematic for the state to run a business and compete with private companies. A research hotel will take away our livelihood using taxpayers’ money, so this is going to cause trouble,” says Ronny Gjøse, who is both head of the Svalbard Tourism Council and director of the Polarhotellet and Funken hotels.
103938.subtitle_en: Ronny Gjøse, head of the Svalbard Tourism Council, warns of a fight after the Local Council approved further work on a research hotel.

103966.excerpt_en: Eyewitnesses said they heard a loud bang and saw the rockslide occur just before nine o’clock on Tuesday morning. The Governor was notified and sent several people up to investigate the slide.
103966.subtitle_en: A large rockslide occurred on the mountainside above Sverdrupbyen on Tuesday morning.

103978.excerpt_en: The Governor was notified at around 10:15 Wednesday morning that a woman needed assistance. “It was a woman with a painful back, but it was nothing dramatic,” says Jarle Odland, the Governor’s officer on duty.
103978.subtitle_en: The Red Cross patrol sent to retrieve a woman with a back injury from Tempelfjorden in the specially built Red Cross vehicle returned to Longyearbyen at 2:40 p.m.

103981.excerpt_en: The Governor’s Office received the alert at around 4 a.m. on Wednesday that the man had suffered a complex ankle injury. He was aboard a Russian vessel just north of Bjørnøya and was evacuated by helicopter.
103981.subtitle_en: A Russian sailor had to be evacuated by helicopter from a vessel north of Bjørnøya during the night leading into Wednesday because of an ankle injury.

103982.excerpt_en: Since last weekend, the Governor’s Office has dispatched helicopters five times to retrieve people injured in the terrain. A week ago Sunday, a ski tourist with a frostbitten finger was picked up in Fardalen, and a person whose finger had been crushed was picked up in Svea.
103982.subtitle_en: A wonderfully quiet Easter with a few uneventful incidents—that is the Governor’s summary of the holiday.

103994.excerpt_en: Photographer Mireille de la Lez had been on Kongsøya, the largest of the islands in Kong Karls Land, with Swedish national Fredrik Granath on a photo assignment for National Geographic Magazine. According to senior police officer Olav Tombre of the Governor’s Office, the two were skiing in the terrain when the woman fell and injured her neck.
103994.subtitle_en: An American female photographer was evacuated by helicopter on Wednesday after a fall on Kong Karls Land.
103994.title_en: American Photographer Evacuated by Helicopter from Kong Karls Land

103998.excerpt_en: Granath and photographer Mireille de la Lez are therefore abandoning the assignment they had been carrying out for National Geographic Magazine before it was completed. “There will be no continuation of the work here this winter.”
103998.subtitle_en: Swedish producer Fredrik Granath is to be picked up by helicopter from Kongsøya in Kong Karls Land on Saturday. On Wednesday evening, the photographer working with him was evacuated after falling and injuring herself.

104004.excerpt_en: So far this year, Isfjord Radio at Kapp Linné has recorded 420 overnight stays. With April fully booked, the figure will reach around 1,050 before the season ends.
104004.subtitle_en: Kapp Linné has nearly twice as many overnight stays this year as last year. But day visits are down because there is no ice on Grønfjorden.

104040.excerpt_en: Two parties had applied to trap at the Governor’s two stations next season. Both had Mushamna as their first choice.
104040.subtitle_en: The trapping party offered a place at Austfjordnes has declined. As a result, the station will stand empty next season.

104045.excerpt_en: Finn Sletten was two years old when he arrived at Kings Bay with his parents and sister in 1954. The people living in the small mining community in Kongsfjorden usually called the place “the camp” or “kingsbay”, rarely Ny-Ålesund.
104045.subtitle_en: Kings Bay was his childhood kingdom. Happiness was followed by 20 years of silence and repression. Now he comes rushing back whenever the opportunity arises.

104047.excerpt_en: “There has always been good cooperation between the school and the business community,” said Store Norske CEO Robert Hermansen before presenting the gift to Anne Ellingsen, general manager of the Childhood and Education Enterprise.
104047.subtitle_en: The Local Council is receiving 300,000 kroner from Store Norske to write the history of Longyearbyen School. The gift was presented during the formal handover of the school from the state to the Local Council.

104063.excerpt_en: The cameras will take pictures around the clock throughout the summer and record everything and everyone coming ashore. The sites selected by the researchers are Storøya just east of Nordaustlandet, Isflakbukta on Phippsøya, Kapp Lee and Andréetangen on Edgeøya, and Havmerra, one of the Tusenøyane islands south of Edgeøya.
104063.subtitle_en: Freedom of movement is becoming increasingly restricted. Now researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute want to place surveillance cameras at five selected walrus haul-out sites around Svalbard.

104069.excerpt_en: One-year-and-two-month-old Erlend Selnes is fifth on the waiting list for a kindergarten place in Longyearbyen. “As things stand, we risk still being in the queue after the main admissions process.”
104069.subtitle_en: Five children are on the waiting list for kindergarten places in Longyearbyen. When the deadline to apply for a place in the autumn expired last week, twelve applications had been received.

104086.excerpt_en: Researcher Christian Lydersen is behind the project. For many years, he has recorded Svalbard’s walrus colonies using helicopters and ships.
104086.subtitle_en: Researchers at the Norwegian Polar Institute want to install surveillance cameras at several locations in Svalbard to study walruses and the impact of tourist visits.

104094.excerpt_en: “We want to take a few minimal, small samples—tiny grains of hair and bone tissue—to carry out analyses and find out whether the lead content in the hair is abnormally high,” says senior consultant Ulf Aasebø at the University Hospital of North Norway in Tromsø (UNN).
104094.subtitle_en: Researchers want to open the mass grave at Kapp Thordsen to determine the cause of death of the 17 trappers who died there during an involuntary overwintering in 1872–73.
104094.title_en: Researchers Want to Open Mass Grave

104102.excerpt_en: “Around midnight, we were told that a worker in Svea had severed a finger, and we sent a helicopter there.”
104102.subtitle_en: Around midnight on Friday night, a person was flown by helicopter from Svea after severing the tip of his thumb.

104106.excerpt_en: “I was hit by a snowmobile at the intersection of Road 200 and Road 232, just below Blåmyra. The snowmobile was crossing Road 232 and did not see my car, but drove straight into my left side.”
104106.subtitle_en: Torgeir Prytz, who lives in Longyearbyen, was hit by a snowmobile on Monday morning while driving his car.

104113.excerpt_en: Only a few minutes had passed after the mobile crane from LNS Spitsbergen had lifted the cableway trestle clear of the ground when a sharp snapping sound rang out. The crane operator immediately stopped hoisting, while Karl Fredheim, a work supervisor with the Governor of Svalbard, and Eero Lindberg, both of whom have worked on the trestle since last summer, inspected the damage.
104113.subtitle_en: While cableway trestle 23 was being erected at Skjæringa this morning, one of its main beams broke. The erection has now been postponed again.

104130.excerpt_en: The boy was reported to the police, and the case has since been under investigation by the Governor’s Office. The assaults have naturally been a great burden for everyone directly affected, and have also affected the town’s youth environment and prompted strong reactions.
104130.subtitle_en: Openness comes at a cost, but silence costs more. Last autumn, a young boy sexually assaulted two girls in Longyearbyen.

104135.excerpt_en: “This is really good news!” says Anne Ellingsen, head of the Child and Youth Welfare Enterprise.
104135.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, the good news became official. Longyearbyen will have 100 percent kindergarten coverage this autumn.
104135.title_en: Everyone Gets a Place in Kindergarten

104139.excerpt_en: “We have reviewed comparable mine fires in South Africa and the United States of the same size and extent of damage, and feel confident that we will come through this well,” says Robert Hermansen. Store Norske is claiming NOK 800 million in insurance compensation after the fire that started in Svea Nord on 30.
104139.subtitle_en: A dispute over the insurance settlement following the Svea Nord fire will be heard by the Nord-Troms District Court in September.
104139.title_en: Svea Nord Fire in District Court

104143.excerpt_en: The assaults are alleged to have taken place last November and are of a particularly serious nature. “This is a serious case.”
104143.subtitle_en: A 15-year-old boy from Longyearbyen has been charged with sexually assaulting two girls aged 12 and 15.

104151.excerpt_en: Store Norske operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad was sentenced in early February by the Nord-Troms District Court to 90 days’ suspended imprisonment and a NOK 30,000 fine. Both parties appealed the sentence, while the Court of Appeal refused to hear the question of guilt.
104151.subtitle_en: The appeal against the sentence in the case involving operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad will be heard by the Hålogaland Court of Appeal in Tromsø at the end of May.
104151.title_en: Fjukstad Case Before the Court of Appeal in May

104164.excerpt_en: The final report from the government working group that has worked on the Svalbard tax will not be presented until tomorrow, Wednesday. There was therefore cheering and applause among the 200 people who had gathered at Huset on Tuesday evening when the justice minister revealed the report’s main conclusion.
104164.subtitle_en: Justice Minister Knut Storberget was cheered when, in his 1 May speech in Longyearbyen, he said the government plans to reduce Svalbard’s tax level to its 2005 level.
104164.title_en: Government to Reverse Svalbard Tax Increase

104176.excerpt_en: See all the results here! 265 skiers lined up at the start, spread across three categories: timed full marathon, untimed recreational class and half marathon. “It’s fantastic to see so many people.”
104176.subtitle_en: This year’s ski marathon took place last Saturday. Brilliant sunshine and good conditions made it a wonderful day for the many people who turned up.

104184.excerpt_en: That time, there was nothing he could do but listen to what the residents had brought forward. He was visibly tense and nervous after his government had raised Svalbard’s tax rate from 8 to 12 percent a few months earlier.
104184.subtitle_en: Once again, Knut Storberget managed to turn a meeting at Huset into a memorable evening. The last time was at the public meeting in January last year.

104189.excerpt_en: Last autumn, the Judicial Appointments Board ranked Rune B. Hansen first for a judgeship in Vestfold.
104189.subtitle_en: Rune B. Hansen, a former deputy governor, will receive NOK 700,000 in compensation from the Ministry of Justice because of gender discrimination.

104201.excerpt_en: Last Friday, Heidi Urdshals was taking a newly purchased snowmobile from Ingeniør G. Paulsen on a short test ride.
104201.subtitle_en: A snowmobile collision involving a Governor’s Office officer and Heidi Urdshals of Longyearbyen will be investigated by another police district.

104207.excerpt_en: According to information obtained by NRK Troms and Finnmark, the government will announce in the revised national budget on 15 May that Store Norske is receiving NOK 250 million.
104207.subtitle_en: All indications are that Store Norske will receive NOK 250 million from the government when the revised national budget is presented on 15 May.

104228.excerpt_en: “Now that was fun,” says Governor’s Office foreman Karl Fredheim when the trestle is in place. Since last summer, he has worked to get it up after the old trestle was blown down in April 2004.
104228.subtitle_en: On the third attempt, they finally succeeded in erecting cableway trestle no. 23. At 4:09 p.m. on Thursday, it stood upright at Skjæringa.
104228.title_en: The Cableway Trestle Is Erected at Skjæringa

104231.excerpt_en: “It is a magnificent sculpture, and we wanted it returned to our warehouse here in Eastern Norway so it could be put up again someday. But when it arrived in Bodø, it became clear that it would have to be cut up further to transport it onward.”
104231.subtitle_en: The controversial sculpture removed from Unis in 2004 was on its way to the Public Art Foundation’s warehouse in Oslo. It ended up at the dump in Bodø.
104231.title_en: Expensive Sculpture Ends Up on the Scrap Heap

104252.excerpt_en: Through his lawyer, Gerhardsson complained to the PFU about Svalbardposten after several articles about dogs that had escaped. Since 2004, the Governor of Svalbard has logged 14 escapes from Svalbard Huskies, which is based at the mouth of Todalen.
104252.subtitle_en: Niklas Gerhardsson, owner of Svalbard Huskies, failed to win his complaint against Svalbardposten before the Norwegian Press Complaints Commission (PFU).

104266.excerpt_en: Unis sells clothing from head to toe to employees, students and guest lecturers. Last December, it announced an agreement with Swedish clothing manufacturer Klättermusen for branded clothing worth more than NOK 2 million.
104266.subtitle_en: Unis is selling outdoor clothing at rock-bottom prices to students, employees and their families. Businesses are reacting because they are losing money on the extensive sales.

104278.excerpt_en: “We know the day marks the end of the Second World War, but we are so young that we have never experienced war. So this is just an ordinary day for us,” says Sara.
104278.subtitle_en: The girls are orange russ this year and soon ready to take the big leap into the world. On Tuesday, they marked Liberation Day by reading poems.

104282.excerpt_en: There were 152 passengers on the day flight, all from Tromsø. Everyone who was originally due to travel on the night flight got a seat.
104282.subtitle_en: Fog over Longyearbyen forced both night flights to return to Tromsø on Monday. After two landing attempts, the day flight also had to give up.
104282.title_en: The Plane Had to Turn Back

104289.excerpt_en: An extra flight to Tromsø will depart at 3:10 a.m. tonight, but not all passengers will get a seat. “SAS Braathens does not have several extra flights.”
104289.subtitle_en: Three flights had to return to Tromsø yesterday, leaving 195 people stranded by the weather in Longyearbyen. Some of them are unlikely to get away before 17 May.

104299.excerpt_en: “I want this to be a robust, forward-looking and environmentally friendly backup power solution. This is a proposal I am very pleased to have secured,” says Justice Minister Knut Storberget.
104299.subtitle_en: The government is providing NOK 20 million for a new backup power plant in Longyearbyen in the revised national budget presented today.
104299.title_en: NOK 20 Million for Backup Power Plant

104311.excerpt_en: “What we understand is that commuting is supposed to take place by air. Now they are facilitating snowmobile travel with marker poles and mobile coverage,” says Ronny Gjøse, head of the Svalbard Tourism Council.
104311.subtitle_en: The Svalbard Tourism Council believes snowmobile traffic in Bolterdalen is too heavy and that the route should not be used by workers traveling to and from Svea.

104321.excerpt_en: See the pictures from the Constitution Day celebrations here. 17.
104321.subtitle_en: Large numbers of people in a festive mood attended all of yesterday’s events.

104326.excerpt_en: And even if we had not taken notice of such things, we may perhaps have spotted the first goose of the year. Most of us are probably content to let nature take its slow course.
104326.subtitle_en: The thaw is under way. The ice is starting to break up; the little that remains is slowly releasing its grip on the land. The snow is doing likewise.

104339.excerpt_en: “This year’s recipient of the Typhus statuette came to Svalbard in 1991.”
104339.subtitle_en: The Typhus statuette has been awarded every year since 1974. This year it went to Heidi Brun for her many years of work in the local community.

104361.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified at around 12:30 p.m. on Sunday that the man had fallen through the ice with his snowmobile in Tempelfjorden. “He had gone through the ice at Kapp Schoultz, and the snowmobile had disappeared.”
104361.subtitle_en: A man in his 60s from Longyearbyen had to be airlifted from Tempelfjorden on Sunday after his snowmobile fell through the ice.

104379.excerpt_en: “Not a single insurance company will insure a production on Spitsbergen,” director Chris Weitz of the epic “The Golden Compass” told filmweb.no. “The Golden Compass” is the first installment in the film adaptation of Philip Pullman’s fantasy trilogy “His Dark Materials”.
104379.subtitle_en: James Bond actor Daniel Craig was not allowed to come to Svalbard during filming of “The Golden Compass”, despite some of the story being set here.
104379.title_en: Svalbard Too Dangerous for James Bond

104390.excerpt_en: It was previously established that a pub would be built on the first floor of the town-center building, with housing on the second.
104390.subtitle_en: The apartments in the town-center building will be rented to tourists and short-term workers in the town. A three-room apartment can be rented for just under NOK 4,000 per day from March to May.

104403.excerpt_en: “The white paper on the High North called for an assessment of a new ice-capable research vessel. 15.”
104403.subtitle_en: A unanimous committee recommends building a new ice-capable research vessel. This could spell the end of research voyages around Svalbard by the “Lance” and “Jan Mayen”.

104407.excerpt_en: This is revealed in a letter the Norwegian Polar Institute (NP) sent to the Governor of Svalbard, the Ministry of Climate and the Environment, the Ministry of Justice and the Directorate for Nature Management. In April, an NP research team observed extensive illegal motor traffic along the east coast.
104407.subtitle_en: Researchers have observed several tourist groups traveling illegally along the east coast in search of polar bears.

104409.excerpt_en: The researchers stayed at the Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association cabin in Mohnbukta for a week and a half in late April while conducting fieldwork on ringed seals. The cabin is ideally situated for observing all traffic along the east coast of Spitsbergen, halfway between Agardhbukta and Negribreen.
104409.subtitle_en: Researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute have sent the Governor of Svalbard a highly remarkable letter, copied to the Directorate for Nature Management and the Ministries of Climate and the Environment and Justice.

104423.excerpt_en: Fifteen witnesses have been called in the appeal case against Store Norske operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad. Thirteen were called by the prosecution and two by Fjukstad’s defense lawyer, Erling O.
104423.subtitle_en: Bjørn Fjukstad’s lawyer, Erling O. Lyngtveit, is critical of the prosecution’s extensive witness list in the appeal case against Fjukstad. The case began in Hålogaland Court of Appeal on Wednesday.
104423.title_en: Critical of the Number of Witnesses

104431.excerpt_en: An American tourist reported to the Governor of Svalbard last Sunday that a beluga calf was lying on shore. Environmental protection officer Rune Bergstrøm made sure the little creature was returned to the water.
104431.subtitle_en: A beluga calf had to be helped back into the water last weekend after becoming stranded in the Sjøområdet area. Watch video of the incident here.
104431.title_en: White Whale Calf Rescued Back into the Sea

104456.excerpt_en: Nearly two years have passed since the breakthrough accident at Svea Nord, which claimed a man’s life. The passage of time meant that many of the witnesses who testified in the Court of Appeal in Tromsø no longer remembered the details surrounding the time of the accident.
104456.subtitle_en: The prosecutor sought a 90-day unconditional prison sentence when the appeal case against Bjørn Fjukstad concluded in Hålogaland Court of Appeal on Thursday. The verdict will be delivered on Wednesday.
104456.title_en: Prosecution Seeks Prison Sentence for Bjørn Fjukstad

104483.excerpt_en: “We have had ventilated smoking rooms, like most other mines. Now the insurance company has demanded that we stop having smoking rooms,” says Robert Hermansen, managing director of Store Norske.
104483.subtitle_en: The miners are no longer allowed to smoke in the break rooms at Svea Nord. The smoking ban was introduced on Thursday.
104483.title_en: Complete Smoking Ban at Svea Nord

104499.excerpt_en: Read the full verdict here! (PDF 7.4 MB) Bjørn Fjukstad was sentenced to 90 days’ suspended imprisonment and fined NOK 30,000 by Nord-Troms District Court in January this year.
104499.subtitle_en: Operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad was today sentenced to 60 days in prison by Hålogaland Court of Appeal. The verdict was unanimous.

104501.excerpt_en: The application by senior consultant Ulf Aasebø of the University Hospital of North Norway and historian Kjell-G. Kjær to take samples from the mass grave at Svenskhuset on Kapp Thordsen has been rejected by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage, even though the Governor of Svalbard recommended approving it.
104501.subtitle_en: The two researchers who want to open the mass grave at Svenskhuset have been turned down by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage. They are now appealing the decision.
104501.title_en: Denied Permission to Open Mass Grave

104505.excerpt_en: JCDecaux has been awarded the advertising rights in the new terminal, which is due to be completed in October. The company has decided to sell all the advertising space to a single advertiser rather than divide up the various placements.
104505.subtitle_en: One advertiser will get all the advertising space in the new terminal being built at Svalbard Airport.

104541.excerpt_en: The backup power station was started and has been running at full capacity since the power station shutdown, but according to a press release from Bydrift, it does not have enough output for all end users. Those with generators installed have started them, helping to alleviate the situation.
104541.subtitle_en: The power station in Longyearbyen shut down on Saturday evening because of a boiler leak. Services for users will be reduced until Tuesday afternoon.

104551.excerpt_en: Ola Mellem of Tromsdalen Athletics was the fastest full-marathon runner, with a time of 03:12:22. In total, 26 people ran the full marathon, 42 ran the half-marathon and 31 ran the Spitsbergen Mile.
104551.subtitle_en: Nearly 100 people took part in the Spitsbergen Marathon at the weekend. Find the results here.

104554.excerpt_en: “I was initially opposed to commercial cabins because I fear they will lead to a flood of field tourism and the damage it causes,” says Umbreit.
104554.subtitle_en: Andreas Umbreit of Spitsbergen Tours is taking a strong stand against the other companies that have applied to build commercial cabins.

104559.excerpt_en: “We are starting work to upgrade the power station now, at the beginning of this month. All three boilers will be refurbished, and the two old chimneys will be replaced with a new one,” says mine director Boris I.
104559.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol is beginning work to upgrade the power station and renovate buildings in Barentsburg. The number of employees will also be increased, according to the mine director.

104572.excerpt_en: Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik announced it already at the turn of the year: the anniversary year was by no means over. And with the revival of the hit show Brødrene Østermanns huskors at Huset on Saturday evening, she was proved right. She got her way, just like her character Anna Søderberg.
104572.subtitle_en: So they did it after all—the people who felt it was not enough to celebrate Longyearbyen’s 100th anniversary in 2006, but thought it was fitting to mark the town’s 101st birthday as well.

104576.excerpt_en: “We have entered into a long-term lease agreement with Store Norske and will take on considerable responsibility for upgrading the station together with them. As owners, they will be responsible for the exterior of the buildings, while we will be responsible for the interior.”
104576.subtitle_en: Basecamp has been awarded a contract by Store Norske to operate Isfjord Radio at Kapp Linné.

104581.excerpt_en: The couple had been ranked second behind Birgit Ryningen and Anders Levoll from Trondheim, but when the latter declined, the Bodø couple got the opportunity—and accepted. “We had tried before, and when we got the opportunity this time, we simply had to act quickly.”
104581.subtitle_en: Tordis and Nils Aga from Bodø will be the new trapping couple at Austfjordnes.

104598.excerpt_en: “Bjørn Fjukstad has appealed the sentencing. The next step is for the Appeals Selection Committee of the Supreme Court to decide whether the case should proceed before the Supreme Court or be halted,” says lawyer Erling O.
104598.subtitle_en: Bjørn Fjukstad has appealed his 60-day prison sentence from the Court of Appeal to the Supreme Court.
104598.title_en: Fjukstad Appeals to the Supreme Court

104600.excerpt_en: For the very ability to let nature envelop you, rest your head and let your thoughts drift, to feel this infinite polar pull—that which is the finest thing about the country—is under pressure. Pressure that increases year by year.
104600.subtitle_en: You will have to go farther than far this summer to find peace and quiet in Svalbard. It is all a strange paradox.

104611.excerpt_en: Within the nightlife industry, rumours have recently circulated that Huset was planning to hire a female bartender who would occasionally show her breasts. General manager André Grytbakk denies that this is a concrete plan.
104611.subtitle_en: There will still be no bare breasts on display at Huset.

104613.excerpt_en: “We believe it is appropriate that the Governor should continue to be able to use air passenger lists,” says Per Martin Borg, senior adviser in the Polar Affairs Department of the Ministry of Justice.
104613.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Justice considers it entirely lawful for the Governor to have access to air passenger lists.

104625.excerpt_en: The hotel, which consisted of a long row of Moelven modules, was erected in connection with construction of the airport at Hotellneset in 1974. Over the years, the temporary barracks complex was used as accommodation, offices and a construction facility.
104625.subtitle_en: Avinor and the Longyearbyen Fire Service demolished the dilapidated “Airport Hotel” by burning it down at the airport on Saturday.

104636.excerpt_en: The prosecutor in the case, State Prosecutor Torstein Hevnskjel, says the case was scheduled for Tuesday but was brought forward by half a day because the defense lawyer introduced several witnesses.
104636.subtitle_en: The trial of the 16-year-old from Longyearbyen charged with sexually assaulting two girls last autumn begins in Nord-Troms District Court on Monday.
104636.title_en: Sexual Assault Case Goes to Court

104669.excerpt_en: At the beginning of May, the Svalbard Tourism Council complained to the Governor that snowmobile traffic in Bolterdalen had become excessive and asked for an explanation of what the Governor defines as commercial traffic.
104669.subtitle_en: The Governor is considering closing Bolterdalen and Tverrdalen to commercial snowmobile traffic as well from 1 March.

104674.excerpt_en: In today’s print edition of Svalbardposten, managing director of Spitsbergen Travel Jan Sverre Sivertsen hoped that “Polar Star” would be ready to sail in a week. The company has now decided to cancel that cruise as well—the fifth of 11 planned departures this summer.
104674.subtitle_en: “Polar Star” will remain in Longyearbyen for at least another two weeks. Next Friday’s cruise has also been cancelled.

104692.excerpt_en: “They took smaller quantities of beer, since a lot had been left outside,” says Chief Inspector Brynjulv Eide. He says the break-in occurred after 2:30 a.m. on Saturday.
104692.subtitle_en: During the night before Saturday, someone broke into Kafé Busen through a storage entrance and stole beer.

104701.excerpt_en: The fisherman was picked up from a Norwegian fishing boat 160 nautical miles east of Hopen because of heart problems. “It was a long helicopter flight,” says Chief Inspector Brynjulv Eide of the Governor’s Office.
104701.subtitle_en: A Faroese fisherman was flown by helicopter to Longyearbyen Hospital on Saturday evening.
104701.title_en: Flew Out Fisherman with Heart Problems

104714.excerpt_en: The community-service period has been set at one year and six months. The 15-year-old must also pay NOK 100,000 in compensation to each of the two girls.
104714.subtitle_en: A 15-year-old boy from Longyearbyen has been sentenced by the Nord-Troms District Court to 400 hours of community service for sexual assault against two girls.

104722.excerpt_en: “Having an EU commissioner come to Svalbard is highly significant for Norway in terms of long-term international cooperation. Many IPY projects are based in Svalbard, and it is important to gain European recognition of what a fantastic research laboratory Svalbard is,” says Øystein Djupedal.
104722.subtitle_en: Minister of Education and Research Øystein Djupedal (SV) was in Svalbard last week together with EU Commissioner Janez Potocnik from Poland.
104722.title_en: On a Research Expedition in Svalbard

104726.excerpt_en: The first flight will be on 27 March next year, and the route will have two weekly departures, on Thursdays and Sundays.
104726.subtitle_en: Norwegian is launching a new direct route between Oslo and Longyearbyen.

104741.excerpt_en: At the beginning of this week, the Governor sent letters to all the companies that had applied to establish a tourist cabin in Svalbard. Half of the six proposed cabins have now received the go-ahead.
104741.subtitle_en: The Governor is permitting tourist cabins in Adolfbukta, Brentskardet and Slettvika.

104753.excerpt_en: To be able to arrive in Svalbard without anyone needing to know, to travel anywhere in the archipelago without anyone caring where. To put an extension on a listed building and erect a flagpole outside without being investigated afterwards.
104753.subtitle_en: It would have been nice to do exactly as one pleased, without worrying about violating the Cultural Heritage Act, the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act, the Motor Traffic Regulations or any other written rules.

104762.excerpt_en: “It is unusual that the Governor is given lists of everyone travelling to and from Svalbard.”
104762.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Data Protection Authority considers it problematic that the Governor has unrestricted access to passenger lists and is calling for the purpose to be established in law.

104769.excerpt_en: The Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association (LJFF) has long campaigned for eider and barnacle goose hunting to be permitted in Svalbard. However, the draft harvesting regulations put out for consultation this spring did not permit hunting of either species.

104889.subtitle_en: The Union of Education Norway in Longyearbyen believes its housing provision has deteriorated since it became part of the local council.

104911.subtitle_en: The tow of MV “Polar Star” to the mainland began Thursday afternoon. The entire cruise season has now been cancelled.

104916.excerpt_en: Chapter One: A couple of months ago, an employee at the Norwegian Polar Institute (NPI) sat down and wrote a letter to the Governor of Svalbard about illegal snowmobile traffic on the east coast.

104942.subtitle_en: Russian researchers shot a polar bear at Giæverneset on Nordaustlandet.

104945.excerpt_en: “We were informed that a fisherman on a Russian boat east of Hopen was seriously ill, and launched a rescue operation,” says Petter Braaten, the duty officer with the Governor of Svalbard. The Governor was contacted at 4 a.m. Tuesday.
104945.subtitle_en: A Russian man died early Tuesday morning aboard a fishing vessel east of Hopen.

104947.excerpt_en: “It’s the first time I’ve seen it up close, and it was in considerably worse condition than it appears to be from town,” exclaims cultural heritage adviser Siri Hoem of the Governor’s Office.
104947.subtitle_en: The 100-year-old coal silo on the mountainside above Longyearbyen is so badly damaged by rot that it cannot be saved. The same applies to several of the cableway trestles.

104955.excerpt_en: Deputy Governor Elisabeth B. Løvold is being very cautious in her handling of the Russians while Governor Per Sefland is on holiday.
104955.subtitle_en: Perhaps the Russians have grown tired of the Governor’s constant demands and orders and decided to test the limits of the arrangement. The flights carried out recently by the Russian helicopter company Air Company Spark Plus are clearly violations of its concession—and also of the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act.

104967.excerpt_en: When the three Russian researchers who had shot a polar bear on Nordaustlandet were questioned, it emerged that they had been flown out by a Russian helicopter from the Kapp Heer base near Barentsburg.
104967.subtitle_en: The Russians are conducting helicopter operations without a valid flight permit, defying the Governor’s repeated refusals.

104988.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard received notification of the accident at 4:35 p.m. Wednesday and immediately launched an operation to rescue the injured. “We had the Super Puma ready almost immediately.”
104988.subtitle_en: Eight passengers were injured when ice from Hornbreen fell onto the Russian tourist vessel «Alexey Maryshev» in Hornsund on Wednesday afternoon. Two of them were seriously injured.
104988.title_en: Two Passengers Seriously Injured as Glacier Calved

105000.excerpt_en: Four passengers have already been flown to Tromsø by air ambulance—two overnight on Wednesday and two on Thursday morning. Two more will be flown to Tromsø later on Thursday.
105000.subtitle_en: The number of injured passengers and crew has risen to 20 after the Russian cruise vessel «Alexey Maryshev» arrived in Longyearbyen on Thursday morning.

105023.excerpt_en: The flight permit from the Norwegian Civil Aviation Authority is both clear and easy to understand: Air Company Spark Plus, the helicopter company used by Trust Arktikugol to operate the one helicopter still in service at Kapp Heer, is only authorised to transport people and equipment between Barentsburg and Longyearbyen in connection with the trust’s mining operations.
105023.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Civil Aviation Authority’s restrictions on Russian helicopter use on Svalbard, and the Governor’s enforcement of the rules, have caused friction in relations with our neighbour to the west.

105036.excerpt_en: It was at the beginning of June that the helicopter from Air Company Spark Plus landed in the middle of a colony of nesting eider ducks and geese on Tromsøya, south of Forlandsundet.
105036.subtitle_en: Earlier this summer, a Russian helicopter devastated a colony of nesting birds in Forlandsundet. The case has been reported to the police and is being investigated for violations of the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act.

105054.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the accident at 10 p.m. Friday. “The man was flown to Longyearbyen Hospital,” says Jan Tømmervold, the Governor’s duty officer.
105054.subtitle_en: A German man with a broken leg had to be picked up by helicopter from a cabin in Krossfjorden on Friday evening.

105058.excerpt_en: On June 4 this year, Store Norske operations engineer Bjørn Fjukstad was sentenced to 60 days’ unconditional imprisonment for a grossly negligent violation of the Working Environment Act in connection with the mine accident at Svea Nord in the summer of 2005.
105058.subtitle_en: The Supreme Court’s Appeals Selection Committee has rejected Bjørn Fjukstad’s appeal against the judgment handed down by the Hålogaland Court of Appeal.

105062.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified that a young boy had driven off the road near Mine 6 in Adventdalen at around 11 a.m. Tuesday. “The car skidded and ended up in the ditch.”
105062.subtitle_en: A young boy drove off the road in Adventdalen on Tuesday morning in a car he had stolen from his employer. The boy is under 18 and does not have a driving licence. He can expect to face the police.
105062.title_en: Drove into Ditch in Stolen Car

105077.excerpt_en: Box after box is carried out of one of the rooms at the Pomor Museum in Barentsburg. Pieces of wood are wrapped in bubble wrap and placed in crates.
105077.subtitle_en: People in Barentsburg witnessed a rare event on Thursday. Cultural heritage objects that had until now been stored at the museum in the Russian town have been moved to Longyearbyen.

105079.excerpt_en: A total of 286 people have applied to shoot reindeer during this year’s hunt. That is ten fewer than last year.
105079.subtitle_en: The number of people wanting to hunt reindeer on Svalbard has fallen slightly since last year.

105102.excerpt_en: When the consultation deadline for the new Svalbard tax proposal expired on August 1, 15 consultation responses containing comments on the proposal had been submitted.
105102.subtitle_en: Businesses in Longyearbyen are mounting strong protests against the proposed increase in corporate tax.
105102.title_en: Massive Protest Against Higher Corporate Tax

105105.excerpt_en: The force of such ice masses is so immense that only chance prevented passengers or crew from being killed on the spot or swept overboard by the wave that washed across the vessel.

105115.excerpt_en: Just three days after the accident at Hornbreen, where 20 people were injured when the glacier calved, the «Aleksey Maryshev» set out on another voyage with new tourists. Deputy Governor Elisabeth B.

105115.title_en: Accident Boat Allowed to Sail On

105130.subtitle_en: Environment Minister Helen Bjørnøy opened the international climate conference in Ny-Ålesund on Monday afternoon. The opening was delayed by heavy blowing snow.

105132.excerpt_en: According to the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, the chance of encountering drifting ice around Svalbard has fallen considerably. The institute’s ice service keeps maritime operators in the north continuously updated on the location of the ice edge and where vessels can expect to encounter drifting ice.
105132.subtitle_en: This year’s Arctic ice extent is the smallest ever recorded, and the melting season will continue for several more weeks. There is already more than one million square kilometres less ice than usual at this time of year.

105136.excerpt_en: There were fears that the plane might leave the runway because of its high speed. According to Nordlys, Langnes Airport, Tromsø police, the ambulance service and the fire brigade were on full alert from 1:30 p.m.
105136.subtitle_en: The mail plane developed flap trouble en route to Longyearbyen on Tuesday. It returned to Tromsø, where the ambulance service and fire brigade were on full alert.
105136.title_en: Mail Plane Had to Turn Back

105152.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten was there when the Governor of Svalbard collected 9,000 objects of cultural and historical value from Barentsburg. See all the pictures from the move here!

105157.subtitle_en: The double grave of Kjell Kjær and Ulf Aasebø, discovered at Kapp Thordsen last Thursday, was found and described as early as 1883.

105367.subtitle_en: It took Store Norske eight months to get the fire at Svea Nord under control. A week on Monday, the court case over the insurance settlement begins.

105479.subtitle_en: A dog was shot near the campsite outside Longyearbyen on Friday morning because it could not be caught.

105520.subtitle_en: Lufttransport fears problems for flights to Svea this winter. The reason is that Avinor employees at the airport can no longer work overtime.
105520.title_en: Air Traffic to Svea to Be Affected

105594.subtitle_en: Driving the wrong way at the new airport terminal could cost you NOK 4,200.

105595.subtitle_en: Large parts of Svalbard’s east coast could be closed to tourists. The Directorate for Nature Management (DN) wants tighter controls on cruise traffic.

105630.subtitle_en: The state prosecutor has charged Jason Roberts over the unlawful work at Taubanelageret. The case will be heard by the district court in April next year.
