In the national budget presented last Friday, the Ministry of Finance backed the working group.
105639.subtitle_en: An interdepartmental working group will assess the issue of commuting between Svalbard and mainland Norway.

105641.excerpt_en: Thursday was an open day at the kindergarten, where stew, tortilla, coffee and cakes were sold to raise money for this year’s televised fundraiser. “Many people came, both parents and others.”
105641.subtitle_en: Children from Polarflokken Kindergarten visited the bank on Monday morning with NOK 6,175 for this year’s televised fundraiser.
105641.title_en: At the Bank for the Televised Fundraiser

105648.excerpt_en: This year, too, the school helped raise money for the annual televised fundraiser. Coffee and sodd were sold in the atrium, and the school of music and the arts staged a performance about Winnie-the-Pooh and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood.
105648.subtitle_en: NOK 52,400 was raised when the school held an open house on Wednesday afternoon and the school of music and the arts staged its version of Winnie-the-Pooh and His Friends.

105657.excerpt_en: The community council leader described the election result as a protest by Longyearbyen’s residents. According to community council leader Sigmund Spjelkavik, the reason was the tax increase and the protection of Reindalen.
105657.subtitle_en: Four years ago, three out of five eligible voters chose not to vote. Turnout fell by around ten percentage points from 2001 to 2003, to 41.1 percent.

105679.excerpt_en: The re-run election for the Longyearbyen Community Council began today at 2 p.m. There are 1,558 eligible voters in Longyearbyen: 953 men and 605 women.
105679.subtitle_en: Turnout at the polling station in Lompensenteret was steady throughout Sunday afternoon after the doors opened at 2 p.m.

105698.excerpt_en: The plan describes the management decisions the Governor of Svalbard plans to make in Hopen Nature Reserve in the years ahead. The reserve was established on 26.
105698.subtitle_en: The Directorate for Nature Management (DN) has approved and adopted the management plan for Hopen.

105703.excerpt_en: Vote counting is in full swing after the polling stations at Lompen Centre closed at 8 p.m. Once the last person had voted, the doors were locked, and Thor Bendiksen, Anne Lise Olsen and Turid Seltveit opened the ballot boxes to count the votes.
105703.subtitle_en: Polling stations in Longyearbyen closed at 8 p.m., and the election committee hopes to have the final result before 10 p.m.

105706.excerpt_en: The polling stations close at 8 p.m., and Sigmund Engdahl, administrative director of Longyearbyen Local Council, expects the advance-vote result to be ready half an hour later. “The preliminary count will begin as soon as possible after the polling stations close, and we hope to have the election result ready before 10 p.m.,” says Engdahl.
105706.subtitle_en: The election committee hopes to have the result ready by 10 p.m. tonight. Svalbardposten.no will keep you updated.

105720.excerpt_en: The result after the advance votes were counted shows that the Labour Party received 49.1 percent of the vote. This suggests that incumbent local council leader Kjell Mork will continue in the post for the next four-year term as Labour’s lead candidate.
105720.subtitle_en: The Labour Party has received nearly half of all advance votes in this year’s local council election. It is therefore comfortably ahead before all the votes have been counted.

105724.excerpt_en: The final election result shows that the Labour Party won a clear victory in this year’s Longyearbyen local council election, securing 45.5 percent of the vote. Incumbent local council leader Kjell Mork is therefore likely to continue as council leader for the next four-year term.
105724.subtitle_en: The Labour Party is the election winner after all the votes were counted. The party wins seven seats on the new local council.

105729.excerpt_en: Because of the forthcoming blues festival in Longyearbyen, flights to Svalbard are packed this week. When the plane scheduled to land on Tuesday had to return to Tromsø because of bad weather, many passengers were told they would not have a new seat until Friday.
105729.subtitle_en: All the passengers on the plane that was unable to land in Longyearbyen on Tuesday got seats on Wednesday’s flight.

105747.excerpt_en: CC Cowboys’ new live album, recorded in the cinema at Huset in March, is released on Monday. The band has also produced a 30-minute DVD covering its entire stay on Svalbard, with footage from the concert and from the days before and after.
105747.subtitle_en: CC Cowboys will release the album “On Svalbard Without Electricity” on Monday. Vocalist Magnus Grønneberg is very pleased with the result.

105757.excerpt_en: By all means, holler—go on, holler away: Winter is here, winter is here. Fuck, it’s great.
105757.subtitle_en: There we are again, right in the middle of the driving snow. How wonderful it is to let yourself be battered by it; to feel the snow lash your face, screw up your eyes, crawl into your down jacket and hunch your back, pull your hat down over your ears, and bury your fists deep in your jacket pockets.

105763.excerpt_en: The festival is growing in step with Longyearbyen’s population and the number of venues. At Svalbar, which opened two weeks ago, Johnny Dyer and Notodden band Spoonful and Blues performed.
105763.subtitle_en: The Dark Season Blues festival began on Thursday with six bands at three venues. This year’s festival is the fifth in a row.
105763.title_en: Dark Season Blues and a Full Moon

105775.excerpt_en: Svalbard Villmarksenter took over Kafé Busen at Lompen Centre in January last year. Karl and Berit Våtvik ran the business with their daughter Silje Våtvik, who served as general manager.
105775.subtitle_en: Customers have stopped coming, employees have been laid off and opening hours have been cut. Svalbard Villmarksenter is now considering selling Kafé Busen.

105777.excerpt_en: “Are you excited? Were there many people here last year?”
105777.subtitle_en: The children at Kullungen nursery did not need asking twice when Jan Tore Lauritsen and Iver Olav Erstad struck up the blues for a dance.

105783.excerpt_en: “We will enter into new local agreements, but we acted pre-emptively and returned to normal operations before the weekend,” says airport manager Ole M. Rambech, pleased.
105783.subtitle_en: The dispute between Avinor and the Norwegian Civil Servants’ Association (NTL) has been called off. This means airport operations are back to normal.

105800.excerpt_en: The man, who works in Longyearbyen, is said to have driven the stolen car off the road near Longyearbyen Hospital at around 11:30 p.m. on Monday. When the Governor of Svalbard arrived at the scene, they reportedly suspected drink-driving.
105800.subtitle_en: A man in his twenties has been charged with drink-driving after driving off the road in a stolen car on Monday evening.

105803.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified that a lower-secondary pupil had struck another pupil around noon on Monday morning. “The pupil sustained an injury to the face and has filed a report.”
105803.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is investigating an act of violence at Longyearbyen School.

105818.excerpt_en: Morten Løberg will be in the studio at around 8:30 a.m. to show images from his latest project—photographs of Svalbard taken with a homemade pinhole camera—writes Fotografi.no. Løberg’s pinhole-camera images will be exhibited at Galleri Svalbard from the 8th.
105818.subtitle_en: On Wednesday morning, viewers can see images from Svalbard taken by Morten Løberg and Synnøve Haga on God morgen Norge on TV2.

105825.excerpt_en: “It’s very interesting to learn more about the professions,” says 12-year-old Emilie Sommervold as she watches a video made by Store Norske. “Do you know what you want to be when you grow up?”
105825.subtitle_en: Around 20 companies, colleges and universities attended Longyearbyen School’s careers fair on Wednesday this week.

105843.excerpt_en: High-gloss polished steel, special glass, mirrors and light from fibre-optic cable will make the top of the seed vault entrance shine. The building will reflect sunlight and light according to the season and time of day.
105843.subtitle_en: The artwork destined to adorn the outside of the seed vault is to be ready for the opening in February. The top of the entrance will shine like a jewel.
105843.title_en: Seed Vault Artwork on Its Way

105849.excerpt_en: We northerners live in a small, varied and extraordinarily rich world. Most of us are more than content to potter around in our local area.
105849.subtitle_en: Svalbard is a land of islands, some vast, some smaller—with a sprinkling of islets and skerries. 63,000 square kilometres of mountains, glaciers, spits, headlands, promontories and low-lying ground barely rising above sea level.

105861.excerpt_en: “In terms of both audiences and music, I don’t think we’ve ever had a better festival,” says Jon Sandmo, head of the Longyearbyen Blues Club. He can look back on a hectic weekend of blues music throughout Longyearbyen, strong attendance and satisfied artists.
105861.subtitle_en: Festival director Jon Sandmo sums up this year’s Dark Season Blues as the best ever.
105861.title_en: The Greatest Blues Festival Ever in Longyearbyen

105867.excerpt_en: On Sunday, he walked through the crowd wearing a black suit jacket, black trousers, a white shirt and a black neckerchief. A black hat sat on his head, and his black hair was tied in a ponytail.
105867.subtitle_en: True enough, he is an Indian, a gypsy and a wandering cowboy—and, to top it all, born in the world’s northernmost town—but Adventdalen proved too cold for “the man in black.”

105873.excerpt_en: The collection contains both historical and modern images documenting Norwegian and foreign activity in the Arctic and Antarctic. Areas including Alaska, Bear Island, Franz Josef Land, Greenland, Jan Mayen, Iceland, Novaya Zemlya, Svalbard, Antarctica, Bouvet Island, Peter I Island, South Georgia, the South Shetland Islands and the South Sandwich Islands are represented in the collection.
105873.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Polar Institute (NP) has posted an image database containing 17,300 polar images on its website.

105886.excerpt_en: After several weeks of wrangling, it is now clear how representatives in the forthcoming local council will be distributed. Kjell Mork will continue as leader, with Heinrich Eggenfellner as deputy leader.
105886.subtitle_en: All the parties in the local council will be represented on the various committees and boards. Kjell Mork (Labour) and Heinrich Eggenfellner (Conservative) will continue as council leader and deputy leader.
105886.title_en: This Is How the Local Council Will Work Together

105890.excerpt_en: What was supposed to be a combined film screening and seminar on Roald Amundsen instead became a straightforward lecture on film history and which films could have been shown if there had been power in the UNIS building.
105890.subtitle_en: The opening of this year’s Kunstpause did not go quite as the organizers had hoped, thanks to a prolonged power outage.

105893.excerpt_en: At around 6:15 p.m. Wednesday, the power went out throughout the town. It was gone for almost an hour before returning.
105893.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen experienced its longest power outage in several years on Wednesday evening when the power station suffered data problems.
105893.title_en: Data Problems Plunged the Town into Darkness

105913.excerpt_en: The Polar Department of the Ministry of Justice has reviewed the practice of using airline passenger lists on Svalbard and proposes a new regulation allowing the tax authorities on Svalbard to receive the passenger lists. “If there is reason to suspect a violation of the provisions of Svalbard’s tax legislation, the Governor of Svalbard may give the tax authorities on Svalbard access to the lists.”
105913.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Justice is considering giving the tax office access to the Governor’s flight lists to prevent tax evasion.

105931.excerpt_en: In a letter to the Civil Aviation Authority, Trust Arktikugol Director General Alexander P. Veselov announces that the company will acquire new helicopters next year.
105931.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol wants to acquire new helicopters and start commercial flights on Svalbard. At the same time, the Russians reject claims that the flights they operated this summer were illegal.
105931.title_en: Russians Want to Operate Commercial Flights

105945.excerpt_en: The 25-year-old was found dead this week in Goa on India’s west coast, where he was on holiday. “The Indian hospital where he is being held has determined that he died of blood poisoning,” says Petter Braaten, chief officer at the Governor’s Office.
105945.subtitle_en: Mads Weis-Fogh (25) from Longyearbyen, who was found dead in India this week, died of blood poisoning.

105952.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified that the Russian trawler had run aground at around 5 a.m. Sunday. “The weather in the area was poor, and the trawler called on the emergency channel.”
105952.subtitle_en: A Russian trawler ran aground off Cape Kåre on Bear Island on Sunday morning.

106010.excerpt_en: Halvor Gustavsen has supplied crosswords to Svalbardposten for 17 years without ever having been to Svalbard. He does not take that particularly hard, since he has seen most of the world and crossed the Equator 130 times.
106010.subtitle_en: He lives in a six-letter place in Lofoten and has been away from his wife for a total of 256 months because of his profession—which has ten letters.

106016.excerpt_en: “It was a fox with paralysis in its hindquarters that came to the station and died there. We want to have the fox analyzed,” says Governor of Svalbard nature management adviser Tor Punsvik.
106016.subtitle_en: Last Friday, the weather station on Bear Island was visited by a mysterious fox. The fox is now being tested for rabies.

106034.excerpt_en: “I bought it at the old quay sometime in the 1970s. Ole Kristian and I stopped by town on a Fyllegod trip,” he says.
106034.subtitle_en: It is something of a miracle that young Johansen (58) and, not least, his fur hat have survived. Both have made a brief visit to town.

106067.excerpt_en: “There is hardly a single weekend when we do not have to respond to people who are extremely intoxicated, and they are not young people or visitors. We often receive reports from licensed venues needing police assistance because people have fallen asleep and cannot be woken,” says Chief Superintendent of the Governor’s Office Olav Tombre.
106067.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is concerned that guests are often over-served at venues in Longyearbyen.

106072.excerpt_en: The construction company Sandmo & Svenkerud had hired out two employees by the hour to Jason Roberts and thus became a party to the case, according to Tollef Svenkerud.
106072.subtitle_en: Sandmo & Svenkerud have accepted a NOK 50,000 fine for the work they carried out at the cableway warehouse.

106074.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Veterinary Institute in Tromsø examined the dead fox and confirmed to NRK Troms that it was not infected with rabies. The fox is now being tested for distemper.
106074.subtitle_en: The fox found dead on Bear Island two weeks ago was not infected with rabies.

106080.excerpt_en: In a letter to the Governor of Svalbard, Trust Arktikugol Director General Alexander P. Veselov writes that the company plans to modernize its helicopter base in Barentsburg and operate two or three helicopters.
106080.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol says it plans to buy three new helicopters and resume operations in Pyramiden.

106086.excerpt_en: No, there is nothing we can do. The only option would be to ignore the whole thing, simply shrug our shoulders and carry on as before.
106086.subtitle_en: They are pressing in—the bureaucrats down south, with their laws and regulations, their prohibitions and restrictions.

106117.excerpt_en: A year ago, the Norwegian Coastal Administration was tasked by the Ministry of Fisheries and Coastal Affairs with preparing a draft regulation on compulsory pilotage for certain vessels operating in the waters around Svalbard. The government’s High North strategy also states that maritime safety around Svalbard is to be strengthened.
106117.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration has prepared the basis for introducing a polar pilotage service on Svalbard. The report on the service, which had been withheld from the public, is now available.
106117.title_en: Proposes Polar Pilotage Service on Svalbard

106128.excerpt_en: The film is a major new production from New Line Cinema, the company behind the “Lord of the Rings” trilogy. The production company chose to create large parts of the film using digital effects, but most of the background footage was filmed in Norway.
106128.subtitle_en: The Norwegian premiere of the blockbuster film “The Golden Compass” took place on Wednesday. Parts of the film were shot on Svalbard.

106135.excerpt_en: Read the ruling here. Store Norske’s claim was approximately NOK 790 million, while the insurers were unwilling to pay more than NOK 258 million. “This shows that it was right for us to bring the case,” says Store Norske CEO Robert Hermansen.
106135.subtitle_en: The Nord-Troms District Court has issued its ruling in the insurance case following the fire at Svea Nord in summer 2005. Compensation has been set at NOK 589 million.

106151.excerpt_en: Kroa’s employees will learn to play music suited to the guests, and Kroa will hire DJs and bands capable of creating a good atmosphere. “There will be a DJ, but not like the one at Huset.”
106151.subtitle_en: DJ Kohib will provide the music at Kroa on Friday and Saturday. The venue is making a major commitment to music.

106178.excerpt_en: The application for an alcohol licence in the new airport terminal was considered by the Administration Committee (AU) on Tuesday, and the committee unanimously decided it should be rejected. “The convenience store is the dominant concept, and there is little separation between the cafeteria area and the rest of the departure hall.”
106178.subtitle_en: Because there is no clear separation, politicians do not want Coop to be allowed to serve alcohol in the new airport terminal.

106183.excerpt_en: “We have not received the figures for how much noise the new backup power generator will produce. The tender documents were sent out last Friday, and the deadline for submitting a bid is Monday,” says Paul Guldstrand, managing director of Bydrift.
106183.subtitle_en: Politicians fear that the new backup power plant in Longyearbyen will be too noisy. Bydrift maintains that it will not be used often enough to disturb people.
106183.title_en: Fears of Noise from Backup Power Plant

106194.excerpt_en: “I think it is quite fantastic. Only one museum in Norway has received this award before, and that was Bryggen Museum in Bergen, in 1978.”
106194.subtitle_en: Svalbard Museum has been awarded the Council of Europe Museum Prize for 2008, in competition with 59 other museums.

106202.excerpt_en: Arnestad has extensive national and international professional experience from industry, offshore, shipping and banking. He joins from the position of investment director and head of direct-investment operations at Norfund, the Norwegian Investment Fund for Developing Countries.
106202.subtitle_en: Bjørn Arnestad (61) from Sulitjelma has been appointed the new managing director of Store Norske.
106202.title_en: New Director Appointed at Store Norske

106223.excerpt_en: “What happened? No, well, I worked at Sjusjøen near Lillehammer.”
106223.subtitle_en: There are said to be 17 more of the Sølvsten species in Denmark. Tina’s migration to Svalbard has clearly weakened the southern species.
106223.title_en: The Girl in the Tin House

106230.excerpt_en: At 6 p.m. on Sunday, a man employed by LNS Spitsbergen was reported missing by his supervisor in Svea. The man was supposed to drive a snowmobile from Longyearbyen to Svea, but never arrived.
106230.subtitle_en: On Sunday evening, the Governor launched a search operation. A man employed by LNS Spitsbergen in Svea failed to report for work as agreed.

106237.excerpt_en: “You have to be three people to form a local branch. Now two of us have joined, and one is interested if we set up a local branch.”
106237.subtitle_en: A local Venstre branch is being planned in Svalbard. For now, the party has two active members.

106251.excerpt_en: However quickly the backward glance, Store Norske stands there blinking black—or red, depending on how you look at it.
106251.subtitle_en: As a year draws to a close, one can certainly take the opportunity to cast a quick glance backward, but it is more important to look ahead.
106251.title_en: We Will Probably See the Light

106262.excerpt_en: Rats and mice could develop into a problem in Longyearbyen. This emerged when the Governor met two weeks ago with several institutions and associations in Longyearbyen, with pest-control experts from the Norwegian Institute of Public Health taking part.
106262.subtitle_en: Rat droppings outside Svalbard Equestrian Centre and a number of other signs in town have prompted a full-scale alert to combat the rats.

106273.excerpt_en: When Tuesday’s flight was cancelled, an extra flight was quickly arranged for its usual time on Wednesday afternoon. It too was cancelled because of crosswinds and an icy runway.
106273.subtitle_en: Tuesday’s flight was cancelled because of an icy runway and crosswinds. Now Wednesday afternoon’s extra flight has also been cancelled for the same reason. SAS will try again tonight.

106280.excerpt_en: In connection with the Tromsø International Film Festival 2008 in January, members of the British film Far North’s crew will come to Longyearbyen. Among them are leading actress Michelle Yeoh, who previously appeared in “Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon” and “Memoirs of a Geisha,” and director Asif Kapadia.
106280.subtitle_en: The film Far North will have its premiere screening on 15 January. The director and some of the actors will also visit.

106285.excerpt_en: According to SAS Ground Services in Longyearbyen, a decision on whether an extra flight will be arranged from Tromsø to Longyearbyen for the passengers stranded by the weather since Tuesday will be made after the daytime flight departs Longyearbyen on Thursday afternoon.
106285.subtitle_en: Both today’s passenger flight and the mail plane have landed, but the passengers who have been waiting in Tromsø since Tuesday still do not know when they will reach the town.

106288.excerpt_en: Rune Jakobsen, managing director of the shipping company Nordsyssel AS, says the number of sailing days has increased from around 100 to 150 during the seven months each year that the vessel operates for the Governor. At the same time, overnight stays and meals have increased from 200 to approximately 1,100 days.
106288.subtitle_en: The use of the Governor’s service vessel for official entertaining has increased sharply in recent years. Governor Per Sefland says this does not reduce its use as an emergency vessel.

106294.excerpt_en: There was virtually no wind, perhaps just the faintest easterly breath in the air—a mere tickle at the tip of the nostril. We were in Adventdalen, a few tiny kilometres from the sea of lights in Longyeardalen, and the sky was full of stars.
106294.subtitle_en: It was one of those crisp days during the Christmas holidays. The temperature hovered casually around minus 20.

106312.excerpt_en: Spitsbergen Travel and WWF have signed an agreement under which Spitsbergen Travel commits to reducing greenhouse-gas emissions. The agreement is part of WWF’s “Climate Savers” business programme, in which companies commit to specific targets and implementation plans for emissions cuts.
106312.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Travel is Norway’s first “Climate Saver.” The company is committing to specific emissions-reduction targets.

106321.excerpt_en: “We have limited the appeal to a couple of issues. We are appealing the business-interruption loss, both the calculation and the extent.”
106321.subtitle_en: Store Norske is appealing the Nord-Troms District Court judgment and is seeking a further NOK 140 million in damages after the fire at Svea Nord.
106321.title_en: Store Norske Appeals the Svea Judgment

106325.excerpt_en: “Excavation in permafrost is complicated and risky. This is known in every engineering community with experience from Svalbard.
106325.subtitle_en: Store Norske fears that urban densification will cause buildings to collapse because excavation in the permafrost may affect nearby buildings.

106342.excerpt_en: Before the many long caravans of snowmobiles once again begin crawling around the terrain. And long before everything and everyone starts scurrying about, buoyed by the sunlight filling us, there might perhaps be time to think a few thoughts.
106342.subtitle_en: Before dawn over Sarkofagen has spread and filled the entire sky. Before the first snowmobile has dared venture onto the fjord ice toward Tempelfjorden.

106344.excerpt_en: As part of a planned amendment to the protection regulations for Svalbard’s large nature reserves and national parks, vessels operating inside protected areas will be required to use marine gas oil as bunker fuel. The ban on using heavy fuel oil in the protected areas on the eastern side came into force on 1.
106344.subtitle_en: The requirement for lighter bunker fuel for vessels inside the national parks has consequences. According to European Cruise Service, many cruise ships will skip Svalbard.
106344.title_en: Forcing Cruise Ships Away from Svalbard

106362.excerpt_en: » Birger Amundsen? Ulf Sigernes (60) originally comes from Hammerfest.
106362.subtitle_en: He has stayed aloft for countless hours over Svalbard’s land and waters, but it is on the ground that he feels most at home. Now he can stretch his legs.

106385.excerpt_en: French adventurer Jean-Louis Étienne is leading the scientific airship expedition, which will among other things measure ice thickness in the polar basin. The project is linked to climate change and the serious threat global warming poses to the polar ice.
106385.subtitle_en: A French airship will arrive in Longyearbyen at the end of March and spend several days in Adventdalen before continuing north. The purpose is scientific.
106385.title_en: Across the Arctic Ocean by Airship

106414.excerpt_en: The 54-metre-long airship was attached to the mooring mast in Fayence, France, when, at around 6:30 Tuesday morning, a powerful gust of wind caught it and tore it free. A 1.5-metre-long iron rod came away with the craft, which drifted off at an altitude of 30 metres.
106414.subtitle_en: The French airship scheduled to arrive in Longyearbyen at the end of March was destroyed after breaking loose from its mooring mast on Tuesday morning.

106428.excerpt_en: “The power plant requires extensive work because it has operated one and a half times longer than planned. That is why it is so run-down,” explains Director General Aleksander P.
106428.subtitle_en: Plans for a new power plant in Barentsburg have been announced for years. Now work has begun on completely renovating the run-down plant.
106428.title_en: Toward an End to Emissions in Barentsburg

106430.excerpt_en: From the days when cold was cold and bit as it should, and the world was globally chilly. There was more creaking, to be sure, but otherwise a blessed calm lay over the land.
106430.subtitle_en: Sometimes things happen in our time that evoke distant historical echoes.

106435.excerpt_en: Few green spaces remain in Longyearbyen. At last week’s meeting, the Environment and Business Committee (MNU) backed building a road across the green area below Blåmyra.
106435.subtitle_en: The Environment and Business Committee supports routing access to the new homes below Blåmyra via Road 232.

106442.excerpt_en: ›› Birger Amundsen She stands all alone with the microphone in her right hand, while her left holds the microphone cable. She is wearing tall boots, blue-black jeans, a white, wide belt and a tank top.
106442.subtitle_en: Malin Jensen, 12, felt butterflies in her stomach at Huset on Saturday—until it was her turn and she stood in front of the audience.

106469.excerpt_en: Before a packed Brasseri Nansen at the Polar Hotel, temporarily converted into a concert venue, Longyearbyen Big Band opened this year’s Polarjazz with the tune “Undecided.” Then it was one number after another, featuring a series of soloists, all from Longyearbyen.
106469.subtitle_en: Polarjazz got underway on Wednesday evening, with local performers singing and playing into the night at the Polar Hotel.

106486.excerpt_en: Because of increasing pressure on the polar bear from the media, researchers and tourists, the Ministry of the Environment has asked the Governor of Svalbard to prepare a strategy paper on approaching polar bears. The paper will focus particularly on film crews, photographers and researchers.
106486.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is preparing a strategy paper on who should be allowed to approach polar bears.

106491.excerpt_en: ›› Birger Amundsen She is like other figures, and not particularly strikingly dressed either, but something about the way she moves reveals that she is a stranger. There is something about the relationship between the figure and her clothes, as though they are heading in different directions.
106491.subtitle_en: On one of those days of blowing snow and foul weather, a person stands at an intersection in Hilmar Rekstens vei and looks around. There is something about the figure.
106491.title_en: A Stranger in Hilmar Rekstens Vei

106506.excerpt_en: Two car drivers and one snowmobile driver have so far this year been investigated for drink-driving. That is half the total for 2007, when two snowmobile drivers and four car drivers were caught.
106506.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has already investigated three cases of drink-driving so far this year, compared with six in all of last year.

106512.excerpt_en: “Kari Bremnes’s production was extraordinary. She herself, the musicians, the music, the sound—it was magical,” says Lasse Stener Hansen.
106512.subtitle_en: Festival director Lasse Stener Hansen can finally breathe a sigh of relief after several hectic days. His greatest festival moment came with Kari Bremnes.

106548.excerpt_en: The first two trips are scheduled for April, with room for two students on each trip. There will then be a break until the end of the school year, before four or five trips may take place starting in the last week of June.
106548.subtitle_en: School students are invited to take part in research on ice and the seabed 250 kilometres north of Svalbard. The project is part of the International Polar Year, IPY, led by the Norwegian Centre for Science Education and the University of Bergen.

106551.excerpt_en: Over the course of one short, hectic week, 65 children and young people, together with instructors from Tromsdalen Kulturhus, improvised the performance. “When Kulta makes performances, we improvise and play with the various forms of expression within the performing arts.”
106551.subtitle_en: A whole crowd of children and young people filled the stage at Huset on Saturday, when Sirkus Svalnardo presented Creation, based on Norse mythology.

106563.excerpt_en: Ever since the 17 trappers spent an involuntary winter at Svenskhuset on Kapp Thordsen in 1872–73, the accepted view has been that they all died of scurvy. Senior physician Ulf Aasebø at the University of Tromsø and historian Kjell G. Kjær dispute this.
106563.subtitle_en: The researchers who were denied permission last year to open the 1873 grave at Svenskhuset are not giving up. They are now submitting a new application to find out why 17 trappers died.
106563.title_en: Still Seeking to Open the Grave

106590.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard gave its unqualified recommendation for the Longyearbyen Field Biology Association (LoFF) application for an eider sign by the dog kennels in Longyearbyen. The Norwegian Public Roads Administration sees no reason to introduce such a sign.
106590.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Public Roads Administration will not put up an eider sign by the dog kennels in Longyearbyen.
106590.title_en: Eiders Won’t Get Their Own Sign

106597.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified by people out on a dog-sledding trip that a polar bear was at the outer end of Adventdalen, between the dog kennels and Mälardalen, around noon on Saturday. Acting duty officer Inge Meløy followed the polar bear farther into the valley for a couple of hours by snowmobile, says chief police officer Olav Tombre.
106597.subtitle_en: A polar bear was spotted at the outer end of Adventdalen on Saturday afternoon.

106610.excerpt_en: All five bearded seals captured on Svalbard ten years ago have died; the last one died this autumn. “The first died very quickly, so it must have had a congenital weakness.”
106610.subtitle_en: Polaria in Tromsø is seeking permission to capture two bearded seals and four ringed seals for its aquarium.

106615.excerpt_en: Last autumn, Unis announced that it intended to use a hovercraft for research. The NOK 6.5 million craft was specially fitted out for use as a research vessel and financed by American marine geophysicist John Hall.
106615.subtitle_en: The Ministry of the Environment (MD) supports banning the use of hovercraft on Svalbard and has commissioned the Norwegian Directorate for Nature Management to draw up regulations.

106692.excerpt_en: At 11:40 Friday morning, the Governor of Svalbard was notified of a snowmobile accident at Kapp Laila. The man, who is in his 30s, was picked up by helicopter and flown to Longyearbyen Hospital.
106692.subtitle_en: A man in his 30s was taken to Longyearbyen Hospital with fractures after a snowmobile rollover at Kapp Laila.

106723.excerpt_en: ›› Birger Amundsen Herta does not like being photographed, and insists that the picture should be no bigger in Svalbardposten than a postage stamp. A small postage stamp.
106723.subtitle_en: Herta Grøndal has firmly etched her name into Svalbard’s history through her photographs. She is a tough, shy woman, with a mischievous streak just beneath the surface.

106763.excerpt_en: “We contacted three or four tour operators and offered both guides and guests the chance to take a breath test before getting on their snowmobiles. We checked around 100 people and didn’t get a single positive result,” says acting duty officer with the Governor of Svalbard, Inge Meløy.
106763.subtitle_en: Tourists and guides alike were checked for alcohol on Saturday morning before setting out on snowmobile trips. Around 100 people were checked.

106769.excerpt_en: The UNIS students had been on a trip to Austfjordnes and were due back in Longyearbyen on Sunday. When they were reported missing on Monday afternoon, the Governor sent out the Super Puma to search for them.
106769.subtitle_en: The two UNIS students reported missing on Monday afternoon have been found safe in Longyearbyen.

106773.excerpt_en: Roger Fossøy from Longyearbyen finished in 15th place after driving 500 kilometres in the Finnmarksløpet. The race started at 8.
106773.subtitle_en: Roger Fossøy of Longyearbyen Hundeklubb finished 15th in the Finnmarksløpet on Tuesday morning.

106791.excerpt_en: Without warning, the international transport company UPS stopped forwarding packages from abroad to Longyearbyen through Posten Norge this week. The reason is probably that UPS considers it too expensive to send packages to Svalbard.
106791.subtitle_en: If you are waiting for a package from abroad sent with UPS, you may have to wait a long time.

106794.excerpt_en: Last Friday, Linda Bakken, Oddbjørn Løkstad and Tommy Sandal agreed to spend a year trapping. Bakken and Løkstad will take over Mushamna in Woodfjorden, while Sandal will move to Austfjordnes in Wijdefjorden.
106794.subtitle_en: The Governor has decided who will be allowed to borrow the trapping cabins next season.

106810.excerpt_en: A dog team comes swooshing from Hiorthhamn across Adventdalen. The cold lies like a veil over the valley, snow whirls through the air, and the sky is clear and pale blue.
106810.subtitle_en: There is something about the sharp bite against soft skin. It increases blood circulation and accentuates the feminine. Polar air does something to people.

106816.excerpt_en: This is the fourth season that the French sailing boat “Vagabond” has spent frozen into the ice in Inglefieldbukta on Spitsbergen’s east coast.
106816.subtitle_en: Many people want to visit “Vagabond” in Inglefieldbukta. The Governor is allowing only one film crew this year.

106836.excerpt_en: Many people took advantage of the fine weather to go on trips this weekend, and snowmobile parties sped into the valleys. According to duty officer Trond Aagesen of the Governor’s Office, the first Easter weekend was quiet apart from a snowmobile accident in the Kapp Heer area.
106836.subtitle_en: Easter week began with plenty of sunshine and little wind. Despite heavy snowmobile traffic, only one accident has been reported.

106850.excerpt_en: The woman was part of a ski party and was taken to Longyearbyen in the vehicle belonging to the Longyearbyen Red Cross Rescue Corps, according to Chief Inspector Jill Gaustad of the Governor’s Office. Changed colour According to Tore Gauperaa, senior consultant at Longyearbyen Hospital, the woman is now doing well.
106850.subtitle_en: A female ski tourist was picked up in Janssondalen on Monday morning with frostbite on her toes.

106853.excerpt_en: “It has been a very quiet Easter, yes, incredibly quiet, without a single rescue incident. It has also been quiet at Longyearbyen’s licensed premises,” says duty chief inspector Petter Braaten of the Governor’s Office.
106853.subtitle_en: This year’s Easter holiday on Svalbard has been exceptionally quiet, without a single rescue operation. The weather has been very good, stable and cold.

106875.excerpt_en: The position of head of environmental protection has been vacant since former head Rune Bergstrøm left on 30 September 2007.
106875.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Justice has abandoned efforts to hire a new head of environmental protection at the Governor’s Office. The new legal adviser has also withdrawn.

106917.excerpt_en: The municipality said that Laila Rode, head of communications and service at Rakkestad Municipality, would become the new assistant governor. Her husband, Iver Henrik Rode, is director of Bydrift, and according to Rakkestad Municipality’s website, Laila Rode had decided to follow him to Svalbard.
106917.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, 1 April, Rakkestad Municipality announced who would succeed Assistant Governor Elisabeth B. Løvold.

106960.excerpt_en: “The pupils here in Longyearbyen essentially have no rights in Troms, only in their home counties. Under this agreement, they will also have rights in Troms,” says Anne Ellingsen, managing director of Oppvekstforetaket.
106960.subtitle_en: A partnership between Oppvekstforetaket and Troms County Municipality will secure more rights for pupils in Longyearbyen.

106965.excerpt_en: ›› Birger AmundsenHe is a meteorological consultant at the airport and works in the tower. From there, he can survey the broad landscape, towards the mouth of Isfjorden or inland across the long Adventdalen valley.
106965.subtitle_en: Not even the tiniest low-pressure system can sneak up on us without Torgeir Mørk noticing. He has his own weather whiskers and is sensitive to changes in pressure.
106965.title_en: The weatherman with his own weather whiskers

106991.excerpt_en: “It is the regulations introduced in the 1980s and 1990s that have caused pollutants such as PCBs, among others, to decline.”
106991.subtitle_en: While levels of legacy pollutants in Svalbard’s polar bears are falling, levels of emerging pollutants are rising. This is revealed in a report from the Barents Sea monitoring group.

107003.excerpt_en: It is bad at the far end of Road 238, but Hilmar Rekstens vei is certainly going to become thoroughly unpleasant too. Groundwork is already under way for a new residential development opposite Kroa.
107003.subtitle_en: Is it progress itself that makes people hell-bent on building houses right up against their neighbours’ steps? Case after case shows the result of poor political workmanship, combined with overzealous contractors plugging every last spot where a building can be squeezed in.

107044.excerpt_en: Last year, Gunn Randi Nordtømme and Stian Uhlen bought the gift shop Rebekkas Gave og Suvenir in the town-centre building in Longyearbyen. In January this year, the shop changed its name to Frisk Briis.
107044.subtitle_en: Frisk Briis, formerly known as Rebekkas Gave og Suvenir, has been subjected to extensive online fraud.

107046.excerpt_en: “It is normal for people to help one another here on Svalbard. Everyone takes their turn; I have always received help with my snowmobile or sled in Barentsburg when I have needed it,” says artist Olaf Storø.
107046.subtitle_en: Private individuals in Longyearbyen have launched a fundraising campaign for those injured and the relatives of the victims of the helicopter crash at Kapp Heer.

107053.excerpt_en: “We received the message at 12.30 on Thursday and sent three men over. The Russians have not requested assistance and are handling the firefighting with their own crews,” says Chief Superintendent Olav Tombre of the Governor’s Office.
107053.subtitle_en: One of the two coal miners missing in Barentsburg after a fire broke out in the mine on Thursday morning has been found dead. The rescue operation is still under way, with personnel from the Governor’s Office present.

107074.excerpt_en: The Directorate for Nature Management (DN) proposes extending the reindeer hunting season by 15 days. At present, reindeer hunting is permitted from 20.
107074.subtitle_en: The proposal for new harvesting regulations allows a longer reindeer hunting season, while imposing tighter restrictions on Arctic char management.

107081.excerpt_en: The politicians on the MNU were in complete agreement when they made their decision on Monday. They disagree with the Governor, who wants an expanded cultural heritage area in Sjøområdet.
107081.subtitle_en: The Environmental and Business Committee (MNU) rejects the Governor’s request to designate a larger part of Sjøområdet as historic buildings.
107081.title_en: Disagreement over cultural heritage in Sjøområdet

107099.excerpt_en: It has been barely three weeks since a Russian helicopter crashed at the Kapp Heer helicopter base, killing three people. Now the Russian mining town of Barentsburg has once again been hit by an accident.
107099.subtitle_en: The 47-year-old Russian who died in the mining accident in Barentsburg was sent to Tromsø on Friday. A Ukrainian man is still missing.
107099.title_en: The Dead Man Has Been Sent to Tromsø

107111.excerpt_en: The fire broke out at around 5 a.m. on Thursday in the coal mine, 450 metres underground, where 31 miners were working. It started at the production site, on the longwall face itself, and is believed to have been caused by ignited methane gas.
107111.subtitle_en: Putting out the fire in the Barentsburg mine is proving more difficult than first thought. The Governor of Svalbard has offered the Russians help, but Trust Arktikugol does not want assistance for now.

107144.excerpt_en: Two men were missing; one was found dead the same day, while the other has still not been found. Barely three weeks earlier, three men died in a helicopter crash at Kapp Heer.
107144.subtitle_en: Our Russian neighbours to the west have once again been hit by a serious accident. Last Thursday, a fire broke out deep inside the mine, 450 metres below ground.

107151.excerpt_en: ›› Birger Amundsen“Many tourists are very concerned about the weather and how they should dress, and it’s a little amusing to watch them once they’ve got everything on and are standing there in the thick down jacket—under the snowmobile suit.”
107151.subtitle_en: She stands there day in and day out, early and late, welcoming tourists who want to get out and let loose. It is a job that takes a woman.

107161.excerpt_en: “I think we will pass 400 participants in total,” says Per Krokan, head of Svalbard Turn. The competitors range in age from 16 to over 70.
107161.subtitle_en: More than 350 participants have registered for tomorrow’s ski marathon. It is a new participation record, according to Per Krokan.

107167.excerpt_en: According to chief police superintendent Olav Tombre of the Governor’s Office, it was a shooting suicide. “Two visitors found the woman at the lookout point above Taubanesentralen.”
107167.subtitle_en: A woman in her 20s was found dead near Platåfjellet on Thursday afternoon.

107170.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten redesigned the newspaper in 2007 and at the same time abandoned the front page it had used for 17 years. The change prompted some reactions among the newspaper’s readers.
107170.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten was awarded the Cover of the Year prize at the Norwegian Association of Local Newspapers’ annual meeting this weekend.

107201.excerpt_en: Or be tempted to do as Store Norske did and build yourself a shack or two in the mountains. If you are caught, lie low.
107201.subtitle_en: Some advice: Should you happen to do something terribly foolish while staying in Svalbard—such as being caught driving a snowmobile in areas closed to snowmobiles, repairing a damaged door at a protected cabin, tearing down walls and extending your house, however protected it may be.

107211.excerpt_en: “The event sells well. What will limit it is the number of beds available.”
107211.subtitle_en: Three hundred and ninety-nine skiers took part in the ski marathon on Saturday. Per Krokan now believes the event has reached its limit.

107213.excerpt_en: At around 12:30 p.m. on Saturday, a female tourist in her 50s drove into the building by the large dip at Kapp Heer. The woman was driving towards Barentsburg and gained so much speed after coming out of the dip that she crashed into the building behind it.
107213.subtitle_en: Two female snowmobile tourists were injured near Barentsburg over the weekend. One fell off her snowmobile; the other drove into a wall.

107219.excerpt_en: The Green in Practice Foundation (GRIP) has approved Svalbard Wilderness Centre and four other businesses as ecotourism enterprises. The ecotourism concept is comprehensive, focusing on offering memorable experiences and being a responsible ecotourism provider for guests, the environment and the local community.
107219.subtitle_en: Svalbard Wilderness Centre has been awarded the title “Approved Norwegian Ecotourism” as one of the first five tourism businesses in the country.

article_keywords_en: Norwegian Society for the Conservation of Nature
107235.excerpt_en: We note that he did not take the trouble to visit Svea. Solheim is, as is well known, a Socialist Left Party member and therefore practically obliged to oppose coal mining.
107235.subtitle_en: Minister of the Environment and International Development Erik Solheim made a brief visit to the archipelago last week, visiting Ny-Ålesund, Hornsund and Barentsburg.

107242.excerpt_en: “I have even found dog poop on the grating outside the entrance to Lompen Shopping Centre. In Gruvedalen, it is absolutely dreadful too.”
107242.subtitle_en: Many dog owners in Longyearbyen leave the mess behind when their best friend does its business. It can be hazardous to health.

107256.excerpt_en: “We were notified by the management of the Trust Arktikugol mine that the man was found dead during the night before Friday. The company says he most likely died from lack of oxygen.”
107256.subtitle_en: A 43-year-old Ukrainian miner died in the mine in Barentsburg on Friday. The Governor of Svalbard is investigating the death.

107265.excerpt_en: On Tuesday evening, Basecamp received permission from the Governor of Svalbard to retrieve «Noorderlicht» from Tempelfjorden. The boat was not to be taken out before the 17th at the earliest.
107265.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, KV «Svalbard» escorted the tourist boat «Noorderlicht» out of Tempelfjorden.

107282.excerpt_en: “As an important part of planning the Lunckefjell project, Store Norske wishes to carry out seam exposure at Marthabreen in summer 2008, specifically in the areas for the breakthrough from the Svea Nord mine and the entrance to the Lunckefjell mine,” Store Norske writes in its application to the Governor of Svalbard.
107282.subtitle_en: Store Norske wants to begin preparations for a new mine in Lunckefjellet as early as this summer.
107282.title_en: Wants to Start Work on New Mine

107304.excerpt_en: Two days before departure for Svalbard, owner and operator Henningsen Transport & Guiding (HTG) was told by the Norwegian Maritime Authority that the boat had to be upgraded to meet new requirements for an approved damage-stability report. HTG owner Stig Henningsen consequently feared the company would go bankrupt.
107304.subtitle_en: MS «Langøysund» has nevertheless been allowed to leave Tromsø, the owner says.

107310.excerpt_en: Both cases have their roots in what conditions were once like here in the north. It is a cliché, but also a truth: until just a few years ago, Longyearbyen was rather run-down.
107310.subtitle_en: The case against Jason Roberts, which is now going to trial, and the case taking shape around Oddny Kjerstad and what she has done since taking over the old provisions warehouse by the old quay, have much in common.

107330.excerpt_en: Crown Prince Haakon, Sweden’s Crown Princess Victoria and Denmark’s Crown Prince Frederik will visit Svalbard from the 21st to the 27th.
107330.subtitle_en: Royals from the three Scandinavian royal houses are coming to Svalbard next month and will visit Longyearbyen and Ny-Ålesund, among other places.

107332.excerpt_en: ›› Birger AmundsenThere is something defiant about the Coast Guard vessel «Svalbard», something angry. It is something about the grey war paint, the blunt hull and the angular shape.
107332.subtitle_en: Angry-looking, not particularly imposing and hardly eye-catching. But good Lord, when fully fired up, hardly anything can stand in its way.
107332.title_en: Norway’s Toughest — But Only on the Outside

107343.excerpt_en: The news agency Rosbalt Sever reports, according to FiskeribladetFiskaren, that Norway attempted to pressure a vessel belonging to the state Russian Fisheries Committee to leave Barentsburg. According to FiskeribladetFiskaren, there has been considerable diplomatic contact between Norway and Russia over the matter during the past week.
107343.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Coast Guard helped pressure the Russian fisheries inspection vessel “Mikula” to move away from Barentsburg.

107345.excerpt_en: Four snowmobiles were travelling south on the ice in Lomfjorden when the accident happened. All four men lived in Longyearbyen. They had been on a fishing trip on the north coast over the weekend and were returning to Longyearbyen when the accident occurred at around 4:30 p.m.
107345.subtitle_en: Karl Erik Wilhelmsen, 32, from Tromsø, died in a snowmobile accident in Lomfjorden on Sunday afternoon.

107352.excerpt_en: It was here at Myteberget by Faksevågen that the snowmobile accident which claimed Karl Erik Wilhelmsen’s life took place. Three snowmobiles went through the ice.
107352.subtitle_en: The picture shows the area where three snowmobiles went through the ice on Sunday.
107352.title_en: This is where the accident happened

107358.excerpt_en: The prosecutor, Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions Hans Tore Høviskeland, also believes Roberts should pay the legal costs. Defense counsel Harald Stabell, for his part, argued that Roberts should be acquitted, or alternatively dealt with as leniently as possible.
107358.subtitle_en: The criminal case against Jason Roberts concluded at Nord-Troms District Court on Thursday. The prosecutor sought 45 days’ suspended imprisonment and a NOK 50,000 fine.

107393.excerpt_en: “We have seen that no one has ever applied for a licence for Longyearbyen. Many areas smaller than Longyearbyen have radio,” says Thomas Giæver, managing director of Argus-Media AS, answering why the company wants to start up here specifically.
107393.subtitle_en: Argus-Media AS will launch a local radio station in Longyearbyen next January.
107393.title_en: Longyearbyen to get local radio station

107395.excerpt_en: There will be a major royal visit to Svalbard at the end of the month. Crown Prince Haakon, Swedish Crown Princess Victoria and Danish Crown Prince Frederik will arrive in Longyearbyen on 21 June.
107395.subtitle_en: In connection with the previously announced visit by Crown Prince Haakon, Crown Princess Victoria and Crown Prince Frederik, the Royal Palace announced today that Crown Princess Mette-Marit will also visit Longyearbyen.

107403.excerpt_en: We merely shrug and chuckle good-naturedly. What a life we lead, we lucky chosen few.
107403.subtitle_en: Naturally, we are not bothered by the snow still lying heavily around the landscape, by a few fresh snowflakes blowing past the other day, or by groups of tourists once again wandering in the middle of the road.

107437.excerpt_en: Nord-Troms District Court has also ordered Roberts to cover NOK 10,000 in the state’s legal costs. District Court Judge Unni Sandbukt writes in the judgment: “Roberts, without reasonable grounds, failed to acknowledge criminal liability and thereby incurred considerable public expense through extensive court proceedings in Svalbard.”
107437.subtitle_en: Jason Roberts has been fined NOK 60,000 for the illegal construction work at Taubanelageret.

107441.excerpt_en: (Video: Eirik Berger) “It is a mini-marathon for children that ran from the school to Huset, the old museum, across Museumsveien and back to the school. The entire course was about three kilometres long,” says Berit Hoel of Sparebanken Nord-Norge, which organized the race together with Svalbard Turn.
107441.subtitle_en: Seventy-five children took part in the Labb and Line race on Saturday. The organizer cannot remember so many having participated before. Watch video from the event here.
107441.title_en: Record number of children in mini-marathon

107447.excerpt_en: And at times wondered what genetic defect drives this polar pull. To be sure, there were many like-minded people who naturally asked themselves the same fundamental question: What am I doing here?
107447.subtitle_en: It is truly remarkable. For years we have clung on here as best we could, allowing ourselves to be battered by low-pressure systems and howling blizzards, by bone-chilling cold and sharp needle pricks.

107449.excerpt_en: There is something trusting about people who spend their free time staring across an apparently lifeless landscape, hoping to catch the tiniest glimpse of a bird—preferably a rarity, a rare species.
107449.subtitle_en: No sooner had they arrived in Svalbard than they made their first sensational observation: down by the shore, right in the middle of Longyearbyen, they spotted a Larus philadelphia.

107454.excerpt_en: “We do not want to compete with businesses over transporting researchers and providing field accommodation. Under the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act, accommodation facilities require permission from the environmental authorities, and the Governor does not want state cabins to be used commercially.”
107454.subtitle_en: Previously, researchers were allowed to use state cabins while working in the field. Now the Governor of Svalbard is putting an end to this practice.

107469.excerpt_en: The man was picked up by helicopter and taken to Longyearbyen Hospital. “It is only by chance that he was not seriously injured.”
107469.subtitle_en: A man drove off a nearly 500-metre-high cliff in Lunckefjellet yesterday morning.

107494.excerpt_en: In June last year, Trust Arktikugol allowed the film company Light House Films LTD to rent the Russian helicopter to look for filming locations. The film company was flown to a number of places, including Grøndalen, St.
107494.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol has been fined NOK 50,000 for an illegal helicopter flight last summer.

107496.excerpt_en: “Through the window, we saw a kayak capsize, and the duty officer went out by boat,” says Jill Gaustad, chief inspector with the Governor of Svalbard. According to duty officer Jon Erland Fløgstad, the rescue operation was carried out without drama.
107496.subtitle_en: Several kayaks were swept away by the wind in Adventfjorden on Wednesday. The Governor’s office went out by boat and picked up the paddlers.

107500.excerpt_en: The Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association (LJFF) has long worked to allow hunting of eider and barnacle geese in Svalbard. However, the draft harvesting regulations circulated for consultation this spring did not allow hunting of either species.
107500.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is proposing to the Norwegian Directorate for Nature Management that eider hunting should be permitted in Svalbard.

107516.excerpt_en: It was on 8 August last year that the Russian ship, carrying British tourists, was too close to the front of Storbreen at the head of Hornsund when the glacier calved.
107516.subtitle_en: Dutch shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions has been fined NOK 800,000 following last summer’s accident involving the tourist ship “Aleksey Maryshev” in Hornsund.

107523.excerpt_en: “I’m very happy about it. We have worked on this for a long time.”
107523.subtitle_en: Ulf Aasebø and Kjell Kjær have long wanted to open the grave at Svenskhuset on Kapp Thordsen to find out what the victims died of. Now they have been granted permission.
107523.title_en: Granted permission to open the grave after all

107539.excerpt_en: “Coal production is going very well at Svea Nord. So far this year, we have produced two million tonnes.”
107539.subtitle_en: Store Norske is selling coal worth NOK 2.5 billion this year and, for the first time in the company’s history, will be debt-free by year-end.

107541.excerpt_en: The man, who works on one of the charter boats in Longyearbyen, was heading ashore in Ymer Bay, at the mouth of Isfjorden, when the accident happened. According to Petter Braaten, duty chief inspector with the Governor of Svalbard, the man remained in the cold sea for 20 minutes while the boat circled him.
107541.subtitle_en: A man in his 60s was thrown overboard when the inflatable boat he was driving hit a chunk of ice in Ymer Bay on Tuesday morning.
107541.title_en: Man ends up in the sea in Ymer Bay

107561.excerpt_en: “He could not walk. He was bruised and in pain, but he was conscious,” said Governor’s Office duty officer Jon Erland Fløgstad on Wednesday.
107561.subtitle_en: A man in his 40s was picked up by helicopter and taken to Longyearbyen Hospital on Wednesday evening after crashing his paraglider at the foot of Sukkertoppen. The man is seriously injured and has now been flown to Tromsø.

107563.excerpt_en: Governor Per Sefland says the Governor’s Office has received notification from Trust Arktikugol that it will not accept the fine of NOK 50,000, but that the Governor’s Office has not looked into the matter further. “But I consider it likely that the matter will be reviewed by the courts in the usual way,” he says.
107563.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol refuses to accept the fine imposed for last summer’s illegal flight. There will probably now be a court case.

107573.excerpt_en: Christian Lydersen and Kit Kovacs, Norwegian Polar Institute/UNIS. Since January 2008, we have received support from the Research Council of Norway for a five-year study of the Svalbard harbour seal population. One result from our previous project on these seals was that they do not live particularly long up here.

107584.excerpt_en: “We have had three cancellations, but we will get all the passengers up today,” says Silje Våtvik of SAS Ground Services (SGS) in Longyearbyen. She says extra flights have been arranged for all departures, and SGS is now busy informing the travellers.
107584.subtitle_en: Three flights to Longyearbyen were cancelled because of fog overnight on Monday. Three extra flights will clear the backlog over the next 24 hours.

107610.excerpt_en: It is not yet clear what caused “Antarctic Dream” to run aground near Alkefjellet in Hinlopen Strait last Wednesday. “The captain has not yet been questioned.”
107610.subtitle_en: “Antarctic Dream” escaped with dents in its hull after running aground last week. The boat may continue sailing, but the Governor’s Office is investigating the case.

107612.excerpt_en: Renovation of the ground floor of the old museum building is already under way. The staircase to the top floor has been enclosed, a wall in the office has been demolished, and the main hall has been completely stripped.
107612.subtitle_en: The Spitsbergen Airship Museum will open in the old museum building in November. Among the visitors will be a grandchild of Umberto Nobile.
107612.title_en: Airship museum to open in November

107619.excerpt_en: It takes little for disagreements between Russians and Norwegians in Svalbard to acquire a political dimension. For a year, the trust’s helicopter use has been shuttled between the Russian state mining company Trust Arktikugol, the Civil Aviation Authority and the Governor’s Office.
107619.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol refuses to accept restrictions on helicopter use and believes Norway is violating the Svalbard Treaty. The government rejects the accusation.
107619.title_en: Russians in helicopter dispute with Norwegian authorities

107627.excerpt_en: “It will be a kind of supermarket selling all sorts of goods. It is also planned that people will be able to pay by credit card,” says director general Aleksander P.
107627.subtitle_en: The Russians are building a shopping centre in central Barentsburg that will be open to everyone. One of the town’s old buildings must make way for the centre.
107627.title_en: The Russians want to build a shopping centre

107665.excerpt_en: “The festival is based on the idea that people living in northern regions have much in common, and understand one another better than people from south and north or east and west,” says Marina Yuzhaninova, director of the Northern Traveling Film Festival. Yuzhaninova is based in St.
107665.subtitle_en: The international film festival in Barentsburg opens today with films from the Barents Region. The festival is open to everyone and ends on Wednesday.

107675.excerpt_en: Teachers Anne Jahren and Hilde Henningsen welcomed the new pupils around a large parachute in all the colours of the rainbow. After learning a new song and running beneath the parachute, the pupils learned where their bags should hang and found their new places in the classroom.
107675.subtitle_en: Twenty-one first-graders played and learned their way through their first day at Longyearbyen School on Wednesday.
107675.title_en: A playful first day of school

107685.excerpt_en: “The man became trapped between the rock wall and a machine,” chief police superintendent Jon Erland Fløgstad at the Governor’s Office told Svalbardposten. The accident occurred at 9:45 a.m. on Thursday, and the man was reportedly conscious when he was flown to hospital.
107685.subtitle_en: A 41-year-old man living in Longyearbyen was flown to the University Hospital in Tromsø after a workplace accident at Mine 7.

107687.excerpt_en: In a letter to the Norwegian Polar Institute, the Governor asks for help in improving the requirements for sailing in front of glacier fronts and icebergs. “This is not about introducing new legislation, but about better information on safe manoeuvring along glacier fronts,” says deputy governor Elisabeth B.
107687.subtitle_en: The Governor wants to impose new requirements on tourist vessels wishing to sail along Svalbard’s glacier fronts.

107689.excerpt_en: “The Russians think the idea is very interesting, and if we get the Governor’s approval, we will discuss the proposal further,” explains German national Hans Peter Neuber.
107689.subtitle_en: A German artist wants to take ten motorhomes carrying German tourists to Pyramiden next summer.

107713.excerpt_en: The accident occurred at around 1 p.m., when the 18-year-old was trapped while a shuttle car was being transported just over a kilometre into the main tunnel. “The man suffered minor shoulder injuries.”
107713.subtitle_en: An 18-year-old man suffered minor injuries in a workplace accident at Mine 7 on Wednesday afternoon.

107733.excerpt_en: “The reason the planes are so full this week is that we sold a great many discounted tickets this summer because of competition from Norwegian,” says SAS route manager Øystein Johansen. He says Norwegian had originally planned flights through September.
107733.subtitle_en: The chances of getting off the island over the next week are slim. All flights from Longyearbyen are sold out until September 12.

107736.excerpt_en: Admittedly, there has also been a steady stream of visitors to our northernmost Norway—exotic Svalbard—this summer. But the tourists are merely extras, here for a few hours or days before leaving again.
107736.subtitle_en: Unlike other tourist towns, which bustle with life in summer and go dormant when autumn arrives, Longyearbyen wakes up in September.

107763.excerpt_en: The 58-year-old blues musician James “Super Chikan” Johnson comes from Clarksdale, Mississippi, Notodden’s sister city. He is undoubtedly the biggest draw at this year’s blues festival in Longyearbyen.
107763.subtitle_en: Super Chikan is the main attraction at this year’s Dark Season Festival in Longyearbyen. Here is the full blues programme.

107791.excerpt_en: Engdahl’s fixed-term contract expires on November 1 next year, and he notified local council chair Kjell Mork in writing on Monday that he would not apply for an extension.
107791.subtitle_en: Sigmund Engdahl is stepping down as chief administrative officer of Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) on November 1 next year.

107814.excerpt_en: This year’s Arctic ice cover is just over 30 percent below the average for 1979–2000. According to the Norwegian Polar Institute (NP), the situation underscores the trend towards an increasingly ice-free Arctic in summer.
107814.subtitle_en: This year’s Arctic ice melt is the greatest since precise satellite measurements began in 1979.

107837.excerpt_en: “We found very high lead levels in the bone remains from the double grave. This indicates very high concentrations of lead in the trappers’ blood,” says senior consultant Ulf Aasebø at the University Hospital of North Norway in Tromsø.
107837.subtitle_en: The 17 trappers at Cape Thordsen had extremely high levels of lead in their skeletons. They probably died of lead poisoning.

107861.excerpt_en: White foam is pumped out from Hotellneset and drifts away from shore. Bydrift’s new boat, a Stridsbåt 90, comes to the rescue.
107861.subtitle_en: Bydrift has acquired a new boat, a Stridsbåt 90. On Wednesday, it took part in the oil-spill response exercise at Hotellneset.

107871.excerpt_en: It has taken longer than Bydrift expected to replace the seawater pumps at the power plant. According to Svalbardposten, well over one million litres of diesel have been used to fuel the backup power plant over the past six weeks.
107871.subtitle_en: A month of backup power has cost Bydrift many millions of kroner more than budgeted.
107871.title_en: Millions in Extra Costs for Bydrift

107876.excerpt_en: A lack of maintenance leads to deterioration and often requires ad hoc solutions, as at the power station in Longyearbyen. 25.

107883.excerpt_en: “At 9:45 p.m. on Monday, we received a message from a man in Longyearbyen. He was worried about a friend who had not returned from a boat trip,” says Senior Police Officer Roar Hilde of the Governor’s Office.
107883.subtitle_en: The alarm was raised on Monday evening when a man from Longyearbyen failed to return home from a boat trip to Diabas. He was found safe and sound at the Diabas cabin.

107887.excerpt_en: The man, who lives in Longyearbyen, was taken into police custody after demanding a knife from the Grillen restaurant because he intended to settle a score with someone outside. The drama unfolded at around 1 a.m. on Saturday.
107887.subtitle_en: A 28-year-old man ended up in custody early Saturday morning after causing trouble outside Grillen.

107901.excerpt_en: “We have provided some professional advice that the Longyearbyen Community Council may choose to follow, but we have also raised six objections that mean the plan cannot be approved,” says Arne Malme, the Governor’s chief environmental officer.
107901.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has several objections to the proposed new land-use plan for Longyearbyen and believes it cannot be approved.

107921.excerpt_en: “We were called by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre at 6:55 on Thursday morning and told that a Russian fisherman had injured his kneecap. The boat was southwest of Van Mijenfjorden, and this was purely an ambulance mission,” says Senior Police Officer Roar Hilde of the Governor’s Office.
107921.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard dispatched a helicopter on Thursday morning to collect an injured Russian fisherman.

107923.excerpt_en: Robert Hermansen stepped down as managing director of Store Norske on February 29, after nine years as the group’s top executive.
107923.subtitle_en: Watch NRK’s program about Robert Hermansen’s departure from Store Norske on online television!

107938.excerpt_en: “I’ve been arguing with the tax authorities in Bergen since 1977, and the whole thing has become complete nonsense. Now I’m more than fed up,” says trapper Harald Soleim, who lives at Cape Wijk.
107938.subtitle_en: Trapper Harald A. Soleim is reporting Bergen’s chief tax official for long-term harassment and repeated attempts at theft.

107960.excerpt_en: The SAS plane scheduled to land in Longyearbyen on Sunday had to turn back because of poor visibility. The aircraft made two landing attempts before giving up and returning to Tromsø.
107960.subtitle_en: SAS is putting on an extra flight to Longyearbyen on Monday after Sunday’s flight had to turn back because of bad weather.

107982.excerpt_en: Members of parliament and government ministers arrive in droves, and the Governor of Svalbard provides transport, whether aboard Nordsyssel or an Airlift helicopter. When Environment Minister Erik Solheim wants to go to Hornsund to see polar bears, the Governor gets the bill.
107982.subtitle_en: Everyone wants to visit Svalbard. Everyone wants to fly by helicopter and reach remote places where no one else is allowed to go.

107983.excerpt_en: At the request of the Ministry of the Environment, the Governor of Svalbard has prepared proposed amendments to the protection regulations for the Nordaust-Svalbard and Søraust-Svalbard nature reserves, and the Nordvest-Spitsbergen, Forlandet and Sør-Spitsbergen national parks. The proposal has now been circulated for consultation, with the deadline on the 10th.
107983.subtitle_en: Parts of Svalbard could be closed to tourists under the new protection regulations for Svalbard’s nature reserves and national parks.

108003.excerpt_en: “It will be exciting to begin this year’s tour in Svalbard,” say the three young people Ul-Juhán Partapuoli (20), Ina-Ristin Danielsen Gundersen (20) and Kristine Marie Inga (19). On Monday, they will visit Longyearbyen Upper Secondary School, where they will lecture on the Sámi language and literature, culture and identity.
108003.subtitle_en: On Monday, Longyearbyen School will be visited by three Sámi guides.

108017.excerpt_en: Jon Landvik is currently a professor of geology at the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (IPM) at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences (UMB) in Ås. The award citation emphasizes, among other things, his role in building up UNIS, where he worked for seven years.
108017.subtitle_en: The Fram Committee’s Nansen Award for 2008 goes to Jon Landvik, who was employed at UNIS for seven years.

108043.excerpt_en: As part of Store Norske’s reorganization, the company advertised the HSE director position at the beginning of July. Store Norske managing director Bjørn Arnestad urged Bjørn Martinsen, then head of the Longyearbyen Workers’ Association, to apply—and he did.
108043.subtitle_en: Bjørn Martinsen was forced out after two days as HSE director at Store Norske. Management is keeping a lid on the matter.

108049.excerpt_en: It is about doing the opposite of acting tactically: forgetting which hat one is wearing and which role one ought to play. When Store Norske director Bjørn Arnestad urged Bjørn Martinsen, then head of the Longyearbyen Workers’ Association, to apply for the position of HSE director, he stepped into a minefield.
108049.subtitle_en: Store Norske has got itself tangled up in a delicate matter. It concerns the famous hats—and how transparent Longyearbyen is.

108051.excerpt_en: As the winner, Longyearbyen School will be visited by Stian Barsnes Simonsen from NRK and artist Maria Haukaas Storeng.
108051.subtitle_en: Reindeer stew, spring rolls, performances and NOK 86,000 raised led Longyearbyen School to win the school competition in this year’s televised fundraising campaign.

108057.excerpt_en: This year’s campaign, which supports Blå Kors, has so far raised just over NOK 190 million. More than NOK 1 million of that came from Svalbard, making it the country’s most generous municipality.
108057.subtitle_en: So far, Svalbard has donated an average of NOK 614 per resident to this year’s televised fundraising campaign.

108094.excerpt_en: This year’s Dark Season Blues got underway across Longyearbyen at the same time, with concerts at Kroa, Svalbar and Barentz Pub. At Kroa, the music was provided by Super Chikan, Rita Engedalen and her band Backbone, and Billy Gibson.
108094.subtitle_en: Multitalented artist James “Super Chikan” Johnson got things started at Kroa as this year’s blues festival kicked off on Thursday evening.

108101.excerpt_en: Residents at the meteorological station on Hopen recently asked the Governor of Svalbard for help because the bear had prevented them from going outdoors. Among other things, it had made it difficult for them to shovel snow for drinking water.
108101.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, the Governor of Svalbard had to transport a troublesome female polar bear from Hopen to Edgeøya.

108121.excerpt_en: Either way, there is something reassuring about knowing that people live scattered around the archipelago. Even in the coldest polar night, warmth and light can be found in Austfjorden and Farmhamna, at Kapp Wijk and at the head of Woodfjorden.
108121.subtitle_en: Many people on Svalbard carry a trapper within them. Some dare to live out the dream; for others, it remains just a thought.

108128.subtitle_en: The trapping station at Mushamna will probably close next summer. Tight budgets are forcing the Governor of Svalbard to cut back.

108137.excerpt_en: On Wednesday last week, the Governor of Svalbard moved a female polar bear from Hopen to Edgeøya because the bear was preventing employees at the meteorological station from going outside. That same day, the station was visited by a new aggressive polar bear, which attacked one of the dogs outside.
108137.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, the Governor of Svalbard decided to euthanise yet another problem bear on Hopen.

108143.excerpt_en: “We are concerned about the artefacts. We want to store and conserve them.”
108143.subtitle_en: The Pomor Museum in Barentsburg is in such poor condition that it has been closed, and the artefacts have been removed. The Governor of Svalbard wants to take them over for the time being, but Trust Arktikugol has so far said no.
108143.title_en: Wants to Take Over Museum Artefacts

108152.excerpt_en: During the four days the blues festival lasted, 14 different concerts were held throughout Longyearbyen. See pictures from the blues concerts here!

Since 2004, he has written numerous letters to the editor of Svalbardposten, demanding answers as to why the Norwegian Polar Institute (NP) tags more polar bears every year.
108165.subtitle_en: Olav Vik Solheim believes polar bear tagging on Svalbard is so excessive that he has reported the Ministry of Climate and Environment to the police.

108173.excerpt_en: When smoke once again began billowing from the power station chimney on 25 September, Bydrift was able to calculate what replacing the seawater pumps at the power station had actually cost.

108173.title_en: A Huge Cost Overrun for Bydrift

108190.excerpt_en: The dense, intense colour is so beautiful it is almost unreal, making Hiorthfjellet look like an enormous set on an even larger theatre stage.
108190.subtitle_en: Winter has arrived, with frost, a few light snow flurries and the blue light.

108221.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is planning to tranquilise and remove a female polar bear with a cub that has been staying near the waste dump in Svea over the past week.

108240.subtitle_en: A week from Saturday, the first museum devoted to the history of airship expeditions towards the North Pole in the early 1900s will open.

108255.excerpt_en: “Sixty is an age people usually celebrate. That is when you start looking towards one hundred,” says Svalbardposten editor Birger Amundsen.
108255.subtitle_en: This month marks exactly 60 years since the first issue of Svalbardposten was published. The anniversary will be marked in several ways.

108263.excerpt_en: From being copied sheets pinned to the walls of barracks in Longyearbyen, Svalbardposten is now a newspaper distributed throughout the world. Of our 1,900 subscribers, 369 live on Svalbard; the rest live in mainland Norway or abroad.
108263.subtitle_en: Age is no disgrace, as the saying goes. And certainly not for a newspaper. The older it gets, the younger it looks, thanks to ever-improving technology and more advanced solutions.

108271.excerpt_en: The female polar bear with a cub that stayed at the waste dump at Kapp Amsterdam in Svea last week has been joined by several others of its kind. A total of eight different individuals were probably observed in Svea over the weekend.
108271.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard will nevertheless not tranquilise and relocate the polar bears staying at the waste dump in Svea. The reason is that there are too many bears.
108271.title_en: Too Many Polar Bears in Svea

108277.excerpt_en: “We know that the resource base is limited, and there is no pressure on us to produce at maximum capacity. We want to take a long-term view of the company and its jobs,” says Store Norske CEO Bjørn Arnestad.
108277.subtitle_en: Store Norske is cutting both production and staffing in the years ahead.

108280.excerpt_en: “We received a report at around 2 a.m. on Tuesday that an extremely intoxicated person had been seen outside,” says Senior Police Officer Roar Hilde of the Governor’s Office. The duty officer went out and took the man to the Governor’s drunk tank.
108280.subtitle_en: On the night before Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard had to collect a drunk man who had fallen asleep in the snow.
108280.title_en: Ended Up in the Drunk Tank
