108297.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is permitting continued year-round tourism operations at Isfjord Radio.

108328.excerpt_en: Since last year, the average price of coal has risen from 82 to 150 dollars per tonne, and Store Norske is increasing its turnover from NOK 1.8 billion to 2.8 billion.
108328.subtitle_en: Store Norske is on course for a result of between NOK 800 million and 900 million in 2008. Management is pleased.

108339.excerpt_en: Kings Bay launched a search early today after a French researcher failed to return to Ny-Ålesund as agreed. The researcher was supposed to travel to Ny-Ålesund from Corbel Station, a French satellite station east of the settlement.
108339.subtitle_en: A French researcher was reported missing on Monday morning after failing to return to Ny-Ålesund at the agreed time. That afternoon, he was found safe and sound in a crevasse south of Corbel Station.

108349.excerpt_en: This emerges from a new report published this week. It proposes abolishing the current special arrangement under which people who do not meet the requirement of 30 consecutive days on Svalbard nevertheless qualify for Svalbard tax.
108349.subtitle_en: Shift workers who travel to the mainland during their time off risk losing their right to Svalbard tax.

108365.excerpt_en: “This position is ideal for me, both in terms of the type of work and the location. Møre og Romsdal is my home county.”
108365.subtitle_en: Governor Per Sefland has applied for a job as County Governor of Møre og Romsdal.
108365.title_en: Applies for Job in Home County

108376.subtitle_en: Earlier spring in Norway is creating problems for migratory birds on Svalbard.

108390.excerpt_en: “This is the only warm office here. People say it’s a sauna, not an office,” Nataly Marchenko laughs as she sits down in the black office chair, which she has just learned has countless functions.
108390.subtitle_en: “I thought we might call this article: She Follows Her Husband with Great Pleasure,” says Nataly Marchenko (42).

108393.subtitle_en: The airline Norwegian will not operate flights to Longyearbyen next season.

108414.subtitle_en: Governor Per Sefland called for closer cooperation between the authorities and residents of Barentsburg at an information meeting in Barentsburg on Monday evening.

108416.subtitle_en: SAS is reviewing its schedule for the peak seasons after Norwegian decided not to fly to Svalbard next summer.

108434.excerpt_en: During the winter months, many Thai residents in Longyearbyen travel home on holiday. The international airport in Bangkok is now occupied, but it does not appear that Thai residents from Longyearbyen have been directly affected by the unrest.
108434.subtitle_en: In November and December, much of Longyearbyen’s Thai population travels home to Thailand on holiday. Now the airport in Bangkok is occupied.

108438.subtitle_en: The Office of the Auditor General criticizes the Ministry of Trade and Industry for focusing too much on money and too little on safety in Svea Nord.

108442.excerpt_en: “Before we can reach a solution, the trust needs to know exactly how the tax revenue from Barentsburg is intended to be used, and it must be used here in Svalbard,” says Aleksander P. Veselov, director general of Trust Arktikugol.
108442.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol has not decided whether to accept the new tax proposal, which will also apply to Barentsburg.
108442.title_en: “Must Know How They Will Be Used”

108459.excerpt_en: “I had no idea the volume of found-dead-wildlife cases was so high. We are working to obtain an overview of the scale and how we should deal with the issue.”
108459.subtitle_en: Trine Krystad is flooded with applications concerning found dead wildlife. In her office, she has a polar bear hide that she does not know what to do with.

108461.subtitle_en: The tourism industry in Longyearbyen is protesting the proposed changes to the protection regulations for national parks and nature reserves.

108466.subtitle_en: Putting the fox in charge of guarding the henhouse is never wise if the aim is to protect what is inside.

108478.excerpt_en: As tradition dictates, a large part of Longyearbyen’s population gathered at the old quay when “Nordsyssel” left Longyearbyen for the last time this year.
108478.subtitle_en: Sunday was time to say goodbye to “Nordsyssel” for the year. The first Sunday of Advent was marked at the same time.

108490.excerpt_en: It was this summer that the Governor began the extensive documentation project on trappers’ cabins in Svalbard. Prins Karls Forland, a long, narrow island between Isfjorden and Kongsfjorden, was chosen as the first area.
108490.subtitle_en: Nine cabins on Prins Karls Forland have been thoroughly documented in a new report commissioned by the Governor. None of the cabins will be preserved for posterity.

108492.excerpt_en: “It looks like it’s having a good flight,” says Professor Jøran Moen, who led the launch campaign. “How does it feel to have sent it up?”
108492.subtitle_en: The aurora rocket ICI-2 lifted off into space shortly after 11:30 a.m. on Friday.

108501.excerpt_en: Marianne Prytz Lund in Farmhamna sees no other solution than shooting her six polar dogs because of the lack of space in Longyearbyen. Prytz Lund lives in Farmhamna, just north of Isfjorden, with her husband Hans Lund and two daughters.
108501.subtitle_en: The shortage of space is having consequences for dog owners in Longyearbyen. The local council is demanding that one kennel be removed, while another owner wants to shoot all her dogs.

108521.excerpt_en: “We had an ambulance call on Sunday afternoon. A man had crushed his hand and was flown to Longyearbyen Hospital for treatment,” says acting Governor’s senior police officer Jill Gaustad.
108521.subtitle_en: A man was flown by helicopter from Svea to Longyearbyen on Sunday afternoon with a crush injury.

108530.excerpt_en: “The blue hour is over now, and we have to hurry so we can get out of Blue Mountain before it closes,” says Anne Jahren, a teacher at Longyearbyen School, after the performance has ended.
108530.subtitle_en: The pupils at Longyearbyen School have recreated the world of the popular TV series Christmas in Blue Mountain.

According to UNIS, the project has an investment budget of NOK 400 million and an annual operating budget of NOK 70–80 million.
108533.subtitle_en: The European Strategy Forum on Research Infrastructures (ESFRI) has approved Svalbard as an international platform for environmental and climate monitoring.

108537.excerpt_en: On Wednesday evening, 19 Thai residents turned up at Næringsbygget in Longyearbyen to talk to the researchers who published the article “No Trees in Sight—Thai Life in Permafrost.” The Thai residents were given the article in their own language and are outraged that it was published.
108537.subtitle_en: Thai residents are upset about how they are portrayed in the article collection “Life in Longyearbyen,” launched on Tuesday.

108554.subtitle_en: A car ran off the road near Svalbard Airport on Thursday afternoon.

108564.excerpt_en: The Ministry of the Environment (MD) has begun work on amending the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act.
108564.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard and the Norwegian Directorate for Nature Management (DN) want significantly stricter cabin regulations and to close Bolterdalen to snowmobile traffic.

108566.subtitle_en: Bjørnøya Nature Reserve was expanded on Friday as part of the government’s efforts to protect the environment in the Barents Sea and Svalbard.

108651.subtitle_en: Governor of Svalbard Per Sefland did not get the position of county governor of Møre og Romsdal. The decision was made in the Council of State.

108682.subtitle_en: Christmas has been very peaceful in Svalbard this year, as in previous years. Weather conditions have varied, with periods of strong winds and heavy snow.

108692.excerpt_en: “When the owner woke up, the fur was gone. The owner found out where it was, and based on that we were able to determine who had stolen it,” says senior police officer Petter Braaten of the Governor’s office.
108692.subtitle_en: A man living in Longyearbyen, who was intoxicated, stole a fur coat from a house during the night before Tuesday.

108703.excerpt_en: Noorderlicht was scheduled to head for Tempelfjorden, where it is to freeze into the ice, at the beginning of the week.
108703.subtitle_en: The sailing ship Noorderlicht has frozen in—but in the wrong fjord.

108709.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard adopted the 2009 Regulations on Arctic Char Fishing in Svalbard. They allow net fishing in four lakes around Isfjorden—three more than in 2008 and than under the draft regulations circulated for consultation a month ago.
108709.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is allowing net fishing in three new lakes under this year’s Arctic char regulations.

108712.excerpt_en: “We patrolled from ten last night until three this morning, but it was quiet and peaceful.”
108712.subtitle_en: New Year’s celebrations in Longyearbyen and elsewhere in Svalbard proceeded peacefully amid optimal, cold weather conditions.

108731.excerpt_en: “We have received many good applications. About half are unqualified due to insufficient education, but among those remaining there are six or seven strong candidates, and at least four or five have solid management experience,” says head of environmental protection Arne Malme.
108731.subtitle_en: It appears that the Governor of Svalbard will finally succeed in finding a new head of environmental protection. Twenty-eight people have applied for the position.
108731.title_en: Many want to become head of environmental protection

108740.excerpt_en: The sun is on schedule and is expected to appear above the horizon at the end of February this year as well. Around 21.
108740.subtitle_en: On Saturday, a streak of sunlight was observed in the southern sky at Agardhbukta.

108754.excerpt_en: Last autumn, Roberts was fined NOK 60,000 and ordered to pay a further NOK 10,000 in legal costs by the North Troms District Court for illegal construction work at Taubanelageret. The listed building is owned by Roberts and is located at Skjæringa in Longyearbyen.
108754.subtitle_en: The appeal case against Jason Roberts began in the Hålogaland Court of Appeal in Tromsø on Wednesday. The prosecution argued that the district court sentence was too lenient and appealed the verdict.

108756.excerpt_en: “We have had a New Year’s baby here in Svalbard too. It was a twin birth that came a little early, so they were born here at the hospital.”
108756.subtitle_en: A boy and a girl were born at Longyearbyen Hospital on Saturday afternoon. At 3:40 p.m. on Saturday, Berit Oldernes and Tore Hoem became parents to a 2,160-gram boy and a 1,740-gram girl.

108760.excerpt_en: “We have been in contact with KV Svalbard, which has agreed to break through the ice for us so that we can get out of Adventfjorden and into Tempelfjorden.”
108760.subtitle_en: The Coast Guard has agreed to break a channel through the ice for Noorderlicht. If all goes according to plan, the vessel will be in Tempelfjorden by the weekend.
108760.title_en: KV Svalbard breaks through the ice

108777.excerpt_en: A tiny girl and a slightly larger boy were born in Longyearbyen on Saturday afternoon, more than six weeks premature. The babies were well developed, but were flown by air ambulance to the University Hospital of North Norway after birth.
108777.subtitle_en: These are the two little ones born at Longyearbyen Hospital on Saturday.

108783.excerpt_en: “The Governor wanted a stronger professional basis for assessing a safe distance from glacier fronts,” says Stein Tore Pedersen, tourism adviser to the Governor of Svalbard. In summer 2007, 23 British tourists were injured when Storbreen in Hornsund calved.
108783.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard recommends keeping 200 metres away from calving glacier fronts following a report by the Norwegian Polar Institute (NPI).

108796.excerpt_en: This week, Sand informed staff that UNIS must make major cuts in the 2009/2010 academic year. “We will have to remove 12 of the 30 subjects from the course catalogue from autumn 2009. This means reducing the number of student-years from 140 in 2008 to 120 this autumn,” Sand explains.
108796.subtitle_en: Twelve subjects and five full-time positions will disappear from UNIS this autumn. Gunnar Sand fears this could lead to fewer applications.

108807.excerpt_en: “We will probably fly out by helicopter in the last week of March and work on mapping polar bear dens until the end of April,” says Jon Aars, who leads the Norwegian Polar Institute's (NP) polar bear research.
108807.subtitle_en: Researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute are resuming den surveys on Kongsøya after a 24-year hiatus. At the same time, a base is being established on Barentsøya for future polar bear research.
108807.title_en: Polar Bear Researchers Head to Kong Karls Land

108809.excerpt_en: “The aircraft landed without difficulty in the normal manner,” says duty senior police officer Jill Gaustad. She says the pilots' report of a landing-gear problem turned out to have been caused by a faulty indicator light.
108809.subtitle_en: Police, fire and hospital crews were dispatched when an aircraft operated by Lufttransport reported a landing-gear problem before landing in Longyearbyen on Sunday evening.

108816.excerpt_en: After spending several hours carefully breaking up the ice around the guest quay in Longyearbyen, KV ‘Svalbard’ was able to tow the sailing ship ‘Noorderlicht’ away from the quay. At around 3:30 p.m., the Coast Guard and the sailing ship set course for Tempelfjorden, where ‘Noorderlicht’ is to freeze in.
108816.subtitle_en: On Saturday afternoon, the Coast Guard vessel KV ‘Svalbard’ helped the sailing ship ‘Noorderlicht’ out of Adventfjorden.

108853.excerpt_en: This week, the Community Council's administration committee recommended taking out a NOK 3.3 million loan for the port authority's 2009 investment budget. “At present, we do not have the capacity to handle the growing number of expedition and cruise ships satisfactorily,” explains harbourmaster Kjetil Bråten.
108853.subtitle_en: New equipment costing NOK 3.3 million will increase capacity at Longyearbyen port. Necessary, says the harbourmaster.

108859.excerpt_en: Under the regulations, leaving a car unnecessarily idling is not permitted, but some Longyearbyen residents do not appear to care about the ban. Nygaard says the Governor's Office has received complaints about cars idling outside Svalbardbutikken, the airport terminal and the kindergartens.
108859.subtitle_en: “We do not condone idling, even when it is cold outside,” says Senior Police Officer Erik Nygaard of the Governor's Office.

108879.excerpt_en: According to the guestbook at Fredheim, the Crown Prince's family stayed at Hilmar Nøis's old trapping station, Villa Fredheim, from June 17 to 4.
108879.subtitle_en: This summer, the Crown Prince's family stayed for several weeks at the former trapping station Fredheim. The holiday photos have now been released.

108881.excerpt_en: “A fish reception facility would make it easier for Russian fishing vessels to land their catches, since it is only an hour from the fishing grounds to Barentsburg. The facility would also secure jobs for Russians in Barentsburg,” Fisheries Committee chairman Andrej Krajnij said, according to Russian news agency RIA Novosti.
108881.subtitle_en: Russian authorities want to complete the design work for the planned fish reception facility in Barentsburg during the year.
108881.title_en: Barentsburg Could Get Fish Reception Facility

108885.excerpt_en: Svalbard Museum set a new visitor record in 2008. Nearly 30,000 visitors stopped by.
108885.subtitle_en: Svalbard Museum set a new visitor record in 2008. Nearly 30,000 visitors stopped by.

108902.excerpt_en: The coal price swung from top to bottom in a very short time. In 2007, Store Norske received an average of 82 dollars per tonne of coal; in 2008, it was 160 dollars—around NOK 1,000.
108902.subtitle_en: Last year Store Norske received NOK 1,000 per tonne for coal. Now the price has fallen by half, and the coal company is losing money on every tonne produced.

108905.excerpt_en: “I've always enjoyed both drawing and writing. It was nice to have something to occupy myself with,” says Arne Nøis.
108905.subtitle_en: For three winters, Arne Nøis trapped with his father, Edvin Nøis. With his sketchbook, he documented everyday life and trapping methods.
108905.title_en: Drew Life on the Trapping Line

108911.excerpt_en: “Due to the financial situation, UNIS is currently unable to enter into an agreement to take over the researchers' guesthouse,” says UNIS director Gunnar Sand. Piling began last week on the site just below the Polar Hotel, where the controversial researcher hotel is to be built.
108911.subtitle_en: UNIS cannot afford to buy the new researcher hotel in the town centre. Nevertheless, piling work on the site is well under way.

108923.excerpt_en: Last summer, Jason Roberts was fined NOK 60,000 but received no prison sentence by the Nord-Troms District Court. He was punished for illegal construction work on the protected cableway depot in Longyearbyen, as well as extensive groundworks immediately beside Taubanesentralen, which is also protected.
108923.subtitle_en: The Court of Appeal has increased the sentence handed down by the District Court, sentencing Jason Roberts to 21 days' suspended imprisonment and a NOK 50,000 fine.

108954.excerpt_en: The Community Council is reversing its 2006 decision to allow three-storey residential buildings at Elvesletta Syd. When it considered the detailed plan for the B1 and B2 areas of Elvesletta Syd on Tuesday, the unanimous council said it did not want more than two storeys in the area.
108954.subtitle_en: The Community Council no longer wants three-storey buildings at Elvesletta Syd after all.

108974.excerpt_en: The fire broke out in the mine at around five o'clock in the morning on April 17 last year.
108974.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has fined Trust Arktikugol NOK 500,000 for the fire that broke out in the mine in Barentsburg last April.

108977.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has summarized the consultation on proposed changes to the protection regulations for the eastern protected areas. Under the proposal, most of Nordaustlandet, Edgeøya and Barentsøya would be off-limits to everyone except researchers.
108977.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard recommends that tourists from expedition cruise ships should still be allowed to travel freely in the eastern protected areas of Svalbard.

108996.excerpt_en: For the first time, all 120 passes put on sale for the festival have sold out. By Wednesday afternoon, only tickets for Friday evening remained.
108996.subtitle_en: This year's Polarjazz festival opened last night after excellent advance sales despite problems with the ticketing system.

109003.excerpt_en: “Ugh, it stinks here!” “It smells like a pigsty!” “It smells like sweaty feet!”
109003.subtitle_en: The children at Polarflokken kindergarten stared in amazement when they saw what happens to the rubbish they throw away.
109003.title_en: Kindergarten Goes on a Rubbish Hunt

109016.excerpt_en: “I'm still rebellious enough to play a Grand Prix song at a jazz festival,” a cheerful Bjørn Eidsvåg chuckled from the stage at the Polar Hotel.
109016.subtitle_en: Bjørn Eidsvåg flirted with the audience and got several rounds of sing-along going during Thursday evening's concert.

109018.excerpt_en: For the second year in a row, Ivan Marchenko charmed the judges with his classical guitar playing and advanced to the UKM county showcase in Finnsnes. “You have an incredibly confident and accomplished style.”
109018.subtitle_en: Four acts advanced to the county showcase from the Norwegian Youth Cultural Festival (UKM) at Huset last Saturday.

109028.excerpt_en: The four women in the Norwegian band Katzenjammer took the stage at the Polar Hotel after Åge Alexandersen and Mikael Wiehe had captivated everyone with their acoustic concert.
109028.subtitle_en: Things got pretty wild at the Polar Hotel during this year's Polarjazz festival when Katzenjammer took the stage.

109034.excerpt_en: “We’re not used to this kind of crime here in Longyearbyen, and I think it’s deeply regrettable that it has happened,” says Petter Braaten, chief inspector at the Governor of Svalbard’s office. He says the vandals damaged the kitchen entrance door at Kroa and broke the shovel they used to try to get inside.
109034.subtitle_en: Someone tried to break into Kroa using a sledgehammer and shovel early Tuesday morning.

109053.excerpt_en: A wide lead opened in the ice outside Fredheim last week, extending inland toward Kapp Schoultz on the southern side of Tempelfjorden.
109053.subtitle_en: Last weekend, Basecamp had to cancel the event on “Noorderlicht” because of an open lead in the ice on Tempelfjorden.

109060.excerpt_en: A police support package allocates NOK 252 million, allowing 460 new civilian positions to be created in the police service. In addition, staff positions included in the 2009 national budget will bring the total increase in police staffing this year to 710 positions.
109060.subtitle_en: Governor Per Sefland is unhappy that none of the many civilian positions being added to the police by the government will go to Svalbard.
109060.title_en: Unhappy with the Ministry of Justice

109062.excerpt_en: “We don’t have the full overview of all costs yet, but based on what we see so far, we certainly won’t run a deficit. In terms of ticket sales, we exceeded the targets we set in the budget by more than we had hoped,” says Lasse Stener Hansen.
109062.subtitle_en: Polarjazz organizers expect to make a profit after last weekend’s festival.
109062.title_en: Festival Organizers Pleased with the Jazz

109086.excerpt_en: Ever since coal mining ended and Pyramiden was emptied in 1998, plans for activities there have circulated. Over the years, decay has taken its toll, while tourists and other visitors have vandalized the site and stolen various movable items.
109086.subtitle_en: The Russians plan to open Pyramiden to tourism, but are being held back by the Governor of Svalbard, who has imposed strict environmental requirements.
109086.title_en: Russians Want Tourists to Visit Pyramiden

109103.excerpt_en: The atmosphere in the cinema auditorium at Huset is nervous and slightly frantic shortly before the audience is admitted to the first of two performances. “Is it ready backstage, is it ready backstage—can we let people in?” shouts Bente Reibo ten minutes before the circus performance is due to begin.
109103.subtitle_en: Sirkus Svalnardo thrilled audiences at Huset last Saturday—and the cultural director most of all. There and then, he promised that the collaboration with Kulta would continue.

109105.excerpt_en: The woman was taking part in an organized snowmobile trip to Barentsburg, and the accident happened as the group was leaving town. “The accident was probably caused by the woman being unfamiliar with the snowmobile and pressing the accelerator instead of the brake. It happened when she was driving out of the parking area and onto the road,” says Jill Gaustad, chief inspector at the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
109105.subtitle_en: A Norwegian woman, 59, suffered a spinal fracture in a snowmobile accident in central Barentsburg on Sunday.

109111.excerpt_en: “Since last year, Basecamp Spitsbergen has increased bed capacity at our outposts, including by using Isfjord Radio,” says Geir Arne Månum, general manager of Basecamp Spitsbergen. Basecamp’s Fangstmannshotellet currently has 42 beds in 16 rooms.
109111.subtitle_en: A new extension will give Basecamp’s Fangstmannshotellet more beds.

109123.excerpt_en: At the end of August, KNM “Tyr” and KV “Harstad” will depart from Tromsø to search for Roald Amundsen, who crashed with the flying boat “Latham” in 1928. NRK reports this on its website.
109123.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Navy is launching new searches for Roald Amundsen and the flying boat “Latham.”

109128.excerpt_en: “The man probably suffered a blow to his helmet while bolting, which resulted in a neck injury,” says Terje Carlsen, communications director at Store Norske.
109128.subtitle_en: A miner suffered neck injuries in a rock-bolting accident in Svea early Wednesday morning.
109128.title_en: Taken to Hospital with Neck Injuries

109795.excerpt_en: Because production at Mine 7 has stopped, coal for the power plant is being taken from the stockpile at Hotellneset. The coal is uncovered and full of snow and ice.
109795.subtitle_en: The cause of last night’s prolonged power outage was excessive snow and ice in the coal from Mine 7.
109795.title_en: Poor Coal Quality Caused Power Failure

109844.excerpt_en: Following a presentation by LNS Spitsbergen (LNSS) at Tuesday’s local council meeting, the politicians voted to reverse the decision made at the previous council meeting.
109844.subtitle_en: The local council now supports allowing three storeys at Elvesletta Syd after all.

109847.excerpt_en: The woman was skiing with a colleague and borrowed dogs several kilometres outside Ny-Ålesund when the accident occurred on Saturday afternoon. She fell and fractured her ankle, and her colleague contacted the watchman in Ny-Ålesund by Iridium phone and requested assistance.
109847.subtitle_en: A woman underwent surgery at Longyearbyen Hospital over the weekend for an ankle fracture sustained in a skiing accident in Ny-Ålesund.

109855.excerpt_en: “The man was getting into the wheel loader when the wind caught the vehicle’s door and struck him, causing him to fall,” says Olav Rusten, construction manager in Svea. The accident happened at around 10 a.m. on Tuesday.
109855.subtitle_en: A man in his 40s was injured when the door of the wheel loader he was getting into was blown into him by strong winds.

109868.excerpt_en: Last year, the Russian company was fined NOK 50,000 for an illegal helicopter flight with a Russian film company in the Isfjorden area. The Russians refused to accept the fine, so the case is now going to court.
109868.subtitle_en: The trial against Russian company Trust Arktikugol begins in Longyearbyen on Monday following the illegal helicopter flight in the summer of 2007.

109915.excerpt_en: “There has been a little bear traffic over the weekend. On Friday, a big bear passed Bjørndalen and Vestpynten.”
109915.subtitle_en: Polar bears have appeared in the area around Longyearbyen in recent days, says duty deputy chief of the Governor of Svalbard’s office, Petter Braaten.

109935.excerpt_en: “I think it’s fun to sail on a sheet. I’ve done it before, but not that many times,” says Sigri Steen.
109935.subtitle_en: There was plenty of action on the sledding hill below the Polar Hotel on Thursday. There was activity inside the library too, where the children made the sun itself.
109935.title_en: Fun and Games with Sleds and Glue

109942.excerpt_en: This emerged when the government presented the second stage of its High North initiative in Tromsø today, with five ministers present. “In recent years, there has been increased shipping—and particularly cruise traffic—around Svalbard. Unlike along the Norwegian coast, there is no AIS coverage in the waters around Svalbard.”
109942.subtitle_en: The government is considering introducing automatic identification systems (AIS) for shipping around Svalbard.
109942.title_en: Government Wants to Control Ship Traffic

110009.excerpt_en: The flight from Oslo to Longyearbyen on Wednesday was unable to land to pick up passengers and cargo in Tromsø, and instead had to land at Harstad Airport, Evenes, to refuel. “The plane is scheduled to land in Longyearbyen at around quarter to four, so we hope to be able to take off …”
110009.subtitle_en: Heavy snowfall in Tromsø is causing delays for flights to and from Longyearbyen.

110016.excerpt_en: The delegates were highly satisfied with the final declaration when the international polar bear meeting concluded in Tromsø today. WWF Canada was also very pleased with the outcome of the three-day meeting, expressing surprise that the declaration was so clear about the climate threat.
110016.subtitle_en: The final declaration from the polar bear meeting in Tromsø states that climate change is the most serious long-term threat to polar bears.
110016.title_en: Climate Change Is the Greatest Threat to Polar Bears

110039.excerpt_en: At around 3:30 p.m., one person was picked up at Kapp Heer near Barentsburg. “One person braced themselves with one leg when the snowmobile overturned,” says Trond Aagesen, the Governor’s duty senior police officer. Not serious. Later that afternoon, a snowmobile passenger had to be picked up at Hollendarbukta.
110039.subtitle_en: The Governor’s helicopter was dispatched on two ambulance missions on Saturday afternoon.

110041.excerpt_en: Ivar Undheim will become the new chief administrative officer of Longyearbyen Local Council. At Tuesday evening’s local council meeting, it was announced that Ivar Undheim (54) will be Longyearbyen Local Council’s new chief administrative officer.
110041.subtitle_en: Ivar Undheim will become the new chief administrative officer of Longyearbyen Local Council.
110041.title_en: New Chief Administrative Officer Takes Office

110044.excerpt_en: “The latest report says the ice is up to 70 centimetres thick in some places in Adventfjorden. It would not be safe for us to sail in, even with assistance from KV ‘Svalbard’,” says Karl Henrik Karlsen, district manager at Bring, formerly Nor-Cargo.
110044.subtitle_en: The cargo ship ‘Norbjørn’ will not reach Svalbard as planned on Monday because of the ice conditions.

110077.excerpt_en: The three left Svea at 4:40 p.m. to travel to Longyearbyen. The woman, who is in her 30s, was riding in the middle and disappeared on Gruvfonna just north of Svea.
110077.subtitle_en: Crews from the Governor’s Office and the Red Cross are searching for a female snowmobile driver who left Svea this afternoon with two other Svea workers.

110110.excerpt_en: “All four are safe and sound, and no one has been injured,” says Liv Asta Ødegaard, communications adviser at the Governor’s Office. The four made telephone contact with the Governor’s Office and reported their position.
110110.subtitle_en: The four snowmobile drivers who were missing near Svea Nord have been picked up by the Governor’s Super Puma helicopter.

110114.excerpt_en: “In any case, I would have had to leave by September 2010 at the latest, when my fixed-term appointment expires. That is why I have chosen to leave this autumn.”
110114.subtitle_en: There will be major staff changes at the Governor’s Office this year. Governor Per Sefland is one of five people stepping down.

110119.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Trade and Industry is supporting the Arctic nature guide programme with one million kroner, thereby securing its launch this autumn. “We’re getting one million? That’s fantastic,” says tourism manager Unni Myklevoll, the programme’s project manager. “I’ve also received a surprisingly positive message from the Polar Affairs Department at the Ministry of Justice.”
110119.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Trade and Industry is supporting the Arctic nature guide programme with one million kroner, thereby securing its launch this autumn.

110130.excerpt_en: Bydrift needs to supplement steam production in order to produce enough steam to run the turbines at Energiverket at full capacity.
110130.subtitle_en: Bydrift will see whether the furnaces at the old power station can be used to produce extra steam for Energiverket. The furnaces will be fired up Wednesday between noon and 1 p.m.
110130.title_en: Firing Up the Old Power Station

110146.excerpt_en: Shortly after 12:30 p.m. Wednesday, smoke began billowing from the chimney at the old power station.
110146.subtitle_en: There was plenty of smoke when Bydrift tested the furnaces at the old power station on Wednesday.

110165.excerpt_en: Three highly excited pupils arrived at headteacher Tove Steig’s office on Tuesday without knowing why they had been summoned. Governor Per Sefland arrived with the drawings in hand and told the three pupils that the decision had been made and that they were the lucky winners of the drawing competition.
110165.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Justice has selected three winners of the school’s drawing competition to adorn the white paper on Svalbard.
110165.title_en: Set to Adorn the Svalbard White Paper

110179.excerpt_en: “We received a report at around six o’clock Sunday morning that three intoxicated people were trying to start a snowmobile at Lompensenteret. We went out and stopped them,” says Jill Gaustad, the Governor’s duty senior police officer.
110179.subtitle_en: The weather in Svalbard was brilliant and cold on Saturday and Sunday. Police reported an injured polar bear and an attempted snowmobile theft.

110184.excerpt_en: At 3:20 p.m. Tuesday, the Governor’s Office was informed by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre that an emergency beacon had been activated near Camp Morton. Helicopter on the way: The Governor’s Super Puma helicopter is heading to the area with medical personnel on board.
110184.subtitle_en: An emergency beacon has been activated in the area near Camp Morton by Van Mijenfjorden.

110198.excerpt_en: According to senior police officer Jill Gaustad of the Governor’s Office, the office was contacted by guides both on Good Friday and earlier in the week. “They reacted to snowmobile drivers appearing to seek out and disturb polar bears on Tempelfjorden,” she says.
110198.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office has received reports that snowmobile drivers actively sought out and disturbed polar bears on Tempelfjorden.
110198.title_en: Seeking Out Polar Bears on Tempelfjorden

110210.excerpt_en: “At 1:30 p.m., we were called by the crew of the ‘Vagabond’. They were on the sea ice at Inglefieldbukta and were going to collect research samples as usual, but because of a five-metre-wide lead, they could not get back,” says senior police officer Jill Gaustad of the Governor’s Office.
110210.subtitle_en: Four rescue and ambulance missions were carried out in the storm on Easter Eve. A fifth operation was called off just before the rescue crews were dispatched.

110231.excerpt_en: “One person had suffered frostbite, and the doctor decided that all five should be flown back to Longyearbyen because they were cold and wet. The doctor wanted to take them to the hospital for a check-up,” says senior police officer Trond Aagesen of the Governor’s Office.
110231.subtitle_en: Five ski tourists had to be collected by helicopter from Lomonosovfonna on Wednesday afternoon.
110231.title_en: Five Frozen Ski Tourists Had to Be Picked Up

110263.excerpt_en: “The Spaniards called our duty phone themselves at around 6 p.m. Friday and asked to be evacuated. It was nearly 30 degrees below zero, with a bitter northerly wind, when we landed,” says senior police officer Inge Meløy of the Governor’s Office.
110263.subtitle_en: Two Spanish ski tourists were picked up by the Governor’s rescue helicopter on Friday afternoon at Trebrepasset, just west of Newtontoppen.

110269.excerpt_en: “A visiting woman suffered an upper-arm fracture after losing control of her snowmobile near Forskningsparken on Sunday evening,” says senior police officer Petter Braaten of the Governor’s Office. The woman became trapped between the snowmobile and a shed beside the snowmobile trail near the building. “The woman was taken to Longyearbyen Hospital,” Braaten explains.
110269.subtitle_en: The Governor was notified of numerous incidents on Sunday evening.
110269.title_en: Broken Arm, Snowmobile Fire and Walk on the Ice

110276.excerpt_en: In the judgment handed down today, the district court writes: “The court finds that a corporate penalty shall be imposed, and sets the penalty at a fine of NOK 50,000, in accordance with the indictment.”
110276.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol lost in Nord-Troms District Court and was fined NOK 50,000 for illegal helicopter flying in 2007.
110276.title_en: The Russians Lose in District Court

110293.excerpt_en: “This year, 370 skiers are coming up from the mainland, which is a record number,” says Per Krokan, head of Svalbard Turn.
110293.subtitle_en: A record number of skiers will line up for this year’s ski marathon.

110300.excerpt_en: Last week, employees at the waste facility found two dog carcasses in two separate wood-waste containers. One was discovered by customers who were disposing of something; the other was spotted by Vegard Strand of Reno Vest in the excavator’s claw as he was lifting wood waste into the shredder.
110300.subtitle_en: Dead dogs in the waste containers are causing problems for the waste facility.

110315.excerpt_en: Store Norske’s long-term plan includes coal reserves through 2023. These include Svea Nord, Lunckefjellet, Ispallen and Svea Øst.
110315.subtitle_en: Store Norske director Bjørn Arnestad does not rule out Store Norske investing in shipping across the Arctic Ocean once coal mining comes to an end.

110316.excerpt_en: For now, the ship is berthed in Longyearbyen and unable to go anywhere. “We finished loading yesterday afternoon and expect to get out tomorrow, if KV ‘Svalbard’ manages to get in,” says Bring district manager Karl-Henrik Karlsen.
110316.subtitle_en: The freighter “Norbjørn” is waiting for assistance from the coastguard vessel “Svalbard” to get out of Adventfjorden.

110322.excerpt_en: “The bear had visited the station daily since 18 April and had been extremely persistent,” explains Liv Asta Ødegaard, information adviser at the Governor’s Office.
110322.subtitle_en: A polar bear was sedated and moved to Edgeøya on Friday after troubling residents at the meteorological station on Hopen for several days.

110338.excerpt_en: On Saturday morning, between 9 and 11, the Governor’s Office visited the various departure points around Longyearbyen to check snowmobile drivers. Four of the 76 people checked tested over the limit.
110338.subtitle_en: A total of six people were prohibited from driving snowmobiles after the Governor’s Office carried out two alcohol checks over the weekend.

110340.excerpt_en: Both Erlend Hoff and Sara Svendsen claimed their third ski marathon victories on Saturday, in the men’s and women’s classes respectively. They will therefore keep the Svalbard Ski Marathon’s perpetual trophies outright.
110340.subtitle_en: Two skiers won the perpetual trophies outright after taking first place in the Svalbard Ski Marathon for the third time on Saturday. The result lists are now complete.

110363.excerpt_en: Member of Parliament and chair of the Standing Committee on Justice Anne Marit Bjørnflaten (Labour) cancelled yesterday as the day’s main speaker because of a death in the family. Former Store Norske director Robert Hermansen stepped in as her replacement.
110363.subtitle_en: Last year, 1 May passed quietly in Longyearbyen. This year, 40 people marched to the war memorial on Skjæringa.

110365.excerpt_en: “I think this job sounds incredibly exciting, in an environment where the government has a high level of ambition.”
110365.subtitle_en: After several rounds of advertising and temporary appointments, a new environmental protection chief has finally been appointed at the Governor’s Office.

110372.excerpt_en: “Nordstjernen” will operate on the mainland instead, replacing the Hurtigruten vessel MS “Nord-Norge”. The reason is that Hurtigruten ASA has extended its agreement with Aker Solutions, in connection with a project in Italy, until July.
110372.subtitle_en: Several hundred of Spitsbergen Travel’s passengers are affected by the fact that “Nordstjernen” will not come to Svalbard this summer.

110389.excerpt_en: “We drove to Barentsburg on Saturday morning and checked the tour groups we encountered along the way. We also carried out checks in Barentsburg.”
110389.subtitle_en: A man from mainland Norway was caught drink-driving a snowmobile in Barentsburg on Saturday.

110397.excerpt_en: Shortly after 1 a.m. on Tuesday, the Governor’s Office was notified that a snowmobile group was missing after failing to arrive at Isfjord Radio at the agreed time. “The last anyone had heard from the group was that they had left Svea at 7:30 p.m. to drive towards Kapp Linné,” says senior police officer …
110397.subtitle_en: A group of seven snowmobilers was found overnight after a search operation near Kapp Linné.

110405.excerpt_en: “The snowmobile drivers were spotted by skiers heading up Larsbreen. They tipped off the Governor’s Office about the illegal driving,” says senior police officer Inge Meløy. The drivers had travelled all the way up Larsbreen, towards Trollsteinen.
110405.subtitle_en: Two young men from Longyearbyen were caught driving snowmobiles illegally on Larsbreen on Wednesday evening, an area closed to snowmobile traffic.

110419.excerpt_en: “Compared with last year, we have cut two weekly departures between Tromsø and Longyearbyen in May. These are overnight flights that arrive late in the evening and leave early the next morning,” says Gro Elin Hansen, SAS information adviser.
110419.subtitle_en: SAS is dropping its night flights between Tromsø and Longyearbyen in May. This is also causing delays for Svalbardposten.

110422.excerpt_en: “We’re absolutely delighted with the number of entries, and pleasantly surprised that one of the commercial kennels is also entering a team, even though they’re in the middle of their season,” says Sébastien Barrault, head of the Longyearbyen Dog Club. Arctic Adventures is the commercial kennel taking part.
110422.subtitle_en: Eleven teams have entered the Trappers Trail dog race, which starts from Longyearbyen on Saturday.

110428.excerpt_en: Today marks 64 years since Liberation Day on 8 May 1945.
110428.subtitle_en: Young people in Longyearbyen commemorated the war with a wreath-laying ceremony and a speech. Gunnar Sønsteby, who visited them two weeks ago, was central to the speech.

110434.excerpt_en: “The two made it across to Nordaustlandet just over a week ago, but couldn’t get back because of heavy waves and little ice,” says senior police officer Inge Meløy of the Governor’s Office. The two men had made their way to Kinnvika and were picked up there. “It was a controlled extraction,” Meløy says.
110434.subtitle_en: Two kayakers who were unable to cross Hinlopen Strait were picked up by helicopter on Saturday evening.

110445.excerpt_en: Janne Søreide recorded the fastest time on the stretch from UNIS to Bikkjebu on Saturday and finished first on Sunday, despite starting last as the fastest team—25 minutes after Saturday’s final competitor. “It’s just for fun.”
110445.subtitle_en: Janne Søreide won the Trappers Trail dog race, probably the first in Longyearbyen’s history.
110445.title_en: Favourite Finishes with the Best Time

110457.excerpt_en: The Russian cargo ship “Petrozavodsk”, a fish transshipment vessel, ended up in the rocks at the southeastern tip of Bjørnøya. The crew spent the night in Barentsburg and will be flown to Longyearbyen during the day for questioning.
110457.subtitle_en: Justice Minister Knut Storberget was briefed this morning by Governor of Svalbard Per Sefland about the accident on Bjørnøya.

110472.excerpt_en: The owners of Lompensenteret are seeking businesses interested in helping to further develop the shopping centre. “We have rebuilt large parts of the ground floor, which now has a good, attractive layout. The shops have also invested quite a bit,” they say.
110472.subtitle_en: The owners of Lompensenteret want to develop the part of the centre where Café Busen is currently located and are looking for interested operators.

110492.excerpt_en: As every year, the people of Longyearbyen were woken by a salute at seven this morning. Since then, events have followed one another in quick succession, with the flag-raising at eight, the laying of a wreath at the Sverdrup memorial by Huset, flowers laid at the mining monument in the square, and a church service.
110492.subtitle_en: The weather was glorious in Longyearbyen during the parade, with temperatures of minus three degrees, sunshine and a northerly breeze in the air.

article_keywords_en: chief police officer to the Governor
110495.excerpt_en: The man was travelling from Inglefieldbukta when he got stuck 20 kilometres from Svea. “His snowmobile had become stuck in a riverbed, and the conditions were such that he could not continue.”
110495.subtitle_en: During the night before 17 May, the Governor of Svalbard had to dispatch a helicopter to retrieve a man whose snowmobile had become stuck in Kjellstrømdalen.

110498.excerpt_en: The man was stopped by the Governor of Svalbard’s officers on Friday afternoon and blew over the limit in a breathalyser test. He was also driving without a licence, according to senior police officer Jill Gaustad of the Governor’s Office.
110498.subtitle_en: A man from Longyearbyen is suspected of driving under the influence without a driving licence.

110505.excerpt_en: Jakobsen received the award for her work with the gymnastics group at Svalbard Turn. She has been a coach at Svalbard Turn for five years and leader of the gymnastics group for the past three.
110505.subtitle_en: Helle Jakobsen received this year’s Tyfus statuette at the 17 May performance at Huset last night. Ivan Marchenko simultaneously received this year’s youth cultural scholarship of NOK 10,000.
110505.title_en: This Year’s Tyfus Award Goes to Helle Jakobsen

110517.excerpt_en: During the first quarter of this year, Spitsbergen Travel suffered a sharp decline in revenues compared with the same period last year. Revenue from hotel operations and tour operations fell by NOK 11 million, from NOK 39.7 million last year to NOK 28.3 million this year.
110517.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Travel’s revenues are sharply down on last year. The company nevertheless expects to avoid layoffs.

110532.excerpt_en: Former deputy governor Rune Bård Hansen, now a presiding judge at Agder Court of Appeal, also wants to return to Svalbard. He served as deputy governor for two terms, completing his second term in autumn 2006.
110532.subtitle_en: Odd Olsen Ingerø, 58, left his post as Governor of Svalbard in February 2005 to become head of Kripos. Now he is one of three candidates seeking to succeed Per Sefland as governor.

110534.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, 19 tourists arrived in Longyearbyen to take part in a combined snowshoeing and sailing trip organized by Oceanwide Expeditions, from which Basecamp has chartered Noorderlicht.
110534.subtitle_en: Noorderlicht was due to carry snowshoeing tourists this week, but is stuck in the ice in Tempelfjorden.

110546.excerpt_en: “Traditional trapping has changed in some cases. It is therefore appropriate to look at the entire issue,” says Per Kyrre Reymert, acting head of environmental protection at the Governor’s Office.
110546.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard believes a review of trapping activities on Svalbard is necessary.

110561.excerpt_en: “With the stroke of a pen, they are taking away our livelihood. Seal hunting and reindeer hunting account for half our income, so I am extremely surprised by the decision,” says Hans Lund.
110561.subtitle_en: Trapper and fisherman Hans Lund is furious that the Governor of Svalbard is refusing to let him hunt reindeer in Farmhamna.

110569.excerpt_en: The main purpose of the visit is to discuss climate challenges in the north. The Millennium Development Goals, the financial crisis and UN reform will also be on the agenda, according to a press release from the Prime Minister’s Office. “It is a pleasure to welcome the UN Secretary-General to Norway,” says Prime Minister Jens Stoltenberg.
110569.subtitle_en: UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon is coming to Svalbard during his visit to Norway from 30 August to 2 September this year.

110608.excerpt_en: “The plan was to hold Saturday’s concerts in Per Teigen’s much-debated Rubbhallen in the Sjøområdet, and we had received all the permits. But it still did not work out because the hall is to be demolished,” says Spitsbergen Rock press officer Line Vangen Roksøy.
110608.subtitle_en: Rubbhallen in Endalen will serve as a concert venue for the Spitsbergen Rock festival next weekend. Organizers report strong interest ahead of the festival.

110612.excerpt_en: A total of 250 young people from across the country were nominated for the 2009 Dream Scholarship. One hundred were selected to receive scholarships, including Ingrid Brenli.
110612.subtitle_en: Today, 16-year-old Ingrid Brenli was awarded the 2009 Dream Scholarship of NOK 10,000. Brenli has sung and acted in theatre since she was two and dreams of becoming an artist.

110618.excerpt_en: “We will discuss with the Governor and the Ministry of Justice whether we should consider the aviation service as a whole. We have not had any concrete meetings about this yet, but I understand that the Governor’s contract with Airlift expires no later than 2014,” says Bjørn Arnestad, managing director of Store Norske.
110618.subtitle_en: Flights between Longyearbyen, Svea and Ny-Ålesund could cease within a few years. Next year, Store Norske’s contract with Lufttransport expires.

110637.excerpt_en: The first three to pass the halfway point after an hour and a half were two Danes and a man from Trondheim. Twenty-five runners started the full marathon—42 kilometres—from Svalbardhallen at 10 a.m. on Saturday, in grey weather and light snowfall.
110637.subtitle_en: At 10 this morning, the starting shot rang out for this year’s marathon in Longyearbyen. A total of 150 entrants will run the full marathon, half-marathon and Spitsbergen Mile.

110652.excerpt_en: This year’s participants competed in both the marathon and half-marathon. In addition, 56 runners completed the Spitsbergen Mile.
110652.subtitle_en: On Saturday, 126 enthusiastic runners took part in Svalbard Turn’s Spitsbergen Marathon. Here are the results.

110656.excerpt_en: KV Svalbard arrives in Longyearbyen on Tuesday morning. “We will change some personnel, and then head into Tempelfjorden,” says duty officer Knut Erik Riiber aboard KV Svalbard.
110656.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, the Coast Guard vessel Svalbard will break the schooner Noorderlicht free from the ice.

110677.excerpt_en: Spitsbergen Rock got underway with a pre-party at Svalbar on Thursday evening. Several festival bands gave the audience a preview of what lies ahead.
110677.subtitle_en: The first rock bands arrived in town on Thursday and offered a small taste of what the weekend will bring.

110694.excerpt_en: A group from Spitsbergen Travel had to be collected by the Governor’s helicopter on Sunday evening. A guide and three ski tourists reached Eolusneset in Sorgfjorden, northern Spitsbergen, on Saturday.
110694.subtitle_en: On Sunday, the Governor of Svalbard had to pick up four skiers from the northern tip of Spitsbergen.

110717.excerpt_en: At midnight, police received a report about an injured, intoxicated man who needed help. The tourist had earlier tried to break into a house on Road 219.
110717.subtitle_en: Police had to deal with a drunk tourist last night.

110731.excerpt_en: “There is a risk that people may take chances they otherwise would not take, knowing that we have a well-developed rescue service,” says Senior Police Officer to the Governor Erik Nygaard.
110731.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard wants to tighten the rules for rescue operations—for tourists and residents alike.

110740.excerpt_en: The former Lyd og Bilde premises at Lompensenteret are now being used as a kiosk. The space is twice as large as the Isbjørnbutikken’s previous location, allowing for a wider product selection and twelve seats overlooking Isfjorden.
110740.subtitle_en: The first customers streamed in when Mix Isbjørnbutikken opened in new premises this morning.

110745.excerpt_en: It was a quiet night for the police in Longyearbyen. But in the early hours, two men needed help finding their way home.
110745.subtitle_en: Not everyone made it home after last night’s party.

110786.excerpt_en: “It appears that the man is doing well. He walked into the ambulance himself and from the ambulance into the hospital, where he was X-rayed,” says Dag Rindal Brox, head of LNS Spitsbergen’s construction projects at Elvesletta Syd.
110786.subtitle_en: A 28-year-old man employed by LNS was injured when five roof trusses toppled on Wednesday afternoon.

110794.excerpt_en: Crown Prince Haakon of Norway, Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden and Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark are writing a book about their experiences in Svalbard and Greenland. The three heirs made their first official trip together last summer.
110794.subtitle_en: The three Scandinavian heirs to the throne are writing a book about the Arctic.

110800.excerpt_en: In an application to the Civil Aviation Authority, copied to the Ministry of Justice, Russian helicopter company Air Company Spark Plus is requesting a general expanded permit for local flights not connected to mining operations in Barentsburg. The company operates flights in Svalbard on behalf of state-owned mining company Trust Arktikugol.
110800.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol and helicopter company Spark Plus are applying to expand their flight permit in Svalbard.

110808.excerpt_en: Last week it was there: a small warning sign with a bird symbol, intended to alert people passing by the dog yard to all the eiders.
110808.subtitle_en: The eiders near the dog yard have received their own sign, despite the lack of permission.

110827.excerpt_en: “For us, the changes made by the politicians mean that the plan will not be completed for a long time yet, and that we cannot build the family apartments provided for in the plan. In addition, the plan will become more expensive,” says Per Christian Frøislie, Store Norske’s property manager.
110827.subtitle_en: Store Norske believes work on the sub-plan for Haugen has taken too long.

110836.excerpt_en: “I’m very pleased. I enjoyed living in Svalbard, and saw this as a final opportunity to return.”
110836.subtitle_en: Kripos chief Odd Olsen Ingerø, 58, is the new Governor of Svalbard.

110841.excerpt_en: “I hope the kids fish while they are down there and come back with good experiences and great pictures,” says Karianne Steen, the children’s and youth coordinator of the Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association (LJFF).
110841.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association is encouraging children and young people in Longyearbyen to spend the summer fishing—and take pictures of it.

110854.excerpt_en: The enormous balloon was released from the airstrip in Longyearbyen at around one o’clock last night. It is probably the largest balloon ever launched from Norwegian soil.
110854.subtitle_en: The balloon weather was perfect last night. Now an 800,000-cubic-metre balloon is heading towards Greenland.

110856.excerpt_en: While the sun is scorching the south, Longyearbyen residents were greeted by snow showers on Tuesday. “Snow and sleet in June are not unusual,” says meteorologist Torgeir Mørk in Longyearbyen.
110856.subtitle_en: The tropical heat has not reached Longyearbyen.

110887.excerpt_en: “We now have a reasonably good overview of the remaining oil on the ship. I expect to receive a new report today,” says Stig Nordaas of the Norwegian Coastal Administration, project manager for the cleanup after the Russian freezer vessel “Petrozavodsk.”
110887.subtitle_en: Crews from the Norwegian Coast Guard and salvage company Titan Salvage have been aboard the Russian freezer vessel that ran aground near Bear Island on 11 May.

110898.excerpt_en: “It was surprising. We expected to find more of the blue, but then something completely different emerged,” says an enthusiastic cultural heritage adviser with the Governor of Svalbard, Siri Hoem.
110898.subtitle_en: Surprising discoveries were made when the old walls of the Amundsen Villa in Ny-Ålesund were uncovered.

110905.excerpt_en: “We are undertaking a tough restructuring of the company. 2009 will be a very steep year,” says Store Norske CEO Bjørn Arnestad.
110905.subtitle_en: Store Norske is restructuring its operations to cope with low coal prices and a declining coal market.

110927.excerpt_en: According to barentsobserver.com, the Audit Chamber’s review of the Russian mining company shows that state transfers from 2006 to 2008 were used inefficiently. The amount involved was 2.17 billion Russian rubles, equivalent to around NOK 445 million.
110927.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol is being criticized by Russia’s Audit Chamber for using state transfers inefficiently.

110929.excerpt_en: “We checked and were sure that Svalbard was on the UNESCO list,” Hurtigruten PR Manager Petra Sestak told dagbladet.no. In its marketing for the coming season, the company advertised that travellers could experience some of UNESCO’s Norwegian World Heritage sites, such as Bryggen in Bergen, the Geirangerfjord and the Vega Islands.
110929.subtitle_en: Hurtigruten has already marketed Svalbard as a World Heritage site, even though the archipelago is currently only a potential candidate.
110929.title_en: Early to Promote World Heritage Status

110951.excerpt_en: “Strictly speaking, we are not building too close to the road; the road is too close to the building.”
110951.subtitle_en: According to LNS, which is building at Elvesletta Syd, it is the road that is too close to the building—not the other way around.

110957.excerpt_en: Vessels not approved to carry more than 12 passengers have no requirements regarding hull strength, stability or watertight subdivisions. The Norwegian Maritime Authority believes this must be offset by other measures and will introduce a requirement for a safety system.
110957.subtitle_en: A new proposed boat regulation is leaving many people uncertain.

110975.excerpt_en: Three of the four girls who make up the Polar Bear Patrol in the Longyearbyen Scout Group told Åndalsnes Avis that it is fun to try something new.
110975.subtitle_en: The scouts from Longyearbyen are attracting interest on the mainland, where they are attending the national camp for the first time.

110978.excerpt_en: Some Longyearbyen residents had seen the tourist, who is in his 30s, sleeping among the graves. They called the Governor of Svalbard, who went out to check whether the man was alive.
110978.subtitle_en: “I’m horny,” the Dutch tourist exclaimed when police woke him on Sunday morning.

110985.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration now hopes pumping the ship out can begin tomorrow. “The crew of the ‘Havservice 1’ has received the equipment they need from England and is heading to Bear Island today.”
110985.subtitle_en: The rescue boat “Havservice 1” is heading from Hammerfest to Bear Island with the equipment needed to empty the “Petrozavodsk.”
110985.title_en: Hopes to Begin Pumping on Wednesday

111001.excerpt_en: “It says a great deal about how drastically the climate is changing,” says Professor Nalân Koç of the Norwegian Polar Institute (NP).
111001.subtitle_en: In 20 years, central parts of the Arctic Ocean could be ice-free for part of the year for the first time in 14 to 15 million years.

111005.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) inspected the site of the bird-observation house after the Longyearbyen Field Biology Association (LoFF) submitted a complaint. Among other things, LoFF complained that Bydrift had taken fill material and thereby damaged the area around the bird-observation house.
111005.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council claims that the LoFF house at Sjøskrenten has been placed too far towards the beach.
111005.title_en: New dispute over the LoFF house

111022.excerpt_en: “We ended up about NOK 20,000 in the red,” says press officer Line Vangen Roksøy of Spitsbergen Rock.
111022.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Rock ran at a loss, but the organisers are already looking ahead optimistically to next year.

111027.excerpt_en: “We have been granted permission for what we applied for and can now do what we need to do. The application was processed very quickly, and the Governor deserves full credit for that,” says Store Norske’s property and exploration manager, Ester Knudsen.
111027.subtitle_en: Store Norske has received permission from the Governor of Svalbard for four coal-seam exposures at Lunckefjellet.

111033.excerpt_en: Salvage company Titan Salvage is anchored 300 metres from the ship with “Havservice 1”, together with the Coast Guard vessel “Harstad”. Crews have been aboard “Petrozavodsk”, but the swell is too heavy to begin pumping it out.
111033.subtitle_en: Pumping out the refrigerated cargo ship “Petrozavodsk” has not yet begun.
111033.title_en: Too much swell to pump out

111071.excerpt_en: “Unfortunately, we are planning to charge for parking. Partly to reduce its use, but also to increase revenue.”
111071.subtitle_en: Airport director Ole M. Rambech wants people to pay to park their cars at the airport.

111077.excerpt_en: “We fear that patients who need rapid transport to the mainland will not get it before it is too late,” says senior consultant Kari Schrøder Hansen at Longyearbyen Hospital.
111077.subtitle_en: A new duty roster for flight crews is making it difficult to get an ambulance to Longyearbyen.

111102.excerpt_en: “The conditions are certainly conducive to rot, with high humidity and warmth. Temperatures of up to 40 degrees have been measured on sun-facing walls.”
111102.subtitle_en: Specialists in dry rot have been granted permission to take samples from a number of protected buildings and ruins.
111102.title_en: Working to prevent cultural heritage from being destroyed

111132.excerpt_en: Swine flu has not yet reached Svalbard. But senior consultant Trond Egil Hansen at Longyearbyen Hospital expects it is on its way. “Yes, we have to expect it.”
111132.subtitle_en: Swine flu could have major consequences for Longyearbyen.

111150.excerpt_en: “We have many applicants, and we are very pleased about that,” says UNIS Managing Director Gunnar Sand. Today he welcomed the new students, the newest members of a student body of almost 400.
111150.subtitle_en: The new students at UNIS attended their first lecture today.

111174.excerpt_en: Svalbard is not prepared for environmental disasters involving major oil spills. That is the view of Governor of Svalbard Per Sefland.
111174.subtitle_en: Svalbard is not prepared for environmental disasters involving major oil spills.
111174.title_en: Says no to heavy fuel oil

111180.excerpt_en: On Thursday, 241 primary and lower-secondary pupils are due to start the 2009/2010 school year. That is 28 more pupils than last year. “It has been a tremendous increase.”
111180.subtitle_en: Never before have so many pupils shown up for the first day at Longyearbyen School.

111185.excerpt_en: Today is Svalbard Day. It commemorates the day Norway assumed sovereignty over the archipelago and the Norwegian flag was raised at Skjæringa for the first time.
111185.subtitle_en: Flags are flying high at Skjæringa and throughout the town today.

111199.excerpt_en: Not everyone plans to try their luck during the first hunting weekend, however. When Svalbardposten spoke to the Governor of Svalbard on Friday afternoon, 132 hunters had collected their hunting permits.
111199.subtitle_en: As of today, reindeer may be hunted. Three hundred and forty-four hunters have been granted permission to shoot one animal each.

111205.excerpt_en: “It’s great—I think it’s simply great,” says Balder Månum. He is one of 29 first-graders who entered Longyearbyen School for the first time today.
111205.subtitle_en: Joy and anticipation at Longyearbyen School as 29 pupils had their first day of school today.

111224.excerpt_en: The man, who is from Libya, has lived in Longyearbyen for the past three years. He has now been sentenced by the Nord-Troms District Court to 75 days in prison for violating the Penal Code.
111224.subtitle_en: A 30-year-old man living in Longyearbyen must go to prison after turning up at Tromsø airport earlier this summer.

111231.excerpt_en: “He was going to fire a warning shot and thought the flare gun was empty. It had already been loaded, and when he inserted another round, it discharged into his hand,” says Governor of Svalbard senior police officer Lene Fagerbakke.
111231.subtitle_en: A sailor in his 60s shot himself in the hand with a flare gun while attempting to warn of a polar bear in Van Keulenfjorden.

111243.excerpt_en: All the new give-way signs are to be uncovered at seven o’clock in the morning. Road 600 between Gruve 7 and the airport will become a priority road, as will the road from Nybyen to Unis.
111243.subtitle_en: On Saturday, all motorists in Longyearbyen will have to pay close attention at intersections. The new give-way and priority-road system will then take effect.

111247.excerpt_en: “KV ‘Harstad’ and KMN ‘Tyr’ are leaving Tromsø today,” says Sven E. Scheiderbauer, director of the Norwegian Aviation Museum.
111247.subtitle_en: Today, the search begins for the seaplane “Latham”, with which Roald Amundsen disappeared in 1928.

111253.excerpt_en: “It was completely surreal. I thought, this can’t be happening, this isn’t happening,” says Svein Nordahl, who witnessed the incident. Nordahl works as a bus driver and was at Bykaia to collect the passenger lists for those due to travel on “Langøysund” to Pyramiden that day.
111253.subtitle_en: The cruise ship “Antarctic Dream” sailed straight into “Langøysund” on Tuesday morning as it lay moored at Bykaia.

111278.excerpt_en: “Busen is ending its contract at the turn of the year,” says Lars Erik Hoel of Eindomsinvestor AS, which owns half of Lompen Centre. Store Norske owns the other half.
111278.subtitle_en: Café Busen is not renewing its contract with Lompen Centre. The café will therefore close at the turn of the year.

111295.excerpt_en: The mini-seminar, held in Møysalen at UNIS next Wednesday, is open to everyone. There will be around 120 seats available for interested members of the public, in addition to those invited in advance.
111295.subtitle_en: People in Longyearbyen will be able to attend a mini-seminar with UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon when he visits Svalbard next week.

111297.excerpt_en: On Thursday, “Polar Star” had completed its final voyage for Spitsbergen Travel in Svalbard. The cruise ship was due to continue with new passengers to Northeast Greenland on Friday afternoon.
111297.subtitle_en: Engine problems forced “Polar Star” to cancel a planned trip to Greenland.

111321.excerpt_en: “It has been inspiring to visit the Arctic. I am here to see for myself how much damage climate change has caused to this vulnerable natural environment.”
111321.subtitle_en: UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon is impressed by research in the Arctic. But he also expresses fear about climate change.

111326.excerpt_en: “It is a democratic problem that votes must be cast two weeks before election day. Many people need to follow the campaign debates for as long as possible before deciding,” says local council leader Kjell Mork.
111326.subtitle_en: Friday is the final deadline for those wishing to vote early from Longyearbyen. The local council leader believes it is too soon.

111341.excerpt_en: “The order requiring the shipping company to remove the wreck still stands, but removal cannot take place before next summer at the earliest,” says Knut Arnhus, chief engineer at the Norwegian Coastal Administration and project manager for the wreck removal.
111341.subtitle_en: “Petrosavodsk” can be removed from Bear Island no earlier than next summer.

111344.excerpt_en: “We will close Funken earlier than planned if the booking situation does not improve. It is sad for those affected, but unfortunately it is something we have to do to cover the losses,” says Trygve Steen, managing director of Spitsbergen Travel.
111344.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Travel is closing Funken earlier than planned and laying off employees temporarily to save money.

111350.excerpt_en: The eight sites being closed are spread across Svalbard. What they have in common is that they contain older, automatically protected cultural heritage sites.
111350.subtitle_en: The government, meeting in council, decided on Friday to close eight sites in Svalbard to visitors. A heavy-fuel-oil ban will also be introduced in the national parks on Svalbard’s west coast.

111367.excerpt_en: Jakobsen is from Kvænangen in North Troms and has a military background. He is a lieutenant colonel and has, among other things, been garrison commander at the Garrison of Porsanger in Finnmark and district commander of the Home Guard in the same county.
111367.subtitle_en: Roger Jakobsen (46) has been appointed the new director of Kings Bay in Ny-Ålesund.

111368.excerpt_en: The Russian Fisheries Committee has presented a proposal for further planning of a fish-processing plant in Barentsburg. Trust Arktikugol has long said it wants to build such a plant, and the plans have now moved a step forward.
111368.subtitle_en: Norwegian specialists will build a fish-processing plant in Barentsburg.

111384.excerpt_en: “I have held a light-aircraft licence since 1994, but it has been a struggle to keep it current when I could only fly while on the mainland,” says Karl Magne Faksdal. So he simply brought the aircraft to Svalbard in mid-August.
111384.subtitle_en: Karl Magne Faksdal flew his own light aircraft from Namsos to Svalbard.

111400.excerpt_en: MS “Quest” had been in Trygghamna, at the outer end of Isfjorden, with passengers and was returning to Longyearbyen when the shot was fired at around 7 p.m. on Friday. “A shot went off inside a cabin.”

One alternative is to mark out a safer course and set up checkpoints that everyone must pass,” says secretary-general Stein Tore Pedersen of Friends of Trollsteinen, which is organising the race.
112410.subtitle_en: The Spitsbergen Up and Down ski race risks being postponed because of avalanche danger.

112426.excerpt_en: “We have marked out the route and avoided the exposed areas,” says secretary-general Stein Tore Pedersen of Friends of Trollsteinen, which is organising the Spitsbergen Up and Down ski race.
112426.subtitle_en: Despite the avalanche danger, today’s ski race will go ahead as planned.
112426.title_en: Ski race to go ahead as planned

112436.excerpt_en: “We received a report of a fight in which two men attacked each other with their bare fists on Vei 238. Several people reacted to the fighting and noise, but everything was quiet and calm when we arrived,” says duty chief superintendent Jan Eivind Myklatun of the Governor of Svalbard.
112436.subtitle_en: Two men in their mid-20s attacked each other on Vei 238 on Tuesday evening.

112439.excerpt_en: “The ski race was a great success. Almost everyone reached the top, and one woman had to be picked up by snowmobile after suffering cramp.”
112439.subtitle_en: Forty-nine people took part in Saturday’s ski race to Trollsteinen. The fastest completed the ascent and descent in 55 minutes.

112454.excerpt_en: Seventy local singers and musicians warmed up Brasserie Nansen and around 250 audience members on Wednesday evening. They delivered a varied programme ranging from ballads to Serbian rhythms, pop and bluegrass.
112454.subtitle_en: As many as 15 bands and choir groups helped jazz up the atmosphere in town.

112460.excerpt_en: The local rescue coordination centre was involved in 81 rescue operations, compared with 72 the previous year, according to the Governor of Svalbard’s annual report. “This is mainly because the number of helicopter ambulance missions has increased,” says Chief Superintendent Erik Nygaard of the Governor’s office. Flying farther: The ambulance missions have also become longer, averaging around two hours last year.
112460.subtitle_en: A record number of rescue missions were carried out in Svalbard last year.

112476.excerpt_en: “We will have a completely new presentation of the evidence in the court of appeal,” says Deputy Governor Lars Fause, who is the prosecutor in the case. It was 8.
112476.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has appealed the sentence handed down to Oceanwide Expeditions. The company has filed a cross-appeal on the question of guilt.
112476.title_en: New round in the Hornsund case

112485.excerpt_en: Songs such as “Moon Landing,” “Belorado,” “Lost At Sea” and other tracks from the CD Moon Landing thundered out over the audience with tremendous energy. To make room for everyone, all the chairs and tables were cleared from the restaurant at the Polar Hotel.
112485.subtitle_en: Sivert Høyem and his band whipped up a veritable polar high-pressure system, with storm-force gusts, at the Polar Hotel on Thursday.
112485.title_en: A polar high-pressure system at Polarjazz

article_keywords_en: chief superintendent of the Governor of Svalbard
112507.excerpt_en: “We received a report at 2:15 a.m. about an extremely intoxicated man who was unable to look after himself and needed medical assistance,” says duty chief superintendent Jan Eivind Myklatun of the Governor of Svalbard. The man, in his early 30s, is a permanent resident of Longyearbyen and was taken in for observation.
112507.subtitle_en: An extremely intoxicated man needed help from the Governor of Svalbard early Sunday morning.

112509.excerpt_en: “We received a concern report about three people who were supposed to have returned from a snowmobile trip to Semmelbu on Saturday evening, and began preparing for a rescue operation,” says duty chief superintendent Jan Eivind Myklatun of the Governor of Svalbard.
112509.subtitle_en: A rescue operation was narrowly averted on Saturday evening.

112527.excerpt_en: “They have both hit their heads, but they were wearing helmets. Their condition is good, as far as we can tell at present,” says Søren Nissen, head of department at Longyearbyen Hospital.
112527.subtitle_en: Two men have been taken to Longyearbyen Hospital after colliding head-on on snowmobiles in Adventdalen.

112535.excerpt_en: The accident happened just after 5 p.m. on Tuesday afternoon. The Governor’s Office was notified about what had happened half an hour later.
112535.subtitle_en: The man injured in a snowmobile accident on Tuesday afternoon was sent to the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) in Tromsø late Tuesday evening with a possible skull fracture.

112548.excerpt_en: Students at Longyearbyen School spontaneously applauded when State Secretary Astri Aas-Hansen (Labour) of the Ministry of Justice announced on Wednesday that, from the autumn, foreign students could attend upper secondary school in Troms County. “The government has instructed the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI) and put in place regulations so that students with a foreign background who do not have a residence permit in Norway will be able to…”
112548.subtitle_en: From the autumn, foreign students at Longyearbyen School can continue their education at upper secondary schools on the mainland.
112548.title_en: Foreign Students Allowed to Attend Upper Secondary School on the Mainland

112580.excerpt_en: “She had pinched or struck an ankle while snowmobiling in the center of Ny-Ålesund. She was flown to Longyearbyen Hospital by air ambulance for an X-ray,” says senior police officer Per Andreassen.
112580.subtitle_en: A woman was picked up by air ambulance in Ny-Ålesund on Tuesday afternoon.

112582.excerpt_en: Stefan Claes and his six dogs reached Passhytta first and crossed the finish line first on Sunday. “The next four teams came close behind,” says Lene Pedersen of Longyearbyen Dog Club, which organized the race.
112582.subtitle_en: The year’s first dog race was held on Sunday. The winner took three and a half hours from the old Northern Lights station to Passhytta and back.

112587.excerpt_en: “The vessel is suspected of failing to notify the Directorate of Fisheries about fishing in Svalbard,” says senior police officer Per Andreassen. The Coast Guard notified the Governor’s Office on Tuesday after inspecting the cargo vessel.
112587.subtitle_en: A Russian cargo vessel has been detained by the Coast Guard near Bjørnøya, suspected of failing to comply with its reporting obligation.

112593.excerpt_en: The transport vessel, owned by Murmansk-based North West Shipping Company, was inspected and detained by the Norwegian Coast Guard near Bjørnøya on Tuesday. The Coast Guard suspected the vessel of failing to notify the Directorate of Fisheries about fishing in Svalbard, and the Governor’s Office flew to the site to question the captain.
112593.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has issued the captain of the Russian freighter “Jupiter” a waiver of prosecution.

112597.excerpt_en: A fellow student alerted the Governor’s Office at around 10 p.m. last night. “The students were supposed to be back at 9 p.m., but the person who reported it had heard nothing from them and could not reach them by mobile phone,” says senior police officer Per Andreassen.
112597.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office and the Red Cross went out last night to search for four students who had not returned from the cave at Larsbreen at the agreed time.

112611.excerpt_en: “This incident falls into that category because at one point it became so slippery that the pilots were unable to control the aircraft.”
112611.subtitle_en: The Accident Investigation Board has classified the incident in which a mail plane skidded off the runway as serious.

112633.excerpt_en: “The search was conducted by helicopter over the ice south of Kaldbukta and across to the other side of the fjord, then farther inland across the ice toward Svea,” says duty senior police officer Trond Aagesen of the Governor’s Office.
112633.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has ended the search operation on Van Mijenfjorden without results. No one has been reported missing.

112638.excerpt_en: “Two local residents staying at a cabin in the area alerted us after seeing the lights from two snowmobiles suddenly disappear out on Van Mijenfjorden,” says duty senior police officer Trond Aagesen of the Governor’s Office.
112638.subtitle_en: Just before midnight, lights from two snowmobiles were seen disappearing on the ice off Blåhuken in Van Mijenfjorden. The Governor’s Office searched the area by helicopter without finding anything.

112651.excerpt_en: “2009 has been a very different year for Store Norske, with significant changes in the company’s operating conditions. Despite this, we achieved a pre-tax result of just over NOK 400 million.”
112651.subtitle_en: Store Norske posted a profit of NOK 400 million last year. It was the second-best result in the company’s history.
112651.title_en: Another Record Year for Store Norske

112665.excerpt_en: “We are very happy to receive an award like this. Being nominated was overwhelming, and when we won I was almost in shock,” says Gry Sneltvedt, general manager of Isbjørnbutikken.
112665.subtitle_en: Isbjørnbutikken has been named MIX Store of the Year 2009.

112672.excerpt_en: Thirty-five tourists were breathalyzed by the Governor of Svalbard at Svalbard Snøscooterutleie (SSU) before setting out. Ten of them were stopped.
112672.subtitle_en: Ten tourists were not allowed to go on a snowmobile trip this morning.
112672.title_en: Ten Caught Driving Under the Influence

112717.excerpt_en: The 25-year-old is from Oslo and was in Svalbard in connection with KunstPause. Saturday the 14th.
