112717.subtitle_en: The 25-year-old man who ended up on the roof in a stolen car last November has been sentenced to 30 days in prison, suspended.

112722.excerpt_en: About 60 snowmobile drivers were stopped in a drink-driving check near the old airport in Adventdalen on Saturday morning. No one was suspected of driving under the influence.
112722.subtitle_en: Senior police officer Erik Nygaard says people need to shape up.

112739.excerpt_en: A man in his early 50s had to be picked up by helicopter after an accident during a snowmobile trip. The incident took place at the head of Adventdalen.
112739.subtitle_en: A local resident had to be picked up by the Governor’s helicopter on Saturday afternoon.

112741.excerpt_en: “We expect lower passenger numbers on expedition cruises this year,” says Frigg Jørgensen, secretary-general of Aeco, the organization for the cruise industry in Svalbard. The reason is a combination of fewer ships arriving and older ships being replaced by newer vessels that are not as large, the secretary-general explains.
112741.subtitle_en: Tour operators are offering fewer berths for this year’s expedition cruises than last year.

112758.excerpt_en: “There were six people traveling from Barentsburg to Longyearbyen. One of them overturned and ended up partly underneath the snowmobile.”
112758.subtitle_en: A woman in her 50s was taken to the hospital in Barentsburg after a snowmobile overturned at Heerodden.

112779.excerpt_en: “This is the worst situation we could have had. We had hoped for as long as possible that the ship would remain intact until summer; now it will be much harder to remove it,” says senior adviser Knut M.
112779.subtitle_en: The Russian reefer that ran aground at the southern tip of Bjørnøya in May last year has split in two.

112785.excerpt_en: Two hundred and sixty adults and 150 young people attended Donkeyboy’s two concerts on Wednesday evening. Most of them jumped. “I have to say it’s an honor to be here in Svalbard.”
112785.subtitle_en: The audience jumped so much that the organizers feared they would break through the floor.

112820.excerpt_en: Instead of offering all employees housing at the same price per square metre, there are now major differences in what UNIS employees have to pay in rent. Employees currently working at UNIS retain their existing housing agreement.
112820.subtitle_en: Employees are reacting to UNIS’s new housing policy.

112838.excerpt_en: The woman probably broke a bone, but Senior Police Officer Inge Meløy is unsure how she was injured. “No vehicle was involved. She was out walking the dog,” says Meløy.
112838.subtitle_en: A foreign woman was airlifted from Adolfbukta last night.

112855.excerpt_en: “And this is what you put yourself through every single year—voluntarily,” exclaims Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik a few minutes before this year’s Sun Festival revue premieres. An hour and a half later, thunderous applause erupted after the revue troupe, with its strong female and male contingent, had delivered 34 numbers at a rapid pace.
112855.subtitle_en: Sun Festival Week concluded with the Ta Sjansen event in Hiorthhamn and a revue at Huset. Enthusiasm was equally high at both venues.

112858.excerpt_en: At 11 a.m., all cafés and restaurants may serve beer and wine. Spirits may be sold from 1 p.m., when the new serving-hour regulations come into force in June.
112858.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, the local council decided that all licensed establishments in town may serve alcohol on equal terms.

112873.excerpt_en: “The woman became so frightened that she did not dare make her way down by herself,” says Senior Police Officer Jill Gaustad. Police received a report from a woman in her late twenties at half past two on Monday.
112873.subtitle_en: A local woman had to be rescued by the Red Cross after becoming frightened during a hike yesterday.

112879.excerpt_en: “We checked 16 snowmobile drivers and two tested positive. One driver was banned from driving.”
112879.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office stopped a person from driving a snowmobile during a preventive drink-driving check this morning.

112912.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, NRK Dagsrevyen claimed that Norway was violating the Svalbard Treaty by downloading weather data from meteorological satellites. According to NRK, data from SvalSat were used by US forces during the invasion of Iraq in 2003.
112912.subtitle_en: Foreign Minister Jonas Gahr Støre rejects the claim that Norway is violating the Svalbard Treaty by SvalSat making weather data available to the outside world.
112912.title_en: No breach of the Svalbard Treaty

112924.excerpt_en: “The weather will be best in the area around Longyearbyen this weekend, so conditions look good for trips to Von Postbreen and Barentsburg,” says Torgeir Mørk, a meteorological consultant at Svalbard Airport. The forecast for Spitsbergen on Saturday and Sunday calls for north-easterly breezes and occasional fresh winds in exposed areas.
112924.subtitle_en: The weather looks set to be quite good across Svalbard in the coming days. But those seeking the best conditions should stay near Longyearbyen.

112946.excerpt_en: “She drove from UNIS straight into the wall at the Polar Centre,” says Senior Police Officer Jill Gaustad. She says the woman, who studies at UNIS, was taken to Longyearbyen Hospital for a medical check-up. “She was discharged immediately,” says Gaustad.
112946.subtitle_en: A woman in her twenties drove straight into the wall of the Polar Centre on Saturday afternoon.

112955.excerpt_en: “The weather will not change much in the days ahead. There will still be easterly winds, but they will ease compared with today,” says Torgeir Mørk, a meteorological consultant at Svalbard Airport.
112955.subtitle_en: Good outdoor weather will continue through the Easter holiday. However, there may be some precipitation in southern and eastern parts of Spitsbergen.

112973.excerpt_en: On Good Friday at around 2 p.m., the Governor’s Office received the Easter holiday’s first operational call. “A woman was airlifted from the mouth of Sassendalen after suffering a minor shoulder injury,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen.
112973.subtitle_en: A female tourist was airlifted after injuring her shoulder in Sassendalen.

112982.excerpt_en: “She fell a few hundred metres from the road. It was so slippery there that it was impossible to drive a snowmobile.”
112982.subtitle_en: A woman in her sixties was airlifted from Bjørndalen on Monday afternoon after falling and injuring herself on the ice.

112990.excerpt_en: The Frenchman’s plan was to fly the “Generali Arctic Observer” balloon over the North Pole. According to Etienne’s website, the balloon passed 88 degrees north at around four o’clock on Wednesday afternoon.
112990.subtitle_en: On Monday morning, Jean-Louis Etienne took off from Adventdalen to fly over the North Pole in a helium balloon. He only almost made it.

112998.excerpt_en: “The tourists have been bothered by the bear all day, and it has now started attacking equipment and provisions at the camp. We have sent a couple of men by helicopter to see what we can do,” says Chief Superintendent Erik Nygaard of the Governor’s Office.
112998.subtitle_en: An intrusive polar bear has caused problems for a French tourist group. Governor’s Office personnel are on their way by helicopter to help the ski tourists.
112998.title_en: Polar bear trouble for French tourists

113026.excerpt_en: “We have introduced paid parking, but in a friendly way. We do not want to catch anyone out,” says Ole M., airport director at Svalbard Airport.
113026.subtitle_en: From today, parking at Svalbard Airport costs money. The airport wants to stop cars from being left there for months.
113026.title_en: You now have to pay for parking

113043.excerpt_en: “Based on the driver’s own account, we assumed a speed of 60 kilometres per hour and offered him a fine of 8,000 kroner and a six-month driving ban,” says Deputy Governor Lars Fause. The driver did not accept the fine and withdrew his statement.
113043.subtitle_en: The man in his twenties who is charged with speeding on Hilmar Rekstens vei in March must stand trial.

113050.excerpt_en: “We have already been told that the daytime flight from Oslo and Tromsø has been cancelled. We do not yet know what will happen to the night flights, but I am not optimistic about the flight from Oslo, at least,” says Ole M., airport director at Svalbard Airport.
113050.subtitle_en: The ash cloud from the volcanic eruption in Iceland has cancelled the daytime flight to Svalbard. The air ambulance cannot reach the archipelago either.
113050.title_en: Air traffic to the mainland halted

113062.excerpt_en: Two hundred and seventy people were due to fly from Longyearbyen today and tonight. The hotels are packed, and Svalbardposten cannot get away from Tromsø.
113062.subtitle_en: Two hundred and seventy people were due to fly from Longyearbyen today and tonight. The hotels are packed, and Svalbardposten cannot get away from Tromsø.

113082.excerpt_en: “They are now calculating how the ash cloud will spread,” says Ole M. Rambech, airport director at Svalbard Airport.
113082.subtitle_en: It is still uncertain when flights to and from the archipelago can resume. Svalbardposten can be purchased as a PDF today by those who want it.

113106.excerpt_en: “There was an enormous amount of logistics involved last year. Everything becomes much easier when we have the festival tent closer to town,” says Patrik Jonsson, deputy chair of the festival board.
113106.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Rock has finalized its artist lineup and moved to the Sjøområdet area.

113112.excerpt_en: “There are now 450 passengers who have been unable to travel south,” says traffic consultant Tone Bendiktsen of SAS Ground Services in Longyearbyen. Today she is sitting at the airport service centre with colleague Margrethe Krane.
113112.subtitle_en: So far, four flights from Svalbard have been cancelled. SAS Ground Services is ensuring that all passengers have shelter and food.

113114.excerpt_en: The SAS aircraft is arriving from Bodø, flying directly to Trondheim, with passengers then being taken by bus onward to Oslo. Check-in at Longyearbyen Airport was in full swing at around 2 p.m. “We will turn the aircraft around as quickly as possible when it lands here,” says traffic consultant Margrethe Krane of SAS Ground Services.
113114.subtitle_en: The aircraft is carrying passengers to Trondheim. There will be no flight from Tromsø to Longyearbyen today, despite Tromsø Airport having reopened.

113125.excerpt_en: Gunnar Ranheim, a traffic consultant with SAS Ground Services in Tromsø, says it is not clear who will be travelling on the flight arriving from Tromsø around 1:30 p.m. “Those we can reach will have the opportunity to travel.”
113125.subtitle_en: An SAS flight from Tromsø is due to land at Svalbard Airport at 1:35 p.m. today. The evening flight to Longyearbyen is also arriving. The air ambulance can now also fly between Svalbard and the mainland.

113138.excerpt_en: This year’s Trappers’ Trail took place in brilliant sunshine over the weekend. Sixteen teams lined up at the starting line on Saturday, with between two and eight dogs each.
113138.subtitle_en: Almost one hundred sled dogs put their strength to the test when the world’s northernmost dog race was held for the second time.

113156.excerpt_en: At the polar bear conference in Tromsø last year, Norway and the United States were tasked with compiling a database of incidents involving polar bears and people. Last week, American researchers Terry DeBruyn and James Wilder of the Fish and Wildlife Service were in Longyearbyen to continue working on it.
113156.subtitle_en: A Norwegian-American database aims to prevent polar bears from being killed by people.

113159.excerpt_en: “Some people in Svea seem to remember that something happened to a researcher, but no one remembers whether it was a natural death or an accident. I have looked everywhere without finding out,” says Stein Arne Ellingsen.
113159.subtitle_en: What happened in Rinders Bay in the summer of 1985, and who was John Willis? These are questions Stein Arne Ellingsen in Svea would very much like answered.

113165.excerpt_en: At 3:15 p.m., police were notified that a man in his 60s had been involved in a snowmobile accident in Pyramiden. The tourist was part of a private travel group.
113165.subtitle_en: A man had to be picked up by helicopter on Sunday afternoon.

113170.excerpt_en: “It is likely to be the same bear we chased earlier this weekend,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office. He believes it looks similar and may have made its way from Hiorthhamn to town during the night.
113170.subtitle_en: A polar bear was spotted near the dog yard early today. The Governor of Svalbard is chasing it farther into Adventdalen.

113179.excerpt_en: “We assume it is the same bear as before,” says Senior Police Officer Inge Meløy of the Governor’s Office. At 6:50 a.m. today, the Governor’s Office was notified that a polar bear was in Adventdalen, level with Isdammen.
113179.subtitle_en: The polar bear driven out of Adventdalen yesterday has returned. It is now being escorted toward Revneset by two senior police officers from the Governor’s Office.

113195.excerpt_en: “We have studied the photographs and can say that it is probably a different individual that we chased today. It is clearly a stronger and larger animal,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office.
113195.subtitle_en: The bear driven toward Revneset today is probably not the same one that was escorted out of Adventdalen yesterday.

113200.excerpt_en: “The man is a tourist and was out riding a snowmobile alone,” says Senior Police Officer Erik Nygaard of the Governor’s Office. He says the Swede, who is between 40 and 50 years old, had become stuck in Gangskaret, between Todalen and Gangdalen.
113200.subtitle_en: A Swedish man activated an emergency beacon in Gangskaret near Fritham during the night. His snowmobile had become stuck, and he was picked up by the Governor of Svalbard’s rescue helicopter.

113208.excerpt_en: The Icelandic ash cloud threatened to halt the Svalbard Ski Marathon, which was held for the 18th time this year.
113208.subtitle_en: Many people made their way to the Svalbard Ski Marathon last weekend. See how the participants performed here.

113226.excerpt_en: “She became separated from her snowmobile group on Slakkbreen,” says Senior Police Officer Rune Fred Jensen of the Governor’s Office. The Governor’s Office was notified of the missing woman at 3:30 p.m. and launched a search from Longyearbyen.
113226.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard launched a search for a female snowmobile rider on Sunday afternoon. She was found in Gustavdalen just over three hours later.

113228.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Workers’ Association was founded during an outdoor meeting at Skjæringa in June 1925. The trade union is affiliated with the Norwegian Union of Municipal and General Employees, which for many years has been dominated by coal miners at Store Norske.
113228.subtitle_en: There will be no May Day parade in Longyearbyen on Saturday, nor any event at Skjæringa. The reason is that Longyearbyen Workers’ Association’s 85-year-old tradition has been broken.

113243.excerpt_en: The man, who is in his 50s, broke his arm in a snowmobile accident near the sailboat “Noorderlicht,” which is frozen into the ice in Tempelfjorden. Police were notified of the incident at around 11 p.m. on Sunday.
113243.subtitle_en: A Danish tourist had to be picked up by helicopter beside his boat in the ice on Sunday evening.

113261.excerpt_en: Police were just about to launch a search when they heard from the man, who had recently been reported missing after ice fishing on Linnévatnet on Sunday. They were notified that he was missing at around 2:30 p.m. today.
113261.subtitle_en: After spending the night outdoors, a local man reported to the Governor of Svalbard.

113279.excerpt_en: The extension of the fiber-optic cable is linked to the Norwegian Mapping Authority’s plans to build a new measuring station costing nearly NOK 200 million in Ny-Ålesund, where rapid data transfer is a requirement.
113279.subtitle_en: The government supports extending the fiber-optic cable from Longyearbyen to Ny-Ålesund and is allocating NOK 60 million for the project.

113288.subtitle_en: The satellite transmitter that failed when researchers were tagging bowhead whales has started working.

113324.excerpt_en: “Lufttransport has decided not to fly today because forecasts indicate that the ash concentration will increase,” says assistant airport manager Morten Ulsnes at Svalbard Airport. He says the airports in Longyearbyen and Svea are theoretically open, but there is ash west and south of Longyearbyen.
113324.subtitle_en: The SAS flight has been cancelled, and Lufttransport has decided to ground its aircraft because of the ash cloud.

113339.excerpt_en: “The flight will operate. The situation is completely different today,” says Knut Morten Johansen, SAS’s head of communications.
113339.subtitle_en: The SAS flight to the mainland will operate as normal today. Ambulance flights are still unable to fly to the archipelago.

113344.excerpt_en: “We hope we can start flying on Svalbard again sometime tomorrow, but it is by no means certain,” says Frank Wilhelmsen, operations director at Lufttransport. The company flies from Longyearbyen to Svea and Ny-Ålesund.
113344.subtitle_en: The ash forecasts for tomorrow look promising. The Air Ambulance Service and Lufttransport hope they will be able to fly.

113360.excerpt_en: Einar Edvardsen, general manager of Henningsen Transport & Guiding (HTG), says that MS “Langøysund” made its first trip on May 16.
113360.subtitle_en: The summer season is just around the corner. “Langøysund” has already been operating for a week.

113365.excerpt_en: “There will be no ash here at all today or tomorrow,” says Torgeir Mørk, a meteorological consultant at Svalbard Airport. Yesterday, Lufttransport’s aircraft remained grounded.
113365.subtitle_en: Lufttransport has resumed flying, but ash in Northern Norway is preventing the Air Ambulance Service from maintaining readiness for Svalbard.

113366.excerpt_en: “The current regulations are cumbersome. They are old and not adapted to Svalbard,” says André Kalstad, a lawyer at the Norwegian Food Safety Authority’s regional office for Troms and Finnmark.
113366.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Food Safety Authority and the Governor of Svalbard believe the rules for keeping dogs on Svalbard should be changed.

113381.excerpt_en: An ash cloud over Northern Norway is causing problems for air traffic. “Tromsø Airport will be closed from 2 p.m. until 8 p.m.,” says SAS information adviser Monica Hovland. Despite the problems, the SAS flight to Longyearbyen will operate as normal.
113381.subtitle_en: Because Tromsø Airport closes at 2 p.m., the flight from Longyearbyen will land in Bodø instead.

113390.excerpt_en: The proposal from the Ministry of the Environment forms part of the amendment to the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act, which has now been circulated for consultation. If the proposed amendment is adopted, the ban will enter into force in 2015.
113390.subtitle_en: From 2015, cruise ships may sail past Svalbard if heavy fuel oil is banned under the revised Svalbard Environmental Protection Act.

113399.excerpt_en: “Both were picked up by helicopter because of illness,” says senior superintendent Erik Nygaard. The hiker on Varden was collected during the day yesterday, while the English fisherman was picked up yesterday evening.
113399.subtitle_en: Yesterday, one person was brought down from Varden in Longyearbyen and another from a fishing boat east of Bear Island.

113407.excerpt_en: “We have now had a couple of warm days during which the ice has weakened, and we will attempt to get ‘Noorderlicht’ out,” says Solfrid Håkenstad, general manager at Basecamp Spitsbergen. The vessel “A.
113407.subtitle_en: The Russian tug “A. Belikov” will break the sailing vessel “Noorderlicht” out of Tempelfjorden tomorrow.

113423.excerpt_en: “They had no problems; it went very well,” says Solfrid Håkenstad, general manager of Basecamp Spitsbergen. “A.
113423.subtitle_en: On Sunday evening, the Russian tug “A. Belikov” succeeded in freeing “Noorderlicht” from the ice in Tempelfjorden.

113446.excerpt_en: From 2015, cruise ships may sail past Svalbard if heavy fuel oil is banned under the revised Svalbard Environmental Protection Act. Port manager Kjetil Bråten believes this would have major economic consequences for Longyearbyen if cruise ships could sail only to Barentsburg and Longyearbyen, as proposed.
113446.subtitle_en: Businesses in Longyearbyen could lose tens of millions if cruise ships choose to sail past Svalbard.

113452.excerpt_en: On Tuesday morning, the board of Spitsbergen Rock learned that the festival tent they had rented was still at the quay in Tromsø and would not be arriving in Longyearbyen. “I thought it was a joke,” says sponsorship manager Nanna Thune.
113452.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Rock will not get the festival tent to town in time. Huset will become the new concert venue.

113456.excerpt_en: “You provide that little extra,” says Karin Mella, head of Svalbard Business Association, as she presents the award on Friday morning. Mella says that people who voted for Posten cited the friendliness of its employees.
113456.subtitle_en: That is what the public believes. Today, Svalbard Business Association presented proof that Posten is the service company of the year 2009.

113468.excerpt_en: Police received a report of a polar bear near the town at half past seven on Friday morning. The bear has remained on the ice in Adventfjorden all day while police kept watch over it.
113468.subtitle_en: The polar bear that has spent all day on Adventfjorden is now being flown by helicopter to Van Keulenfjorden.

113476.excerpt_en: “This is an absolutely fantastic opening,” says Line V. Roksøy, an enthusiastic press chief for Spitsbergen Rock tonight.
113476.subtitle_en: Kråkesølv opened Spitsbergen Rock on Friday evening.

113478.excerpt_en: The strike by the Norwegian Transport Workers’ Union has resulted in all terminals owned by Bring Logistics being closed. Consequently, all freight transport to Svalbard aboard “Norbjørn” has been suspended until further notice. “Norbjørn” operates a regular route between Tromsø and Longyearbyen, departing Tromsø every fourteen days.
113478.subtitle_en: Bring Logistics has cancelled “Norbjørn’s” Friday departure from Tromsø with goods for Svalbard. Zahl Transport is sailing as normal with “Green Frost”.

113491.excerpt_en: “This will be expensive for us,” confirms Line V. Roksøy, press officer for Spitsbergen Rock.
113491.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Rock is running a deficit again this year.
113491.title_en: Rock Festival Runs at a Loss

113500.excerpt_en: “The issue is that Store Norske is gagging us. We must have an opportunity to comment.”
113500.subtitle_en: Svalbard Villmarkssenter is not buying Svalbard Huskies after all. The reason is a disagreement over Store Norske’s lease contract.

113505.excerpt_en: “Conditions are a little murky at workplaces without collective agreements,” says Audun Kristoffersen, youth secretary for LO Troms. He was in Longyearbyen in mid-May to see what conditions are like for the town’s workers.
113505.subtitle_en: LO believes working conditions are questionable at several companies in the unorganised part of the restaurant and nightlife industry.

113518.excerpt_en: “Those who run the full marathon travel around the world taking part in races, and they say that the race in Longyearbyen has a distinctive character.”
113518.subtitle_en: Half of those who took part in this year’s Spitsbergen Marathon on Saturday were visitors, most of them from European countries.

113524.excerpt_en: Last Friday, “Norbjørn” was due to travel to Longyearbyen, but the trip was cancelled because of the strike. Bring Logistics has now rescheduled the departure for this coming Friday.
113524.subtitle_en: The transport strike is over, and Bring has arranged an extra trip for “Nordbjørn” on Friday.

113527.excerpt_en: Just before ten o’clock on Tuesday evening, police received a report from a guide about fresh bear tracks on Platåberget, who said the tracks led down towards Longyearbyen. “When I went up towards Sverdrupbyen to see if I could find any tracks, I spotted the bear in Nybyen,” says acting chief superintendent Per Andreassen.
113527.subtitle_en: A polar bear was chased away from Longyearbyen yesterday evening.

113539.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen was founded 104 years ago. That was when the American John M.
113539.subtitle_en: Children from Kullungen Kindergarten marked Longyearbyen’s founding day with flags and cheers.

113555.excerpt_en: The best marathon runner this year was UNIS student Gjermund Thorson Nordskar. He completed the 42-kilometre course in three hours, four minutes and 26 seconds.
113555.subtitle_en: A total of 106 runners took part in this year’s Spitsbergen Marathon.

113599.excerpt_en: “I applied for the job because it is an exciting position, and I would like to live on Svalbard,” says Aasen. She currently works as acting managing director of Undervisningsbygg Oslo and has worked in management and the public sector since 1988.
113599.subtitle_en: Marianne Stokkereit Aasen will become the new head of Bydrift.

113611.excerpt_en: Statistics Norway conducted a living-conditions survey in Longyearbyen last autumn, with 372 people over the age of 16 taking part. Nearly 60 percent of them were men.
113611.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen remains a community with a predominance of men. Virtually all of them are employed, and they earn good wages.

113622.excerpt_en: Robert Hermansen, former managing director of Store Norske, is under intense scrutiny following this week’s revelations on TV 2. The case is based on a report prepared by brokerage firm Pareto Securities for the Ministry of Trade and Industry last year.
113622.subtitle_en: Trade and Industry Minister Trond Giske (Labour) expects all private connections between Robert Hermansen and subcontractors to be investigated, according to TV 2 News.

113627.excerpt_en: It was TV 2 News that made the report on Store Norske public on Monday. The report was available on the 20th.
113627.subtitle_en: The report prepared by brokerage firm Pareto last year for the Ministry of Trade and Industry is devastating for Store Norske.

113643.excerpt_en: Robert Hermansen is resigning from all board positions with immediate effect. Earlier this week, TV 2 News published a series of critical reports about Hermansen, who was formerly managing director of Store Norske.
113643.subtitle_en: Robert Hermansen is resigning from all board positions with immediate effect.

113649.excerpt_en: The tour operator was acquitted by the Nord-Troms District Court in November last year. The prosecution appealed the case to the Court of Appeal, and today’s judgment fully upholds the prosecution’s claims.
113649.subtitle_en: The Dutch tour operator Oceanwide Expeditions was fined NOK 300,000 today by the Hålogaland Court of Appeal following the accident at Hornsund in August 2007.

113663.excerpt_en: His sentence is 36 hours of community service and a nine-month driving ban, according to the Governor’s office. He must also pay NOK 2,000 in legal costs.
113663.subtitle_en: A man in his 20s has been convicted of driving at 71 kilometres per hour in the 30 km/h zone on Hilmar Rekstens vei.

113668.excerpt_en: “I am very happy to be back in Ny-Ålesund. I have been here before, but have never attended the symposium,” said the Crown Prince, who is patron of the symposium.
113668.subtitle_en: Crown Prince Haakon was the first to take the podium when this year’s climate symposium opened this afternoon.

113670.excerpt_en: “It looked a little ugly,” says Governor’s officer Svein Olav Grini. On Tuesday evening, he went out to catch a loose dog that was chasing reindeer near the airport.
113670.subtitle_en: The Governor’s office had to catch a loose dog last night.

113683.excerpt_en: Bård Heio, Tollef Svenkerud and John-Einar Lockert have bought Huset, as well as the building housing Basecamp Spitsbergen and Kroa. The three own equal shares in Saxifraga Eiendom, which purchased the buildings.
113683.subtitle_en: The new owners all have ties to Svalbard.

113706.excerpt_en: The Amundsen Villa has been stripped. The yellow-orange cladding that has covered the building in recent years is gone, and the original exterior is once again exposed to the midnight sun. “We will now repair the damaged sections of the panelling and make the building as windproof as possible,” says adviser Bodil Paulsen of Kings Bay.
113706.subtitle_en: Roald Amundsen spent several periods in Ny-Ålesund. Work to restore the villa named after him is now well under way.
113706.title_en: The Amundsen Villa Restored to Its Original Appearance

113721.excerpt_en: Store Norske’s board has just concluded an extraordinary board meeting in Oslo, where the contractual arrangements discussed in the Pareto report were the only item on the agenda.
113721.subtitle_en: Store Norske’s board has today decided to contact the prosecuting authorities following findings made during a review of the company’s contractual arrangements.

113734.excerpt_en: According to the Governor, no one was injured in the grounding, and the ship managed to refloat under its own power. MS “Nordsyssel” has been sent to the grounded vessel.
113734.subtitle_en: The cruise ship “Polar Star” ran aground off Hornsund yesterday with 67 passengers on board.

113745.excerpt_en: “We want to err on the side of caution and transfer the passengers to ‘Fram’. They will be transported back to Longyearbyen today,” says Trygve Steen, director of Spitsbergen Travel.
113745.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Travel has sent “Fram” to Hornsund to pick up the passengers from “Polar Star”.

113748.excerpt_en: “Polar Star” may proceed to Longyearbyen escorted by the Hurtigruten ship “Fram”. Communications director Eilif Fjon of the Norwegian Maritime Authority writes this in an email to Svalbardposten. “All the passengers from ‘Polar Star’ are now aboard ‘Fram’, and morale is good,” says managing director Trygve Steen.
113748.subtitle_en: “Polar Star” has received permission from the Norwegian Maritime Authority to sail to Longyearbyen.

113774.excerpt_en: “We learned about the plaque this winter, and do not know who the person was or who put up the plaque. The church does not know either,” says cultural heritage adviser Per Kyrre Reymert at the Governor’s office.
113774.subtitle_en: Who was Viktor Kornilov, and who attached a memorial plaque to a stone by the cemetery in Longyearbyen?

113777.excerpt_en: “The ship has been cleared and approved and will sail this evening,” says Trygve Steen, managing director of Spitsbergen Travel. “Polar Star” ran aground at Hornsund on Wednesday and suffered damage to its hull. Water entered one of the ship’s compartments.
113777.subtitle_en: “Polar Star” has been sealed and will take tourists out this evening.

113790.excerpt_en: “We received a report from Store Norske on Friday. We are now reviewing it to get an overview of what it concerns,” says Deputy Governor Lars Fause.
113790.subtitle_en: Store Norske’s board has reported the contractual arrangements revealed in the Pareto report.

113799.excerpt_en: The CinemArctic board believes it has been given too little time to organise this year’s festival. “We saw that we had put together an impressive guest list.”
113799.subtitle_en: The planned CinemArctic festival will not be held this year after all.

113813.excerpt_en: When the Eiscat facility on Svalbard was planned in the early 1990s, the goal was already to have three antennas on Gruve 7 mountain. The new antenna will have a dish between 45 and 50 metres in diameter, making it the largest at the facility.
113813.subtitle_en: An antenna with a diameter of up to 50 metres is planned at the Eiscat facility.
113813.title_en: To Be Joined by a Third Antenna

113836.excerpt_en: Just after 10:30 p.m. on Saturday, police were notified of intoxicated people and a minor brawl in the town centre. “We received a complaint from Svalbar pub asking us to come by,” says Governor of Svalbard senior police officer Jill Gaustad.
113836.subtitle_en: A man was arrested for drunk driving, while two other people emptied fire extinguishers in a building on Vei 222.

113839.excerpt_en: At around nine o’clock Tuesday morning, the Governor of Svalbard was notified by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre of an accident at work on a boat 40 nautical miles north of Bear Island. They dispatched the Super Puma with a doctor and nurse on board to retrieve the fisherman.
113839.subtitle_en: Rescuers are going to retrieve a fisherman who needs medical attention after an accident at work north of Bear Island.

113850.excerpt_en: Today it became clear that Økokrim will investigate Store Norske’s contractual arrangements, which are more than ten years old. Two weeks ago, Store Norske filed a report with the Governor of Svalbard, who does not have the capacity to investigate the case.
113850.subtitle_en: The public prosecutors for Troms and Finnmark are asking Økokrim to investigate the Store Norske case.
113850.title_en: Store Norske Case Referred to Økokrim

113862.excerpt_en: “We have terminated our lease with Svalbard Museum, which is the landlord. We are moving out after this summer season.”
113862.subtitle_en: High electricity prices mean that the Spitsbergen Airship Museum is now looking for new premises.

113866.excerpt_en: “I don’t understand what happened. There was no freight service to Svalbard last night,” says Helge Rochmann, head of SAS Cargo in Tromsø.
113866.subtitle_en: SAS Cargo did not load Svalbardposten onto last night’s flight. As a result, the newspaper will not arrive until the afternoon flight.

113881.excerpt_en: “Among other things, they will check what types of paint were used on the ship and what other pollution remains on board,” says Kystverket section head Rune Bergstrøm. The Russian refrigerated ship “Petrozavodsk” ran aground south of Bear Island in May last year.
113881.subtitle_en: “Petrozavodsk” will not be removed this year. Researchers will now assess the environmental impact of leaving the ship permanently at Bear Island.

113900.excerpt_en: “The girl was part of a school class that walked from the campsite inland towards Bjørndalen on Saturday,” says Governor of Svalbard officer Ole Kristian Bækkedal. The group had come a considerable distance into Bjørndalen when they activated the emergency beacon because the 18-year-old girl had fallen ill.
113900.subtitle_en: An emergency beacon was activated in Bjørndalen yesterday afternoon. The Governor of Svalbard airlifted a sick Dutch girl by helicopter.

113932.excerpt_en: The ship has loaded 72,500 tonnes of coal at Cape Amsterdam and is the first of around 30 ships due to collect coal from Svea before this year’s shipping season ends in early November. Previously, the season started as early as 1 July.
113932.subtitle_en: “Legiony Polskie” is returning to the Netherlands today with this year’s first coal shipment from Svea.
113932.title_en: First Coal Ship of the Year

113934.excerpt_en: KomRev Nord has examined Energiverket and concluded, among other things, that poor locking procedures leave the power plant vulnerable. As things stand, the door is open between eight in the morning and four in the afternoon.
113934.subtitle_en: Energiverket is not adequately secured against unauthorised access. Now the doors will be locked.

113945.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Climate and Environment (MD) is abandoning the Norwegian Environment Agency (DN)’s proposal to allow cruise tourists to go ashore at only 16 locations in the eastern part of the archipelago. Instead, it is tasking the Governor of Svalbard with drawing up a comprehensive management plan with new regulations covering all types of traffic in the area.
113945.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Climate and Environment is asking the Governor of Svalbard to assess all traffic in the nature reserves in the eastern part of the archipelago, not just cruise traffic.

113958.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard travelled to Hyttevika today to find out what happened when a polar bear was wounded by gunfire last week. On Monday last week, the Governor of Svalbard was notified of an injured or sick polar bear near Hyttevika.
113958.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard travelled to Hyttevika today to find out what happened when a polar bear was wounded by gunfire last week.

113971.excerpt_en: “On 8 July, a Polish researcher fired a shot intended as a warning shot,” says Governor of Svalbard senior police officer Per Andreassen.
113971.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has found out what happened when a polar bear was wounded by gunfire in Hyttevika.
113971.title_en: Polish Researcher Shot the Polar Bear

114004.excerpt_en: “The man who shot the bear says it let go of his companion after the first shot, and that he then continued shooting until the magazine was empty. There were at least four shots,” says Governor of Svalbard senior police officer Per Andreassen.
114004.subtitle_en: The polar bear that attacked two kayakers on Nordaustlandet was shot several times. The bear is now in Longyearbyen.

114017.excerpt_en: A board meeting for the United Nations Foundation (UNF) in Norway is being prepared these days. The UNF was founded by CNN founder Ted Turner in 1998, and its board consists of 13 prominent people.
114017.subtitle_en: CNN founder Ted Turner may be making another high-profile visit. Joining him will be figures such as Gro Harlem Brundtland and Kofi Annan.

114044.excerpt_en: The Civil Aviation Authority has granted Trust Arktikogul an exemption to fly for Avinor in connection with the installation of three new air-navigation facilities in the archipelago. The trust uses the Russian helicopter company Air Company Spark Plus as its helicopter operator.
114044.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol’s helicopter is only authorised to fly in connection with the company’s mining operations. This summer, the Russians are flying for Avinor because the Norwegian companies were too expensive.

114075.excerpt_en: It was on TV 2 Nyhetene on Monday that Mads Gilbert compared Longyearbyen’s surgical preparedness to “a game with death as the stake”. Gilbert is chief consultant at the emergency medicine clinic at the University Hospital of North Norway, and therefore has professional responsibility for Longyearbyen Hospital.
114075.subtitle_en: If you need surgery, you must either choose the right day or hope the surgeon who is off duty is in Longyearbyen.

114088.excerpt_en: “The woman is believed to have injured her foot yesterday when she fell on or near Sveabreen,” says Governor of Svalbard officer Ole Kristian Bækkedal. She was part of an organised tour.
114088.subtitle_en: An 18-year-old English woman was flown to Longyearbyen by helicopter with an injured leg.

114096.excerpt_en: “The man is at Cape Dufferin, about 10 kilometres south of Agardh Bay. He is having equipment problems, including a leaking dry suit,” says Governor of Svalbard senior police officer Arild Lyssand.
114096.subtitle_en: A kayaker must be picked up from Spitsbergen’s east coast after experiencing equipment problems.
114096.title_en: Coast Guard to Pick Up Kayaker

114100.excerpt_en: The man, a 46-year-old German citizen, was picked up at Kapp Duffering, on the southern side of Agardhbukta, on Thursday afternoon. KV Svalbard is on a routine patrol in the waters.
114100.subtitle_en: The Coast Guard vessel Svalbard picked up the kayaker on Thursday after he reported equipment problems on the eastern side of Spitsbergen on Monday.

114104.excerpt_en: “The health minister plans to visit Svalbard next week. She will then receive a full briefing on the situation and meet those working at the hospital,” says Knut Albert Solem, communications adviser at the Ministry of Health and Care Services.
114104.subtitle_en: Emergency preparedness at Longyearbyen Hospital is a concern. The health minister will visit Svalbard next week.

114119.excerpt_en: In a letter to the Governor’s Office, Priitta and Anton Trøen of Spitsbergen Experience write that “lowering the ridge by 80 centimetres entails completely demolishing the structure down to the platform floor and rebuilding it from there.” “That means the cabin must be demolished down to the first floor to reduce its height by 80 centimetres.”
114119.subtitle_en: Large parts of the commercial cabin in Adolfbukta must be demolished if its illegal height is to be reduced. That is the view of Spitsbergen Experience.
114119.title_en: Cabin Must Be Demolished to Lower It

114129.excerpt_en: “Between 11 and 11:30 today, we discovered that one of the petrol pumps was leaking,” says Roger Eriksen, general manager of Svalbard Auto. The petrol station therefore had to be cordoned off, and the fire brigade was called.
114129.subtitle_en: Svalbard Auto closed on Friday morning because of a leak from a petrol pump.

114132.excerpt_en: Just before 6:30 p.m. on Saturday, the Governor’s Office received a report of an American tourist who had injured her knee on a hike and was unable to get back to Longyearbyen without assistance.
114132.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office had to retrieve an American tourist who injured her knee on a guided tour.

114165.excerpt_en: “We received a report of a fire in Brucebyen at five past three yesterday,” says senior police officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office. Brucebyen consists of three large cabins and a small hut.
114165.subtitle_en: One of the cabins in Billefjorden burned to the ground yesterday afternoon.

114183.excerpt_en: According to nrk.no, the Civil Aviation Authority has given Boeing permission to test its new Dreamliner at Longyearbyen Airport. The tests will be conducted without passengers.
114183.subtitle_en: Within the next month, a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner will make test landings and takeoffs at Longyearbyen Airport.

114200.excerpt_en: Three years ago, during the 2007–08 season, Nils Aga overwintered with his wife, Tordis Aga, at the Austfjordnes trapping station in Wijdefjorden. The lawyer is now among the eleven applicants for a position with the Governor’s Office.
114200.subtitle_en: Among the eleven applicants for the position of deputy governor is lawyer and former trapper Nils Aga, 64, from Bodø.

114221.excerpt_en: “A man at Hotellneset saw a person in a single kayak capsize and was unable to get back into the kayak without help,” says duty senior police officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office.
114221.subtitle_en: The tourist vessel Polargirl picked up a kayaker in Adventfjorden this morning after he capsized.

114231.excerpt_en: Today was the first day of school in Longyearbyen. It was an especially important day for the 20 pupils starting first grade and having their very first day at school.
114231.subtitle_en: Twenty brand-new pupils had to come on stage and greet the principal today.

114235.excerpt_en: “On Monday afternoon, the Governor’s Office received a call from Barentsburg. Someone had found a Greenland dog running loose in town,” says Governor’s Office officer Ole Kristian Bækkedal.
114235.subtitle_en: The German tourists who lost a Greenland dog in Barentsburg on Monday have got it back.

114245.excerpt_en: “The animal was hit in such a way that some time probably passed between it being shot and its death. We do not know how long it survived after being wounded,” says Governor’s Office officer Ole Kristian Bækkedal.
114245.subtitle_en: A reindeer found dead in Hollendardalen on Saturday had been wounded by gunfire before it died.
114245.title_en: Died After Being Wounded by Gunfire

114255.excerpt_en: The National Authority for Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Environmental Crime has carried out a major operation to secure evidence across the country. Chief Public Prosecutor Bård Thorsen of the authority would not comment to TV2 on the ongoing investigation, other than to say that extensive evidence-gathering was under way.
114255.subtitle_en: According to TV2 News, Robert Hermansen was questioned by the National Authority for Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Environmental Crime today after being charged with aggravated breach of trust.
114255.title_en: Charged with Aggravated Breach of Trust

114272.excerpt_en: Relations between Esso Norge and Kings Bay, which owns Ny-Ålesund, have grown increasingly tense throughout the summer.
114272.subtitle_en: As a solution to a dispute with Kings Bay, Esso Norge threatened this summer to empty the diesel tanks in Ny-Ålesund. That would have brought all activity at the site to a halt.

114282.excerpt_en: “Here we have the opportunity to follow the entire energy chain for carbon, from coal being extracted from the mine to CO2 being stored underground. And it all takes place within a radius of seven kilometres,” says Snorre Olaussen, a professor of Arctic petroleum geology at UNIS.
114282.subtitle_en: UNIS wants to give students the opportunity to learn what happens to carbon after it is extracted from the mine as coal.

114293.excerpt_en: “We are keeping the bear under observation,” says senior police officer Sidsel Svarstad of the Governor’s Office. She says the animal was spotted from the Governor’s Office at 11 this morning. “We have notified those who were due to take trips to Hiorthhamn.”
114293.subtitle_en: A polar bear is staying in Hiorthhamn, where it has a walrus carcass to feed on.

114296.excerpt_en: The bear was first spotted from the Governor’s Office on Monday. It was then eating a walrus carcass that had washed ashore in Hiorthhamn.
114296.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard removed the walrus carcass in Hiorthhamn. Since then, the polar bear has stayed away.

114299.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Food Safety Authority has received a tip that there is a cat in Longyearbyen. “We will ask the police to investigate the case. We consider it extremely serious that anyone defies the measures we introduce to prevent infectious disease,” says Harald Os, a special inspector with the Norwegian Food Safety Authority.
114299.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Food Safety Authority is reacting strongly to a cat being spotted in Longyearbyen despite the ban on the animal. In Barentsburg, cats have roamed freely for years.

114310.excerpt_en: “People in Longyearbyen flocked to Knut Lindvig’s exhibitions when he still lived on Svalbard,” says Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik.
114310.subtitle_en: An exhibition of photographs by former Store Norske mechanic Knut Lindvig, 86, opens at Funken on Tuesday.

114313.excerpt_en: One of them lies at the foot of Gruve 7 Mountain and belongs to Ragnheid Skogseth and Frank Nilsen. The bear forced its way through the cabin door, wrecked the kitchen and turned one of the hotplates on an electric stove up to full power.
114313.subtitle_en: A polar bear has broken into at least three cabins in the area between Gruve 7 Mountain and Foxdalen.

114337.excerpt_en: “The aircraft first made a low pass over the airport, then circled and landed ahead of schedule,” says airport manager Ole M. Rambech.
114337.subtitle_en: The Boeing 787 Dreamliner, a dream aircraft, landed at Svalbard Airport on Wednesday afternoon and attracted considerable attention from the many people who had turned up.

114366.excerpt_en: “We’re really looking forward to it. Timbuktu is a major artist,” says Zandra Zadewasser, restaurant manager at Kroa.
114366.subtitle_en: Swedish rapper Timbuktu is performing at Kroa tomorrow.
114366.title_en: Invites People to a Music Festival

114369.excerpt_en: After several rounds in the Norwegian courts, the Hornsund case is now moving to the English legal system. The case came before the High Court in London for an initial hearing last Thursday, after 16 of the injured passengers sued Discover the World.
114369.subtitle_en: The cruise passengers injured in Hornsund three years ago are suing the British tour operator Discover the World.

114395.excerpt_en: “Paying for excess weight by the kilo is over. The rules will be easier for customers to understand.”
114395.subtitle_en: SAS is introducing new baggage rules, and from now on you will have to pay for an extra piece of luggage if your baggage is too heavy.

114399.excerpt_en: For many years, Svalbardposten has written about the shortage of homes on Longyearbyen’s private market. The market has now changed, and several people are finding it difficult to sell their homes.
114399.subtitle_en: No one wants to buy homes in Longyearbyen at the moment, but the rental market is booming.

114411.excerpt_en: “Those of us who currently rent from Longyearbyen Local Council should not have to pay for inadequate maintenance in the past,” says Tom Ramberg, head of the Education Union in Longyearbyen. The basis of Longyearbyen Local Council’s housing scheme is that it should pay for itself.
114411.subtitle_en: Employees of Longyearbyen Local Council fear higher rents.
114411.title_en: Housing Dispute in Longyearbyen Local Council

114420.excerpt_en: The Governor’s Office received a message from the sailing boat’s captain at 3:20 p.m. saying that the vessel was in trouble. Twenty passengers and five crew members were on board, and the ship was in danger of being squeezed into the shore by the ice, the Governor’s Office reports on its website.
114420.subtitle_en: The Dutch sailing vessel Noorderlicht ran into trouble with pack ice north of Hinlopen Strait on Saturday afternoon.

114425.excerpt_en: The rescue helicopter was dispatched this afternoon to search for the two women, who had not returned at the agreed time after a hunting trip in Bjørndalen, the Governor’s Office writes on its website. Became stranded: The women had entered difficult terrain and become stuck on a mountain ledge.
114425.subtitle_en: The Governor’s rescue helicopter brought two women in their twenties down from the mountains in Bjørndalen. The women were found safe and well at around 4 p.m. this afternoon.

114436.excerpt_en: The works in question are watercolours hanging on the gallery’s north-facing wall. Above the paintings are 15 windows that now need to be replaced.
114436.subtitle_en: The backing boards on two of Kåre Tveter’s paintings at Galleri Svalbard had to be replaced after being damaged by water during the winter.

114444.excerpt_en: “This means we have to reassess the basis for operations,” says Trygve Steen, managing director of Spitsbergen Travel. He says the Polar Hotel concept is built around food and wine. “We have to change the entire business concept.”
114444.subtitle_en: The local council does not want alcohol service at the cultural centre. Spitsbergen Travel is now reconsidering its plans.

114447.excerpt_en: “The energy plant is Longyearbyen’s heart, supplying electricity, heat and infrastructure. I would say it is the most important building in Longyearbyen.”
114447.subtitle_en: The reserve power station in Longyearbyen lacks firefighting equipment.

114460.excerpt_en: The state-owned company Kings Bay, which owns and operates Ny-Ålesund, has been in conflict with Esso Norway for some time over the storage facility in Ny-Ålesund. The dispute stems from an order by the Norwegian Climate and Pollution Agency (Klif) requiring Esso Norway to secure the facility it owns in Ny-Ålesund against leaks.
114460.subtitle_en: The conflict between Esso Norway and Kings Bay is escalating. The oil company is resorting to falsehoods to put further pressure on Kings Bay.
114460.title_en: Esso Norway Puts Pressure on Kings Bay

114468.excerpt_en: The two executives at the construction company have been charged by Økokrim with aggravated corruption in the ongoing case involving Store Norske and former managing director Robert Hermansen. Shock: “This has come as a shock to all of us.”
114468.subtitle_en: Managing director Malvin Nilsen and chair Frode Nilsen of Leonhard Nilsen & Sønner AS (LNS) are stepping down from their positions.

114488.excerpt_en: Store Norske managing director Bjørn Arnestad says he is taking the corruption allegations against the managing director seriously.
114488.subtitle_en: The corruption allegations against the managing director and chair of Leonhard Nilsen & Sønner are creating challenges in its cooperation with Store Norske.
114488.title_en: Corruption Charges Put Cooperation to the Test

114491.excerpt_en: “The government is committed to establishing a faster and more efficient rescue helicopter service that can come to the aid of as many people as possible in a difficult situation,” State Secretary Terje Moland Pedersen says in a press release from the Ministry of Justice.
114491.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s rescue helicopter service will be substantially strengthened in the future. It will most likely consist of two large helicopters and a considerably higher level of preparedness.
114491.title_en: Plans to Strengthen Svalbard Helicopter Preparedness

114503.excerpt_en: The government is proposing an increase of NOK 4.8 million for UNIS to establish 20 new study places and continue 20 new study places from last year. A total allocation of NOK 97.2 million is proposed.
114503.subtitle_en: At 10 a.m. today, the government presented its proposal for next year’s national budget.
114503.title_en: University and Museum to Receive Boost

114512.excerpt_en: “My first impression is very good. There are many positive people here with a strong professional interest,” says Marianne S.
114512.subtitle_en: Marianne S. Aasen (42) is the new managing director of Bydrift.
114512.title_en: Ready to Take on the Challenge

114530.excerpt_en: At present, there is no doctor on call as backup at Longyearbyen Hospital.
114530.subtitle_en: The University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) wants to increase staffing at Longyearbyen Hospital so it can handle more simultaneous emergencies.

114539.excerpt_en: The conflict between Esso Norway and Kings Bay, which owns and operates Ny-Ålesund, threatened for a time to plunge the research settlement into darkness. The parties have now agreed that Kings Bay will take over the storage facility and receive NOK 500,000 in compensation.
114539.subtitle_en: Kings Bay is taking over the diesel storage facility in Ny-Ålesund after a long-running dispute with Esso Norway.
114539.title_en: Esso Norway and Kings Bay Reach Agreement

114565.excerpt_en: On 8 August 2007, the Russian coastal cruise ship Aleksey Maryshev was hit by a rogue wave and chunks of ice when Storbreen glacier at the head of Hornsund calved.
114565.subtitle_en: The accident that injured 23 people aboard a cruise ship in Hornsund three years ago is heading to the Supreme Court.

114578.excerpt_en: Since January, Svalbard Museum has been working to digitize its photograph collection. The first result of this work is now available, with 3,000 photographs posted online and made searchable.
114578.subtitle_en: On Thursday evening, Svalbard Museum launched its new website, allowing anyone to search through old photographs.

114589.excerpt_en: “There were four students hiking on Sarkofagen who fired a red flare at something they were not entirely sure about,” says duty senior police officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office. Sarkofagen lies at the head of Longyeardalen, between Larsbreen and Longyearbreen.
114589.subtitle_en: Four students who fired a red signal flare on Sarkofagen prompted a response by the Governor’s Super Puma helicopter at around 7:30 p.m.

114591.excerpt_en: “The audience can expect plenty of great music. There will be major names from both Norway and abroad, and music both to dance to and listen to,” says Dark Season Blues director Marianne B.
114591.subtitle_en: Next Thursday, people can once again enjoy the blues in Longyearbyen.
114591.title_en: Ready for a New Blues Festival

114595.excerpt_en: After suffering for a long time from sore, watery eyes, a sore throat and headaches, Knut Johannessen decided to pay for Mycoteam to analyse samples from the home.
114595.subtitle_en: Store Norske is clearing out two houses on Skjæringa after alarming levels of health-threatening mould were found.
114595.title_en: Forced to Move Because of Mould

114606.excerpt_en: “We received a report at 8 p.m. that a man had been found lifeless at the power station in Barentsburg,” says Senior Police Officer Sidsel Svarstad of the Governor’s Office. The man was in his mid-fifties and was working at the power station.
114606.subtitle_en: A Russian man was found dead in Barentsburg on Sunday evening.

114612.excerpt_en: Today, the tax lists were published nationwide. The overview of Svalbard’s taxpayers can be viewed on the ground floor of the Post and Bank Building.
114612.subtitle_en: You can now find out who is the richest person on the island.

114615.excerpt_en: Yesterday, Thursday, Dark Season Blues, the festival of the blues, got under way in Longyearbyen. One of the headline acts is Noora Noor.
114615.subtitle_en: Ledfoot had to play alone when Noora Noor missed her flight on Thursday.

114627.excerpt_en: “We have service personnel here carrying out a safety check at the plant. They did something we do not have an overview of,” says energy manager Knut Flå.
114627.subtitle_en: The power went out twice last night. First, something went wrong during servicing at the plant. Then the power station had trouble switching from backup power to the main power plant.
114627.title_en: Power Failure at the Power Station

114636.excerpt_en: The case involving the warehouse that Australian Jason Roberts converted into a residence has followed the Governor for more than four years. The building stands right next to Taubanesentralen in Skjæringa, just a stone’s throw from the Governor’s office building.
114636.subtitle_en: After several years of dispute, the Governor said this summer that everything was in order concerning Taubanelageret. The Ministry of the Environment strongly disagrees.

114640.excerpt_en: “We have spoken with a number of interested parties. We can say that there will not be another large café like Busen.”
114640.subtitle_en: There will be no restaurant in the premises formerly occupied by Kafé Busen. Instead, the space will be converted into shops.

114650.excerpt_en: Shortly before 11 a.m. on Friday, the Governor was notified that an all-terrain vehicle carrying two people had gone off the road by the bridge in Endalen. A group of five people and a guide were on an ATV trip in Endalen.
114650.subtitle_en: A woman in her sixties was taken to hospital for a check-up after driving off the road in Endalen.

114660.excerpt_en: It was by chance that journalist Julie C. Knarvik and photographer Sverre Chr.
114660.subtitle_en: The story of trapper Tommy Sandal (37) on Austfjordnes has been captured and bound between hard covers.

114771.excerpt_en: The Art and Crafts Centre is preparing for this year’s Art Break. Fabrics will be cut, photographs framed and paintings completed.
114771.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen will soon be able to enjoy a well-deserved Art Break.

114779.excerpt_en: A total of 80 participants took part in this year’s final sports exchange at Svalbardhallen on Saturday. “The matches went very well, and the atmosphere was great, as it always is,” says Christian Svarstad, coordinator at Svalbard Turn.
114779.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen took the most victories during this weekend’s sports exchange.

114789.excerpt_en: In recent years, the Governor’s vessel has not weighed anchor until the first Sunday of Advent. Then townspeople have been able to wave goodbye, the Governor has given a speech and choral singing has rung out across the quay.
114789.subtitle_en: Yesterday, the Governor’s vessel “Nordsyssel” left Svalbard without any fanfare.

114805.excerpt_en: Seventy-one of Svalbard’s species are classified as red-listed in the new overview from the Norwegian Biodiversity Information Centre. Five of them are new additions to the list, which was last updated in 2006.
114805.subtitle_en: The thick-billed murre is a new entry on the Norwegian Red List for Species 2010, published on Tuesday. The Svalbard population has declined sharply in recent years.
114805.title_en: New Species Added to the Red List

114818.excerpt_en: In January, a new surgeon specializing in obstetrics and gynaecology will arrive in Longyearbyen.
114818.subtitle_en: From next year, pregnant women will probably no longer have to travel to Tromsø for ultrasound examinations.

114841.excerpt_en: “We are very pleased. The impression is that the houses have been full.”
114841.subtitle_en: “Tregangertre” was packed, while the theatre production “Eksperimentet” was half full.

114848.excerpt_en: The annual exercise weekend is approaching. Two instructors from the mainland will come to work on our fitness, coordination, mobility and balance.
114848.subtitle_en: On Friday, it is time to get out the tracksuit and gym shoes. For three days, the town’s residents will be getting active.

114851.excerpt_en: “In August last year, I spent some time in Ny-Ålesund on a grant from the Norwegian Association of Visual Artists, walking around with a video camera and filming a great deal,” says Stana.
114851.subtitle_en: Next week, Norwegian visual artist Ingeborg Stana will take part in a film festival in St. Petersburg with her film “Ny-Ålesund.”

114872.excerpt_en: The inquiry was initially addressed to the Governor by Danish company MT Højgaard AS, which is involved in the operation.
114872.subtitle_en: An Australian mining company, which will begin extracting zinc in northeastern Greenland next year, wants to use Longyearbyen Hospital as an emergency hospital.

114875.excerpt_en: “Now that the cultural centre has opened, it is important that Huset becomes attractive. We will raise the standard,” says Bård Heio.
114875.subtitle_en: Work to renovate and remodel the ground floor of Huset is already underway.

114887.excerpt_en: This winter there will be more northern lights than last year because we are emerging from a low point in the Sun’s activity cycle. Professor Dag Lorentzen has tips for aurora hunters.
114887.subtitle_en: Here is advice if you want to go hunting for the northern lights.

114901.excerpt_en: “We are extremely pleased. Before, we were probably lucky if we won one match, but now so many people play football that we can easily win a few matches,” says Trond Martin Gustavsen.
114901.subtitle_en: Young footballers made the town proud during the Julestjerna tournament in Tromsø this weekend.

114913.excerpt_en: Bydrift did not want the skate ramp standing in front of the entrance to the new cultural centre. The children’s popular meeting place has now been moved to the square.
114913.subtitle_en: The skate ramp was moved from the youth club to the square today, Tuesday.

114915.excerpt_en: The repercussions of the accident in August 2007, when Storbreen calved in Hornsund and 23 tourists aboard the coastal cruise ship Aleksey Maryshev were injured, have still not subsided.
114915.subtitle_en: There will be no court case over the Hornsund accident after the tour operators agreed to compensation claims in England.

114932.excerpt_en: After Christmas, the e-paper will be Svalbardposten’s digital alternative. “The PDF will be discontinued from 2011, and we are adopting a system used by very many newspapers and magazines,” says editor Birger Amundsen.
114932.subtitle_en: After New Year, Svalbardposten will no longer be available in PDF format.

114940.excerpt_en: “Two of the drivers we stopped had blood alcohol levels below the criminal threshold. It indicates that they had been drinking,” says Senior Police Officer Erik Nygaard of the Governor’s Office.
114940.subtitle_en: No one was caught driving under the influence in the early hours of Sunday, but two drivers tested positive on the breathalyzer.

114943.excerpt_en: In August, former Store Norske director Robert Hermansen was charged with aggravated economic infidelity. The charge has been changed to corruption, NRK reports.
114943.subtitle_en: Robert Hermansen has been charged with aggravated corruption.

114955.excerpt_en: According to the Governor, it is an aggravating circumstance that the man has previously been fined for violence. The man, who lives in Longyearbyen, has admitted hitting the bouncer.
114955.subtitle_en: A man in his twenties has been fined NOK 10,000 for hitting a bouncer at Huset in the early hours of Saturday.

114988.excerpt_en: Lars Erik Alfheim, 39, currently works as a state prosecutor at the Oslo State Prosecutor’s Office. He will join the Governor’s Office in April. “I have worked extensively on criminal cases, where the level of conflict is high.”
114988.subtitle_en: State prosecutor Lars Erik Alfheim has been appointed the new deputy governor after Lars Fause.

115004.excerpt_en: “We apologize!” says the Longyearbyen local council’s website today.
115004.subtitle_en: This weekend’s film screenings have been cancelled because an important part for the cinema projector is missing.

115012.excerpt_en: Robert Hermansen, charged with corruption, was elected to the local council for the Labour Party in 2007 and remained there after stepping down as head of Store Norske. Hermansen is still on the local council and chairs the council’s control committee.
115012.subtitle_en: Robert Hermansen resigned from all his positions, but not from the local council after being charged by Økokrim.

115026.excerpt_en: The review conducted by Store Norske concludes that the agreement with Jebsen was overpriced. The agreement with Jebsen ran until 2022.
115026.subtitle_en: Store Norske is ending its cooperation with Kristian Jebsen Rederi AS on coal transport from Svalbard.

115037.excerpt_en: “This is one of the highlights of the year,” says parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen of Svalbard Church. On Tuesday, he travelled to the Polish research station in Hornsund together with Catholic priest Miroslaw Ksiazek and representatives of the Governor’s Office.
115037.subtitle_en: There was a festive Christmas atmosphere for both guests and hosts at the research station in Hornsund.

115061.excerpt_en: December 13 is Saint Lucy’s Day, and it was marked with a Lucia procession at the library.
115061.subtitle_en: Today, the whole town is filled with soft children’s voices, lights and saffron buns.

115072.excerpt_en: The Governor’s office building at Skjæringa is bursting at the seams. Chief Administrative Officer Øyvind Alnæs has now prepared an overview showing that an extension of 387 square metres is needed.
115072.subtitle_en: While the Governor awaits an expansion of the control offices at Skjæringa, the office is applying to put up two portable buildings.

115076.excerpt_en: “In addition to terminating the contract with the shipping company, we are demanding that Jebsen repay what we overpaid,” says Store Norske CEO Bjørn Arnestad. Kristian Jebsen’s shipping company has had an agreement with Store Norske to transport coal from Svalbard since 1965.
115076.subtitle_en: Store Norske is demanding that Kristian Jebsen’s shipping company repay several hundred million kroner. The company believes it overpaid for transporting coal from Svea.

115098.excerpt_en: The group of four left Svea for Longyearbyen on three snowmobiles on Sunday afternoon. Around 9 p.m., the Governor was notified that the group had not arrived by the agreed time. “We sent a helicopter and Red Cross personnel to search.”
115098.subtitle_en: The Governor launched a search operation when four people failed to return at the agreed time yesterday evening.

115108.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten was informed this morning that the mail plane had not prioritized transporting the newspaper’s Christmas edition from Tromsø to Svalbard today. “It’s regrettable, sad and irritating.”
115108.subtitle_en: The mail plane had no room for Svalbardposten today.

115121.excerpt_en: In November last year, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) adopted a model for upper-secondary education under which students have three teacherless lessons a week. The model also means that some subjects are offered only every other year.
115121.subtitle_en: Upper-secondary students are not receiving approved education. The school is not complying with the law, and the students risk not receiving valid diplomas.

115140.excerpt_en: The sailing ship “Noorderlicht” arrived in Longyearbyen on Monday morning. The vessel is chartered by Basecamp Spitsbergen and will freeze into the ice in Tempelfjorden for the tenth consecutive year, serving as accommodation for tourists.
115140.subtitle_en: The small Russian icebreaker “A. Belikov” will break “Noorderlicht” into Tempelfjorden on Christmas Eve.
115140.title_en: Icebreaker to Clear a Passage on Christmas Eve

115142.excerpt_en: In the summer of 2007, Spitsbergen Experience was granted permission to build a cabin in Adolfbukta in Billefjorden. During an inspection in October last year, the Governor of Svalbard learned that the cabin was 80 centimetres higher than shown in the approved drawings.
115142.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Experience has been fined NOK 15,000 for building its commercial cabin in Adolfbukta too high.

115155.excerpt_en: “I am very pleased that the Supreme Court has followed the Court of Appeal’s—and especially the prosecution’s—view. It has been a long battle with three rounds in court, but I am glad that we were ultimately vindicated,” says deputy governor Lars Fause.
115155.subtitle_en: The Supreme Court rejects Oceanwide Expeditions’ appeal in the Hornsund case.

115170.excerpt_en: At 10 p.m. on Christmas Day, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that a man had not returned as agreed after a snowmobile trip to Barentsburg. “We then launched an operation to find out where he was.”
115170.subtitle_en: Things were quiet in Longyearbyen over Christmas, but on Christmas Day the Governor of Svalbard had to launch a search operation.

115173.excerpt_en: “We have been working towards this for a long time, and I think it is absolutely fantastic,” says pollution adviser Halvard R. Pedersen at the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
115173.subtitle_en: The last fluorescent lamps containing hazardous pollutants will soon be shipped off the island.
115173.title_en: The PCB Project Comes to an End

115189.excerpt_en: The fox approached the meteorological station, which has four dogs, on Tuesday (Correction: The Norwegian Food Safety Authority previously stated that the attack occurred on Wednesday; the correct day is Tuesday). “It attacked the dogs, and eventually the dogs killed the fox,” says Arne Mjøs, district director of the Norwegian Food Safety Authority in Tromsø.
115189.subtitle_en: An Arctic fox attacked the dogs at the meteorological station on Hopen. The fox is now being tested for rabies.

115207.excerpt_en: This autumn, Store Norske terminated its agreement with the American company Oxbow Corporation concerning coal sales. The agreement, which ran until 2015, will now be settled in court.
115207.subtitle_en: Store Norske and Oxbow Corporation will face off in Oslo District Court this autumn.

115222.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, the Arctic fox attacked the dogs at Hopen Meteorological Station. It tried to bite the dogs’ legs and bit one of them on the nose.
115222.subtitle_en: The fox that attacked dogs at Hopen had rabies.

115233.excerpt_en: “On the advice of the Norwegian Veterinary Institute, we have concluded that we will take blood samples from the dogs,” says Arne Mjøs of the Norwegian Food Safety Authority. The dogs are vaccinated against rabies, and the blood tests will show whether they have sufficient rabies antibodies.
115233.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Food Safety Authority will take blood samples from the dogs attacked by the rabid fox on Tuesday. It will then assess whether the dogs can live or must be put down.

115236.excerpt_en: The number of travellers to and from Svalbard Airport, Longyear, was 125,800 last year, according to Avinor. That was 28.3 percent fewer than the previous year.
115236.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Airport had far fewer visitors last year than the year before.

115258.excerpt_en: The report confirms that the wreck contains dangerous pollutants, including brominated flame retardants, mercury and lead.
115258.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard recommends that the Norwegian Coastal Administration remove the wreck of the “Petrozavodsk” after receiving an environmental report showing that the ship contains a range of hazardous pollutants.

115264.excerpt_en: Tour operator Spitsbergen Experience built its commercial cabin in Adolfbukta in Billefjorden 80 centimetres higher than the company was permitted to. In October, the Governor of Svalbard ruled that Spitsbergen Experience did not have to rebuild the cabin.
115264.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Climate and Environment disagrees with the Governor of Svalbard that Spitsbergen Experience should be allowed to avoid rebuilding the cabin in Adolfbukta.

115272.excerpt_en: “Tyson,” our best bear dog, alerted us. We thought it was a bear, but it turned out to be a fox,” says station manager Ragnar Sønstebø by telephone from Hopen Meteorological Station.
115272.subtitle_en: The crew at Hopen hope the dogs bitten by the fox will survive. They themselves are not worried about rabies infection.

115277.excerpt_en: “We are going to mark the fact that this is the Nansen-Amundsen Year,” says Eva Therese Jenssen, information adviser at UNIS. She is one of the organizers of the Svalbard Seminar, which begins on Tuesday.
115277.subtitle_en: Over the next three weeks, you can learn more about Amundsen, Nansen, seabirds and Svalbard politics.

115289.excerpt_en: This week, the students on the Arctic Nature Guide course have been preparing for barbecuing and ice bathing tomorrow evening. When Svalbardposten meets the students, they have just begun the work.
115289.subtitle_en: Tomorrow, Arctic nature guides are hosting Spitsbergen Hot n Cold.
115289.title_en: Invites People for an Ice Bath

115301.excerpt_en: Last week, the Governor of Svalbard recommended that the Norwegian Coastal Administration remove the wreck of the Russian refrigerated cargo ship “Petrozavodsk.”
115301.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration will determine how much it would cost to remove the “Petrozavodsk” before deciding the ship’s fate.

115308.excerpt_en: The four dogs at Hopen Meteorological Station came into contact with a rabid fox two weeks ago. On Saturday, one of the four men staying on the island was bitten by one of the dogs. “He wasn’t bitten because the dog was aggressive.”
115308.subtitle_en: One of the residents at Hopen was bitten by one of the dogs at the meteorological station on Saturday.

115315.excerpt_en: “We got the result we wanted. All the dogs have sufficient rabies antibodies,” says Arne Mjøs, district director of the Norwegian Food Safety Authority in Tromsø.
115315.subtitle_en: Blood tests show that the dogs at Hopen are protected against rabies.

115330.excerpt_en: Kristian Svarstad won the competition in 54 minutes and 10 seconds. Last year’s winner, Sigmund Andersen, came second, completing the trip in 58 minutes and 15 seconds.
115330.subtitle_en: 82 people signed up for today’s race to Trolsteinen. The winner took 54 minutes up and down.

115334.excerpt_en: This year marks 150 years since Fridtjof Nansen was born and 100 years since Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole. “Just think of the significance they had while they were alive.”
115334.subtitle_en: The Nansen-Amundsen Year opens in Tromsø today. The heroes will also be honored on Svalbard during 2011.

115346.excerpt_en: “The service should be more consistent than it is today. At present, it is random how often there is a veterinarian on Svalbard, and the service is governed by vaccination schedules rather than the pet owners’ need for veterinary care.”
115346.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard supports the dog club’s proposal to strengthen veterinary services in Longyearbyen.

115356.excerpt_en: On Thursday afternoon, the Governor of Svalbard was notified by airport staff that a passenger was too drunk to board the flight from Longyearbyen to the mainland that day.
115356.subtitle_en: A man will have to stay one night longer than planned in Longyearbyen.

115390.excerpt_en: The popular jazz singer has the honor of opening this year’s jazz festival in Longyearbyen, with a concert at the Polar Hotel on Thursday evening. Festival director Lasse Stener Hansen is delighted to have Slettahjell on the program.
115390.subtitle_en: Solveig Slettahjell was one of last year’s Polarjazz headliners. She had to cancel then, but she is coming this year.

115402.excerpt_en: The man lives in Longyearbyen and is in his early 30s. He planned to ski to Ny-Ålesund with a dog, but was picked up by the Governor of Svalbard at Gipsvika.
115402.subtitle_en: A man who planned to ski from Longyearbyen to Ny-Ålesund ran into trouble because of the cold on Sunday. He was picked up by the Governor of Svalbard in the afternoon.

115415.excerpt_en: “It is clear that this is hugely popular,” says festival director Lasse Stener Hansen after Wednesday’s jazz pre-party. Around 200 people watched the 40 local artists who took the stage across 19 performances.
115415.subtitle_en: The festival opened with local singers, bands, a world premiere and angels. See the photo gallery!

115423.excerpt_en: The ship touched bottom, causing damage to the outer hull. The International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO) issued a press release about the incident the same day.
115423.subtitle_en: On Monday, the cruise ship “Polar Star” had an accident while anchoring in Antarctica.

115429.excerpt_en: The darkness has begun to lift, and the tourism industry is optimistic about the future. Basecamp started the season unusually early two weeks ago with a residents’ trip to “Noorderlicht,” which is frozen into the ice in Tempelfjorden.
115429.subtitle_en: For those who have not done so, it is time to fire up the snowmobile. Tour operators have been under way for a long time.

115443.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Kjell Mork (Labour) has the support of the Conservative Party and the Cross-Party Joint List. They do not share Jon Sandmo’s lack of confidence. “I have exceptionally strong confidence in him.”
115443.subtitle_en: Local Council leader Kjell Mork (Labour) has the support of the Conservative Party and the Cross-Party Joint List. They do not share Jon Sandmo’s lack of confidence.

115448.excerpt_en: Seven experts with many years of experience sailing in the eastern areas of Svalbard have been brought in to analyze the probability of ship accidents in eastern Svalbard. The greatest threat to all shipping in the east is inadequate surveying and incomplete nautical charts.
115448.subtitle_en: Experts on sailing around eastern Svalbard propose mapping safe corridors in the least charted areas.

115451.excerpt_en: “We were notified by a cabin owner at Vindodden that the ice had broken up near the shore,” says Chief Superintendent Erik Nygaard. The report came at around 8 p.m. Friday and stated that two snowmobiles had gone through the ice at Vindodden.
115451.subtitle_en: Two snowmobiles broke through the ice at Vindodden. The Governor of Svalbard warns against driving on the ice in the area.
