115470.excerpt_en: “Around 550 people came on Saturday night, and I don’t think we have ever had so many people inside before,” says Polarjazz board member Helen Flå.
115470.subtitle_en: Record numbers turned out to hear Halvdan Sivertsen perform at Polarjazz.

115472.excerpt_en: In a letter to Store Norske Gull (SNG), the Governor of Svalbard writes that the company’s helicopter use deviated from what it was authorized to do. The Governor considers the deviations so serious that it is considering reporting the company if similar deviations are uncovered in the future.
115472.subtitle_en: Store Norske Gull has received a warning from the Governor of Svalbard for making too many helicopter landings during gold exploration in St. Jonsfjorden.

115489.excerpt_en: The rock festival owes NOK 140,000 after last year’s festival. “We are charging NOK 200 for a ticket to the concert, and we are telling people they can give more if they wish. That would make us happy,” says Hege Jakobsen, who was the festival’s finance officer.
115489.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Rock is holding a concert with rappers OnklP and Jaa9 to pay down its debt.

115516.excerpt_en: “It was the boiler at the power plant that stopped. If it receives signals it does not like, it is supposed to stop, but we do not yet know what happened,” says energy manager Knut Flå of Bydrift.
115516.subtitle_en: The power went out across Longyearbyen on Friday evening.

115518.excerpt_en: At 9:30 this morning, the Governor of Svalbard was notified of a polar bear near the town dog yard just outside Longyearbyen. The bear is believed to have found some seal meat to eat.
115518.subtitle_en: The polar bear that came to Longyearbyen on Saturday is now staying out on the ice on Adventfjorden.

115535.excerpt_en: Ten teams took part in this year’s first dog race on Svalbard. The winner was Solfrid Haakenstad, who completed the course in 2 hours and 22 minutes.
115535.subtitle_en: Solfrid Haakenstad won this year’s Hilmar Nøis’ Trail.

115545.excerpt_en: “It is wrong to think that there will not be more polar-bear incidents, given the thick, good ice and the fact that the bears are moving on the fjord. People must remain vigilant and report any polar bears they see in the vicinity,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen.
115545.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen, Barentsburg and Isfjord Radio were all visited by polar bears this weekend. Extensive fjord ice makes it easier for the bears to move around. A polar bear was also spotted on Adventfjorden today.

115547.excerpt_en: Just after 4 p.m. yesterday, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that a tourist in a guided snowmobile group had been injured near Semmelbu in Semmeldalen. “He developed back pain from riding, but it was not believed to be serious,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen.
115547.subtitle_en: A man was picked up by helicopter near Semmelbu yesterday afternoon after injuring his back.

115549.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the bear at 2:15 a.m. today. “It had found something to eat near the dog yard,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen.
115549.subtitle_en: A polar bear was chased away from the dog yard just outside Longyearbyen again last night.
115549.title_en: Chased Polar Bear Away from Dog Yard

115559.excerpt_en: A dog was killed by a polar bear yesterday afternoon near the Polish research station in Hornsund.
115559.subtitle_en: A dog was killed by a polar bear yesterday afternoon near the Polish research station in Hornsund.

115572.excerpt_en: It is the Japanese Nihondaira Zoo that wants to bring a female polar bear from Svalbard. It is seeking a female aged two or younger to keep its three-year-old male company.
115572.subtitle_en: A Japanese zoo wants to bring a female polar bear from Svalbard. It already has a male bear it wants the female to mate with.

115600.excerpt_en: The weather changed today, Monday, as cold conditions gave way to milder weather and rain. The rain made the runway slippery, and combined with the wind conditions, this led the SAS captain to return to Tromsø this afternoon.
115600.subtitle_en: The flight from Tromsø to Longyearbyen had to return to the mainland because the runway was too slippery.

115615.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Health and Care Services decided this month to strengthen emergency preparedness in Svalbard. “That is excellent,” says department head Søren Nissen at Longyearbyen Hospital. At present, there is no doctor on standby at Longyearbyen Hospital.
115615.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Hospital is getting more doctors and nurses so it can handle two incidents at the same time.

115633.excerpt_en: “We are having problems because conditions are extremely poor,” says senior police officer Arild Lyssand of the Governor of Svalbard’s office. It rained all Saturday, and there is wind and no visibility.
115633.subtitle_en: Both the helicopter and the snowmobile patrol sent to retrieve three tourists deep in Grøndalen had to turn back because of the weather. The Governor of Svalbard’s office will now send a tracked vehicle.

115645.excerpt_en: “We had to give up because of heavy snow showers in Colesbukta. We are going to make another attempt now, initially with just the helicopter.”
115645.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s office has been unable to transport the snowmobile patrol to Colesbukta because of the weather. They are now waiting to see how the situation develops.

115649.excerpt_en: “Both a snowmobile patrol and a tracked vehicle are on their way. The weather is a little better now,” says senior police officer Sidsel Svarstad of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
115649.subtitle_en: The helicopter had to turn back again after attempting to reach the three tourists in distress in Grøndalen Pass. But the Governor of Svalbard’s office has now sent both a snowmobile patrol and a tracked vehicle.

115662.excerpt_en: “They are now returning to Longyearbyen in a tracked vehicle,” says senior police officer Sidsel Svarstad of the Governor of Svalbard’s office. She says the three—a father and two sons aged 11 and 20—were picked up from the small cabin at the entrance to Semmeldalen where they had sought shelter.
115662.subtitle_en: The three Swedish tourists stranded in Grøndalen Pass have been found safe and sound.

115668.excerpt_en: “It appears that stones or loose asphalt were thrown up into the aircraft’s tail section. Probably during takeoff in Oslo,” says assistant duty manager Egil Lindberg of SAS Ground Services in Tromsø.
115668.subtitle_en: The daytime flight was grounded in Tromsø because of damage. An extra flight will operate this evening.

115671.excerpt_en: “We cannot see that there are any other online newspapers covering the entire region in the way we intend to. We hope we will be able to cover Svalbard as extensively as the other counties,” says editor Espen Bless Stenberg.
115671.subtitle_en: A new online newspaper launching today will cover all of Northern Norway, including Svalbard.
115671.title_en: New Online Newspaper in the North

115682.excerpt_en: The report, prepared by the consultancy Econ Pöyry, was paid for by LNS itself, according to Dagens Næringsliv. Its main conclusion is that the contracts between LNS and Store Norske were not overpriced by “several hundred million kroner,” as previously claimed, but instead underpriced by NOK 198 million.
115682.subtitle_en: A new inquiry report claims that the contracts between Leonhard Nilsen & Sønner (LNS) and Store Norske were underpriced by nearly NOK 200 million.

115685.excerpt_en: The father and his two sons, aged 11 and 20, set out on their own by snowmobile from Barentsburg towards Longyearbyen last Saturday, despite being advised not to. The trip ended in a 13-hour rescue operation.
115685.subtitle_en: The Swedish family rescued by the Governor of Svalbard’s office on Saturday risks having to pay for the rescue operation.
115685.title_en: They May Have to Pay the Bill Themselves

115706.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s office was notified of a loose dog near Gruve 6 at around 10 a.m. Friday. The dog chased and injured at least one reindeer in the area.
115706.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s office is reporting a dog owner for failing to control their dog after it chased reindeer on Friday morning.

115726.excerpt_en: “We are here today to celebrate the sun’s return to Longyearbyen. It’s wonderful that so many people have come here to celebrate the sun’s return!”
115726.subtitle_en: Snow and wind kept the sun’s rays from reaching the old hospital steps at Skjæringa. But the weather did nothing to dampen the mood.

115736.excerpt_en: “He was going to drive from Svalbard Snowmobile Rental and take photographs in Adventdalen. He had no GPS or weapon and couldn’t find his way back to town,” says senior police officer Per Andreassen of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
115736.subtitle_en: A male tourist had to be picked up by the Governor of Svalbard’s office at Hiorthhamn.

115749.excerpt_en: “The mail plane not arriving for two days in a row—and three days in one week—surely hasn’t happened before,” says customer service representative Helge Ask at the post office in Longyearbyen. He says packages that should have gone on Monday’s flight were sent by boat from Tromsø on Tuesday.
115749.subtitle_en: Wind, snow and a slippery runway have halted the mail plane three times this week. The postal service is arranging an extra flight from Tromsø tomorrow to catch up.

115756.excerpt_en: Last year, the port had revenue of NOK 7.7 million and a profit of NOK 1.6 million. “Our revenue has almost increased tenfold in ten years,” says port director Kjetil Bråten.
115756.subtitle_en: Larger boats and more port services mean that Longyearbyen Port is making increasingly more money.

115772.excerpt_en: “I hope we can establish a local party branch in Longyearbyen so that the party will once again be represented in the election for a new local council this autumn,” says Siv Jensen. Nearly 40 people turned up for a public meeting at the Polar Hotel on Thursday to hear the Progress Party leader.
115772.subtitle_en: Progress Party leader Siv Jensen wants to revive the local party branch after the Progress Party has been absent from Svalbard since the municipal election four years ago.

115782.excerpt_en: “A local woman had her snowmobile fall on top of her during a trip to Isfjord Radio today. She has probably broken her arm and is being picked up by the rescue helicopter right now,” says duty senior police officer Per Andreassen of the Governor of Svalbard’s office at 6:30 p.m. Saturday.
115782.subtitle_en: A woman is believed to have broken her arm in a snowmobile accident at Isfjord Radio today. Another woman crashed her snowmobile near SSU.

115784.excerpt_en: “We have learned about the queen and the princess,” explain Kristine Frostvoll Kuraas (5) and point to a collage of pictures of everyone in the Norwegian royal family. Svalbardposten is visiting Longyearbyen Kindergarten and has been given three guides to show us around.
115784.subtitle_en: “We can!” That is the slogan for National Kindergarten Day, which is being held today. At Longyearbyen Kindergarten, the children themselves gave a tour to show what they can do.

115812.excerpt_en: The two men activated an emergency locator beacon last night after their tent was destroyed. The men are tourists from mainland Norway and are in their mid-30s and mid-40s.
115812.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office is making a new attempt at 7:30 a.m. to pick up the two skiers experiencing problems on Tryggvebreen.
115812.title_en: New Attempt to Pick Up Skiers

115815.excerpt_en: “Tent blown to pieces. Have to get us down to a trapper’s cabin.”
115815.subtitle_en: One of the two men stranded by the weather on Tryggvebreen comments on the situation on Facebook.

115821.excerpt_en: “They are in good condition under the circumstances and are doing well,” says Liv Ødegaard, communications adviser at the Governor’s Office. The two men, André Spica, 34, and Øystein Breidablik, in his mid-40s, set out on a long trip on the 11th.
115821.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office managed to reach the two skiers on Tryggvebreen between 8:30 and 9 this morning. The helicopter landed in Longyearbyen just before 10.

115827.excerpt_en: One hundred and fifty passengers were due to fly from Tromsø to Longyearbyen today.
115827.subtitle_en: Neither the scheduled flight nor the mail plane will arrive in Longyearbyen today, Thursday, because the runway is too slippery.

115833.excerpt_en: “We have found the fault on the line in Nybyen and Hotellneset,” says Bydrift general manager Marianne Aasen. Power went out across the town at 11 p.m. yesterday after the weather caused flashovers on the high-voltage lines.
115833.subtitle_en: Nybyen and Hotellneset have regained power after an outage that began at 11 p.m. Thursday. Adventdalen is still without electricity.

115852.excerpt_en: The students were visiting the ice cave in Longyearbreen on Sunday morning. They went up on skis, but had neither a GPS nor a map and compass.
115852.subtitle_en: Six UNIS students needed help from the Governor’s Office to get down from Longyearbreen.
115852.title_en: Had to Be Picked Up from Longyearbreen

115865.excerpt_en: On Friday nearly three weeks ago, the woman let three sled dogs run loose in Bolterdalen. One of the dogs attacked a reindeer.
115865.subtitle_en: A dog owner has been fined NOK 3,000 for violating the leash regulations after her dog attacked a reindeer in Bolterdalen.

115888.excerpt_en: “Environmental considerations were a decisive criterion for entering into an agreement with the Danish shipping company,” stresses Store Norske CEO Bjørn Arnestad. Store Norske ended its long-standing cooperation with Kristian Jebsens Rederi in Bergen last December.
115888.subtitle_en: Store Norske has signed a five-year contract with Danish shipping company Norden to transport coal to the mainland.

115917.excerpt_en: A father who was in Longyearbyen with his two sons, the youngest aged eleven, ignored warnings against travelling alone to Barentsburg. The trip ended in a 13-hour rescue operation.
115917.subtitle_en: The Swedish family picked up in Grøndalen on 26 February will not have to pay for the rescue operation. The Governor’s Office is nevertheless considering changing its practice of charging for rescue operations outside Area 10.

115932.excerpt_en: Following numerous rescue operations in recent years, the Governor’s Office has discussed changing the practice for covering rescue expenses for tour groups that are required to have insurance. All visitors travelling independently outside Area 10 must either have insurance or a bank guarantee, in addition to being required to report to the Governor’s Office.
115932.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office will begin requiring insurance companies to pay for rescue operations in Svalbard.

115946.excerpt_en: “We are trying to keep the cave open, since we know it is a popular attraction for many people,” says Tore Hoem, production manager at Spitsbergen Travel.
115946.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Travel has reopened the entrance to the ice cave on Longyearbreen.

115962.excerpt_en: Bydrift plans to fine everyone who leaves outdoor lights on during the bright season. “We are doing this to save electricity and reduce coal consumption,” says Bydrift general manager Marianne Aasen.
115962.subtitle_en: Bydrift plans to fine everyone who leaves outdoor lights on during the bright season.

115985.excerpt_en: The group consists of one female and two male guide students from Arctic Nature Guide, four women in their 30s and 40s who live in Longyearbyen, and two dogs. They were taken to Verlegenhuken on Thursday and had planned to spend a month reaching Sørkapp.
115985.subtitle_en: The ski trip is already over for the seven people from Longyearbyen who planned to cross Spitsbergen from north to south. The Governor’s Office picked them up on Sunday.

115992.excerpt_en: The Governor’s Office recommends that the Ministry of Climate and the Environment approve Store Norske’s environmental impact assessment and grant permission for coal mining. A permit would allow the coal company to build a road between Svea Nord and Lunckefjellet across Marthabreen and establish aggregate extraction, infrastructure and surface facilities on both sides of the glacier.
115992.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office supports Store Norske’s plans to open a new coal mine at Lunckefjellet.

115996.excerpt_en: Here are the results of this year’s draw: • Texas Bar: Heinrich Eggenfellner (alternate Lars Karvonen) • Worsleyhamna: Hallvar Gisnås (alternate Sondre Rorgemoen) • Calypsobyen: Frank-Johnny Olsen (alternate Morten Stegarud) • Austbotnhytta: Christian Engelke (alternate Anne Rakel Kristiansen) • Krosspynten: Trond Hovelsrud (alternate Ivar Andersen) • Villa Møen: Kristin Woxholth (alternate Bente Bull) • Villa Purpur: Håkan Ericsson…
115996.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office has drawn the names for the ten cabins being lent out over Easter.

116008.excerpt_en: “Some of the reactions we received were that people understood there was a message behind it, even though it was an April Fool’s joke. That is positive,” says Bydrift general manager Marianne Aasen.
116008.subtitle_en: The news that Bydrift would issue fines for outdoor lighting has produced results.

116016.excerpt_en: In April last year, Store Norske received 80 dollars per tonne for its coal. The company now obtains as much as 150–160 dollars for high-quality coal for the metallurgical industry, according to deputy CEO Dag Ivar Brekke of Store Norske.
116016.subtitle_en: The situation in Japan following the earthquake and tsunami, together with unrest in North Africa, has doubled the price of coal since last year.

116021.excerpt_en: While other students are interns at tourism businesses around town, Anved Kvammen, Ingebjørg Schrøder and Steinar Rorgemoen chose to guide four women from Longyearbyen across Spitsbergen from north to south.
116021.subtitle_en: UNIS and Arctic Nature Guide will learn from the trip that resulted in seven people having to be rescued from Mosseldalen on Sunday.

116029.excerpt_en: “We received a tip about suspicious behaviour at around 1:30 last night and found a man who admitted to driving a car while over the legal alcohol limit,” says duty chief inspector Inge Meløy of the Governor’s Office.
116029.subtitle_en: The Governor arrested a local man for drunk driving early Saturday morning.

116041.excerpt_en: Noise, escaping dogs, and reindeer, Arctic foxes and birds being chased away. That is what cabin owners in Todalen envision if more dog kennels are built in the area.
116041.subtitle_en: Cabin owners in Todalen do not want dog kennels as their neighbours.

116043.excerpt_en: The county final of the Youth Cultural Showcase was held in Finnsnes over the weekend. Fourteen young people, performing seven acts, represented Longyearbyen.
116043.subtitle_en: Svalnardojentan Ida Sigernes and Marianne Bøe advanced to the final of the Youth Cultural Showcase.
116043.title_en: Circus act advances to county finals

116052.excerpt_en: Håkenstad drove with seven dogs in her team and completed the 70-kilometre course in three hours and 47 minutes. “I have a young team, and it’s fun for me that they’re going so fast. It’s also incredibly good that so many are taking part in the race.”
116052.subtitle_en: The world’s northernmost dog race, Trappers Trail, was won this year by Solfrid Håkenstad. Fifteen teams took part in this year’s race, the third to be held.

116056.excerpt_en: Morten Langerud, property manager at Bydrift, says the owner will be compensated for the kicksled. “Sportscenteret is sold out, and the season is over on the mainland, so we’ll repair her sled temporarily and replace it with a new one later,” says Langerud.
116056.subtitle_en: The mild weather has left roofs laden with snow and icicles. Yesterday, a kicksled was crushed by ice falling from the cultural centre’s roof.

116084.excerpt_en: Initially, around 600 of the 15,000 digitised negatives have been made available to the public. More images will follow continuously as they are prepared for publication.
116084.subtitle_en: After lying hidden in drawers and cupboards for decades, dust has been blown off and thousands of Svalbardposten film negatives digitised. The images can be viewed online.

116086.excerpt_en: Today, Winther was appointed by the King in Council of State to his second six-year fixed term. Winther graduated as a civil engineer from NTNU in 1987 and holds a PhD.
116086.subtitle_en: Director Jan-Gunnar Winther will continue as director of the Norwegian Polar Institute.

article_keywords_en: chief inspector at the Governor’s Office
116110.excerpt_en: “It has been exceptionally quiet and peaceful,” says duty chief inspector Trond Aagesen of the Governor’s Office. He says the Governor’s Office has seen no particular increase in activity because of Easter.
116110.subtitle_en: The first weekend of Easter passed without rescue operations or serious incidents.

116112.excerpt_en: A party from Basecamp Spitsbergen was returning to Longyearbyen this morning after spending the night aboard the “Noorderlicht” when two of the snowmobiles broke through the ice near Murdoch Hole. The party consisted of six people and a guide.
116112.subtitle_en: Two snowmobiles have broken through the ice in Tempelfjorden.

116125.excerpt_en: “The party was going to travel from Båten i isen towards Von Postbreen before heading home to Longyearbyen. We normally use a route across the middle of the fjord, but because of surface water, the guide chose to drive somewhat farther north,” says Solfrid Håkenstad, general manager of Basecamp Spitsbergen.
116125.subtitle_en: The snowmobile party in which two machines broke through the ice on Tempelfjorden drove into an opening in the ice measuring 20 metres long and four metres wide.

116129.excerpt_en: A series of low-pressure systems will pass over Spitsbergen during Easter, bringing unsettled weather to the area around Longyearbyen. “There will be no long periods of fine weather,” says meteorological consultant Torgeir Mørk.
116129.subtitle_en: Meteorological consultant Torgeir Mørk at the airport reports plenty of weather over Easter. The best conditions will come from Friday to Sunday.

116138.excerpt_en: “We have begun gathering information about the location of Murdoch Hole and why it is there. We have also spoken to the guide and Basecamp about their procedures,” says duty chief inspector Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office.
116138.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is investigating Monday’s near-accident in Tempelfjorden and working to obtain information about the so-called Murdoch Hole.

116153.excerpt_en: “It appears that he walked home from a party wearing too little clothing and under the influence of alcohol, and sought shelter in a car. The car’s owner woke up when the man leaned on the horn,” says duty chief inspector Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office.
116153.subtitle_en: A young man was taken to Longyearbyen Hospital on Wednesday morning after falling asleep in a car and becoming hypothermic.

116158.excerpt_en: As usual, there is strong participation from the mainland in the Svalbard Ski Marathon. Of the 410 who have registered so far, most come from the mainland. Two hundred and fifty skiers, 74 of them women, will compete in the timed full marathon.
116158.subtitle_en: A total of 410 skiers have registered for Saturday’s ski marathon. The organisers report that everything is on track.

116173.excerpt_en: “I’m starting to get old. When they hired me, I was 61, and we agreed on a three-year fixed-term contract because of my advanced age,” says Bjørn Arnestad.
116173.subtitle_en: Store Norske is seeking a new managing director. Bjørn Arnestad will leave next March.

116182.excerpt_en: Three people ended up in the water when six snowmobiles and a guide turned towards Von Postbreen after spending the night aboard the “Noorderlicht”. They had driven straight into the so-called Murdoch Hole, an area where the ice is never safe.
116182.subtitle_en: The snowmobile party from Basecamp Spitsbergen that broke through the ice on Monday, April 18, drove straight into Murdoch Hole in Tempelfjorden.

116200.excerpt_en: “The man was alone, had lost his sunglasses and become snow-blind. He could see nothing,” says Inge Meløy, the Governor’s duty officer.
116200.subtitle_en: A 51-year-old man from Poland became snow-blind during a ski trip and had to be rescued by the Governor of Svalbard in Petuniabukta.

116203.excerpt_en: Held in brilliant sunshine and on fast snow, the Svalbard Ski Marathon took place for the 19th time yesterday.
116203.subtitle_en: A total of 520 people took part in the Svalbard Ski Marathon yesterday. That is a new record.

116224.excerpt_en: Kristoffersen is therefore Labour’s new candidate for the local council chair’s position when Kjell Mork steps down this autumn. “I think it’s an honour, without a doubt.”
116224.subtitle_en: Christin Kristoffersen, 37, won yesterday’s Labour Party nomination meeting.

116238.excerpt_en: On Tuesday this week, all flights from Longyearbyen to Tromsø were fully booked for more than a week ahead. The first available flight was Thursday the 12th.
116238.subtitle_en: Getting off the archipelago at the beginning of May is no easy matter.

116243.excerpt_en: “The new booking system is proving to be a scandal. The smaller the company, the greater the damage.”
116243.subtitle_en: Small tourism operators are losing guests because Svalbard Reiseliv’s booking system is not working.

116260.excerpt_en: The list consists of eight people, with Jørn Dybdahl at the top. Jens Abild follows him, with Trond Berg in third place.
116260.subtitle_en: Jørn Dybdahl heads the Consequence List, which is standing in this autumn’s local elections.

116273.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard conducted a drink-driving check on the flat below Svalbard Snowmobile Rental. “We checked everyone who passed between 12:45 and 1:30 p.m.,” says senior police officer Trond Aagesen of the Governor’s office. He is pleased with the result after checking 107 people. “No one was over the limit,” he says.
116273.subtitle_en: A total of 107 snowmobile drivers were checked on Saturday morning. All were allowed to continue driving.

116275.excerpt_en: A unanimous jury named the newspaper Local Newspaper of the Year for 2010. It cited the paper’s impressively high journalistic standard as the reason for its choice.
116275.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten was named Local Newspaper of the Year on Saturday evening. The award was presented at the national meeting of the Landslaget for lokalaviser in Oslo.

116277.excerpt_en: The grant was presented today during the tourism conference “Exceptional Opportunities for Norwegian Tourism” aboard MS “Color Fantasy” between Oslo and Kiel. Minister of Trade and Industry Trond Giske of the Labour Party presented the grant to Basecamp Spitsbergen on behalf of the Norwegian Foundation for Internationalization of Business (NORINT).
116277.subtitle_en: Basecamp Spitsbergen has received a NOK 500,000 grant for its international expansion.

116288.excerpt_en: Mallards are not a common sight in Svalbard. But one generally turns up every year, according to Bjørn Frantzen, head of the Longyearbyen Field Biology Association.
116288.subtitle_en: A mallard in central Longyearbyen has attracted considerable attention over the past week. Many people have encountered the bird, which does not normally inhabit the Arctic.
116288.title_en: Bringing life to the town centre

116302.excerpt_en: “I am confident that I have a good party to represent and good people behind me,” says Kristin Furu Grøtting. The manual therapist has lived in Svalbard for 14 years and has served on the local council for the Cross-Party Joint List for the past four years.
116302.subtitle_en: Kristin Furu Grøtting is first on the list of the Cross-Party Joint List.

116306.excerpt_en: “We simply have to comply with it and follow the conditions that have been set,” says airport director Morten Ulsnes after reading the ministry’s decision. Following a lengthy discussion, the local council decided in September last year to allow alcohol to be served in the airport departure hall.
116306.subtitle_en: The airport must cordon off the serving area. That is the ruling of the Ministry of Health and Care Services.
116306.title_en: Beer drinkers must be fenced in

116318.excerpt_en: “We will retain the business, but are trying to find someone who will take over the dogs. These are good working dogs, well known in Svalbard,” says Priitta Trøen, general manager of Spitsbergen Experience.
116318.subtitle_en: Two of the companies offering dog sledding in Svalbard are for sale. A third company has found a new owner.

116320.excerpt_en: After years of deterioration, the Russian state-owned mining company Trust Arktikugol has begun renovating the Kapp Heer helicopter base just outside Barentsburg. The base was highly controversial when it was established by the Soviet Russians in the mid-1970s.
116320.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol has ambitions for the Kapp Heer helicopter base. Last week, the base was inspected by Norwegian aviation authorities.

116328.excerpt_en: “I am standing as the lead candidate and am motivated for the job,” says Geir Hekne. He works as a fire chief in Longyearbyen and will have lived in Svalbard for 40 years this December.
116328.subtitle_en: Geir Hekne, 47, heads the Conservative Party’s list for the autumn election.

116341.excerpt_en: Svalbard Reiseliv launched new websites using TellUs IT’s GM Booking solution in September last year. Svalbardposten has previously reported that small tourism companies experienced booking problems as a result of the changeover.
116341.subtitle_en: The supplier of Svalbard Reiseliv’s accommodation booking system, TellUs IT, denies being responsible for the online booking problems experienced by small tourism companies in Svalbard.

116351.excerpt_en: “It’s a shame. We want to keep the jogging group going and hope more people will join.”
116351.subtitle_en: Svalbard Turn has entered a team in the Holmenkoll Relay in Oslo every year since 1986. This year, the run will come to an end.
116351.title_en: First year without a relay team

116364.excerpt_en: The community-minded enthusiast was honoured for his work on behalf of Longyearbyen.
116364.subtitle_en: Per Krokan, 68, was awarded the Tyfus statuette during the 17 May performance at the Cultural Centre.

116397.excerpt_en: Earlier this year, Basecamp Spitsbergen applied for permission to break the sailing ship “Noorderlicht” free of the ice in Tempelfjorden on 10 May.
116397.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard will not allow Basecamp to break the “Noorderlicht” free of the ice before the time is right, out of consideration for wildlife and the safety of tourists.

116401.excerpt_en: “Norway will benefit greatly from Galileo. It is important to be part of it, because there may be discussions about how the system should be designed and financed,” says Bo Andersen, director general of the Norwegian Space Centre.
116401.subtitle_en: One of the ground stations for the Galileo satellite navigation system was inaugurated at SvalSat today. The first two satellites are due to be launched during the year.

116425.excerpt_en: “We are assessing the situation constantly, and there are indications that the airspace could be closed. There may be a window when we cannot fly, but we do not know whether the forecasts will come true.”
116425.subtitle_en: The ash cloud from the eruption of Iceland’s Grimsvötn volcano could ground ambulance flights between Svalbard and the mainland. For now, they can fly as normal.

116428.excerpt_en: “It looks as though we will have trouble flying to Svalbard over the next 24 hours. But for now, these are only forecasts,” says Frank Wilhelmsen, operations director at Lufttransport.
116428.subtitle_en: According to the forecasts, the ash cloud will approach Svalbard during the evening and night.

116431.excerpt_en: “The ash cloud is about to reach as far north as Van Mijenfjorden,” says Morten Ulsnes, airport director at Svalbard Airport. Technically, Longyearbyen Airport is not closed, but because parts of the airspace have been designated a danger zone, flying there is prohibited.
116431.subtitle_en: Parts of the airspace over Svalbard are closed. As a result, today’s SAS flight and the mail plane have been cancelled, and Lufttransport has grounded its aircraft.
116431.title_en: Ash cloud affects all air traffic

116443.excerpt_en: “The ash cloud is expected to move into the area affecting air traffic between Longyearbyen and Svea. Since we do not have reliable emergency preparedness in place, we have chosen to halt operations until further notice,” says Einar Fjerdingøy, HSE director at Store Norske.
116443.subtitle_en: Store Norske has chosen to halt all activity in Svea Nord because emergency preparedness in Svalbard has been weakened.

116454.excerpt_en: “Of course, we think it’s terribly sad. We’ve been planning and working towards this for many months, and now it won’t happen.”
116454.subtitle_en: The ash cloud has also put a stop to the environmental symposium in Ny-Ålesund this weekend.

116457.excerpt_en: “Air transport has resumed, and the mail plane is planning two flights today. There is nothing to indicate that air traffic will not operate normally,” says Morten Ulsnes, airport director at Svalbard Airport.
116457.subtitle_en: The Grimsvötn volcano in Iceland has stopped spewing ash, and all flights between Svalbard and the mainland are operating normally again.

116476.excerpt_en: So far, 857 passengers have booked places on the 11 expedition cruises aboard the popular tourist vessel.
116476.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Travel is cancelling all cruises with MS “Polar Star” in Svalbard this summer. The reason is that the shipping company is in financial trouble and the vessel is stranded in Spain.

116481.excerpt_en: “It’s going to be an absolute nightmare to clear the snow. And what about deliveries?”
116481.subtitle_en: Businesses at Elvesletta Nord are frustrated that the parking area is being separated from the road by a fence.

According to deputy chief inspector Per Andreassen, the last digit of the personal identification number had been changed.

116536.excerpt_en: “A midnight-sun eclipse is quite an exclusive phenomenon at our latitudes. You have to be north of the Arctic Circle to experience it,” says astronomer Knut Jørgen Røed Ødegaard of the University of Oslo’s Centre for Science Education.
116536.subtitle_en: Between 10:30 and 12:30 tonight, you may catch an exclusive midnight-sun eclipse in Longyearbyen.

116552.excerpt_en: However, the MNU was divided when it voted on Monday to put the local plan for the researcher hotel out for a new round of public consultation. A casting vote from committee chair Odd Gunnar Brøto Braathen (Labour) was needed to pass the decision.
116552.subtitle_en: UNIS wants to convert UNIS Guest House into student housing. The first step is to amend the local plan for the researcher hotel, which the Environment and Business Committee is open to allowing.

116567.excerpt_en: According to Barents Observer, Russia’s Ministry of Natural Resources has approved a clean-up costing 186 million roubles, or NOK 36 million. The work will be carried out from this year through 2013.
116567.subtitle_en: Russia will spend NOK 36 million cleaning up Russian settlements in Svalbard.

116571.excerpt_en: In recent years, the Governor’s Office has taken people from Longyearbyen on beach-cleaning voyages north of the archipelago. The trip is very popular, and this year 178 permanent residents signed up.
116571.subtitle_en: Twenty-one people will join the Governor of Svalbard on a clean-up voyage north of Spitsbergen in July.

116583.excerpt_en: “I received an email on Sunday, 22 May, saying that I had won a photography award, and the prize was 5,000 dollars.”
116583.subtitle_en: An image from Reindalen took first place in the international “Extreme Environment Photographic Competition.”
116583.title_en: Wins Photography Award with Svalbard Image

116597.excerpt_en: Geir Wing Gabrielsen has researched seabirds for many years. In the book “Seabirds in the Arctic,” he and Kirsti Blom take readers to Svalbard’s seabirds, the Norwegian Polar Institute writes on its website.
116597.subtitle_en: Researcher Geir Wing Gabrielsen of the Norwegian Polar Institute and author Kirsti Blom are publishing a new book in the Brage Prize-nominated polar series.

116609.excerpt_en: Previously, hunters could join forces and apply for the same area as one hunting party.
116609.subtitle_en: It will not be possible to apply as a hunting party ahead of this year’s reindeer hunt. The deadline for applying for a culling permit is 10 July.

116632.excerpt_en: “This is a significant strengthening of Svalbard’s rescue preparedness,” says State Secretary Terje Moland Pedersen at the Ministry of Justice. The news has been well received by the Governor’s Office.
116632.subtitle_en: The government proposes that, from 2014, the Governor of Svalbard should have two large helicopters instead of the one large and one small helicopter currently in service.

116634.excerpt_en: “This is a spring release from the Labour Party,” says Christin Kristoffersen, the party’s candidate for local council leader in the autumn election. She visits Svalbardposten with AUF leader Astrid Sylte, list candidate Viljar Hanssen and outgoing local council leader Kjell Mork to present the party’s first campaign promise for the autumn election.
116634.subtitle_en: The Labour Party wants to make cinema, exercise and exhibitions cheaper for young people.

116653.excerpt_en: Brundtland and 11 other members of the United Nations Foundation (UNF) board have held a meeting in Oslo in recent days. Today they arrived in Longyearbyen.
116653.subtitle_en: Gro Harlem Brundtland arrived in Longyearbyen today with a prominent delegation set to study the climate in the north.

116658.excerpt_en: “At the weekend we saw two pairs of northern gannets breeding on Alkeholmen, at the very south of Bjørnøya. Four other birds were also perched on a mountain ledge,” says bird researcher Hallvard Strøm of the Norwegian Polar Institute.
116658.subtitle_en: Researchers have found a new breeding species on Bjørnøya. According to the researchers, the sighting of the northern gannet is a sign of a warmer climate in the north, allowing new species to establish themselves.

116667.excerpt_en: The four sites are Bjørnøya, Hopen, Sørkapp and parts of the Nordenskiöld Coast. The Ramsar Convention is a global agreement on wetland conservation drawn up in the city of Ramsar, Iran, on 2.
116667.subtitle_en: Four new sites in Svalbard are today receiving international status as Ramsar sites.

116693.excerpt_en: The trip to Svalbard is part of the United Nations Foundation (UNF) board’s visit to Norway, a foundation Turner established in 1998. The board has 13 members, including former Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland and former UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
116693.subtitle_en: CNN founder Ted Turner went boating in Isfjorden yesterday with, among others, Gro Harlem Brundtland to discuss climate issues.

116695.excerpt_en: Several of Bydrift’s buildings have not received the necessary maintenance since the 1970s. Windows and roofs should have been replaced 10–15 years ago.
116695.subtitle_en: Maintenance of Bydrift’s buildings has been neglected for years. Bringing them up to standard will cost NOK 210 million.

116707.excerpt_en: “They submitted the best overall bid, which is why we chose them,” says Store Norske CEO Bjørn Arnestad. AF Gruppen is Norway’s third-largest construction company.
116707.subtitle_en: AF Gruppen will take over transport, construction and maintenance services in Svea from 1 September.
116707.title_en: Svea Contract Awarded to AF Gruppen

116722.excerpt_en: The new fence at Elvesletta Nord sparked strong reactions when it was erected at the turn of May and June. Many were concerned about traffic safety.
116722.subtitle_en: Many are concerned about traffic safety with the new fence on Elvesletta. The fire service believes it will be harder to get through.

116727.excerpt_en: This summer, the Governor’s office and Trust Arktikugol entered into a partnership to halt Pyramiden’s accelerating deterioration. Two Russian and three Norwegian carpenters will work together to replace windows in four of the buildings.
116727.subtitle_en: Norwegians and Russians are working together to seal up the Russian mining town of Pyramiden.

116740.excerpt_en: A large, square shape filled with coal covers the floor in the middle of one of the exhibition rooms at Svalbard Gallery. Terje Roalkvam is crouching down, adding a few more pieces of coal.
116740.subtitle_en: Visual artist Terje Roalkvam is trying to find the balance between stone, coal, wood and aluminium.

116769.excerpt_en: “He had read online that there had been a break-in at a container, and got a little frightened. He came and turned himself in straight away,” says constable Trond Olsen of the Governor’s office.
116769.subtitle_en: A man came forward to the Governor’s office this afternoon and said he was the one who had opened the container at Bykaia.

116782.excerpt_en: The idea of an annual film festival in Svalbard arose in 2008, after the Northern Travelling Film Festival was held in Barentsburg. Last year, the CinemArctic film festival was cancelled.
116782.subtitle_en: There will be no film festival in Svalbard this year either. A new board will try to organise a smaller event.

116803.excerpt_en: The Governor’s office was notified of the accident at around 2 p.m. today. The two people, a young woman and a somewhat older man, were picked up by ambulance and taken to Longyearbyen Hospital.
116803.subtitle_en: On Wednesday afternoon, two ATV tourists drove off a 15-metre-high cliff.

116813.excerpt_en: Because of the large amount of rock mixed in, Store Norske was eager to start cleaning the coal from Svea Nord. Without removing the rock, the coal would not have been saleable.
116813.subtitle_en: Coal cleaning is in full swing at the new processing plant in Svea. The day after receiving permission from the authorities, the plant was in full production.
116813.title_en: Coal-washing plant in Svea up and running

116825.excerpt_en: “It has been a quiet summer, at least according to the statistics,” says Trygve Steen, managing director of Spitsbergen Travel. Figures from Svalbard Tourism show that there were 2,000 fewer guest nights in June than the previous year.
116825.subtitle_en: Tourists stayed away from Svalbard in June. Around 800 fewer people travelled to the archipelago than the previous year.

116843.excerpt_en: The bear was first observed approaching the centre from the airport. It stopped for a while by the dog yard, then continued down into the centre, according to Kings Bay’s website.
116843.subtitle_en: Ny-Ålesund received a visit from a big bear yesterday. A bear went for a stroll between the houses early in the morning.

116857.excerpt_en: “There was an opening at SINTEF that sounded very exciting, but it required me to be back by 1 January,” says Gunnar Sand, managing director of UNIS.
116857.subtitle_en: Gunnar Sand is leaving UNIS six months before his term expires.

116862.excerpt_en: A gasket at the power plant ruptured on Saturday, 25 June, and between 200 and 300 litres of hydraulic oil spilled onto the floor, then into a cooling-water well and out into Adventfjorden.
116862.subtitle_en: A failure at the power plant caused between 200 and 300 litres of oil to leak into Adventfjorden via the cooling water.
116862.title_en: Oil spill from the power plant

116870.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten has had it confirmed by local council leader Kjell Mork (Labour) that five young people from Longyearbyen were at the AUF camp on Utøya yesterday. One is seriously injured and one is missing.
116870.subtitle_en: Young people from Longyearbyen are among both the injured and the missing after Friday afternoon’s shooting on Utøya.

116885.excerpt_en: Johannes Buø is missing. Viljar Hanssen was hit by several bullets and is seriously injured at Oslo University Hospital.
116885.subtitle_en: Johannes Buø (14) is missing after the shooting on Utøya. Viljar Hanssen (17) is seriously injured.

116888.excerpt_en: “Everyone is welcome to write a few words,” says Deputy Governor Lars Erik Alfheim. He says that such books are being made available throughout the country. “The book will remain available until further notice and can be accessed during the Governor’s office opening hours,” says Alfheim.
116888.subtitle_en: The Governor will make a condolence book available at the administration building in Skjæringa on Wednesday morning.

116891.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, the Dutch tourist ship “Plancius” had to help the Polish sailing boat “Eltanin” towards the quay in Longyearbyen. The sailing boat, which mainly transports researchers, had become stuck in the ice in Adventfjorden.
116891.subtitle_en: Large amounts of pack ice off Spitsbergen’s west coast and in the fjords are causing problems for shipping.

116904.subtitle_en: The pack ice that has filled the fjords of Spitsbergen over the past week will probably remain until next week, says a meteorologist and ice consultant at the Norwegian Meteorological Institute in Tromsø.
116904.title_en: No improvement in the ice before next week

116908.excerpt_en: Since Friday’s tragedy on Utøya, Johannes Buø of Longyearbyen had been listed as missing.
116908.subtitle_en: On Thursday, it was confirmed that Johannes Buø (14) was among those killed in the Utøya shooting.

116916.excerpt_en: “We carried out a preventive check and caught two on the spot,” says senior constable Inge Meløy of the Governor’s office. The Governor’s officers stopped every car they encountered, ten in all.
116916.subtitle_en: Two drivers lost their licences in Longyearbyen during the night to Sunday.

116957.excerpt_en: Flags are flying at half-mast in Longyearbyen today, Friday. Johannes Buø (14), from Longyearbyen, was killed on Utøya while attending AUF’s summer camp.
116957.subtitle_en: Johannes Buø will be buried today from Mandal Church.

116974.excerpt_en: “This strengthens relations between the Norwegian and Russian communities,” says Svalbardposten editor Birger Amundsen. The newspaper has entered into a partnership with the mining company Trust Arktikugol to publish Svalbardposten in Russian.
116974.subtitle_en: Two Russian-language editions of Svalbardposten will be published this autumn.

117009.subtitle_en: A man was found dead in Barentsburg on Sunday morning.

117011.excerpt_en: “We have discussed and negotiated and reached an agreement. That is good for all parties.”
117011.subtitle_en: Store Norske and Kristian Jebsens Rederi have reached a settlement.

117023.excerpt_en: On Sunday morning, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that a 51-year-old Russian man had been found dead in Barentsburg. The preliminary autopsy reveals nothing indicating that a crime has occurred.
117023.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard does not suspect that anything criminal caused a Russian man’s death last Sunday.

117037.subtitle_en: Father of young children Bård Gundersen does not want his children playing on the ramp in the town square.

117059.subtitle_en: Two foreigners and a permanent resident have been punished for drink-driving.

117077.excerpt_en: After the first half of 2011, Hurtigruten had a NOK 64 million deficit across its operations. The poor result was partly due to weak results on Svalbard, the company reported in its interim report.
117077.subtitle_en: Increased competition and cancelled “Polar Star” sailings resulted in a NOK 36 million loss in revenue.

117079.excerpt_en: The election campaign got under way on the mainland last weekend. Election Day for the municipal and county council elections is 12.
117079.subtitle_en: Advance voting for the local council election starts today. For municipal elections on the mainland, you must have voted by 7 September.

117105.excerpt_en: In today’s Svalbardposten, we write that advance voting for the local council election in October starts today, but it will not begin until a month from now—on 19 September.
117105.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten was a month too early.
117105.title_en: Advance Voting Not Until a Month from Now

117113.subtitle_en: This summer’s ultimate test of mettle is to tackle all twelve of Topptrimmen’s peaks in one great push.

117119.excerpt_en: “Welcome, everyone. We have been looking forward to your arrival,” says headteacher Anne Gellein. On the stage with her are 15 expectant first-graders who have just greeted the headteacher and their future teacher, Tone Edvardsen, for the first time.
117119.subtitle_en: Fifteen excited pupils turned up today for their first day at Longyearbyen School.
117119.title_en: The Very First Day of School

117128.excerpt_en: Svalbard is one of several potential candidates for UNESCO’s World Heritage List. It is now being considered whether a possible new coal mine at Lunckefjellet would prevent its nomination to the prestigious list.
117128.subtitle_en: If a mine is developed at Lunckefjellet, the UN may not want Svalbard on the World Heritage List.

117142.excerpt_en: “We are not asking for 200-square-metre palaces. We would simply like to keep the small apartments we have,” says Pernilla Carlsson.

117142.title_en: Do Not Want to Live at the Research Hotel

117144.excerpt_en: “Ten years of use have shown that the Act is an important tool for safeguarding Svalbard’s vulnerable natural environment. We are proposing a clean-up to ensure that the Act is consistent with developments in environmental policy.”
117144.subtitle_en: It may become mandatory to have knowledge of protection against polar bear attacks. Today, the Ministry of the Environment presented a proposal to amend the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act.
117144.title_en: Wants Polar Bear Protection Required by Law

117157.subtitle_en: Kristian Jebsens Rederi has accepted a NOK 4 million fine following the indictment for aggravated corruption. The charges against the company have therefore been withdrawn.

117169.excerpt_en: The first issue of Svalbardposten in Russian was published last Friday in connection with Trust Arktikugol’s 80th-anniversary celebration. Interest in the Russian edition was high, and several guests asked where they could obtain it.
117169.subtitle_en: The Russian edition of Svalbardposten is attracting considerable interest in Barentsburg.

117180.excerpt_en: “Fifteen years ago, the aircraft carrying workers to Barentsburg and Pyramiden crashed. We remember the day, mourn the dead and do not forget their relatives,” Consul General Alexander Antipov said during the ceremony. 29.
117180.subtitle_en: Monday marked 15 years since a Russian aircraft crashed into Operafjellet. The accident was commemorated on Sunday.

117187.excerpt_en: During the first two years the programme existed, students had something called academic specialisation. They were to plan and carry out a trip and link it to theory.
117187.subtitle_en: Students in Arctic Nature Guide training are no longer allowed to go on long trips on their own.

117200.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, LO Svalbard invited people to a conference on Arctic policy from Longyearbyen’s perspective. LO leader Roar Flåthen gave a speech, as did Arne O.

117208.excerpt_en: “We understood that they were going to conduct research internally for the trust, but that was wrong,” says Ole Martin Erikstad, director of the legal department at the Civil Aviation Authority. On 22 June, Trust Arktikugol applied for permission to fly a group of biologists in the helicopter operated by Convers Avia Airline.
117208.subtitle_en: This summer, the Russian helicopter was permitted to fly biologists to Nordaustlandet and Barentsøya. The Civil Aviation Authority now admits it made a mistake.

117213.subtitle_en: A permanent resident has been fined NOK 2,000 for altering the year of birth on his own bank card to buy alcohol.

117219.excerpt_en: “We have been planning the conference for two years, and now the day has finally arrived. It was prompted by the commemoration of the Nansen–Amundsen Year 2011.”
117219.subtitle_en: The “Narrating the High North” conference opened at Svalbard Museum on Tuesday. The conference focuses in particular on Fridtjof Nansen and his historic work “In Northern Mists.”

117233.excerpt_en: Some politicians went to great lengths to allow UNIS to use the research hotel as a dormitory, but the Conservative Party objected during Monday’s meeting of the Environment and Business Committee. Changes: This spring, UNIS applied to convert the research hotel from commercial use to a combination of residential and commercial use, so it could serve as accommodation for doctoral fellows.
117233.subtitle_en: UNIS will not get a dormitory, but politicians are opening the door for doctoral fellows to live temporarily at the research hotel for a few years.

117243.excerpt_en: Last autumn, Store Norske terminated its agreement with the American company Oxbow Corporation because it believed the deal was overpriced. Oxbow had an agreement to sell Store Norske coal through 2015.
117243.subtitle_en: The court case between Oxbow Corporation and Store Norske begins on Tuesday. Oxbow is claiming NOK 365 million in damages.

117252.excerpt_en: “As I thought about it, it became important that he should not be allowed to take it away from us. He wasn’t going to get it.”
117252.subtitle_en: Neither Christin Kristoffersen nor her son Viljar Hanssen (18) was ever really in doubt about standing for election in Longyearbyen.

117276.excerpt_en: The woman was bitten by the Arctic fox near Svalbard Auto in the harbor area, the Governor says on its website. She received medical treatment at Longyearbyen Hospital.
117276.subtitle_en: The Governor is warning people in Longyearbyen after a woman was bitten by an Arctic fox on Monday afternoon.

117280.excerpt_en: They were driving at 62 and 63 kilometers per hour, respectively, and each received a NOK 2,900 fine. The speed limit at the site is 50 kilometers per hour.
117280.subtitle_en: Two drivers were caught in a speed check outside Longyearbyen School on Wednesday morning.

117300.excerpt_en: “The hunter had injured himself in Fardalen and was having problems with a knee,” says Chief Constable Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office. After the man activated the emergency beacon at around 10 p.m., the Governor sent out a helicopter with a doctor on board.
117300.subtitle_en: On Thursday evening, the Governor had to respond to a hunter who activated an emergency beacon.

117304.excerpt_en: The Danish dog driver has taken over the kennel belonging to Jens Abild, who runs the tourism company Arctic Adventures. Abild is keeping the company and will continue renting out snowmobiles, while the kennel in Bolterdalen will form the backbone of Martin Munck’s new company, Greendog.
117304.subtitle_en: Martin Munck (39) is moving from Greenland with his family to run dogs on Svalbard.

117317.excerpt_en: So far, activity has been very low among the parties running in Longyearbyen’s local election on the 9th and 10th.
117317.subtitle_en: With roses, a manifesto and singing, Svalbard Labour launched Longyearbyen’s own local election campaign this week.
117317.title_en: Our own election campaign gets under way

117324.subtitle_en: The fox killed by a dog in Longyearbyen on Monday had rabies.

117339.subtitle_en: Over the weekend, the Governor euthanized and disposed of two reindeer near Longyearbyen because of suspected rabies.

117349.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Food Safety Authority and the Governor want to capture as many foxes as possible near Longyearbyen to prevent the spread of rabies.

117353.subtitle_en: The two reindeer euthanized on Sunday had rabies.

117366.excerpt_en: After three consecutive six-month periods with more people moving away from Svalbard than moving in, the trend has reversed this year. In the first half of the year, the population increased by 145 people, bringing the total number of registered residents on Svalbard to 2,539.
117366.subtitle_en: Foreigners account for the largest population growth on Svalbard.

117387.excerpt_en: “It is a pilot project that we hope will really take off,” says Martha Otte, project manager at CinemArctic. The idea for an annual film festival on Svalbard arose in 2008, after the Northern Travelling Film Festival was held in Barentsburg.
117387.subtitle_en: After much back and forth, there will be an Arctic film festival on Svalbard. It starts in just one week.

117396.excerpt_en: This afternoon, Bård Thorsen, chief public prosecutor at Økokrim, sought a prison sentence of two years and eight months for former Store Norske director Robert Hermansen. He is also demanding the confiscation of NOK 4 million.
117396.subtitle_en: The prosecution is seeking a prison sentence of two years and eight months for Robert Hermansen.

117422.excerpt_en: Store Norske is taking a new approach to adding some color to life in Svea.
117422.subtitle_en: The mining equipment at Svea Nord has acquired a feminine touch.

117428.excerpt_en: “We searched for the fox and another dead fox, but found neither. The researchers also reported five dead reindeer, but we found three,” says Espen Stokke, a senior adviser with the Governor’s Office.
117428.subtitle_en: The Governor has taken samples from three dead reindeer in Hornsund. A week ago, an aggressive fox attacked one of the researchers at the Polish station.

117443.excerpt_en: On Sunday, the Governor took samples from a reindeer on Platåberget, which the Norwegian Veterinary Institute analyzed. The results show that the reindeer had rabies.
117443.subtitle_en: The reindeer found on Platåberget over the weekend also had rabies.

117453.excerpt_en: “I can sum up these years in three words: exciting, challenging and demanding,” says outgoing local council chairman Kjell Mork (Labour). On 20 September, he chaired his final local council meeting.
117453.subtitle_en: Kjell Mork (62) is stepping down after five years at the helm of the local council. His tenure has been marked by hard work and good cooperation.
117453.title_en: The chain gets a new bearer

117478.subtitle_en: Svalbard CinemArctic opened on Friday evening with “Nanook of the North.” A total of 20 films will be screened in Longyearbyen and Barentsburg this weekend.

117492.subtitle_en: Over the weekend, the Governor of Svalbard and the Norwegian Food Safety Authority tested four reindeer suspected of being infected with rabies.

117501.excerpt_en: “I’m surprised by the severity of the sentence, and naturally I’m upset. I’m almost 73 and have a hell of a lot I still want to do, so I want to serve the sentence as quickly as possible.”
117501.subtitle_en: Robert Hermansen has been sentenced to two years in prison and ordered to forfeit NOK 4 million.

117504.excerpt_en: This became clear on Monday afternoon, when the Norwegian Veterinary Institute’s test results were ready. The fox was shot by the Governor of Svalbard because it was behaving abnormally.

117504.title_en: Another fox tests positive for rabies

117509.subtitle_en: The government proposes allocating NOK 14.6 million to clean emissions from the power plant.

117522.subtitle_en: On Thursday morning, the first fox was caught in a trap set by the Governor of Svalbard and the Norwegian Polar Institute.

117544.excerpt_en: Today is the final day of advance voting in Longyearbyen. On Sunday, the polling station will open at the media center at Lompen Centre. “We have received more advance votes now than in the previous election.”
117544.subtitle_en: The ballot box opens in Longyearbyen on Sunday. Political secretary Svein Olav Ween is hoping for a higher turnout than four years ago.

117547.excerpt_en: Two of the youngest were 16-year-old Emilie Sommervold and her friend Ragnhild Engan (17). “I was afraid of making a mistake, but it went perfectly well,” says Emilie Sommervold. She had already decided which party to vote for.
117547.subtitle_en: There was a queue outside when the polling station opened at 2 p.m. on Sunday. Young first-time voters also turned up to cast their ballots.

117562.excerpt_en: “The plan is to issue two different forecasts for Svalbard. We will keep the old forecast and create a new, more detailed one for Nordenskiöld Land.”
117562.subtitle_en: The North Norway Weather Service says it will provide more detailed forecasts for the central part of Spitsbergen.

117568.excerpt_en: The Labour Party is the election’s big winner with 393 votes. That could give the party seven seats.
117568.subtitle_en: Of 1,592 eligible voters, 907 voted in this year’s local election in Longyearbyen. That gives a turnout of 57 percent, compared with 40 percent in the 2007 election.

117571.excerpt_en: “It’s very gratifying to be elected community council leader. I have no objection to cooperation—we’ve managed it before.”
117571.subtitle_en: Christin Kristoffersen (Labour) and the Labour Party are the election’s big winners. The party won 43 percent of the votes cast, and Kristoffersen will become the new leader of the Longyearbyen Community Council.

117583.excerpt_en: “The intense hunting pressure the population experienced for 100 years before protection took effect most likely eliminated breeding females from some areas of Svalbard, and we are now seeing those areas being used again as denning habitat,” says polar-bear researcher Jon Aars of the Norwegian Polar Institute in an article on…
117583.subtitle_en: Polar bears in Svalbard are now using more denning areas than they did before the population was protected in 1973.

117593.excerpt_en: Polarflokken day-care center was expanded last year. Even so, many children are on the waiting list for a place.
117593.subtitle_en: The day-care centers in Longyearbyen are full. More money is needed to provide places for everyone from the New Year.

117621.excerpt_en: The atmosphere at Kroa was electric from the first note by Canadian blues artist JW-Jones. At Barentz Pub, Micke & Lefty whipped up the crowd with acoustic blues and roots from Finland.
117621.subtitle_en: This year’s Polar Night Blues Festival opened on Thursday with four bands performing—two at Barentz Pub at the Polar Hotel and two at Kroa.

117643.excerpt_en: By Monday morning, NOK 1,024,894 had been raised for the telethon in Longyearbyen and Ny-Ålesund. The amount is expected to rise further as all the donations come in.
117643.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen has raised the most money per person for the telethon.

117653.excerpt_en: “The aircraft was too heavy relative to the braking performance we were able to provide today. We had freezing rain this morning and late morning.”
117653.subtitle_en: Both SAS and the postal flight have canceled today’s service to Longyearbyen. That means passengers, mail and Svalbardposten will all be unable to reach the town today.

117657.excerpt_en: “It was a gift from Lufttransport that we were going to auction off. The Governor of Svalbard believed such a trip was illegal, so we had to give it up,” says Oddny Kjerstad, head of the telethon.
117657.subtitle_en: Lufttransport AS donated a flight to Ny-Ålesund for 14 people to this year’s telethon. The Governor of Svalbard considers it sightseeing, and therefore not permitted.

117663.excerpt_en: Airlift’s contract for helicopter flights in Svalbard runs until April 1, 2014.
117663.subtitle_en: Airlift is not on the list of helicopter companies set to compete for flights in Svalbard after 2014. The company has appealed the decision.
117663.title_en: Airlift left out of the running

117676.excerpt_en: The season normally starts on 1 November, but because of the ongoing rabies outbreak, the Governor of Svalbard put fox trapping on hold. “We have taken time to establish the facts.”
117676.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard decided today that regular fox trapping will take place this winter. Trapping begins on 1 December.

117680.excerpt_en: “I’m really looking forward to getting started in this job,” Per Andersson says in a press release. He succeeds Bjørn Arnestad, who took over as managing director in March 2008.
117680.subtitle_en: Per Andersson (54) has been appointed the new managing director of Store Norske. He will take up the position on January 1.

117703.excerpt_en: “We are working to improve our websites. We have increased the speed, so pages load faster.”
117703.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten is working to upgrade its website. Readers can now comment on the newspaper’s online stories on Facebook.

117715.excerpt_en: There are 2,077 people living in the town today. Of these, 20 percent are foreign nationals from 44 countries. “The increase in the number of foreigners is a reality, and we are dealing with it.”
117715.subtitle_en: The number of foreigners in Longyearbyen is steadily growing. Politicians now want to address the problems and opportunities this development creates.

117720.excerpt_en: There was a large turnout at Svalbard Gallery when the tenth edition of Kunstpause opened on Thursday evening. Newly elected local council leader Christin Kristoffersen officially opened the festival, making it her first official task as local council leader.
117720.subtitle_en: The local cultural festival Kunstpause got under way on Thursday.

117745.excerpt_en: Because of the polar night, the Governor of Svalbard has ended helicopter searches for sick and dead animals in the areas around Longyearbyen. In cooperation with the Norwegian Polar Institute, the Governor will nevertheless continue culling foxes until mid-December.
117745.subtitle_en: Helicopter searches for sick and dead animals have ended, but the hunt for rabies is not over.

117767.excerpt_en: “Many are still struggling and see little hope for the future. 4.”
117767.subtitle_en: Viljar Hanssen, 18, was highlighted during Storberget’s account of emergency preparedness on 22 July.

117774.excerpt_en: “It is very understandable, especially considering that he has served as Minister of Justice for six years. It is a shame for Svalbard, because he has done a fantastic job and been an excellent Svalbard minister,” says local council leader Christin Kristoffersen.
117774.subtitle_en: After six years as Minister of Justice, Knut Storberget stepped down from the government today. The local council leader is not surprised.

117777.excerpt_en: The world’s northernmost jazz festival will take place in February for the 15th time, and as before, several big names are on the bill.
117777.subtitle_en: The rockers from Rogaland are ready for a new tour of Norway and will begin their journey at Polarjazz in Longyearbyen.
117777.title_en: Kaizers to Kick Off in Longyearbyen

117791.excerpt_en: “It was completely uneventful. Everything went well and the family is doing fine,” says midwife Reidun Holte.
117791.subtitle_en: Midwife Reidun Holte delivered a baby girl at Longyearbyen Hospital on Monday, four weeks before her due date.

117792.excerpt_en: “It’s foolish to hold a party in the middle of the week when most people have to go to work,” says senior police officer Per Andreassen. He was notified about the party shortly after midnight. “There was a party in a complex with several flats.”
117792.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard ended a party in the early hours of Wednesday after it disturbed the neighbours’ sleep.

117799.excerpt_en: Last Friday, Knut Storberget stepped down as Minister of Justice. The politician has been popular in Svalbard, and he has also maintained close contact with local council politician Viljar Hanssen and his family following the terrorist attacks on 22 July.
117799.subtitle_en: The outgoing Minister of Justice wants to make his planned trip to Svalbard.

117812.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard and the Norwegian Food Safety Authority opened the season for fox trapping despite the ongoing rabies outbreak. Trapping begins on 1 December.
117812.subtitle_en: Fifty-five people applied for permission to trap foxes next season. Twenty-three were allocated an area.

117820.excerpt_en: “We will be the main station for the Sentinel satellites. The first in a series of three satellites will be launched in 2013.”
117820.subtitle_en: Last week, the European Space Agency, ESA, decided that SvalSat will have primary responsibility for servicing a new series of Earth-observation satellites.

117824.excerpt_en: Public Art Norway, KORO, is the state agency for art in public spaces. “Planning, implementation and quality assurance of art projects are at the heart of our work,” according to the agency.
117824.subtitle_en: Six years ago, Unis cut up a work of art and sent it to the mainland for recycling. Now another state-funded artwork outside the institution appears doomed.

117836.excerpt_en: The duo Gaute Ormåsen and Cecilia Vennersten will take to the cultural centre with their Christmas concert, “Our Christmas”. Video greeting. This is the second year the two singers have embarked on a nationwide tour equipped with Christmas songs.
117836.subtitle_en: Christmas is still more than a month away, but on Sunday you can already get your first taste of the festive spirit.

117847.excerpt_en: A Store Norske employee in his 40s was injured in a workplace accident in Svea at around 5:30 a.m. on Sunday. The accident occurred when the man was inspecting a funnel-shaped coal screen.
117847.subtitle_en: Man fell into a hopper and inhaled coal dust.

117857.excerpt_en: The incident occurred when the SAS flight from Tromsø landed at Svalbard Airport shortly after 2 p.m. this afternoon. “Not dramatic.” The SAS aircraft, carrying 120 passengers, landed normally on the runway and began braking. Near the end of the runway, the plane hit an icy patch.
117857.subtitle_en: An icy patch on the runway caused the scheduled flight from Tromsø to finish its landing across the runway. Today’s flight to Tromsø has been cancelled.
117857.title_en: Icy Runway Caused Plane to Stop Sideways

117872.excerpt_en: The mail plane encountered problems while braking shortly after landing on Monday, 25 January last year.
117872.subtitle_en: The accident during the mail plane’s landing in January last year has been classified as a “serious aviation incident” in the Accident Investigation Board’s report, published today.
117872.title_en: Mail Plane Came Close to Disaster

117875.excerpt_en: The flight from Tromsø had 96 passengers on board, according to duty manager Yngve Ryel of SAS Ground Services in Tromsø. In Longyearbyen, 130 people were due to take the flight back to the mainland.
117875.subtitle_en: Strong crosswinds prevented the SAS flight from landing in Longyearbyen on Thursday. An extra evening flight has been scheduled.

117889.excerpt_en: The dimensions are immense: 85 metres long and 20 metres wide. A floating concrete box that could become Longyearbyen’s new large quay. “Harbour operations in Svalbard are no gold mine.”
117889.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen harbour is short of space. This enormous concrete box could be the solution.
117889.title_en: This Could Become the City’s New Quay

117891.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Mapping Authority has conducted geodetic measurements in Ny-Ålesund since 1994 and now plans to build a new, larger station at Brandalpynten, 1.5 kilometres northwest of the existing facility. Geodesy involves recording even the smallest changes in the Earth’s crust.
117891.subtitle_en: There is strong scepticism about the Norwegian Mapping Authority’s plans to locate a geodetic station at Brandalpynten near Ny-Ålesund. According to the Mapping Authority, there are no alternatives.

117896.excerpt_en: The evaluation, commissioned by the Research Council of Norway, was published earlier this month. It is based on a review of all research results from 2005 to 2009, as well as self-reporting by the research communities, forskning.no writes.
117896.subtitle_en: Research on the ocean and sea ice at the Norwegian Polar Institute has come in for strong criticism in a new report. The institute is also criticised for poor organisation and research planning.

117898.excerpt_en: “This was the last project under my direction. Now it is up to Longyearbyen to decide what they want and what they want to do,” says Janne Nilsen, who has been the circus’s project manager.
117898.subtitle_en: Saturday’s performances were the last for Sirkus Svalnardo—at least with Janne Nilsen as project manager.

117913.excerpt_en: During Sunday’s Advent celebration, there was, as always, a torchlight procession from Huset via Nybyen to the square. On the way, the procession stopped below Mine 2, where Santa lives, so the children could put their wish lists in his mailbox.
117913.subtitle_en: Santa’s mailbox by Mine 2 is now ready to receive your wish list.

117925.excerpt_en: Waiting for the flight to the mainland can be a long, tedious affair, but now you can shorten the wait with free internet at Svalbard Airport. No more coupons. Avinor introduced free internet at all its airports, including Gardermoen, this summer.
117925.subtitle_en: From today, you can surf for free at the country’s airports. You get online by sending a text message.

117933.excerpt_en: Despite several meetings and clear instructions from the Governor of Svalbard, a Russian research institute in St. Petersburg chose to begin construction of a satellite station without permission having been granted.
117933.subtitle_en: The Russians defied the Governor of Svalbard and built a satellite facility without permission. Now the Governor says it must be removed.

117960.excerpt_en: “He has been contacted about it and knows that he will receive an offer,” says Unis board chair Tore Vorren. The selection of a new director was made at the board meeting over the weekend.
117960.subtitle_en: Unis is offering Lasse Lønnum the chance to return to the director’s job at the university centre.

117974.excerpt_en: In October this year, two men aged 22 and 31 were caught driving snowmobiles while over the legal alcohol limit. The cases will be heard as so-called confession cases by the Nord-Troms District Court on Monday.
117974.subtitle_en: When the 22-year-old saw his friend being arrested for drunk driving, he hid the snowmobile and took a taxi home.
117974.title_en: Hid the Snowmobile from the Governor

118000.excerpt_en: “We have had problems with the grate on the boiler that is operating. Last night we switched to backup power,” says operations manager Odd Jostein Sylte at the power station.
118000.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen lost power twice this Friday. Problems with a boiler at the power station and engines shutting down on their own are to blame.

118008.excerpt_en: At 1:45 p.m., the moon will begin moving into the Earth’s shadow. At 3:06 p.m., it will be completely dark, according to himmelkalenderen.com.
118008.subtitle_en: This afternoon there will be a total lunar eclipse, as the moon is swallowed by the Earth’s shadow.
118008.title_en: The Full Moon Will Turn Dark

118012.excerpt_en: The French Air Force wanted to test-fly its new Falcon 2000 LX minijet between the United States and the Black Sea. The route was to cross the Arctic to test the aircraft in cold weather.
118012.subtitle_en: Norwegian authorities refused permission for the French Air Force to land in Longyearbyen.
118012.title_en: French Air Force Denied Landing Permission

118021.excerpt_en: The claim from US-owned Oxbow Coal amounted to NOK 400 million after Store Norske chose last autumn to terminate the agreement to sell coal from the Svea Nord mine. Store Norske argued that the agreement was significantly overpriced.
118021.subtitle_en: Store Norske has been acquitted by the Oslo District Court in the case involving Oxbow Coal and awarded NOK 6 million in legal costs.

118024.excerpt_en: Slowly but surely, the Earth’s shadow moved in front of the moon that afternoon. Shortly after 3 p.m., the moon was hidden.
118024.subtitle_en: The polar night and clear skies made Saturday’s lunar eclipse a beautiful sight in Longyearbyen.

118028.excerpt_en: Officers from the Governor of Svalbard’s office were preparing for a sobriety check when they stopped a car with ice-covered windows. The driver is now suspected of driving under the influence. “I think it’s deplorable that the first person we encounter is impaired,” says chief police officer Per Andreassen.
118028.subtitle_en: A woman was stopped by police on Saturday morning and suspected of drunk driving.

118035.excerpt_en: Environment Minister Erik Solheim (SV) further says in a press release from the Ministry of the Environment that, after ten years in use, the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act has proved to be an important tool for safeguarding Svalbard’s vulnerable natural environment.
118035.subtitle_en: Amendments to the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act will be considered by Parliament on Monday. The act entered into force in 2002 and is now becoming an even better tool for protecting Svalbard’s nature, according to the environment minister.
118035.title_en: Svalbard Environmental Protection Act in Parliament

118040.excerpt_en: The Unis board offered Lasse Lønnum the directorship two weeks ago, but Lønnum has declined. Instead, he will continue as director at the University of Tromsø.
118040.subtitle_en: The search for a new Unis director continues after Lasse Lønnum declined to return.

118043.excerpt_en: A crowd of children dressed in white wound their way between the library’s bookshelves this morning. Holding a Lucia celebration at the library is a Longyearbyen tradition.
118043.subtitle_en: Children from Polarflokken kindergarten held a Lucia procession at the library today.

118053.excerpt_en: The County Governor of Troms is giving Longyearbyen’s healthcare services a proper Christmas present. The hospital is receiving NOK 550,000 for an additional public health nursing position for 2012.
118053.subtitle_en: Public health nurse Reidun Holte is getting a colleague, and Longyearbyen will have an additional public health nurse next year.
118053.title_en: Two Public Health Nurses Next Year

118065.excerpt_en: A total of twelve foxes were caught by employees of the Norwegian Polar Institute (NPI). According to the NPI, few or no foxes remain in the vicinity of Longyearbyen now, but new foxes are likely to arrive.
118065.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has provisionally concluded the work to combat rabies and removed the fox traps in the area around Longyearbyen.

118076.excerpt_en: The incident took place in October this year, and the cases were heard by the Nord-Troms District Court earlier this week. The two men, in their 20s and 30s, were sentenced to pay NOK 39,000 and 34,000, respectively.
118076.subtitle_en: Two men must pay NOK 39,000 and 34,000 for driving snowmobiles while under the influence of alcohol.

118091.excerpt_en: Land uplift in Svalbard is currently about 8.5 millimetres per year. On the mainland, Trysil has the greatest uplift, at 7.7 millimetres per year, according to forskning.no.
118091.subtitle_en: Land uplift in Svalbard is unusually large. The cause is ice changes over the past 150 years.

118103.excerpt_en: Tomorrow is Gunnar Sand’s final working day as director at Unis, and the board has now found his successor.
