118103.subtitle_en: The search for a director at Unis is over. Ole Arve Misund has accepted the position.
118103.title_en: Here Is the New Unis Director

118129.excerpt_en: Gunnar Sand joined Unis in 2006 and has served as director ever since. Today was his final working day at the university centre, and he also moved away from Longyearbyen.
118129.subtitle_en: After almost six years, Gunnar Sand packed his bags and left Svalbard today. “It is bittersweet,” says the outgoing Unis director.

118137.excerpt_en: Employees at Airlift’s Longyearbyen base have been living with uncertainty since it became clear earlier this autumn that Airlift was not in the running to operate in Svalbard after 1 April 2014.
118137.subtitle_en: Regardless of which helicopter company takes over from Airlift in Svalbard in 2014, the employees are guaranteed jobs.

118144.excerpt_en: An EU rule means ambulance aircraft cannot take on the fuel they need in difficult weather conditions, NRK Nordnytt reports. Seeking an exemption, the strict EU regulations have led to discussions between health professionals and Norwegian and European aviation authorities.
118144.subtitle_en: Strict EU weight requirements could prevent ambulance aircraft from taking on enough fuel to reach Svalbard.

118154.excerpt_en: “It really wasn’t that bad once you had jumped in, but it was awful watching the others swim before me. It was strange going under in the slush,” says Pastor Leif Magne Helgesen.
118154.subtitle_en: Pastor Leif Magne Helgesen took the opportunity to go for a Christmas swim while visiting the crew at Hopen on Wednesday.

118156.excerpt_en: The existing geodetic observatory in Ny-Ålesund urgently needs replacing. Today, the government decided that a new facility will be built at a cost of NOK 219 million.
118156.subtitle_en: The government is investing more than NOK 200 million in a new observatory in Ny-Ålesund. It will provide better climate knowledge.

118171.excerpt_en: “Svalbard has an entirely unique and rare Arctic wilderness. We will now begin the work of determining whether parts of Svalbard should be nominated for the World Heritage List,” says State Secretary Heidi Sørensen in a press release.
118171.subtitle_en: The government is beginning work on nominating parts of Svalbard for UNESCO’s World Heritage List.
118171.title_en: Could Make the World Heritage List

118179.excerpt_en: “This year, we have introduced a limit of 500 competitors because of logistics and safety along the course. This year we received many registrations during the final week, especially the day before the race.”
118179.subtitle_en: Anyone wishing to take part in next year’s ski marathon must hurry. On Friday morning, only two places remained.

118184.excerpt_en: The man was supposed to camp between Fardalen and Endalen, but when his contact in town received an unclear message over a poor satellite-phone connection, the Governor’s office was alerted. Chief inspector Sidsel Svarstad says the man had agreed to call his contact every other day.
118184.subtitle_en: On 23 December, the Governor of Svalbard sent a helicopter to retrieve a man camping between Fardalen and Endalen.

118191.excerpt_en: “It looks as though there could be quite a bit of wind from the south-southeast, but not enough to send the fireworks sideways. I think they will go straight up,” says meteorological consultant Torgeir Mørk at Longyearbyen airport.
118191.subtitle_en: The weather on New Year’s Eve will be unsettled, with some wind, a chance of light snow and rising temperatures. The wind will increase during the evening and night.
118191.title_en: Unsettled Weather on New Year’s Eve

118201.excerpt_en: Soleim began his trapping life in Svalbard in 1976. He spent his first winter at Bjonahamna in Tempelfjorden, but moved to Kapp Wijk the following year.
118201.subtitle_en: Harald A. Soleim (71) is the only trapper in Svalbard spending Christmas at the trapping station this year.

118226.excerpt_en: The snowmobile accident, the 22 July terrorist attack and the polar bear attack in Tempelfjorden were the articles most readers clicked on in the past year.
118226.subtitle_en: The story about a snowmobile driver seriously injured in Adventdalen was the most-read article on svalbardposten.no last year.

118240.excerpt_en: The final permit to open a new coal mine in Lunckefjell came two days before Christmas. By then, Store Norske had repeatedly chased the Ministry of the Environment, which had left the application sitting for months without taking action.
118240.subtitle_en: Per Andersson (54) practically had the Lunckefjell mine dropped into his lap when he took up his post as Store Norske’s new managing director on Tuesday.
118240.title_en: There at Just the Right Moment

118243.excerpt_en: Despite fine words from the Governor of Svalbard, as well as the country’s highest authorities, the trapping industry—the oldest industry in Svalbard—is struggling to make a living.
118243.subtitle_en: The number of trappers overwintering has not been this low since the 1970s. Only Harald A. Soleim at Kapp Wijk is holding out.

118277.excerpt_en: A total of 126,350 passengers passed through Svalbard Airport last year, an increase of 0.5 percent. This was the first increase since 2008, which remains the record year with nearly 140,000 passengers.
118277.subtitle_en: Svalbard Airport saw a slight increase in the number of air passengers last year.

118280.excerpt_en: Recently, Longyearbyen Post Office has applied a strict, inflexible addressing policy to B-mail. Many letters and parcels arrive in Svalbard with the correct recipient’s name and residential address, but without a postbox address.
118280.subtitle_en: The post office has returned letters and parcels without a postbox address. It has caused an uproar.
118280.title_en: Return Policy on the Way Out

118291.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten has twice asked Bydrift for access to the full report following an unannounced emergency preparedness exercise at the power station on 17 November.
118291.subtitle_en: In November, Arctic Safety conducted an emergency preparedness exercise at the power station. But Bydrift is keeping the company’s assessment of its preparedness secret.
118291.title_en: You Won’t Get to See This Report

118306.excerpt_en: The rib fragment is at the Polar Museum in Tromsø, after the museum acquired it two years ago. “We do not know whether the skeletal fragment came from Andrée or Frænkel, but we know it did not come from Strindberg.”
118306.subtitle_en: The cause of death of the Andrée Expedition has been a mystery since the remains of the three Swedes were found on Kvitøya in 1930. Researchers now want to examine part of a rib.
118306.title_en: What Did the Andrée Expedition Die Of?

118315.excerpt_en: “The bear was spotted by an experienced tour guide with Spitsbergen Travel, so the sighting is confirmed. It was seen at around 1:30 p.m. heading towards the mouth of Adventdalen,” says duty chief inspector Per Andreassen of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
118315.subtitle_en: A polar bear was spotted at Jernsenga, about ten kilometres into Adventdalen, around midday on Sunday.

118320.excerpt_en: “Margrethe Keyser was responsible for the polar bear database at the Governor of Svalbard’s office. She has an overview of how many encounters there have been and their outcomes.”
118320.subtitle_en: Polar bears and people are the first topic at the Svalbard Seminar 2012, which begins today.

118333.excerpt_en: In April, the man allegedly put a woman in a chokehold, dragged her by the hair and hit her in the face with a hard-plastic-coated glove somewhere in Longyearbyen. He also allegedly kicked and/or stomped on a man’s face and/or throat while the man was lying in his bed.
118333.subtitle_en: A man from Longyearbyen is charged with injuring a woman under especially aggravating circumstances. The court proceedings concluded yesterday.

118339.excerpt_en: Alone on a snowmobile in an avalanche-prone area, in the middle of the polar night, without a weapon and with a healthy dose of arrogance. That combination led the Governor of Svalbard to dispatch a helicopter at around 10:30 p.m. on Tuesday.
118339.subtitle_en: A headstrong Israeli tourist heading towards Fardalen prompted the Governor of Svalbard to deploy a helicopter on Tuesday evening.

118349.excerpt_en: The agitated Arctic fox was first spotted by a motorist on Road 300 between the church and Huset. The fox was biting a snow pole at the time.
118349.subtitle_en: A student nearly came under attack by an agitated fox between the school and Nybyen on Tuesday afternoon.

118352.excerpt_en: The accident happened when the snowmobile driver hit a rise on the glacier and was thrown off the vehicle. “This happened in the lower part of Longyearbreen at around 8:30 p.m. on Wednesday,” says Per Andreassen, chief inspector with the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
118352.subtitle_en: A teenager suffered moderate injuries in a snowmobile accident on Longyearbreen on Wednesday evening.

118355.excerpt_en: Seven frustrated young people visited Svalbardposten on Tuesday afternoon.
118355.subtitle_en: Eight tenth-graders want to take the Technical and Industrial Production vocational programme next year. Today, Oppvekstforetaket will decide their future.

118378.excerpt_en: Eight tenth-grade students want to take the Technical and Industrial Production (TIP) programme next school year.
118378.subtitle_en: Politicians will do everything they can to meet the vocational education preferences of the tenth-graders. There could now be two vocational programmes this autumn.
118378.title_en: Opening the door to technical vocational studies

118395.excerpt_en: While last winter was the old-fashioned, chilly kind, this winter looks set to be a mild one. Since last autumn, the entire region has experienced unusually mild weather.
118395.subtitle_en: The temperature in Longyearbyen has been 10 degrees higher than normal over the past month. Much suggests that this will continue.

118403.excerpt_en: “Oxbow is appealing the entire ruling. We believe the Oslo District Court’s judgment was thorough and well founded, and that it was entirely correct.”
118403.subtitle_en: Coal trading company Oxbow Coal is appealing the Oslo District Court ruling, in which the company lost its NOK 400 million lawsuit against Store Norske.

118416.excerpt_en: Frustration was running high among the young people who showed up at Svalbardposten’s offices last week. Eight out of 10.
118416.subtitle_en: Young people can celebrate. There will be two vocational programmes in Longyearbyen this autumn.

118453.excerpt_en: Over the past year, several buildings in Barentsburg have received a facelift, thanks to funding from the Russian Ministry of Natural Resources. Last summer, work began on improving the hotel building’s insulation and cladding it with new siding.
118453.subtitle_en: The hotel in Barentsburg is getting a major upgrade. That means its doors will remain closed until March.

118481.excerpt_en: “Yesterday was completely hopeless. We had no chance of achieving the braking effect required,” says Morten Ulsnes, airport manager in Longyearbyen.
118481.subtitle_en: Sunday’s SAS flight from Tromsø was cancelled. Two flights are scheduled today, but it is uncertain whether they can land in Longyearbyen.

118484.excerpt_en: “We’re heading out in convoy now and will reassess the conditions later today,” says Marianne Aasen, general manager of Bydrift. She cannot say how long convoy traffic will continue. “We’ll see what is needed.”
118484.subtitle_en: Bydrift has now reopened Airport Road for convoy traffic.

118490.excerpt_en: While the mainland is enjoying pleasant, cold winter days, the situation is completely different in Svalbard. Heavy precipitation and mild weather triggered avalanches and led to several road closures in and around Longyearbyen.
118490.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen was the warmest place in the country on Monday.

118513.excerpt_en: The weather in Longyearbyen is highly unstable, and ground crews at Svalbard Airport have been working flat out to make landing possible. “The runway was slippery, so the aircraft had to turn around and return to Tromsø,” says Karianne Andersen, a senior consultant with SAS.
118513.subtitle_en: Tuesday’s SAS flight from Tromsø to Longyearbyen had to turn back.

118521.excerpt_en: Yesterday, the SAS aircraft had to turn around and fly back to Tromsø because of snow on the runway in Longyearbyen. Air traffic is also experiencing problems today because of the weather conditions at Svalbard Airport.
118521.subtitle_en: Air traffic between Tromsø and Longyearbyen has faced major problems for the second day in a row.

118541.excerpt_en: On Sunday and Tuesday, SAS scheduled flights between Tromsø and Longyearbyen were cancelled. Yesterday’s extra flight was also cancelled, while the scheduled flight hit the mark and managed to land in Longyearbyen.
118541.subtitle_en: After several days of flight chaos and waiting, all SAS passengers have now arrived in Longyearbyen.

118544.excerpt_en: “The warm-up is always a great thing. We’re off to a kick-start.”
118544.subtitle_en: Local musicians kicked off the jazz festival on Wednesday. Now the festival director hopes the artists can make it to town.
118544.title_en: Festival gets off to a hot start

118548.excerpt_en: The air ambulances cannot fly when temperatures drop below 54 degrees below zero, which is not unusual at 30,000 feet in winter. The planes must then fly lower than usual and use more fuel.
118548.subtitle_en: The new air ambulances cannot reach Longyearbyen in cold weather. Now the Air Ambulance Service must take action.

118549.excerpt_en: Unis wants to house its doctoral students at the researcher hotel Unis Guest House until 2017. On Monday, politicians on the Environment and Business Committee (MNU) said no.
118549.subtitle_en: Politicians will not let Unis use the researcher hotel to house doctoral students. Unis reacts with disbelief.

118567.excerpt_en: At long last, everything came together, and the Rogaland rockers could perform in Longyearbyen and at Polarjazz for the first time. The band was welcomed by an enthusiastic audience at the Cultural Centre, and Kaizers delivered a blistering marathon concert.
118567.subtitle_en: The Cultural Centre was packed to the rafters during Kaizers Orchestra’s concert yesterday. And no one was disappointed.

118577.excerpt_en: According to the judgment, the man put his former girlfriend in a chokehold, dragged her by the hair and hit her in the face with a hard-plastic-coated glove. He then attacked a man who was with the woman.
118577.subtitle_en: A man in his 20s has been sentenced to 45 days in prison after attacking two people in Longyearbyen in April last year.

118591.excerpt_en: The newspaper is planning a “Nordic edition” at the end of this month. In connection with it, they want to speak with the world’s northernmost inhabitant.
118591.subtitle_en: Canadian newspaper Metro in Montreal wants to speak with the world’s northernmost villager, whom it believes lives in Longyearbyen.

118596.excerpt_en: At around 5 a.m. on Wednesday, the weather station at Svalbard Airport recorded a full 7.0°C. This is by far the highest temperature the station has measured in February since it began operating in 1975.
118596.subtitle_en: With a full 7°C, Longyearbyen has set a new February temperature record. A new temperature record has also been set in Svea.

118598.excerpt_en: “It is unfortunate that this is the case. We will place greater emphasis on and raise awareness of this issue going forward, and continue with checks,” says Chief Superintendent Erik Nygaard of the Governor’s Office.
118598.subtitle_en: Thirteen people were caught driving under the influence last year, compared with two the year before. The Governor of Svalbard is following up with checks.

118609.excerpt_en: Last November, Bydrift hired Arctic Safety to conduct an unannounced emergency preparedness exercise at Energiverket. However, large parts of the consultancy’s report were kept from the public.
118609.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard upheld Svalbardposten’s appeal. The entire report from the emergency preparedness exercise at Energiverket is therefore being made public.

118621.excerpt_en: The athletes from the neighbouring towns competed in badminton, football, table tennis, indoor hockey, volleyball and basketball.
118621.subtitle_en: Barentsburg took on Longyearbyen’s athletes in ball games on Saturday. Longyearbyen won a narrow overall victory.

118634.excerpt_en: “That feels so good—brilliant,” says Trond Espen Haug. He is standing in the finish area when he learns that his time is a new record for the route from Nybyen to Trollsteinen and back down. “The weather and conditions were incredibly good.”
118634.subtitle_en: Trond Espen Haug set a new record of 50 minutes and 26 seconds in Spitsbergen Up and Down on Saturday evening.

118640.excerpt_en: The past few days have brought brilliant winter weather, with beautiful light and gorgeous colours. The twilight in the middle of the day signals that the polar night is now over.
118640.subtitle_en: The polar night is over, and on Thursday the sun will once again rise above the horizon in Longyearbyen.

118668.excerpt_en: There is currently intense activity at the imposing processing plant in Svea, after it had been closed since 20 November last year.
118668.subtitle_en: After five months of operation, Store Norske had to shut down the coal-processing plant in Svea this autumn. The plant was not designed for Svalbard conditions, and the installation is substandard.

118671.excerpt_en: “To ensure the safety of residents and others staying in Svalbard, we will lease an air ambulance for two months. The aircraft will be based in Tromsø and will also be used for air-ambulance flights on the long-runway network in Northern Norway,” says Jan Norum, medical director at Helse Nord RHF, in a press release.
118671.subtitle_en: Helse Nord RHF is now leasing a jet to ensure air-ambulance preparedness for Longyearbyen in March and April.

118682.excerpt_en: For several years, there has been talk of introducing compulsory pilotage in Svalbard to improve maritime safety. Last autumn, the government decided to establish a state pilot service in Svalbard waters, as on the mainland.
118682.subtitle_en: Large vessels sailing in Svalbard waters must now have a pilot. The Norwegian Coastal Administration proposes that ships bound for Svea must already carry a pilot this summer.

118685.excerpt_en: According to the Longyearbyen Community Council’s website, the two senior politicians will visit the town. “This is great fun, and it’s nice that they wanted to take part in the Sun Festival.”
118685.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen will receive distinguished visitors on Sun Day, 8 March. Both Foreign Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and the EU’s “foreign minister,” Lady Ashton, will visit Longyearbyen.
118685.title_en: Støre to Attend Sun Festival Week

118699.excerpt_en: “We have suspended our tours until Tuesday to see how things develop,” says Sveinung Toppe, head of guiding at Spitsbergen Travel. He says the collapse occurred about 50 metres inside the cave and blocked the passage.
118699.subtitle_en: On Wednesday afternoon, between 10 and 20 cubic metres of ice collapsed in the ice cave in Longyearbreen.

118713.excerpt_en: Last weekend, Troms AUF held its annual meeting, with Svalbard AUF very well represented by five delegates. This reflects the local branch’s growing membership.
118713.subtitle_en: Over the past year, membership in Svalbard AUF has more than doubled.

118716.excerpt_en: Those who were a little slow off the mark, or were unsure whether they wanted to trudge through the ski tracks with blood in their mouths, are getting another chance.
118716.subtitle_en: In December, the organizers of the Svalbard Ski Marathon said the race was fully booked after runner number 500 signed up. Now they are making a U-turn.
118716.title_en: Room for More on the Trails

118721.excerpt_en: By 15 May, three large concrete foundations for satellite antennas, along with cable trenches and two container cabins, must be removed from the mountain just behind Barentsburg.
118721.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is demanding that the Russians remove the illegally erected satellite-station installation in Barentsburg.
118721.title_en: Russians Ordered to Remove Illegal Antenna Installation

118728.excerpt_en: Kjell Mork has just moved into his newly built boathouse in the Sjøområdet district, in northern Longyearbyen. The newspaper singled out Kjell Mork after speaking with Kjersti Ellen Norås of Svalbard Tourism.
118728.subtitle_en: Canadian newspaper Métro Montréal has named Kjell Mork the northernmost inhabitant in the world.
118728.title_en: Believes Kjell Lives Farther North Than Anyone

118749.excerpt_en: After the Brünnich’s guillemot was listed as near threatened in Svalbard in the 2010 Red List, the Directorate for Nature Management (DN) proposed protecting the bird from hunters’ guns. Following a public consultation, it has reached the same conclusion.
118749.subtitle_en: Following a public consultation, the Directorate for Nature Management has concluded that Brünnich’s guillemot may not be hunted in Svalbard.
118749.title_en: Brünnich’s Guillemot Removed from the Hunting List

118781.excerpt_en: The documentary “Tilbake” will be broadcast tonight on NRK1. The programme lets viewers follow three young people’s return to everyday life after the 22 July attacks.
118781.subtitle_en: Viljar Hanssen has been followed by TV cameras since mid-August. Tonight, the documentary about his road back is being shown.

118788.excerpt_en: Local council Conservative Trond E. Johansen is reacting strongly to the research hotel case being brought back before the Environment and Industry Committee (MNU) on Monday.
118788.subtitle_en: In January, the Environment and Industry Committee rejected Unis’s request to use the research hotel as student accommodation. On Monday, the matter will be reconsidered after the Labour members of the committee changed their minds.

118796.excerpt_en: Every year on 8 March, children in Longyearbyen put on sun collars, eat sun buns and call for the yellow, warming orb that has been absent for so long.
118796.subtitle_en: The sun has not appeared on Sun Day since 2005. It does not look as though it will make an appearance this year either.

118801.excerpt_en: The cloud cover did nothing to dampen the mood by the old hospital steps below Svalbard Church. Nursery and schoolchildren wore sun collars and sang, while Viljar Hanssen guided the many attendees through the event.
118801.subtitle_en: Lots of children, sun collars, two foreign ministers, laughter and singing. The only thing missing was the sun.
118801.title_en: Sang for Støre and the sun

118812.excerpt_en: Last week it became clear that the research hotel case would be reconsidered, after the Environment and Business Committee (MNU) rejected changing the area’s local development plan a month and a half earlier.
118812.subtitle_en: The Labour Party forced through a new review of the research hotel proposal. A deputy representative from the party ensured on Monday that they nevertheless failed to prevail.

118825.excerpt_en: Until now, employees of Longyearbyen Local Council have been able to rent homes at an exceptionally favourable price. On Tuesday, politicians on the Administration Committee (AU) backed raising the price per square metre from NOK 28.41 to NOK 45.
118825.subtitle_en: Politicians expect an uproar after backing higher rents for Longyearbyen Local Council housing.

118832.subtitle_en: Many people have been annoyed by major errors in yr.no’s temperature forecasts for Svalbard. Now the weather service promises improvements.

118839.excerpt_en: The story takes place aboard an isolated research vessel during the Second World War, where the conflicts of the war unfold. The vessel used during filming is the Swedish tourist ship “Stockholm”, which has spent many years operating in Svalbard.
118839.subtitle_en: The Swedish film “En fiende att dö för” premieres in Sweden on Friday. The film was partly shot in Svalbard and is an international thriller drama.

118854.excerpt_en: The nurse was checking the man’s blood pressure when he put her in a chokehold and said, “I’m going to kill you.” This happened late one evening in September last year.
118854.subtitle_en: A man in his 20s put a nurse at Longyearbyen Hospital in a chokehold in September last year and made threats.

118859.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the accident at 7:10 p.m. Shortly afterwards, the rescue helicopter hovered and illuminated the mountainside, while rescuers made their way up to the accident site, around 100–150 metres up the slope, near the cemetery. “Two men had made their way up Platåberget.”
118859.subtitle_en: A local man in his 30s has been taken to Longyearbyen Hospital with serious injuries after jumping from the top of Platåfjellet with a paraglider.

118893.excerpt_en: The Longyearbyen man was seriously injured and flown by air ambulance to Tromsø on Tuesday evening. “He does not have a licence to fly a paraglider and is not a member of the Norwegian Air Sports Federation either. We had a similar case on the mainland last autumn in which a pilot was badly injured.”
118893.subtitle_en: The man who crashed into a mountainside with a paraglider on Tuesday has neither a licence nor training, and may face charges.

118896.excerpt_en: We have to go all the way back to 30 December last year to find a day that was colder than Longyearbyen’s normal temperature.
118896.subtitle_en: Every day in 2012 has been far warmer than normal for Longyearbyen.

118899.excerpt_en: The artist painted several pictures after visiting Svalbard. In 1995, Galleri Svalbard was established on the basis of 40 oil paintings, watercolours and screen prints by Tveter, mainly featuring Svalbard motifs.
118899.subtitle_en: Svalbard painter Kåre Tveter has died after a long illness. He was 90.

118910.excerpt_en: Former Environment Minister Erik Solheim was supposed to host his Nordic counterparts during their Svalbard trip today and tomorrow. Instead, Bård Vegar Solhjell will receive the other Nordic environment ministers.
118910.subtitle_en: The Nordic environment ministers are visiting Svalbard this afternoon.

118915.excerpt_en: On Monday afternoon, a Greenland dog slipped out of a cabin at Vestpynten. Two dogs have killed one reindeer each this week. “It caught a reindeer and injured it.”
118915.subtitle_en: On Monday afternoon, a Greenland dog slipped out of a cabin at Vestpynten. Two dogs have killed one reindeer each this week.

118920.excerpt_en: “The biggest challenge is transporting all the machinery and equipment from Svea across the glaciers and here,” says project manager Jostein Nordstrøm of Veidekke Entreprenører. He looks around from where he is standing at the foot of Skollfjellet, watching the machines at work.
118920.subtitle_en: Work to prepare for a new mine at Lunckefjellet began on Monday. By the end of August, construction machinery and vehicles should be able to cross Marthabreen.
118920.title_en: Work begins on a new coal mine

118940.excerpt_en: However, some of the cabins are more difficult to reach because of a lack of ice on the lakes, while there is plenty of snow on land.
118940.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s cabin draw is complete. Twenty-five people applied to borrow their ten cabins over Easter.

118942.excerpt_en: Bydrift wants to save electricity and money by replacing today’s streetlights with new LED lights. A report from Electronova concludes that such a replacement could save at least 75 percent in energy and more than NOK 200,000 a year.
118942.subtitle_en: The LED lamps tested by Bydrift use 75 percent less energy than today’s streetlights. From next year, the entire town will be lit with LEDs.

118966.excerpt_en: “Blasting was carried out that should not have taken place before a response had been received from the Governor of Svalbard. Veidekke blasted before the permit had formally been granted.”
118966.subtitle_en: Without waiting for a response to an application to the Governor of Svalbard, Veidekke carried out blasting at Skollfjellet earlier this week to trigger an avalanche.

118980.excerpt_en: The aggressive Arctic fox was first spotted by a motorist on Road 300 between the church and Huset. The fox was then standing and biting a snow pole.
118980.subtitle_en: The fox put down by a police officer in Longyearbyen on 17 January had rabies. This is shown by the results of analyses from the Norwegian Veterinary Institute.

118988.excerpt_en: Unis needs CO2 to test whether it can be stored in the bedrock beneath Adventdalen. Last summer, Bydrift and Unis applied to the Ministry of Justice for NOK 5 million for a preliminary project.
118988.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Justice has no CO2 funding to offer Unis and Bydrift. But Unis is not giving up.

article_keywords_en: senior police officer of the Governor’s Office
118997.excerpt_en: “She hit her head so hard that her helmet cracked, but she is not believed to be seriously injured,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office. The woman was part of a guided snowmobile group.
118997.subtitle_en: A Danish woman in her 40s hit her head when her snowmobile overturned in Grøndalen. She was flown to Longyearbyen by helicopter.

119007.excerpt_en: With temperatures around minus 15 degrees Celsius in Longyearbyen, the past few days have been of the old, normal variety. Many are especially eager to see the forecast for the Easter holiday, and the outlook looks very good.
119007.subtitle_en: The weather is shaping up for a really fine Easter. Little cloud and wind, along with low temperatures, are expected through the week.

119024.excerpt_en: “Now we will try to get the boat back into the ice. We will see what conditions are like in Tempelfjorden and assess the situation from there,” says Steinar Rorgemoen, general manager of Basecamp Spitsbergen.
119024.subtitle_en: ‘Noorderlicht’ arrived in Longyearbyen on Sunday after the ice in Tempelfjorden was broken up. Today, Basecamp is attempting to get the vessel back into position.

119027.excerpt_en: The incident occurred in September last year, when the nurse was checking the 19-year-old man’s blood pressure. He startled and put the nurse in a chokehold.
119027.subtitle_en: A young man has been sentenced to 45 hours of community service for putting a nurse in a chokehold at Longyearbyen Hospital.

119035.excerpt_en: “A person was injured in a snowmobile accident on the moraine at Longyearbreen. Based on the report, the doctor wanted the person picked up by helicopter,” says Senior Police Officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office.
119035.subtitle_en: A young man was picked up from the moraine at Longyearbreen by the Governor’s rescue helicopter on Wednesday evening.

119049.excerpt_en: “Generally speaking, it has been a fantastic Easter weather-wise, and it has been quiet,” says Chief Superintendent Erik Nygaard of the Governor’s Office. There were no major rescue or search operations during Easter, but a total of four people were picked up by the Governor’s rescue helicopter after being injured on snowmobile trips.
119049.subtitle_en: Blue skies and few rescue operations—that is how Easter can be summed up.

119067.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten has received concerned reports from people in Longyearbyen that some of those travelling to the east coast are behaving far from appropriately around a female polar bear with two vulnerable cubs.
119067.subtitle_en: A female polar bear with two two-year-old cubs has recently drawn many people to take snowmobiles along the east coast of Spitsbergen. Not everyone is behaving properly.

119075.excerpt_en: Over the past few days, representatives of the Conservative Party have received a thorough briefing on the energy situation and the prospects for CO2 capture. Strengthened in their conviction: in January, the party proposed building a new coal-fired power station with CO2 capture and storage from day one.
119075.subtitle_en: The Conservative Party wants a new power station with full CO2 capture in Longyearbyen. This week, the party has been visiting Svalbard.
119075.title_en: Powering Up Efforts on CO2 Capture

119086.excerpt_en: If there is one event that matters to Longyearbyen’s dog-sledding community, it is Trappers Trail. This weekend saw this year’s edition of the race.
119086.subtitle_en: With a margin of just six minutes, Liv Bjørsvik won Sunday afternoon’s Trappers Trail for large sleds.

119088.excerpt_en: This weekend, the county showcase for Troms was held in Finnsnes. From around 100 stage acts and 74 art entries, the two girls from Longyearbyen were sent on to the national showcase in Trondheim in June.
119088.subtitle_en: Marlene Mellum (16) and Erle Haldorsen (15) have advanced to the national showcase of the Youth Cultural Festival (UKM).

119101.excerpt_en: The owner of a sled dog let it run loose in Longyeardalen in February. The dog then ran off and mauled a reindeer until it bled.
119101.subtitle_en: Two dog owners must pay several thousand kroner for letting their dogs run loose.
119101.title_en: Fined for Letting Dogs Run Loose

119125.excerpt_en: The annual Gruveløpet is being held for the eighth time, with 45 skiers registered for the 42-kilometre race from Svea to Longyearbyen. Guessing the winner: race director Roy Are Hanssen does not expect any major surprises this year.
119125.subtitle_en: Tomorrow, 45 skiers will set off from Svea for Longyearbyen.

119132.excerpt_en: A leaking pipe caused the power station to shut down on Friday. “We were in the process of replacing the control system on one of the boilers, so we couldn’t simply start boiler number two when the one in operation stopped,” says energy manager Knut Flå.
119132.subtitle_en: Parts of Longyearbyen were without power for three hours on Saturday. Both the power station and the backup power station were out of operation.

119137.excerpt_en: After lengthy and at times tough negotiations between Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) and Store Norske, the parties have reached a new agreement on coal deliveries from Mine 7 to the power station. Up 30 percent. The new agreement alone will increase the electricity price by 10 øre per kWh over the next two years.
119137.subtitle_en: Just before Christmas, politicians voted to raise the electricity price by 25 øre per kWh. Now electricity is set to become even more expensive.
119137.title_en: New Agreement Means Higher Electricity Prices

119144.excerpt_en: The two fastest completed the route, which started at 9:57 a.m., in just under two and a half hours. “I heard about Gruveløpet and thought I’d try to join in. It was a fantastic trip,” says Ola Eggen (32), who crossed the finish line at 12:23 p.m.
119144.subtitle_en: Ola Eggen and Halvard Pedersen were the fastest from Svea to Longyearbyen on Saturday. Ståle Pedersen came third.

119148.excerpt_en: “The revised Svalbard Environmental Protection Act has become an even better tool for protecting nature in Svalbard. The amendments are mainly adjustments to the provisions after the Act has been in use for ten years.”
119148.subtitle_en: The revised Svalbard Environmental Protection Act was sanctioned by the King in Council today. The amendments enter into force on 1 July.

119160.excerpt_en: The seven properties, comprising 106 small apartments and bedsits, were put up for sale just before Easter. The total valuation was NOK 57.2 million, and the sale was completed on Monday afternoon.
119160.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council has sold seven of its properties to Tromsø-based company Triko.

119165.excerpt_en: This year, 628 people have applied to study at UNIS—200 more than four years ago. UNIS is naturally very pleased with the development. “It shows that we are an attractive place for students seeking Arctic expertise,” says UNIS director Ole Arve Misund.
119165.subtitle_en: With more than 600 applicants, UNIS is experiencing record-high interest.

119175.excerpt_en: “We have adopted an overall plan stating that we are to reduce alcohol consumption. That means we must also dare to take action.”
119175.subtitle_en: Next Tuesday, the local council will decide on the town’s liquor-licensing applications. At Tuesday’s executive committee meeting, politicians warned of tighter restrictions.
119175.title_en: Cutting Off the Booze at Midnight

119189.excerpt_en: According to Store Norske CEO Per Andersson, mixed rock has caused coal production at Svea Nord to proceed very slowly over the past three months. “We reached a point where there was nothing else to do but end production.”
119189.subtitle_en: Coal production at Svea Nord was halted with immediate effect last Friday. The reason is the large amount of rock and extensive wear on the equipment.

119192.excerpt_en: “The delegation from the research institution China Institute of Radiowave Propagation is carrying out a technical review of the facility, and we are also looking at the infrastructure required,” says project manager Arvid Øvergård. Towering domeEiscat Svalbard Radar currently consists of two antennas with diameters of 32 and 42 metres.
119192.subtitle_en: After a long period of uncertainty, prospects are brightening for a third antenna at the Eiscat facility. A Chinese delegation inspected the facility this week in preparation for its expansion.

119194.excerpt_en: With 599 registered participants, Saturday’s marathon through Todalen, Bødalen and Gangdalen was set to be especially crowded. Because of poor visibility at Fritham, the race was postponed by an hour, but at 11 a.m. the marathon could finally get under way, to the organizers’ relief.
119194.subtitle_en: Kjetil Watne of Oslo was the fastest man in Saturday’s Svalbard Ski Marathon.

119205.excerpt_en: As last year, the parade will go from Skjæringa to the miners’ monument in the square. This will be followed by an event at the cultural centre.
119205.subtitle_en: May Day is being marked today with a parade and a speech by Labour Party deputy leader Helga Pedersen.
119205.title_en: Labour Party heavyweight for May Day

119210.excerpt_en: There has been plenty of weather this winter: everything from long mild spells, slush avalanches and icy conditions to beautiful Easter days and heavy snowfall.
119210.subtitle_en: April was winter’s coldest month, and May has got off to a very snowy start.

119217.excerpt_en: Together with a nurse, senior consultant Kari Schrøder Hansen travelled to the settlement on Monday this week. There, they took blood samples from several of the sick.
119217.subtitle_en: A fierce flu outbreak has knocked out Ny-Ålesund.

119232.excerpt_en: “I’m really looking forward to it. I think it’s fantastic that the royal family is showing so much care and support,” says Aslak Klungseth Brattset, 16, deputy leader of Svalbard AUF.
119232.subtitle_en: Today, Aslak Klungseth Brattset will speak with the king and queen about his experiences after Utøya.

119236.excerpt_en: Eurogym is a gymnastics event for young people from across Europe, and this year it will be held in Coimbra, Portugal. Among the 5,000 registered participants are eleven gymnasts from Svalbard Turn.
119236.subtitle_en: In July, eleven local gymnasts are travelling to Portugal. The young athletes need money for the trip.
119236.title_en: Selling cakes to fund gymnastics event

119241.excerpt_en: Convers Avia Airline, the Russian operator running the Mi-8 helicopter at the Kapp Heer base near Barentsburg, has been allowed to make eight flights to Edgeøya. The purpose is to transport snowmobiles, sleds and equipment for Jason Roberts Productions (JRP).
119241.subtitle_en: The Civil Aviation Authority permits the Russians’ helicopter to be used commercially on Svalbard, in direct contradiction to the Russians’ general flight permit from the same authority.

119261.excerpt_en: The proposal has now been considered by Parliament’s Standing Committee on Energy and the Environment and is supported by the committee members from the Progress Party and the Christian Democratic Party. They believe that a power plant with CO2 capture on Svalbard, combined with underground CO2 storage, would help develop forward-looking and efficient carbon-management technology.
119261.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, Parliament will discuss whether Longyearbyen should get a new coal-fired power station with CO2 capture, as proposed by the Conservative Party.

119300.excerpt_en: “There were blue skies and sunshine; we’ve had a fantastic day,” says Trine Håkonsen, one of the 15 runners representing Svalbard Turn in Oslo this weekend. Svalbard Turn has entered a team in the relay every year since 1986, except last year.
119300.subtitle_en: After taking last year off, runners from Longyearbyen were back in Saturday’s Holmenkollen Relay in Oslo.

119315.excerpt_en: “We are proposing this to launch the groundworks for the building, which must be done this summer. The hangar itself will be constructed next year,” Justice Minister Grete Faremo (Labour) tells Svalbardposten.
119315.subtitle_en: The government is allocating NOK 14 million for a new helicopter hangar in Longyearbyen in its proposed revised national budget.

119319.excerpt_en: As always, the 17 May parade started at the church, passed through the town centre and ended at the monument at Skjæringa.
119319.subtitle_en: In brilliant sunshine and a fresh breeze, Longyearbyen celebrated Constitution Day.

119328.excerpt_en: The man was injured in the mine in Barentsburg, but it is not known how the accident happened. The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the incident at around 4 a.m. on Thursday.
119328.subtitle_en: A Russian man in his twenties has been sent to hospital in Tromsø after a workplace accident in Barentsburg.

119339.excerpt_en: The versatile and cheerful woman has been a central figure in the town’s cultural life, as well as its political life, for many years. In recognition of her long-standing efforts, she was honored with the Tyfus statuette during the gala performance at the cultural centre this evening.
119339.subtitle_en: “Intense and awesome!” says Kristin Furu Grøtting about receiving this year’s Tyfus statuette.

119345.excerpt_en: “It was a great end to the season, with insanely fast participants,” says Stein Tore Pedersen of Trollsteinens venner, which organized the competition. Forty-two people took part in Wednesday evening’s Chinese Downhill, where everyone starts together and the first one down wins.
119345.subtitle_en: It took the fastest racer 3 minutes and 56 seconds to get from Trollsteinen to Nybyen in this year’s Chinese Downhill.

119363.excerpt_en: “Dear fellow citizens, congratulations on the day! Today we celebrate Norway’s Constitution Day, commemorating the Eidsvoll Constitution, which was adopted on 17
119363.subtitle_en: Here is the speech delivered by local council leader Christin Kristoffersen during the gala performance at the cultural centre on 17 May.
119363.title_en: The local council leader’s Constitution Day speech

119371.excerpt_en: This is a fairly small eclipse, but it is larger the farther north you go. The best conditions will be here in Svalbard.
119371.subtitle_en: On Monday night, there will be a partial solar eclipse in Northern Norway. The moon will cover a small part of the sun.

119379.excerpt_en: It was the Grimsvötn volcano that began spewing ash at the end of May last year, bringing air traffic to Svalbard to a complete standstill. “We are using much of the same program we were going to use last year. The theme is climate and technology.”
119379.subtitle_en: Last year, an ash cloud from Iceland ruined the environmental symposium in Ny-Ålesund. This year, everything is in place for a cloudless event.

119389.excerpt_en: “I think that once I start talking, he and the setting won’t matter much; I’ll become like a machine. But it will probably be uncomfortable, and I’m dreading it,” says Viljar Hanssen.
119389.subtitle_en: Viljar Hanssen, 18, was seriously injured on Utøya. On Tuesday, he will testify in Oslo District Court.

119406.excerpt_en: The money comes from the DNB NOR Savings Bank Foundation and was presented at Longyearbyen Airport on Thursday. “Of around 3,000 applications, barely 300 were approved, and we were particularly impressed by Longyearbyen Blues Club’s application. We can see that freight costs for instruments and equipment make things especially challenging for organizers up here.”
119406.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Blues Club receives NOK 350,000 for technical equipment and instruments.

119441.excerpt_en: The new security checkpoint at Svalbard Airport is scheduled to be ready by 1 July.
119441.subtitle_en: Work to rebuild the security checkpoint has begun. Avinor hopes it will lead to shorter queues.

119452.excerpt_en: The plan is to gather geese along the stretch from Deltaneset eastwards to Fredheim. A large enclosure will be placed at the mouth of the Sassenelva, and the helicopter will be used to drive the geese into it.
119452.subtitle_en: Danish researchers want to use a helicopter to chase pink-footed geese along the south side of Sassenfjorden. The birds will be driven into traps to be tagged for scientific research.
119452.title_en: Want to Chase Geese with a Helicopter

119463.excerpt_en: A local resident skiing with her dog was travelling from Longyearbyen to Svea when they became separated near Höganäsbreen on Monday. “A snowmobile driver found the dog by the snowmobile trail. He thought it looked a little forlorn and brought it to Longyearbyen,” says senior Governor’s Office officer Erik Nygaard.
119463.subtitle_en: A dog and its owner became separated while travelling to Svea on Monday. But it ended well.

119482.excerpt_en: Reisner was supposed to fly from Oslo to Svolvær last Friday. Instead, she ended up 1,100 kilometres farther north—in Longyearbyen. “I was shocked and initially extremely embarrassed.”
119482.subtitle_en: When American Ellen Reisner (70) stepped off the plane and saw a stuffed polar bear, she realised she had ended up very, very far from where she intended.

119487.excerpt_en: The incident occurred at around 9 p.m. on Friday. The woman was hiking with a friend on Larsbreen when she broke her foot. “She was unable to get back down on her own, so we picked her up by helicopter,” says senior Governor’s Office officer Erik Nygaard.
119487.subtitle_en: A woman had to be picked up by helicopter after breaking her foot on Larsbreen on Friday evening.

119499.excerpt_en: The limited road system around Longyearbyen was no obstacle for the Spitsbergen Marathon. The race took place for the 18th time on Saturday.
119499.subtitle_en: A marathon is just over 42 kilometres—the same number of kilometres as there are roads in Longyearbyen.
119499.title_en: Fleet Feet Take to the Roads

119506.excerpt_en: The transit of Venus is about to take place—that is, the planet Venus will pass in front of the sun. The event occurs between 12:04 a.m. and 6:54 a.m. tonight, meaning that only places with the midnight sun can experience the entire transit.
119506.subtitle_en: Four minutes after midnight, you can witness an event that will not happen again until 2117.

119510.excerpt_en: Tourists who had followed the ship from the mainland went ashore in Longyearbyen on Tuesday morning. This afternoon, they will head back out into the fjord to experience Spitsbergen’s northwest coast. As it has done for so many years, the «Nordstjernen» will take tourists on an expedition cruise along Spitsbergen’s west coast.
119510.subtitle_en: The «Nordstjernen» docked in Longyearbyen on Tuesday morning. This summer, the old lady will bid farewell to Svalbard.

119519.excerpt_en: It will be more than 105 years before the planet experiences another transit of Venus. Last night, four minutes after midnight, Venus appeared at the edge of the sun’s disc.
119519.subtitle_en: Several hundred people eagerly watched for the transit of Venus last night. Only the most patient were rewarded.

119550.excerpt_en: “We were notified about construction machinery, specifically a telehandler, that had been started in the Sjøområdet area,” says Governor’s Office officer Dag Hovden. The incident occurred around midnight on Friday.
119550.subtitle_en: A woman in her twenties, under the influence, climbed behind the controls of a telehandler and started the machine.

119552.excerpt_en: The Governor’s Office received word of the ill cruise passenger at around 1 p.m. on Sunday. The passenger was aboard a cruise ship in Magdalenefjorden, so the Governor’s Office sent out a helicopter to pick them up.
119552.subtitle_en: A helicopter was dispatched to pick up an ill passenger from a cruise ship in Magdalenefjorden.

119557.excerpt_en: The maritime tourist season has already been under way for several weeks, but it was not until Sunday morning that Longyearbyen truly got a taste of cruise tourism.
119557.subtitle_en: This morning, the first of the really large cruise ships arrived in Longyearbyen.

119563.excerpt_en: Ivar Undheim (57), chief administrative officer of Longyearbyen Local Council, will most likely return to the position of chief administrative officer in the Jæren municipality of Klepp. According to Jærbladet, Klepp’s executive committee nominated Undheim as the new chief administrative officer last week.
119563.subtitle_en: Klepp’s executive committee wants Ivar Undheim as the municipality’s new chief administrative officer.

119575.excerpt_en: Seventeen years ago, there were 2,400 post offices in this country. In two years, only 30 will remain.
119575.subtitle_en: In two years, the post office in Longyearbyen will join a very exclusive club.

119587.excerpt_en: The cabin is currently owned by Spitsbergen Experience AS and will change hands in September. It will be available to guests from next winter. “We will develop this into an ecotourism destination,” says Steinar Rorgemoen, general manager of Basecamp Spitsbergen, in a press release.
119587.subtitle_en: Basecamp Spitsbergen has bought a commercial cabin in Adolfbukta by Nordenskiöldbreen.

119588.excerpt_en: The dog reportedly broke loose in Hiorthhamn and began chasing a reindeer. The Governor’s Office was notified of the incident at around 5 p.m. and sent out a helicopter to look for the dog, says Governor’s Office officer Dag Hovden.
119588.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office sent out a helicopter on Thursday afternoon to search for a loose dog.

119593.excerpt_en: “At 8 a.m. on Friday, 14 September, a new chapter in Svalbardposten’s history begins,” says editor Birger Amundsen of Svalbardposten.
119593.subtitle_en: This autumn, clicking on most of the articles at www.svalbardposten.no will cost money.
119593.title_en: We’re Going to Charge for Online Access

119650.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten wrote in February that Taste of Thai and a sushi restaurant hoped to be ready before summer at Lompensenteret. It is only now that the contractors have begun renovating the old Kafé Busen premises.
119650.subtitle_en: Two restaurants are due to open at Lompensenteret within the next few months.

119678.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Veterinary Institute has analysed samples from two reindeer found in Barentsburg in March and at Revneset in April, respectively. Neither animal had rabies, the Governor reports.
119678.subtitle_en: Two new rabies tests are negative, but the Governor will not call off the rabies outbreak.

119685.excerpt_en: The backup power plant has not always worked as it should. From 7 p.m. on Sunday, we will be completely dependent on the plant to provide electricity and district heating to the town’s households.
119685.subtitle_en: From Sunday evening, the backup power plant will have to prove what it can do.

119689.excerpt_en: The seven-tonne rocket is the largest ever launched from Norway. Shortly after 9 p.m. on Friday evening, it was launched from Andøya.
119689.subtitle_en: The flight of Norway’s largest rocket, Shefex 2, ended 150 kilometres south of Spitsbergen. No one has seen it since.
119689.title_en: Giant Rocket Falls Into the Sea

119710.excerpt_en: This year’s summer exhibition opens at the gallery in Nybyen this evening and consists of prints and paintings. The three artists are Kari Finborud, Kristian Finborud and Tormod Ropstad.
119710.subtitle_en: Three artists will be present with their works at Galleri Svalbard this evening.

119713.excerpt_en: Marlene Mellum and Erle Haldorsen have completed every stage of the Youth Cultural Festival (UKM), from the local showcase at the cultural centre to the prestigious national showcase at Olavshallen in Trondheim. The Longyearbyen girls slept in the same dormitory as 550 participants from across the country.
119713.subtitle_en: Marlene Mellum (17) and Erle Harldorsen (15) enjoyed three days at the national UKM showcase in Trondheim.

119725.excerpt_en: “I can confirm that there will be no hydrographic surveys in Svalbard this year, but there will be new surveys from next year,” says Evert Flier, director of the Norwegian Mapping Authority’s Hydrographic Service. Extensive surveying last year: Last summer, the Mapping Authority spent 15 weeks in Svalbard.
119725.subtitle_en: This summer, the Norwegian Mapping Authority will continue its hydrographic surveys—but not in Svalbard.

119734.excerpt_en: Yesterday, compulsory pilotage was introduced for larger ships to Svea, and from next year most of Svalbard will also be covered. Although the requirement does not yet apply to the approach to Longyearbyen, the first official pilotage assignment in Svalbard was carried out here this morning.
119734.subtitle_en: Yesterday, the pilotage regulations for Svalbard came into force, and today the first cruise ship was piloted into Adventfjorden.

119739.excerpt_en: A Russian citizen got his arm caught while working in the mine in Barentsburg during the night of 17 May this year.
119739.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority wants to know how Trust Arktikugol follows up employees who experience accidents and traumatic incidents.

119746.excerpt_en: The distinctly Norwegian ban on bonus points on domestic routes came into force in summer 2007. On Wednesday, the EFTA Surveillance Authority (ESA) concluded that the ban violates the EEA Agreement.
119746.subtitle_en: The ban on bonus points for domestic flights may be on its way out.

119761.excerpt_en: This autumn will mark two years since the Spitsbergen Airship Museum closed. At the time, it was housed in the old premises of the Svalbard Museum at Skjæringa.
119761.subtitle_en: Stefano Poli is nearly ready to open new doors to the old airship museum.

119781.excerpt_en: Last week, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) took over the new pavilion outside the school. This means the after-school programme can move out of the second floor and into the new building.
119781.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen School will have more space next school year.

119791.excerpt_en: The incident occurred at around 5 p.m. on Tuesday. The boat was near Grumant in Isfjorden when it ran aground. “We do not know why the boat ran aground.”
119791.subtitle_en: With 28 people on board, the tourist boat “Polargirl” ran aground off Grumant.

119805.excerpt_en: During a survey carried out by UNIS and the Geological Survey of Norway (NGU), geologists happened to discover two potential landslide hazards in Longyearbyen: a rocky outcrop on the slope behind Nybyen and a rock fissure directly above the entrance to Mine 2b.
119805.subtitle_en: Last autumn, geologists discovered unstable mountain sections near Nybyen and recommend that the risk be assessed further.

119825.excerpt_en: Chairman Wiggo Lund reports heavy attendance when Taste of Thai held a trial opening on Saturday. The official opening is not until eleven o’clock today.
119825.subtitle_en: The world’s northernmost Thai restaurant is delighted to finally welcome customers at Lompensenteret.

119840.excerpt_en: “A man fell during routine maintenance on an aircraft. He was sent to Longyearbyen Hospital for a check-up,” says Governor’s officer Dag Einar Aas.
119840.subtitle_en: A man was injured during maintenance work on one of Lufttransport’s aircraft.

119847.excerpt_en: It has been one year since Johannes Buø (14) was killed and Viljar Hanssen (18) seriously injured. Three other local AUF members escaped the massacre without physical injuries.
119847.subtitle_en: Sunday marks one year since five of Longyearbyen’s young people were attacked on Utøya.

119859.excerpt_en: “Viking Explorer” is owned by UNIS and is moored at Bykaia. The boat is used extensively by students and researchers. UNIS technician Lars Frode Stangeland faces daily challenges related to the berth: “It gets shallower and shallower when it isn’t dredged.”
119859.subtitle_en: UNIS is unhappy with the quay facilities at Bykaia and is calling for improvements from Municipal Operations.

119863.excerpt_en: In April last year, the Storting decided that Svalbard would not be covered by the Data Retention Directive. The reason is that the archipelago is not part of the EEA.
119863.subtitle_en: Kripos fears Svalbard could become a safe haven for child pornography, drugs and other crimes if the Data Retention Directive does not apply there.

119882.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the incident by the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre on Monday evening and prepared a rescue operation. “After a short time, we established that the passengers and crew were not in danger.”
119882.subtitle_en: The coastal cruise ship “Expedition” ran aground on Monday evening. The ship is now heading to Ny-Ålesund for divers to examine it.

119897.excerpt_en: A new study shows that brown bears and polar bears began diverging as long as four to five million years ago. That is far earlier than researchers had previously believed.
119897.subtitle_en: The polar bear as a species is far older than researchers have believed.

119906.excerpt_en: The waiting list for the Arctic Nature Guide programme at Finnmark University College (HiF) became so long that this year it will not be available through the late-admissions list. All 24 places have been filled.
119906.subtitle_en: The Arctic Nature Guide programme received a record number of applicants for the autumn term. Now it is moving into new premises.

119909.excerpt_en: “Expedition” ran aground on Monday evening at Isispynten in eastern Nordaustlandet, with 157 people on board. The initial reports said there was no damage to the ship and no leaks.
119909.subtitle_en: “Expedition” began taking on water after running aground on Monday evening. The coastal cruise ship has now arrived in Longyearbyen.

119919.excerpt_en: “Following negotiations, we have reached an agreement with ‘Nordsyssel’ for another year,” says senior police officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office. For ten years, the Governor’s Office has leased “Nordsyssel” as a service vessel from April to November.
119919.subtitle_en: “Nordsyssel” will operate for the Governor of Svalbard again next year.

119930.excerpt_en: “We’re doing fine, apart from a little sunburn on the back of our necks,” sums up Erlend Foss Telstø (16) from Longyearbyen. Together with twelve teammates, he began the biggest youth football festival, Norway Cup, yesterday.
119930.subtitle_en: The year’s first encounter with grass ended in a 4–0 defeat for the boys from Longyearbyen. But the girls are doing just fine.

119947.excerpt_en: The first proper walrus census was conducted in 2006. At the time, there were around 3,000 walruses in Svalbard, and researchers saw almost exclusively males.
119947.subtitle_en: Much suggests that the walrus population is growing. They will be counted in a few weeks.

119970.excerpt_en: The transshipment vessel “Frio Arkhangelsk” was carrying too much cod. The Governor’s Office reports this on its website.
119970.subtitle_en: Shipping company Rainbow Refeers LTD must pay up after failing to report its catch.

119979.excerpt_en: This summer, ancient history has come to the surface at Hollendarhaugen, the area west of the quay in Ny-Ålesund. The settlement’s old burial ground was once located here.
119979.subtitle_en: Permafrost is pushing old graves up from Hollendarhaugen in Ny-Ålesund.

120004.excerpt_en: The Governor’s Office was notified about the tourists a week earlier, on Saturday, by a tour operator who was concerned about their equipment. They were a father and son who said they were, among other things, planning to travel to Pyramiden.
120004.subtitle_en: On Sunday afternoon, the Governor of Svalbard had to search for two German tourists after their family reported concerns.

120009.excerpt_en: On August 14, 1925, the Norwegian flag was raised at Skjæringa for the first time.
120009.subtitle_en: August 14 is Svalbard Day, commemorating the day Norway assumed sovereignty over the archipelago.

120012.excerpt_en: “Store Norske retains formal responsibility for coal sales, and all decisions are made internally. Glencore has a larger network than we do and serves as an adviser and door opener,” says Aleksander Askeland, Store Norske’s marketing and product director.
120012.subtitle_en: Two years ago, Store Norske terminated its agreement with Oxbow Coal on the sale of coal from Svea. A new agreement has been reached with Swiss company Glencore International.

120036.excerpt_en: From Wednesday to Saturday, Barentsburg will host a cultural celebration and film festival. The event is a collaboration between Trust Arktikugol and The Northern Travelling Film Festival.
120036.subtitle_en: Next week there will be a cultural celebration in Barentsburg. Those interested are invited to a film festival, tours around the town and lessons about the history of research.

120041.excerpt_en: It is still the midnight sun, but before too long darkness will return to Svalbard. That means good opportunities to see the northern lights.
120041.subtitle_en: The northern lights are fickle and not always easy to spot. But now you can get valuable help—from your mobile phone.
120041.title_en: Mobile help for spotting the northern lights

120050.excerpt_en: Today, Tuesday, Community Council leader Christin Kristoffersen and Director-General of Cultural Heritage Jørn Holme will open a small exhibition at Svalbard Museum. The gavel used in community council meetings and the council leader’s jewelry will be placed in a glass display case in the reception area.
120050.subtitle_en: This year, Longyearbyen Community Council turns ten. The anniversary begins with a small exhibition.
120050.title_en: Exhibiting a piece of jewelry and a gavel

120060.excerpt_en: The cabin cruiser, with three people aboard, left Longyearbyen on Wednesday afternoon. The boat was heading north, but in Forlandsundet the engine overheated and stopped.
120060.subtitle_en: The Port Authority’s “Fjell” had to head out early Thursday morning to pick up a cabin cruiser with engine trouble in Forlandsundet.
120060.title_en: Cabin cruiser comes to the rescue

120086.excerpt_en: It is time to take down the aluminum foil and blackout blinds, because the night is slowly but surely returning. But exactly when does the sun go below the horizon?
120086.subtitle_en: Tonight, the sun in Longyearbyen will dip below the horizon for the first time since April.
120086.title_en: The sun sets—but what about the foot?

120114.excerpt_en: “We have been there and examined some traces. So far, we have found no signs of forced entry.”
120114.subtitle_en: Someone broke into Fruene Café and stole cash.

120121.excerpt_en: As early as Monday this week, students at Longyearbyen Upper Secondary School watched the documentary “To the Youth,” which follows four politically engaged young people from summer 2009 to autumn 2011. The film premieres nationally today and will be shown at Longyearbyen Cinema both this evening and on Sunday.
120121.subtitle_en: Today, the documentary “To the Youth” premieres. In connection with the premiere, young people in Longyearbyen left their mark on Magne Furuholmen’s July 22 sculpture and wrote letters to the future.

120133.excerpt_en: “Nordsyssel” reached the ship early Friday morning and spoke with the crew. No one was injured. “The ship must now be refloated and checked for damage,” says acting senior police officer Per Andreassen.
120133.subtitle_en: On Friday night, the vessel “La Malouine” broke loose from its anchor and went aground in Gåshamna.

120159.excerpt_en: “They arrived late on Thursday evening and had read online that you can sleep in public places in Longyearbyen because doors are left open due to the polar-bear danger,” says acting senior police officer Per Andreassen.
120159.subtitle_en: Two Spanish men in their twenties chose to stay on the second floor of the Post and Bank Building when they visited Longyearbyen at the weekend. On Saturday, things went wrong.

120169.excerpt_en: Trust Director General Aleksander P. Veselov emphasizes that the publication will not be a news newspaper, but more of a magazine or journal featuring material about Svalbard.
120169.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol is launching its own newspaper, with the first issue planned in two weeks. The “Russian Svalbard Journal” will be published every other month.
120169.title_en: The Russians get their own newspaper

120176.excerpt_en: During August, Longyearbyen had 17 days with precipitation. On seven or eight days, the sun barely broke through before disappearing again.
120176.subtitle_en: This year’s August was blanketed in clouds. Only on August 18 could people in Longyearbyen enjoy sunshine all day.
120176.title_en: One day of sunshine in August

120182.excerpt_en: “We were notified of the accident at 11:05 p.m. on Tuesday after the two sailors activated their emergency beacon. Our rescue helicopter arrived at the site at around 1:30 a.m. and picked the two up from a rubber dinghy,” says acting senior police officer Per Andreassen of the Governor’s Office.
120182.subtitle_en: Two Englishmen were rescued by the Governor of Svalbard’s rescue helicopter last night after their sailboat sank near Kobbskjera, north of Raudfjorden.
120182.title_en: Sailboat sinks off the north coast

120184.excerpt_en: Norway holds the presidency of the Nordic Council of Ministers this year, and Minister Rigmor Aasrud hosted her Nordic colleagues this week. She brought the meeting to Longyearbyen. “We want to showcase some of what is distinctly Nordic while also offering a different impression of Norwegian society.”
120184.subtitle_en: The Nordic cooperation ministers have spent the past 24 hours in Longyearbyen.
120184.title_en: The Nordic countries unite in Longyearbyen

120202.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen is offering a varied programme this autumn. It begins tomorrow at Huset with Spellemann Award winners Ila Auto and local band Blåmyra.
120202.subtitle_en: On Saturday, Ila Auto and Blåmyra will play at Huset. After that, the autumn events will come thick and fast.
120202.title_en: The autumn cultural season gets under way

120207.excerpt_en: “There will be no brass band or fanfare, but on 14 September we will launch a new website.”
120207.subtitle_en: Next Friday, Svalbardposten is introducing a digital newspaper and online payment.

120226.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has granted the Norwegian Mapping Authority permission to build a new geodetic Earth observation observatory with an antenna array, instrument building and access road at Brandalpynten in Ny-Ålesund. “Construction can now begin, and we are pleased about that,” says project manager Line Langkaas of the Norwegian Mapping Authority’s Geodesy Division in a press release.
120226.subtitle_en: The funding is in place, and now the Governor of Svalbard has also approved the new geodetic observatory in Ny-Ålesund.

120229.excerpt_en: Ptarmigan hunting season begins today, and apparently the ptarmigans in Longyearbyen have heard about it. In the early hours of the morning, 14 ptarmigans sought shelter at Longyearbyen kindergarten. “It has been so much fun.”
120229.title_en: The ptarmigans seek refuge with the children

120252.excerpt_en: “This is hugely positive. Now we have the opportunity to do what we have been saying for the past two years that we need to do,” says Marianne Aasen, general manager of Bydrift.
120252.subtitle_en: At the Storting’s request, Gassnova will assess the possibilities for a new power plant with CO2 capture in Longyearbyen.
120252.tags_en: coal, power plant, CO2, Bydrift, news, Gassnova

120279.excerpt_en: Store Norske has invited a number of companies to compete for the contract to transport coal from the Lunckefjell mine across Marthabreen. According to plan, the development work will begin in a year.
120279.subtitle_en: Store Norske will decide during the autumn which company gets the contract to transport coal from the new mine at Lunckefjellet.
120279.tags_en: news, Marthabreen, Lunckefjell, coal, mine, Store Norske

120286.excerpt_en: The East Svalbard case is an incredibly intractable matter. Work to introduce new restrictions on travel in Nordaustlandet, Barentsøya and Edgeøya, as well as a large number of smaller islands, has been going on for years.

120299.excerpt_en: Since 2010, the Longyearbyen Dog Club has worked to establish a veterinary position in Longyearbyen. Last January, the Governor of Svalbard asked the Ministry of Agriculture and Food and the Norwegian Food Safety Authority to assess the possibility of supporting a veterinary service in Longyearbyen.
120299.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Agriculture and Food will neither amend the law nor pay for a veterinary service in Longyearbyen. It is passing the matter on to the Governor of Svalbard.
120299.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, veterinarian, dog, veterinary surgeon, news

120309.excerpt_en: In August, the children at Kullungen kindergarten got to try out their brand-new climbing tower. “The goal is for the other kindergartens to get outdoor climbing towers too,” says Anne Ellingsen, general manager of Oppvekstforetaket. In the coming years, the outdoor areas at the kindergartens and school will be upgraded.
120309.subtitle_en: The climbing tower at Kullungen kindergarten opened this summer. Next year, Longyearbyen kindergarten is next, if everything goes according to plan.
120309.title_en: All the children get to climb

120338.excerpt_en: In his resignation letter, director Jan-Gunnar Winther writes: “The reason is that, in my view, the academy acts and takes positions on behalf of the scientific community in a way that neither reflects the research nor the members’ views in a balanced manner.” In a reply to Winther, president Ola M. rejects this.
120338.subtitle_en: The director of the Norwegian Polar Institute is unhappy with the Academy of Sciences’ involvement in the East Svalbard case and is resigning as a member.

120367.excerpt_en: In August, the Labour Inspection Authority carried out an unannounced inspection at Classic Pizza in Lompensenteret after receiving tips about conditions at the restaurant. In an eight-page report, the authority points to the company’s breaches of the Working Environment Act. “What we found was that the employees were generally working too much.”
120367.subtitle_en: Excessively long working days, along with uncertainties surrounding pay and employment contracts at Classic Pizza. That is the conclusion of an inspection report from the Labour Inspection Authority.
120367.tags_en: news, Labour Inspection Authority, Working Environment Act, inspection, violations

120379.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, the Svalbard Business Association warned the town’s politicians about problems caused by the shortage and high cost of privately owned housing. Businesses are struggling to recruit employees because of the housing market.
120379.subtitle_en: Politicians want to facilitate private homebuilding, but have not decided how.

120385.excerpt_en: Last weekend, the local campaign group began its telethon fundraising with a car wash, raffle and Thai dancing. “We have all the events we usually hold, and then we are trying something new as well. Among other things, a corporate relay race in cooperation with Svalbard Turn,” says Lene Villumsen, campaign leader in Longyearbyen.
120385.subtitle_en: Campaign leader Lene Villumsen is urging the town’s businesses to put on their running shoes and race for Amnesty International.
120385.title_en: Running to raise money for the telethon

120394.excerpt_en: Recently, I have received many questions and comments about the port’s finances. I see that not everyone is aware of how port accounting works.

120407.excerpt_en: “This is a day of joy for Norwegian research,” said Jan-Gunnar Winther, director of the Norwegian Polar Institute, when details from the national budget were leaked on Wednesday. The research vessel will be owned by the Norwegian Polar Institute and operated by the Institute of Marine Research’s shipping division, according to the institute’s website.
120407.subtitle_en: The government is allocating funds in next year’s national budget for a new ice-strengthened research vessel.

120423.excerpt_en: When the Labour Inspection Authority inspected Classic Pizza, two representatives from Skatt Nord were also present. “The Tax Administration conducts continuous checks of businesses. Svalbard is part of that.”
120423.subtitle_en: Skatt Nord also carried out an inspection at Classic Pizza.

120426.excerpt_en: “We have never experienced anything like it; this is without a doubt our best touring experience ever,” the enthusiastic ballet director told Svalbardposten shortly after the performance. See pictures from the performance here. “We would be delighted to return as soon as possible.”
120426.subtitle_en: Ballet director Ingrid Lorentzen is full of enthusiasm about the reception given to the Norwegian National Ballet in Longyearbyen.

120436.excerpt_en: “I have a realistic attitude toward my illness, and I do not see death as something terrible. Dark thoughts have never been part of me.”
120436.subtitle_en: Doctor, local politician and tour guide Jon Sandmo, 63, was told this summer that he has a serious cancer diagnosis. Now he is preparing for whatever may come.
120436.tags_en: news, cancer, terminally ill, profile, magazine

120473.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, organizers of the international Europan architecture competition visited Longyearbyen to take a closer look at Sjøområdet. “We believe it would be excellent for Longyearbyen to determine what Sjøområdet is to become. We got the impression that the area was governed by a mild form of anarchy.”
120473.subtitle_en: The organizers of an architecture competition want to clean up Sjøområdet. Longyearbyen Community Council cannot agree among its members on whether to take part.
120473.tags_en: problem area, Europan, Sjøområdet, architecture, architecture competition, news

120487.excerpt_en: Katja Burlutskaya talks energetically about life, from A to N. At 36, one can hardly say she has made it any further.
120487.subtitle_en: Katja Burlutskaya (36) has castrated animals and delivered calves in the cowshed in Barentsburg. Now a new Katja Burlutskaja has arrived in the same town.

120507.excerpt_en: On 27 June, guides from the cruise ship “Ocean Nova” went ashore at Torellneset with a group of 44 tourists.
120507.subtitle_en: The Coast Guard wanted to check that tourists were not frightening a walrus resting on land. This resulted in the Coast Guard frightening walruses at sea.
120507.tags_en: frightened, Coast Guard, walrus, Governor of Svalbard, news

120513.excerpt_en: A series of emails linked to the incident at Torellneset on 27 June were withheld from public access by not being entered in the Governor’s official journal.
120513.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard failed to register documents in a case involving the Coast Guard and the Governor’s own personnel. The deputy governor says it was all due to an oversight.
120513.tags_en: transparency, official journal, Freedom of Information Act, chased, walrus, archive, news

120544.excerpt_en: “The vandalism must have occurred after the National Ballet’s concert. We discovered it on Friday,” says Terje Carlsen, communications director at Store Norske.
120544.subtitle_en: Someone has written obscenities and smashed windows at Vinkel Station in Adventdalen. Store Norske has reported the matter to the police.

120546.excerpt_en: Last year, the CinemArctic film festival was held for the first time, with around 20 films screened in Longyearbyen and Barentsburg. Project manager Martha Otte, who is also director of the Tromsø International Film Festival (TIFF), hopes they can arrange a sequel to CinemArctic.
120546.subtitle_en: There will be no film festival this year, but there is a good chance of film screenings in Longyearbyen in connection with the Tromsø International Film Festival in January.
120546.title_en: CinemArctic could become a TIFF satellite

120593.subtitle_en: Helse Nord and Air Ambulance Services ANS are hiring a jet again this winter to ensure emergency preparedness on Svalbard.

120625.excerpt_en: For the first time, a corporate relay is being held in Longyearbyen as part of the TV fundraiser, and 14 teams have already registered. They include Svalsat, Store Norske, the Governor of Svalbard’s office, Unis and Bydrift. “And in true Svalbard spirit, registrations are still coming in at the last minute,” says Helle Jakobsen, coordinator at Svalbard Turn.
120625.subtitle_en: Fourteen teams have already signed up for the TV fundraiser’s relay on Saturday.
120625.tags_en: Svalbard life, TV fundraiser, culture, relay

120628.excerpt_en: It is astonishing how poorly Store Norske has managed things in Longyearbyen—especially considering the enormous revenues the coal company has enjoyed since operations at Svea Nord began ten or twelve years ago.

120651.excerpt_en: “We have decided that we will stop all work and take a timeout when the injury situation develops unacceptably. It is important that we stop and think, because we know that many minor injuries ultimately lead to something far more serious.”
120651.subtitle_en: After a period of several minor injuries, Store Norske managing director Per Andersson ordered a one-hour work stoppage in Svea and Longyearbyen. Bedriftsnytt, Store Norske’s in-house magazine, reports this.

120672.excerpt_en: It is Minister of Trade and Industry Trond Giske (Labour) who is giving advance notice of news from next year’s national budget. The budget will be presented on Monday. “The Czechs have expressed interest in their own research station on Svalbard for quite some time, but Kings Bay has not had the means to invest in a new building.”
120672.subtitle_en: The government is putting NOK 7 million toward construction of a new research station in Ny-Ålesund. The station will house Czech researchers.
120672.tags_en: national budget, Ny-Ålesund, research, Czech, news

120678.excerpt_en: Many also came to watch the event. The Governor’s mixed men’s and women’s team won, while the Unis students’ men’s team covered the route through central Longyearbyen fastest of all.
120678.subtitle_en: Despite sub-zero temperatures and a biting wind, a large group of running enthusiasts turned up outside Svalbardbutikken on Saturday for a relay race.
