125374.excerpt_en: At the beginning of September, a polar bear was sedated by researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute. This happened at Meodden, in the far north of Edgeøya in Svalbard.
125374.subtitle_en: The polar bear vomited after researchers sedated it. The fact that it was left lying uphill may have contributed to its suffocation.

125382.excerpt_en: The autopsy report from the Norwegian Veterinary Institute is clear about why the male bear died after being sedated by researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute at Meodden, in the far north of Edgeøya, at the beginning of September. The conclusion is “aspiration of stomach contents”, meaning that the bear inhaled stomach contents into its lungs and suffocated.
125382.subtitle_en: The polar bear vomited while sedated, and stomach contents entered its lungs. Leaving the bear with its head raised may have contributed to this happening.
125382.title_en: This Is Why the Polar Bear Died

125390.excerpt_en: The mine in Barentsburg was closed this time on 10 September after a miner was seriously injured.
125390.subtitle_en: The Labour Inspection Authority believes Trust Arktikugol has no control over rock stress in the Barentsburg mine. It has therefore been closed indefinitely.

125410.excerpt_en: Norway’s incoming prime minister has made it clear: the focus on the High North will continue with full force. Svalbard is mentioned only once in the 75-page document known as the Sundvolden platform, but in the 17.

125418.excerpt_en: In several reports this year, the Labour Inspection Authority has criticised the safety culture of the Russian coal company Trust Arktikugol, which operates the coal mine in Barentsburg. Over the past year, there have been seven serious workplace accidents in the mine, including two fatalities.
125418.subtitle_en: The Labour Inspection Authority has rejected several requests from Trust Arktikugol to reopen the coal mine in Barentsburg.

125440.excerpt_en: Ole Arve Misund, managing director of UNIS, peers into the crystal ball. It has been a year and a half since he moved from the Institute of Marine Research to his job in Longyearbyen.
125440.subtitle_en: In a few years, the University Centre in Svalbard will have 1,000 students, its director believes.

125448.excerpt_en: In autumn 1993, the University Centre in Svalbard (UNIS) opened its doors to 25 students. A group of committed “Svalbard academics”, led by Professor Olav Rønning, had succeeded in convincing the authorities that establishing a university centre in Svalbard would be forward-looking.
125448.subtitle_en: OPINION: Ole Arve Misund, managing director of UNIS.

125480.excerpt_en: “The most difficult part of combating bullying is discovering that it is actually happening. Too much takes place in secret, and half of the victims do not tell their parents or teachers,” says Erling Roland.
125480.subtitle_en: If bullying is not addressed in the right way, the problem can become worse.

125490.excerpt_en: When people gather for an auction in Longyearbyen, they mean business—especially when the proceeds go to the annual TV fundraising campaign.
125490.subtitle_en: Who would pay 14,000 to help collect rubbish? Or 23,000 for a visit from two chefs?

125525.excerpt_en: Snow brings many wonderful experiences. Already, it has settled on the ground like a thin, white blanket.
125525.subtitle_en: What does a snowflake actually look like? Jessica and Nils Roar have the answer.
125525.tags_en: snow, life in Svalbard, people, research

125557.excerpt_en: That is what Truls Johannessen, regional director of the Labour Inspection Authority in Northern Norway, says. “It is clear that the Russian authorities are interested in restarting mining operations. The acting Russian consul general attended the meeting we had with Trust Arktikugol,” he says.
125557.subtitle_en: The acting Russian consul general attended last week’s meeting between the Labour Inspection Authority and the trust.

125565.excerpt_en: Johan Sletten, chairman of the board of Bykaia Lagerutleie AS, has won his claim. “The decision from the Ministry of Local Government and Regional Development is clear. Longyearbyen Local Council is holding money it collected from us on an unlawful basis,” he says.
125565.subtitle_en: Johan Sletten has spent two years fighting what he believes are illegally high fees set by Longyearbyen Local Council. Now he has received support from the ministry.

125573.excerpt_en: According to chief administrative officer Lars Ole Saugnes, Longyearbyen Local Council has not yet fully decided what the outcome of the legality review by the Ministry of Local Government and Regional Development (KRD) means. “We have no lawyer on the local council and must have the decision interpreted.”
125573.subtitle_en: The NOK 953,000 that Bykaia Lagerutleie AS paid in fees will remain in LL’s possession until the rates have been calculated correctly.

125608.excerpt_en: This week, activity around the meeting table on the second floor of the Lompen Centre has been hectic.
125608.subtitle_en: They have been working on the festival for a year and believe this year’s Dark Season Blues will be one of the best.
125608.title_en: The Town Gets the Blues Again

125618.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Dog Club (LHK) has all the formalities in order to expand the dog yard eastwards, towards Isdammen. The plan is to double the area, thereby increasing capacity with a number of kennels and making it possible for more people to enjoy the dog yard.
125618.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Dog Club’s greatest wish is to create a strong dog-owning community at the town’s dog yard. But rejection of the KORK application could create problems.

125628.excerpt_en: When it became known that the Ministry of Local Government and Regional Development (KRD) had upheld Bykaia Lagerutleie’s appeal in the fee case, several people breathed a sigh of relief. The company paid a total of NOK 953,000 in connection fees to Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) in 2011.
125628.subtitle_en: Several parties are closely following the fee case involving Bykaia Lagerutleie. Avinor is one of them.

125646.excerpt_en: “Although coal prices have been low in recent years and Store Norske is struggling somewhat, we feel it is important to support Dark Season Blues.”
125646.subtitle_en: Dark Season Blues in Longyearbyen was officially opened on Thursday evening.

125678.excerpt_en: The joy of contributing is an important driving force. It stems from knowing that your contribution makes a difference and that the total, when everything is added together, can bring about significant change.
125678.subtitle_en: The local community has every reason to be proud of its own efforts, its volunteers, businesses and agencies, and everyone who has contributed in their own way.

125686.excerpt_en: An employee of Store Norske was flown to Longyearbyen Hospital on Sunday evening in the Governor of Svalbard’s Super Puma helicopter after an accident at the workshop in the Lunckefjell mine. The man received an electric shock and had to undergo a routine medical examination. “The employee is doing well.”
125686.subtitle_en: A man had to undergo a check-up after receiving an electric shock on Sunday evening.

125694.excerpt_en: When artists come to Longyearbyen, they can count on being seen and heard. “This has been absolutely fantastic.”
125694.subtitle_en: This year’s Dark Season Blues in Longyearbyen was inspiring for the organisers, and next year’s festival is already being planned.

125702.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the workplace accident at 4:30 p.m. on Tuesday and sent a Super Puma helicopter to Svea to collect the injured man. He was taken to Longyearbyen Hospital, where a fracture in one foot was confirmed.
125702.subtitle_en: A mine worker in his twenties was struck on the foot by a boom on Tuesday. A fracture has been confirmed.

125718.excerpt_en: When the Administrative Committee considered the KORK applications on Monday, there was suspense surrounding Longyearbyen Dog Club’s (LHK) application. Initially, the chief administrative officer had recommended rejecting support for an expanded dog yard.
125718.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Dog Club received NOK 200,000 in KORK funding to expand the town’s dog yard and create a community for all dog owners.
125718.title_en: Received Funding at the Eleventh Hour

125730.excerpt_en: From the festival began on Thursday until the final riff was played at the jam session at Funken on Sunday, crowds gathered around the artists and stages that made up this year’s Dark Season Blues 2013.
125730.subtitle_en: Dark Season Blues 2013 goes down in history as one of the most successful editions.
125730.title_en: Blues Fever Infected a Record Number

125746.excerpt_en: Schrøder Hansen moved to Oslo this week to take up a position as head of professional affairs at the Norwegian Medical Association.
125746.subtitle_en: After five years in Longyearbyen, surgeon Kari Schrøder Hansen is so professionally behind that she does not want to return to the operating table.

125764.excerpt_en: I would like to take this opportunity to say goodbye after more than five years as a senior consultant at Longyearbyen Hospital. Longyearbyen is a “mini-community” with many qualities that the wider society can learn from, particularly in emergency preparedness.
125764.subtitle_en: I would like to take this opportunity to say goodbye after more than five years as a senior consultant at Longyearbyen Hospital.
125764.title_en: A Community Mainland Norway Can Learn From

125800.excerpt_en: In mid-October, the man, who is in his thirties, was sentenced by a district court in Northern Norway. He was convicted in two cases of violating Section 200 of the Penal Code, concerning sexual acts with children under 16.
125800.subtitle_en: A Svalbard resident has been given a suspended prison sentence for indecent acts involving two underage girls.
125800.tags_en: court ruling, Governor of Svalbard, news

125804.excerpt_en: “Lompensenteret is interesting because it would become the northernmost of all the Thon Group’s shopping centres, while a purchase would give the Amfi Group the kingdom’s northernmost and southernmost shopping centres,” Thon says, pointing out that his retail chain also owns the 170,000-square-metre Sørlandssenteret in Kristiansand.
125804.subtitle_en: Olav Thon is negotiating to buy Lompensenteret in Longyearbyen.

125812.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the incident shortly after 4 p.m. on Saturday. “To be on the safe side, we chose to collect the injured man by helicopter.”
125812.subtitle_en: A man was airlifted from Svea on Saturday after getting a splinter in his face.
125812.title_en: Got a Splinter in His Face

125820.excerpt_en: The Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators (AECO), an organisation for cruise operators in the Arctic, was founded ten years ago by cruise operators in Svalbard. Its purpose is to ensure environmentally friendly, responsible and sustainable cruise tourism, and seven years ago AECO chose to expand its area of operations to include Jan Mayen and Greenland as well.
125820.subtitle_en: Extending beyond Arctic Canada and the Russian Arctic.

125838.excerpt_en: The smell of sweat is growing increasingly intense inside the sports hall in Barentsburg. There are fierce clashes on the court, while teammates and spectators cheer from the stands.
125838.subtitle_en: Things got heated on the court, but for Svalbard’s neighbours, the sporting exchanges are about more than the game.

125858.excerpt_en: “I’m pleased with myself,” Daniil Dubov concludes after the final chess game is over and he can leave the table. His opponent has certainly been a worthy one, and the match ended 1–1 during the sporting exchange between Barentsburg and Longyearbyen last Saturday (see pages 16 and 17).
125858.subtitle_en: You have to analyse your opponent. Continuously.

125866.excerpt_en: Last Friday, I—a usually even-tempered permanent resident—choked on my coffee for the first time in a long while when I read the article “Stagnant in Longyearbyen” in our local newspaper, Svalbardposten.
125866.subtitle_en: “Last Friday, I—a usually even-tempered permanent resident—choked on my coffee for the first time in a long while.”
125866.title_en: Has our healthcare system been left behind?

125874.excerpt_en: There have been three accidents involving personal injury in Svea over the past couple of weeks. The Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority will, together with the Svalbard Mining Inspectorate, investigate the circumstances. “We have asked for an account of what happened and what the company itself is doing in connection with the incidents.”
125874.subtitle_en: Following several accidents, Svea, Lunckefjellet and Barentsburg will be visited by the Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority.
125874.tags_en: Store Norske, news, Lunckefjellet, mine, Barentsburg, Svea

125882.excerpt_en: Lars Løseth, managing director of Thon Drift AS, says the company is currently reviewing the details of a possible purchase of Lompensenteret in Longyearbyen.
125882.subtitle_en: Before long, Lompensenteret will become part of Olav Thon’s shopping-centre empire.

125919.excerpt_en: The days are growing shorter and soon the Arctic will enter a period of darkness around the clock. A large number of satellites orbit above Platåfjellet.
125919.subtitle_en: As the Arctic Council works on a major risk analysis for the Arctic, KSAT is positioning itself to become even more important in environmental monitoring in the north.
125919.tags_en: news, oil spill response, environment, Svalsat

125933.excerpt_en: Many people recognised the billionaire property magnate Olav Thon’s distinctive cap in Longyearbyen late last week. It was not difficult to understand that this was no ordinary weekend trip.
125933.subtitle_en: The Thon Group’s arrival is significant far beyond the centre’s walls.

125957.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard lends the trapping station at Austfjordnes to people who wish to continue the tradition of overwinter trapping on Svalbard. Anyone may apply in principle, but in addition to hunting and trapping experience, the requirements include knowledge of nature and wilderness, as well as good health and a clean record.
125957.subtitle_en: Experience from polar regions is an advantage.
125957.title_en: Would you like to spend the winter here?

125975.excerpt_en: “We must ensure that we do not lose established traffic, and money must be made; otherwise, having cruise ships here is pointless. Everyone has to work then, not just sit around waiting,” says Terje Aunevik, managing director of Pole Position Logistics.
125975.subtitle_en: This is how cruise tourists will stay longer and spend more money.
125975.title_en: A new course for cruise tourism

125994.excerpt_en: On Tuesday evening, the local council finally approved the recommendations from the Administration Committee concerning Museumsveien. But not without fierce opposition from parts of the Conservative Party and the Cross-Party List (TF).
125994.subtitle_en: A new bridge on Museumsveien means higher road tolls. And several more bridges will soon need replacing.
125994.tags_en: news, road tolls, Longyearbyen local council

126002.excerpt_en: Group leader Geir Heknes’s strongest argument for turning Longyearbyen port into a limited company (AS) is the development opportunities he believes this would create. “We do not have the capital needed to develop the port.”
126002.subtitle_en: The Conservative Party proposed changing the organisation of both the port and Energiverket, but failed to win support.

126028.excerpt_en: Svalbard Reiseliv created a lively atmosphere in the square during the annual marketplace event held as part of Kunstpause. Beforehand, people had walked the Longyearcity March from Titankrana to the town centre, and several also stopped at Ateliér Storø along the way to see Nypressa art and enjoy a lunch concert with Olaf Storø and singer Berit Meland.
126028.subtitle_en: There was plenty of food, drink and entertainment in the square on Saturday, but for Jessica, Nelly and Liv-Anna, the puppies were the highlight.

126048.excerpt_en: Enthusiasm prevailed when the first coal load emerged from Lunckefjellet at the end of October. Its meeting with daylight marked the beginning of a new era for Store Norske Spitsbergen Kulkompani.
126048.subtitle_en: Store Norske and its employees on Svalbard are paying a high price for it.
126048.tags_en: opinion, editorial, coal mining, gas, Store Norske

126056.excerpt_en: At the very beginning of November, the Thon Group was in Longyearbyen. Olav Thon, the main shareholder in the Amfi Group, already hinted then that he was very keen to acquire Lompensenteret.
126056.subtitle_en: Lompensenteret has been sold. From the New Year, the Longyearbyen shopping centre will become part of the Amfi chain.

126066.excerpt_en: Last week, the Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority and the Svalbard Mining Inspectorate inspected mining operations in both Svea and Barentsburg. In the latter, reopening may be on the horizon after several months of suspension due to unsafe working conditions.
126066.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority is optimistic on behalf of Trust Arktikugol in Barentsburg.

126074.excerpt_en: Airlines certainly deserve some of the credit for helping make the world smaller. A journey that could take several days just a few decades ago is now little more than a quick trip.
126074.subtitle_en: When politicians and trade unions complain about the decision, they have good reason: the change means that the journey between Svalbard and Northern Norway will become long and expensive.

126082.excerpt_en: There is still a long time to go before the Svalbard Ski Marathon, but managing director Helle M. Jakobsen has been working at full speed for many months.
126082.subtitle_en: Several skiing stars, current and emerging, are pointing their skis towards Svalbard.

126092.excerpt_en: The tourism industry in Longyearbyen is now leaving no stone unturned to prevent cruise ships from dropping Svalbard calls during the summer season.
126092.title_en: Russians plan tourism centre in Longyearbyen

126106.excerpt_en: Apart from a few recreational fishermen catching food from the quay in Barentsburg, there is little to suggest fishing or fisheries in the mining town. But not far from the quay, Arctic Resource Norge AS plans to build a fish reception facility, probably with a cold-storage warehouse.
126106.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol hopes for a fish reception facility in Barentsburg, but does not want to become a co-owner.
126106.title_en: Does not want an ownership stake

126122.excerpt_en: SAS has decided to eliminate stopovers in Tromsø on Wednesdays and Fridays next year. Travellers going that way on those days will have to travel via Oslo.
126122.subtitle_en: Heidi Jorunn Brun got quite a shock when she went to buy a plane ticket.
126122.title_en: The Tromsø Trip Could Cost Four Times as Much

126130.excerpt_en: Knut-Morten Johansen of SAS rejects the suggestion that the company is failing in its social responsibility regarding Longyearbyen and Svalbard. “In general, we have been proactive in our route offering to Svalbard. Norwegian has also entered the market, and seat capacity has increased significantly in recent times.”
126130.subtitle_en: The reason for SAS’s change is simple and market-driven. Fewer and fewer people are travelling to Tromsø, while demand for Oslo has increased.

126138.excerpt_en: Since early November, the Amfi chain has been negotiating with Store Norske Spitsbergen Kullkompani AS and Eiendomsinvestor AS to buy Lompensenteret. When Olav Thon, Sissel Berdal Haga and Lars Løseth were in Longyearbyen, Thon made no secret of the fact that he wanted the world’s northernmost shopping centre.
126138.subtitle_en: This week, the parties agreed that Lompensenteret in Longyearbyen will be bought by the Thon-controlled company Amfi Eiendom AS. The takeover will take place at the turn of the year.

126146.excerpt_en: Olav Thon’s companies are fond of building monuments. Lompensenteret fits that way of thinking too. “We already have shopping centres from Mandal in the south to Alta and Kirkenes in the north.”
126146.subtitle_en: He has plans for Lompensenteret, but is keeping his cards close to his chest.

126178.excerpt_en: “We have some mechanical problems that need to be fixed. That is why the backup power plant was connected today,” says energy manager Roar Blomstrand.
126178.subtitle_en: The power station was shut down all day Tuesday for maintenance.

126186.excerpt_en: AECO (Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators) has received a total of NOK 650,000 from the Environmental Protection Fund for the project. The printed edition was first published in 2007 and has served as guidelines for cruise operators and tourists in the Arctic.
126186.subtitle_en: The printed edition of “Visitor Guidelines in the Arctic” is being turned into an animated film.

126202.excerpt_en: The choice in Lunckefjellet is between room-and-pillar mining and longwall mining. Total project investments are around NOK 1.2 billion, while investment in production equipment is estimated at approximately NOK 225 million to NOK 320 million, respectively.
126202.subtitle_en: The decision on how Store Norske will extract coal from what is described as one of Norway’s most challenging projects is coming earlier than planned.
126202.tags_en: Store Norske, mine, Lunckefjellet, news, Svea

126214.excerpt_en: The last boat left Svea on the morning of Friday, 22 November.
126214.subtitle_en: Store Norske shipped almost 800,000 more tonnes of coal from Svea Nord this year than in 2012. The company now needs more storage space in Svea.
126214.tags_en: Store Norske, Svea, Lunckefjellet, mine, news

126230.excerpt_en: Nine Longyearbyen residents have been captured in the spotlight. They now hang on the walls inside the museum, frozen in different scenes from everyday life.
126230.subtitle_en: The 24-year-old has let photographers into her life.

126240.excerpt_en: Pernilla Carlsson admits that she was nervous when she defended her doctoral thesis last week. But no one could tell by looking at her.
126240.subtitle_en: “I was calm until two days before my defence. Then the nerves started to set in.”

126252.excerpt_en: Anja Boman and Abigael Winsvold started with 55 children. A week later, they put on a show featuring dance, comedy, acrobatics and a recurring theme.
126252.subtitle_en: Well over 300 people watched nearly 60 children put on a circus in Longyearbyen.

126266.excerpt_en: Vegard Faksdal (16) and Kristoffer Grønås (15) readily admit that they were among the very first to start their snowmobile at the beginning of November.
126266.subtitle_en: Call them radd if you like. It is, after all, a term of honour.

126298.excerpt_en: UNIS students Bjarte Rismyhr and Michael Lawrence got the shock of their lives on Tuesday this week while studying rock samples in a cabin in Endalen outside Longyearbyen. It was purely by chance that polar bear and human did not come face to face.
126298.subtitle_en: While the geology students worked inside a cabin, the polar bear crept past just outside the door.
126298.title_en: Polar Bear Right Outside the Door

126308.excerpt_en: Since Longyearbyen’s Christmas tree was lit on Sunday, pictures of the small, spindly tree have become a nationwide talking point. Nordlys and TV 2 are among the media outlets questioning whether Longyearbyen’s tree is “Norway’s most pathetic”.
126308.subtitle_en: After Longyearbyen’s Christmas tree was mocked as “Norway’s most pathetic”, the supplier felt guilty. A new tree is being sent to Longyearbyen today.
126308.title_en: A Change of Heart in the Christmas-Tree Saga

126352.excerpt_en: “I’m really looking forward to it. And my enthusiasm will rub off on those who are going to contribute,” says Trine Krystad.
126352.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen is to become one of the first places in Norway able to call itself a Sustainable Destination.

126369.excerpt_en: “Why are you pretending to be Santa Claus?” the two seven-year-olds asked when they each received a bag of sweets. They got no answer.
126369.subtitle_en: Three Santas appeared in the square on the first Sunday of Advent. Adelia Sunde Øverli (7) and Elise Fredheim (7) were sceptical about whether the man handing them sweets was the real Santa Claus.
126369.title_en: Christmas Spirit Descended on the Town

126385.excerpt_en: “We are refunding the entire fee paid by Bykaia Lagerutleie AS because it was calculated on an incorrect basis. It amounts to just under one million kroner,” says chief administrative officer Lars Ole Saugnes.
126385.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) has decided to refund the entire connection fee to Bykaia Lagerutleie AS.
126385.title_en: Longyearbyen Local Council to Refund Fee

126415.excerpt_en: Early this morning, the Governor of Svalbard was informed that flags were to fly at half-mast from noon to 3 p.m. on Friday. The occasion was the death yesterday in South Africa of liberation hero Nelson Mandela, 12,000 kilometres away.
126415.subtitle_en: Flags will fly at half-mast for Nelson Mandela at five locations in Longyearbyen.

126439.excerpt_en: This year marks 40 years since the agreement on polar-bear protection was signed. Last week, representatives of Norway, Denmark (Greenland), Russia, Canada and the United States met in Moscow to sign a declaration on continued cooperation to protect polar bears.
126439.subtitle_en: The five polar-bear nations will strengthen cooperation on protecting the species.
126439.title_en: Stepping Up Efforts for the Polar Bear

126453.excerpt_en: Canadian Foreign Minister John Baird confirms that Canada will claim the North Pole and the resource-rich sea around it. He also confirms that the claim will be submitted in connection with an application to the UN to extend the country’s territorial boundary in the north, NTB reports.
126453.subtitle_en: Canada will claim the North Pole and the resource-rich sea around it.
126453.tags_en: North Pole, news, Arctic, continental shelf
126453.title_en: The Race for the North Pole Continues

126505.excerpt_en: Store Norske Boliger (SNB) posted a result of NOK 6.8 million in 2012. The company, which has equity of more than a quarter of a billion kroner, owns almost 400 homes in Longyearbyen.
126505.subtitle_en: Håvar Fjerdingøy, managing director of Store Norske Boliger AS, understands that it is difficult for families without subsidized housing to live in Longyearbyen.
126505.title_en: Understands That the Housing Situation Is Difficult

126513.excerpt_en: The pathetic Christmas tree in Longyearbyen attracted even more national attention after Svalbardposten’s report on it last week.
126513.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen’s puny Christmas tree has been replaced.

126525.excerpt_en: Fewer politicians and committees are intended to make politics clearer and more accessible to the general public. On Tuesday, the local council adopted a new political structure, involving fewer boards and a shorter route to decision-makers.
126525.subtitle_en: The local council is to become more accessible.
126525.title_en: Wants Help from the Common People

126559.excerpt_en: WHAT IS it that drives the price per square metre for rental housing on Svalbard to a level matched by only a handful of other Norwegian cities?
126559.subtitle_en: In practice, that means we get a second-string team.

126567.excerpt_en: Parents were able to enjoy their sweet little ones taking part in Lucia processions at the kindergartens this morning. Kullungen Kindergarten spread joy outside the kindergarten as well, visiting Næringsbygget and Lompen Shopping Centre.
126567.subtitle_en: All the kindergartens in Longyearbyen held Lucia celebrations early this morning.

126577.excerpt_en: The local council has elected Carl Einar Ianssen as a new member of Svalbardposten’s board. Ianssen will replace Jarle Berg-Oksfjellelv when he moves to the mainland early next year.
126577.subtitle_en: These are the people who will take over.

126609.excerpt_en: The man left Svea at around 9 p.m. yesterday, but did not return as agreed. A helicopter search was therefore launched. “We found the man in Reindalen.”
126609.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard launched a search last night for a man on a snowmobile who failed to return to Svea as agreed.

126635.excerpt_en: At the back, down a few steps in the third wine cellar, there it is. “1834” is printed in white letters on the Portuguese bottle.
126635.subtitle_en: With 20,000 bottles in the wine cellar, champagne costing 24,000 and Madeira from 1834, Huset is in a class of its own—even in Europe, in fact.

126673.excerpt_en: Turnaround ports in Northern Norway open up major opportunities for expedition ships visiting Svalbard. That is the view of Cruise Northern Norway & Svalbard.
126673.subtitle_en: Opportunities for Svalbard, says cruise organization.

126677.excerpt_en: Japan wants a new research station because it plans to increase its activity. Germany has also indicated a need for more space and wants to spend more time studying marine life during the polar night.
126677.subtitle_en: Both the number of researcher-days and the number of tourists are declining in Ny-Ålesund, but interest in using the settlement is now growing.
126677.title_en: More Want to Conduct Research in Ny-Ålesund

126687.excerpt_en: At Kings Bay’s traditional Christmas seminar in Oslo, where everyone from the polar network had gathered, Knut Ore received plenty of praise. Newly elected chair Unni Steinsmo thanked him for his long and valuable service and was especially pleased by the way he had welcomed her. “The company is well run.”
126687.subtitle_en: Knut Ore was forced to step down as chair of Kings Bay against his will. Now he has been honored as an honorary citizen of the unique research settlement.

126695.excerpt_en: THE LAST FEW DAYS of the year are nearly over. 2013 has been a challenging year in many ways.
126695.subtitle_en: If the cards are played right, it could produce even better returns.
126695.tags_en: Svalbard, opinion, editorial, mine, research, travel

126715.excerpt_en: There is one overwhelmingly important reason the associations have decided to replace kerosene with battery-powered LED lamps: the risk of fire. “It is because of the fire hazard posed by oil lamps. We must reduce the risk of cultural heritage sites burning down—and of people losing their lives,” says Steinar Strøm of To-Takteren.
126715.subtitle_en: To-Takteren has removed all kerosene lamps from its cabins. Now the Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association is doing the same.

126737.excerpt_en: Ousdal played the third member of the ill-fated Swedish polar expedition of 1897. Knut Hjalmar Ferdinand Frænkel is little mentioned in history, but Magnus Carlsson has brought this man to light and written a book about him.
126737.subtitle_en: When curious onlookers followed the filming of “Engineer André’s Flight” in 1981, many asked Sverre Anker Ousdal who he was playing.

126855.excerpt_en: The pupils have taken part in a so-called reverse Christmas calendar, an initiative organized by SOS Children’s Villages. Instead of receiving a small gift each day, the principle is that the pupils bring an anonymous cash donation in an envelope.
126855.subtitle_en: Most children are used to receiving something behind each door of an Advent calendar. But this year, first through fourth grade at Longyearbyen School turned the whole thing around. They gave.
126855.title_en: Turned the Advent Calendar Upside Down

126865.excerpt_en: “Green Frost,” operated by Bodø-based Zahl Transport AS, arrived in Svea a week ago carrying, among other things, spare parts for coal mining operations in Svea. By then, however, the spare parts and most of the other goods in the hold had become unusable.
126865.subtitle_en: The ship “Green Frost” ran into heavy weather on its way to Svea, causing extensive damage to both its cargo and cargo hold.

126875.excerpt_en: The Svalbard seminars have become a tradition during the polar night, when researchers and historians are challenged to entertain audiences with popular-science lectures at the University Centre in Svalbard. Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9 p.m.
126875.subtitle_en: How healthy are fish, seals and whales, really? What should you do—and what should you avoid—when traveling on Svalbard? These three hope to provide the answers.

126895.excerpt_en: It was Labour’s Jonas Gahr Støre who stated that he wanted to change the oil fund’s course. Over the weekend, the deputy chair of the Finance Committee called for a national debate on how Norway can end its investments in coal.
126895.subtitle_en: It is hypocritical to withdraw the oil fund from international coal mining while simultaneously operating a state-owned coal mine on Svalbard, the Conservative Party says.

126927.excerpt_en: Like many museums, Svalbard Museum has its own mystery. A pattern on the floor, directly in front of where Edvard Munch’s painting “Self-Portrait with Cigarette” hung when it was displayed in Longyearbyen just over a year ago, may resemble the outline of a human being.
126927.subtitle_en: “I thought it became clear that a dead person had been lying there.”

127008.excerpt_en: Svalbard on Display: For the first time, Svalbard presented itself at a travel fair. For four days, people could visit the stand at the fair at Sjølyst and get answers to questions about Svalbard.
127008.subtitle_en: Svalbard makes its debut at a travel fair, cabins are wrecked by polar bears, and the ministry decides what equipment Svalbardposten will receive.

127012.excerpt_en: The withdrawal means, among other things, that the company’s expedition cruise ships will no longer be required to follow the guidelines for environmentally friendly, safe and culturally responsible operations to which members of AECO (Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators) have committed themselves.
127012.subtitle_en: German Hapag-Lloyd Cruises will not disclose why the cruise operator has withdrawn from the organization for environmentally friendly, safe and culturally responsible operations in the Arctic.

127021.excerpt_en: In the latest issue of Svalbardposten, we wrote about efforts to limit and eradicate alien and harmful species on Svalbard. Among other things, the Norwegian Polar Institute referred to a study of the shoes of travelers arriving by air in the summer of 2008.
127021.subtitle_en: Tourists are now being asked to clean their clothes and footwear before coming to Svalbard.
127021.title_en: Taking Action to Prevent the Spread

127089.excerpt_en: Rasmus Hansson of the Green Party (MDG) has no doubts after the Labour Party announced that it would support withdrawing the oil fund from coal investments. “Norwegian coal production on Svalbard must be ended. Even if the oil fund is not invested in Svea, it is still Norwegian money.”
127089.subtitle_en: “There is now a majority in the Storting in favor of withdrawing the oil fund from coal investments. That also means we should end coal mining in Svea.”

127097.excerpt_en: “Perhaps I should have trained a little more often,” says Sven Are Johansen with a smile and a grimace as he gasps for breath on the exercise mat. Last Friday’s circuit training was definitely not for people in poor shape.
127097.subtitle_en: Polar Puls’s fitness festival is no ladies’ club. The men found that out too.
127097.title_en: A Party of Sweat and Sore Muscles

127119.excerpt_en: Last year was exceptionally difficult for the Russian mining community. Two men died in accidents, while a third had to have a foot amputated after being trapped inside the mine.
127119.subtitle_en: The Labour Inspection Authority is satisfied with the measures Trust Arktikugol has taken at the Barentsburg mine and has granted permission for operations to resume.

127135.excerpt_en: “The SAS flight has just landed, Lufttransport has resumed flights to and from Svea, and the mail is on its way,” says airport director Morten Ulsnes. The runway ice problems are over.
127135.subtitle_en: UPDATED: Air traffic has resumed at Svalbard Airport.

127163.excerpt_en: Recently, Lars Løseth, managing director of Amfi, visited Longyearbyen to meet the centre’s tenants, brief them and gather input. One conclusion is that the architects will most likely begin work on the new Lompen within the next two months.
127163.subtitle_en: Both shop owners and customers will notice that Lompen has a new and more active owner, the Amfi chief says. The task now is to create a shopping centre that fits into Longyearbyen.

127172.excerpt_en: “In general, everything seemed positive after the meeting. Everyone is looking forward to this,” says Gry Sneltvedt.
127172.subtitle_en: The tenants are looking forward to getting a modern shopping centre.
127172.title_en: Looking Forward to Getting Started on the Modernisation

127198.excerpt_en: Today is the dress rehearsal, and tomorrow, Saturday, it gets serious: two performances at the Cultural Centre. The musical is called Stop!

127215.excerpt_en: My wife and I stand on the Mine 7 mountain one evening, looking out over a landscape illuminated by a faint but growing moon. It is cold, with more stars than anyone could count.
127215.subtitle_en: If there was anyone I would have felt safe with on a high-speed boat from Stavanger to Bergen, it was the skipper of “Sleipner”.
127215.title_en: Who Are We, and Who Is Robert Hermansen?

127231.excerpt_en: Despite her young age, star soprano Julia Novikova has forged a meteoric career in opera. Together with pianist Sergej Osadchuk, she is coming to Longyearbyen to give an intimate concert at Galleri Svalbard this Thursday at 7 p.m.

127261.excerpt_en: Expedition leader aboard “Helmer Hanssen”, Stig Falk-Petersen, stresses that the researchers’ work must be communicated widely. Bringing along Virgine Garin from French radio station RTL and Veronique Reyberotte from Radio France Culture may be an obvious smart move in that regard.
127261.subtitle_en: “We are trying to tell the French people about the situation in the Arctic—about developments and researchers’ views on the situation.”
127261.title_en: From Paris to the Polar Night

127269.excerpt_en: In its latest decision, the Labour Inspection Authority allowed Trust Arktikugol to resume operations at the Barentsburg coal mine after a lengthy shutdown because worker safety was not considered adequate. Two conditions However, the authority has imposed two non-negotiable conditions for reopening.
127269.subtitle_en: The Labour Inspection Authority believes Trust Arktikugol has seriously followed up on the orders it was given. The mine in Barentsburg has reopened.

127287.excerpt_en: At the safety briefing before the research vessel Helmer Hanssen leaves the quay in Longyearbyen, one person stands out in particular. With a large, furry microphone on a stand and sound equipment in his lap, Trond Lossius sits on the back bench, listening intently through his headphones.
127287.subtitle_en: Artist Trond Lossius (47) brings a little more to a research expedition than art alone.

127311.excerpt_en: Around 100 people took part in Spitsbergen Up & Down, held for the fifth year in Spitsbergen. Participants had to climb four kilometres to a mountain summit before skiing back down.
127311.subtitle_en: See what it is like to ski down the mountains of Spitsbergen with a headlamp as the only source of light.
127311.title_en: Full Speed Down the Mountain in the Polar Night

127327.excerpt_en: Radisson has earned the Nordic Swan Ecolabel, Funken is to receive environmental certification, we use four-stroke snowmobiles and have introduced several energy-efficiency measures. The question is what we can do next. Ida Dyreng, marketing director at Spitsbergen Travel, is looking for more ways the company can improve its environmental profile.
127327.subtitle_en: The travel industry has acquired a taste for sustainability. In 2014, it intends to secure proof that it is sustainable.
127327.tags_en: Travel industry, environment, cruise, tourism, news

127337.excerpt_en: Nevertheless, this year’s Polarjazz programme is full of treats. “We have hoped that Polarjazz would establish itself as a festival, and that people would also attend concerts out of curiosity and interest,” says Lasse Stener Hansen, head of Polarjazz. A surprise This completely jazz-dominated programme will therefore be a test.
127337.subtitle_en: For the 17th time, they are jazzing up Svalbard. And this year it will be nothing but jazz. Clearly a little daring, the organisers admit.

127345.excerpt_en: On Saturday, the pupils at Longyearbyen School performed “Stop! Don’t Bully!” no fewer than twice—a musical addressing the problem of bullying.
127345.subtitle_en: It was a busy Saturday for musicians, actors and prop crews at the cultural centre.

127357.excerpt_en: Records were set to fall when Spitsbergen Up and Down was held for the fifth time on Saturday. A total of 96 people started: 72 in the recreational class and the rest in the competition class.
127357.subtitle_en: Vegar was determined and gave it everything. Others enjoyed a spectacular outdoor experience.
127357.title_en: More Records Fall in Up and Down

127384.excerpt_en: This year’s sun drawing is signed by Nikolas Ottemo (6). 1.
127384.subtitle_en: Nikolas Ottemo’s (6) sun was selected from among 88 entries.
127384.title_en: Here Is This Year’s Sun Artist

127392.excerpt_en: Inside the workshop at Mine 7, two brand-new shuttle cars are undergoing overhauls.
127392.subtitle_en: But we are on the right track, says Store Norske shop steward Arild Olsen.
127392.title_en: “It Has Been Tough, and It Will Be Tough”

127410.excerpt_en: Hole took up the leadership position at Longyearbyen Local Council in 2003 and held it for about ten years. She was therefore central to Longyearbyen’s development.
127410.subtitle_en: Public agencies in Longyearbyen are flying flags at half-mast today following the death of longtime head of planning and development Vigdis Hole.

127434.excerpt_en: The innermost part of Petuniabukta has begun to freeze, and in the next few days the ship “Noorderlicht” will head for Tempelfjorden to let itself freeze in. But for that to make a difference, the wind must die down and temperatures must drop considerably.
127434.subtitle_en: Warm water is being pushed into the fjords, preventing them from freezing over. In other words, it will still be a while before “Noorderlicht” is frozen into Tempelfjorden.
127434.title_en: Ice in the Stomach—but Not on the Fjord

127470.excerpt_en: “I think it is perfectly fine to use it at work. I have dreamed of having it as a hobby,” says Marius Opsanger Jonassen as he lifts a red-and-white model.
127470.subtitle_en: For most people, model aircraft are toys. For Marius, they are about meteorology and PhDs.

127478.excerpt_en: DSB is pointing to the lack of so-called guy-wire markers: clearly visible, brightly colored plastic tubes along the wires that hold up electrical poles.
127478.subtitle_en: The Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Planning (DSB) believes Energiverket must secure its steel guy wires with clear markings. They can be life-threatening for snowmobile drivers.

127489.excerpt_en: The children at Longyearbyen Kindergarten play energetically in the snow caves built in the playground outside. Some pop up, while others disappear down inside.
127489.subtitle_en: Seventeen of them were preschool-aged children.

127509.excerpt_en: He knows every nook and cranny of the research vessel. It has been his workplace since 1988, although he did very different work on board back then.
127509.subtitle_en: Jan Roald Dalsbø joined the “Helmer Hanssen” when the boat was new and called “Jan Mayen.” Back then, it was all about shrimp trawling.

127519.excerpt_en: More than 400 people turned out to see Mezzoforte and Lissie at the cultural center. Lissie toured as the opening act for Lenny Kravitz in 2008, among others, and has since built a solid reputation.

127545.excerpt_en: The purpose of the interviews is to establish what happened and determine whether any negligence may have occurred when the female student suffered burns in an accident involving a camping stove inside Rusanovhytta in Colesbukta on Sunday morning.
127545.subtitle_en: Participants on the trip during which a 26-year-old student suffered burns were questioned by police on Monday.

127553.excerpt_en: “I almost have to pinch myself. This is practically a dream,” said Urban Tunnel’s Klezmerband frontman and clarinetist, Morten Michelsen, after the concert at the cultural center in Barentsburg.
127553.subtitle_en: They woke up in Grünerløkka and ended the day to deafening applause from the audience at the cultural center in Barentsburg. Those attending had skipped Putin’s televised address to hear Norwegian klezmer music.

127593.excerpt_en: Seventy percent of business activity in Longyearbyen is a basic industry that generates its revenue outside Svalbard. This is the foundation for local demand, says Hilde Grimstad of Multiconsult.
127593.subtitle_en: Six hundred jobs would disappear in an instant if Store Norske suddenly went under.

127603.excerpt_en: The 23-year-old Canadian graduate student was one of nine people who traveled to Rusanovhytta in Colesbukta last Sunday, and has been chosen as their spokesperson. A 26-year-old woman suffered burns over large parts of her body after an accident while the students were preparing breakfast.
127603.subtitle_en: “The way we do things inside a cabin has changed forever after what happened to us this weekend,” says Vincent Carrier.
127603.title_en: “The Flames Reached Right Up to the Ceiling”

127614.excerpt_en: The demand relates to the construction of Avinor’s new hangar at Svalbard Airport, where the company believes Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) breached the cost-price principle.
127614.subtitle_en: Avinor is demanding that Longyearbyen Local Council repay more than NOK 1.8 million that the company paid in connection fees for water and district heating.

127636.excerpt_en: “We are very pleased with the weekend. There were lots of people, and everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves, which is the most important thing.”
127636.subtitle_en: Well over 1,200 people attended the various concerts during this weekend’s Polarjazz festival.

127652.excerpt_en: Until March last year, John Asle worked in a kindergarten and in the hospitality industry in Tromsø. When it became clear that he would be moving to Svalbard, the children needed an explanation. “When they understood where I was going, they started talking about both polar bears and ice princesses.”
127652.subtitle_en: John Asle Boine Somby (27) told the kindergarten children that he had moved to Svalbard to find the ice princess.
127652.tags_en: people, life on svalbard, back page

127668.excerpt_en: Many people took time today to enjoy the sight of sunlight on the other side of Adventfjorden. Hiorthfjellet and Operafjellet were crowned with golden light on their summits and down their south-facing slopes.
127668.subtitle_en: It will not be long before the sun’s rays reach Longyearbyen.
127668.title_en: The Light Is Coming to the North

127676.excerpt_en: Riots in the capital, Kiev, had continued since November and took a dramatic turn on Tuesday. According to various media reports, at least 28 people were killed and 287 hospitalized during Tuesday and Wednesday.
127676.subtitle_en: “I think about them all the time,” says Ukrainian Angelina Voronina (25) in Longyearbyen.
127676.title_en: Worried About Family and Friends in Ukraine

127738.excerpt_en: “Bouldering is fun. But climbing with a rope is even more fun.”
127738.subtitle_en: The higher they get above the floor, the more fun it is. Climbing on a wall is both social and exciting.

127748.excerpt_en: “The need is already there today. The challenge up here is that the sailing season is—as things stand—short.”
127748.subtitle_en: Work to create more quay space will begin in 2015. Svalbard Reiseliv is looking forward to it.

127756.excerpt_en: Three times as many injuries as in mainland mines Last year, 41 injuries were recorded in the mines—the best result ever. Even so, the injury rate in Longyearbyen’s mines is three times higher than the average for Norway’s mining industry. “The only encouraging thing is that there were no fatal accidents last year.”
127756.subtitle_en: Store Norske’s injury statistics were the main story in Svalbardposten 25 years ago.

127804.excerpt_en: The mountainside above Marthabreen was crowded outside the mine entrance before the formal ceremony. It has been 14 years since a mine was last opened on Svalbard, although the giant Svea Nord mine is now in its final phase.
127804.subtitle_en: The deficit was smaller in 2013 than the year before, but Store Norske’s chairman does not expect a surplus in 2014 either. Tuesday was nevertheless a day of celebration, as the new Lunckefjell mine was officially opened.
127804.title_en: Big Celebration at the Mine Entrance

127845.excerpt_en: DROVE HOME DRUNK A man in his 20s will appear before the Nord-Troms District Court charged with drunk driving, driving without a valid license and attempting to steal a car in Longyearbyen, Nordlys reports. According to the prosecution, the drunk-driving incident took place early on a Thursday morning in April last year.
127845.subtitle_en: Brief news items from the latest edition.

127849.excerpt_en: Because participation in the vessels featured in recent editions of “Ta Sjansen” has been declining, the organizers of Solfestuka 2014 have tried to think outside the box. Together with the Arctic Nature Guide program, they welcome visitors to the “Sun Games.”
127849.subtitle_en: Fewer vessels mean Solfestuka has to think again.

127857.excerpt_en: Last autumn, the old Nordsyssel left Svalbard for good. The plan was for a new ship to be in place next summer, but it is now uncertain whether it will arrive in time.
127857.subtitle_en: It is still uncertain when the Governor’s new vessel will be completed.

127894.excerpt_en: Tor Ingebrigtsen, managing director of UNN, was unavailable for comment to Svalbardposten, but left the response to communications director Hilde Annie Pettersen. “We did not consider Kari Schrøder Hansen a whistleblower at any point.”
127894.subtitle_en: “If you follow what is happening in society, several people claim the whistleblower label and adopt the role of a victim.”

127902.excerpt_en: “We have been in Ny-Ålesund for 30 years and in Svea for 25 years, and we were active when UNIS was established.”
127902.subtitle_en: Establishes an office after 30 years of presence on Svalbard.
127902.title_en: SINTEF Wants a Piece of the Arctic

127914.excerpt_en: Sure, I could have shown up with a camera and notepad, stood in the finishing area and asked what it was like to take part in a sled-dog race.
127914.subtitle_en: Some sped through Bolterdalen Rundt, while others spent half the race deciding who should pull.
127914.title_en: A Dog That Loves to Run

127926.excerpt_en: The buildings contain six apartments each. Robert Nilsen, who runs Svalbard Husky AS, bought one of them.
127926.subtitle_en: The twelve apartments at Skjæringa had stood empty and been on the market for years. Now they have been sold.
127926.title_en: Sold After Years of Sitting Empty

127968.excerpt_en: Many people spend years living on Svalbard without catching sight of a polar bear. Others see them in abundance.
127968.subtitle_en: Watch the video of the polar bear family. While the mother lies dozing, the cubs watch the photographer’s activities with curiosity.

127976.excerpt_en: “I have no doubt I’ll make it to Nome; the only question is how long it will take,” Jordbrudal joked when we met him a few hours before the start in Anchorage, Alaska’s most populous city. It is the last time he will see “civilisation.”
127976.subtitle_en: Tommy Jordbrudal from Longyearbyen admits he set off on Saturday with a mixture of fear and excitement for a 1,600-kilometre journey through Alaska’s most inaccessible and desolate wilderness.
127976.title_en: This Is Where Tommy’s Adventure Begins

127988.excerpt_en: The debate over where Norway should invest its oil wealth is in full swing. The Government Pension Fund, best known as the oil fund, seems to face one dilemma after another.
127988.subtitle_en: In plain terms, this must be interpreted as a repudiation of what made Norway a welfare state and one of the world’s richest countries.
127988.tags_en: oil, opinion, editorial, coal, gas, environment

127996.excerpt_en: “The goal is to continue the trapping tradition on Svalbard within certain parameters. That is what we want to achieve,” says Guri Tveito, chief environmental protection officer at the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
127996.subtitle_en: Not just anyone can spend the winter at the Austfjordnes trapping station.
127996.title_en: Made It Through the Eye of the Needle

128008.excerpt_en: The photograph was taken last weekend on the eastern side of Spitsbergen. Tourists and residents on snowmobile trips got to see a large number of polar bears in a small area.
128008.subtitle_en: “I wouldn’t bet on the population around Svalbard being in decline,” says a polar bear researcher.

128020.excerpt_en: According to The Observer, the latest estimates confirm researchers’ concern that the polar bear population in Western Hudson Bay has little chance of surviving in the long term. The first reliable figures from a monitoring programme date from 1987, when the population stood at 1,200 animals.
128020.subtitle_en: Canadian researchers are uncertain whether there will be polar bears in Western Hudson Bay in 2020.

128056.excerpt_en: Together with her partner Sergey Kondakov, Posrednikova helped prepare a dog team for a guided tour with Green Dog last week. “We’re on holiday, and chose to go to Svalbard because we’re not very fond of being somewhere extremely hot.”
128056.subtitle_en: “This is a fantastic place to experience. Coming during the polar night must also be something truly special,” says Ukrainian Anastasiia Posrednikova.
128056.title_en: The Polar Night Mystery May Be Solved

128070.excerpt_en: “What is unequivocally positive in the figures we have now received is that the growth has extended into the polar night. It began with Norwegian’s flight service, but that alone does not explain everything.”
128070.subtitle_en: In January alone, the number of commercial guest nights in Longyearbyen rose by 37 percent from last year.
128070.title_en: “We Are on the Verge of Succeeding”

128078.excerpt_en: On March 20 next year, shortly after ten o’clock, the moon will pass in front of the sun, giving us something as rare as a total solar eclipse.
128078.subtitle_en: Travel packages for next year’s solar eclipse on Svalbard are being sold for around NOK 60,000. The local community has begun preparing.
128078.title_en: Preparing for an Influx of Visitors for the Eclipse

128096.excerpt_en: The tension on the Crimean Peninsula affects Svalbard. Most of Barentsburg’s residents are Ukrainians employed by Trust Arktikgol, the Russian mining company.
128096.subtitle_en: Here, the delegation for Arctic cooperation gets a close-up look at mining. Just a few miles away, 300 Ukrainians are following developments in their homeland.

128112.excerpt_en: Dumdum Boys are considered one of the most influential bands in Norwegian rock history. Although their biggest and most legendary hits are around 20 years old, Prepple, Kjartan and the rest of the band are still going strong.
128112.subtitle_en: The hits kept coming as the Trondheim rockers performed at the Cultural Centre on Friday evening.
128112.title_en: “Split the Pine” for a Real Ruckus

128124.excerpt_en: For many years, the sun has been conspicuous by its absence on Sun Day, March 8.
128124.subtitle_en: The sun did its best to show up for Sun Day.

128182.excerpt_en: Røed Ødegaard has no hesitation in calling next year’s solar eclipse, best viewed from Svalbard, a global event. “I don’t have the full picture yet, but I assume there will be considerable pressure from people wanting to go to Svalbard to experience it,” says Knut Jørgen Røed…
128182.subtitle_en: Astrophysicist Knut Jørgen Røed Ødegaard recommends that people in Longyearbyen prepare thoroughly for the total solar eclipse on March 20 next year.

128198.excerpt_en: “This was the first case that landed on my desk after I started the job.”
128198.subtitle_en: Director Ole Arve Misund has worked on the rent issue since he started at UNIS. His main priority has been to establish a principle of equal treatment.

128206.excerpt_en: As tradition dictates, Longyearbyen celebrated the sun’s return last Saturday. It has been many years since the sun appeared on the actual Day, but this year it at least made a valiant attempt.
128206.subtitle_en: In addition to light and warmth, the sun’s return brings the prospect of sled-dog racing.

128222.excerpt_en: “We have tried to handle this matter quietly, but it has now become so heated that we must try to resolve it properly,” says Steve Coulson, chief union representative for the Norwegian Association of Researchers at UNIS. NOK 70,000 pay cut. The background is as follows: Before 2010, all employees at…
128222.subtitle_en: UNIS is raising the rent. Employees are responding by bringing in a lawyer.
128222.title_en: Researchers Hire Lawyer After Rent Dispute

128230.excerpt_en: The helicopter was sent to Svea on Sunday to pick up a man in his 60s who had been injured while riding a snowmobile. At quarter past twelve, Longyearbyen police received a report of the incident involving the man, who was part of a travelling party.
128230.subtitle_en: A person was taken to Longyearbyen Hospital on Saturday evening after an accident at work in Svea. On Sunday, the helicopter had to be dispatched again.

128238.excerpt_en: This year marks 200 years since Norway adopted its own constitution, and the slogan for Kindergarten Day on 18 March this year was “I Have Something to Say”.
128238.subtitle_en: The slogan for this year’s International Kindergarten Day was “I Have Something to Say”.

128252.excerpt_en: Tuesday’s news about the group that set off on its own prompted many reactions. The eleven were on a business trip to Svalbard, rented snowmobiles and set off without a local guide or GPS.
128252.subtitle_en: What makes an entire group of strangers believe that it is enough to rent a vehicle, clothing and a helmet and set off on a trip in Svalbard?

128274.excerpt_en: Production was higher than expected during the first part of January, but the cutting boom eventually encountered harder rock. In early March, Store Norske was in serious trouble when the cutting machine broke down—quite literally splitting in two.
128274.subtitle_en: The crew sorted things out when the cutting boom broke at Svea Nord.

128298.excerpt_en: This homemade guitar can be found in the exhibition at Svalbard Museum. It was carefully built from elements that were available “to hand”.
128298.subtitle_en: Imagine playing this guitar. It was found in 1965.

128306.excerpt_en: Marina van Dijk owns one of the boathouses in the Sjøområdet area. Like most of the others, hers is used as a residence.
128306.subtitle_en: Marina van Dijk (pictured) believes the head of administration has focused too much on “getting people out” and too little on solving the problems.

128322.excerpt_en: The new Governor’s vessel will be delayed by two to three months, so Remøy Management AS has meanwhile chartered the Icelandic coastguard vessel “Tyr” (pictured) for the Governor. The contract between the parties states that the daily rate is NOK 153,000.
128322.subtitle_en: It was hardly planned, but the Governor is saving money because of the delay to the new “Polarsyssel”.

128436.excerpt_en: In the end, Barentsburg won 6–0 overall. Svalbard Turn nevertheless reports a great snowmobile trip to the neighbouring settlement and a good atmosphere throughout the stay.
128436.subtitle_en: There were several close contests, but our neighbours in Barentsburg prevailed every time during last weekend’s sporting exchange.

128466.excerpt_en: “At today’s traffic level, there is a shortfall of 250 quay metres,” harbourmaster Kjetil Bråten states after serving coffee in the lounge in the middle of the harbour building, shared by Longyearbyen Harbour and Pole Position at Bykaia.
128466.subtitle_en: Next year they will receive a 333.5-metre-long cruise ship. Longyearbyen harbour has an 84-metre quay on the outside.

128497.excerpt_en: A German private pilot has been refused permission to fly to Svalbard. He planned to fly a single-engine light aircraft from Düsseldorf to Longyearbyen via Tromsø and wrote in his application that, in addition to being a “passionate pilot” who wanted to see beautiful scenery, he would be selling equipment to commercial kitchens.
128497.subtitle_en: When the light-aircraft pilot appealed the refusal to fly to Svalbard, the Governor looked up SAS’s timetable.

128509.excerpt_en: The company is marking its first year of flights to Svalbard and will continue through the summer and autumn with three weekly services. But from the next polar night onwards, the low-cost airline will cut the Wednesday flight.
128509.subtitle_en: The airline will reduce its schedule to two weekly flights as the next polar night approaches.

128575.excerpt_en: Knut Harald Holst-Hansen took over as managing director of Spitsbergen Travel just a few months ago.
128575.subtitle_en: Knut Harald Holst-Hansen, managing director of Spitsbergen Travel, admits that the company may not have been a good enough employer.

128583.excerpt_en: Photographers Roy Mangersnes and Ole Jørgen Liodden are behind the venture through the company Wildphoto Travel AS. The newcomer opens on Saturday in premises at Elvesletta Nord, between the Sports Centre and the Wilderness Centre. “The gallery will feature a selection of exclusive photographs from Svalbard.”
128583.subtitle_en: Wildphoto Travel & Gallery is the newest addition to Longyearbyen’s gallery scene.

128630.excerpt_en: When the season begins and the first cruise ship docks in mid-June, it also marks the start of the final season with calls at Ny-Ålesund and Magdalenefjorden, in the northwest of the island.
128630.subtitle_en: The truth is that most tourists are probably in the wilderness at the very moment they step out of the 737 after landing.

128638.excerpt_en: “I find it remarkable that they are out so early,” says Jon Aars, a researcher at the Norwegian Polar Institute. He has studied polar bears in Svalbard for many years and therefore knows their behaviour well.
128638.subtitle_en: The polar bear family is enjoying itself on the ice, but the scene is striking to researchers. Either the cubs are exceptionally small, or it is at least a month too early.

128658.excerpt_en: There are still places available, and Frode Benjaminsen, project manager for the block-based course, hopes to have 20 students before the application deadline on 15 April. “We sincerely hope so,” says Benjaminsen, who also teaches mathematics and physics.
128658.subtitle_en: The engineering programme has so far received 17 applications for the preparatory course in Longyearbyen.

128670.excerpt_en: The next major mining project has therefore been made public. Store Norske plans to carry out several drillings at Ispallen in 2014, but preliminary estimates indicate that the mountain contains more than ten million tonnes of coal—1.5 million tonnes more than Lunckefjellet.
128670.subtitle_en: Store Norske is now beginning an assessment of mining operations at Ispallen. At current coal prices, the mountain contains coal worth NOK 5 billion. But the environmental impact will be substantial.
128670.tags_en: Store Norske, Ispallen, Svea, mining, news
128670.title_en: Planning Begins for New Coal Mine

128724.excerpt_en: An antenna in the nose reveals that the fuselage contains more than the original technology. The aircraft, a DC-3, is operated by the Alfred Wegener Institute and is used to collect data.
128724.subtitle_en: The 1942 research aircraft was based in Longyearbyen in March.

128734.excerpt_en: On 27 March, the new doctor, Anastasia Rjaguzova, took up her post at the hospital in Barentsburg. Rjaguzova was a locum at the hospital in 2012, when then-chief physician Sergey Zavadsky was away on holiday.
128734.subtitle_en: The hospital in Barentsburg has a new doctor.

128742.excerpt_en: A total of 25 applications were received when the Governor of Svalbard announced the loan of cabins on Svalbard over Easter, from the 17th to the 21st.
128742.subtitle_en: The lucky applicants have been drawn.
128742.title_en: These People Will Borrow Cabins over Easter

128794.excerpt_en: Police received a report at 11:41 a.m. today that a man in a convoy of 10 snowmobiles had driven into a wind hole. The man, in his early 60s, complained of back pain, and it was decided to collect him by rescue helicopter.
128794.subtitle_en: A rescue helicopter had to evacuate a tourist after he went off the trail on Saturday.

128798.excerpt_en: “The goal is to reach the finish,” grins Urban Forsberg, patting Leo (one year and three months old) and lead dog Ravna (7). Gunn Beate Paasche nods.
128798.subtitle_en: In glorious weather, 22 teams set off in the world’s northernmost dog sled race.

128810.excerpt_en: The hiker was part of a group when he fell into a crevasse near Nordenskiöldtoppen just outside Longyearbyen on Sunday. At 3:15 p.m., police received a report of the accident.
128810.subtitle_en: A rescue operation is under way to retrieve a hiker who fell into a crevasse on Svalbard.

128818.excerpt_en: The rescue operation ended at around 6 p.m. on Sunday. “We have brought him up and, according to the reports I have received, he is safe and well despite a fall of 25 metres. I do not know the angle of the crevasse, but he was down there for two hours.”
128818.subtitle_en: The man who fell into the crevasse below Nordenskiöldtoppen is safe and well, but is receiving routine follow-up at the hospital.

128840.excerpt_en: The matter of Sjøområdet, the boathouses and the so-called wild residents is simmering away and, by all appearances, will continue to do so even after the chief administrative officer’s deadlines expire this summer. In short, the story is that several boathouses have been converted and are being used as homes without official approval.
128840.subtitle_en: One can only guess what the next step will be in normalising living conditions in Longyearbyen.

128848.excerpt_en: Last week, the price was NOK 468 per tonne. Store Norske needs NOK 510 to make a profit when Lunckefjellet is in normal operation.
128848.subtitle_en: Store Norske may have enough coal for 15 years of operations in the Svea area, but needs much higher prices to avoid losses when Lunckefjellet is operating.
128848.tags_en: Store Norske, news, Lunckefjellet, Ispallen, mine, Svea

128856.excerpt_en: Spectators and volunteers move around to keep warm as they wait for the mushers to come down Longyearbreen and follow the river to the finish at Huset in Longyeardalen. On Sunday the sky is clear and the temperature low, but Thomas Grant Olsen has worked up a sweat.
128856.subtitle_en: In biting cold and glittering sunshine, they arrive one by one after completing the world’s northernmost dog sled race.

128889.excerpt_en: Smoke rose from the power station’s backup facility on Sunday evening, as well as from the boiler houses around town that supplement the buildings with district heating.
128889.subtitle_en: The power station could not wait any longer. On Sunday, the boiler literally overflowed.

128899.excerpt_en: The sun was shining and spirits were high when the group set out from Nybyen at the top of Longyeardalen on Sunday, 6 April.
128899.subtitle_en: The ground gave way beneath Stefan Schöttl’s feet, and he fell 25 metres. Now he recounts the dramatic hours.
128899.title_en: Stefan, 25, Trapped in a Crevasse for Two Hours

128909.excerpt_en: Strictly speaking, Longyearbyen’s alpine slope is not an alpine slope at all, but a large sledding hill. That does not deter the sport’s most enthusiastic participants.
128909.subtitle_en: Every evening this winter, the slope behind the school has been full of enthusiastic young skiers. They want a new alpine ski slope in Longyearbyen.
128909.title_en: Calls for a New Alpine Ski Slope

128917.excerpt_en: At Tuesday’s meeting between the administration of Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) and technical experts on one side, and the boathouse owners on the other, many questions were raised without any concrete answers. At times, the discussion also became heated.
128917.subtitle_en: Although the chief administrative officer has ruled out “wild living” in Sjøområdet, cleaning up the situation will be a long and difficult process.

128929.excerpt_en: Sval and Bard can best be described as tourist trolls. They do not speak, but grunt and laugh coarsely in true troll fashion.
128929.subtitle_en: Their names are Sval and Bard, and they are well on their way to becoming something many people associate with Svalbard.
128929.title_en: These Two Will Welcome You to Svalbard

128949.excerpt_en: “We have been waiting all winter for ice to use in a sea-ice course, and the plan was to do this at Hornsund. But there is no ice in that area. We therefore applied to the Governor of Svalbard for permission to take the boat Lance a few boat lengths into safe ice in Dicksonfjorden.”
128949.subtitle_en: UNIS apologises for failing to notify trapper Harald Soleim when an ice channel was made in Dicksonfjorden on 10 April.
128949.title_en: The Trapper Should Have Been Notified

129021.excerpt_en: It was pure luck that Stefan Shöttl emerged from the drama at Nordenskiöldtoppen unharmed. The group of nine had no idea of the danger when they set off for the summit, a popular hiking destination.
129021.subtitle_en: There is no guarantee that we will witness such a chain of fortunate circumstances the next time an accident occurs.
129021.tags_en: opinions, editorial, emergency preparedness, rescue operation

129029.excerpt_en: The polar bear was involuntarily stranded on Hopen when the ice retreated in January. Closer to Easter, it finally had ice to walk on again and could head out seal hunting.
129029.subtitle_en: For the first time, the crew on Hopen have experienced a “winter bear”.
129029.title_en: Polar bear stranded by the climate on Hopen

129063.excerpt_en: The party held its national congress over the weekend, where the coal mines on Svalbard were among the topics discussed. The party, led by Member of Parliament Rasmus Hansson, has previously called for the closure of Svalbard’s coal mines.
129063.subtitle_en: The national congress of the Green Party is calling on the Storting to begin phasing out mining operations on Svalbard.
129063.title_en: Wants to close the coal mines

129069.excerpt_en: Forty-seven participants set off from Svea on Saturday morning, heading for Bolterdalen. Trond Espen Haug had to ski alone for most of the roughly 40-kilometre trip. “Yes, it turned out that way, but the snowmobile made good company,” says Haug, who calls himself a recreational skier.
129069.subtitle_en: Participants in Gruverennet got dream weather. First in was Trond Espen Haug—just as last year.

129072.excerpt_en: This year’s beach clean-up expedition will take place from 20 to 27.
129072.subtitle_en: A full 151 people applied to take part in this year’s clean-up expedition. Here are the 22 lucky ones.
129072.title_en: These are joining the clean-up expedition

129110.excerpt_en: The opening ceremony inside the aircraft hangar featured speeches, choral singing and the presentation of gifts. The hangar project had a budget of NOK 118 million, and Avinor chief Dag Falk Petersen was pleased to have completed it on schedule and under budget.
129110.subtitle_en: Governor Odd Olsen Ingerø says he did not always feel confident sending helicopters out on missions in bad weather. Now a new hangar and new helicopters are in place.

129124.excerpt_en: “A clearer ownership strategy is needed. We have enough money to operate at a break-even point, but developing the community and meeting today’s requirements will take more money,” Øiseth tells Svalbardposten.
129124.subtitle_en: Kings Bay director Ole Øiseth is unhappy that Japanese researchers have to make do with an old barracks, and says this is not good enough for Norway as host in Ny-Ålesund.

129127.excerpt_en: The former Store Norske chief has just finished Gruverennet and is standing chatting with old colleagues from the mining company. The mood is good on this last Saturday in April.
129127.subtitle_en: In a year, he may be debt-free. But Robert Hermansen deeply regrets the loan he took out from the late shipowner Atle Jebsen.

129137.excerpt_en: Svalbard showed itself at its very best when Gruverennet started from Svea on Saturday morning in 2014. The 47 participants had about 40 kilometres of groomed trail ahead of them. “Fantastic course!”
129137.subtitle_en: Participants in Gruverennet got dream weather. At the finish, there was coffee, sausages, hot cordial and champagne.

129157.excerpt_en: Last year was the national-team skier’s first time on Svalbard. He was hugely impressed by both the ski race and the arrangements surrounding the event. “Last year’s participation was part of a private sponsorship agreement.”
129157.subtitle_en: Eldar Rønning (32) got a taste for the Svalbard Ski Marathon. This year he is bringing several national-team skiers.
129157.title_en: Looking forward to another spectacular ski race

129162.excerpt_en: This is the 22nd time Svalbard Turn has organized the Svalbard Ski Marathon.
129162.subtitle_en: “The snow conditions on this year’s course mean that conditions are better than ever,” says Kåre Hovland.

129177.excerpt_en: The editor of Svalbardposten wrote an editorial in the previous issue about the incident on Nordenskiöldfjellet, headlined “A Wake-Up Call”. Sunday 6.
129177.subtitle_en: More important than learning how to get out of a tight spot, however, is knowing how to avoid dangerous situations.

129179.excerpt_en: The girls, who are in the tenth grade at Longyearbyen School, pack an envelope for each participant.
129179.subtitle_en: They spend several hours preparing for participants in the Svalbard Ski Marathon. At the same time, they are preparing for their own sporting experience.

129203.excerpt_en: In addition to the main cabin, the complex consists of four annexes with an unknown number of beds and a sauna.
129203.subtitle_en: Benn Eidissen has agreed with Robert Hermansen to buy his cabin complex in Bjørndalen. The price is NOK 2.5 million.

129255.excerpt_en: Bjørn Henningsen and Hans Lund are arguing over who owns Farmhamna, but the matter could end with the Governor of Svalbard taking over the trapping station built in the early 1990s. Distance – “My client is demanding ownership of Farmhamna,” says lawyer Per Ove Tønnessen.
129255.subtitle_en: One claims to have a purchase contract. The other denies signing anything.
129255.title_en: Years-long dispute ends up in court

129258.excerpt_en: “It’s called a rescuer, yes,” confirms the 34-year-old, who made it through the eye of the needle last June. She is now part of Lufttransport’s helicopter crew on Svalbard, one of seven rescuers.
129258.subtitle_en: If you get into trouble and need rescuing, your rescuer may well be named Mari Mowe Martinsen.
129258.title_en: Breaking ground in a man’s profession

129264.excerpt_en: Finn Løken (pictured) began the work last spring and returned this spring to put the finishing touches on it. “I’ll finish this week,” he said when Svalbardposten met him on 29 April.
129264.subtitle_en: Renovation of the old Telegraph Station in Ny-Ålesund is complete.
129264.title_en: The grand old building is ready

129307.excerpt_en: His journey from Bremen, Germany, began in March. At the end of April, he arrived in Longyearbyen, completely unprepared for what awaited him. “It was extremely cold the first night in the tent.”
129307.subtitle_en: Backpacker Lars Kaiser (20) admits he did not really know what awaited him when he boarded a plane to Longyearbyen.

129312.excerpt_en: The introduction of the Health Personnel Act on Svalbard has been under consideration for a long time. Last week, the patient and user ombudsman offices in the three northernmost counties visited Longyearbyen. “We have proposed that patient rights from the mainland should also apply on Svalbard.”
129312.subtitle_en: The patient and user ombudsmen in the three northernmost counties propose that mainland patient rights should also apply on Svalbard.

129314.excerpt_en: Some time ago, Giskegjerde (16) stopped by Svalbardposten to say hello and find out how we work. The students also needed an interview subject for a school project, and the 16-year-old was the one who drew the longest straw.
129314.subtitle_en: Graduating students Vårin Sandring Storø, Christian André Pedersen and Erik Kroknes Giskegjerde at Longyearbyen School have been working with media.

129347.excerpt_en: With skipper Oddvar Instanes and Stig Onarheim in the wheelhouse, we took a trip to Ny-Ålesund. For the occasion, the latter was fitted with a camera on his helmet by Svalbardposten, to give our readers Svalbard from a slightly different perspective.
129347.subtitle_en: Especially when Svalbard is showing its best side.
129347.title_en: A Decent View from the Office

129349.excerpt_en: Taking on the role of host entails obligations. If the guests are modest enough, the reaction may well be absent—but at some point, patience runs out.
129349.subtitle_en: This is a site of global significance.
129349.tags_en: opinion, editorial, climate, Kings Bay, Ny-Ålesund

129375.excerpt_en: LNS Spitsbergen AS wants to build more small housing units and has therefore applied for an exemption from the requirement that at least 50 percent of the homes in this area must be four- or five-room apartments. The developer wants to build more small units, but the local council majority disagrees.
129375.subtitle_en: The majority on the local council is unwilling to depart from the zoning plan for Elvesletta South.

129380.excerpt_en: “We will succeed,” says local council chair Christin Kristoffersen. On Tuesday, the local council adopted the Strategic Business Plan.
129380.subtitle_en: “Previously, people were told what to do on Svalbard. Now Svalbard is telling us what to do.”

129399.excerpt_en: “We tagged Kara last spring. The transmitter stopped sending in the winter,” says polar bear researcher Jon Aars of the Norwegian Polar Institute.
129399.subtitle_en: The polar bear Kara is one tough lady. No polar bear ever tagged in Svalbard has covered such long distances before.

129401.excerpt_en: “The world’s newest used helicopter,” jokes Stig Næsh, managing director of Lufttransport, as he shows off LN-OLR, an AS332-L1 Super Puma—the first of two helicopters the company will use under its contract with the Governor of Svalbard.
129401.subtitle_en: This helicopter was actually wrecked after the 2011 tsunami in Japan.
129401.title_en: Found Svalbard’s New Helicopter on Google

129420.excerpt_en: They will meet by the July 22 memorial at Skjæringa as early as eight o’clock to play the first beats.
