129420.subtitle_en: Young drummers will provide brass-band music from early morning on Constitution Day.
129420.title_en: Brass Band Wakes Up the Town

129471.excerpt_en: “Tyr” docked in Longyearbyen on Thursday evening. The vessel has been chartered until the new “Polarsyssel” is ready and comes from the Icelandic Coast Guard.
129471.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s replacement vessel is now in Svalbard.

129488.excerpt_en: The celebrations of Constitution Day and the bicentenary of the Constitution began as early as 8 a.m. and ended in the evening with a gala performance in the cultural hall. Here are a few glimpses from May 17.
129488.subtitle_en: It started a little bitterly cold early in the morning, but then the sun came out and warmed up Longyearbyen.

129493.excerpt_en: A grateful Per Kyrre Reymert accepted the 2014 Typhus Statuette, Longyearbyen’s cultural award. This year marks 40 years since Svalbard adopted its first regulations protecting cultural heritage.
129493.subtitle_en: “I must admit that I have sometimes put myself forward or said yes before being asked.”

129516.excerpt_en: Constitution Day was duly celebrated with ice at every meal and a noisy little civic parade, Linda Bakken says of the May 17 celebrations in Svea.
129516.subtitle_en: There was no shortage of good spirits in Svea. Others celebrated Constitution Day on top of Ispallen.

129534.subtitle_en: Just a few years ago, everyone thought Blomstrandhalvøya was a peninsula. Then the ice melted.

129540.excerpt_en: “It was christened at KB. They kept the diploma and bouquet at the cultural center, but I held on to the statuette for the rest of the evening and into the early morning,” says Reymert, who was honored on Saturday with the award for his contribution to the good of society.
129540.subtitle_en: Per Kyrre Reymert loves people and loves telling stories. On May 17, the archaeologist also celebrated with the 2014 Typhus Statuette.

129578.excerpt_en: “At the moment, it looks as though we are in the process of filling all the kindergartens for the next school year,” says unit manager Anne Jahre of Longyearbyen Local Council (LL). She stresses that not all cancellations of kindergarten places have been received.
129578.subtitle_en: Last year, Longyearbyen’s kindergartens had to cut back operations because there were fewer children. Now the trend is reversing.
129578.title_en: The Number of Children Is Rising Again

129591.excerpt_en: In the latter half of August this year, the “Cable Innovator” will arrive in Longyearbyen. The English-registered specialist vessel has a gross tonnage of 14,277 tonnes, is 146 meters long and 24 meters wide.
129591.subtitle_en: The project to lay a subsea fiber-optic cable between Longyearbyen and Ny-Ålesund this summer will be both lengthy and demanding.
129591.title_en: A Colossally Heavy Subsea Cable Operation

129601.excerpt_en: The politicians on the local council are preparing for this year’s strategy conference in June.
129601.subtitle_en: The era of a single electricity price around the clock may be coming to an end.
129601.title_en: Aiming to Avoid Costly Power Peaks

129630.excerpt_en: UN climate chief Christiana Figueres’s proposal to shut down mining on Svalbard was met with enthusiasm by environmental politicians and the environmental movement. Figueres was essentially following up on the debate over coal mining on Svalbard, which has raged for the past six months—particularly on the mainland.
129630.subtitle_en: Believing that everything will sort itself out without any policy tools, as suggested on NRK Alltid Nyheter, is optimistic at best.

129667.excerpt_en: “It definitely isn’t, and in the transition away from coal, Norwegian gas could play a role, internationally as well. But until new energy sources are in place, it is important that we develop new technology to capture carbon from coal operations,” says Sundtoft.
129667.subtitle_en: Coal is not the energy source of the future, says Minister of Climate and the Environment Tine Sundtoft (Conservative).

129680.excerpt_en: The first overseas cruise ship of the season is expected in Longyearbyen in mid-June. Over time, the trend has been for ships to become fewer in number but larger.
129680.subtitle_en: Most tourists come here only once. They are also willing to spend money on Svalbard.
129680.title_en: Plans to get more from each cruise passenger

129682.excerpt_en: Equipped with white gloves and silk scarves, three men were to conquer the North Pole by balloon. The journey was supposed to last only a few days, and they were to land safely on the other side of the Arctic Ocean.
129682.subtitle_en: Take a generous portion of suffering, a few unsolved mysteries, death and a little unconditional love, and you have a story that lasts forever. This month’s object comes from such a story.

129701.excerpt_en: Sébastien Barrault had barely heard of Svalbard when a friend told him about the place. Back home, he studied the map, and eventually a plan began to take shape.
129701.subtitle_en: Sébastien likes snow. So much so that he swapped the Alps for Ny-Ålesund.
129701.title_en: A quick trip to the far north

129762.excerpt_en: The tour boat is now moored in Longyearbyen and may not leave the harbour until inspectors from the Norwegian Maritime Authority have approved the vessel following repairs. MS “Langøysund” had eight passengers, a guide and a crew of four on board when it ran aground in Borebukta on Friday evening.
129762.subtitle_en: This is where “Langøysund” is resting on the reef. The passengers were evacuated after the incident.

129765.excerpt_en: On Monday afternoon, telephone and data connections were brought to a standstill. A fault at a station in Harstad suddenly made it impossible to make outgoing calls, either from landlines or mobile phones.
129765.subtitle_en: At the same time, it is highly troubling that a fault at a mainland station brought most telecommunications traffic and communications on Svalbard to such a complete standstill.

129772.excerpt_en: A little after 2:30 p.m., the telephone lines went quiet and Svalbard residents’ browsers began responding again. Telenor quickly got involved and announced that a fault in Harstad had caused an unexpected problem.
129772.subtitle_en: After four and a half hours isolated from the outside world, telephone and internet connections to Svalbard were restored.

129778.excerpt_en: As soon as the Governor was able to use the telephone again, he took the opportunity. — Since the outage, I have repeatedly been in contact with the central authorities. In my view, this has shown that we need an alternative connection to the mainland, says Odd Olsen Ingerø.
129778.subtitle_en: Governor Odd Olsen Ingerø believes it is unacceptable that emergency services could be put out of action.

129781.excerpt_en: Information manager Per Arild Meling can recall disruptions to the connection with Svalbard, but never on the scale seen on Monday. — We have begun discussions internally and externally with affected parties about what kind of backup we should put in place if this happens again, he says.
129781.subtitle_en: Per Arild Meling has 25 years behind him in the Telenor system. He has never experienced anything similar.
129781.title_en: Did not believe a total outage was possible

Its recommendation to the politicians is to amend the regulations so that developers themselves arrange the construction of roads, water and sewage infrastructure.
129819.subtitle_en: Cost-price construction of roads, water and sewage infrastructure is to be ensured by having businesses build it themselves. They will then hand the facilities over to Longyearbyen Local Council.

129838.excerpt_en: The 23-year-old was born and raised in Moscow, a city of 15 million inhabitants, but in April she found her way to Barentsburg, with a population of around 500. — In my opinion, it is more pleasant here.
129838.subtitle_en: Elena Shmeleva prefers having fewer people around.

129850.excerpt_en: Semb led the marathon from virtually start to finish. For most of the race, Max Sjålin was in second place, while Poland’s Thomas Polanski was third.
129850.subtitle_en: No one could challenge Knut Harald Semb in the Spitsbergen Marathon. But the Gjerpen runner struggled towards the end.

129853.excerpt_en: Head teacher Lene Høgnes Jørgensen is exasperated. Last week, someone tried to smash one of the large windows in the climbing tower at Kullungen Kindergarten.
129853.subtitle_en: Littering and outright vandalism mean that the outdoor areas at Kullungen Kindergarten will, from today, be closed to children and young people without adult supervision in the afternoon and evening.

129862.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Veterinary Institute cannot determine with certainty why the approximately one-year-old female polar bear died. The carcass was found in Petuniabukta on the 7th.
129862.subtitle_en: The female polar bear may have been chased before she had recovered from the anaesthetic, causing her to overheat.
129862.title_en: Overheating killed the female polar bear

129879.excerpt_en: Since current director Knut Harald Holst-Hansen took up the job last autumn, activity has been intense at Spitsbergen Travel AS (Spitra). Expansion plans costing an undisclosed number of millions are already on the table.
129879.subtitle_en: Polarhotellet is to be substantially expanded with 40–50 rooms and a terrace area, Funken will get a spa, and an Aurora centre is planned in Adventdalen. Spitsbergen Travel is preparing to meet the competition in Longyearbyen.

129897.excerpt_en: This spring, the Svalbardposten editorial team has been working on a newcomer aimed at visitors to Longyearbyen. — We are taking a new direction and have created a magazine for people travelling to Svalbard and those interested in the Arctic.
129897.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten’s English-language magazine, Top of the World, will soon be ready for tourists.

129929.excerpt_en: That is roughly the starting point for the programme Innovation Norway is currently running together with the tourism industry in Longyearbyen.
129929.subtitle_en: There is little point in having many guests if they do not pay their way.

129935.excerpt_en: Ongoing vandalism at Kullungen Kindergarten led Longyearbyen Local Council last week to decide to close the kindergarten’s outdoor areas to children and young people in the evenings. Children and young people are not allowed to use the outdoor areas without an accompanying adult. — I think it was absolutely right of the local council to do this.
129935.subtitle_en: The leader of the Longyearbyen Youth Council thinks it is perfectly reasonable for the local council to close the kindergarten when it is plagued by vandalism.
129935.title_en: — It’s only natural to behave properly

129971.subtitle_en: In just a few days, we will launch “Top of the World”, a new English-language magazine about Svalbard and the Arctic.

129980.subtitle_en: The sun is at its highest, but blues enthusiasts in Longyearbyen know that darkness will return—and that means a new edition of Dark Season Blues.
129980.title_en: Sailing into This Year’s Blues Festival

129987.subtitle_en: The story of “Maksim Gorkij” is an important reminder.

130022.excerpt_en: On 19 June, it became known that the company had to halt development work on the first production panel in the margin zone, making the panel 216 metres shorter than planned.
130022.subtitle_en: Store Norske will probably have to carry out additional drilling in Lunckefjell to determine whether there is more waste rock in the coal.

130089.excerpt_en: Mr Editor, you invite readers to comment on the “small” changes you have made to the newspaper’s layout.
130089.subtitle_en: Today’s Svalbardpost exceeds all my ideas of what a future local newspaper could be.

130123.excerpt_en: Police responded after members of the public reported seeing the man get behind the wheel and drive down from Huset early Sunday morning. It was about 3:45 when the car, driven by the older man, was stopped farther down the road along the northwest side of Longyeardalen.
130123.subtitle_en: The driver was more than just tipsy when police stopped him.
130123.title_en: Drove with a Blood-Alcohol Level of 2.4

130131.subtitle_en: The dispute was halted when the parties reached a settlement.

130141.excerpt_en: Over the past 15 years, a solid corps of polar researchers has been built up at several universities in the Czech Republic. Every summer, a group of students and teachers has stayed on Svalbard, and the research has been highly focused.
130141.subtitle_en: The Czech Republic is investing heavily in polar research with a new station in Longyearbyen, a modest field station and strong Arctic expertise.
130141.title_en: The Czechs Make Their Mark in the North

130180.excerpt_en: In Kongsfjorden and out towards Brøggerhalvøya, Kings Bay is now undertaking a major survey of the remnants left by researchers who have departed and abandoned their equipment. Research adviser Sébastien Barrault says they are asking the research stations in Ny-Ålesund to report equipment placed out in the terrain.
130180.subtitle_en: Waste left behind by researchers who fail to clean up has become a problem on Svalbard.

130191.excerpt_en: For the second time, he is presenting his own exhibition on Svalbard. This time it is “Arctic Messages,” featuring themes drawn from Svalbard and treated with considerable artistic freedom.
130191.subtitle_en: “I have been afraid. I have,” says Terje Risberg.

130209.excerpt_en: Svalbard Airport, Longyearbyen Airport—or whatever the airport will eventually be called—is now taking shape. Huge trucks constantly haul fill material, while bulldozers and rollers level and compact it.
130209.subtitle_en: The once peaceful and beautiful tundra west of Hotellneset has been transformed into a dusty, hectic work site.

130223.excerpt_en: The snow is still a metre and a half deep, but the spring sun is blazing against the sheltered wall by the Yellow House. The working day is over and dinner has been eaten in the research village, the world’s northernmost permanent settlement, and the weather is far too good to go indoors on this May day.
130223.subtitle_en: Ny-Ålesund attracts researchers and climate leaders from around the world. The employees of Kings Bay facilitate world-class climate research. And when there is a community workday, everyone turns up. Absolutely everyone.

130234.excerpt_en: Over the past few weeks, the media have brought us several stories about the destination that we would rather have been without. Accusations of social dumping and misleading customers are not what lifts the tourism industry’s summer mood.
130234.subtitle_en: That is where all of us in the tourism industry should focus—and I believe the guest who wrote the reader’s letter thinks so too.

130253.excerpt_en: Forty-seven-year-old Ghylanie Pouseler died after being struck by a chunk of ice when Esmarkbreen calved at the head of Ymerbukta. The tender boat carrying tourists was too close to the glacier when the accident occurred on the 21st.
130253.subtitle_en: Tour operators knew too little about calculating distances to glacier fronts on Svalbard. This is stated in the accident report following the fatal accident in Ymerbukta in August 2012.
130253.title_en: Too Close to the Glacier Front

130293.excerpt_en: Henningsen Transport & Guiding AS (HTG) feels stabbed in the back by the Norwegian authorities. First, the company was given the go-ahead to sail in Svalbard under the NIS flag, making it possible to pay seafarers according to the tariff agreement in their home country as a starting point.
130293.subtitle_en: “This is an extremely difficult case for us, and it is imposing major strains and financial consequences on Svalbard and everyone else involved,” writes Stig Henningsen.

130328.excerpt_en: From the outside, the community centre will probably look the same from autumn onwards, but that is only on the outside. Major changes are taking place inside, except in the cinema, which will remain as it is.
130328.subtitle_en: Huset has always been an important gathering place in Longyearbyen. The plan to renovate it and change its operations therefore attracted considerable attention when it became known. This article was published on 2 July 1977.
130328.title_en: “Exciting Renovation of Huset This Summer—but Unclear Whether Draught Beer and Wine Will Be Available from the Autumn”

130352.excerpt_en: According to Svalbardposten, the first phase involves just over 30 positions, including miners, electricians and mechanics. Most are temporary and will end in August next year.
130352.subtitle_en: Store Norske has barely completed the biggest staff reduction in its history. Now the company must hire more people to meet the schedule and secure sufficient coal.
130352.title_en: Store Norske Now Needs More Workers

130358.excerpt_en: The coal pile at Hotellneset comes from development work in the new mine on Svalbard and is the first Lunckefjell coal to be shipped from Svea. The shipment took place at the end of June, and the coal’s quality will now be tested at the power plant.
130358.subtitle_en: Coal from Lunckefjell provides power and heat in Longyearbyen—and new knowledge for Store Norske.

130364.excerpt_en: The station will accommodate 16 researchers, and a total of 232 packages weighing 210 tonnes will be flown in. The packages total 958 cubic metres; Antonov aircraft carry an average of 60 cubic metres, and construction begins on the 20th.
130364.subtitle_en: When the Danes build a new research station in Greenland, the simplest option is to transport it by air from Longyearbyen.

130382.subtitle_en: The markings on the runways are now changing colour.

130416.excerpt_en: After more than two months of birds staying put on their nests, many have already left the colony between the two dog kennels in Longyearbyen.
130416.subtitle_en: The eider colony by the dog kennels is thinning out as the chicks leave the nests—and because of the foxes.

130453.excerpt_en: The cruise ship “Funchal” docked in Longyearbyen harbour in Svalbard this afternoon. Norovirus has been spreading aboard, prompting the Governor of Svalbard to take a woman by helicopter early today and have her admitted to Longyearbyen Hospital.
130453.subtitle_en: Passengers allowed to go ashore from the “Funchal” may not visit restaurants or have close contact with permanent residents.

130480.excerpt_en: On 4 July, Svalbardposten ran a story about the problems caused by marine litter around Svalbard.
130480.subtitle_en: For two weeks, the Governor of Svalbard has been trying to find the animal.
130480.title_en: Bamse Wanders Around with a Nylon Loop Around His Neck

130488.excerpt_en: While most of us prefer to holiday beneath the sun and warmth of the south—or at least in somewhat better climatic conditions than Svalbard—Rolf Lundgren from Verdal travels as far north as possible.
130488.subtitle_en: It is holiday season. Rolf Lundgren said he chose the silence of the far north when Svalbardposten spoke to him in 1977.

130510.excerpt_en: From time to time, the subject of elderly care in Svalbard has surfaced. Local council leader Christin Kristoffersen (Labour) has given the matter a great deal of thought and believes it is not a good idea.
130510.subtitle_en: The local council leader believes that elderly care as we know it from the mainland would cause the foundations of Svalbard society to disappear.

130513.excerpt_en: The poster is displayed at Svalbard Airport and Tromsø Airport. It attracted attention in May, when the newspaper Nordlys discovered that it did not say anywhere where Mary-Ann’s Polarrigg was located.
130513.subtitle_en: An advertising poster for Mary-Ann’s Polarrigg has been reported to the Norwegian Directorate of Health as illegal alcohol advertising.

130529.excerpt_en: Norovirus was detected aboard the Portuguese cruise ship “Funchal” as early as 7 July.
130529.subtitle_en: Passengers infected with norovirus from the “Funchal” faced restrictions in Longyearbyen and were not allowed to go ashore in Ny-Ålesund at all. “Svalbard’s communities are particularly vulnerable,” says senior consultant Erik Krag Jenssen.

130535.excerpt_en: It is only just over a year since the Liverpool legend last visited the archipelago, invited by Liverbirds Svalbard.
130535.subtitle_en: Phil Neal (63) can thank Bjørge Lillelien for his popularity in Norway. He visited Svalbard once again at the weekend.
130535.title_en: “The Pig” Opened the World Cup Final

130610.subtitle_en: In a few weeks, AECO, the Governor of Svalbard and two cruise operators being considered for cleanup cruises in Svalbard will meet.

130620.excerpt_en: Journalists are not an unusual sight to Svalbard residents. But when they come all the way from Singapore, it is a little special.
130620.subtitle_en: Dave Fox describes Svalbard and Longyearbyen for The Straits Times in Singapore.

130670.excerpt_en: People have been packed into central Longyearbyen like sardines several times this summer. When cruise ships such as the “Costa Pacifica” dock, with capacity for 3,780 passengers, things quickly get crowded in a town that in summer probably has no more than 1,500 permanent residents present.
130670.subtitle_en: Today, you can forget about getting anything “done quickly” in Longyearbyen. For a while, the town’s population increases fivefold.

130685.excerpt_en: In August 1982, Tom Ramberg (62) appeared in Svalbardposten for the first time, as one of several newly appointed teachers at Longyearbyen School. This was the year war broke out in the Falkland Islands, the year Nelson Mandela was released from Robben Island—and, not least, the year Brå broke his pole.
130685.subtitle_en: “I ended up staying in Svalbard for twenty years, partly because I was lazy,” says Tom Ramberg.
130685.tags_en: people, life in Svalbard, back page

130698.excerpt_en: The Longyearbyen School Band came, played and won at the regional festival for junior bands at Hovin in Sør-Trøndelag during the Whitsun weekend. The band not only attracted attention with its two sets of uniforms, but also stole the show during Sunday’s concert.
130698.subtitle_en: School bands have been an important fixture over the years. Longyearbyen School Band also attracted attention when it attended a band festival on the mainland in late summer 1984.

130750.excerpt_en: What makes a man approaching 70 travel to Svalbard during the harshest time of year and then seek shelter in a lonely place deep in Sassenfjorden?
130750.subtitle_en: Trapper Edvin Nøis lays down his walking stick.

130782.excerpt_en: It is the middle of the polar night at Skolteneset, the northernmost point on Sørkappøya. A gale has raged for three days, and the icy wind blows straight through the drafty walls.
130782.subtitle_en: He sits there thinking about his son, about his little feet.
130782.tags_en: object of the month, life in Svalbard, culture

130794.excerpt_en: It was more or less by chance that Gunn Beate Paasche (30) ended up in Svalbard. She was offered the opportunity when she—quite by chance—was on an adventure in Australia four years ago. “I drove around in a car I lived in, taking odd jobs whenever I came across them.”
130794.subtitle_en: Gunn Beathe Paasche never turns down an adventure.

130834.excerpt_en: The cruise season is over. A few ships do remain, admittedly, but the summer season is definitely drawing to a close.

130860.subtitle_en: A man was airlifted after an accident at the Lunckefjell mine early Thursday morning.

130910.excerpt_en: When it became clear last winter that the Norwegian Broadcasting Corporation would introduce television in Longyearbyen from the autumn, and that half a million kroner had been allocated for the purpose in the national budget, the reaction in town was not wholly positive.
130910.subtitle_en: Sunday, 14 September, was a historic day in Svalbard. The first television broadcast went on air. Since then, TV broadcasts have brought nothing but good cheer and joy here.

130922.excerpt_en: Bjørke, pictured here on assignment in a helicopter, began as a temporary replacement at Svalbardposten in May 2013. During this period, many have enjoyed Bjørke’s writing and photographic skills, but he will soon be heading back to the mainland and the newspaper Vårt Land.
130922.subtitle_en: After just over a year and three months, Christian Nicolai Bjørke has finished his temporary post at Svalbardposten.

130932.subtitle_en: Scouts from Drammen jumped into Adventfjorden on Wednesday. On Friday, they are inviting the town’s residents to a campfire in Sjøområdet.

130958.excerpt_en: This spring, Frigga Kruse of the University of Groningen in the Netherlands received support from Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund to research marble extraction on Blomstrandhalvøya from 1910 to 1932.
130958.subtitle_en: Frigga Kruse and Benjamin Koster believe the quality of the marble on Blomstrandhalvøya may be one reason operations were shut down 80 years ago. But there may also be other reasons.

130961.excerpt_en: The ear tag on the female bear was found by the Governor’s office’s rubbish-collection patrol, stuck in a 170-kilogram fishing net. The bear tore off both the ear tag and the net when the Governor’s helicopter came across it and stressed it.
130961.subtitle_en: The polar bear in Sorgfjorden would not have become trapped if not for the ear tag fitted by researchers. Polar bear researcher Jon Aars has never experienced anything similar.

130965.excerpt_en: There are two main reasons for this. One is a shortfall in advertising revenue.
130965.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten posted a deficit of nearly NOK 540,000 last year.

130983.excerpt_en: It stands in Sjøområdet, just outside the centre of Longyearbyen. A substantial structure of rubbish and timber, with “Ocean Hope” flying in red in the wind.
130983.subtitle_en: A cairn made of rubbish warns that humans are in the process of destroying the ocean.

131040.excerpt_en: “It went so-so,” says Solvår Nesbakken Oma, 10. She has just launched her rocket, Flamme, on the football pitch in Longyearbyen.
131040.subtitle_en: This week, 27 children started the school year a week early. On Wednesday, they launched rockets.

131055.excerpt_en: At the end of July, the Governor of Svalbard received a report concerning the Greenpeace ship Esperanza. Today, it is once again suspected of violating the pilotage requirement. “As a matter of routine, we previously reported Esperanza and its captain for violating the pilotage requirement earlier this summer,” says pilotage chief Roy Arne Rotnes of the Norwegian Coastal Administration.

131057.subtitle_en: Svalbard celebrates Norwegian sovereignty over the archipelago.

131090.excerpt_en: The trapping station was put up for sale this summer, with a bidding deadline of 1 July. “Several buyers have come forward, but nothing has been settled yet.”
131090.subtitle_en: According to owner Hans Lund, many have expressed interest in Farmhamna, but the sales process is taking time.

131093.excerpt_en: On the library counter lie the mattresses for the princess and the pea. They will soon be ready to join librarian Karina Bording Halgunset on an adventure.
131093.subtitle_en: Librarian Karina Bording Halgunset has put all her stories in a box. Now she is ready to conjure them up for the town’s children.

131111.excerpt_en: The first students have already begun the autumn semester at UNIS. Six Arctic geophysics students line up beside one of the docks in Småbåthavna.
131111.subtitle_en: New students have arrived at UNIS. Never before have they come from so many different countries.

131141.excerpt_en: First they were allowed to use UNIS, then they had to leave. Now, after two years in the Red Cross’s premises, the nature guides are back at UNIS for good. “Being at the Red Cross worked well, but this is where the programme belongs,” says university lecturer Sigmund Andersen.
131141.subtitle_en: The Arctic Nature Guide programme and lecturer Sigmund Andersen have been welcomed back to UNIS.
131141.tags_en: education, UNIS, news, Arctic nature guide, start of semester

131155.excerpt_en: A man was injured while working at the Lunckefjell mine last Thursday. According to Oddmund Rønning, HSE manager at Store Norske, the man injured seven fingers while installing a track roller.
131155.subtitle_en: A man was injured while working at the Lunckefjell mine last Thursday.

131162.excerpt_en: The captain appeared for questioning at the Governor’s office on Friday and accepted a NOK 50,000 fine for breaches of the Pilotage Act. The Governor’s office reports this on its website. Esperanza first violated the pilotage requirement at the end of July.
131162.subtitle_en: The captain of the Greenpeace ship Esperanza must pay NOK 50,000 for violating the pilotage requirement in Svalbard twice.
131162.tags_en: legal violations, news, Greenpeace, pilotage requirement

131183.excerpt_en: The polar bear, a young male, was first spotted by passers-by on Wednesday evening. The Governor of Svalbard went out during the night to observe the bear’s movements. “The observations are being made to ensure that the polar bear does not move towards the town,” says senior police officer Trond Olsen of the Governor’s office.
131183.subtitle_en: A polar bear has been staying at Revneset for the past day.

131212.excerpt_en: On 1 September, Minister of Trade and Industry Monica Mæland (Conservative) will make her first official visit to Svalbard.
131212.subtitle_en: Now she has the chance to reveal her first budget measure.

131251.excerpt_en: The cableway trestle standing between the hospital and the Business Building is not doing very well. It has begun to rot at the base, in the active layer between the permafrost and the air.
131251.subtitle_en: Three researchers are trying to determine what can be done to prevent wooden foundations from rotting. Laying insulation on the ground could be one solution.

131254.excerpt_en: For the past twelve years, the interdisciplinary Svalex course has been offered to students in fields including geophysics, geology and petroleum studies. The students are introduced to the geological development of the north and the Barents Sea.
131254.subtitle_en: Statoil has withdrawn as a sponsor of Svalex. As a result, the Unis course will be held for the final time.
131254.title_en: Svalex Course to Be Held for the Last Time

131261.excerpt_en: The book about Hopen has been published in a new edition with updated information. It is titled Hopen 2014—Ishavsøy and Meteorological Station. “It is a useful reference work on everything that has happened on Hopen over the years.”
131261.subtitle_en: Life on Hopen has been documented from 1596 right up to the present day.
131261.title_en: New and Old Information About Hopen

131304.excerpt_en: Principal Anne Søvold Vikanes has a luxury problem when she and the school leadership hire new teachers. Around 140 people applied for jobs at Longyearbyen School for the coming academic year, and ten of them can start the school year with new pupils in the coming days.
131304.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen School follows the town’s normal staff turnover.
131304.title_en: One in Four Teachers Is New

131322.excerpt_en: Whales as far as the eye can see in several parts of the Barents Sea—that is the impression capturing the attention of the watch crew aboard KV Nordkapp. Many whales, both in number and species, can be spotted by watching their blows on the horizon.
131322.subtitle_en: KV Nordkapp encounters plenty of whales.
131322.tags_en: letters to the editor, opinions, reader submission
131322.title_en: Whale Blows as Far as the Eye Can See

131338.excerpt_en: We are crossing Holtedahlfonna on our way to Ny-Ålesund when a sled breaks at a weld, so we have to stop and improvise—this is no place to settle in. Powerful and striking impressions.
131338.tags_en: reader contribution, opinion, letter to the editor

131345.excerpt_en: At the end of July, the Norwegian Coastal Administration reported the Greenpeace ship Esperanza for violating the Pilotage Act. Last Friday, the ship was reported again.
131345.subtitle_en: The Greenpeace ship Esperanza violated the pilotage requirement twice. The captain was fined NOK 50,000.
131345.title_en: Greenpeace Fined for Sailing Without a Pilot

131386.excerpt_en: At 3 p.m. on Friday, the young male polar bear once again entered the cabin belonging to Anders Ringheim at Revneset, after wrecking it while searching for food two days earlier.
131386.subtitle_en: On Friday afternoon, the polar bear once again entered a cabin at Revneset. The Governor of Svalbard has now driven the bear away from Longyearbyen.

131406.excerpt_en: It stands just as firm as it did 114 years ago. A 4.36-metre-high cairn that helps tell the story of the greatest research expedition in Svalbard’s history.
131406.subtitle_en: The cairn on Černyševfjellet was one of the keys to solving the mystery of the shape of the Earth.

131460.excerpt_en: The start of the school year is just around the corner, and the media are busy warning about the annual lice infestation that invades kindergartens and schools when children return after the holidays. We are therefore encouraged to dig out the nit comb.
131460.subtitle_en: Our modern plastic nit comb is an exact replica of the “lice combs” found in archaeological excavations dating from the Bronze Age, through the Iron Age and Viking Age, and right up to the present day.

131478.excerpt_en: This week, the board of Store Norske held its first regular meeting after it became known that Per Andersson is stepping down as managing director. The most important item was also the appointment of a new managing director, but neither employee representatives nor board chair Annette Malm Justad want to say anything about the process.
131478.subtitle_en: The board of Store Norske has begun the search for a new managing director.
131478.title_en: Keeping Quiet About the Search for a New Boss

131503.excerpt_en: Following the reorganization of Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) in January this year, the kindergarten regulations must be amended. In addition to the change in ownership of the kindergartens, the administration has proposed, among other things, requiring children to take three consecutive weeks of holiday during the school summer break.
131503.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council wants to require parents to give their children three consecutive weeks of holiday from kindergarten in the summer. Politicians are skeptical.
131503.title_en: Could Be Ordered to Take Summer Leave

131540.excerpt_en: Stefan Nordlie has brought Hiorthfjellet into the climbing wall at Svalbardhallen. Two weeks ago, he finished the final brushstroke. “My painting style is fierce and aggressive.”
131540.subtitle_en: You no longer have to cross Adventfjorden to reach the summit of Hiorthfjellet.

131568.excerpt_en: Last weekend, several days after the polar bear had arrived in the area, quite a few boats headed out onto Adventfjorden to get a closer look. The bear was clearly curious about its surroundings and took the presence of people completely calmly.
131568.subtitle_en: Many people had a rare opportunity to see a polar bear. But for a while, the Governor of Svalbard considered whether onlookers had got too close.

131589.excerpt_en: At around 11 a.m. on Friday, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that a polar bear had once again been spotted in Hiorthhamn. “We went to take a look at the bear. It reacted to the helicopter noise and was led up into Mälardalen.”
131589.subtitle_en: A polar bear was spotted in Hiorthhamn on Friday morning. Later that day, the Governor of Svalbard herded it into Mälardalen by helicopter.

131600.excerpt_en: It has been 18 years since a Russian Tupolev 154M aircraft operated by Moscow’s Vnukovo Airlines crashed into Operafjellet while approaching Svalbard Airport, Longyear. All 141 people on board were killed in what was the worst aviation accident on Norwegian soil.
131600.subtitle_en: On Friday, the Governor of Svalbard took part in the annual memorial ceremony for the plane crash on Operafjellet.

131608.excerpt_en: The polar bear was observed in Adventdalen on Friday, but disappeared before turning up again today. On Saturday morning, it was observed heading east through Adventdalen, in the area between Helvetiafjellet and Halwylfjellet.
131608.subtitle_en: The polar bear that has been down in Adventdalen is moving away from the settlement. On Saturday afternoon, it took a lunch break at Janssonhaugen.

131659.excerpt_en: “I called home: ‘Mum! We’ve seen blue whales!’” says Sylvi Lundgren, studying the photographs.
131659.subtitle_en: For two hours, Frank Bakken and Sylvi Lundgren followed the giants in Isfjorden. There have been more blue whales around Svalbard.

131661.excerpt_en: He has returned several times since then. Roald worked in Svalbard from 1954 to 1956, first in the mess hall and later at the loading facility at Hotellneset, where one of his duties was operating the weighbridge. “It was a great job, really pleasant down there on the quay.”
131661.subtitle_en: Many people talk about the Svalbard bug. For Roald Westerbotn, it came back to life during a visit in 2007.

131663.excerpt_en: A tired but happy Natalia Shmatova and Timofey Rogozhin—respectively the head of cultural projects and the deputy director of tourism—meet us after the final concert. From 28 August to 1
131663.subtitle_en: The Grumant Festival became a five-day musical journey. It concluded in Longyearbyen on Monday evening.
131663.title_en: Reaching the Finish Line with a Musical Journey

131681.excerpt_en: When places were allocated in May, it appeared that Longyearbyen’s three kindergartens would have a total of five vacancies. During the summer, several withdrawals have been received.
131681.subtitle_en: The kindergartens need two fewer groups than expected, but all kindergarten employees will keep their jobs.

131699.excerpt_en: “It has been an exhausting summer with many worries,” says Katja Will. Together with Lisa Heigl and owner Michelle van Dijk, she has run Longyearbyen Camping this summer. “We have many ‘cheap’ guests who end up at the campsite.”
131699.subtitle_en: In recent years, the campsite has received many guests without tents, sleeping bags or an understanding of the polar-bear danger.

131722.excerpt_en: On 29 August, work began on laying the fibre-optic cable, which will connect the new geodetic station with the rest of the world, on the seabed.
131722.subtitle_en: “Cable Innovator” has recently laid a cable from Longyearbyen to Ny-Ålesund. Only two vessels of this type exist in the world.

131750.excerpt_en: “It is important that this business plan is created by those who live and work here on Svalbard.”
131750.subtitle_en: Minister of Trade and Industry Monica Mæland (Conservative Party) promises that the Strategic Business Plan for Svalbard will not be left in a drawer.
131750.title_en: Mæland wants to join the team

131752.excerpt_en: “It’s not really a great achievement. Willem Barents did it before us many years ago,” Håvard Tjora says with a laugh.
131752.subtitle_en: They knew little about sailing. Nevertheless, they decided to sail from Tromsø to Longyearbyen in August.

131775.excerpt_en: “There are some reindeer over there. Can we shoot them now?” one of the toddlers asked while standing by the car on the road. “No.”
131775.subtitle_en: The children put on hearing protection as soon as they got out of the car. Ten minutes later, the hunters had scored two direct hits.

131847.excerpt_en: On Sunday, the Governor was notified about a Russian fisherman who had fallen ill aboard a trawler located approximately 150 nautical miles east of Hopen. It was a long journey for the rescue crew. “The helicopter first flew to Hopen to refuel.”
131847.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen rescue helicopter was far east of Hopen last night to pick up a sick fisherman.

131861.excerpt_en: “Many of you are heavily dependent on polar stories,” Per Kyrre Reymert declared before, after the laughter in the room, beginning to read aloud selected texts written by Odd Lønø. Over many years, Lønø has written extensively about overwintering trapping on Svalbard and Jan Mayen.
131861.subtitle_en: At last, Odd Lønø’s texts have been collected between two covers.

131872.excerpt_en: It has been only five months since Anundsen last visited Svalbard. Among other things, he officially opened the new helicopter hangar at the airport during that visit.
131872.subtitle_en: Minister of Justice and Public Security Anders Anundsen (Progress Party) is coming to Svalbard next week. The new Governor’s boat will then be christened.
131872.tags_en: news, Governor’s boat, Minister of Justice and Public Security

131897.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen today has a high level of research and development activity (R&D). Ny-Ålesund and Longyearbyen are home to an internationally leading research community focused on Arctic climate, environmental and technology research.
131897.subtitle_en: For the first time in history, local residents can now take the introductory part of an engineering degree here in Longyearbyen.

131912.excerpt_en: “We can see that we are now hitting the ceiling with the capacity we have. For long periods, there is simply no more to be gained,” says tourism director Ronny Brunvoll.
131912.subtitle_en: There were about as many guests as the accommodation businesses were able to handle in July.

131926.excerpt_en: “Now the task is to work concretely, creatively and action-oriented on the action plan,” says Trine Krystad, who leads the “Sustainable Destination” project. In addition to meeting the criteria set by Innovation Norway, its content reflects what the tourism industry itself has determined it wants to focus on, she explains.
131926.subtitle_en: The groundwork has been approved. During the coming year, tourism on Svalbard is to become sustainable.

131936.excerpt_en: The rain fell lightly, but did nothing to dampen the mood as the starting signal sounded, the first paddle strokes were taken and the 20 kayaks picked up speed on the water outside the sailing association’s clubhouse.
131936.subtitle_en: Twenty teams and individuals faced off in the annual competition organised by Svalbard Sailing Association.
131936.title_en: Fresh strokes in the test of strength

131945.excerpt_en: It weighs more than 7,000 tonnes, costs over NOK 300 million and was originally purchased for the new Lunckefjell mine. Because of the coal crisis, Store Norske instead decided to deploy it at Svea Nord, where it will extract a 1.2-kilometre-long coal panel at the back of the mine.
131945.subtitle_en: In April, Store Norske will begin coal production in Svea with a brand-new longwall shearer.
131945.title_en: The new shearer is being assembled

131981.excerpt_en: At the beginning of August, Solveig Egeland’s rubbish hut was completed in Sjøområdet. Rubbish from the Governor’s clean-up cruises was used to build an artwork warning that rubbish is in the process of destroying the ocean.
131981.subtitle_en: The art hut in Sjøområdet must be removed by 1 October. The artist will take it down unless someone wants to take it over.
131981.title_en: It becomes rubbish if no one wants it

131984.excerpt_en: “2013 was a good year, and this year looks set to be at least as good for Spitsbergen Travel,” says a pleased managing director, Knut Harald Holst-Hansen.
131984.subtitle_en: With a pre-tax profit of NOK 15 million last year, Spitsbergen Travel AS has enough to live on.

132019.excerpt_en: “I was probably a little crazy when I moved here with my partner two and a half years ago. I didn’t have a job, after all.”
132019.subtitle_en: Jan Sivert Hauglid (53) quit his job to move to the photographic paradise of Svalbard.
132019.tags_en: people, life on Svalbard, back page

132048.excerpt_en: The nine, all young Belgians, had set out on a several-day trek starting from Isfjord Radio. Their route had taken them south towards Van Mijenfjorden.
132048.subtitle_en: Nine Belgian hikers found themselves in an impossible situation while hiking in bad weather in Ytterdalen on Svalbard.

132057.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Coast Guard notified the Governor of Svalbard on Sunday morning that a vessel carrying heavy fuel oil was in Recherchefjorden, south of Bellsund at the entrance to Van Keulenfjorden. The area is part of Sør-Spitsbergen National Park, where ships carrying heavy fuel oil are prohibited from sailing.
132057.subtitle_en: A ship has been issued a fine after violating the ban on heavy fuel oil in Sør-Spitsbergen National Park.

132080.excerpt_en: Spitsbergen Travel AS and Hurtigruten ASA want to further strengthen their position on Svalbard. They have now chartered the old Hurtigruten ship MS “Nordstjernen” for three months next year. “The ship is being hired for the whole of June, July and August.”
132080.subtitle_en: Next year, the venerable MS “Nordstjernen” will once again sail around Svalbard.

132093.excerpt_en: The tusk has been removed from a skeleton near Rubypynten in Recherchefjorden. “We were there on the round trip on Saturday, September 6.”
132093.subtitle_en: When the Governor went to collect a narwhal skeleton for Svalbard Museum, the tusk was gone. The Governor has now opened a criminal case.
132093.tags_en: skeleton, nature and environment, whale, theft, news

132096.excerpt_en: The Governor’s brand-new service vessel arrived in Longyearbyen on Thursday, several months behind schedule. “Polarsyssel” will be christened at Gammelkaia on Saturday morning by former Governor’s Office lawyer Inger Aarvag Stokke, with Justice Minister Anders Anundsen in attendance. The boat was built at the Havyard shipyard in Sogn for the shipping company Remøy Management AS.
132096.subtitle_en: At 1:37 p.m. on Thursday, “Polarsyssel” docked in Longyearbyen for the first time. Its arrival was marked by a blast of the horn and a large crowd of spectators.

132120.excerpt_en: In July, there were approximately as many overnight stays on Svalbard as the accommodation providers had capacity to handle. The figures from Visit Svalbard, the umbrella organization for tourism businesses, cover everything from hotels to campsites.
132120.subtitle_en: “The experiences and impressions belong to the tourists.”

132171.excerpt_en: The photographers were divided into two groups and set off in opposite directions along a route with checkpoints. One of the places where the most photographs were taken was Sjøområdet.
132171.subtitle_en: Fifteen enthusiastic amateur photographers searched high and low in Longyearbyen.

132194.excerpt_en: Upgraded, protected by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage and with a new owner, “Nordstjernen” will return to Longyearbyen next summer. In August 2012, the old lady sailed out of Adventfjorden for what was supposed to be the last time.
132194.subtitle_en: The old lady will once again cruise the northwest coast of Spitsbergen in summer.

132202.excerpt_en: This year’s TV fundraiser supports Kirkens Nødhjelp, which will provide people in parts of Africa and Asia with clean water and safe sanitation. “Some of us who have lived in Longyearbyen for a long time know how important clean water is.”
132202.subtitle_en: This year’s TV fundraiser kicks off with a relay tomorrow. The proceeds will provide clean water—something this year’s campaign committee knows the importance of.

132219.excerpt_en: After a ten-week expedition around Svalbard, the Norwegian Mapping Authority’s vessel “Hydrograf” is moored in Longyearbyen on this second Wednesday in September. For the past five weeks, hydrographer Glenn Maan has been part of the crew. “We have mostly been in Hinlopen Strait, Dicksonfjorden and Ekmanfjorden,” he says.
132219.subtitle_en: This year, two new survey vessels mapped what lies beneath the surface in Svalbard’s fjords. They found several new, treacherous shoals.

132229.excerpt_en: The Governor is currently working on a new management plan for West Svalbard (see the next article). This summer, working groups representing tourism, research and education, and local residents have contributed input to the planning process. “This is an important recreational area, and it is important to retain the opportunity to experience nature there.”
132229.subtitle_en: The national parks in the west are important to researchers, tourism operators and locals alike. With a new management plan, many fear it will become harder to travel there.
132229.tags_en: nature and environment, news, management plan
132229.title_en: Fears of tighter restrictions in the west

132242.excerpt_en: Work has begun on a management plan for the national parks and bird reserves in West Spitsbergen. The Governor aims to draft a new plan over the next six months.
132242.subtitle_en: The Governor is mapping how the national parks in West Svalbard are used.

132254.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, we showed a picture of Alfred Thiefenthal with his plane, a Jodel 180. Here, the pilot is pictured on a trip from Adventdalen to Svea in May 1974, photographed by Herleiv Alvheim.
132254.tags_en: historical photo, life on Svalbard, history

132272.excerpt_en: See the photo gallery on the right! The new Governor’s vessel has eight decks in all, including the engine room.
132272.subtitle_en: “Polarsyssel” docked in Longyearbyen on Thursday. Now you can join a tour of the ship.

132308.excerpt_en: With a helicopter on deck, men’s-choir singing, speeches of thanks and spectators both young and old, “Polarsyssel” was christened on Saturday. The godmother was former Governor’s Office lawyer Inger Aarvaag Stokke, who during her term worked extensively to secure a new boat for the Governor.
132308.subtitle_en: The champagne bottle shattered on the first attempt when godmother Inger Aarvaag Stokke christened the Governor’s new service vessel.

132312.excerpt_en: Gruve 7’s Joachim Myhrvang put in a tremendous sprint on the fifth and final leg, despite being alone in the finish area. “We tried to match KSAT’s winning time from last year,” he said. But they did not manage it.
132312.subtitle_en: Ten teams took part in this year’s relay in aid of the annual TV fundraiser. Gruve 7 crossed the finish line first.
132312.title_en: Full speed through the town center

132321.excerpt_en: For several years, China has worked to have a third antenna built at the Eiscat Svalbard Radar at Breinosa in Adventdalen. Now the Ministry of Education and Research is putting its foot down. “The purpose of the facility is to conduct research in space.”
132321.subtitle_en: China will not be allowed to build a third antenna at the Eiscat facility.

132327.excerpt_en: “No one has offered to take over the hut. I have agreed with the waste facility that they will help me take it down,” says Egeland.
132327.subtitle_en: No one wants to take over the garbage hut in Sjøområdet. Next week, artist Solveig Egeland will come to dismantle it.
132327.tags_en: news, garbage hut, art, nature and environment
132327.title_en: The hut will be removed next week

132347.excerpt_en: Since the opening of the new Svalbard Museum, the rifle with the jammed cartridge has told a dramatic story from its display case.
132347.subtitle_en: A jammed cartridge is not enough. New requirements mean Svalbard Museum may have to remove the rifle from its exhibition.
132347.title_en: A historic rifle faces an uncertain fate

132366.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Mapping Authority recently completed this year’s survey around Svalbard. During several hectic weeks, the “Hydrograf” carried out charting in Hinlopen Strait, Dicksonfjorden and Ekmanfjorden, as well as in the area from Hornsund to Sørkapp.
132366.subtitle_en: Standing on the bridge this summer has been an eye-opener.

132385.excerpt_en: “May good luck and fortune follow you in all waters,” godmother Inger Aarvaag Stokke said to “Polarsyssel” before the boat was christened in champagne on Saturday. The boat is currently the latest element in strengthening emergency preparedness on Svalbard.
132385.subtitle_en: First, “Polarsyssel” passed her baptism of fire in a storm from the mainland to Longyearbyen. Then she was christened in champagne and celebrated as a strengthening of emergency preparedness.

132392.excerpt_en: “Today is a day of joy. We now have new helicopters, a new hangar and a new boat.”
132392.subtitle_en: Svalbard Minister Anders Anundsen (Progress Party) is pleased with the improvements made to emergency preparedness, but still has more work to do.
132392.tags_en: news, Polarsyssel, Minister of Justice and Public Security, christening, minister

132412.excerpt_en: “After the war, operation of the Governor’s vessel was taken over by the Norwegian Society for Sea Rescue, now known as the Norwegian Red Cross at Sea. For the rest of the year, the boats operated as rescue vessels.”
132412.subtitle_en: The Governor’s boats have always been important on Svalbard. Even so, the records of which boats served the Governor are incomplete.

132416.excerpt_en: “We are looking for patients,” says Sigvart Bjøntegaard in the finish area of the TV campaign relay outside Svalbardbutikken. Equipped with a white coat, mask and an extra backbone, the hired doctor is ready for action.
132416.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Hospital did its best to find sick and injured people on Saturday.

132450.excerpt_en: Last year, the University Centre in Svalbard (UNIS) and the Institute of Marine Research (IMR) launched a new collaboration through the course “Ecosystem Based Management of Arctic Marine Systems”—ecosystem-based management of marine systems in the Arctic.

132472.excerpt_en: Tanaværing Stein Tore Pedersen (42) sits down at the office in the large workshop at Henningsen Transport & Guiding. So far today, he has taken out two taillights and punctured a rubber boat with the forklift.
132472.subtitle_en: Stein Tore Pedersen may have landed his first job on Svalbard because he is exceptionally good with carburetors.
132472.tags_en: man, life on Svalbard, back page, people

132496.excerpt_en: The snow has barely settled, and we assume many mushers are looking forward to their first trip with a sled team. Today, mushers are in good company, but in 1974 there were not many people to go on trips with.
132496.tags_en: historical photo, life on Svalbard, history

132538.excerpt_en: New figures from Statistics Norway (SSB) show that 2,562 residents were registered on Svalbard on 1 July this year.
132538.subtitle_en: During the first six months of the year, Svalbard’s population grew by 16. Foreign nationals account for the entire increase.

132550.excerpt_en: Station manager Sølvi Jacobsen at SAS Ground Handling says there were no landing conditions at the airport on Thursday afternoon. Before SAS can consider returning to Longyearbyen, it needs favourable weather reports from the meteorologists. “Then SAS has to see what crew and aircraft it can get hold of to come back up.”
132550.subtitle_en: The aircraft had to return to Tromsø because of fog. Friday’s edition of Svalbardposten may therefore be delayed, and tonight’s book event with Arne O. Holm will miss the launch of the book about Robert Hermansen.

132560.excerpt_en: “This is tough and absolutely authentic! It has not been sanitised or dressed up.”
132560.subtitle_en: Mine 3 could become one of Svalbard’s most important tourist attractions, experts in sustainability and the experience economy believe. But the retail sector must be part of the effort.
132560.title_en: A Coal Mine Could Become a Gold Mine

132566.excerpt_en: The Office of the Auditor General has examined how society’s investments in research are utilised and how Norwegian research performs in the broader picture. Norway invests in research to acquire knowledge about nature and the world we live in, enabling the development of modern, sustainable societies for the future.
132566.subtitle_en: Norwegian research on Svalbard is better and more extensive than the Office of the Auditor General’s report suggests.
132566.tags_en: reader’s letter, opinion piece, research, opinions
132566.title_en: More Research Than the Auditor General Thinks

132569.excerpt_en: This week saw the launch of the book “Røde Robert Hermansen – Redningsmann og syndebukk” (“Red Robert Hermansen – Rescuer and Scapegoat”). Written by Otto Ulseth, the book covers Hermansen’s life, from his rise at Store Norske to the downfall that ended with the former coal company director serving two years in prison.
132569.subtitle_en: It is about the battle over one’s legacy.

132607.excerpt_en: Pål Skaare sent us this picture of “Nordsyssel”, taken on a summer day in 1974. This was the first “Nordsyssel”, and the name later became one of two traditional names for the service vessels.
132607.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s ships have received extensive coverage in the newspaper recently in connection with the christening of a new vessel.
132607.tags_en: historical picture, life in Svalbard, history

132615.excerpt_en: Their eyes follow him attentively. Their ears stand alert, and their tails begin wagging every time he approaches the kennels.
132615.subtitle_en: Things quickly snowball when you start keeping dogs. Just ask Steinar.
132615.title_en: A Dog’s Life in the Valley

132629.excerpt_en: Few people showed up to say goodbye to the garbage hut in Sjøområdet on Tuesday evening. This was supposed to be its final day before the hut was dismantled and thrown away at the waste facility.
132629.subtitle_en: A group of locals wants to take over the garbage hut. The artist is now leaving it in place for another week, hoping it will not end up at the waste facility after all.
132629.tags_en: news, artist, garbage hut, nature and environment
132629.title_en: New Hope for the Garbage Hut

132634.excerpt_en: It is Tuesday morning, and fresh snow has laid a thin blanket over the ground. Astrid Meek, senior development adviser at the Longyearbyen Community Council, is in Sjøområdet looking for footprints in the snow.
132634.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen Community Council is checking that no one is living in boathouses that have not been approved as holiday homes.
132634.title_en: Checking Whether the Squatters Are Out

132651.excerpt_en: There is now almost no more room to build in Longyearbyen. New issues have also emerged, leading the Longyearbyen Community Council to conclude that the land-use plan must be updated. “There is a lot that needs to be reviewed.”
132651.subtitle_en: Next year, the land-use plan for Longyearbyen will be updated. It could make room for a new harbour area, a new ski slope and new commercial zones.
132651.title_en: Drawing Up a New Plan for the Town

132657.excerpt_en: Signs advertising a closing-down sale and 70 per cent discounts now draw attention away from the mannequins at Barents Fashion AS. After just over a year under new owners and with a new name, the clothing store at Lompensenteret has gone bankrupt.
132657.subtitle_en: Last spring, Barents Fashion took over Motekroken at Lompensenteret. Now the clothing store is closing down. Frost is also reporting losses.

132673.excerpt_en: In an email to G Adventures and the Governor of Svalbard, Reschner writes that two of the company’s wildlife specialists allegedly barked and grunted loudly at three walruses in the water.
132673.subtitle_en: Kate Reschner was on a cruise with G Adventures aboard the MS “Expedition” when two wildlife specialists entered the water and disturbed walruses to create a good photo opportunity.

132694.excerpt_en: In a report, the Office of the Auditor General concludes that Norwegian research investments in the Arctic can and should be better utilised. UNIS director Ole Arve Misund agrees with many of the conclusions, but is not entirely happy that UNIS and Svalbard Research Park were not included in the assessment.
132694.subtitle_en: The Office of the Auditor General concludes that Norwegian investments in the Arctic should be better utilised. But UNIS and Svalbard Research Park are not counted as “investments.”

132710.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten has therefore not been delivered to customers or points of sale, but will arrive on a Friday afternoon flight. “This is highly regrettable, but there is nothing we can do about the weather. We will deliver the newspaper to our customers and points of sale as soon as possible,” says editor Eirik Palm.
132710.subtitle_en: The paper was due to arrive on the SAS flight on Thursday, but the aircraft had to return to Tromsø because of fog in Longyearbyen.

132757.excerpt_en: On Friday, Kings Bay handed over the road to Brandalslaguna, where the new geodetic station will be built. On Saturday, the foundation stone—or rather, the foundation pile—was driven into the ground. Minister of Local Government and Modernisation Jan Tore Sanner (Conservative) conducted the ceremony. —Strengthens Norway’s position—“This strengthens Norway’s position in the High North.”
132757.subtitle_en: The first pile for the Norwegian Mapping Authority’s new Earth observatory was driven into the ground on Saturday.
132757.tags_en: Norwegian Mapping Authority, Earth observatory, Ny-Ålesund, news, Svalbard, geodesy

132763.excerpt_en: “It has been fantastic so far,” says campaign leader Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik. More than NOK 85,000 was raised at a flea market over the weekend, while Polarflokken Kindergarten brought in just over NOK 16,500 by serving reindeer dinner and selling art and raffle tickets last week.
132763.subtitle_en: The TV campaign in Longyearbyen has already raised more than NOK 100,000.

132765.excerpt_en: The polar bear has visited Pyramiden for several days, wandering through the streets. Repeated attempts have been made to scare the bear away, and the Governor has been called to the Russian settlement.
132765.subtitle_en: A polar bear has visited Pyramiden for several days running. In the early hours of Monday, it took a trip into the hotel bar.

132785.excerpt_en: Two equivalent helicopters, a hangar, a new boat and more staff for the Governor, as well as funding for a treatment plant at the power station, were among the things Svalbard received extra funds for in the 2014 national budget. These projects are fully funded this year, and the Svalbard budget for 2015 has been reduced.
132785.subtitle_en: While the government allowed money to rain down on Svalbard last year, this year’s budget is more restrained.

132795.excerpt_en: The government was well aware that Kings Bay needed to build a new research building for the Japanese researchers in Ny-Ålesund. They currently occupy an old hut far from the other buildings, and the state-owned company is expected to construct a new one.
132795.subtitle_en: Japanese researchers must continue to make do in a draughty old hut.
132795.tags_en: research, national budget, Ny-Ålesund, Kings Bay, news
132795.title_en: No Support for New Research Stations

132798.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Culture proposes granting Kunsthall Svalbard NOK 2.5 million in start-up funding. “Our ambition is for Kunsthall Svalbard to be a venue for high-level international contemporary art,” says director Knut Ljøgodt in a press release.
132798.subtitle_en: The Northern Norwegian Art Museum has received support to establish a branch in Longyearbyen. The art will be in place as early as this autumn and exhibited at Svalbard Museum.
132798.title_en: Svalbard to Get an Art Hall

132822.excerpt_en: The weekend flea market raised around NOK 85,000 for the Telethon. Items worth NOK 70,000 were sold, along with Thai food for NOK 15,000. “That is a record of another world.”
132822.subtitle_en: Many people were pleased with the bargains they picked up at the weekend. In total, items worth more than NOK 70,000 were bought. That is a new record.

132825.excerpt_en: “Signatur” is the title of Olaf Storø’s substantial book, which will be officially launched on 5 November at Huset.
132825.subtitle_en: Olaf Storø has worked on Svalbard for 25 years. To mark the occasion, he is publishing his first book.
132825.title_en: Filling in the Blanks Between the Lines

132829.excerpt_en: “Red Robert Hermansen: Saviour and Scapegoat” is the title of Otto Ulseth’s unauthorised biography of the former director of Store Norske.
132829.subtitle_en: Emotions ran high when Robert Hermansen took part in the launch of Otto Ulseth’s book about the former Store Norske chief executive.

132850.excerpt_en: Tveit arrived in Longyearbyen in September with her husband and three children aged 2, 8 and 12. She comes from the position of director at Petter Stordalen’s Quality Hotel Leangkollen in Asker, where she worked for four years.
132850.subtitle_en: Anne-Margrethe Tveit (41) will run Spitsbergen Travel’s hotel operations.
132850.title_en: New Hotel Manager Takes Up Post

132874.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) has now begun a major cleanup process in Sjøområdet. In addition to private boathouses being rented out illegally, commercial operators are also renting boathouses to tourists.
132874.subtitle_en: Svalbard Villmarkssenter rents out a holiday home in Sjøområdet to tourists. It is not allowed to do so.

132888.excerpt_en: Local elections will be held on Svalbard at the beginning of October next year. What the local council will look like after the election is a very open question, as none of the current group leaders knows whether they will stand for election.
132888.subtitle_en: Deputy leader of Longyearbyen Local Council, Geir Hekne (H), is leaving local politics. Council leader Christin Kristoffersen (Ap) has not decided whether she will continue.
132888.title_en: Hekne Is Stepping Down Next Year

132912.excerpt_en: Robert Hermansen came home to his own people when he took the stage at the cultural centre on Thursday last week. And he had the audience in the palm of his hand.
132912.subtitle_en: The pride is still there, and emotions are running high.

132932.excerpt_en: On 2 September, the Russian government approved a permanent research centre in Barentsburg with up to 100 employees.
132932.subtitle_en: The research centre in Barentsburg is unlikely to become a competitor to Ny-Ålesund, a Russia expert believes. And the coal in Colesbukta will probably remain there for good.
132932.title_en: Russia Expected to Turn Its Back on Coal

132938.excerpt_en: Relations between Russia and Western countries have been strained since the country annexed parts of the Crimean Peninsula earlier this year, and Western sanctions have been met with reactions in the East.
132938.subtitle_en: While relations between Russia and the West have cooled, it is business as usual at UNIS.
132938.title_en: One in Four Students Here Is from Russia

132942.excerpt_en: In addition, a Spaniard is in the process of ending her stay on Svalbard. Susana Garcia Espada, who comes from Madrid, was packing up when the foundation stone was laid at Brandalslaguna, a couple of kilometres beyond today’s observatory.
132942.subtitle_en: A German, an Australian, an American and a Norwegian make up the staff at the Earth observation facility in Ny-Ålesund.
132942.tags_en: news, Ny-Ålesund, Norwegian Mapping Authority, Earth observation facility, geodesy, Svalbard
132942.title_en: Brought Together from All Corners of the World

132953.excerpt_en: “This is a day I have been waiting for for seven years. I’m so moved I could cry!”
132953.subtitle_en: Ny-Ålesund has contact with celestial bodies up to 12 billion light-years away. The new Earth observation facility will make navigation and climate research even more precise.
132953.tags_en: news, Earth observation facility, Norwegian Mapping Authority, Svalbard, Ny-Ålesund, geodesy

132974.excerpt_en: This year, money from the Telethon will give one million people lasting access to clean water. Norwegian Church Aid will carry out water projects in Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia, Tanzania, Afghanistan, Pakistan and Haiti.
132974.subtitle_en: Polarflokken kindergarten has raised NOK 17,250 for this year’s Telethon.

132983.excerpt_en: Some time ago, we showed a picture of Kjell Lavik with his dog team heading up Adventdalen. Here he is again with his team in Longyeardalen.

133058.excerpt_en: Just before 8 a.m. on Sunday, the Governor was notified of a polar bear near Longyearbyen. “The bear was on the east side of Isdammen. Signal shots were fired, to which the bear responded, and it then headed towards Hiorthhamn,” says Senior Police Officer Arild Lyssand.
133058.subtitle_en: The Governor responded when a polar bear came close to Longyearbyen on Sunday morning.

133061.excerpt_en: It was around 8:30 p.m. on Sunday that the object appeared in the sky west/northwest of Longyearbyen. The meteor was travelling north/northeast when it was observed over Isfjorden for several seconds before disappearing behind Hiorthfjellet, apparently leaving a long tail of fire behind it.
133061.subtitle_en: Several people on Svalbard got a surprise on Sunday evening when this object came streaking across the sky.
133061.tags_en: Northern Lights Observatory, news, Longyearbyen, meteor
133061.title_en: Set Out to Photograph the Northern Lights…

133073.excerpt_en: The Governor was notified about the bear just before 7:30 a.m. on Wednesday. “We encountered it by the dog yard, fired noise shots at it and guided it towards Hiorthhamn.”
133073.subtitle_en: Fresh bear tracks were found in the snow outside one of the apartment buildings in Road 238 on Wednesday morning.
133073.title_en: Polar Bear Right Up Against the House

133078.excerpt_en: There has been considerable discussion about what exactly appeared in the sky northwest of Longyearbyen shortly after 8:30 p.m. on Sunday. On Tuesday, Svalbardposten wrote about Omid Abolhasani, who photographed the object as it passed across the sky.
133078.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Meteor Network believes it may have been the remains of an old Soviet rocket.
133078.title_en: Omid Thinks He Saw Space Junk

133090.excerpt_en: “Two tranquilizer darts were fired at the bear at 12:15. It moved further into the valley, and we fired a couple more shots until the bear fell asleep by the old northern-lights station.”
133090.subtitle_en: On Thursday afternoon, the Governor of Svalbard and the Norwegian Polar Institute succeeded in anaesthetizing the polar bear that had been staying near Longyearbyen. It is now being flown away by helicopter.
133090.tags_en: Svalbard, polar bear, Governor of Svalbard, news

133118.excerpt_en: We have previously written about prominent Conservative politicians who thought the Red-Green government’s investment in, among other things, Svalbard’s power plant was rather feeble. In 2012, Nicolai Astrup stated that “everything is in place for a new and modern coal-fired power plant with full carbon capture.”
133118.subtitle_en: One can only hope that Longyearbyen is first in line when Norway builds its first carbon-capture plant.
133118.tags_en: opinions, editorial, climate, power plant, environment

133157.excerpt_en: To ensure access to housing and thereby support recruitment, the state has a special arrangement involving a housing pool for state, municipal and private organizations. Statsbygg has argued that Avinor, as a limited company, does not fall under this scheme.
133157.subtitle_en: Statsbygg is obliged to provide housing for Avinor, despite it being a state-owned limited company. The Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation has made this clear.

133164.excerpt_en: “This is something we have worked on continuously. Everyone is in the service industry,” says Avinor manager Morten Ulsnes in Svalbard.
133164.subtitle_en: Air passengers travelling to and from Svalbard are among the most satisfied, if the survey conducted at European airports is anything to go by.

133175.excerpt_en: Early Wednesday morning, Ingvild Sæbu Vatn received a message from a neighbour saying there were polar-bear tracks just outside their house at Vei 238-23b. She lives on the first floor.
133175.subtitle_en: On Wednesday morning, a polar bear wandered right up to the walls of a house on Road 238. Polar-bear researcher Jon Aars believes we will have to get used to seeing more bears in Isfjorden.
133175.tags_en: Norwegian Polar Institute, polar bear, news, Longyearbyen

133196.excerpt_en: With 60 artists and 35 concerts over four days, the board of Longyearbyen Bluesklubb has plenty to do one week before the 12th edition of Dark Season Blues.
133196.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Bluesklubb has high hopes for this year’s blues festival. Demand for tickets has been strong, and festival passes sold out early.
133196.tags_en: magazine, culture, Dark Season Blues, news

133206.excerpt_en: The signs were made of iron, and some were cast in bronze, but most were made of wood. When the landholdings were established in Svalbard in 1926–27, the annexation signs lost their function.
133206.subtitle_en: Annexation signs were used in Svalbard from 1900 and marked areas claimed for mining.

133208.excerpt_en: The annual TV fundraiser is approaching. This year’s collection is for Norwegian Church Aid, which will provide water for more than one million people in eight countries.
133208.subtitle_en: For several weeks, people have been pulling out all the stops for this year’s TV fundraiser.

133253.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Polar Institute (NP) anaesthetizes between 60 and 90 polar bears in Svalbard each year. Now it wants to study the short-term effects of the anaesthetic and has applied to the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund for nearly NOK 390,000. “The time it takes for polar bears to recover after anaesthesia varies greatly.”
133253.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Polar Institute will study the after-effects of the anaesthesia used on polar bears during tagging.
133253.tags_en: nature and the environment, news, research, researchers, polar bear

133268.excerpt_en: Last week we revisited Kjell Lavik’s dog team during the 1974 Sun Festival. We are sticking with the 1970s, and this time the subject is summer activities.
133268.subtitle_en: Poles are hauled from a lorry at Skjæringa.

133274.excerpt_en: Lights shine from two windows on the second floor of Barrack 1 in Nybyen.
133274.subtitle_en: Freia has lived in this apartment in Nybyen for 30 years. Now she can no longer stay here, but she is not leaving Svalbard for good.

133358.excerpt_en: At around 10:30 p.m. on Sunday, after the traditional auction had ended, the account stood at NOK 1,015,380. “And not everything has come in yet,” says fundraising coordinator Anne Lise Sandvik.
133358.subtitle_en: People on Svalbard have gone all out for this year’s TV fundraiser, and on Sunday evening the account passed one million kroner.
133358.title_en: Went All Out for the TV Fundraiser

133360.excerpt_en: The polar bear lost its GPS transmitter sometime between 11 p.m. on Thursday and 1 a.m. on Friday. “GPS transmitters are not originally designed for male bears. A male bear’s neck is too wide in relation to its skull, so it is easy for them to remove the transmitter.”
133360.subtitle_en: The polar bear moved from Longyearbyen to Nordaustlandet last Thursday removed its GPS transmitter collar that same evening.

133382.excerpt_en: Store Norske’s HSE manager, Einar Fjerdingøy, says the accident happened when a support plate used to hold the working face in place fell down. The plate landed on the steel conveyor belt that carries coal out of the stope and became wedged beneath it.
133382.subtitle_en: A man was injured while working at Svea Nord.
133382.title_en: Broke His Arm in the Mine

133386.excerpt_en: Reports that guides disturbed a group of walruses have prompted a reaction. A tourist who took part in an expedition cruise this summer reported to the Governor of Svalbard what she believed was deliberate action to obtain good photo opportunities for the cruise guests.
133386.subtitle_en: As we know, it is also others who decide what they will think and believe about us.

133400.excerpt_en: But there is plenty to suggest that Inge (28), Markus (26) and Håkon Wegge (21) are anything but ordinary outdoor enthusiasts. On Sunday, they were in Longyearbyen to promote the film “Bear Island – Follow the Dream,” which had its preview at the cultural centre.
133400.subtitle_en: Finding a safe place for a surfboard while a snowstorm rages is not usually a problem for people camping in the mountains.

133406.excerpt_en: Children aged two to 14 took part in the sports games at Svalbardhallen, which included running, javelin and relay races. When Svalbardposten dropped by, we met this group, who enthusiastically told us about throwing the javelin 30 metres, jumping 1.64 metres and sprinting 40 metres from one end wall to the other in a lightning-fast 6.5 seconds.
133406.subtitle_en: As many as 65 children in Longyearbyen were busy taking part in sports on Saturday.
133406.title_en: Packed House at the Sports Games

133425.excerpt_en: “We don’t have to deal with this in Norway. While water is a matter of course for us, others have to carry it for hours to get water to their homes,” says Katrine Apeland.
133425.subtitle_en: Katrine and Silvia paid to carry water across Longyeardalen. The sum of activities and fundraising stunts surrounding the annual TV fundraiser put Svalbard at the top of the donation rankings once again this year.

133427.subtitle_en: Absolutely everything. And the money goes to the fundraising campaign.

133446.excerpt_en: It therefore seems fitting to look back at a festive gathering sometime in 1974. The date is unknown, but the photograph was taken by Svalbardposten’s former editor and shows that the dance floor in the main hall was packed that evening.
133446.subtitle_en: This weekend brings another blues festival, and on Saturday Huset will once again be filled with music and an audience.

133448.excerpt_en: So far, 26 ships have announced their arrival in Longyearbyen for the 2015 season. At this time last year, the figure was around 30.
133448.subtitle_en: AIDAcara has also announced an arrival in 2015, but the decline in cruise traffic is now coming as a result of the heavy-fuel-oil ban in Svalbard.

133450.excerpt_en: On the last weekend in September, Securitas inspected the licensed venues in Longyearbyen. On Friday, inspectors saw several people carrying alcohol in the area outside the tent where Spitsbergen Travel’s October festival was being held.
133450.subtitle_en: During the beer festival at the Polar Hotel, many people drank alcohol outside the licensed premises. Several other venues were also reprimanded after liquor-control inspections.

133498.excerpt_en: “For being a local politician in Longyearbyen to be fun, you need money to spend. We now have NOK 40 million in the bank, and it has to be used to save the power station.”
133498.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council is beginning a review of all the services it provides to identify where money can be saved.
133498.tags_en: news, turnaround process, Longyearbyen Community Council

133514.excerpt_en: How satisfied are you with the quality of the drinking water, pedestrian facilities, the environment in which children grow up, and the opportunity to obtain your own residential plot?
133514.subtitle_en: Politicians are asking Longyearbyen residents for advice.

133516.excerpt_en: Artist Solveig Egeland originally had permission to keep the hut in place until 1 October, but the deadline was extended by a few weeks because several locals expressed a wish for it to remain.
