146838.excerpt_en: The satellite is a Norwegian initiative involving, among others, the Norwegian Space Centre and Space Norway. KSAT will download the data, and the antennas on Svalbard will see increased activity.
146838.subtitle_en: The Norwegian HEO satellite now being planned will provide communications to many of today’s most challenging internet regions.

146840.excerpt_en: The world’s northernmost newspaper has managed something the entire media industry struggles with: turning a profit. Last year’s result was a welcome NOK 159,000; in 2014, the deficit was NOK 296,000, and in 2013 the result was minus NOK 538,000.
146840.subtitle_en: After years of losses, Svalbardposten made a profit last year.

146844.excerpt_en: Free school meals are one of the measures many believe could have a major positive impact on pupils’ wellbeing and learning at school. Research shows that school meals have a positive effect on pupils, mainly by helping them maintain their concentration throughout the school day.
146844.subtitle_en: Why can’t all pupils in Norwegian schools be offered free school meals?

146855.excerpt_en: Prevention is an obvious part of emergency preparedness, but prevention is limited to incidents we know about. The other side of preparedness is preparing for the unknown.
146855.subtitle_en: Suddenly it is there—the accident, the disaster—that hits so hard. One thing is certain: It will happen again. We do not know when. We do not know where. We do not know what. But we know for certain that it will happen again.
146855.title_en: Local preparedness is the most important

146861.excerpt_en: Climate change may have major consequences and create serious problems for future generations. In this reader’s letter, I would like to discuss climate change on Earth.
146861.subtitle_en: Our entire planet is threatened by global warming. Our future is quite simply at risk.
146861.tags_en: reader’s letter, opinions, climate, Working Environment Act

146877.excerpt_en: Store Norske’s subsidiary is looking for new business areas to create profitable, secure jobs in Longyearbyen. Svalbardposten has already covered work on the Gruve 3 museum, Sari—short for Svalbard Arctic Research Infrastructure—in Svea, and Hotellneset.
146877.subtitle_en: Using the EasyPark mobile app, Store Norske Momentum aims to create income and jobs—and do its bit for the environment in Longyearbyen.

146880.excerpt_en: The beautiful little bird is notorious on Svalbard for being aggressive, readily using its bill on approaching people until the blood sprays. New research shows that the bird has other abilities too: The small tern is highly likely to be the migratory bird with the world record for annual travel.
146880.subtitle_en: Over its lifetime, the Arctic tern flies a distance equivalent to traveling to the Moon and back three times.
146880.tags_en: Arctic nature guide, magazine, wildlife, news, birds
146880.title_en: Every winter, the Arctic tern flies to Antarctica

146899.excerpt_en: The women, who both work at Coop Svalbard, were sitting in the lunchroom on the second floor at around half past twelve on Tuesday. Together with five or six others, they were just starting their lunch break.
146899.subtitle_en: Vigdis Folde and Karin Mella had a close encounter with Tuesday’s earthquake.
146899.title_en: Felt dizzy and nauseous after the tremors

146910.excerpt_en: The earthquake’s epicentre was in Storfjorden between Edgeøya and Spitsbergen. The tremors began 10–17 kilometres below the Earth’s crust and measured 5.3 on the Richter scale. The Richter scale classifies quakes between 5.0 and 5.9 as “destructive shaking.”
146910.subtitle_en: If Tuesday’s earthquake had occurred beneath Longyearbyen, it would have been impossible to stand upright. UNIS researchers will now investigate the cause.

146929.excerpt_en: Visit Svalbard and NHO Troms and Svalbard are dismayed by an unexpected and highly negative message received during Easter. Finnish airline Finnair will not be able to operate flights to Svalbard as planned from this summer.
146929.subtitle_en: The tourism industry has been told that thousands of visitors will no longer be coming after all.

146937.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten happened to arrange an interview with Mona on her 42nd birthday. The newly minted 42-year-old used it as an excuse to bring cake.
146937.subtitle_en: Mona Ada Andersen (42) works with plans, but prefers a loose structure in her free time.
146937.tags_en: people, life on Svalbard, back page

146939.excerpt_en: The incident serves as a reminder of the risks associated with rechargeable lithium or lithium-ion batteries. Such batteries are found in almost all portable electronic devices.
146939.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten (18 March 2016, p. 3) reports that the fire at Stormessa was probably caused by an electrical appliance left charging.
146939.tags_en: letter to the editor, fire, opinions

146952.excerpt_en: Eight government institutions, including UNIS, have launched a six-year research project that will cost just over NOK 800 million.
146952.subtitle_en: The waters around and north of Svalbard contain many secrets that researchers will now seek to uncover.
146952.title_en: Norway steps up its Arctic efforts

146991.excerpt_en: Lufttransport has been testing a highly distinctive asymmetric black-and-white pattern on its two Dornier aircraft for some time. The results are good, and Widerøe has now begun painting its aircraft propellers.
146991.subtitle_en: Distinctive patterns on the propellers of Svalbard aircraft keep dangerous birds at bay.

146996.excerpt_en: On Friday, business developer Pål Berg of Store Norske Momentum told Svalbardposten that the company would introduce parking charges at selected locations in Longyearbyen. A dedicated service department at Store Norske would handle fines and complaints, creating five or six new jobs in the local community.
146996.subtitle_en: No, there will be no parking charges.

147041.excerpt_en: Many small households find ordinary loaves too large; half is often thrown away after going stale or mouldy. “The message from, among others, the Svalbard shops was clear: customers wanted a smaller loaf. We have now made one,” says Kjell Vidar Jensen, operations and production manager at Bakehuset.
147041.subtitle_en: Customers in Longyearbyen are getting their wish. The local bakery is now starting production of small loaves.
147041.title_en: Small loaves from a new bakery

147052.excerpt_en: It was during the night of 16 January that the man drove a snowmobile in Adventdalen, when the Governor of Svalbard received a tip that he was under the influence of alcohol.
147052.subtitle_en: A local man in his 30s drove a snowmobile with what is known as a high blood-alcohol level.

147056.excerpt_en: Next Tuesday, a public meeting will be held at the cultural centre about the new land-use plan proposal, which is now being sent out for public consultation. The plan proposal makes room for an entirely new approach to land use in the town.
147056.subtitle_en: The community council wants public input on numerous proposals for changes to the town.
147056.tags_en: Sjøskrenten, news, land-use plan, Skjæringa, waterfront area
147056.title_en: Skjæringa East to become new residential area

147076.excerpt_en: Until 2042, the antennas on Platåfjellet will download data from weather satellites for the European meteorological organisation Eumetsat. The contract is worth approximately
147076.subtitle_en: KSAT has signed a major contract with the EU’s weather service, securing long-term activity on Svalbard.

147082.excerpt_en: Recently, the German Svalbard veteran had to take the Norwegian Tax Administration to court to establish that the authorities had erred when she was deregistered from Norway in 1975. The ruling confirms that she herself did not report moving to Germany.
147082.subtitle_en: After 48 years as a permanent resident of Svalbard, Freia Hutzschenreuter (78) is still officially registered as having no place of residence.

147097.excerpt_en: Archaeologists from the Governor of Svalbard are preparing to examine three graves that are gradually being eroded by the sea. At Likneset in Smeerenburgfjorden, approximately
147097.subtitle_en: Likneset conceals nothing less than a treasure trove of European textile history. Three endangered graves are now to be examined.

147106.excerpt_en: Innovation Norway is behind the distinction, which is awarded to the tourism industry as a whole after strict criteria have been met. Visit Svalbard has worked systematically for a long time to achieve sustainable-destination status.
147106.subtitle_en: Together with Geilo, Longyearbyen is among the first destinations to receive the “Sustainable Destination” designation.

147112.excerpt_en: Research and education will play a bigger role in Longyearbyen. The goal is at least 400 student-years at UNIS—twice as many as today.
147112.subtitle_en: UNIS is stepping up its efforts and will launch several new courses. The major universities will take responsibility for creating more activity in the north.

147119.excerpt_en: At the same time, the population has remained fairly stable despite severe cuts at Store Norske. According to fresh figures from Statistics Norway, 2,654 people were resident in the Norwegian and Russian “towns” on Svalbard at the turn of the year.
147119.subtitle_en: The number of elderly people and foreigners in Longyearbyen is rising. There are fewer Norwegians, and fewer children are being born.

147134.excerpt_en: Ekran jokingly described herself as ballast as she shared a sled and dog team with Tommy Jordbrudal. Both have impressive long-distance sled-dog racing records, including participation in the Iditarod and Finnmarksløpet.
147134.subtitle_en: “Great fun. An amazing trip,” world champion Sigrid Ekran beams after completing the 100-kilometre Trappers Trail.

147138.excerpt_en: It started innocently enough with an application from Coal Miner’s Cabins for extended serving hours. When the revision of the drug policy action plan came up, the debate developed into one the council had rarely, if ever, seen before.
147138.subtitle_en: The Green Party (MDG) sparked an unusually heated debate in the Longyearbyen Community Council.
147138.tags_en: news, politics, alcohol, Longyearbyen Community Council
147138.title_en: Tug-of-war over drug policy action plan

147151.excerpt_en: The location of the new waste facility has been a hot-button issue for a long time. The dividing line runs between the Conservatives and the Green Party (MDG) on one side, and Labour and the Liberals on the other.
147151.subtitle_en: Once again, the community council voted to build the new waste facility at Hotellneset.
147151.tags_en: news, politics, waste facility, Longyearbyen Community Council

147171.excerpt_en: Things could have gone badly for a dog that turned up at Longyearbyen Airport at the weekend. A specific risk assessment, a dispensation from Svalbard Vet and the Norwegian Food Safety Authority, through specialist inspector Harald Os, meant the dog avoided being sent to the eternal hunting grounds.
147171.subtitle_en: People arriving in Svalbard with dogs lacking permits and legally required vaccinations risk having the animal euthanized.
147171.tags_en: Norwegian Food Safety Authority, news, dogs

147184.excerpt_en: Five unplanned puppies have brought life and received loving care this winter in Svalbard’s most remote settlement. The 11 employees and three dogs at the Polish research station in Hornsund have had more than research to occupy them this winter.
147184.subtitle_en: An accidental mating led to plenty of joy—and a 500-kilometre snowmobile trip.

147188.excerpt_en: Fifty-two applications were received in this round, and 22 of them received funding from the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund. “There was a decrease in the number of applications, and we see that some applicants have reapplied after improving their applications,” says fund director Morten Ruud.
147188.subtitle_en: On Friday, the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund awarded NOK 6.1 million.
147188.title_en: Millions for Mine Facilities, Tapeworm and Information Centre

147200.excerpt_en: At around 2 p.m. on Saturday, the Governor responded to a report that a polar bear had been shot in self-defence at Verlegenhuken, in the far north of Spitsbergen. A Finnish tour group of four men had been approached by the bear.
147200.subtitle_en: The Governor carried out the final euthanization of a 150-kilogram male bear.
147200.tags_en: news, Governor of Svalbard, polar bear

147209.excerpt_en: On Tuesday morning, the Governor and Arctic Autorent were notified that a company vehicle was standing in the stream running down from Vannledningsdalen. No one could say that morning how the vehicle had ended up there.
147209.subtitle_en: A foreign tourist has admitted driving a van while over the alcohol limit.

147232.excerpt_en: Preparations are now under way for the operational hiatus. Activity inside the mountain has stopped.
147232.subtitle_en: As the last piece of coal was extracted from the mines in Svea, a production record was set.
147232.title_en: Hopes for a Short Mining Hiatus

147234.excerpt_en: The mining community will soon go into hibernation. At the same time, the first tourists have appeared, the pub has come back to life, interest in the area’s history has grown, and the large green accommodation block could become a hotel.
147234.subtitle_en: While coal mining is on hold, Svea could become an important centre for research, tourism, conferences and perhaps a unique folk high school.
147234.tags_en: Store Norske, coal production, coal, Svea, news

147254.excerpt_en: The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) was present in Longyearbyen for much of the winter that has just ended. Filming began at the end of October and continued until the end of March.
147254.subtitle_en: In September, parts of the lives of several permanent residents will become television entertainment for millions.
147254.title_en: Svalbard Residents to Star in BBC Documentary

147266.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen has around 800 polar dogs, along with a steadily growing number of small, feisty, friendly, cuddly dogs—the kind you can take onto a plane.
147266.subtitle_en: “Texas” is tough and likes snowmobile trips. “Ross” has crossed the Rocky Mountains. “King” sleeps outside at minus 20. While “Liselott” is simply cute.

147285.excerpt_en: The reindeer was limping and had suffered an injury to its left hind thigh, but the Governor does not know how serious the injury is. “We were five metres from the animal and could not get any closer. We will drive out later today and take a look,” says senior police officer Sidsel Svarstad.
147285.subtitle_en: On Tuesday morning, the Governor brought in a dog that had attacked a reindeer in Adventdalen.
147285.title_en: Had to Separate Dog and Reindeer

147299.excerpt_en: At Urskog-Høland Railway’s specialist workshop in Sørumsand, worn plates will be replaced, old and new will be riveted together, and the correct paint applied. The restoration is done by hand, using the same construction methods as when the steam locomotive was new in 1909.
147299.subtitle_en: After 99 years of being battered and rusting in Ny-Ålesund, the world’s northernmost locomotive is enjoying a well-deserved “spa treatment.”

147302.excerpt_en: Everything fell into place. The weather was the finest of the year.
147302.subtitle_en: “This was absolutely awesome,” said Astrid Uhrenholdt Jacobsen, promising that this will not be her last ski marathon on Svalbard.

147326.excerpt_en: The 1 May parade has probably been more impressive in the past. Around 35 people marched behind the band and the three banners: “Ensure the continuation of coal mining.”
147326.subtitle_en: Thirty-five people took part in Longyearbyen’s 1 May parade.

147328.excerpt_en: It took place at Elveneset, northeast of Longyearbyen. “The main reason is that it is a beautiful place. But from here we face Sassenfjorden, which has been ice-free all winter, and less ice is a consequence of climate change,” says Leif Magne Helgesen.
147328.subtitle_en: On Tuesday evening, parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen held a service to focus attention on changes in the climate.

147331.excerpt_en: That would mean many of today’s large cruise ships would not be welcome farther north. Some of the traffic across and along the Arctic Ocean also runs on heavy fuel oil.
147331.subtitle_en: A number of American organizations are calling for a ban on ships using heavy fuel oil in the Arctic.
147331.tags_en: news, heavy fuel oil ban, cruise
147331.title_en: Calls for Ban on Heavy Fuel Oil

147341.excerpt_en: The application deadline for jobs on Bear Island, Hopen and Jan Mayen expires next week. For the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, the number of applicants looks set to be very high. “We have a permanent staff of veterans who have held these positions before and would happily return.”
147341.subtitle_en: Meteorological Institute once attracted regulars to its Arctic islands. Now adventurous young people are queuing up.

147354.excerpt_en: Most of the male ptarmigans have returned to Adventdalen, where they mark their territories and wait for the females to arrive. Another sure sign of spring is the arrival of the ptarmigan researchers, who come to monitor the birds.
147354.subtitle_en: The Svalbard rock ptarmigan is the only bird that does not migrate south. But where are the flocks in the coldest part of winter?

147365.excerpt_en: The Svalbard rock ptarmigan, its eggs and chicks are already on the menu of Arctic foxes, glaucous gulls and Arctic skuas. Pink-footed geese and barnacle geese are increasingly competing for grazing areas. “So far, there is no evidence that the large birds of prey are breeding on Svalbard.”
147365.subtitle_en: Ravens and snowy owls have been observed on Svalbard. That is bad news for the rock ptarmigan.
147365.title_en: A Warmer Climate Brings New Enemies

147387.excerpt_en: “It took quite a long time because we could not see the bear. We fired a flare gun into the cave to try to scare it out, but it did not work,” says Chief Superintendent Christian Svarstad.
147387.subtitle_en: The polar bear that was put down at Verlegenhuken hid in a cave in the shoreline talus. It came out only after the Governor of Svalbard dug down to it.

147403.excerpt_en: Expedition leader Kari Kossila has set the camera to self-timer and is ready for the celebratory photo. He, Mikko Uimonen, Eero Oura and Joonas Hiltunen have reached their destination: Verlegenhuken.
147403.subtitle_en: At the very tip of Verlegenhuken, the Finnish ski tourists spotted the polar bear. Everyone was in the wrong place at the wrong time.
147403.tags_en: polar bear, news, nature and environment, polar bear attack

147431.excerpt_en: For many years, Telenor has used Longyearbyen to test new products. Now a new initiative is being launched, with an outcome nobody knows yet. “We envisage premises equipped with modern communications.”
147431.subtitle_en: The buildings at Skjæringa are beginning to show their age. Now Telenor is planning a new building.

147433.excerpt_en: Today, mobile coverage is available only in certain places outside Longyearbyen and Barentsburg. Satellite phones are supposed to provide coverage everywhere, but in practice they do not always work, and such phones are not available to everyone. “We are particularly focused on improving emergency preparedness along the coast.”
147433.subtitle_en: Telenor wants a series of stations that can provide 4G mobile coverage across the entire archipelago and well out to sea.
147433.title_en: Working to provide mobile coverage across Svalbard

147444.excerpt_en: The paint manufacturer is keeping the formula secret. Tests will be conducted on Telenor’s masts in Svalbard. “They will test their products at our station at Skolten.”
147444.subtitle_en: Jotun is developing a coating intended to prevent ice from forming on masts and power lines.

147465.excerpt_en: Kjell Farstad has given Svalbardposten a number of interesting photographs from Svalbard in the 1970s. This week’s selected picture is from 1979 and clearly comes from a canteen where dinner and coffee are being served.

147475.excerpt_en: “We could not have been luckier,” he says after completing the marathon alongside 871 other participants. Everything fell into place: the weather was the most beautiful of the year.
147475.subtitle_en: Oslo resident Hallvard Selboe is beaming after fantastic days in the north. The ski marathon was a highlight of four adventure-filled days in Svalbard.
147475.tags_en: Svalbard Ski Marathon, Svalbard life, culture

147480.excerpt_en: Svalbard’s own Daniel Husdal did it again. Of everyone who set out in the ski marathon, the 13-year-old was the first to cross the finish line.
147480.tags_en: Svalbard Ski Marathon, Svalbard life, culture

147490.excerpt_en: The day after the ski marathon, the younger generation took over the venue on the flat by Todalen. The more than 100 participants showed no shortage of determination, and many displayed impressive skiing technique.
147490.subtitle_en: High speed, broad smiles and genuine skiing joy marked this year’s Children’s Ski Festival.
147490.tags_en: culture, life in Svalbard, children’s ski festival

147507.excerpt_en: When spring arrives, Kjellrun Eggenfellner plans to carefully take the Arctic paintings down from the walls. She will pack them away together with large quantities of books and other keepsakes.
147507.subtitle_en: Kjellrun Eggenfellner taught an entire generation to take pride in Svalbard’s history. Now she is soon to become part of Svalbard’s history herself.
147507.tags_en: news, on the way out, magazine

147510.excerpt_en: It is Thursday afternoon. Three journalists from the sixth grade...
147510.subtitle_en: Lasse, Live and Pia have sharpened their pencils and switched on the microphone. Svalbardposten is facing competition from a hot-off-the-press newspaper.

147514.excerpt_en: Last Friday, the Hurtigruten ship “Fram” sailed into Adventfjorden for the first time this season. The first cruise tourists took pictures of the Santa Claus mailbox.
147514.title_en: Who should the ski marathon be for? The celebrity runners paid to come north? Marathon enthusiasts?

147526.excerpt_en: “The number of pupils fluctuates, and this year there are no pupils in the final year of upper secondary school,” says department head Anne-Line Pedersen at Longyearbyen School.
147526.subtitle_en: Last year, Ida Christine Aske Lima and Aina Malerud brought colour, sound and activity to the 17 May parade. This year, others will have to provide the antics.

147534.excerpt_en: Russian and Norwegian researchers will jointly map the archipelago’s many moss species. The work will begin this summer and continue for two years.
147534.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s smallest, and perhaps oldest, plants are now to be studied.

147552.excerpt_en: Harald Ellingsen is 62 and is currently a professor and head of department at the Department of Marine Technology at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU). “I have been fascinated by the High North and Svalbard as a place and a community.”
147552.subtitle_en: Harald Ellingsen has been appointed the new director at UNIS. He starts the job on 1 October.

147565.excerpt_en: The government wants a more diverse business sector, preferably with more private operators. It wants year-round, stable jobs that are profitable from a business perspective.
147565.subtitle_en: Tourism and research are expected to play a larger role in Svalbard in the proposal for the new White Paper to be presented today.

147571.excerpt_en: “What they have done is list a number of the local strategies we ourselves have developed,” says Arild Olsen (Labour). He is not disappointed, but neither is he particularly pleased. “Naturally, I will read the White Paper carefully, but based on the presentation given, I have several questions.”
147571.subtitle_en: Expected more from the Svalbard White Paper.

147574.excerpt_en: “We are extremely pleased. It is a major nomination,” says Renate Pedersen, sales manager at Basecamp Spitsbergen.
147574.title_en: Basecamp nominated for the 2016 Tourism Award

147586.excerpt_en: Just before midnight on Sunday, the Governor of Svalbard was alerted that a car had driven off the road just before the airport. “The police rushed out and arrested a person near the scene. It was a visiting man with Norwegian citizenship,” says Chief Superintendent Ståle Nylund.
147586.subtitle_en: A visiting man ended up in a ditch in a stolen car on Sunday evening.
147586.title_en: Drove drunk without a driving licence

147598.excerpt_en: They all marched together in the 17 May parade.
147598.title_en: “There is no need to force people out through fixed-term contracts”

147621.excerpt_en: Earlier this spring, Space Norway discovered that one of the two fiber-optic cables between Longyearbyen and the mainland was not lying as it should. “Something has come into contact with it, causing the cable to bend.”
147621.subtitle_en: “Neither icebergs nor trawlers can reach down to it.”
147621.title_en: Something or someone has shifted the fiber-optic cable to the mainland

147641.excerpt_en: There are many bird enthusiasts around the world who would pay dearly to see some of the many species living in the river delta in Adventdalen. This year’s birdwatching season is just getting started.
147641.subtitle_en: Birdwatching could become a million-kroner business.
147641.title_en: “Much Cooler to See an Ivory Gull Than a Polar Bear”

147650.excerpt_en: After a week’s break, we are once again bringing out one of Kjell Farstad’s photographs. The scene is from 1979, at Mine 7’s surface facilities.
147650.tags_en: historical photograph, life in Svalbard, Mine 7, history

147670.excerpt_en: We read with astonishment in the Svalbard White Paper that drastic changes have been proposed for Kings Bay AS and Ny-Ålesund. This will have major consequences for the company, the community of Ny-Ålesund and the research conducted there.
147670.title_en: “It is unwise and poor corporate governance”

147688.excerpt_en: “Someone cleaned out the entrance to Svalbard Lodge of shoes during the night leading into Thursday,” says hotel manager Stein-Ove Johannessen. Among those robbed of their shoes was an Indian family of eight.
147688.subtitle_en: Family of eight lost their shoes.
147688.title_en: Eleven Pairs of Shoes Disappeared from Here

147693.excerpt_en: At around 7 p.m. on Tuesday, personnel from the Governor of Svalbard’s police department went to Bolterdalen. Several dogs had escaped and attacked a reindeer.
147693.subtitle_en: Several dogs chased reindeer after escaping from their dog sitter in Bolterdalen.

147695.excerpt_en: On Wednesday afternoon, an emergency beacon was activated at the head of Bjørndalen, southwest of Longyearbyen. The Governor of Svalbard responded by helicopter. “It was a foreign tourist who was convinced he would not manage to get back to Longyearbyen alive on his own,” says Arve Johnsen, senior police officer with the Governor of Svalbard.
147695.subtitle_en: Foreign tourist rescued by helicopter at the head of Bjørndalen.
147695.title_en: “Convinced He Wouldn’t Make It Back Alive”

147704.excerpt_en: Parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen pointed to humanity’s responsibility for the climate in SP on 13 May 2016.
147704.subtitle_en: A letter to the editor from Reinhard Mook.
147704.title_en: “The Climate Itself Is Not Threatened. Rather, the Climate May Threaten Human Existence”

147725.excerpt_en: The figures remain modest for Trust Arktikugol’s tourism company. Around 300 Russian tourists made their way to Barentsburg this winter.
147725.title_en: Twice as Many Tourists Travel to Barentsburg

147730.excerpt_en: The snow bunting was among the first, followed by the geese, eider ducks and all the others. Some come in flocks, others in pairs or alone.
147730.subtitle_en: The valley is now springing to life.
147730.tags_en: king eider, barnacle goose, birds, snow bunting, news

147751.excerpt_en: This year marks 100 years since Longyearbyen got its first hospital, and 25 years since the current hospital was completed. That’s enough material for a book!

147764.excerpt_en: Eva-Britt Kornfeldt heads the Svalbard Cruise Network and, on behalf of the entire industry, has high hopes for this year’s tourist season. Almost everything is to be ready to receive 38 large cruise ships, in addition to a number of smaller expedition cruises.
147764.subtitle_en: Early Wednesday morning, she wants as many people as possible to line Burmaveien with flags and welcome the first cruise ship of the year.

147777.excerpt_en: “As far as registrations are concerned, we’re 40 ahead of schedule. At this point last year we had 200 registered, whereas so far this year we have 240,” says Silje M.
147777.subtitle_en: There is one week to go until the Spitsbergen Marathon. All indications are that participation could reach record levels.
147777.title_en: Heading for a Record-Breaking Spitsbergen Marathon

147790.excerpt_en: The cultural school had not originally planned to put on a spring performance.
147790.subtitle_en: In honour of Atle Husby, who died in the avalanche.

147813.excerpt_en: For someone who fell in love with Svalbard as a young researcher and Norwegian Polar Institute employee in Ny-Ålesund in the 1970s, the new Svalbard white papers make interesting reading. This time too, as it may be a defining moment for Longyearbyen and Norway’s continued control over Svalbard.
147813.subtitle_en: For someone who fell in love with Svalbard as a young researcher and Norwegian Polar Institute employee in Ny-Ålesund in the 1970s, the new Svalbard white papers make interesting reading.
