147819.subtitle_en: The three ten-year-olds receiving English lessons in Barentsburg have gained more classmates over the past year.

147822.excerpt_en: Kristin M. Nybakken Abild and Jens Abild are the developers of the home at Vei 232.
147822.subtitle_en: A design error in this extension means it will be almost a metre higher than the rest of the row of houses.

147835.excerpt_en: The past two issues of Svalbardposten have criticized the government’s proposed organization of activities in Ny-Ålesund. Among other things, it is claimed that the Norwegian Polar Institute is being given responsibility for Ny-Ålesund.
147835.subtitle_en: The past two issues of Svalbardposten have criticized the government’s proposed organization of activities in Ny-Ålesund.
147835.tags_en: Norwegian Polar Institute, opinion, reader’s letter, Ny-Ålesund
147835.title_en: The Norwegian Polar Institute and the Svalbard white paper

147864.excerpt_en: They have cut and glued, colored and sprinkled artificial snow. Everything is being assembled into a large picture—an artwork Longyearbyen has never seen before.
147864.subtitle_en: Sixty to 70 children are pouring their imaginations into an exciting artwork that will soon be unveiled at the bank.

147867.excerpt_en: This year’s cultural exchange will be remembered for its high tempo, rapid scene changes, colors and meaningful content performed by charming and talented participants. Last weekend, Longyearbyen visited Barentsburg with a performance, singing and a show.
147867.subtitle_en: “Magical” was the audience’s verdict. Barentsburg’s cultural scene impressed once again and brought the evening to a close with “Simply the Best.”

147869.excerpt_en: Frantzen originally planned to row alone, but has brought Pettersen along for this summer’s expedition. They have put the boats in the water, and their first trial run went from Longyearbyen to Grumant and back in a brisk wind. “We’re really going to feel it in our backsides and backs.”
147869.subtitle_en: In July, Tommy Sjöö Frantzen and Jan Ivar Pettersen will row the same route that ended tragically for 17 men in 1872.
147869.title_en: Preparing for a Historic Rowing Expedition

147879.excerpt_en: Flour, sugar and coffee were not the only things on the future trappers’ minds when they went on a “power-shopping” spree and rapidly filled their carts in town. Gard Christophersen (29) and Bård Blæsterdalen (28) will spend the winter trapping at Austfjordneset and left last week aboard Polarsyssel for their new home.
147879.subtitle_en: How much flour is needed to bake bread in a wood-fired oven for an entire year? Gard and Bård have faced major challenges in recent days.
147879.title_en: Full Speed Ahead Before a Year as Trappers

147896.excerpt_en: “Kings Bay will continue to run the community in Ny-Ålesund, and then we’ll see when the new strategy is in place whether there will be any changes,” says State Secretary Lars Andreas Lunde (Conservative Party) at the Ministry of Climate and Environment.
147896.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Climate and Environment defends the decision to have the Norwegian Polar Institute take over in Ny-Ålesund. What will happen to Kings Bay is not yet clear.
147896.tags_en: Ny-Ålesund, news, Kings Bay, research, Norwegian Polar Institute

147903.excerpt_en: Work on the Svalbard white paper will get fully under way after the summer holidays. 29.
147903.subtitle_en: Trine Skei Grande (Liberal Party) will lead the continued work on the Svalbard white paper. After the summer holidays, everyone who wants to will have the chance to make their voice heard.
147903.tags_en: Svalbard white paper, Liberal Party, news
147903.title_en: Invites the Public to a Hearing

147913.excerpt_en: A large house with a bright green facade has sprung up at Sjøskrenten. It has been named Russki Dom, Russian home.
147913.subtitle_en: At Russki Dom, tourists can stay, eat and join expedition trips. They will also get a little Pomor atmosphere.

147917.excerpt_en: Silje M. Hagen of Aktiv i friluft carries a black summit-trip mailbox over her shoulder and heads toward the bunker opposite Skjæringa this Saturday.
147917.subtitle_en: This year, there will be dedicated summit-trail boxes for children.

147944.excerpt_en: After many long delays, the school book commissioned by Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) is finished. “It’s a day of joy. It feels really good to see it with a cover and everything.”
147944.subtitle_en: Six years behind schedule, the history of Longyearbyen School has been published in hardcover. It will be celebrated with a launch party at Huset next Friday.

147962.excerpt_en: Once again, there was a major volunteer effort at the marina this weekend. The pontoons had to be put out after spending the winter ashore, while repairs, cleaning and decorating were also carried out.
147962.subtitle_en: The latest from the small-boat harbour: You no longer have to lug around jerry cans.

147965.excerpt_en: In 2012, perfluorinated compounds (PFAS) were detected at the fire-training ground in Longyearbyen. The substances are extremely hazardous to the environment and are characterized by not breaking down in nature.
147965.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard suspects hazardous-substance releases at several locations on Svalbard. Now the snow bunting is being recruited in the fight against environmental toxins.

147968.excerpt_en: Every year, it is a recurring topic: the rubbish floating around town.
147968.subtitle_en: “Then we don’t need to tell the tourists loudly that sewage and food waste are discharged untreated straight into the fjord.”
147968.title_en: “Why isn’t there the same commitment to local rubbish?”

147981.excerpt_en: On Friday afternoon, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre of Northern Norway (HRS) received a report from the passenger ship “Ortelius,” which was in Hinlopen Strait near Vaigattøyane. “The boat was right at the edge of the ice with engine failure,” says rescue leader Lars Nedrevåg of HRS.
147981.subtitle_en: “Polarsyssel” is now towing the ship, which has 105 passengers on board.
147981.title_en: Passenger ship suffers engine failure in Hinlopen Strait

147993.excerpt_en: “It was an easy race for me. I ran with a group during the first kilometer, but the pace was sluggish.”
147993.subtitle_en: A Pole was utterly dominant in the men’s marathon, but there were several strong local performances in the Spitsbergen Marathon.

148004.excerpt_en: Wednesday was Hilde Kristin Røsvik’s first day at work in Longyearbyen. “It’s really exciting, and there’s a lot to get to grips with.”
148004.subtitle_en: Editor Hilde Kristin Røsvik is in place. Now she will draw up the plan for the newspaper’s future.

148013.excerpt_en: On Friday afternoon, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre of Northern Norway (HRS) received a report from the passenger ship “Ortelius,” which had suffered engine failure in Hinlopen Strait, near Vaigattøyane. The Governor’s vessel “Polarsyssel” was sent to the site and towed “Ortelius” back to Longyearbyen. “They encountered KV ‘Sortland’ some distance north of Forlandet.”
148013.subtitle_en: The “Ortelius” arrived in Longyearbyen on Sunday evening. Passengers are now being offered activities departing from Longyearbyen.

148016.excerpt_en: Tourism director Ronny Brunvoll and deputy chair of the local council Eirik Berger today received the prestigious label for sustainable tourism. After many years of targeted work, Svalbard has passed the stringent assessment and achieved the status.
148016.subtitle_en: Today, Svalbard received the “Sustainable Destination” label from the minister of trade and industry.
148016.tags_en: tourism, news, Visit Svalbard, travel industry

148038.excerpt_en: Culture Minister Linda Hofstad Helleland arrives on Sunday. She is coming to Longyearbyen in connection with Olav Christopher Jenssen’s exhibition at Kunsthall Svalbard. “I’ll be bringing a little news in my suitcase,” says Helleland.
148038.subtitle_en: Over the coming week, Svalbard will receive visits from the culture minister, the foreign minister and his American counterpart.

148054.excerpt_en: For the first time, the kindergartens in Longyearbyen visited their peers in Barentsburg. It was a visit the children in both communities will remember for a long time. “They had lots of nice toys there, but I didn’t understand anything they said,” Eva Helen Hultgren, 5, says after the trip.
148054.subtitle_en: But that was no obstacle when the kindergartens in Longyearbyen visited their peers in Barentsburg.
148054.title_en: “They had lots of nice toys there, but I didn’t understand what they were saying”

148068.excerpt_en: “I’ve been here several times before, and it’s one of my favorite places on Earth,” says Suzette McQuie from Sydney, Australia. Suzette has an extraordinary year behind her.
148068.subtitle_en: Suzette McQuie rounded off her extraordinary year on Svalbard.

148081.excerpt_en: This week, the Acquisitions Fund for Norwegian Craft Art visited Svalbard for the first time and bought two artworks by Morten Høgmo from the exhibition Dear Friend at Galleri Svalbard.
148081.subtitle_en: A solid recognition, says the director of Galleri Svalbard.

148106.excerpt_en: The government and several private actors will establish an artist residency and artists’ workshop in Longyearbyen. The project will be organized as a foundation.
148106.subtitle_en: The government wants to put Svalbard on the international art map.
148106.title_en: Artist residency to be established in Longyearbyen

148112.excerpt_en: “Gymnastics is great fun,” Agnes Zadewasser, 9, says spontaneously. She was one of the children who performed at Svalbardhallen on Sunday. “Everything is fun,” she says.
148112.subtitle_en: Gymnasts young and old showed what they can do as the gymnastics group ended the season at Svalbardhallen on Sunday.
148112.title_en: Gymnastics season comes to an end

148140.excerpt_en: Store manager Karin Mella is overwhelmed. When Norsk Tipping called, she initially thought it was a joke.
148140.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken sold the lottery ticket that won NOK 13.5 million on Saturday.

148161.excerpt_en: Kerry is making a one-day visit to Svalbard. He will meet researchers and receive a briefing from them on climate issues.
148161.subtitle_en: US Secretary of State John Kerry went straight from his Boeing 757 to a small plane taking him to Ny-Ålesund.

148169.excerpt_en: There have been intense preparations for the high-profile visit in recent days. A minute-by-minute programme has been prepared.
148169.subtitle_en: During three hectic hours in Ny-Ålesund, John Kerry experienced both Arctic terns and reindeer, and saw climate change with his own eyes.
148169.title_en: Busy hours for Kerry in the research village

148177.excerpt_en: Later in the summer, the distinctive pattern forms in the snow on the mountainside of Operafjellet. The pattern looks like a champagne glass.
148177.subtitle_en: There is still so much snow on the side of Operafjellet that the “champagne glass” has not yet taken shape.

148189.excerpt_en: Gard Christophersen and Bård Blæsterdalen arrived at the Austfjordnes trapping station on 28 May.
148189.subtitle_en: On Monday, a female polar bear was shot by the trappers at Austfjordnes. Her cub had to be euthanized by the Governor of Svalbard. They still have few details about the incident.

148208.excerpt_en: Aars has studied polar bears for several decades and is considered one of the country’s foremost experts on the species.
148208.subtitle_en: Polar bear researcher Jon Aars of the Norwegian Polar Institute has never encountered a similar case before.
148208.tags_en: nature and environment, news, polar bear

148213.excerpt_en: The government and several private players will establish a new artist’s residence and studio in Longyearbyen. It was the gift that Culture Minister Linda Hofstad Helleland brought to Longyearbyen on Sunday. “This initiative will put Svalbard and Norway on the international art map.”
148213.subtitle_en: The residence will supplement today’s accommodation in Nybyen and put Svalbard on the international art map.
148213.title_en: An artist’s residence in her suitcase

148223.excerpt_en: Ragnhild Røsseland and Frode Skar are sitting on the tundra in Bolterdalen, each holding a dog. It has been just over a week since they returned to Longyearbyen after two years at Austfjordnes. “It felt sad to leave.”
148223.subtitle_en: Ragnhild Røsseland and Frode Skar have lived off nature for two years. The eider ducks provided the closest experience of nature.
148223.tags_en: nature and environment, news, trapping life
148223.title_en: Two years trapping could mean a double duvet

148237.excerpt_en: Last Saturday evening, the doors opened to Olav Christopher’s exhibition, The Expedition, at Kunsthall Svalbard. Artists are exhibiting works he created in Longyearbyen. “It has been a very generous residency.”
148237.subtitle_en: Olav Christopher Jenssen felt like an Arab prince in Longyearbyen. In the harem, he took in Svalbard Museum’s old animals.
148237.title_en: Brought the old museum into the exhibition

148240.excerpt_en: At Huset, where a priest once filled small children with knowledge, around 50 listeners learned how it all came about. “I would put it this strongly: without the school, we would not have managed to meet the state’s requirements for a strong family community.”
148240.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen School is the cornerstone of the family community. Last Friday, author Kjersti Strømmen launched her book about it.
148240.title_en: Finally able to tell the school’s story

148257.excerpt_en: Culture Minister Linda Hofstad Helleland brought very good news in her suitcase when she arrived in Longyearbyen. Together with several private players, the government will establish a permanent artist’s residence and studio in the town.
148257.subtitle_en: “A thriving cultural life contributes to both quality of life and the desire to live here.”
148257.title_en: A boost for culture and tourism

148281.excerpt_en: Helly Hansen has been chosen as the clothing supplier for UNIS students. A group of students took part in the process of selecting the new supplier.
148281.subtitle_en: They will not be hard to spot. In the new year, the students will wear bright red jackets with the UNIS logo.

148291.excerpt_en: The Store Norske Mandskor concert at Svalbard Brewery on Friday evening ranged from the powerful Ave Mari Stella to familiar and beloved drinking songs. The ranks also included the brewmaster himself, Andreas Hegermann Riis.
148291.subtitle_en: The first, but surely not the last, brewery concert took place at the weekend. Many people turned up to listen.

148303.excerpt_en: This was later followed by suggestions that Norwegian presence could be threatened as a result of Trust Arcticugol’s intensified focus on tourism. A bizarre angle from the state broadcaster, based on old news and detached from reality.
148303.subtitle_en: NRK ran a story on Monday suggesting this. “The Russians step up the battle for Svalbard tourists” was the headline.
148303.tags_en: reader submission, opinion, letter to the editor
148303.title_en: Tourism drive in Barentsburg a threat to Longyearbyen?

148315.excerpt_en: Like a bolt from the blue, we could read in the Svalbard white paper that the role of the research institution and the government’s advisory scientific body, the Norwegian Polar Institute (NPI), in Ny-Ålesund will be strengthened by giving it responsibility for the operational implementation and follow-up of the research strategy in Ny-Ålesund.
148315.subtitle_en: My message is that the “patient”, Kings Bay AS, is certainly not acutely ill; there is no reason to resort to hasty cardiac massage with a sledgehammer.
148315.title_en: If it’s working, don’t fix it…

148324.excerpt_en: “Fast track for new homes” (SP 20 May 2016) and “Not allowed to move here” (SP 27 May 2016) show that homes below Skjæringa face opposition, however advantageous the area may be technically and practically.
148324.subtitle_en: By the 1990s at the latest, the avalanche risk in Lia, based on modelling, was known to Svalbard Samfunnsdrift.

148335.excerpt_en: It was such fun to read Svalbardposten’s 29 April article, “Freia breathes a sigh of relief.”
148335.subtitle_en: It is a great pleasure for me to know that this is now in the bag for Freia.
148335.tags_en: reader submission, opinion, letter to the editor

148353.excerpt_en: This winter, a debate raged over whether temporary installations should be allowed in the field for use as rest stops for tourists on guided trips. But at the time, the Governor of Svalbard, represented by environmental protection director Knut Fossum, would not allow this.
148353.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is launching a process aimed at allowing more permanent tourist cabins and temporary installations.
148353.title_en: Mobile grill huts from next season?

148374.excerpt_en: Poor ice conditions have made it difficult for tourist groups to reach Pyramiden. Until now, the only route such groups have been able to take has been across the fjord ice on Tempelfjorden and Billefjorden.
148374.subtitle_en: From the coming season, tourists will be allowed to drive across the glacier system to Pyramiden.

148380.excerpt_en: The children at Polarflokken kindergarten, Tundra department, aged one to three, have been out picking up litter in the local area as part of the Rusken campaign. At Elvesletta, beneath the pipeline, the children found empty snus boxes, used snus pouches and many cigarette butts. “This is incredibly filthy.”
148380.subtitle_en: The kindergartens have taken part in the Rusken clean-up campaign.

148388.excerpt_en: Abundant plankton algae provide food for krill and baleen whales. In mid-May this year, the spring bloom of plankton algae arrived in Isfjorden, dominated by beautiful and nutritious diatoms, which in turn provide food for zooplankton such as copepods—and, not least, krill.
148388.subtitle_en: From plankton to blue whales. Isfjorden has it all.
148388.title_en: A thriving life in Isfjorden—from plankton algae to blue whales

148416.excerpt_en: Last November, the Community Council decided to completely renovate Næringsbygget and rebuild it so that the library could be accommodated on the first floor. The project also involved partially rebuilding Kulturhuset, creating a shared entrance for Kulturhuset and Næringsbygget.
148416.subtitle_en: Renovating and rebuilding Næringsbygget will cost NOK 32 million. Some local politicians think that is too much.

148470.excerpt_en: Many politicians and government officials visit Svalbard, but receiving the US secretary of state is still out of the ordinary. Extensive security measures were put in place during John Kerry’s visit.
148470.subtitle_en: The visit helps strengthen the position of the local research community.
148470.title_en: An important visit for the climate

148479.excerpt_en: Nothing was left to chance when the US secretary of state came to visit. John Kerry has shown a personal commitment to the Arctic and is concerned about climate change and the marine environment.
148479.subtitle_en: John Kerry had a packed and busy visit to Ny-Ålesund.
148479.title_en: High activity in the research village

148493.excerpt_en: Those who made the trip enjoyed a pleasant morning before the rain arrived. A small group had gathered around the fire, where two large coffee pots stood ready with genuine campfire coffee.
148493.subtitle_en: The food stalls and fire pits in the Sjøområdet area would have welcomed even more visitors on Saturday morning.

148520.excerpt_en: Many people came to Galleri Svalbard for the opening. Lively accordion music welcomed everyone.
148520.subtitle_en: On Saturday, the exhibition “Svalbard’s Lines” by Swiss artist Daniel Rohrbasser opened at Galleri Svalbard.
148520.tags_en: culture, news, nature and the environment

148533.excerpt_en: On 19 December last year, two people lost their lives when an avalanche broke loose from Sukkertoppen after prolonged easterly winds and large amounts of snow.
148533.subtitle_en: The public prosecutor drops the case following the avalanche accident in Longyearbyen last December.

148546.excerpt_en: More than 50 children from first to ninth grade took part in the TINE football school organised by Svalbard Turn. Two coaches from the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF), Remy Uteng and Bo Folke Gustavson, had been brought in for the occasion.
148546.subtitle_en: Like newly released calves on green grass, eager football players ran around on the gravel pitch and in the ball cage outside the school this weekend.
148546.title_en: Play and learning on the football pitch

148549.excerpt_en: Six excited field inspectors stand on the quay, fully packed and ready to depart aboard “Polarsyssel” on Friday, 17 June.
148549.subtitle_en: Bjørn Eirik N. Moe resigned from his permanent position as an adviser with Troms County Municipality to work as a field inspector for two months this summer.

148575.excerpt_en: “The door is locked, the gate is closed. Everything is done for the very last time; give me your hand before you leave, sit quite still on my lap,” the children from Rypa sang last Wednesday.
148575.subtitle_en: Last week, the children said goodbye to Rypa and Longyearbyen Kindergarten. This summer, caretakers will move into the kindergarten building.

148598.excerpt_en: On Tuesday evening, Visit Svalbard invited everyone working in tourism to a ceremony marking Svalbard’s certification as a sustainable destination by Innovation Norway. Tourism director Ronny Brunvoll and deputy Community Council leader Eirik Berger (V) received the award from Minister of Trade and Industry Monica Mæland in Oslo on the 9th.
148598.subtitle_en: At last, everyone could take part in the celebration of the sustainable destination certification.

148614.excerpt_en: “I think it must have been love at first sight. The snow, the mountains, the sun, the perfectly still fjord—everything was so beautiful,” she says with a broad smile.
148614.subtitle_en: Late one April evening in 1999, Aud Andersen (45) called her mother from the airport bus on the way into Longyearbyen and said that she was going to stay here.
148614.tags_en: culture, people, Basecamp Spitsbergen, back page, Svalbard life

148620.excerpt_en: Elvesletta and other areas along Longyearelva are emerging as safe places to locate even more homes in the future. But before that can happen, flood-control measures must be implemented in the river.
148620.subtitle_en: Longyearelva will be protected against flooding at a cost of nearly NOK 20 million over the next few years.

148666.excerpt_en: The working title for the new company is Svea Spitsbergen Experience. The concept is to offer visitors to Svea a varied range of activities and services.
148666.subtitle_en: Together with Spitsbergen Travel, Store Norske will invest in tourism in Svea.
148666.tags_en: Store Norske, Svea, news, Spitsbergen Travel
148666.title_en: Store Norske enters the tourism industry

148690.excerpt_en: Two people from Asplan Viak and two local plumbers sort through rubbish bags on a large table inside the waste facility. Cathrine Lyche from Asplan Viak holds up half an ear of corn.“Should this have gone into the food-waste grinder?”
148690.subtitle_en: When some people are too poor at sorting their waste, the costs are passed on to the community. Longyearbyen Community Council is now taking action to make people more aware of waste sorting.
148690.title_en: Waste sorting is not good enough

148707.excerpt_en: It is rare for a case to go to trial in Svalbard. On Tuesday this week, one was brought before the court at Polarhotellet, after the public prosecutors for Troms and Finnmark indicted a 22-year-old woman for aggravated arson at the Northern Troms District Court.
148707.subtitle_en: The 22-year-old woman does not know why she set fire to a mattress in a storage shed on 20 March last year.

148709.excerpt_en: Erik spends the summer earning a little extra money. He plans to use it to buy a larger, better computer. “I sell fossils on the quayside to cruise tourists.”
148709.subtitle_en: Fossils, fish and litter picking are good sources of income for Erik Ekeblad Eggenfellner (14).
148709.tags_en: litter clean-up, Svalbard life, culture, people, youth

148747.excerpt_en: Earlier this year, Stein-Ove Johannesen and Leif-Arne Plahter bought Isbjørnbutikken, or the kiosk as people usually call it. They have now brought Lasse Stener Hansen into the ownership group.
148747.subtitle_en: By autumn, Isbjørnbutikken will have been converted into a takeaway and hamburger restaurant.
148747.title_en: Bringing late-night food back to town

148756.excerpt_en: The planned work to map avalanche risk around Longyearbyen will begin between 4 and 7 [date incomplete].
148756.subtitle_en: The work of mapping avalanche risk around Longyearbyen begins next week.

148783.excerpt_en: “We are Tromsø’s largest whale-watching operator and had a 100 per cent hit rate there over four months. I’m confident we’ll deliver just as well in Longyearbyen.”
148783.subtitle_en: MS “Aurora Explorer” will start whale-watching trips twice a week from August.

148804.excerpt_en: Office manager Ottar Svensen is happy to connect himself to a device that monitors heart rate, oxygen levels and blood pressure, for the photographer’s benefit. The hospital has received two such mobile, rechargeable devices as a gift from the Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators (AECO).
148804.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Hospital received vital equipment following a fundraising drive in the expedition-cruise network.

148810.excerpt_en: ›› Ole Magnus RappAccording to the Geological Survey of Norway and the Mining Inspectorate of Svalbard, the mineral deposits have been inadequately mapped.“We would very much like to carry out thorough surveys of the whole of Svalbard,” says Morten Smelror, director of the Geological Survey of Norway (NGU).Precious stonesNearly a hundred years ago, an extensive search for new mining opportunities was under way.
148810.subtitle_en: Svalbard may contain exciting minerals that the global electronics industry would pay a great deal for.
148810.title_en: – Know too little about Svalbard’s minerals

148828.excerpt_en: This week, a five-person counting team has spent its days counting reindeer in Adventdalen and its side valleys. This is part of the annual national monitoring programme that has been carried out since 1979.“Numbers fluctuate somewhat, but the overall trend is an increasing population.”
148828.subtitle_en: “Svalbard reindeer could potentially be both winners and losers as the climate changes,” says Åshild Ønvik Pedersen of the Norwegian Polar Institute.

148852.excerpt_en: An unusually large amount of rain fell overnight on Monday. The infrastructure around Longyearbyen has felt the effects.
148852.subtitle_en: The road into Endalen has been destroyed by huge volumes of water.

148873.excerpt_en: “The polar night we went through six months ago was different. It was not just dark.”
148873.subtitle_en: Svalbard parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen talks about the avalanche that claimed two lives last winter and the time afterward on Sommer i P2 on Tuesday 5 July and Wednesday 6 July.
148873.title_en: The Parish Priest on Sommer i P2

148892.excerpt_en: Anders Lindseth got the clean-up expedition started. The task was to clear the beaches at Kapp Schoultz, where LJFF has a cabin. The response was overwhelming. “We expected about ten people, but nearly 30 signed up.”
148892.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association received an overwhelming response to its clean-up expedition on Saturday.

148920.excerpt_en: The work is part of NVE’s nationwide mapping programme, but following the avalanche accident this winter, the work in Svalbard has been brought forward. “That incident revealed the need for a comprehensive assessment providing an overall picture of the avalanche risk,” says Jaran Wasrud of NVE.
148920.subtitle_en: Multiconsult has begun mapping avalanche risk in and around Longyearbyen on behalf of the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE).

148942.excerpt_en: “Spitsbergen Travel opened a new shop in central Longyearbyen on Saturday to accommodate an increase in tourism activity in Svalbard.”
148942.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Travel is taking an offensive approach and has now opened a new shop in central Longyearbyen.

148943.excerpt_en: Eight years ago, the Longyearbyen Field Biology Association (LoFF) received support from the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund to facilitate bird breeding in and around several small ponds outside the campsite at Hotellneset, southeast of Longyearbyen. Only this year have the efforts produced clear results. 130 pairs—relax.
148943.subtitle_en: Arctic terns will peck you bloody if you get too close to the nest. Now the aggressive species is having a good year in Svalbard.
148943.title_en: Record Year for the Aggressive Arctic Tern

148946.excerpt_en: Veterinarian Ragnhild Mehli has been hired on a six-month contract at Svalbard Vet.
148946.subtitle_en: This summer, Svalbard Vet has secured a temporary replacement. That is good news for Longyearbyen’s four-legged residents and their owners.
148946.title_en: Good News for the Town’s Four-Legged Residents

148971.excerpt_en: Many people know Ester from football pools and Norsk Tipping at Coop. Svalbardbutikken was her workplace for 19 years.
148971.subtitle_en: After 31 years in Longyearbyen, this is Ester Margrete Nergård’s (59) final summer. She has already begun packing, throwing things out and clearing up.

148991.excerpt_en: Katerina Zwonckova, sales and marketing manager for Trust Arktikugol’s tourism company in Longyearbyen, says they want to further develop Pyramiden as a tourist destination. Pyramiden is a Russian mining town abandoned in 1998.
148991.subtitle_en: A new floating jetty, kayaks and touring bicycles are intended to attract more tourists to Pyramiden.
148991.tags_en: news, culture, business, nature and environment
148991.title_en: Plans to Further Develop Pyramiden as a Destination

149014.excerpt_en: Neither cunning foxes nor aggressive Arctic skuas can get in here. The snowmobile will not be used for a long time and is neatly parked for summer storage.
149014.subtitle_en: Under the bonnet of a bright-red Polaris 800, a pair of snow buntings has built the town’s safest nest.
149014.title_en: A Safe Nest Among 800 Cubic Centimetres

149016.excerpt_en: The project “Isfjorden as the Most Important Area for Nature-Based Tourism in Svalbard” will be carried out by Visit Svalbard. Visit Svalbard Managing Director Ronny Brunvoll is delighted with the funding.
149016.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is providing NOK 8 million in support for a project to further develop Longyearbyen as a green tourism destination.
149016.tags_en: tourism director, business, news, Visit Svalbard, tourism

149020.excerpt_en: Hilde Haug, head of section at the Norwegian Food Safety Authority’s Troms and Svalbard office, says Benjamin L. Vidmar’s application has not been fully processed, but that strict rules generally apply to the import of animals. “We follow the Svalbard regulations.”
149020.subtitle_en: An application from Benjamin L. Vidmar of Polar Permaculture Solutions to import pigs, hens and quail is currently with the Norwegian Food Safety Authority.

149029.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has granted NOK 8 million to Visit Svalbard to develop Longyearbyen as a green tourism destination. This will accelerate existing plans to develop experiences close to town and improve the infrastructure.
149029.subtitle_en: Strong emphasis must be placed on sustainability and healthy development of the tourism industry, with high value creation, secure jobs and an attractive destination in one of the world’s most unique wilderness areas.

149049.excerpt_en: The consequences for the ecosystem are currently unclear, but could be dramatic. With such rapid change, it may be difficult to predict the effects on animals and plants, since the knowledge we have today is based on the climate conditions we have known so far.
149049.subtitle_en: Svalbard is among the areas on Earth currently experiencing the greatest and fastest climate changes—it is quickly becoming milder and wetter.

149053.excerpt_en: “Ulla Rinman” was pulled free by the Coast Guard on Thursday evening. The boat is now proceeding under its own power, escorted by the Coast Guard to Longyearbyen, says Chief Superintendent Christian Svarstad of the Governor’s office.
149053.subtitle_en: “Ulla Rinman” is being escorted by the Coast Guard from Liefdefjorden to Longyearbyen.

149115.excerpt_en: On the afternoon of 14 June, Store Norske was informed by the power plant that its electricity supply had to be restricted because a diesel generator could not be restarted after a major maintenance overhaul.
149115.subtitle_en: Mine 7 produced more than 3,000 fewer tonnes because of problems at the power plant.
149115.tags_en: Longyearbyen Local Council, news, power plant, Mine 7

149117.excerpt_en: As part of revising the zoning plan for the cabin areas, Store Norske has assessed avalanche risks in connection with development in the cabin fields.
149117.subtitle_en: Store Norske is seeing strong demand for cabin plots and has commissioned avalanche mapping of the areas to make this possible.

149134.excerpt_en: Since starting up in 1997, Svalsat has steadily expanded its operations. The company now has nearly 30 employees, and its staff continues to grow.
149134.subtitle_en: Svalsat is expanding its administration building and has awarded the contract to Sandmo & Svenkerud.

149154.excerpt_en: Lars Bremnes is one of the first artists to appear this autumn. “I’m really looking forward to playing in Longyearbyen, and I’ve heard many wonderful things about Longyearbyen as a music town.”
149154.subtitle_en: Cultural director Roger Zahl Ødegård hopes to offer Longyearbyen a vibrant autumn of varied cultural events.

149162.excerpt_en: Trond Hellstad, branch manager at SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge Svalbard, has referred the matter to the bank’s legal department in Tromsø. “It is a problem for us that the new leases contain a clause making the properties almost impossible to sell.”
149162.subtitle_en: New ground-lease agreements are causing problems for developers. SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge believes the new leases are not secure enough.

149177.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration is carrying out thorough and comprehensive work on a new port structure in Longyearbyen. Its project team has conducted 40 in-depth interviews in Longyearbyen with organizations, businesses and individuals to map needs, wishes and expectations.
149177.subtitle_en: Nearly 40 in-depth interviews have been conducted, and a meeting has been held with Longyearbyen Local Council. A new status report is due to be submitted to the Ministry of Transport and Communications at the beginning of August.
149177.tags_en: news, business, port structure, port, nature and environment

149181.excerpt_en: Sharp decline. In a normal year, there have previously been just over 3,000 breeding pairs of eiders in Kongsfjorden. But numbers have declined in recent years.
149181.subtitle_en: This year’s eider counts in Kongsfjorden show a decline in the number of breeding eiders in the fjord. Since we began systematic counts here, we have never recorded so few breeding eiders.
149181.title_en: Are Climate Changes Making Life Harder for Eiders in Svalbard?

149197.excerpt_en: “Socks, shoes, trousers… where is my SLR camera?” Jennie Olsson Qvist asks her mother, Carina Qvist, as she tries to fill her sports bag with everything she needs for the Governor’s beach-cleanup expedition.
149197.subtitle_en: When the Governor of Svalbard announced that one place had become available on this year’s beach-cleanup expedition, Jennie Olsson Qvist took action.
149197.title_en: Joined the beach-cleanup voyage at short notice

149229.excerpt_en: The dense fog over Longyearbyen is causing problems for air traffic. Since Friday evening, six scheduled flight arrivals have been affected by the weather. “Right now, we are having problems with vertical visibility.”
149229.subtitle_en: The dense fog over Longyearbyen will remain through the weekend.

149251.excerpt_en: Late on the evening of Friday, 20 March last year, the woman entered a storage room in an apartment building at Vei 222 and set fire to a foam mattress. She then went to bed.
149251.subtitle_en: The court recommends that the 22-year-old woman serve part of her two-year-and-three-month sentence at a substance-abuse treatment facility.
149251.title_en: More than two years in prison for arson

149271.excerpt_en: Several historic buildings owned by Longyearbyen Local Council were covered in graffiti on Monday night by one or more visiting tourists. It appears to have been German football hooligans who went on a spray-painting spree.
149271.subtitle_en: The graffiti is criminal damage and should be treated and punished as such.

149276.excerpt_en: In the workshop hall, Beate Flak is installing a brand-new condenser.
149276.subtitle_en: Even though it is summer and holiday season, there is plenty of activity at the power plant. Many old, rusty parts are being replaced with shiny new ones. The bill comes to NOK 52.5 million.
149276.title_en: Major overhaul at the power plant

149302.excerpt_en: At 2:30 p.m. on Monday, a German citizen born in 1986 was arrested after several buildings in Longyearbyen were covered in graffiti. The graffiti referred to the German football club SG Dynamo Dresden, which plays in Germany’s second tier. “Our view is that we got hold of the right person.”
149302.subtitle_en: The man arrested for graffiti in Longyearbyen denies criminal liability.

149306.excerpt_en: “The old spillway is small and damaged, and cannot carry away enough water during a flood,” says operations engineer Einar Olsen of Longyearbyen Local Council. This means that the road into Adventdalen is often vulnerable to flooding.
149306.subtitle_en: A new spillway will be built at Isdammen. The project has a budget of NOK 22 million and will prevent the drinking-water source from being damaged by flooding.

149340.excerpt_en: Brewing manager Andreas Hegermann Riis says he had water stored in a cistern for use in production. When he ran out, he stopped production. “Even though the treatment plant is supposed to be good and everything goes through a filter, the water is discolored.”
149340.subtitle_en: After the heavy rain last week, the water became discolored. Svalbard Brewery was unsure of its quality and temporarily halted production.
149340.title_en: Back at full speed after shutdown

149342.excerpt_en: We are at the entrance to Bjørndalen, heading up the mountainside where the little auk reigns supreme. UNIS students Ellen Kristine Keilen, Anne Bøttcher, Lydia Messingfeld and Silje Marie Kristiansen follow visiting lecturer Johanna Hovinen up the slope as if it were child’s play.
149342.subtitle_en: We joined UNIS students as they captured little auks to study how the birds contribute to Svalbard’s ecosystem.
149342.title_en: Into the realm of the little auk

149375.excerpt_en: A team of eight set out on a botanical expedition along the west coast this week. They have spent almost six months planning the trip, identifying the most suitable places to stop and collect plant and soil samples.
149375.subtitle_en: They will search for small green pockets of moss tundra to map the plants’ nutrient content.

149380.excerpt_en: Kongsfjordhallen is a three-in-one facility containing most essential amenities: heated garages for five or six large vehicles, storage for the airport’s grit, a parts warehouse serving much of the town’s needs—and, on top, a large conference hall.
149380.subtitle_en: The new community hub in Ny-Ålesund is ready to boost activity in the unique research town.

149409.excerpt_en: “It’s going extremely well,” says Terje Aunevik about the project many dismissed outright when the plans became known last autumn.
149409.subtitle_en: Svalbardi, the hugely expensive bottled water made from melted glacier ice, has been named the world’s best water. Now the company’s founder is moving to Svalbard.

149416.excerpt_en: Five years have passed since terror struck Norway. The attacks in Oslo’s government quarter and the massacre on Utøya claimed a total of 77 lives.
149416.subtitle_en: Today marks five years since terror struck Norway.
149416.title_en: Memorial service at the church after 22 July

149460.excerpt_en: At around 8 p.m. on Tuesday evening, the Governor of Svalbard received a report that a polar dog had attacked a reindeer on the plain beyond Svalbard Snowmobile Rental in Longyearbyen. “The dog got loose when its owner was getting into his car and seized the reindeer,” says senior police officer Arve Johnsen at the Governor’s Office.
149460.subtitle_en: The reindeer was so badly mauled that it had to be euthanized.

149463.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council is now laying a new water main along Hilmar Rekstens vei up to Haugen.

149474.excerpt_en: Kim Rune Røkenes and Pia Sivertsen lost their daughter Nikoline (2) when the avalanche from Sukkertoppen swept away their house last December.
149474.subtitle_en: Attorney Christian Lundin of the law firm Ness Lundin believes there may have been gross negligence in the discharge of official duties when homes were rented out despite the avalanche danger.
149474.title_en: Calls for Criminal Case over Avalanche

149516.excerpt_en: The weather is no longer what it used to be. New records continue to be set.
149516.subtitle_en: So far in July, there have been 11 summer days with a 24-hour average temperature above ten degrees. That is a July record. At the same time, a precipitation record has been set.
149516.tags_en: record, weather, nature and environment, news

149518.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has organized clean-up cruises for permanent residents ever since 2000. It is a popular initiative with many applicants.
149518.subtitle_en: Ninety-three cubic metres of rubbish were collected during the Governor of Svalbard's clean-up cruise this summer. The Norwegian Environment Agency is now intensifying efforts against marine litter.
149518.title_en: Stepping Up the Fight Against Rubbish

149542.excerpt_en: “From the outside, it will probably seem strange that we have laid off so many people and are now looking for new workers,” says Per Nilssen, mining manager at Store Norske. Miners with smoke-diving qualifications are part of an on-call rota in the voluntary emergency preparedness system.
149542.subtitle_en: Over the past year, between 10 and 15 miners with smoke-diving qualifications have resigned from Store Norske. After several rounds of redundancies, the company now has to recruit again.

149545.excerpt_en: The boats, carrying 70 kilos of supplies, are hoisted aboard K/V “Svalbard”. On the quay, two excited men watch to ensure that everything proceeds according to plan.
149545.subtitle_en: After extensive training and preparations, the day has finally arrived. Tommy Sjöö Frantzen and Jan Ivar Pettersen are ready to cover 200 nautical miles in a rowboat.
149545.tags_en: boat trip, news, nature and environment
149545.title_en: Ready for Three Full Weeks in a Rowboat

149561.excerpt_en: This week’s historic photograph comes from Kjell Farstad’s collection. He is behind the camera, while Britt Jorunn Beinset, in the middle, and the acting barracks manager at a barracks in Sverdrupbyen are on their way to Huset.
149561.subtitle_en: When Sverdrupbyen was home, people would walk this way to enjoy themselves at Huset.
149561.tags_en: historic photograph, life in Svalbard, history

149582.excerpt_en: “I think Svalbard Church is a church for everyone. It is open, simple and beautiful.”
149582.subtitle_en: Gitte Bergstuen (49) had dreamed of Svalbard since she was 20. But she had never imagined that she would experience the Arctic through a summer job as a priest.

149592.excerpt_en: Emma Johansson-Karlsson emerged as the winner of Svalbardposten's competition to guess when Stetten would go. She was the only person who guessed the 22nd.
149592.subtitle_en: Only one person guessed the correct date.

149611.excerpt_en: On Saturday morning, the Governor of Svalbard had to respond to the trapper's cabin at Austfjordnes to help remove a persistent polar bear.
149611.subtitle_en: A polar bear refused to leave the trapper's cabin at Austfjordnes.

149615.excerpt_en: On Monday, the Governor of Svalbard was at Austfjordnes to inform the trapper who shot a female polar bear on June 13 of the state prosecutor's decision.
149615.subtitle_en: The trapper who shot a female polar bear at Austfjordnes earlier this summer was fined, but will be allowed to continue trapping.

149626.excerpt_en: “She believes the case concerns criminal damage, not arson.”
149626.subtitle_en: The woman sentenced to more than two years in prison for arson in Longyearbyen is appealing the verdict.

149645.excerpt_en: At 5:45 p.m. on Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard received a tip about possible boating under the influence on a commercial sailboat with tourists aboard. The boat was stopped in Isfjorden, and the captain was subsequently taken in on suspicion of boating under the influence.
149645.subtitle_en: The captain of a sailboat carrying tourists blew over the legal limit on a breathalyser.
149645.title_en: Captain Charged with Boating Under the Influence

149649.excerpt_en: The puppies Willy and Wonka are Svalbard Husky's newest members. They are busy expanding their world, and the eight-week-old brothers happily run around the tundra and play-fight under the supervision of their “foster father”, Thomas Wegener, who works as a guide and dog driver.
149649.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Dog Club has around 100 dogs waiting for a place in a kennel. The number of dogs in Svalbard increases every year, both among private owners and in commercial operations.

149651.excerpt_en: “The episode I think is the best this season is being broadcast on the same day as the opening ceremony of the Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, so I am sure no one will watch it,” says Francisco, laughing.
149651.subtitle_en: Brazilian Francisco Mattos has been given his own documentary series about his life in the Arctic, now being broadcast on television in his home country.
149651.title_en: Finding Success in Brazil with TV Series from Svalbard

149681.excerpt_en: Several grocery chains want to enter Longyearbyen, but they all impose the same requirement. “We are continually assessing new potential markets and are not opposed to the idea of establishing ourselves in Longyearbyen. Nothing has been decided yet.”
149681.subtitle_en: Grocery stores want to establish themselves in Longyearbyen, but they will not come until Nordpolet gets its own entrance. Politicians are considering imposing requirements on Svalbardbutikken.
149681.title_en: If Rema Moves In, the Liquor Store Must Move Out

149684.excerpt_en: “We simply have to deal with the situation as it is. We just have to wait,” says Morten Helliksen, managing director of Coop Svalbard.
149684.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken was supposed to start work on its expansion this spring. Now it must wait for a new detailed plan for the town centre. They will not comment on competition.

149695.excerpt_en: “Given the current conditions, with little or no sea ice, I can only use the northern side of my trapping area during the fox-trapping season. I have only one cabin there, at Kapp Schollin,” says Sandal.
149695.subtitle_en: Trapper Tommy Sandal will set up two outposts to make fox trapping easier.

149711.excerpt_en: For more than 30 years, hunters in Svalbard have carried out substantial work collecting jaws and hunting statistics on harvested reindeer. As part of the Norwegian Polar Institute's (NP) population monitoring, hunters are now also being asked to collect carcass weights from harvested reindeer.
149711.subtitle_en: Reindeer researchers want hunters to weigh their kills in the field. (External article)
149711.title_en: Hunter Data to Provide New Knowledge

149722.excerpt_en: The dispute over having a separate entrance to Nordpolet is not new. In 2010, the issue filled Svalbardposten's columns and was also debated politically, without the arrangement being changed at the time.
149722.subtitle_en: It is important to find solutions that distort competition as little as possible.
149722.title_en: Time to Give the Liquor Store Its Own Premises

149736.excerpt_en: “We are counting on this being an investment that will secure the building for another 30 years,” says Knut Harald Holst-Hansen, director of Spitsbergen Travel, about the investment of between five and ten million kroner. Svalbard Bygg will carry out the work together with subcontractors.
149736.subtitle_en: Parts of Funken will get entirely new legs to stand on. A total of 92 piles will be drilled into the permafrost, preparing the old staff canteen for the future.

149742.excerpt_en: That is the conclusion of a report from the Norwegian Centre for Climate Services (NCCS). The report was presented in June and contains observed and projected climate changes in Svalbard.
149742.subtitle_en: This year brought record rainfall and high temperatures in July. It will become wetter and warmer. The consequences may include flooding, thawing permafrost, milder winters and less sea ice.
149742.title_en: Avalanche Risk Rises with Heavy Rainfall

149745.excerpt_en: Gun Tone Letting (51) came to Svalbard for a summer job on 2 June 1995.
149745.subtitle_en: A full container stands ready outside Reitgjerdet. Her time on Svalbard is over, and everything she has bought is to go home to Halden.

149758.excerpt_en: In this year's issue 13 of Svalbardposten, Ole Magnus Rapp writes that the eastern vole was first recorded by Finnish researchers in 1966. Really? On April 1, 1963, Kristen Bøen, Torleif Tollefsen and I set out on a week-long sled trip around Nordenskiöld Land.
149758.subtitle_en: These probably arrived before 1966, as Svalbardposten wrote earlier this year, Kjell Henrik Torp believes in this letter to the editor.
149758.title_en: Of Mice and Men and Mälardalshytta

149790.excerpt_en: According to Svalbardbutikken managing director Morten Helliksen, the flight cancellation was because the mail plane bound for Tromsø yesterday had to land at Evenes due to fog in Tromsø. “Today’s mail-plane delivery to Svalbardbutikken was supposed to include milk and other Tine products, fresh goods from Coop and Gilde, as well as vegetables.”
149790.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken warns that it will run out of milk and other fresh goods over the weekend.

149806.excerpt_en: On Tuesday and Friday, coffins containing the remains of three whalers buried at Likneset in northwestern Spitsbergen were transported to Svalbard Museum. The three are believed to have been buried there sometime between the 1600s and 1700s, and probably came from the Netherlands or England.
149806.subtitle_en: For the first time in 26 years, new archaeological excavations have been carried out at Likneset. Three graves dating back several hundred years were at risk of being claimed by the sea.

149826.excerpt_en: At around 5:30 p.m. on Saturday, a man in his 20s and a man in his 30s contacted the Governor of Svalbard because they were about to drive off the road in central Longyearbyen and needed help with the car to keep it out of the ditch. “When we arrived to help them, we also carried out a…”
149826.subtitle_en: Called the police himself for help with the car.
149826.title_en: Arrested for Drunk Driving in Town Centre

149832.excerpt_en: The SAS flight scheduled to depart at 2:45 p.m. on Tuesday was cancelled due to a technical fault. A new departure has been scheduled for 8:10 p.m.
149832.subtitle_en: A technical fault grounded Tuesday’s SAS aircraft in Longyearbyen.

149843.excerpt_en: A Russian researcher shot a polar bear at Selvågen on Prins Karls Forland. The bear was a two-year-old female weighing 155 kilos and had been tagged by the Norwegian Polar Institute.
149843.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is investigating the case.
149843.title_en: Polar Bear Shot by Russian Researcher

149847.excerpt_en: This summer, Svalbardposten has reported several records for both heat and precipitation. The fact that we have seen warmer-temperature records may not, on its own, be enough to say with certainty that the climate is changing.
149847.subtitle_en: Everyone has a responsibility to slow this development, and everyone can contribute in their own way.

149873.excerpt_en: Poli and Løyning have built up a major collection about expeditions to the North Pole from Svalbard.
149873.subtitle_en: If North Pole Expedition Museum is not used more in the coming years, owners Stefano Poli and Ingunn Løyning are considering moving the museum to a larger city.
149873.tags_en: news, museum, business, nature and environment
149873.title_en: The Buses and Millions Roll On By

149889.excerpt_en: Principal Siv Tove Sødal is taking over, while principal Anne Søvold Vikanes is moving to a new job. They will have an overlap period until the 22nd.
149889.subtitle_en: On Thursday, everyday life begins for 263 pupils in Longyearbyen with a new principal, a new vocational education program and six mainland pupils.

149902.excerpt_en: On Friday, the last two of three coffins containing the remains of whalers arrived through the back door of Svalbard Museum. The Governor of Svalbard has just completed work to save three graves that were at risk of ending up in the sea.
149902.subtitle_en: These remains were buried at Likneset 300 to 400 years ago. Now archaeologists hope the man in the coffin can reveal more about Svalbard’s earliest history.

149912.excerpt_en: We meet Mona Ada Andersen at Bykaia. She normally works for Longyearbyen Local Council, but on Saturday she was one of the volunteers who stepped in to guide the endless stream of passengers from the MSC “Splendida.” “I’ll be a bus guide for German tourists.”
149912.subtitle_en: There were so many tourists in town on Saturday that local volunteers stepped in as guides. We joined Mona Ada Andersen and a group of German tourists on a sightseeing tour through Longyearbyen.

149937.excerpt_en: “We have a tradition of sending postcards to the firm when we travel. The only thing I wrote on the card from Svalbard was: ‘Happiness is here.’”
149937.subtitle_en: Hrefna Dögg Gunnarsdóttir (32) has worked as a lawyer in Iceland since 2012. During a visit to Svalbard last year, everything changed. Almost.
149937.title_en: Combining a Legal Career with Guiding

149961.excerpt_en: The board of Coop Svalbard has decided to postpone plans to expand Svalbardbutikken. The decision follows information from Longyearbyen Local Council that the administration will not approve the framework application, but will forward it for political consideration.
149961.subtitle_en: “We hope the debate surrounding Nordpolet can reach a swift conclusion, that the detailed plan for the Central Area is a good one, and that the basis will still be in place to carry out the store expansion at a later date.”

149972.excerpt_en: “You’re suddenly on Swedish territory,” says Captain Mattias Petersson as he takes off his life jacket. He has just been out in the tender boat to check whether more research equipment has arrived for the expedition they are about to embark on, and to pick up the undersigned.
149972.subtitle_en: While Norway’s research icebreaker is still under construction, preparations are being made for Sweden’s “Oden” to make new discoveries in the ice.
149972.title_en: Preparing “Oden” to Chew Through the Ice

149977.excerpt_en: In Italy, surrounded by a construction hall and scaffolding, stands “Kronprins Haakon.” Maritime coordinator Øystein Mikelborg is also there, overseeing the project for the Norwegian Polar Institute (NPI). “It will probably be the best-equipped research vessel in the world.”
149977.subtitle_en: Norway’s new icebreaker “Kronprins Haakon” is now being fitted with advanced equipment. The vessel is expected to be ready next year.

149985.excerpt_en: From October last year until this spring, a BBC film crew followed ten locals. Taxi driver Wiggo Antonsen and his pipe have already made headlines across the country after Aftenposten and Dagbladet published a video clip of him online.
149985.subtitle_en: Ten Svalbard residents are on the verge of becoming celebrities. The BBC program “Svalbard: Life on the Edge” will show the world who we are.
149985.title_en: Svalbard Put on Display for the World

150023.excerpt_en: During a Luftransport flight on Friday, which Svalbardposten joined, it was discovered that a major landslide had occurred west of Carolinedalen, north of Longyearbyen. According to pilot Stig Onarheim, the slide occurred at Forkastningsfjellet.
150023.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard urges people to exercise caution in the terrain.

150039.excerpt_en: At approximately 9:30 a.m. on Saturday, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that a female polar bear and her cub had been spotted at Revneset. “There are quite a few cabins out there, and members of the public called to alert us.”
150039.subtitle_en: A female polar bear and her cub have been spotted at Revneset.

150043.excerpt_en: “It’s brutally hard. I ran with a heart rate of 170 almost the entire way,” says Håkon Lohne.
150043.title_en: New Race Record in the Topptrim Challenge

150051.excerpt_en: On Saturday afternoon, the Governor received a call about a bird that had become trapped. It was caught in a fishing net secured to the shore a couple of hundred metres inside Gammelkaia. “The bird was active and trying to free itself.”
150051.subtitle_en: On Saturday, the Governor freed a common eider that had become caught in a fishing net.

150062.excerpt_en: On Saturday, five archaeologists and four botanists travelled to Longyearbyen for the weekend from their camp in Advent City, where they are conducting excavations. At the same time, a mother bear and her cub were observed nearby at Revneset.
150062.subtitle_en: The mother polar bear and her cub have taken over the archaeological excavation at Advent City. After waiting for several days, the researchers are now packing up.
150062.title_en: Polar Bears Take Over Excavation Site

150084.excerpt_en: The hopeful youngsters were welcomed by principal Siv Tove Sødal and got to meet their new teachers, who had also prepared a song for the new pupils. After everyone had been called up, there was a photo session so eager parents could capture the moment.
150084.subtitle_en: On Thursday, 22 excited children started first grade at Longyearbyen School. Alexander Naalsund Berger (6) was also celebrating his birthday.
150084.title_en: The Very First Day of School

150119.excerpt_en: Over the past week, a mother polar bear and her cub have stayed at Revneset. Helene Hvedding, whose photograph appears above, has been kept indoors by the bear.
150119.subtitle_en: The mother and cub at Revneset and the bear shot on Forlandet were both local. More bears on the west coast will lead to more confrontations.
150119.tags_en: nature and environment, news, polar bear

150125.excerpt_en: “It is a serious warning when four bears have been shot and the year is not over yet. At some point, the Governor must sit down and reflect on the situation,” says Birger Amundsen.
150125.subtitle_en: So far this year, four bears have had to pay with their lives, and we must expect more encounters between bears and people. Birger Amundsen believes the Governor must take action.
150125.title_en: Believes the Shootings Are a Serious Warning

150128.excerpt_en: Entrepreneur Eivind Trondsen looks out over the power station from the corner office of Svalbard Science Destination. He has taken over the former director’s office in the Store Norske building.
150128.subtitle_en: Svalbard is to become a science destination for tourists as well. Last week, two Italians gained insight into the importance of seed banks.

150143.excerpt_en: “It will be nice when something appears in those windows,” says Lines about the large glass panes above the entrance to Lompensenteret. There, on the second floor,
150143.subtitle_en: In November, Nina Lines and Maren Bekkeheien will open “Snøstjerna.” It was born on a plane.

150171.excerpt_en: Last week, the fourth polar bear so far this year was shot on Svalbard. It is more than ten years since so many polar bears were shot here in a single year.
150171.subtitle_en: The Governor must ensure measures are taken to keep the level of conflict between polar bears and people as low as possible.

150176.excerpt_en: “This is relatively large and unusual. I have travelled extensively along Svalbard’s coast and have not observed anything similar,” says Anders Solheim, director of Natural Hazards at NGI (the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute).
150176.subtitle_en: A large rockslide has occurred in a mountain formation of sandstone and shale at Forkastningsfjellet, north of Longyearbyen.
150176.tags_en: nature and environment, rockslide, news, landslide

150210.excerpt_en: When the researchers discovered the bear, it was reportedly about 130 metres from the tent camp as the crow flies.
150210.subtitle_en: Last Tuesday, the polar bear pictured was shot by a Russian researcher at Selvågen on Prins Karls Forland.

150213.excerpt_en: “We talked about it last autumn, that it would be fun to have a hill race here,” says Nina Lines, general manager of Svalbard Turn. Now the idea has become reality, and on Saturday, August 27,
150213.subtitle_en: On Saturday, August 27, Svalbard Turn is organizing the Svalbard Spacerun hill race together with Kongsberg Satellite Services (KSAT).

150216.excerpt_en: In July, Svalbard Museum had approximately 11,000 visitors, compared with 9,000 in the same month last year. It is a new record.

150216.title_en: Record Visitor Numbers at Svalbard Museum

150231.excerpt_en: “It will be incredibly exciting to see how a school operates in the Arctic,” says Siv Tove, gazing at Platåfjellet through the office window. “It is a fantastic view. Though I suppose there will also be four months when I won’t see anything.”
150231.subtitle_en: Siv Tove Sødal (49) is passionately committed to education. That bodes well as she takes up the position of principal at Longyearbyen School.

150263.excerpt_en: Trond Ståle Rørtveit of Norsk Rikstoto visited Svalbardbutikken this week. He says the sales work being done there has attracted attention in Oslo.
150263.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken’s sales efforts have been noticed by Norsk Rikstoto.

150276.excerpt_en: The Governor was notified on Sunday evening that a local family of three aboard a recreational boat was in trouble off Kapp Laila. An unusually low tide left the boat firmly stuck on a shoal.
150276.subtitle_en: The recreational boat ran aground on a shoal. Neither the Coast Guard nor the Governor’s patrol boat could get close enough to help.

150286.excerpt_en: Senior police officers Trond Olsen and Ståle Nylund checked drivers’ blood alcohol levels, seat belts and child restraints. No one was fined, but the Governor issued a verbal order, and parents were given guidance on securing children more safely in cars.
150286.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard pulled 24 cars over by Polarflokken Kindergarten on Wednesday morning.

150296.excerpt_en: Svalbard’s long “day” is over for now. Fred Sigernes, head of the Kjell Henriksen Observatory, can confirm that. “During the night before Wednesday this week, the sun’s disk was halfway below the horizon in the minutes around midnight.”
150296.subtitle_en: The days are inexorably growing darker.
150296.tags_en: sun festival, Sun Festival Week, news, polar night, Sun Day

150313.excerpt_en: A few hundred children and adults turned up to cheer on Svalbard Turn, who played against former professional footballers Jan Åge Fjørtoft, Vidar Riseth, Erlend Johnsen and Gunnar Halle on Thursday evening. Also present was coach Egil “Drillo” Olsen, complete with rubber boots and everything.
150313.subtitle_en: On Thursday evening, a football match took place outside Svalbardhallen, with some illustrious visitors.

150328.excerpt_en: Marit Karlsen Brandal at the Innovation Norway office in Longyearbyen has received a NOK 20 million fund to give entrepreneurial activity in the town an extra boost. Recently, she has received many inquiries. “I’m now seeing a sharp increase in the number of inquiries, including from the mainland.”
150328.subtitle_en: If you have a good idea, determination and business sense, help is available.

150359.excerpt_en: When yet another mining accident struck Ny-Ålesund on November 5, 1962, it caused political chaos in Norway.
150359.subtitle_en: From mining to research in Ny-Ålesund.
150359.title_en: 50 Years Since Researchers Arrived in Svalbard

150361.excerpt_en: In performance art, artists use themselves, objects and their surroundings to convey a message or expression to an audience. Stein Henningsen has practiced the art form for several years, and last year he hosted several international artists in Longyearbyen.
150361.subtitle_en: Stein Henningsen, 53, is leading a ten-day performance festival at the end of September.
150361.title_en: Bringing Artists Together in the Arctic

150381.excerpt_en: Comments on Birger Amundsen’s book “Uten Nåde,” the chapter “Platåberget 1995,” and the incident. Why am I writing this now, 21 years after the incident?
150381.subtitle_en: Her friend corrects the account of what happened when Nina Jeanette Olaussen was killed.

150387.excerpt_en: These days, turbine 2 from the power plant is being serviced in Rotterdam. Considerable damage has been discovered on the rotor blades, resulting in additional expenses.
150387.subtitle_en: Turbine 2 at the power plant has suffered more extensive damage than initially thought. This means significantly higher costs.

150391.excerpt_en: On Tuesday this week, a team from Moss-based Power Controls AS began work that will provide Avinor with 18.3 kilowatt-hours of electricity, completely free, from the sun. “We will install solar panels on a south-facing wall and on the roof, oriented east–west,” says the company’s project manager, Dag Halvorsen.
150391.subtitle_en: Installing solar panels on the airport roof is only the beginning.
150391.title_en: Avinor to Get Power from the Sun

150399.excerpt_en: This autumn, Svalbard Turn will get a new website and a new logo. It will be shared by the sports club, Svalbard Marathon and other events held under its auspices.
150399.subtitle_en: Today, members of Svalbard Turn will decide whether the sports club should change its name.

150431.excerpt_en: Considering that Longyearbyen has around 2,000 permanent residents, it seems utterly extraordinary that there are 24 liquor licenses among us. Fortunately, the heavy tourist traffic is the main reason so many establishments can serve alcohol profitably.
150431.subtitle_en: “There certainly are a lot of watering holes in this town,” said Eirik Berger (V) as the Administration Committee renewed 24 liquor licenses.
150431.tags_en: drug and alcohol policy action plan, licensed premises, news

150433.excerpt_en: Lundin of the law firm Ness Lundin DA is assisting Kim Rune Røkenes and Pia Sivertsen, who lost their two-year-old daughter Nikoline in the avalanche. Their older daughter, four, was also caught in the snow, but survived.
150433.subtitle_en: Assistance lawyer Christian Lundin believes Store Norske and Longyearbyen Local Council were grossly negligent before last December’s avalanche.

150437.excerpt_en: On Monday, Trine Skei Grande (V), the parliamentary rapporteur for the Svalbard white paper, will take part in a public meeting at the culture centre in Longyearbyen. It is an important opportunity for everyone who wants to provide input on the white paper presented this spring.
150437.subtitle_en: “It is important now that residents get involved.”
150437.title_en: Svalbard White Paper on the Agenda

150449.excerpt_en: “Now we’re just waiting for the equipment we need to arrive,” says form teacher Tom Robert Nyvoll Hansen. Together with students Kim Balisado, Erik Fastvold, Steffen Rognmo, Erlend Nes, Arthur Andersen and Ole Sondre Holte Gunhilberget, he cleared space on Tuesday in the old fire station next to the power plant.
150449.subtitle_en: Six school students have chosen building and construction technology as their upper-secondary track. The programme is new in Svalbard this year.
150449.title_en: Clearing Their Way into the Workshop

150464.excerpt_en: The Airbus AS332L1 rescue helicopter, better known as the Super Puma, takes off from Svalbard Airport. On board are Captain Oddvar Instanes, copilot Stig Onarheim, rescue technician Stein Sætermo, hoist operator Eldar Rotihaug and systems operator Olav Bjørke.
150464.subtitle_en: We joined Lufttransport on a training exercise to find out what it is like to provide search and rescue services in Svalbard.

150492.excerpt_en: “I was too young to remember what it was like growing up here, but the way I feel about it, we had a good life,” says Birger-Johan. His father had worked as a trapper for two or three years before getting a job as a mine foreman at Store Norske.
150492.subtitle_en: Birger-Johan Lund was born in Svalbard on August 21, 1936. Last weekend, he returned to celebrate his 80th birthday.

150494.excerpt_en: Lars Ole Saugnes, chief administrative officer of Longyearbyen Local Council (LL), has now handed over the baton to Elin Dolmseth. He is moving south and taking up a position as municipal chief executive in Gran Municipality. “I’ve turned 60, and if I was going to have another exciting job, it had to be now.”
150494.subtitle_en: Chief Administrative Officer Lars Ole Saugnes had his last day in Longyearbyen on Friday.

150517.excerpt_en: Dry and relatively cold weather, with quite a bit of wind, greeted participants in the first Svalbard Spacerun on Saturday. There was a good atmosphere before the recreational race started from the Cableway Central Station.
150517.subtitle_en: Fifteen-year-old Marius Bakke from Søgne in Vest-Agder left everyone behind in the first Svalbard Spacerun. He crossed the finish line in splendid isolation.

150526.excerpt_en: A female polar bear and her cub were spotted in the Foxdalen cabin area on Friday. The Governor’s Office responded by helicopter and scared the bears to the other side of the valley, and on Saturday morning the bears were at Innerhytta.
150526.subtitle_en: “We hope the bears have gone into a side valley towards Sassen,” says Senior Police Officer Irene Sætermoen at the Governor’s Office.

150543.excerpt_en: “We ask people to keep away from the area. We are monitoring the situation closely and assessing whether measures should be taken to drive the bears away,” writes Senior Police Officer Ole Jakob Malmo on the Governor’s Office website.
150543.subtitle_en: Two days after the “Tempelfjord female” and her cub disappeared from Innerhytta, she has turned up at Hiorthamn.

150557.excerpt_en: “The animals are now heading towards Diabas. It looks as though they are responding well to the deterrence,” says Senior Police Officer Bjørn Pedersen at the Governor’s Office.
150557.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has succeeded in scaring the female polar bear and her cub away from the cabin areas at Hiorthamn and Revneset.

150563.excerpt_en: It was a close race between Svalbard Turn and Svalbard IL at first, but when the final votes were counted, it became clear that the sports club would keep its name. Svalbard Turn received nine votes, against six for Svalbard IL.
150563.subtitle_en: Svalbard Turn or Svalbard IL. Fifteen people attended the general meeting and voted on the club’s future name on Tuesday evening.
150563.title_en: A Close Race over the Name

150574.excerpt_en: On Friday evening, the Governor of Svalbard was informed by a cabin owner in the Foxdalen cabin area that a polar bear was lying close to his cabin. It was a female with a cub, and is believed to be the so-called “Tempelfjord female,” which was staying at Revneset a couple of weeks ago.
150574.subtitle_en: The “Tempelfjord female” and her cub are staying near Innerhytta.

150587.excerpt_en: One of them is editor Hilde Røsvik. “It’s a big party, with 1,500 people invited. Now people are starting to trickle in.”
150587.subtitle_en: Around 20 residents from Svalbard are now in the Queen’s Park by the Royal Palace.

150589.excerpt_en: Trine Skei Grande (V), rapporteur for the Svalbard white paper, spent four days in Longyearbyen gathering feedback on the paper presented this spring. She met with several businesses, the business association, the research and education community, the leadership of Longyearbyen Community Council, local politicians, the Governor of Svalbard, trade unions and the management of Store Norske.
150589.subtitle_en: The white paper being presented should be more concrete about what the state actually wants and can contribute.

150593.excerpt_en: “I have received many clear messages. We must build a good enough port and ensure that the tourism industry has the opportunity to develop, including with regard to how we enforce environmental legislation,” Skei Grande says of some of the main challenges raised with her.
150593.subtitle_en: After four hectic days of meetings in Longyearbyen, Trine Skei Grande has many challenges and contributions for the Svalbard white paper written down.

150603.excerpt_en: When the 15 Post-it notes had been drawn from the bowl and the votes counted on Tuesday, it became clear that Svalbard Turn would retain the name the sports club adopted in 1930. “With a clear majority, we have made a historic choice.”
150603.subtitle_en: Of the 850 members, 15 showed up to decide the historically important question: Should Svalbard Turn become Svalbard IL?

150615.excerpt_en: From last autumn until this spring, Svalbard Vet’s capacity was stretched to the limit. “In connection with the summer holiday period, I hired a veterinarian on a six-month contract. That is as long as I know I can afford to pay a salary,” says general manager and veterinarian Astrid Vaag Vikaune.
150615.subtitle_en: On Sunday, Svalbard Vet met with Trine Skei Grande (V) about the need for an on-call veterinary service.

150635.excerpt_en: Around 80 people attended the public meeting on the new Svalbard white paper on Monday. There were ample opportunities to offer input to the white paper’s parliamentary rapporteur, Trine Skei Grande, which she can take back to the Storting before it is considered.
150635.subtitle_en: Most of the contributions were things both Trine Skei Grande and the gathering had heard before.
150635.title_en: Not much new to take away

150647.excerpt_en: On Tuesday this week, Per Lund and Tom Jørgensen of Norkring began installing the DAB transmitter in Telenor’s building at Skjæringa.
150647.subtitle_en: The first broadcasts in the new radio format could be heard this week.

150662.excerpt_en: The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) spent more than seven months in total in Longyearbyen, from last autumn until this spring. The result is the documentary series “Ice Town: Life on the Edge”, which will be shown on BBC Earth every Monday for the foreseeable future.
150662.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen residents appreciated the first two episodes of the BBC documentary series about the world’s northernmost urban community.

150679.excerpt_en: Store Norske never applied for a change of use before it began using Mine 3 as a museum and tourist attraction. Earlier this summer, Longyearbyen Community Council asked it to apply, while warning that it could halt use of the facility.
150679.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council initially announced that use of Mine 3 would cease, but is now granting temporary permission for tourist tours.

150680.excerpt_en: Per Arne Totland is a longtime journalist, business adviser and author with a strong commitment to Svalbard. In his latest book, “Kaldfront”, launched on Monday, he examines Norwegian Svalbard policy over a hundred years.
150680.subtitle_en: Conflicts between Norway and Russia over Svalbard are not like other conflicts. And the Svalbard white paper does not address the real issues.

150707.excerpt_en: Like an Ultima Thule, they lie there with their secrets and myths. No one has really seen them up close, and scarcely any facts about them exist.
150707.subtitle_en: Like an Ultima Thule, they lie there with their secrets and myths. We are talking about glacier fronts—beyond the boundaries of the known world.

150755.excerpt_en: A fishing boat located the sailboat, with a 20-year-old man from Bodø aboard, 10–12 nautical miles northwest of Sørøya in Finnmark. The Joint Rescue Coordination Centre of Northern Norway told NRK.

150757.subtitle_en: The sailboat “Argo”, with one man aboard, is missing on its journey to Svalbard. The Joint Rescue Coordination Centre of Northern Norway is concerned.

150830.excerpt_en: The final list of applicants for the position of chief administrative officer at Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) contained 30 names. By the application deadline, there had been 47 applicants.
150830.subtitle_en: Many want to become chief administrative officer of Longyearbyen Local Council.

150842.excerpt_en: Endrine Øsby (5), Pernille Røkenes (4) and Emma Kleczka (5) are standing on the deck of the “Polar Girl”. They are ready for Polarflokken’s eighth rubbish-collecting expedition—and to appear in the newspaper.
150842.subtitle_en: The children at Polarflokken nursery want to prevent animals from ingesting plastic and dying.

150859.excerpt_en: Svalcom is a newly established company in Longyearbyen. It is so new that so far it has only around one-third of its employees in place. “In the long term, we aim to have 15–20 employees.”

150872.excerpt_en: He assured attendees that the Government would encourage creativity, while stressing the importance of preserving Longyearbyen’s distinctive character. “Longyearbyen should not be developed into a cradle-to-grave community; living here should be different from living on the mainland,” the minister said.
150872.subtitle_en: Svalbard Minister Anders Anundsen said Svalbard had shown that it was highly adaptable when he opened the Friske fraspark conference.

150882.excerpt_en: Fourteen Svalbard residents attended the royal couple’s garden party in Queen’s Park. Bendicte Klyve was one of the lucky guests who got to shake the King’s hand. “What did the King say?” “He thanked me for congratulating him on the anniversary.”
150882.subtitle_en: The royal couple’s garden party was a warm encounter between the people and the royals.
150882.title_en: A heartfelt meeting with the King
