150930.excerpt_en: The new station manager at the Norwegian Mapping Authority’s new geodetic station in Ny-Ålesund followed a personal longing when he accepted the job. He spent 20 years growing up in Longyearbyen and on Svalbard, and almost 25 years after leaving the archipelago, he wants to relive the paradise of his childhood.
150930.subtitle_en: Since leaving Svalbard as a teenager, Stig Pedersen (47) has thought about the archipelago every single day.
150930.title_en: The bug that never went away

150948.excerpt_en: “Students can come to us with major and minor problems such as concentration difficulties, exam nerves, relationship problems, loneliness, problems with their parents, anxiety or depression,” says psychologist Hanne Rieber. “Anything connected with coping with life,” says social worker and student counsellor Tone Toft.
150948.subtitle_en: UNIS students can receive free help from a psychologist and counsellor at the Student Counselling Service in Tromsø.

150957.excerpt_en: Inside the waste facility in Longyearbyen, project manager Jannike Falk-Andersson of Norut is holding a registration form and speaking through an interpreter with a Russian fisherman. “We have found a large trawl bag that was tied up and deliberately dumped,” she says.
150957.subtitle_en: Tons of rubbish end up on Svalbard’s beaches. Now researchers, with the help of industry, will find out why it ends up here and what can be done to prevent it.

150970.excerpt_en: Hunting rock ptarmigan has a long tradition on Svalbard. It probably began with overwintering trapping in the 19th century; today, many permanent residents, some visitors and a handful of trappers hunt ptarmigan.
150970.subtitle_en: While researchers’ counts show more ptarmigan, hunters are shooting fewer birds.
150970.title_en: What does the red hunting data say about the state of Svalbard rock ptarmigan?

151052.excerpt_en: The black-and-white dog belongs in Longyearbyen and is half Greenland dog. Now, more than a month after disappearing, it is still loose in the terrain.
151052.subtitle_en: A dog went missing from its owners near Fredheim at the end of July. It was spotted again on Sunday, but could not be caught.
151052.title_en: Dog on the Loose Since July

151083.excerpt_en: “We thrive here. There are many great activities, little logistics and we are not caught in the proverbial time squeeze that affects so many others,” says the young mother.
151083.subtitle_en: Perhaps it was her urge to explore that prompted Ane Hammervoll Bjørsvik (40) to move to Svalbard? After eight years in Longyearbyen, she has no plans to move back to the mainland.
151083.title_en: Young Mother with a Twinkle in Her Eye

151106.excerpt_en: Researchers and students connected to a biology course at UNIS have just returned from an expedition—one that aimed to gain insight into an environment very few people have previously been able to study at close range: glacier fronts.
151106.subtitle_en: Researchers and students connected to a biology course at UNIS have just returned from an expedition—one that aimed to gain insight into an environment very few people have previously been able to study at close range: glacier fronts.

151156.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen is Telenor’s showcase. This month, the company completed its latest major upgrade.

151188.excerpt_en: After Longyearbyen Local Council and Store Norske had discussed who was responsible for avalanche prevention in Longyearbyen for an extended period, it became clear in 2013 that NVE would assume that role.
151188.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) was given responsibility for avalanche prevention in Longyearbyen in 2013, but did not prioritise the work.

151195.excerpt_en: Christian Lundin, a lawyer at Ness Lundin DA, says the DSB report confirms what the bereaved have believed so far. “Both Longyearbyen Local Council and Store Norske were aware of the avalanche danger when they entered into an agreement in 2008, but neither took responsibility for following it up.”
151195.subtitle_en: Lundin, the victims’ assistance lawyer, believes the DSB report supports Longyearbyen Local Council’s and Store Norske’s liability for compensation. They have not yet taken a position on the claim.

151221.excerpt_en: “We were notified of the incident shortly after 9.30 last night. We assisted with ‘Polarsyssel’,” says Bjørn Pedersen, senior police officer at the Governor’s Office.

151234.excerpt_en: At around 7 p.m. on Sunday evening, the Governor was notified that an Alaska husky had escaped.
151234.subtitle_en: The Governor once again urges people to keep their dogs under control.

151247.excerpt_en: Fisheries Minister Per Sandberg is hosting this year’s symposium. With His Royal Highness Crown Prince Haakon at the forefront, international researchers and business leaders are gathering to discuss how the ocean can help solve global challenges linked to the growing need for food, medicine and energy.
151247.subtitle_en: This year’s symposium opens in Ny-Ålesund today. The theme is how research and innovation can contribute to sustainable growth.

The scenario involved a plane experiencing problems while approaching Svalbard Airport and landing outside the runway, injuring ten people. “We are practising the acute phase, organising the accident site, evacuation and treatment.”
151281.subtitle_en: The emergency services held an exercise together with Avinor.

151292.excerpt_en: The starting signal for this year’s Oktoberfest was given on Thursday afternoon with a parade through Longyearbyen. This is the eighth edition of the festival, which was first held in 2009.
151292.subtitle_en: They braved the cold weather and opened Oktoberfest with a parade and lederhosen.

151308.excerpt_en: “They said they were professional chefs, but they were not,” says Wiggo Lund, chairman of Taste of Thai. He adds that it is with a heavy heart that he and his wife, Rung-Arun Sianglam, are sending them home.
151308.subtitle_en: Wiggo Lund, chairman of Taste of Thai, says the café employees did not know how to do the work they were supposed to do.

151342.subtitle_en: LPO Arkitekter has been in Longyearbyen for five years and is now hiring more staff to help shape the town of the future.

151357.subtitle_en: Passenger flights to Svalbard in the 1960s: Meteorological requirements for flight.

151387.excerpt_en: For student council president Andreas Alexander from Kaufbeuren, Germany, it is important that everyone is well looked after. He and the council’s 12 other members play an important role in making sure of that. “A lot of it is about students getting involved in their own academic lives.”
151387.subtitle_en: A total of 452 new students have now begun the autumn semester at UNIS. The university’s student population increased by around 100 in the 2016 calendar year compared with the previous year, and the total is now approaching 800 students over the course of a year.

151400.excerpt_en: Today, only three per cent of the world’s food production comes from the ocean, even though the ocean covers 75 per cent of the planet. How the ocean can provide more food for the planet’s steadily growing population was one of the issues highlighted during the symposium.
151400.subtitle_en: Researchers, politicians and industry leaders from 15 different nations gathered to share knowledge about how the ocean can help solve global challenges.

151406.excerpt_en: “Last year, we were at around 45 percent. We have not calculated the exact figure for this year, but it appears to have increased somewhat,” says Frank Nilsen, acting director of UNIS.
151406.subtitle_en: UNIS is taking steps to comply with the Ministry of Education’s directive that around 50 percent of its students should be affiliated with Norwegian universities on the mainland.

151409.excerpt_en: The plane lands in Longyearbyen at 2:00 a.m. on Thursday and returns at
151409.subtitle_en: From 19 October, SAS will introduce evening flights on Wednesdays.

151421.excerpt_en: At the end of October, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) will receive the avalanche-mapping report prepared by Multiconsult on behalf of NVE.
151421.subtitle_en: In one month, NVE and Longyearbyen Local Council will receive the avalanche-protection report. It could lead to considerable changes in the town.
151421.tags_en: news, avalanche protection, nature and environment, NVE

151452.excerpt_en: The tourists aboard the boat’s final trip of the season were given a two-hour stop in the Russian town, while the kindergarten and schoolchildren were allowed on board for a trip out into the fjord. “It’s a lot of fun.”
151452.subtitle_en: Last Thursday, the children of Barentsburg were, as is tradition, invited on a boat trip aboard the “Polargirl.”
151452.title_en: Boat Trip for the Children in Barentsburg

151470.excerpt_en: “I’m really looking forward to it. This will be exciting,” says Hege Walør Fagertun, Longyearbyen Local Council’s new chief administrative officer. The 50-year-old was selected from among 48 applicants and will start the job on 1.
151470.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council’s new chief administrative officer comes from the position of municipal chief executive in Bardu municipality.
151470.tags_en: Longyearbyen Local Council, news, chief administrative officer
151470.title_en: Looking Forward to the Top Job

151507.excerpt_en: A polar dog escaped from its owner in July and has been observed intermittently in the Sassen area ever since. The Governor searched for the dog by helicopter without success until today. “The dog was spotted while a helicopter was out on a training mission.”
151507.subtitle_en: The Governor saw no alternative but to shoot the dog that escaped from its owner in July.

151543.excerpt_en: Ronny Brunvoll, tourism director at Visit Svalbard, accepted the nomination in Ljubljana. “We’re very proud of this recognition of the good sustainability work being done locally, even though we acknowledge that we still have a long way to go.”
151543.subtitle_en: Svalbard has been nominated for the “Top 100 Green Destinations” list, featuring the 100 best green destinations in the world.

151560.excerpt_en: At the Storting’s open hearing on the Svalbard White Paper on Thursday morning, Devold outlined ABB’s view of Svalbard’s future energy supply.
151560.subtitle_en: ABB technology director Håvard Devold believes a power cable to Svalbard is a good alternative to continuing to burn coal.
151560.title_en: Calls for Study of Power Cable

151587.excerpt_en: Having been wrapped in plastic, she “unwrapped herself” and left a trail of plastic across the entire public square. Rasmussen is one of ten artists who took part in the Arctic Action performance festival in Longyearbyen over the past week.
151587.subtitle_en: It was Saturday afternoon when Danish artist Lilibeth Cuenca Rasmussen performed her performance art in the square in Longyearbyen.
151587.title_en: Wrapped Up in the Town Centre

151612.excerpt_en: “We got to ride with the siren on.” “This truck is much taller than yours, Dad.” “It was a good thing there wasn’t a fire while we were along. Then we would have had to put it out.”
151612.subtitle_en: Many boys and girls dream of becoming firefighters. Last weekend, even more such dreams were born.
151612.tags_en: open day, Longyearbyen Fire Service, news, magazine
151612.title_en: Few Things Are More Fun Than a Ride in a Red Fire Engine

151648.excerpt_en: Tough for you, Hilde, even after all these years. I spent a few seasons in Longyearbyen as a mine mechanic at Mine 7.
151648.subtitle_en: “We were a little older and very lucky.”

151671.excerpt_en: “This is not something you should call a road. It’s really bad,” says Rune Moen, pointing to the road leading towards Bjørndalen.
151671.subtitle_en: Svalbard Maxi Taxi avoids trips to Bjørndalen wherever possible. General manager Rune Moen is anything but satisfied with the roads in Longyearbyen.

151681.excerpt_en: “We’re really enjoying it,” say Ingvild Birkely (16), Sina Joten Søndmør (17), Leïa Bescond (17), Solveig Thoresen (17), Teodor Dahl Knutsen (17) and Øyvind Fæste (18).
151681.subtitle_en: This year, six students from the mainland are attending Longyearbyen School. The arrangement helps strengthen the educational offering in Longyearbyen.

151718.excerpt_en: “I remember being angry when Dad got a job in Svalbard and we were going to move here. But now you can see how it turned out,” Tove says with a laugh.
151718.subtitle_en: Tove Bendiksen (41) has lived in Longyearbyen since she was eight. Now she is ready to try something new and is moving away.

151729.excerpt_en: Population statistics for Svalbard show a slight overall increase. During the past six months, the population of the settlements in Longyearbyen, Ny-Ålesund and Barentsburg has increased by 13.
151729.subtitle_en: Over three years, Longyearbyen has seen 60 fewer daycare children.

151750.excerpt_en: This week’s historic image was taken in the late 1950s. At the time, Store Norske was carrying out exploration work at Mine 4, at the head of Longyeardalen.
151750.subtitle_en: From the exploration of Mine 4 at the head of Longyeardalen.

151784.excerpt_en: On Thursday, the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence held a hearing on the parliamentary white paper on Svalbard. The first to speak was the local council, represented by its leader Arild Olsen (Labour). “First, I must emphasise that these are the local council leader’s own descriptions.”
151784.subtitle_en: The Conservative Party, Liberals and Greens object to Local Council leader Arild Olsen not speaking on behalf of the council during Thursday’s hearing on the Svalbard white paper.
151784.title_en: Fellow Politicians React to Solo Statement

151801.excerpt_en: Snow fell heavily at times throughout Monday, accompanied by gusts of wind. This weather will continue for a while yet. “The snowfall is partly due to northerly winds, which brought some snow with them.”
151801.subtitle_en: Monday’s intense snowfall is deceptive. Winter is not here yet.

151803.excerpt_en: In its white paper on Svalbard, the government advocates strengthening Norwegian hosting and coordination of research activities in Ny-Ålesund. As part of this effort, it therefore proposes allocating NOK 20.5 million for a new building to be shared by researchers and research institutions. “Interest in conducting research in Svalbard is growing.”
151803.subtitle_en: In the national budget, the government proposes allocating NOK 20.5 million for a new building for joint research in Ny-Ålesund.
151803.title_en: NOK 20.5 Million for New Research Building

151830.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten previously reported that NOK 7 million would go towards strengthening the Governor’s police department with three positions, to enhance control and presence at Svalbard Airport and improve emergency preparedness in general.
151830.subtitle_en: The government expects interest in Svalbard to increase and the Governor of Svalbard to receive more high-level political visitors. As a result, funding has been allocated for four new police positions.

151833.excerpt_en: This year, UNIS received NOK 125.6 million through the national budget. For next year, this has been adjusted for inflation to NOK 128.9 million.
151833.subtitle_en: The Research Council of Norway will receive NOK 10 million more to spend in Svalbard, but UNIS will not receive funding to expand under next year’s proposed national budget.

151845.excerpt_en: “The Norwegian Coastal Administration has been tasked with assessing the concept proposed by Longyearbyen Local Council to upgrade port infrastructure. The Coastal Administration’s report is scheduled to be ready in October 2016.” This is the only mention of the port in the government’s proposed national budget for next year.
151845.subtitle_en: The development of Longyearbyen port is barely mentioned in the proposed national budget.
151845.title_en: Port Plans Up in the Air

151854.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen is going through a challenging period, with society entirely dependent on new industries and business activity for the population to grow and the number of Norwegians to remain stable. Several measures have already been launched to promote new business development in the town.
151854.subtitle_en: Cumbersome bureaucracy that makes processes take far too long is the last thing we need right now.

151857.excerpt_en: Svalbard Bygg has received both a framework permit and a start-up permit for a new office and warehouse building. Now the windows are in storage and the foundations are ready for installation on the site between the fire station and the ISS building in Sjøområdet. “Of course, this is a major setback for us.”
151857.subtitle_en: Everything was ready for a new office and warehouse building. Then the bank stopped Svalbard Bygg in its tracks.

151881.excerpt_en: “Feminists are not only concerned with women’s issues. We care about equality between the genders, no matter what.”
151881.subtitle_en: Malin Nilssen Alexandersen (17) does not know what she wants to be when she grows up. But she is absolutely certain that she is a feminist.
151881.tags_en: people, life in Svalbard, back page

151886.excerpt_en: The finance manager at Basecamp Spitsbergen AS is one of 12 people selected for Agenda Northern Norway’s ambassador programme.
151886.subtitle_en: Western Norwegian Merete Nordheim (29) is passionate about Northern Norway and will champion Svalbard’s interests over the coming year.

151895.excerpt_en: Developers holding the new standard ground-rent agreements, introduced on 16 November 2015, are the ones who are not being granted loans.
151895.subtitle_en: SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge has still not received clarification from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries concerning the new leases for real property. It is therefore not granting loans to customers who hold these new plots.

151909.excerpt_en: “We are ready to drive the piles into the ground now, and are only waiting for a start-up permit from Longyearbyen Local Council (LL).”
151909.subtitle_en: The construction fence is up, and the first shovel can soon be put in the ground for a new hotel at Elvesletta. Svalbard Adventure Group will operate the hotel.
151909.title_en: Hotel Construction Set to Begin at Elvesletta

151921.excerpt_en: Today, Longyearbyen’s two daycare centres are packed, and one child is on the waiting list. Twenty-two births are expected during the year.
151921.subtitle_en: Politicians want a plan for where temporary daycare places could be provided, but they want to shield the youth centre (Uhu).

151948.excerpt_en: Archaeologist Arild Skjærveland Vivås is the project’s field leader. He has put on a white coat and gloves.
151948.subtitle_en: A tall, fair, long-haired man is retrieved and documented piece by piece. This summer’s emergency excavation ensured that he could tell his story.
151948.title_en: Bringing the Whaling Story Out of the Grave

151964.excerpt_en: Silje Hagen got the idea at Aktiv i friluft after driving to Skjæringa, where the Governor’s environmental department is based. “There was a lot of rubbish on the slope below the Governor’s office. I think the signal it sends is a little wrong,” says project manager Silje Hagen of Aktiv i friluft.
151964.subtitle_en: When the snow melts in spring, hopefully no old sins will reappear.

151968.excerpt_en: Trym was the only participant from Svalbard Turn at the national swimming championships for people with intellectual disabilities in Stavanger on the 24th and 25th.
151968.subtitle_en: Proud 14-year-old Trym Eide Aunevik returned home with five gold and two silver medals after a swimming meet in Stavanger.

151978.excerpt_en: This week’s historical picture was taken in 1958 or 1959. The location is the common room at Mine 4.
151978.subtitle_en: Lively conversation in the common room.
151978.tags_en: historical picture, life in Svalbard, history

151985.excerpt_en: “Bruk Hue” is Norway’s largest anti-bullying tour, visiting schools across the country to discuss cyberbullying. On 29 September, a global campaign against cyberbullying was held, with events in both Europe and Asia.
151985.subtitle_en: Last Thursday, sixth- and seventh-graders at Longyearbyen School took part in a global campaign against cyberbullying.

152027.excerpt_en: “It is important to look after nature, and it is better for the animals when there is not so much rubbish lying around.” Tiril Hermansen (9) and Astrid Andersen (7) clearly understand why they are helping to pick up rubbish in town on Sunday.
152027.subtitle_en: Many people helped make the town cleaner on Sunday.
152027.title_en: A Strong Desire to Clean Up

152075.excerpt_en: Svalbard Husky has worked on this issue and expressed its interest at an early stage, but is somewhat bemused by the process now being initiated. In every other respect, the Governor is careful to emphasize that the policy in the White Paper …
152075.subtitle_en: As a desired business in Svalbard, Svalbard Husky AS does not consider itself able to meet the criteria for an application at present.
152075.title_en: Establishing Commercial Cabins and Temporary Facilities in Tourism

152087.excerpt_en: My name is Silje Marie Våtvik, and I am so ashamed to be Norwegian over the decision concerning wolf hunting. I grew up in Svalbard.
152087.subtitle_en: I support a healthy natural environment and have always seen myself as a polar-bear ambassador. Now I have also become a wolf ambassador!

152089.excerpt_en: Arnt Vegar Jensen was quick to come out in defense of the owner of Taste of Thai following Svalbardposten’s report two weeks ago. This concerns a personnel matter and possible breaches of the Working Environment Act that have been given column space in the local newspaper.
152089.subtitle_en: In his role as ombudsman, Jensen adopts a top-down attitude when he practically gives the public a lesson in foreigners’ rights in Svalbardposten.

152103.excerpt_en: “I have been looking forward to this for a long time,” says the new UNIS director with a broad smile. His first week has been packed with meetings and introductions to many new people.
152103.subtitle_en: On Sunday, new UNIS director Harald Ellingsen moved to Longyearbyen. A new office, a new apartment and an exciting job await him.
152103.title_en: Engaged Director Meets Students at UNIS

152111.excerpt_en: Mobakken started in a newly created two-year project position in August. She has spent her first months getting to know the town and its businesses. “I have visited almost all the businesses here.”
152111.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council’s new business adviser, Kirstin Lillevåg Mobakken, is focused on building business relationships that can produce results both in the short and long term.

152119.excerpt_en: “We planned to open an online store around this time last year. The idea was to have it ready for Christmas.”
152119.subtitle_en: Chocolate grams and gift boxes can now be ordered online and sent both to mainland Norway and locally in Longyearbyen.
152119.tags_en: Fruene, chocolate, news, online store, business

152170.excerpt_en: This week’s historical picture was taken in 1958 and, like the pictures from the preceding weeks, comes from the common room at Mine 4. Since the men in the picture have no coal dust on their faces or hands, we must assume they are waiting to start their shift.
152170.subtitle_en: Mine 4 crew before the start of their shift.
152170.tags_en: historical picture, life in Svalbard, history

152173.excerpt_en: Together with her older sister Hedda, mother Ingrid and father Erlend, the ten-year-old was visiting Longyearbyen for three days.
152173.subtitle_en: “It was really cool to see the old skeleton. Imagine, those are the bones of someone who lived an incredibly long time ago,” said Emma Gutvik Einarsen (10).

152175.excerpt_en: “A Meaningful Trip” was the title of Aktiv i friluft Longyearbyen’s autumn community cleanup last weekend. The initiative was spearheaded by project manager Silje M.
152175.subtitle_en: Roofing felt, insulation, broken glass, bags and cigarette butts. The cleanup crew left nothing behind.
152175.tags_en: beach cleanup expedition, cleanup expedition, magazine, active outdoors, news

152206.excerpt_en: He drinks green tea and eats Fruene’s chocolate as he talks. His smile comes easily, as does his laughter.
152206.subtitle_en: Snorre W. Steen, 44, was where he wanted to be while his heart stood still. Everything was fine.

152208.excerpt_en: Sometime between 1920 and 1960, eastern field voles arrived at the Russian settlement of Grumantbyen. They probably came as stowaways aboard ships carrying hay and straw for the animals there.
152208.subtitle_en: Researchers will, for the first time, check whether a deadly parasite is present in dogs in Longyearbyen and whether it poses a health risk to humans.

152212.excerpt_en: “This time, we have conducted an inspection and collected the basis for an avalanche assessment of the cabin areas. It was good to have a helicopter inspection, and we had excellent flying and helicopter conditions,” says engineering geologist Maria Hannus of Multiconsult.
152212.subtitle_en: Multiconsult has carried out an avalanche assessment in the cabin areas. The avalanche report for the cabin fields will be ready during December.

152233.excerpt_en: On board were five girls from Svea who were heading to an autumn party in Ny-Ålesund, along with the pilot. Eyewitnesses said the plane climbed steeply after taking off from the airport and suddenly lost altitude.
152233.subtitle_en: Tuesday marked 30 years since six people died when a light aircraft crashed near the airport in Longyearbyen.

152259.excerpt_en: Darkness is falling, and the blue notes that signal the start of the dark season are not far away. “We have a fantastic lineup this year as well, with 15 bands from eight different countries,” says festival director Espen Helgesen of Dark Season Blues. He points to two major draws from England.
152259.subtitle_en: In just under two weeks, 15 bands will take over 14 of the town’s venues during Dark Season Blues. For the third time, the festival has been nominated for the European Festival Awards.
152259.title_en: Into the Darkness with Blue Notes

152292.excerpt_en: Every autumn, large numbers of songbirds on the mainland migrate south to survive the winter. Some of them, especially first-time migrant juveniles, navigate in the wrong direction or are blown off their usual route by strong winds that carry them north.
152292.subtitle_en: Rare songbirds are most often seen in Longyearbyen this month.

152301.excerpt_en: On Sunday, 9 October, I finally sat down with Svalbardposten for 30.
152301.subtitle_en: Peder Åsmund was one of the first people to be born during overwintering in Svalbard.
152301.title_en: In Memory of Peder Åsmund Pedersen

152314.excerpt_en: “Yes, I have enough to get by. But the tax lists do not tell the whole truth,” says Turid Telebond.
152314.subtitle_en: Turid Telebond is Svalbard’s wealthiest woman, but is almost one billion kroner behind the person at the top of the list.

152327.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Meteorological Institute has issued a warning for Longyearbyen. It says, among other things, that there is a risk of water running where it should not, local flooding, and small landslides and debris flows in steep terrain. “A low-pressure system will pass during the day.”
152327.subtitle_en: Thirty millimetres of rain is expected to fall in Longyearbyen by Saturday afternoon. That much rain occurs only every 17 to 20 years.
152327.title_en: A Wet Start to the Weekend

152336.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s office was notified of the landslide at 8:53 a.m. Saturday. No one was caught in the landslide that occurred at Platåberget. “It happened right by the cemetery, closer to Skjæringa.”
152336.subtitle_en: A landslide has occurred by the cemetery. The road between Huset and the old museum is closed.

152367.excerpt_en: The boat had two people aboard when it reported that it was in trouble. “The ‘Spitsbergen Express’ ran into problems north of Isfjord Radio. At the same time, they encountered strong winds in the area and were unsure whether they could manage on their own.”
152367.subtitle_en: The “Spitsbergen Express” suffered engine trouble just north of Isfjord Radio. The Joint Rescue Coordination Centre sent a helicopter from Longyearbyen to assist.

152388.excerpt_en: “Thanks to extremely capable electricians who worked throughout the morning, the fault has now been fixed,” says Morten Helliksen, managing director of Svalbardbutikken. The power went out at…
152388.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken has reopened after Monday morning’s power outage.

152390.excerpt_en: Before the weekend, the Governor of Svalbard’s office was notified that a sailboat was in trouble near Nordaustlandet. “We have sent the ‘Polarsyssel’ to Duvefjorden on Nordaustlandet to assist a sailboat named ‘Arktika 2’ that has engine trouble. There were three people and seven dogs aboard the sailboat.”
152390.subtitle_en: The “Polarsyssel” is assisting a sailboat that suffered engine trouble near Nordaustlandet.

152405.excerpt_en: Road 300 was closed on Saturday morning after a landslide broke loose just below the summit of Platåberget.
152405.subtitle_en: Road 300 between the old museum and Huset will be cleared of debris, but will not be reopened for now. Also watch drone footage of the landslide in the article.

152435.excerpt_en: Yesterday, LNS removed the landslide debris from the road below Platåberget, and this afternoon the roadblocks were removed. “We can never guarantee anything, but the slope has shown no signs of change today, so we have decided to reopen it,” says Kjersti Olsen Ingerø, acting head of the technical sector in…
152435.subtitle_en: On Tuesday afternoon, the roadblocks were gone and it was once again possible to walk or drive from the old museum to Huset.

152449.excerpt_en: At 12:30 a.m. last night, the Governor of Svalbard’s office received a report from someone in Nybyen who heard the landslide. Police first responded by car and later by helicopter. “We have located what we believe is a landslide that came down from Platåberget between Tverrdalen and Sverdrupbyen.”
152449.subtitle_en: A landslide occurred overnight between Tverrdalen and Sverdrupbyen. The Governor of Svalbard still urges people to think twice before entering steep terrain.

152452.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen is not like other towns. Year after year, Svalbard tops the annual TV campaign’s per-capita giving rankings.
152452.subtitle_en: The town’s tremendous commitment to the collection builds both community and solidarity.

152455.excerpt_en: “Yes, it is true that water entered the facility over the weekend. We have now secured the area where the water got in,” says Hege Njaa Aschim, communications director at Statsbygg, which has been tasked with handling all inquiries about the leak.
152455.subtitle_en: Firefighters had to respond and help when water seeped into the seed vault during the extreme rainfall over the weekend.

152472.excerpt_en: They are a little unsure who came up with the idea of inviting people to a festival, but Mikaela Dasilva and Ingeborg Runde are happy to invite everyone in Longyearbyen. The themed event will focus on the town-centre plan.
152472.subtitle_en: On Saturday, there will be a Town Centre Festival outside Rabalder. Everyone, young and old, will get to share their views on what they think the town centre should be like.
152472.tags_en: Longyearbyen Local Council, news, town-centre sub-plan, culture
152472.title_en: Everyone Gets to Have Their Say

152479.excerpt_en: The ground floor of the Commercial Building has now been cleared of furniture and interior fittings.
152479.subtitle_en: The city’s new library will be among the country’s most modern when it opens next summer.
152479.title_en: Work Begins on the City’s “Living Room”

152490.excerpt_en: When a warning of heavy rain in Longyearbyen was issued ahead of the weekend, Kjersti Olsen Ingerø, acting head of the technical sector in the Longyearbyen Community Council, contacted UNIS. “We commissioned a report to document how nature coped with the precipitation under the conditions that prevailed when the weather…”
152490.subtitle_en: UNIS geologists say, among other things, that monitoring stations must be established to help predict when landslides could threaten the city.
152490.title_en: More Information Needed to Keep the City Safe

152510.excerpt_en: On the second floor of Svalbard Museum, two of Norway’s leading experts in the analysis of human bone material are working. Professor of anatomy Per Holck and osteologist Elin Brødholt spent two days studying the remains of the three whalers excavated at the beginning of August this year. “This is very interesting.”
152510.subtitle_en: One of the three skeletons recovered from Likneset this summer may belong to a woman.
152510.tags_en: news, Likneset, culture, skeleton, nature and environment

152527.excerpt_en: Since this summer, Store Norske and Spitsbergen Travel have been working to establish a dedicated tourism company in Svea. It is now operational, and two people have been hired for project positions at Svea Svalbard AS.
152527.subtitle_en: Through Svea Svalbard AS, the mining community is to become a tourist destination. Having been sceptical of what he feared was state-funded competition, the tourism director is now positive.

152563.excerpt_en: The proposed opening hours create particular challenges for expedition cruises, including the “Nordstjernen.” Flights for that ship have largely already been booked, according to tourism director Ronny Brunvoll. “Night flights make it possible in summer to reach Longyearbyen from abroad without spending the night in Oslo.”
152563.subtitle_en: Svalbard Airport is to get new lighting and a flatter runway. That is why the airport was scheduled to close at night this summer. The travel industry is not happy about it.

152573.excerpt_en: The priest stands eyeing an Easter chick amid the chaos of people and flea-market finds in the UNIS cafeteria this Saturday. “I found an ice scraper and a couple of books. It’s a fun kind of chaos.”
152573.subtitle_en: Parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen reveals something he has not disclosed to the queen until now.
152573.tags_en: parish priest, Svalbard life, flea market, culture
152573.title_en: Bagged a Flea-Market Bargain a Couple of Years Ago

152577.excerpt_en: The land in Longyearbyen belonged to Store Norske Spitsbergen Kullkompani (SNSK) from 1916 until the state purchased the company’s properties in 2015 as part of the refinancing of its mining operations. Apart from a few years after the separation of what was initially Store Norske’s subsidiary Svalbard Samfunnsdrift, SNSK has administered the land.
152577.subtitle_en: SNSK urges us to focus now on developing Longyearbyen through cooperation, respect for one another’s roles and making use of the potential among the key players in the community up here.
152577.tags_en: opinion, reader’s letter, property, Store Norske
152577.title_en: The Recurring Battle over Land in Longyearbyen

152582.excerpt_en: Paul Lutnæs of the Governor of Svalbard’s office unpacks two polar bear skins from a Zarges case and lays them neatly across the floor. He is a senior adviser in nature and species management, but on Sunday he will serve as auctioneer at the auction where one of the skins will be sold.
152582.subtitle_en: At Sunday’s auction in aid of the annual TV fundraising campaign, polar bear skins will be put up for sale. Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik cannot decide which one to choose.
152582.tags_en: news, TV fundraising campaign, polar bear skins
152582.title_en: Two Polar Bear Skins to Choose From

152597.excerpt_en: He had spent several days in Longyearbyen—staying at a hotel, going sightseeing around town and dog-sledding on wheels, and visiting a couple of local restaurants—and was now on his way aboard one of the expedition ships anchored in Adventfjorden to join a week-long trip…
152597.subtitle_en: “I don’t do cruising anymore, I do expeditions,” an adult American, well dressed for the Arctic summer, told me when he stopped by the tourist information tent at Bykaia this summer.

152609.excerpt_en: In this week’s historical picture, we are wondering who is sitting next to Rasmus Jensen from Malangen. If anyone has information about the man on the right in the picture, or where it was taken, please email line@svalbardposten.no.
152609.subtitle_en: This picture was taken in 1958 and was loaned by Roald Westerbotn. But who is the man on the right?

152647.excerpt_en: A foreign national resident was caught driving under the influence early Saturday morning. Police responded after members of the public contacted them and stopped the driver. “It all proceeded without any drama,” says senior police officer Arve Johnsen of the Governor’s Office.
152647.subtitle_en: Police have been called out on several assignments over the past 24 hours.

152684.excerpt_en: On Monday morning, the provisional total for the TV campaign stood at NOK 1,012,860. On average, each Svalbard resident had donated NOK 441—the highest of all municipalities in the country.
152684.subtitle_en: Svalbard tops the per-capita donation statistics and has raised more than one million kroner so far. Money for the TV campaign and the Red Cross is still pouring in.

152709.excerpt_en: The trio, consisting of parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen, Torunn Sørensen and Espen Klungseth Rotevatn, is already in place in Oslo. So are Jovna Zakharias Dunfjell and Hans-Gunnar Skreslett, who also contributed to the CD. “This will be fun.”
152709.subtitle_en: On Friday, Svalbard Church’s Trio will release the album “Det blå loftet” at Kafé Asylet in Grønland, Oslo.

152719.excerpt_en: The 14th Dark Season Blues is under way.
152719.subtitle_en: While local council leader Arild Olsen had the honour of officially opening Dark Season Blues, it was five guys from Barcelona who really set the mood.

152751.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen says Longyearbyen Local Council’s lawyers are in dialogue with the family’s lawyer, Christian Lundin. “We are working on the basis that the family should receive fair and proper treatment. We want to avoid this case ending up in court.”
152751.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council wants to avoid a lawsuit, but has not acknowledged liability for compensation after Nikoline, 2, died in last year’s avalanche. Nor has Store Norske.

152767.excerpt_en: In May came the news that Air Ambulance Services ANS, which operates flights to Svalbard on behalf of Helse Nord, among other routes, would deploy jet aircraft in Tromsø and Oslo. “Introducing jets into the Air Ambulance Services would be a quantum leap, improving preparedness for Svalbard and patient safety throughout the country.”
152767.subtitle_en: A jet aircraft in Tromsø was to significantly strengthen ambulance preparedness for Svalbard from 2019. Following criticism from Finnmark, the proposal has been dropped.

152777.excerpt_en: Askholt was not informed about the turn of events in the air-ambulance case until last Friday. “I believe the matter should have been considered both by the emergency preparedness council in Longyearbyen and possibly by the interministerial Polar Committee. It is regrettable that there has not been a proper process following what has happened in Longyearbyen over the past year.”
152777.subtitle_en: Governor Kjerstin Askholt reacts to the fact that no one on Svalbard is involved in the air-ambulance process.

152779.excerpt_en: Enthusiastic collectors set off in groups from the post office and bank building at three o’clock on Sunday afternoon. After two weeks of tremendous effort throughout the town, campaign day had finally arrived.
152779.subtitle_en: Svalbard once again tops the per-capita donation statistics and has raised more than one million kroner in total for the TV campaign and the Red Cross.
152779.tags_en: news, culture, Red Cross, TV campaign
152779.title_en: Well Over One Million Kroner for the TV Campaign

152808.excerpt_en: “It is no problem whatsoever for me to stand here today and explain, defend and apologise for what happened at the open hearing in the Storting,” local council leader Arild Olsen told his fellow politicians on Tuesday.
152808.subtitle_en: At Tuesday’s local council meeting, the accusations against Arild Olsen (Labour) were harsh, following his alleged solo initiative during the open hearing on the Svalbard white paper.

152810.excerpt_en: “Let me try to reassure him.” Espen Klungseth Rotevatn (MDG) has to step in with a retort. “I can live with that.” Terje Aunevik (V) has been calmed down. “I’ll have to say no thanks to that.”
152810.subtitle_en: We collect choice remarks from politicians. Here are some from the Local Council meeting on 25 October.

152827.excerpt_en: The young people who turned up on Saturday for the Town Centre Festival and ideas workshop for Longyearbyen and the new town-centre plan had plenty of thoughts about what they would like to see.
152827.subtitle_en: Young people with creative ideas for the town centre.
152827.tags_en: town-centre plan, land-use plan, young people, news

152833.excerpt_en: The final and highest bid of the evening was NOK 110,000. Torunn Sørensen, a deaconry worker at Svalbard Church, had decided she wanted the polar-bear skin and made her move. “I’ll take it,” she said, winning the bid to applause from the audience.
152833.subtitle_en: It was a long—and for some, costly—evening at the Polar Hotel on Sunday. As Paul Lutnæs wielded the auctioneer’s gavel, people willingly opened their wallets for the TV campaign and the Red Cross.

152874.excerpt_en: The reader’s letter by Store Norske’s property and administration manager in Svalbardposten on Friday, 21 October 2016, calls for “calm regarding the landownership issue and respect for each other’s roles.” As an elected representative, I am first and foremost astonished by the letter’s understanding of local democracy.
152874.subtitle_en: Opinion: Store Norske’s property and administration manager misunderstands the role of local democracy when he calls for calm over land-management issues in Longyearbyen.

152879.excerpt_en: Archaeologist Åsne Dolve Meyer, 41, is trained as an archaeologist and works as an adviser to Kings Bay on cultural heritage, land-use planning and the environment. You may find her at the shooting range training researchers who are taking a safety course, in the harbour as harbour watch, behind the shop counter, behind the bar or serving when needed.
152879.subtitle_en: She does not just sit in the office. In Ny-Ålesund, everyone has to pitch in.
152879.tags_en: Ny-Ålesund, life in Svalbard, people, Kings Bay
152879.title_en: Åsne the Woman of Many Talents

152888.excerpt_en: I read with bemusement in the previous issue of Svalbardposten that Store Norske’s property and administration manager, Sveinung Lystrup Thesen, has written an article arguing against local politicians’ wish to take over management of the state’s properties within Longyearbyen’s planning area—and then asks Longyearbyen’s local politicians to…
152888.subtitle_en: Opinion: At a time when Longyearbyen is facing a difficult transition, the debate over land management should be raised to the local political level rather than suppressed.

152889.excerpt_en: When the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund’s board distributed NOK 6.1 million among various projects this spring, UNIS was awarded NOK 650,000. The money went to the project “Will There Be Ice in Isfjorden This Year?”, which will measure ocean currents and temperatures, among other things, to determine whether the fjord will freeze over.
152889.subtitle_en: Two weather stations on the seabed outside Bjørndalen will forecast ice conditions in Isfjorden.
152889.title_en: UNIS to Record Ice in the Fjord

152904.excerpt_en: In May, the Air Ambulance Service announced the procurement of two new, robust jet aircraft. One was to be stationed in Tromsø, which they believed would improve Svalbard’s emergency preparedness by a “quantum leap.”
152904.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office, the local council and Longyearbyen Hospital were not informed during the process. This is deeply regrettable. On 14 November, the directors of the regional health authorities will meet to decide the future air-ambulance structure.

152919.excerpt_en: There is a buzz around Longyearbyen’s sports and cultural activities, where volunteers, supported by local businesses among others, create fantastic experiences for those of us who live here and for visitors to the town.
152919.subtitle_en: Opinion: Innovation Norway has event tourism as one of its priority areas, and the latest Svalbard white paper points to the potential in linking culture and tourism locally as well. Festival season is now under way in Longyearbyen, and we can clearly see the effect a vibrant cultural offering has on our industry. This is an effect we want to develop and strengthen.

152934.excerpt_en: Governor Kjerstin Askholt supports the Director of Public Prosecutions’ decision. “We support the decision. It is important that the case is thoroughly investigated so that the bereaved and the public receive answers, and so that no one is unnecessarily subjected to suspicion, as stated in the Director of Public Prosecutions’ press release,” says Governor Kjerstin Askholt.
152934.subtitle_en: The Director of Public Prosecutions overturns the state prosecutor’s decision to drop the case and orders further investigation into the avalanche accident.
152934.title_en: Director of Public Prosecutions orders new investigation

152969.excerpt_en: It was a few minutes past 9:30 on Wednesday morning when the whole town went dark. The power flickered a couple of times but did not come back on until an hour after the outage.
152969.subtitle_en: A substation fault at Mine 7 caused the power outage on Wednesday morning.

152972.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen is pleased with the outcome. “First, I would like to thank the Norwegian Coastal Administration for the good work it has done. The assessment reflects what we have worked on locally, both administratively and politically.”
152972.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration recommends expanding Longyearbyen port in its concept assessment. The analyses show that a floating-quay solution is best suited.

153026.excerpt_en: “This is really great. I think the youth card will lead to a more social community for young people.”
153026.subtitle_en: From the New Year, Martin Higraff (13) and other young people may get cheaper smoothies and many other benefits.

153028.excerpt_en: The question of who was actually responsible for securing those living in the pointed-roof houses in Lia has made its long, painful journey between Longyearbyen Local Council, Store Norske and the Governor of Svalbard. No one has accepted liability for compensation.
153028.subtitle_en: Whether they conclude that someone should be punished or not, it is important that the investigation provides more answers.

153031.excerpt_en: At this time of year, the cold should be settled and the ground covered in snow. Instead, Longyearbyen is experiencing landslides, precipitation records and temperatures 7–8 degrees higher than normal. “Everything points to a temperature record both for October and for the whole of 2016,” says climate researcher Jostein Mamen of the Norwegian Meteorological Institute.
153031.subtitle_en: October was the mildest and wettest month since meteorological measurements began in Svalbard.
153031.tags_en: temperature, nature and environment, climate, weather, news

153056.excerpt_en: “No one would have thought that, in the final days of October, we could sit outside with a cup of coffee in beautiful, mild autumn weather,” say Roy Tore Strøm and Arnt Roar Olsen.
153056.subtitle_en: The blues enthusiasts from Alta had no use for thick woollen long johns, mittens or hats.
153056.tags_en: temperature, weather, nature and environment, climate, news

153061.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen is pleased with the outcome. “First, I would like to thank the Norwegian Coastal Administration for the good work it has done. The assessment reflects what we have worked on locally, both administratively and politically.”
153061.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration recommends expanding Longyearbyen port in its concept assessment. It believes up to half a billion kroner should be allocated for a new fishing and floating quay.
153061.title_en: Opting for fishing and floating quay

153077.excerpt_en: She believes the Polar Department of the Ministry of Justice should have been informed about the case at an early stage of the proceedings. This was not the case. “I hope for a constructive meeting where we can elaborate on our professional arguments.”
153077.subtitle_en: Governor Kjerstin Askholt is asking to meet with Helse Nord in connection with the air-ambulance case.
153077.title_en: Asks to meet with Helse Nord

153085.excerpt_en: Who are these men in the picture? Svalbardposten knows neither who took the picture nor when it was taken.
153085.subtitle_en: Six men wait to be taken up the mountainside by the lift.
153085.tags_en: historical picture, life in Svalbard, history

153100.excerpt_en: “There were lots of people and a great atmosphere. It was nice that so many Svalbard residents came,” says parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen.
153100.subtitle_en: A happy group is back after launching their CD in Oslo. Around a hundred people attended the release party for “Det blå loftet” at the brown-pub Asylet in Grønland.

153108.excerpt_en: From Thursday through Sunday, it was almost impossible to walk past a bar in town without hearing blues music from one band or another performing its songs. The 14th.
153108.subtitle_en: Dark Season Blues was buzzing all weekend. Preparations for next year’s anniversary are already under way.

153115.excerpt_en: The original plan was to shoot the film in three locations: Tromsø, Målselv and Ny-Ålesund. “In the end, financial and logistical reasons led us to decide to drop the footage from the mining area in Ny-Ålesund. We did not need those shots,” says producer John M.
153115.subtitle_en: The film “Kings Bay” has a dramatic Svalbard incident as its backdrop. But not a single scene from the archipelago.

153158.excerpt_en: The logic of law can sometimes lead to conclusions that do not square with everyday common sense. Legal and moral duties may point in different directions.
153158.subtitle_en: Letter to the editor: A conviction following last year’s avalanche accident could set a precedent and thus clarify who should be held responsible for no measures having been implemented before the accident.

153161.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen is pleased with the outcome. “First, I would like to thank the Norwegian Coastal Administration for the good work it has done. The assessment reflects what we have worked on locally, both administratively and politically.”
153161.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration recommends expanding Longyearbyen port in its concept assessment. It believes up to half a billion kroner should be allocated for a new fishing and floating quay.
153161.title_en: Opting for fishing and floating quay

153182.excerpt_en: On Thursday evening, the Governor of Svalbard received a tip from the public about drink-driving in town. A patrol was dispatched and found the suspect and a passenger at their residence.
153182.subtitle_en: A man in his 20s has been charged with drink-driving in Longyearbyen on Thursday evening.

153193.excerpt_en: Adult pundits can say all the fine things they like about how the centenarian Store Norske built Longyearbyen. But the tear in the corner of the eye only comes when the youngest give of themselves to show gratitude for what has been.
153193.subtitle_en: The children at Longyearbyen School of Culture presented drama, dance, music and heartfelt thanks to Store Norske.
153193.title_en: A heartfelt tribute to the mining company

153201.excerpt_en: “We were preparing for the forecast weather and reconnected the town’s dual power supply via Road 219. During the work, the wrong switch was engaged, causing a short circuit,” says Kim Rune Røkenes, energy manager at Longyearbyen Community Council.
153201.subtitle_en: Large parts of Longyearbyen were without power for about half an hour on Monday morning.
153201.title_en: Short Circuit Blacked Out the Town

153211.excerpt_en: At 9 a.m., NVE and the Norwegian Meteorological Institute are meeting to discuss the weather situation on Svalbard. “Based on the expert advice they give us, we will assess several measures during the day.”
153211.subtitle_en: Based on advice from NVE and the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, the authorities will assess whether parts of the town should be evacuated.

153217.excerpt_en: “Norwegian is on its way, and so is SAS, even though neither has got farther than Tromsø so far. Conditions at Longyearbyen Airport are fine, although it is somewhat windy,” says airport manager Morten Ulsnes.
153217.subtitle_en: SAS, Norwegian and Posten are all heading to Longyearbyen as scheduled.

153233.excerpt_en: “The evacuation will begin as quickly as possible and no later than 3 p.m.,” Governor Kjerstin Askholt announced in a press release.
153233.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office has decided that a number of homes in Lia must be evacuated. In addition, all of Nybyen and the area from the church to and including the old bakery will be evacuated.

153241.excerpt_en: Community Council leader Arild Olsen says they have now begun getting an overview of how many people need to be evacuated, but he does not yet have the final figure. “At the same time, we are working to establish an overview of available housing and available hotel rooms.”
153241.subtitle_en: Eighty-six students have been evacuated from the student housing in Nybyen. Biology students Marie Westvik, 21, and Nanna Devantier, 23, are among those who had to collect their belongings.

153277.excerpt_en: “The rain has increased quite sharply over the past few hours and will only intensify,” says Geir Bøyum, the duty meteorologist at the weather forecasting office in Tromsø. The temperature is now around six degrees and will remain that warm until around midnight.
153277.subtitle_en: Rain in Longyearbyen will intensify through the afternoon and evening. It will be at its worst around nine o’clock tonight.

153297.excerpt_en: Following a meeting between the Governor’s Office, Longyearbyen Community Council and NVE, it was decided to maintain the evacuation. “We are now working to gain an overview of the situation, including an aerial survey by helicopter with personnel from the Governor’s Office, Longyearbyen Community Council and an avalanche expert. More precipitation and rising temperatures are expected overnight.”
153297.subtitle_en: No one will be allowed to return home for the time being. A new assessment will be made this afternoon.

153310.excerpt_en: At 9:10 a.m., Hovland witnessed the avalanche that reached the rearmost row of kennels at the town dog yard. Around ten kennels were destroyed.
153310.subtitle_en: “I heard a slushy sound, and then it went clack, clack, clack,” says Alexander Hovland of the Longyearbyen Dog Club.

153315.excerpt_en: “The decision to continue the evacuation was made in consultation with Longyearbyen Community Council and the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate,” Governor Kjerstin Askholt announced. Minor landslides have been recorded on the mountainside above Lia and Nybyen, along with some signs of subsidence.
153315.subtitle_en: On Tuesday afternoon, the Governor’s Office decided that large parts of Longyearbyen would remain evacuated and subject to a travel ban. Meteorologists say freezing temperatures will not arrive until the middle of next week.

153318.excerpt_en: The family of five stopped by Rabalder to register, but had arranged somewhere to stay for the night. “I have actually thought about the possibility of this happening when you look at the slope up toward Sukkertoppen, where there is a lot of loose material,” says the father of three.
153318.subtitle_en: Bård Heitmann and his family have been evacuated from Gruvedalen. He thinks it is fine that precautions are being taken.

153360.excerpt_en: The road up to Nybyen is open again. The lifting of the evacuation and travel ban also applies to Huset and Sverdrupbyen.
153360.subtitle_en: Activities at Svalbard Church will resume as normal on Thursday morning after the Governor’s Office lifted the evacuation of most of the town on Wednesday evening.

153365.excerpt_en: The lawyer is assisting Kim Rune Røkenes and Pia Sivertsen, who lost their two-year-old daughter, Nikoline, in the avalanche that came down from Sukkertoppen last December. The lawyer from Ness Lundin DA sent claims for compensation this summer to the homeowner, Longyearbyen Community Council, and the landowner, Store Norske.
153365.subtitle_en: Lawyer Christian Lundin is also asking the Governor’s Office to acknowledge liability for damages following last December’s avalanche accident.

153379.excerpt_en: On Thursday morning, people from Longyearbyen Community Council and UNIS went into the field to determine whether it was safe to lift the evacuation of the households in Gruvedalen and the town kennels. “Based on these investigations, we have concluded that the evacuation can be lifted,” Governor Kjerstin Askholt announced.
153379.subtitle_en: Both the residents at the top of Gruvedalen and the dogs at the town’s dog kennels can move back today.

153383.excerpt_en: “It could have turned into something nasty,” says Senior Police Officer Arve Johnsen of the Governor’s Office. He says both the charger and the battery were original. “We urge people to be careful and not charge devices while they are sleeping,” says Johnsen.
153383.subtitle_en: A fire started in a home in Gruvedalen on Monday when a headlamp left charging exploded.

153396.excerpt_en: “It has been completely extreme. We have been on alert the whole time, with full staffing and round-the-clock duty,” says Hege Njaa Aschim, communications director at Statsbygg.
153396.subtitle_en: The extreme amounts of precipitation earlier this week created challenges for Statsbygg at the seed vault.
153396.title_en: Had to Work to Keep Water Out of the Seed Vault

153402.excerpt_en: There are many guides in Longyearbyen. A good guide is an important ambassador who speaks vividly and with enthusiasm.
153402.subtitle_en: Reader’s letter: Leif Magne Helgesen dispels some of the myths surrounding life on Svalbard.
153402.title_en: The Right to Die on Svalbard

153405.excerpt_en: Some time ago, a guide stood in Svalbard Church and explained the church’s history to a small but interested group of tourists. Among other things, he said that the pewter plate hanging on the northwest wall of the sitting room was the church’s first baptismal font.
153405.subtitle_en: Reader’s letter: Hallvard Holm calls on the tourism industry to provide guides on the island with more thorough training.

153417.excerpt_en: ‘Kunstpause Svalbard’ is back as the polar night truly descends on Longyearbyen. On this occasion, I would like to highlight an artist whose work was connected to Svalbard, and whose significance perhaps few people are aware of today.
153417.subtitle_en: Reader’s letter: Else Christie Kielland spent several periods working as an artist in Longyearbyen in the 1930s. She constantly wanted to return to the island, where she found inspiration for her art.
153417.title_en: Else Christie Kielland—Artist in Interwar Svalbard

153461.excerpt_en: Ingeborg and Eivind Oldernes Hoem (7) were two of quite a few customers who visited Lompensenteret’s newest shop, Snøstjerna, on the second floor on Saturday. “It’s nice here.”
153461.subtitle_en: People in Longyearbyen have so far embraced the new Snøstjerna shop at Lompensenteret.

153463.excerpt_en: The Svalbard Choir Festival 2016 took place over the weekend, with strong participation from the mainland. Lesja and Lesjaskogen Song Choir from Oppland and Varia Vocalis from Lambertseter were visiting.
153463.subtitle_en: Choir tours to Svalbard have become popular, and planning for next year is already under way.
153463.tags_en: news, Great Norwegian Male Choir, Svalbard Choir Festival, Tundradundrene, Longyearbyen Mixed Choir
153463.title_en: This Year’s Choir Tour to a Different World

153491.excerpt_en: Is this what the future will look like? Many are probably asking themselves that question after an autumn with unusually heavy rain and high temperatures.
153491.subtitle_en: Although this is something we would rather have avoided, it has been a learning experience that may prove useful.

153497.excerpt_en: Each tourist arriving by cruise ship spent NOK 937 per day in Longyearbyen. In addition, the shipping companies pay port fees, as well as for electricity, water and supplies, while NOK 150 per passenger goes to the environmental protection fund.
153497.subtitle_en: The tourism industry is pleased with this year’s cruise season and is now making plans to bring in even more next year.

153509.excerpt_en: There was a fish-processing plant and family community here, pleasant ski races, wonderful Christmas dinners, keen interest from media around the world, spectacular North Pole expeditions, world-class new research and dramatic coal mining that brought down a government. These days, the “town” by Kongsfjorden is turning 100.
153509.subtitle_en: Ny-Ålesund is much more than the world’s northernmost settlement with a tragic mining accident.
153509.tags_en: Ny-Ålesund, magazine, culture, Kings Bay, news

153518.excerpt_en: Large parts of Lia, all of Nybyen, a row of houses in Gruvedalen and the church were still evacuated when Svalbardposten went to press on Wednesday. Several roads were closed and travel bans were in effect across large areas.
153518.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, 259 people had been evacuated in Longyearbyen. Local council leader Arild Olsen wants to prevent the town from having to evacuate again.

153562.excerpt_en: They competed in seven different sports at Svalbardhallen on Saturday afternoon. A volleyball match has just ended, and Christopher from Canada, who plays for Svalbard Turn’s team, goes over to Aleksandra Zhestokova (25) to congratulate her on the good play.
153562.subtitle_en: Twenty-two Russian youths, adults and team leaders came to Longyearbyen from Barentsburg on Saturday to compete.

153566.excerpt_en: “The road to Vestpynten and Bjørndalen has now reopened thanks to a tremendous effort by LNSS. Thanks also to the Local Council and the Governor for the fastest case processing ever,” writes Store Norske property manager Sveinung Lystrup Thesen on the praise and information pages on Facebook.
153566.subtitle_en: The road to Vestpynten and Bjørndalen has now reopened after being closed following the storm.

153577.excerpt_en: There will be a jet at Gardermoen from 2019; the rest of the air service will remain as it is today, Air Ambulance Services ANS writes in a press release. The decision was made by the managing directors of the country’s four regional health authorities.
153577.subtitle_en: On Monday it was decided that Svalbard’s air ambulance service will not be strengthened with a jet in Tromsø. Governor Kjerstin Askholt is disappointed.

153598.excerpt_en: Rapporteur for the Svalbard White Paper Trine Skei Grande (Liberal) believes all the issues raised during her visit to Longyearbyen in August are included in the recommendation presented today by the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence.
153598.subtitle_en: The revised White Paper includes plans for energy, stronger beer and an on-call veterinary service. But it remains vague about Store Norske’s future role.
153598.title_en: No clear direction for Store Norske

153604.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence presented its recommendation on the government’s Svalbard White Paper. Local businesses are rewarded for raising their concerns with rapporteur Trine Skei Grande (Liberal), who was in Longyearbyen in August after the first draft of the White Paper was presented.
153604.subtitle_en: The new Svalbard White Paper proposal calls for an on-call veterinary service, stronger beer and an energy plan. Store Norske’s future remains unclear.

153610.excerpt_en: In the latest Svalbardposten, Hallvard Holm highlights guides’ lack of knowledge when showing visitors around Longyearbyen and challenges the tourism industry to provide more thorough training. He is right to do so, even though much also works very well and the overall quality of the guide corps is very high.
153610.subtitle_en: Ronny Brunvoll agrees with Hallvard Holm’s criticism of Longyearbyen’s tourist guides, but nevertheless maintains that their overall quality is good. The tourism industry works continuously to provide its employees with solid training.
153610.title_en: Hallvard Holm is right to criticise—but the guides are high-quality

153615.excerpt_en: Earlier this year, the government presented its proposal for a new Svalbard White Paper. On Wednesday, the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence issued its recommendation, including proposed changes.
153615.subtitle_en: The Svalbard Business Association believes it has been heard in the process leading to the new Svalbard White Paper.
153615.tags_en: Svalbard Vet, Svalbard Brewery, news, the Svalbard White Paper, Svalbard Business Association

153624.excerpt_en: There will be a jet at Gardermoen from 2019; the rest of the air service will remain as it is today, the Norwegian Air Ambulance Service ANS announced on Monday.
153624.subtitle_en: Nevertheless, the regional health authorities decided that the quantum leap in Svalbard emergency preparedness would not happen. If the jet is to become a reality, more parties must contribute.

153652.excerpt_en: “It actually went remarkably well. But a lot more will probably emerge when the light returns,” says Kjersti Olsen Ingerø, head of the technical sector at Longyearbyen Local Council (LL).
153652.subtitle_en: Heavy rain and strong winds caused several minor incidents in and around Longyearbyen last week.

153680.excerpt_en: “This is a win-win situation for the community,” believes Torgeir Prytz (Conservative). “This would change how the small-boat harbour is used and therefore cannot be permitted,” says Community Council Leader Arild Olsen (Labour).
153680.subtitle_en: “A commercial floating dock is not a small-boat harbour activity,” says Terje Aunevik (Liberal).
153680.tags_en: Longyearbyen Community Council, news, Longyearbyen Port
153680.title_en: Another no to floating dock at small-boat harbour

153685.excerpt_en: At Tuesday’s local council meeting, the council leader briefed politicians on the process during last week’s evacuations. Arild Olsen praised the Governor of Svalbard, the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate, Longyearbyen Local Council, UNIS and, not least, individuals who helped evacuated fellow residents during the situation that arose.
153685.subtitle_en: “It will become untenable if the same residents have to be evacuated time and again,” says local council leader Arild Olsen (Labour).

153695.excerpt_en: This summer, Turbine 2 was routinely sent to Rotterdam in the Netherlands for an overhaul. Considerable damage was found in parts of the outer edges, which Energiverket assumes was caused by the turbine operating under low load for an extended period.
153695.subtitle_en: The turbine that underwent an overhaul is back and working well. But Energiverket is struggling to meet certain emissions requirements.

153697.excerpt_en: “From April, we could find ourselves in a situation where we do not have enough nursery places,” said Anne Søvold Vikanes, sector manager for education and culture, during a briefing at Tuesday’s community council meeting. Longyearbyen Kindergarten is currently closed.
153697.subtitle_en: There may be a shortage of nursery places in Longyearbyen in April.
153697.tags_en: news, Polarflokken Kindergarten, Longyearbyen Kindergarten, Kullungen Kindergarten, Longyearbyen Community Council

153708.excerpt_en: Basecamp Explorer, one of Svalbard’s largest tourism companies, was honoured in London before the weekend. The company received a Green Apple Award for its tree-planting project in the Maasai Mara in Kenya, accepting it at the Houses of Parliament in the British capital.
153708.subtitle_en: Basecamp Explorer has planted 5,100 trees in the Gruve 3 forest in the Maasai Mara in Kenya.

153722.excerpt_en: This week’s historic photograph was taken in 1964 and loaned to the newspaper by Leif Langnes. We see a towering surface facility, with heaps of material on the mountainside below.

153724.excerpt_en: This week it became clear that no air ambulance jet will be stationed in Tromsø, as everyone here had hoped. The disappointment locally is naturally considerable.
153724.subtitle_en: It is a major task to decide what constitutes the right use of public funds.

153728.excerpt_en: Next week, Rotevatn will meet Iselin Nybø (Liberal) on the Standing Committee on Education and Research at the Storting. “We know laws can be changed. Just look back at the battle Robert Johansen and Svalbard Brewery fought for several years before finally succeeding.”
153728.subtitle_en: The law does not allow folk high schools to operate on Svalbard. Espen Klungseth Rotevatn intends to change that.

153740.excerpt_en: “We have rearranged things and adapted them so that all flights already scheduled can operate,” says airport manager Morten Ulsnes at Svalbard Airport. Svalbardposten wrote on the 21st.
153740.subtitle_en: The airport manager has managed to make the pieces fit so the tourism industry gets the summer flights it had planned for.

153750.excerpt_en: The concert became a somewhat melancholic evening filled with love, longing and mining life. Despite the small tables and refreshments, the hall was completely silent throughout the concert.
153750.subtitle_en: On Saturday evening, Liv Mari Schei took the audience on a journey through her four album releases over the past decade.

153754.excerpt_en: Svea is currently zoned for mining. Store Norske has therefore drawn up a proposal for a new land-use plan that would open the area to tourism.
153754.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard fears the consequences for nature around Svea and rejects the tourism plans.

153767.excerpt_en: A photo and art exhibition celebrating Store Norske and a varied hymn evening at Svalbard Church, entirely free of coal, helped bring light, sound and colour to the days. All under the shared cultural umbrella of “Art Break.”
153767.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen’s first weekend in total darkness was by no means without its bright spots.

153772.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen won in floorball, volleyball, chess and badminton, while the Russians won in basketball, football and table tennis. “It’s great to see the joy of sport that the participants bring to the court.”
153772.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen emerged victorious from the weekend tournament against 22 Russian athletes from Barentsburg.

153796.excerpt_en: Pole Position organised the transport of AF Gruppen’s equipment from Svea to the mainland this week. MV “Atlantic” was chartered for the assignment.
153796.subtitle_en: Some of AF Gruppen’s equipment broke loose during transport from Svea to Fredrikstad.
153796.tags_en: Pole Position, AF Gruppen, Svea, news

153832.excerpt_en: The White Paper is intended to set out Svalbard policy for the years ahead. It has been eight years since the previous paper.
153832.subtitle_en: Parliament considered the Svalbard White Paper on Tuesday. Watch the recording here.
153832.title_en: Watch the debate on the Svalbard White Paper

153847.excerpt_en: “This went as well as it possibly could, and then some,” says Espen Klungseth Rotevatn (Green Party), who together with Eirik Berger (Liberal) met three politicians from the Standing Committee on Education and Research on Thursday.
153847.subtitle_en: On Thursday, the Liberal Party submitted a private member’s motion in Parliament. The aim is to extend the Folk High School Act to also apply in Svalbard.

153857.excerpt_en: Svalbard Minister Anders Anundsen (Progress Party) was very pleased with the strong engagement in the Svalbard community during the presentation of the Svalbard White Paper. “The fact that the entire polar affairs section is here shows that this matters. Svalbard will continue to be characterised by continuity and predictability.”
153857.subtitle_en: Many took to the podium in Parliament on Tuesday to voice their opinions. The entire polar affairs section occupied the visitors’ gallery.

153860.excerpt_en: The Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence believes the range of educational programmes in Svalbard should be further developed and expanded.
153860.subtitle_en: UNIS must be given more educational programmes and support to expand its research park.

153873.excerpt_en: The Svalbard White Paper adopted on Tuesday this week has gained both more substance and clearer direction thanks to local engagement and national politicians who listened to many of the contributions they received along the way. The Svalbard White Paper was first presented to the Council of State by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security on 11.
153873.subtitle_en: The work ahead must now be accelerated.

153895.excerpt_en: LL’s Planning Department was strengthened last year and now consists of three people, two of whom are on one-year contracts. During the working meetings on next year’s budget, politicians were made aware that planning and development will require resources in the years ahead as well.
153895.subtitle_en: In the coming years, the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) must set aside substantial funds for planning work.

153904.excerpt_en: “I have received reactions to the local council appointing board members to the local newspaper,” said Elise Strømseng (Labour) at Tuesday’s meeting of the Administration Committee (AU). She herself sits on the newspaper’s board and has another Labour politician, Svein Jonny Albrigtsen, as her personal alternate.
153904.subtitle_en: Several politicians feel uncomfortable appointing board members to Svalbardposten AS.

153908.excerpt_en: On Thursday we enter the Christmas month of December, and to mark the occasion we are bringing you a photograph from Roald Westerbotten’s collection. Taken in 1958, it shows smartly dressed people walking around the Christmas tree.

153913.excerpt_en: “Last year, well over a hundred people took part in the first edition of the Christmas orienteering calendar, and we hope for at least as many treasure hunters this year,” says project manager Silje M. Hagen of Aktiv i friluft.
153913.subtitle_en: A new clue is posted every day during Advent.
153913.title_en: Hunt for treasures in the dark

153936.excerpt_en: Everyone arriving and leaving must stop by reception. Reception manager Hilde has the overview. “This is, in many ways, the heart of this small community,” she says with a broad smile.
153936.subtitle_en: Hilde Jørgensen (47) of Kings Bay is probably the first person you meet.

153951.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard believes the French captain of the “Arktika” is guilty of violating the traffic ban on Kong Karls Land, as well as illegally bringing dogs into Svalbard.
153951.subtitle_en: The captain of the “Arktika” disagrees with the prosecution.

153962.excerpt_en: On Monday morning, Pål Remen came across a line of dead polar cod at Kullkaia. The fish were lying along the high-water mark. “Perhaps there is a natural explanation.”
153962.subtitle_en: A number of dead polar cod lie just above the high-water mark at Kullkaia. Haakon Hop of the Norwegian Polar Institute explains why.

153985.excerpt_en: The avalanche from Sukkertoppen buried ten people inside their homes. Two of them died.
153985.subtitle_en: The investigation into the avalanche accident of 19 December 2015 is scheduled to be completed by April.

153993.excerpt_en: At the end of October, legal aid lawyer Christian Lundin sent Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) a letter containing new points that he believes support the claim that LL acted with gross negligence before the avalanche. The lawyer represents Pia Sivertsen and Kim Rune Røkenes, who lost their daughter Nikoline (2) in the avalanche.
153993.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council rejects claims that it failed to follow up advice from the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute on avalanche protection measures in Lia in autumn 2015.

154001.excerpt_en: The relevant weather reports from the Norwegian Meteorological Institute before the avalanche did not warrant an evacuation order, writes the Governor’s lawyer, Karl Otto Thorheim of the Office of the Attorney General, in a letter to legal aid lawyer Christian Lundin. No warnings. Snow and blowing snow were not part of the extreme weather warning.
154001.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard did not have information indicating that Lia should have been evacuated, according to the Governor’s lawyer.

154027.excerpt_en: “It makes you feel inspired and curious,” admits Community Council leader Arild Olsen. “Northern Sphere” is the name of the new exhibition at Kunsthall Svalbard, which opened on Saturday. The Northern Norway Art Museum has selected highlights from its collection of more than 2,000 works.
154027.subtitle_en: The Northern Norway Art Museum opened an exhibition on Saturday.
154027.title_en: Arctic Works at the Art Hall

154032.excerpt_en: It is Monday morning, and just over a week remains until the 20th Polarjazz Festival begins.
154032.subtitle_en: Twenty years ago, someone had a good idea. Such a good idea that it is still swinging, albeit in somewhat diluted form.

154038.excerpt_en: This week’s historical photograph comes from the collection of Stig Onarheim. His father, Kjell Onarheim, was Longyearbyen’s fire chief and photographed Prime Minister Kåre Willoch in the summer of 1985.

154047.excerpt_en: Last Saturday, Road 300 was closed from the junction with Road 501 all the way up to Gruvelageret. By then, four or five smaller avalanches had occurred on the mountainside, one of which had stopped against the ski trail.
154047.subtitle_en: Unusually large wind slabs high on the mountainside above Platåberget could trigger major avalanches.

154062.excerpt_en: On Sunday, a female polar bear and her two cubs were escorted by two snowmobiles and a helicopter from the Governor of Svalbard. The entourage went up Endalen and to Skiferdalen, where the three appear to be keeping calm.
154062.subtitle_en: If there is a polar bear in town, you must be prepared for it to attack, warns a polar bear researcher.

154088.excerpt_en: Queen Sonja will arrive in Longyearbyen on the day of the opening and return the following day. “The Queen has no other official programme than the opening that day,” says Sven Gjeruldsen, assistant head of communications at the Royal Palace. As far as Gjeruldsen knows, the Queen will not exhibit here on this occasion.
154088.subtitle_en: On 30 March, Queen Sonja will open Artica Svalbard’s workshop in Sjøområdet. It will become a new venue for national and international artists and writers.
154088.tags_en: artists’ workshop, Artica Svalbard, news, Queen Sonja
