154098.excerpt_en: When the press release about the new foundation was issued by the Ministry of Culture in November last year, it surprised everyone. No local organisations had been involved in the plans for Artica Svalbard.
154098.subtitle_en: Artica Svalbard still gives unclear answers about how the art will be presented and rooted locally.
154098.title_en: Art Foundation Still Vague on Local Art Collaboration

154123.excerpt_en: Tourism in Svalbard continues to develop well, and our shared ambition is to help create more year-round jobs in Longyearbyen. Visit Svalbard and its member companies are also taking the so-called “green transition” seriously, as demonstrated, among other things, by the “Sustainable Destination” certification we received last year.
154123.subtitle_en: Visit Svalbard and its member companies are taking the “green transition” seriously, writes tourism director Ronny Brunvoll in this opinion piece.
154123.title_en: Developing Destinations from a Green Perspective

154131.excerpt_en: Attorney Christian Lundin of Ness Lundin Law Firm DA says that, after receiving responses from Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) and the Governor of Svalbard, he requested further information. “But I am not getting it; they simply refer to the fact that an investigation is under way.”
154131.subtitle_en: Legal counsel for the bereaved asks for more answers after the 2015 avalanche accident.

154136.excerpt_en: Thorium-based nuclear power should be investigated as a possible future energy source for Svalbard, as an alternative to other possible solutions based on CO2 capture and storage, wind turbines, hydrogen as a fuel, or power transmission from the mainland.
154136.subtitle_en: Compact, small-scale thorium-based nuclear power is an option that should be investigated to meet Svalbard’s future need for electricity and heat.
154136.title_en: Svalbard Could Launch a New Norwegian Energy Adventure

154169.excerpt_en: “We pumped for about two hours before the Coast Guard arrived. The engines had stopped, and there were one-metre waves.”
154169.subtitle_en: The boat took on water, and everyone aboard was cold and wet when twelve UNIS students and teachers were rescued by the Coast Guard vessel Svalbard.
154169.title_en: Rescued Twelve from Freezing Boat Accident

154170.excerpt_en: It took seven hours from problems began aboard the ten-metre boat until they were safely ashore in Longyearbyen. For five of those hours, the twelve people on board—students, teachers and the skipper—worked to pump out water, keep their spirits up and avoid serious frostbite.
154170.subtitle_en: “It has been a shocking experience for those involved. But the students are coping well and are receiving follow-up support,” says the UNIS head.

154183.excerpt_en: “This was entirely self-inflicted this time,” says energy manager Kim Rune Røkenes. The power went out throughout the town, except in the Sjøområdet district.
154183.subtitle_en: Shortly before nine o’clock on Monday, the power went out across large parts of the town.
154183.title_en: Blackout Hit the Town by Mistake

154227.excerpt_en: The fresh-food counter has been hit hardest during interruptions to deliveries to Svalbardbutikken, but the shop has also run out of other items such as coffee beans and snus.
154227.subtitle_en: The fresh-food shelves at Svalbardbutikken are almost empty.

154236.excerpt_en: It is the festival’s 20th anniversary this year, with a long list of artists. At Wednesday evening’s warm-up, the Youth Big Band set the tone before just over 300 enthusiastic listeners.
154236.subtitle_en: And so it begins. This weekend, jazz will take over the town. On Wednesday, the locals got the party started—and with plenty of punch.
154236.title_en: Polarjazz Gets Underway with a Bang

154239.excerpt_en: A Polarcirkel boat from UNIS carrying twelve people suffered engine failure and began taking on water. It remained stranded for two hours before help arrived.
154239.subtitle_en: The two hours spent at sea in a boat taking on water were extremely dramatic for those involved; this should never have happened.

154244.excerpt_en: During the Standing Committee on Family and Cultural Affairs, Education and Research’s consideration of the proposal to make the Folk High School Act applicable to Svalbard, the Conservative Party and the Progress Party secured a majority to submit the bill to the government.
154244.subtitle_en: The Conservative Party and the Progress Party support a folk high school in Longyearbyen.
154244.title_en: One Step Closer to Folk High School

154255.excerpt_en: “In general, GPS and Iridium work well. But we would like to know if periods are coming when the systems cannot be trusted,” says helicopter pilot Stig Onarheim.
154255.subtitle_en: The pilots of the Governor of Svalbard’s rescue helicopter welcome warnings about space weather.
154255.title_en: Wants Warnings of Bad Space Weather

154271.excerpt_en: Sunday opening is now being prepared, and in September there will already be a literary festival with an exciting program. Boktrivsel Library is preparing to move from cramped attic premises to one of the best locations by the pedestrian street.
154271.subtitle_en: In brand-new premises, surrounded by Svalbard’s distinctive colors, books, pictures and games, the library hopes to welcome everyone to the town’s new community hub in six months.

154293.excerpt_en: “I am afraid we will make a rushed decision because Rema is knocking on the door and wants to establish itself here. The car park is Longyearbyen’s most attractive plot,” Bente Næverdal (Labour) said at Tuesday’s meeting of the Technical Committee.
154293.subtitle_en: Politicians want control over what will be built on the car park in the town centre.

154299.excerpt_en: Svalbard Turn’s cabin in Grøndalen has long stood in disrepair.
154299.subtitle_en: The Governor is taking over and refurbishing the cabin in Grøndalen for Svalbard Turn. In addition, the sports club will be allowed to borrow the cabin on Nordenskiöldtoppen.
154299.title_en: Svalbard Turn gets two rental cabins

154308.excerpt_en: It took just under two hours from the alarm being raised until help arrived. Everyone on board took part in pumping out the water.
154308.subtitle_en: Twelve soaked and freezing students and UNIS employees were rescued by the Coast Guard on Friday. Their boat took on water and both engines had stopped.
154308.title_en: Four Taken to Hospital After Boat Accident

154321.excerpt_en: “We fully understand that those on board were frightened and perceived the accident as a dangerous situation,” says Fred Skancke Hansen, UNIS director of health, safety and environment.
154321.subtitle_en: UNIS will investigate why the boat filled with water and both engines stopped.

154323.excerpt_en: This is what attorney Christian Lundin of Ness Lundin Law Firm writes in a notice of intended legal proceedings to Longyearbyen Community Council (LL). Lundin represents Kim Rune Røkenes and Pia Sivertsen, who lost their two-year-old daughter Nikoline in the avalanche on the 19th.
154323.subtitle_en: Unless Longyearbyen Community Council accepts liability or presents a specific proposed solution, the avalanche case will end up in court.

154337.excerpt_en: “We will take part in the effort to establish the cause. For now, we do not know whether this constitutes a criminal matter that we need to investigate further,” says Senior Police Officer Ole Jakob Malmo of the Governor’s Office.
154337.subtitle_en: The Governor has not decided whether to open a case against Unis over the incident.

154356.excerpt_en: In a letter to the Polar Department of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, it requests NOK 100 million for this. NVE has been presented with proposed avalanche-protection measures for the town in a report by Almaviva, and is now assessing which measures may be appropriate to implement.
154356.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) wants to begin protective works in the town next year.
154356.title_en: Requests NOK 100 million to start protective works

154380.excerpt_en: “There is a lot behind these figures: demolishing houses, clearing up, shipping material to the mainland and possibly rebuilding,” says Gjensidige communications director Arne Voll.
154380.subtitle_en: The total insurance settlement after the avalanche will amount to nearly NOK 50 million, according to Gjensidige.

154390.excerpt_en: And if things go her way, Longyearbyen will see more of Carmen Klausbruckner (32). The Austrian is now taking a master’s degree in marine biology, and then she plans to learn Norwegian.
154390.subtitle_en: Simply going to the shop is an adventure, admits the only UNIS student with a doctorate in law.

154397.excerpt_en: Polar hero Roald Amundsen’s disappearance in 1928 has sparked much speculation—and several books—in the years since. At the end of March, Monica Kristensen will publish “Roald Amundsen’s Last Journey,” in which she presents her theory.
154397.subtitle_en: Monica Kristensen unveils unpublished theories in her forthcoming book.

154407.excerpt_en: A frozen landscape lends itself to simple photographic techniques—in other words, black and white. Photographer Roy Mangersnes of WildPhoto has spent a total of one year on photographic safaris in the archipelago, and many impressions are stored on his memory card. “It struck me that Svalbard has a landscape crying out to be photographed in black and white.”
154407.subtitle_en: Photographer Roy Mangersnes opened the exhibition after a year on photographic safari.

154412.excerpt_en: The plot had it all: “US intelligence was behind the 1962 mine explosion. The Soviet Union would be blamed, and the result would be that Norway and the United States could jointly find oil on Svalbard.” Journalist Harrieth Hansen of Nordlys is the film’s main character.
154412.subtitle_en: The new Kings Bay film unleashes some truly grand conspiracy theories.

154424.excerpt_en: We continue publishing historical photographs from Stig Onarheim’s collection. As in the previous issue, this photograph was taken in 1985 in connection with the 60th anniversary of the Svalbard Treaty.
154424.subtitle_en: Historical photograph: the 60th anniversary of the Svalbard Treaty.

154432.excerpt_en: And the answer is not always easy to find. Take Linnéfjella or Linnévannet, for example.
154432.subtitle_en: Was Jules Verne on Svalbard? When we find a historical link between a person and Svalbard, we often ask: Have they been to Svalbard? Or we ask what the connection is between this person and Svalbard.
154432.title_en: Svalbard Museum’s object of the month: MOBILIS IN MOBILE

154478.excerpt_en: On the meteorologists’ list of the country’s warmest places, eight of 14 locations are in Svalbard, in addition to Jan Mayen. Svea and Akseløya were the warmest, at 4.1 degrees at seven o’clock this morning.
154478.subtitle_en: Sveagruva tops the list of the country’s ten warmest places on Tuesday.
154478.title_en: Svalbard warmest place in the country

154485.excerpt_en: “We want to err on the side of caution and take no chances,” says acting head Kjersti Olsen Ingerø of the technical sector of the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL).

154509.excerpt_en: German Angar Bruchardt and Jakub Both are attending a major mathematics conference in Longyearbyen this week. “It’s quite warm.”
154509.subtitle_en: The snowmobile trip for participants at this week’s major mathematics conference was rained off. A couple on their honeymoon could not get to the seed vault, but they did see the Northern Lights.
154509.title_en: Longyearbyen is washed away by rain

154518.excerpt_en: “Here, potential developers can go straight to submitting a building application. Of course, there are requirements for roads, green spaces and other infrastructure, but in principle the area is ready,” says Linn Tautra Grønseth of the planning and development unit at the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL).
154518.subtitle_en: Next week, it may theoretically be possible to submit a building application for a site in Gruvedalen. But even if the land-use plan is adopted, much planning remains.
154518.title_en: Milestone paves the way for housing construction

154534.excerpt_en: Managing Director Frank Jakobsen understands the motivation behind—and the necessity of—the new land-use plan. But he expects transforming Sjøområdet to be a long and difficult process.
154534.subtitle_en: LNS Spitsbergen is wondering who will pay for the transformation of Sjøområdet.
154534.tags_en: Sjøområdet, news, LNS Spitsbergen, Elvesletta, land-use plan, Statsbygg

154554.excerpt_en: “We have never been to Svalbard before, but thought it was the perfect opportunity to take a trip when there was also a music festival here.”
154554.subtitle_en: The Polarjazz brand markets itself. Several of this year’s festival attendees have booked hotel rooms for next year’s festival without knowing anything about the programme.

154571.excerpt_en: “I thought I’d tell a few good tall tales,” says Stein-Arve Sørensen (62). He takes over Svalbardposten’s premises in connection with his 11th
154571.subtitle_en: Stein-Arve Sørensen made Longyearbyen dependent on fresh milk and Polarjazz.

154577.excerpt_en: “We don’t know the artists very well, although we have heard of them. But we almost have to show up when something happens for young people in town,” Hanna Hjelløkken (15) and Ksenia Sushkevich (14) said before the concert at the Youth House on Friday evening.
154577.subtitle_en: Arif & Unge Ferrari established a close and positive connection with Longyearbyen’s young people.

154588.excerpt_en: Jørgen Stene sits on a box in the cinema and concert hall at the cultural centre. Sivert Høyem’s equipment has been packed away and properly labelled.
154588.subtitle_en: Jørgen Stene has created the Polarjazz sound since the first chord was struck in 1998.

154591.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Community Council wants to be able to offer a complete vocational education programme. By coordinating subjects, including practical vocational courses, the school can offer two years of schooling for the price of one.
154591.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council wants to run the first and second years of vocational training in parallel so the town can recruit local carpenters. These tenth-graders are delighted.

154605.excerpt_en: The plans for the Lompensenter of the future are now almost ready. In a room on the second floor
154605.subtitle_en: Thon Group wants to turn Lompensenteret into a tourist destination. If everything goes according to plan, a “new” centre will be ready next year.
154605.title_en: The Centre Is Set to Become Seriously Cool

154607.excerpt_en: For several days, the Governor chased the mother and her two cubs away from the area around Longyearbyen. Monday the 16th
154607.subtitle_en: The Governor was criticized after a mother polar bear and her two cubs came all the way into Road 238. They now respond that they cannot guarantee a polar-bear-free town.

154627.excerpt_en: The deadline for Gard Christophersen and Bård Blæsterdalen to apply for an extension of their trapping stay at Austfjordnes expired on 1 February. “They have not applied, so there will be a new round,” says Knut Fossum, head of environmental protection at the Governor’s Office.
154627.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is seeking new trappers for Austfjordnes. The Governor’s Office has already received several enquiries from people who want to spend the winter there.

154645.excerpt_en: The Governor has opened a case and will now investigate whether anyone can be held responsible for a Unis boat suffering an accident with twelve people on board. The temperature was minus 20 degrees, the vessel began taking on water, and both engines stopped.
154645.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Maritime Authority is examining which regulations apply to the Unis boats. It is highly likely that passenger transport in winter is prohibited.

154647.excerpt_en: In 1983, 34 gigawatt-hours per year (GWh) were used for district heating; in 2016, consumption had risen to 63 GWh. The town’s homes are the biggest consumers of district heating.
154647.subtitle_en: District-heating consumption has nearly doubled since 1983. The head of energy wants to do something about it.

154653.excerpt_en: It could take another two years before a new reserve power station is completed. During periods of high electricity consumption, when there is a complete shutdown, or when essential maintenance must be carried out at the coal-fired power plant, additional electricity must be supplied.
154653.subtitle_en: Work to establish a new reserve power station should have started earlier. The price tag is NOK 78 million.

154664.excerpt_en: The technical sector of the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) is now working to find out how we can improve waste sorting. Plastic collection is on the way.
154664.subtitle_en: A pilot project for collecting plastic is taking shape. Good practical solutions still need to be found.
154664.tags_en: news, plastic collection, waste facility, recycling

154703.excerpt_en: Two bands, a circus act and several singers. There will also be an art exhibition.
154703.subtitle_en: Nine acts will take the stage during Friday’s local selection for the Youth Culture Festival (UKM).

154711.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries took over landholdings from Store Norske in spring 2015 as part of the company’s restructuring. The ministry then drew up new standard agreements for leasing land in Svalbard.
154711.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries is proposing a loan guarantee scheme to give businesses the opportunity to obtain construction loans in Svalbard.

154717.excerpt_en: Last week, Svalbard was the warmest place in the country. The Perleporten bridge over the Vannledningselva was closed because of the risk of slush avalanches, and rain poured down.
154717.subtitle_en: After torrential rain and above-zero temperatures last week, the snow and cold are back. For now, they look set to stay.

154743.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, Longyearbyen Community Council sent a letter saying that Statsbygg had begun converting its warehouse in the Sjøområdet district into an artists’ studio without permission. “Through the media, we have learned that the project has begun. We request an explanation of this.”
154743.subtitle_en: Received a letter about illegal construction—but it turned out to be a mistake.

154750.excerpt_en: At the baby group in the library, the little ones crawl around exploring their surroundings, which consist of rattles, building blocks and one another. Meanwhile, the mothers talk about everyday life and the future.
154750.subtitle_en: There is currently little certainty for parents whose children are due to start nursery.
154750.title_en: Struggling to Find a Nursery Place

154758.excerpt_en: The unattended cooking happened because people fell asleep while food was on the stove, often at night. According to the fire service’s annual report, those cooking the food were often under the influence of alcohol.
154758.subtitle_en: Half of the fire incidents were caused by unattended cooking, but the fire chief also warns against charging batteries without supervision.

154767.excerpt_en: When the prices for activities in the culture and sports unit were debated in the Community Council on Monday, Jakobsen’s personal training business became a topic. She runs a private business on the council’s premises, and the debate concerned how much rent she should pay to operate there.
154767.subtitle_en: Personal trainer Helle Myhrvang Jakobsen must pay five percent of her turnover to Longyearbyen Community Council. She is perfectly happy with that.
154767.title_en: A Good Start for the Trainer from the Community Council

154782.excerpt_en: The Community Council podium can be used for many things, including admitting mistakes. Elise Strømseng did just that when the council considered the revision of the 2017–2020 waste management plan. “I must freely admit that for years I’ve put pizza boxes and cardboard in the paper container.”
154782.subtitle_en: Elise Strømseng (Labour) has been sorting her waste incorrectly for years. She believes waste containers need clearer labels.
154782.tags_en: Longyearbyen Community Council, news, waste management plan

154798.excerpt_en: All the parties in the Community Council were full of praise for the work the administration has done on the zoning plan in recent years. The consultation processes in particular, where everyone was heard, received a great deal of praise.
154798.subtitle_en: The zoning plan was adopted by acclamation in the Community Council. But not before the Labour Party made a few last-minute tweaks.
154798.tags_en: Longyearbyen Community Council, news, zoning plan

154815.excerpt_en: The war hero has not been forgotten. For a long time, wreaths were laid at his grave on commemorative days.
154815.subtitle_en: Captain Trond Vigtel gave his life for Svalbard’s freedom, and the local population wanted his grave to remain in Longyearbyen.
154815.title_en: The War Hero Must Not Be Forgotten

154824.excerpt_en: A football match has ended, and the players are thanking each other for the game. The picture comes from the collection of Stig Onarheim, which he inherited from his father, former fire chief Kjell Onarheim.
154824.subtitle_en: Thanking each other for the game.
154824.tags_en: historic picture, life in Svalbard, history

154828.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Hospital and the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) are pulling out all the stops to mark 100 years of activity. Everyone, young and old, will get to see, experience and hear the history of the small hospital with the big responsibilities.
154828.subtitle_en: A cabinet minister’s visit, celebrity doctors, an open day and a book launch are just some of the events when Longyearbyen Hospital celebrates its centenary next week.
154828.title_en: Celebrating a Milestone with Plenty of Punch

154838.excerpt_en: “This year’s sun drawing stood out by being a little different, and it featured a very cheerful sun that won over the committee.” This was the reason third-grader Joanna Matea Rut Eriksson’s drawing was chosen as this year’s sun drawing.
154838.subtitle_en: Joanna (8) stood out by drawing a very cheerful sun.

154878.excerpt_en: In autumn 2016, Svalbardposten wrote that data from hunting statistics and monitoring of Svalbard rock ptarmigan diverged: the hunting statistics showed that the proportion of birds shot was falling, while monitoring showed that the density of the spring population was stable or increasing.
154878.subtitle_en: That is what researchers want help finding out.
154878.title_en: Will There Be More or Fewer Rock Ptarmigan?

154881.excerpt_en: We are nearing the end of the twilight season in Svalbard. This is the period when the sun is six degrees below the horizon until it crosses the southern sea horizon on the 16th.
154881.subtitle_en: We are in the most beautiful time of year, but also the most dangerous. It is important that we look out for one another and care, so that no one becomes isolated and remains in the darkness.

154888.excerpt_en: For 100 years, Longyearbyen Hospital has provided emergency medical care to the town’s population. Its development over a century of service has been enormous.
154888.subtitle_en: The hospital has been, and remains, hugely important to those who live in or visit the town. It provides security for their own and others’ health.

154905.excerpt_en: In autumn 2015, the International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (Icarda) retrieved 128 boxes from Svalbard’s Seed Vault because everything in its gene bank had been destroyed in the war in Aleppo. On Wednesday, 53 boxes of seed samples will be returned.
154905.subtitle_en: The seed samples removed from the Seed Vault in 2015 after the gene bank in Aleppo, Syria, was destroyed are returning for safekeeping.
154905.title_en: A Landmark Day for the Seed Vault

154908.excerpt_en: Those taking part in the exercise are the Red Cross, the hospital, Air Transport and the Governor of Svalbard. “Many people will be involved that day.”
154908.subtitle_en: The annual avalanche exercise will take place in the vicinity of Longyearbyen early Sunday afternoon.

article_keywords_en: chief superintendent of the Governor’s Office
154951.excerpt_en: “An avalanche has struck Vei 228—that is what we know so far. We have received no reports of anyone being caught.”
154951.subtitle_en: An avalanche has struck Vei 228. The Governor of Svalbard has received no reports of anyone being caught or missing.

154954.excerpt_en: Minister of Education Torbjørn Røe Isaksen (H) said in the Storting today that he finds the idea of a folk high school on Svalbard particularly exciting. He pointed out that a research community has been built up on Svalbard in recent years, and that a Norwegian presence is important.
154954.subtitle_en: Today, the Storting asked the government to submit a proposal for the Folk High School Act to apply to Svalbard. Minister of Education Torbjørn Røe Isaksen is positive.

154990.excerpt_en: “We have received no reports of anyone being caught in the avalanche or missing. The avalanche team is now searching the area to double-check as thoroughly as possible,” said Chief Superintendent Bjørn Pedersen of the Governor’s Office at around 1:30 p.m. on Tuesday.
154990.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard reports on its website that the avalanche area has now been searched and that no one is missing. Police are still at the site near Vei 228. See pictures from the avalanche area here.
154990.title_en: The Avalanche Area Has Been Searched

155013.excerpt_en: Avalanche experts flew up by helicopter this afternoon to assess the avalanche hazard. An update will come later this evening.
155013.subtitle_en: The NVE failed to warn that the buildings were threatened, so no one was evacuated before the avalanche struck shortly before noon today.

155021.excerpt_en: About 150 residents attended Tuesday evening’s public meeting at the cultural centre. Many had questions after Tuesday’s avalanche from Sukkertoppen reached homes in Vei 228.
155021.subtitle_en: Several people declared that they no longer trust the avalanche warning system at Tuesday evening’s public meeting at the cultural centre.
155021.title_en: “Trust in the Avalanche Warning System Is Dead”

155043.excerpt_en: Today, avalanche experts from the NVE have arrived in town and will assess Lia, which is currently evacuated. “During the afternoon, we will make a new assessment of the traffic ban and the evacuation situation.”
155043.subtitle_en: Governor Kjerstin Askholt is awaiting the avalanche experts’ assessment of whether it is safe to let people move back to Lia. Hopefully, the answer will come at the public meeting at 8 p.m. tonight.

155081.excerpt_en: Everyone in Vei 230 can move home, as can those living in the lowest rows of terraced houses in Vei 228, 226 and 224. The evacuation remains in force for the upper row of houses in Vei 228, Vei 226 and 222. “Thorough avalanche assessments have now been carried out for the entire mountainside at Sukkertoppen.”
155081.subtitle_en: Following thorough avalanche assessments, the Governor of Svalbard is lifting parts of the evacuation order.

155086.excerpt_en: Shortly before Wednesday’s information meeting, the Governor of Svalbard announced which homes must remain evacuated. It is the upper row of houses in Vei 222, 224 and 226, closest to Sukkertoppen. “We should increase the number of safeguards protecting the buildings.”
155086.subtitle_en: The 13 housing units that remain evacuated could serve as an additional safeguard until more permanent avalanche protection is put in place.
155086.title_en: Row of Houses Could Provide Extra Protection

155104.excerpt_en: This Thursday, roses and chocolates are on the counter at Arctica in Lompensenteret. Cake will soon be served to customers and other guests. “Arne Kristoffersen has been there from the very beginning.”
155104.subtitle_en: Arctica turns 20 and celebrates with balloons and cake.

155129.excerpt_en: Married couple Megan Kovacs (34) and Gunhild Kristoffersen (31) both play in Susanne Sundfør’s band, but also have a band project of their own.
155129.subtitle_en: The band Bow To Each Other is on Svalbard to find creative inspiration.
155129.tags_en: people, life on Svalbard, back page

155149.excerpt_en: What wasn’t supposed to happen has happened again. Those who lived in Vei 228 thought they were safe in their own homes.
155149.subtitle_en: If those responsible cannot reassure people with the existing warning system, they must find new and better warning systems.

155157.excerpt_en: Knut Hoseth, acting regional director at the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE), sat with geologist Odd Arne Mikkelsen in a meeting with Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) to discuss various protective measures when the avalanche came down from Sukkertoppen on Tuesday morning. “This incident brings even greater focus to the need for permanent protective measures.”
155157.subtitle_en: NVE believes the latest avalanche shows how important it is to quickly establish permanent avalanche protection.

155168.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen (A) is pleased that the ministry has found a solution. “This means that the business community can finally resume projects that have been on hold and pick up activity again. It is not unreasonable that when the NFD (Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries) …”
155168.subtitle_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen is pleased that the problems with construction-loan applications that had been on hold at the local bank appear to be getting resolved.

155174.excerpt_en: Stein Vidar Loftås, communications manager at SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge, points out that the loan-guarantee scheme is currently only a proposal to be put before and considered by the Storting in connection with the revised national budget. “Until then, we cannot change our practice.”
155174.subtitle_en: The bank will wait before granting construction loans until the loan-guarantee scheme has been adopted.

155188.excerpt_en: Three creative hosts guided the audience through ten acts in an entertaining way, dressed for every change of scene. Two bands, numerous soloists and musicians, circus and acrobatics, and visual art took the stage in turn.
155188.subtitle_en: Creative young people presented a wide range of cultural performances during the local UKM showcase at the cultural centre on Friday.

155218.excerpt_en: On 19 February last year, Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) ordered the evacuation of the Old Hospital.
155218.subtitle_en: A year ago, the Old Hospital was evacuated and its doors bolted shut. For the owners, the investment in their homes has become a catastrophe.

155221.excerpt_en: Are there any readers out there who can tell us who we see in this photo? The picture comes from Stig Onarheim’s family album and was probably taken by his father Kjell or mother Ba in 1966.

155251.excerpt_en: “A mortgage on a home is established to protect the bank if the borrower’s ability to service the loan disappears.”
155251.subtitle_en: SpareBank 1 held mortgages on several of the apartments at the Old Hospital. Even so, it is the owners who must bear the loss when the apartments become worthless.

155254.excerpt_en: Geir Arne Olsen, Roy Albrigsen and Arve Are bought the Old Hospital in 1996. They renovated the building and converted it into an apartment complex with 13 units ranging from 20 to 100 square metres.
155254.subtitle_en: The old hospital had a cooling system to protect against settlement damage. Those who bought the building do not want to comment on what happened to the system.

155258.excerpt_en: Initiator Jim Johansen is delighted and thanks everyone who attended the concert and contributed in various ways. “Everything went smoothly. A lot of people came, and they seemed to enjoy themselves throughout the evening.”
155258.subtitle_en: The concert at Gruve 3 on Saturday evening raised NOK 90,950 for Tove Klaven, who has undergone stem-cell treatment in Russia.

155279.excerpt_en: Tunabreen last surged in 2004. Until now, researchers believed that the glacier had a surge cycle of 35 to 40 years, and therefore expected the next surge around 2040.
155279.subtitle_en: Tunabreen may surge earlier than expected

155281.excerpt_en: Rema 1000 wants to establish itself in town. The customer base is limited, but also geographically isolated.
155281.subtitle_en: Will the offering improve with two grocery stores, asks the author of this article.

155283.excerpt_en: Once again, a slab avalanche struck after an easterly storm and a large accumulation of wind-packed snow. Like a cannon shot, the mass of snow tore through a house.
155283.subtitle_en: Questions the lack of measuring instruments.

155299.excerpt_en: Governor Kjerstin Askholt is now using the Police Act to maintain the evacuation of the rearmost row of houses toward Lia. “The immediate avalanche danger is over. At the same time, NVE’s latest assessment showed that the mountains, during the thaw earlier in February, had in a sense become ‘slightly glazed’, with a thin layer of faceted snow on top.”
155299.subtitle_en: Neither the Governor nor the Community Council wants people living at the top of Lia, but several questions remain about what happens next.

155320.excerpt_en: On Sunday afternoon, a relatively large avalanche came down at the foot of Hiorthfjellet, across Adventfjorden. The area is frequently used for travel, so, as a precaution, the avalanche area was searched by helicopter and by personnel from the Governor’s office and Longyearbyen Red Cross.
155320.subtitle_en: There is no indication that anyone was caught in today’s avalanche on Hiorthfjellet.

155334.excerpt_en: The two cabinet ministers arrived in Longyearbyen overnight and have a packed schedule before departing this afternoon. They are due to meet with the Governor and parts of the Community Council, as well as some residents affected by the avalanche last Tuesday.
155334.subtitle_en: Minister of Justice and Public Security Per Willy Amundsen and Minister of Petroleum and Energy Terje Søviknes (both Progress Party) inspected the avalanche area in Longyearbyen on Monday morning.

155341.excerpt_en: Arctic World Archive is the name of the newcomer. The company Piql AS has worked with Store Norske for a year to create a new vault for storing irreplaceable material of national or global importance on Svalbard. “The Seed Vault is a success.”
155341.subtitle_en: Sometime in the future, when the volume of “fake news” has become so vast and confusing that the truth is unclear, people can enter the data vault in Mine 3 and check the facts.

155355.excerpt_en: It has been a hectic week for the crew at Spitsbergen Revue Group. This year’s revue, “Coal Hair and the Three Bears.”
155355.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Revue Group is honing its act.

155371.excerpt_en: Last week we showed a team photo from a football match in 1966, from Stig Onarheim’s collection. We’re staying with sports this week, showing a photo from the same year.
155371.subtitle_en: We continue with photos of sporting activity from days gone by.

155393.excerpt_en: It was a fitting celebration of Longyearbyen Hospital over the weekend. The gala performance at the cultural centre featured everything from heartfelt praise for the hospital and its importance over 100 years to hilarious revue numbers.
155393.subtitle_en: “I can see that you are proud, and you have every reason to be,” Health Minister Bent Høie (H) declared.

155412.excerpt_en: The book “Longyearbyen Hospital 1916–2016: From Mining Hospital to UNN” was presented during the anniversary weekend. Eighty people attended the launch, which is partly based on the author’s lifelong commitment to and interest in Svalbard.
155412.subtitle_en: Rolf Hanoa has not merely written a book about the history of Longyearbyen Hospital. He has also produced a reference work.

155422.excerpt_en: Although we now have most of the answers, there is considerable uncertainty in town about what actually caused it. Fifty-four housing units in the uppermost row of houses in Lia are still evacuated.
155422.subtitle_en: There has been plenty of fear, unease and frustration around lunch tables over the past week, with good reason. NVE’s avalanche warning system, which we have all trusted, failed completely.

155435.excerpt_en: Per Sanderud, director of the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE), accepted responsibility for the misjudgment. “Unfortunately, we failed this time,” he said. The avalanche that started at the top of Sukkertoppen and destroyed the two uppermost apartment blocks on Road 228 reached as far as the five-thousand-year zone.
155435.subtitle_en: No warning was ever issued that last week’s avalanche could reach the settlement. NVE’s director accepted full responsibility after the misjudgment.

155455.excerpt_en: There are 24 warning regions in Norway. One of them is Nordenskiöld Land.
155455.subtitle_en: Local avalanche forecasting in Longyearbyen relies on local helpers who go out several times a week to “read” the snow conditions.
155455.title_en: Collecting Vital Snow Data for NVE

155460.excerpt_en: The sun casts a pink glow on Operafjellet, while two boys brighten a snowdrift by the Pointed Houses on Road 230. Sigurd Bruseth, 14, digs with a red shovel, while Olai Birkeland, 13, uses a blue one. “We’ve only just started building.”
155460.subtitle_en: Soon a new fortress will stand between the Pointed Houses and Blåmyra. And the sun too.

155465.excerpt_en: In 1897, three fit Swedes take off by balloon from Virgohamna, bound for the North Pole. Just over three days later, the balloon crashes, and the three men of the Andrée expedition travel for 88 days before reaching Kvitøya and establishing camp.
155465.subtitle_en: Swedish researcher Bea Uusma is energetically working to solve one of the polar region’s greatest mysteries.

155482.excerpt_en: Politicians have asked the administration of Longyearbyen Community Council to accelerate work on providing new homes in Longyearbyen. The planning department is now working full steam to clarify building plots, but the planning framework stands in the way in some areas. “On Friday, as previously agreed, we met with the Governor.”
155482.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council wants the planning framework set aside to speed up housing construction.

155489.excerpt_en: LL has asked to develop the area, but Store Norske wants to take overall responsibility for its development itself. “LL will of course have its housing needs met, and we are happy to run the development project in close dialogue and cooperation with them.”
155489.subtitle_en: Store Norske wants to develop the residential area in Gruvedalen itself and hopes to begin pile-driving this summer.

155507.excerpt_en: Jon Bautz trudges through the snow below his house between Roads 224 and 226. “It’s usually pretty wind-scoured above here, but the last avalanche came not far from us,” he says, pointing up at black patches on Sukkertoppen.
155507.subtitle_en: Jon Bautz had a detached house in the centre with a great view and slept soundly at night. That was before the avalanche.

155517.excerpt_en: The housing situation before Tuesday’s avalanche, which destroyed several homes on Road 228, was critical. Now it is completely untenable.
155517.subtitle_en: At the meeting with the two ministers, calls were made for quick solutions for new housing and safety measures.

155527.excerpt_en: No community in the world has lost such a large number of homes with so few fatalities due to avalanches. This is more a result of luck and coincidence than skill.
155527.subtitle_en: We need improved political leadership if we want these accidents to stop.

155568.excerpt_en: Hilarious and thought-provoking points rolled onto the stage like pearls on a string during the premiere of this year’s Solfest revue on Friday. As expected, the polar bear and the Governor received plenty of attention in this year’s revue, “Coal Hair and the Three Bears.”
155568.subtitle_en: Solfest Revue is the year’s most hilarious highlight. In this photo series, you can see who came under the satirical spotlight this year.

155574.excerpt_en: The owner discovered that the car, a Toyota passenger car, had disappeared from Road 232 on Sunday morning. At first, it was thought that acquaintances had borrowed it, but a closer investigation showed that this was not the case.
155574.subtitle_en: The car was found again on Sunday afternoon by the water reservoir in Gruvedalen.

155582.excerpt_en: Tomorrow, March 8, is Sun Day itself in Longyearbyen.
155582.subtitle_en: The children will probably be the only ones lighting up the old hospital steps on Sun Day.

155600.excerpt_en: As Sara Heitmann sang “Here Comes the Sun,” the sun appeared. The applause and cheers from everyone who had turned up were immediate.
155600.subtitle_en: The sun just peeked over the glacier and sent rays toward the hospital steps and everyone waiting there. Watch a video of the magical experience here.

155603.excerpt_en: Breakfast and live radio broadcasts appear to be popular. More than 100 people stopped by to listen on both mornings.
155603.subtitle_en: Many got up early and tuned in to P3’s broadcasts from 6 to 9 a.m. at Svalbard Museum on Wednesday and Thursday.
155603.title_en: P3 Got People Out of Bed

155622.excerpt_en: The law of supply and demand is being felt brutally in Longyearbyen. The housing shortage is prompting sellers to demand far more for homes than they did just a short time ago.
155622.subtitle_en: The housing shortage following the latest avalanche is creating wild conditions in the market.
155622.title_en: Price in August: NOK 1.95 Million. Now: NOK 2.8 Million

155625.excerpt_en: Olsen believes it is natural that pressure in the housing market has intensified recently. Even before the latest avalanche, it was known that homes were selling for far more than could be expected under normal circumstances.
155625.subtitle_en: They believe more housing will lead to lower prices.

155659.excerpt_en: In recent issues, we have focused on sporting activities in Longyearbyen in the 1960s. But no sporting event is complete without an enthusiastic audience.

155666.excerpt_en: Believe it or not, our beloved Hjørdis Røren, “the kindergarten auntie of all kindergarten aunties,” died on March 2, aged 91.
155666.subtitle_en: “The kindergarten auntie of all kindergarten aunties” died on March 2, aged 91.

155680.excerpt_en: Long-term storage of digital information presents many challenges. Norwegian technology and Mine 3 on Svalbard could be the solution.
155680.subtitle_en: Long-term storage of digital information presents many challenges. Norwegian technology and Mine 3 on Svalbard could be the solution.
155680.title_en: The World’s Information Bank on Svalbard?

155684.excerpt_en: In issue 8, we showed a team photo from a football match, and here two women believe they recognize familiar faces. In the back row are, first, a man who has so far remained unidentified, then Svein Sørensen, George W.
155684.subtitle_en: The Det skjer editorial team has received inquiries about two historic pictures from Stig Onarheim’s collection.

155687.excerpt_en: Tore Magne Hoem (41) is director of experiences at Hurtigruten Svalbard. That means he is responsible for the experience products produced by the company.
155687.subtitle_en: A perfect day includes smiling guests with rosy cheeks.

155699.excerpt_en: In February this year, Svalbardposten published an excellent article by Ole Magnus Rapp about Captain Trond Vigtel, who is buried in the cemetery in Longyearbyen. There are, however, some misunderstandings, and clarifications seem appropriate.
155699.subtitle_en: The war heroes of Svalbard and the defense of Norwegian sovereignty during the war on and around the archipelago must never be forgotten!
155699.title_en: The War Heroes Must Not Be Forgotten

155708.excerpt_en: REMA-Reitan once again shows how greedy he is. Now he plans to fleece the mining community and put an end to COOP, as Reinhard Mook fears.
155708.subtitle_en: REMA-Reitan once again shows how greedy he is, writes Sivert Fløttum in this contribution.

155717.excerpt_en: “I was planning to do something about the difference between Longyearbyen and Barentsburg, but then I came here and was inspired by modern life in Longyearbyen,” says photographer Julia de Cooker, who opened her first solo exhibition on Sunday. She is exhibiting 13 photographs at Galleri Svalbard.
155717.subtitle_en: Photographer Julia de Cooker was surprised when she arrived in Longyearbyen. As a result, the art project did not turn out quite as she had envisioned.
155717.title_en: Opened with an Outsider’s Photographic Perspective

155734.excerpt_en: In a letter to the Governor, which was forwarded to NVE, he writes that he wants to implement immediate measures to prevent future accidents involving people and property in Nybyen. This is pending any permanent protection, which may take a long time to put in place.
155734.subtitle_en: Arne Kristoffersen, who owns Gjestehus 101, is asking for permission to organize the blasting of snow cornices in Nybyen himself.

155737.excerpt_en: This week, the Norwegian Association of Local Newspapers (LLA) presented circulation figures for 100 local newspapers, with a combined net circulation of around 325,000 copies. One-third of them increased their circulation over the past year. “I’m pleased that circulation is holding steady and even increasing somewhat.”
155737.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten increased its circulation by 2 percent from 2015 to 2016. Editor Hilde Røsvik is pleased.

155743.excerpt_en: After the avalanche on December 19, Reinhard Mook was quick to call for measuring instruments to be installed in Lia. “I took it for granted that this would be done that summer, and I am surprised that it wasn’t,” says Mook.
155743.subtitle_en: Reinhard Mook believes measuring equipment should be installed in Lia to provide continuous information about snow conditions.

155756.excerpt_en: The deadline for applications to trap at the Governor’s trapping station at Austfjordnes expired on March 1.
155756.subtitle_en: Several local names are among the applicants for a trapping season at Austfjordnes.
155756.title_en: Seven Teams Want to Trap Here

155761.excerpt_en: Acting regional director Knut Hoseth of NVE Region North says they have based snow assessments around Longyearbyen on the same methodology used on the mainland. “Quite a lot of field measurements are carried out, and then one relies on available data.”
155761.subtitle_en: Only after two avalanches in Lia is NVE considering deploying measuring instruments to improve avalanche warnings.

155770.excerpt_en: At last, the sun is back in Longyearbyen. Wednesday, 8.
155770.subtitle_en: It feels wonderful to experience the very first rays of sunshine after a long dark season.

155791.excerpt_en: While the congregation parked their snowmobiles at Brinken, parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen was helped into his clerical robe over his snowmobile suit.
155791.subtitle_en: Around 30 people attended the outdoor service at Hiorthfjell on Sunday morning.
155791.title_en: Outdoor Service with a Touch of Sunshine

155828.excerpt_en: Due to the avalanche risk, Gruvelageret will be closed until Sunday. Huset has an open bistro and restaurant for groups with advance bookings.
155828.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is closing Gruvelageret due to avalanche risk.

155835.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten received several tips on Friday afternoon that that day’s Norwegian flight had made a hard landing in Longyearbyen and that several passengers found the experience unpleasant.
155835.subtitle_en: Blames it on a loudspeaker failure.

155847.excerpt_en: The snowmobile driver first noticed sparks and smoke coming from the vehicle before it caught fire. The driver managed to get off in time, and no one was injured. “Everything went well, and the fire was quickly extinguished.”
155847.subtitle_en: A snowmobile caught fire near SSU on Sunday morning. No one was injured.

155862.excerpt_en: The road between Gruvelageret and Huset is open, and both Huset and Gruvelageret are operating normally. The road and ski trail from the old museum to Huset will remain closed until further notice. “We had another meeting with NVE today regarding the avalanche risk.”
155862.subtitle_en: Following Sunday’s meeting with the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate, the Governor of Svalbard has lifted the evacuation order for Gruvelageret.

155868.excerpt_en: Bjørn Ove Finseth says the crew at the meteorological station on Hopen have seen five bears so far this season, that is, since the beginning of December.
155868.subtitle_en: On Sunday, the crew at Hopen encountered their fifth bear of the season.

155878.excerpt_en: The parents are reacting primarily to the process and the lack of information. It has been proposed to reduce the space requirement at Polarflokken kindergarten and establish an outdoor group for the oldest children.
155878.subtitle_en: Parents at Polarflokken kindergarten are reacting to plans to create six temporary places to address the shortage of kindergarten places.

155879.excerpt_en: On Monday, representatives from Longyearbyen Local Council inspected the pool at Svalbardhallen. On Saturday, a 40-year-old man injured himself on loose tiles at the bottom of the pool.
155879.subtitle_en: The pool will remain closed this week while attempts are made to repair the damage to its floor.

155887.excerpt_en: The politicians on OKU held a lengthy discussion about the kindergartens and the proposal to temporarily depart from the space requirements for three months to make room for four young children on Polarflokken kindergarten’s waiting list before summer.
155887.subtitle_en: Parents who attended Tuesday’s meeting of the Committee for Education, Children and Culture (OKU) felt that the consequences of squeezing more children into Polarflokken kindergarten had not been adequately assessed.

155899.excerpt_en: Vassdal and Remen had not quite taken it all in when Svalbardposten met them in the kennel on Tuesday evening. That same day, they learned they had been selected as the new trappers at Austfjordnes from the summer for one year. “This is just fantastic.”
155899.subtitle_en: Six huskies will accompany Linda Marie Monsen Vassdal (27) and Pål Remen (37) to Austfjordnes.

155919.excerpt_en: “A sketch has been drawn up of what the area could look like, taking the pressure on available land into account. We have initially envisaged twelve buildings, in pairs.”
155919.subtitle_en: Store Norske wants to start work on the new residential area in Gruvedalen before the frost lets go.

155935.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, Svalbardposten wrote that the Local Council was conducting ground surveys on the northernmost hotel plot at Elvesletta, where the lease agreement has not yet gone through. Chinese national Po Lin Lee applied to build a hotel on the plot in 2014.
155935.subtitle_en: Two of the designated hotel plots at Elvesletta still lie untouched and may be considered for housing.

155953.excerpt_en: There is heavy boat traffic throughout the archipelago during the entire summer season. Boat traffic is also heavy in winter.
155953.subtitle_en: The KV Svalbard is getting more robust oil booms for use in ice-filled waters.

155970.excerpt_en: At the end of February, Svalbardposten wrote that it had been a year since the Old Hospital at Haugen was evacuated following a condition report by Multiconsult. The owners are now left with loans on apartments that are worthless, and will receive nothing from their insurance.
155970.subtitle_en: Both Longyearbyen Local Council and the Governor of Svalbard support making the Old Hospital habitable again. The big question is who will pay.
155970.title_en: Wants Preservation, Says No to Funding

155980.excerpt_en: So far, the turtles are the only ones not to have bred at the Halsvik family’s home at 232 Vei. If they do, it will be a world record for breeding this far north. “Everyone seems to be thriving,” smiles Gustav Halsvik in his tropical extension.
155980.subtitle_en: The warm extension is already too small. Tropical birds and fish are breeding in the polar night and need more space.

155986.excerpt_en: This week, we have something as rare as a horse appearing in the historic picture. The horse was a faithful helper in Longyearbyen for many years, before machines took over all the transport work.
155986.subtitle_en: Do any of our readers recognize the horse in the picture?
155986.tags_en: historic picture, life on Svalbard, history

156002.excerpt_en: In Svalbardposten, Hallvard Holm and Ronny Brunvoll have written about guides’ and tour leaders’ inadequate knowledge of the history of Longyearbyen and Svalbard. Svalbardposten is an important source for the many people who are to tell visitors about the history of the archipelago.
156002.subtitle_en: Per Kyrre Reymert corrects Walling Gorter’s correction.
156002.title_en: Serious Errors About the Second World War

156022.excerpt_en: We celebrated the sun’s return—the sun that is also humanity’s enemy in dry climates.
156022.subtitle_en: In 1.5 billion years, ground temperatures could reach 70 degrees and vegetation could be gone. Eventually the oceans will evaporate, writes Reinhard Mook in this article.
156022.title_en: A Glimpse Beyond the Sun Festival

156034.excerpt_en: Sky-high house prices, few homes on the market and only one plot ready for construction make the situation difficult both for those who want to buy and those who want to rent in Longyearbyen. The town has always had a very special housing arrangement.
156034.subtitle_en: It is time to reassess housing policy.

156045.excerpt_en: The Big Band, which turned ten last year, celebrated a year late. They held the party together with two choirs and a number of solo artists.
156045.subtitle_en: Solfestuka ended with a large joint concert at the cultural centre, conducted by the Big Band.
156045.title_en: The Big Band Brings It to a Close

156087.excerpt_en: On 19 October last year, the sailing boat “Arktika” was towed into Longyearbyen by the Governor of Svalbard.
156087.subtitle_en: The captain of the sailing boat “Arktika” must pay a NOK 30,000 fine and NOK 10,000 in legal costs.

156135.excerpt_en: The clock has just struck twelve, and the first schoolchildren rush out into the schoolyard in Longyearbyen. The favourite activity this winter is so-called OneFoot skiing.
156135.subtitle_en: The shouting is deafening. During recess, the children are enjoying the latest craze on the ski scene – OneFoot.
156135.tags_en: ski play, Longyearbyen School, magazine, children, news, sledding
156135.title_en: Twice the Fun on One Ski

156138.excerpt_en: In our last issue, we published a picture of a horse in Longyearbyen harnessed to a sled carrying milk churns.
156138.subtitle_en: The horse Rector enjoying himself in Pyramiden in 1990.

156160.excerpt_en: Last November’s storm caused the sea to approach Christiane Hübner and Wolfgang Zach’s cabin at great speed. Now they are ready to begin moving it. “It was very quick to get a new anchoring point.”
156160.subtitle_en: It was almost swept away by the sea.

156165.excerpt_en: The National Transport Plan (NTP) 2014–2023 included pledges of NOK 200 million in public funding for a new port in Longyearbyen. In the NTP 2018–2029, to be presented before Easter, that amount has been increased to NOK 300 million.
156165.subtitle_en: If the governing parties get their way, NOK 300 million will be allocated for a new port in Longyearbyen over the coming years.
156165.tags_en: National Transport Plan, port, news, Longyearbyen port

156183.excerpt_en: If the weather and logistics otherwise are on Longyearbyen’s side, it takes at least five to six hours for medical assistance to arrive from Tromsø. After an avalanche buried ten people in Lia in 2015, it took five hours for the first of four air ambulance planes to arrive.
156183.subtitle_en: Local treatment is the weak link when an accident strikes and help is too far away. Now UNN and Helse Nord are demanding that the ministries provide a jet.
156183.title_en: Elevating Air Ambulance Jets to Ministerial Level

article_keywords_en: Ministry of Health and Care Services
156197.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen is clear that emergency preparedness in Longyearbyen must be strengthened with an air ambulance jet in Tromsø. “We have raised the importance of a jet through several channels. Most recently when the Polar Affairs Department was in Longyearbyen last week,” Olsen says.
156197.subtitle_en: The local council agrees that the ministries must get involved in the jet issue, but Minister of Justice Per-Willy Amundsen and Minister of Health Bent Høie make no promises.

156206.excerpt_en: Minister of Health and Care Services Bent Høie goes a long way toward promising funding for a psychology service in Longyearbyen. He last visited the town in connection with Longyearbyen Hospital’s 100th anniversary at the end of February.
156206.subtitle_en: Minister of Health and Care Services Bent Høie goes a long way toward promising funding for a psychology service in Longyearbyen.

156210.excerpt_en: On Friday, Minister of Trade and Industry Monica Mæland (Con.) presented the white paper “Experience Norway – Unique and Extraordinary.” Tourism employs approximately 160,000 people in Norway, and growth here is even stronger than the average international increase.
156210.subtitle_en: It is progress that Svalbard is mentioned at all in the white paper on tourism, several industry representatives believe.

156228.excerpt_en: The hospital in Ny-Ålesund was a so-called “Swedish barracks” dating from 1945 and had been used as a snowmobile garage in recent years. Now it is being converted into twelve new bedsits.
156228.subtitle_en: The old hospital was on its last legs. Then Espen Blix and his helpers stepped in.

156247.excerpt_en: Per Kyrre Reymert points out several minor errors that I myself mention in issue 11 of Svalbardposten. I have the greatest respect for Per Kyrre.
156247.subtitle_en: The debate about the Second World War continues. Here, Waling Gorter responds to Per Kyrre Reymert.
156247.title_en: Speaking Truth to Rome Comes at a Cost

156259.excerpt_en: A good letter to the editor in the latest issue, number 11, dated March 17, about correcting “alternative facts” concerning World War II.

156268.excerpt_en: The latest avalanche in central Longyearbyen in February clearly shows that we have no guarantee that larger disasters cannot strike the archipelago again, hard and brutally. Fortunately, things went well this time.
156268.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen cannot afford to let this issue become a bureaucratic football.

156274.excerpt_en: Last year was yet another record year for Norway’s tourism industry. More and more people are travelling to Svalbard.
156274.subtitle_en: Minister of Trade and Industry Monica Mæland on the new white paper on tourism.

156286.excerpt_en: The administration of the Longyearbyen local council asked the Education and Culture Committee for clarification on the use of Longyearbyen Kindergarten as soon as possible after the avalanche-hazard report from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) was presented. The report was released in mid-December last year and shows that the kindergarten is located in an avalanche-prone area.
156286.subtitle_en: The Education and Culture Committee did not want a kindergarten in an avalanche-prone area and therefore supported closing Longyearbyen Kindergarten.

156292.excerpt_en: Low air temperatures for several days have produced the spectacle of dancing, fluttering and swirling mist above the fjord. Molecules of fjord water escape as invisible vapour into the surrounding air.
156292.subtitle_en: Reinhard Mook explains why it occurs.

156295.excerpt_en: The course leaders were Petter Skants, emergency preparedness coordinator at the Norwegian Seamen’s Church, and offshore chaplain Annstein Lothe. The seminar’s main topics were stress-management techniques, difficult conversations, and social media and crisis management. “This was a very practical course.”
156295.subtitle_en: This weekend, 16 people from Longyearbyen travelled to a crisis-management seminar in Ny-Ålesund.
156295.title_en: Emergency Preparedness Training on the Agenda

156323.excerpt_en: The race committee decided today that this year’s edition of Trappers Trail will be shortened. “It’s because of the weather forecast.”
156323.subtitle_en: Increased avalanche danger is forcing the organizers to alter the race.
156323.title_en: Trappers Trail Has to Be Changed

156335.excerpt_en: Hanevold comes from the position of station chief at the Norwegian Polar Institute’s station in Ny-Ålesund, Sverdrup Station. He will take up the directorship this autumn, succeeding Ole Øiseth, whose fixed-term appointment has ended.
156335.subtitle_en: Per Erik Hanevold has been appointed the new director of Kings Bay, succeeding Ole Øiseth.

156354.excerpt_en: The race committees were suddenly busy as the start of “spring’s most beautiful Svalbard adventure” approached. Low temperatures and winds reaching near gale force in gusts made it virtually impossible to run the planned course to Kapp Laila on Saturday and back to town through Fardalen on Sunday.
156354.subtitle_en: Trappers Trail 2017 had to be changed at the last minute. But the organizers are pleased with the result.
156354.title_en: Safely in Port After Shortened Race

156359.excerpt_en: Managing director Audhild Dahlstrøm is talking to property managers from Statsbygg when Svalbardposten visits Artica Svalbard’s workshop in Sjøområdet on this Tuesday morning.
156359.subtitle_en: On Thursday, Queen Sonja opens Artica Svalbard, which will be celebrated over four days. Here is how the art foundation will develop a local character.

156376.excerpt_en: On 21 February, six residential units were destroyed by an avalanche.
156376.subtitle_en: No one may move back to the upper row of houses in Lia until the snow is gone.

156378.excerpt_en: The Queen will officially open the Artica Svalbard art foundation at Longyearbyen Kulturhus tonight, together with Minister of Culture Linda Hofstad Helleland and local council leader Arild Olsen. Guest artists and writers will be introduced during the opening.
156378.subtitle_en: Today, Queen Sonja arrives in Longyearbyen together with Minister of Culture Linda Hofstad Helleland.

156388.excerpt_en: The first proof had already been completed before the Queen arrived. Magne Furuholmen was among those there to welcome her.
156388.subtitle_en: Queen Sonja received a warm welcome when she arrived at Artica Svalbard’s studio in Sjøområdet this afternoon.
156388.title_en: A Warm Welcome at the Studio

156405.excerpt_en: “There is something about this island kingdom that is both greater and quieter than any words can contain. More powerful.”
156405.subtitle_en: Svalbard has a magical pull on Queen Sonja, and the archipelago played a major role in her becoming an artist.
156405.title_en: An Engaged, Artistic Opening by the Queen

156420.excerpt_en: Spanish filmmaker Carlos Casas, Finnish visual artist Tiina Kivinen and Norwegian musician Mette Henriette are the first guest artists at Artica Svalbard. “They will be here throughout the spring and summer,” says director Audhild Dahlstrøm. The three will take over the studio the art foundation has fitted out in the Sjøområdet district.
156420.subtitle_en: Eleven acclaimed artists and local collaboration are on the agenda for Artica Svalbard, which was launched on Thursday.
156420.title_en: Artica invites artists and locals in

156450.excerpt_en: Almost exactly one year after the Drammen-based company Piql contacted Store Norske about leasing and using part of Mine 3 for the long-term storage of important documents on high-resolution film, the Arctic World Archive was ready to open on Monday this week.
156450.subtitle_en: The written heritage of Mexico’s ancient civilizations is among the first collections of documents to be stored in the Arctic World Archive in Mine 3.

156479.excerpt_en: This week’s historic image was sent to us by Tor Ole Ree. He was inspired by the back-page interview with Stein-Arve Sørensen in issue 6.
156479.subtitle_en: “Milkmaids” at work with the iron cow.

156500.excerpt_en: Less sea ice has dramatic consequences for ice algae, also known as the “grass of the sea,” which form the foundation of the entire marine ecosystem in the Arctic. Researchers have now established an ice observatory in Van Mijenfjorden to map the environmental conditions for the algae.
156500.subtitle_en: Ice algae are the foundation of the Arctic marine ecosystem. What does less sea ice mean for them?
156500.title_en: When the Ice Melts Beneath Arctic Researchers’ Feet

156521.subtitle_en: Sofia Berger, 15, grew up with the dog race in Longyearbyen. This weekend, she won her class for the first time.
156521.title_en: Sofia, 15, finally wins after five Trapper’s Trails

156535.excerpt_en: Former chief administrative officer Sigmund Engdal played a key role when the first agreements between Store Norske and Longyearbyen Local Council were drawn up. He says it all began in the 1990s, when it was decided that Svalbard Samfunnsdrift would manage the land on behalf of Store Norske.
156535.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council and Store Norske reached an agreement on land, roads and river management, but failed to agree on avalanche protection.

156537.excerpt_en: There’s a saying that if you want something done, you should give the task to someone who’s busy.
156537.subtitle_en: Nina Elisabeth Nerbø Storvik (40) is bad at saying no—and loves organizing things.

156563.excerpt_en: Since the landslide occurred just over a month ago, the small family of three has moved from Mary-Ann’s Polarrigg to various apartments. They have told little Sofie Madelen (3) that they have been on holiday.
156563.subtitle_en: Jon Bautz is relying on his lawyer and on the state buying his apartment.

156575.excerpt_en: Hanevold comes from the position of station manager at the Norwegian Polar Institute’s station in Ny-Ålesund, Sverdrup Station. He will take up the directorship this autumn, succeeding Ole Øiseth, who is stepping down at the end of his fixed-term appointment.
156575.subtitle_en: Per Erik Hanevold has been appointed the new director of Kings Bay, succeeding Ole Øiseth.

156589.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Education and Research has asked the Research Council of Norway for input on an overarching strategy for research and higher education in Svalbard, as well as to develop a separate research strategy for Ny-Ålesund. The Research Council has drawn up questions in cooperation with UNIS and is seeking feedback through dialogue meetings and written submissions.
156589.subtitle_en: The overarching research strategy for Svalbard is to be ready by 1 June.

156599.excerpt_en: Svalpro AS wants to facilitate between 35 and 40 apartments of varying sizes. Most are planned as three-room apartments measuring between 60 and 80 square metres.
156599.subtitle_en: Svalpro wants to build two apartment blocks next to its hotel at Elvesletta.

156632.excerpt_en: Eighteen adults and 14 children met Queen Sonja on Friday morning. Parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen says the visit had a warm, relaxed atmosphere.
156632.subtitle_en: During her visit to Longyearbyen, Queen Sonja met relatives and others affected by the two avalanches.
156632.title_en: The Queen Met Avalanche Survivors’ Families

156636.excerpt_en: “A local woman was starting her snowmobile in the parking lot outside Svalbard Snøscooterutleie, and it appears that the throttle had frozen. She was thrown off the snowmobile, which continued on its own,” says Senior Police Officer Irene Welle of the Governor’s Office.
156636.subtitle_en: A snowmobile drove off on its own from Svalbard Snøscooterutleie. This is where the journey ended.

156648.excerpt_en: An older Norwegian man visiting the area overturned on a snowmobile on Monday, and the Governor responded by helicopter to Fredheim near Tempelfjorden. “The man overturned while traversing a slope. He hit his head on a rocky section and suffered injuries to one shoulder and his face.”
156648.title_en: Taken to Hospital After Snowmobile Accident

156663.excerpt_en: Bjørn Frantzen of the Longyearbyen Field Biology Association has sent us these photographs of wildlife in and around Longyearbyen. “Although it is cold, the species that in previous years have followed the calendar more than the temperature are returning,” Frantzen writes.
156663.subtitle_en: Snow buntings and little auks have appeared, while resident species are also thriving in the brighter surroundings.
156663.title_en: Signs of Spring in the Animal Kingdom

156670.excerpt_en: In recent days, many customers have been frustrated that Svalbardbutikken has, among other things, run out of toilet paper. From time to time, other goods have also been unavailable.
156670.subtitle_en: Product availability has been a challenge for Svalbardbutikken in recent weeks.

156677.excerpt_en: At the opening of the new Artica Svalbard arts foundation in Longyearbyen, several people said they felt they had jumped onto an express train already in motion. They were probably not alone.
156677.subtitle_en: Let’s hope the artists who arrive manage both to inspire and provoke.
156677.title_en: High-Speed Train of Art and Culture

156700.excerpt_en: Van Mijenfjorden is currently within Management Area 10, the area that the White Paper on Svalbard (2015–2016) identifies as the main area where tourism is to be facilitated. Van Mijenfjorden in Svalbard is the third-longest fjord in Svalbard.
156700.subtitle_en: “We believe that ever-increasing tourism and traffic generally cause more disturbance to wildlife and degradation of the wilderness than coal mining ever did in Van Mijenfjorden.”
156700.title_en: Van Mijenfjorden and Disturbance of Wildlife

156710.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) is most likely presenting its evaluation report on the February 21 avalanche this week.
156710.subtitle_en: NVE has improved its avalanche forecasting following experience from the February 21 avalanche.

156738.excerpt_en: Because of the historically inadequate focus on alternative business development in Longyearbyen, there was for a time an emphasis on continuing SNSK in order to secure the Norwegian settlement on Svalbard.
156738.subtitle_en: And just as pertinently: What do we mean by local democracy in Longyearbyen?
156738.title_en: What Do We Really Want for Svalbard?

156741.excerpt_en: Nina Jeanette Olaussen was 22 and in her third year of law school when she and a friend were visiting Longyearbyen. They decided to cross Platåberget when they were attacked by a polar bear.
156741.subtitle_en: Every year, a wreath is laid at Ninavarden. This year marks 22 years since student Nina Jeanette Olaussen was killed by a polar bear.
156741.tags_en: nature and environment, news, culture, magazine
156741.title_en: “It Means a Lot to the Family”

156743.excerpt_en: In April, when the days begin to lengthen in Svalbard, it is time for the Norwegian Polar Institute’s glaciologists to unpack their equipment for another field season in Ny-Ålesund. The Norwegian Polar Institute began measuring the mass balance of selected glaciers near Ny-Ålesund in Svalbard as early as 1967.
156743.subtitle_en: The history of mass-balance measurements of glaciers in Svalbard began as early as 1948, when Olav Liestøl was hired as the first glaciologist at the Norwegian Polar Institute.
156743.title_en: 50 Years of Glacier Mass-Balance Measurements in Ny-Ålesund

156763.excerpt_en: The idea for Artica Svalbard arose when the Queen was in Longyearbyen for the opening of Kunsthall Svalbard a couple of years ago. Now it is a reality. “Some of us began talking together.”
156763.subtitle_en: Queen Sonja was one of those who came up with the idea for the Artica Svalbard arts foundation. She hopes Longyearbyen will give the artists a warm welcome.

156769.excerpt_en: The trapping wintering expedition in Tjuvfjorden on Edgeøya during the 1964/65 season ended in a shipwreck in Agardhbukta. After a long, exhausting journey without food or equipment, I arrived in Longyearbyen on the 10th.
156769.subtitle_en: “It was incredibly strange to see the huge, illuminated oil rig there in the Arctic night. Fifty men, a cinema, mess hall, engine room and accommodation. Bulldozers and trucks.”

156792.excerpt_en: “We think it is a great victory for Northern Norway and Svalbard to be named Museum of the Year. This is not a competition among art museums, but among all the museums in the country, so it is significant.”
156792.subtitle_en: The same day the Queen opened Artica Svalbard in Longyearbyen, the Nordnorsk Kunstmuseum and Kunsthall Svalbard received an award. They plan to continue investing in Longyearbyen.

156815.excerpt_en: ›› Line Nagell YlvisåkerA coat-clad Morten Flygel walks through the palace gardens in spring 1995 and finds the world absurd. His back pocket is full of diamonds, but he has no money for food.
156815.subtitle_en: Morten Flygel is trying again in Longyearbyen, where it all began with diamonds on glossy paper.

156821.excerpt_en: Since the first precious drops were bottled at Svalbard Brewery on August 7, 2015, the arrows have pointed in one direction—upward.
156821.subtitle_en: This year, Svalbard Brewery expects to produce 180,000 litres of beer. Owner Robert Johansen and his wife Anne-Grete are now negotiating to bring northern Norway’s beer giant Mack into the ownership group.
156821.title_en: Svalbard Beer Goes Global with Mack

156842.excerpt_en: No contract for deliveries to the airline has been signed yet, but Svalbard Brewery has received a verbal request. “For now, Norwegian has asked to buy 7,500 cans a month.”
156842.subtitle_en: The airline Norwegian also wants to take Svalbard Brewery out into the world.

156864.excerpt_en: During Easter week itself, Longyearbyen will be visited by opera singers Leif Jone Ølberg (baritone) and Beate Mordal (soprano), who together with church musician Jovna Z. Dunfjell will shape the Easter services and also give concerts of their own.
156864.subtitle_en: During Easter week itself, Longyearbyen will be visited by opera singers Leif Jone Ølberg (baritone) and Beate Mordal.

156874.excerpt_en: We return to June 1967. The photograph is from Stig Onarheim’s collection and is part of a series called “Alkemiddag på Revneset.”

156878.excerpt_en: The Governor and Store Norske still disagree over the use of Svea. Last year, the mining company began work on a new plan describing how the areas in Svea are to be used now that the company is in a care-and-maintenance phase.
156878.subtitle_en: The Governor believes Store Norske is now operating illegal tourism activities in Svea. The company disagrees and is appealing the matter to the ministry.

156897.excerpt_en: Emma Hoette (30) grins from ear to ear as she sits down in 13 degrees below zero to talk to Svalbardposten.
156897.subtitle_en: Happiness is her default setting, and she is full of abstractions about life in the Arctic.

156916.excerpt_en: The rider was out driving when he noticed flames shooting out of the snowmobile. The fire service was alerted and extinguished the fire. “The snowmobile is burned out, but no one was injured,” says senior police officer Arve Johnsen of the Governor of Svalbard.
156916.subtitle_en: The fire in the snowmobile was quickly extinguished by the fire service. No one was injured.

156933.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of an avalanche heading down towards the snowmobile trail up towards Linken, above Hiorthhamn, at 3:20 p.m. on Sunday. It was a small, shallow avalanche, and no rescue operation has been launched. “No one has been reported missing after the avalanche,” says senior police officer Bjørn Pedersen of the Governor of Svalbard.
156933.subtitle_en: No one is missing after a minor avalanche near the snowmobile trail leading up to Linken.
156933.title_en: Minor Avalanche Near the Linken Trail

156954.excerpt_en: Leif Jone Ølberg and church musician Jovna Z. Dunfjell opened the concert gently and beautifully with Bach’s “Air” on organ and violin.
156954.subtitle_en: A beautiful concert at Svalbard Church was interrupted by a somewhat unusual pause.
156954.title_en: Concert with an Unexpected Artistic Pause

156970.excerpt_en: The rider, a local woman in her 40s, fell off the snowmobile and was injured on the trail opposite Isdammen. “A helicopter was initially requested, but it was decided to collect her by ambulance from the road,” says senior police officer Marit Ellingsen of the Governor of Svalbard. The extent of her injuries is unknown.
156970.subtitle_en: A snowmobile rider was injured and taken to Longyearbyen Hospital on Wednesday afternoon. It was the third snowmobile accident of the day.

156976.excerpt_en: “It feels strange to stand here. Yesterday I thought that picture fit well where it is hanging.”
156976.subtitle_en: Rakel Huglen has transferred walls from Pyramiden onto screen prints. The exhibition opens on Thursday evening.

157007.excerpt_en: The 25 students talk over one another when Svalbardposten pays a quick visit on Tuesday morning. They have just learned that their research project on polar bears has been selected for the national finals of the 2017 Nysgjerrigper competition. “We have researched polar bears and borders.”
157007.subtitle_en: Third grade at Longyearbyen School is heading to the national finals of the 2017 Nysgjerrigper competition.
157007.title_en: Among the Country’s Most Curious Students

157013.excerpt_en: The incident took place shortly after midnight. Police were notified of a minor traffic accident in Longyearbyen. “The driver had hit another car while driving.”
157013.subtitle_en: A local man in his 30s is suspected of drunk driving following an incident early Wednesday morning.

157019.excerpt_en: At nine o’clock on Thursday, the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) published its evaluation report following the avalanche that hit the buildings in Longyearbyen on 21 February.
157019.subtitle_en: NVE concludes that we must expect numerous evacuations each winter until permanent protection is in place.

157021.excerpt_en: “If disagreements arise among those preparing the final warning, we must choose the most conservative option.”
157021.subtitle_en: To protect the buildings as effectively as possible, NVE concludes that larger safety margins must be introduced and that there will be more evacuations until permanent protection is in place.

157052.excerpt_en: “We must conclude that, for the most part, it was a quiet Easter,” says police department head Ole Jakob Malmo at the Governor’s Office. Wednesday, right at the beginning of the holiday, was the exception this Easter.
157052.subtitle_en: Despite a few snowmobile accidents, both the authorities and the public enjoyed the fine weather this Easter.

157091.excerpt_en: They found the eggs under the Mix kiosk together with their mother, Anette, and grandmother, Heidi Vasdal.
