They completed the entire trail in one day, taking a break halfway at Fruene. “It was a little difficult to find the station by the kindergarten and the one by the sea,” says Frøy.
157091.subtitle_en: Frøy Vasdal Gundersen (10) and her little sister Eira (8) went hunting for the Easter Bunny’s eggs.

157094.excerpt_en: We are featuring yet another photo from Stig Onarheim’s collection. In his younger days, his father Kjell Onarheim was an avid sports enthusiast and athlete.
157094.subtitle_en: Where in Longyearbyen was this photo taken?

157117.excerpt_en: In eastern inland Norway, the wolf is held up as the great bogeyman. Here in Svalbard, local council leader Arild Olsen points to Store Norske while crying wolf.
157117.subtitle_en: Store Norske CEO Wenche Ravlo says local council leader Arild Olsen’s portrayal of Store Norske as reversing democracy in Longyearbyen is inaccurate and unreasonable.
157117.title_en: The Boy Who Cried Wolf, Local Council Leader?

157138.excerpt_en: Lucas normally lives in Vardø with his caregiver and owner, Elisa Jensen. During Easter, they visited Elisa’s father, Arnt Vegar Jensen, and his family, who live in Longyearbyen.
157138.subtitle_en: Lucas, the nearly nine-month-old Chihuahua, was not allowed to return home with Elisa Jensen (16) after their Easter holiday in Svalbard.
157138.title_en: Lucas Had to Return to Svalbard for Quarantine

157141.excerpt_en: In March 1969, I was attending technical school in Gothenburg. I then received a telegram from the oil company Norsk Polarnavigasjon.
157141.subtitle_en: The engine that was still running began to get dangerously hot. The oil pressure dropped. I sat in the back of the cargo compartment, watching the engine instruments over the pilot’s shoulder.

157161.excerpt_en: The Longyearbyen community is changing rapidly. In recent years, the Governor of Svalbard has received more resources in line with growing challenges, on the water, in the air and on land.
157161.subtitle_en: In May, the University Hospital of North Norway and Longyearbyen Hospital will conduct a comprehensive review of primary healthcare and emergency preparedness. That is good—and absolutely necessary.

157177.excerpt_en: Several people have encountered temporary doctors at the hospital in Longyearbyen in recent weeks. The Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority now confirms that there is a conflict at the hospital.
157177.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority calls the situation at Longyearbyen Hospital serious.

157182.excerpt_en: Randi and Birgit became RaBis. Together, they started the shop that was moved from Sjøskrenten to the pedestrian street in 1992.
157182.subtitle_en: Randi Stene Pettersen and Birgit Sjåfjell Brekken have supplied clothing, sewing materials and handicrafts for more than 20 years. Now they hope someone will carry on the business.

157188.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Hospital is responsible both for people seriously injured on snowmobiles or fishing boats and for sick children with high fevers and adults wondering whether something might be seriously wrong. It is both an emergency hospital and a primary healthcare service.
157188.subtitle_en: In May, work will begin to determine what Longyearbyen Hospital should be in the future.

157194.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten reported in March that the University Hospital of North Norway believes an ambulance jet must be stationed in Tromsø to provide Longyearbyen Hospital with rapid assistance in the event of major accidents. Health North sent five.
157194.subtitle_en: UNN is exploring the possibility of stationing an ambulance jet in Tromsø during the winter.

157209.excerpt_en: During a long, dark winter, wind, temperatures and waves have created ice sculptures that would be a success in any gallery. Here are beautiful formations and stylish patterns.
157209.subtitle_en: Nature itself is the artist behind a fantastic exhibition now on display at Kongsfjorden.

157231.excerpt_en: “The rest is up to you now. I recommend kitesurfing,” said pilot Robert Johansen after landing in Svea.
157231.subtitle_en: Strong winds, snow and canceled flights on Friday evening were not ideal for the organizers of Gruveløpet. But the race went ahead—and so did the sunshine.

157266.excerpt_en: On Saturday, Longyearbyen’s emergency preparedness council was called in to examine the cornice problem on Gruvefjellet between the Old Hospital and Nybyen. “Yesterday we flew by helicopter with the local avalanche observers. We wanted to see how large the cornices were, whether they had cracks and whether there were avalanche tracks down the relevant area,” says Senior Police Officer Trond Olsen at the Governor’s Office.
157266.subtitle_en: Cornices on Gruvefjellet fall every year, triggering avalanches toward buildings and roads. Longyearbyen Local Council and the Governor of Svalbard are urging people to take precautions.

157300.excerpt_en: “It was a unanimous jury that decided to award first prize in the ‘boundaries’ category to the third grade at Longyearbyen School,” says Marit Møllhausen of the Research Council of Norway’s research communications department.
157300.subtitle_en: The news of their victory in the national Nysgjerrigper competition reached Line Jansrud’s pupils as she emerged from a garbage bin.

157335.excerpt_en: Presenter Vår Staude landed in Longyearbyen on Thursday afternoon with a friend. It is Staude’s first ever visit to Svalbard, and she will ski the marathon on Saturday. “I’ve wanted to travel to Svalbard for years.”
157335.subtitle_en: On Friday morning, TV 2 will broadcast live from Svalbard during its Good Morning Norway program.

157373.excerpt_en: Relations with Russia have soured since the politicians visited in 2004 and 2012. In 2004, they even visited Barentsburg.
157373.subtitle_en: Russia calls the meeting of NATO’s Parliamentary Assembly provocative, unnecessary and a breach of the spirit of the Svalbard Treaty. The reaction is hardly surprising.
157373.title_en: A NATO Meeting Heavy with Symbolism

157385.excerpt_en: On Tuesday this week, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) held a safety day at which politicians, the LL administration, the Governor’s Office and NVE (the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate) exchanged information about future protection measures, areas of responsibility and expectations. The purpose was to give politicians knowledge of the local council’s role as an authority and to highlight the complexity of different protection measures.
157385.subtitle_en: Frequent evacuations are exhausting for people living in exposed areas, local authorities and those who have to make the decisions.
157385.title_en: Frequent Evacuations Are Stressing the Population

157409.excerpt_en: Svalbard Turn general manager Nina Lines sees no drama in the postponement. The jury agreed to push back the start time.
157409.subtitle_en: The jury has decided to move the start of the Svalbard Ski Marathon back by two hours because of a better weather forecast later in the day.

157414.excerpt_en: It all began with a ski race between Longyearbyen and Barentsburg, with the two towns taking turns hosting the start. When people on the mainland asked to take part, the race was expanded.
157414.subtitle_en: Skiing legend Oddvar Brå was the very first to cross the finish line in the Svalbard Ski Marathon in 1993.

157457.excerpt_en: According to Ravlo, Arild Olsen says that “Store Norske has a clearly defined governmental role in the local community—a role exempt from democratic oversight.” The real problem is probably that Store Norske takes on such a role, and there are many examples of it.
157457.subtitle_en: “As Ravlo rightly points out, business activity on Svalbard will remain a marginal undertaking for some. And the last thing we need then is for a company living on the state’s grace and goodwill to compete with private enterprise.”

157462.excerpt_en: NVE Report 31-2017 on the avalanche on February 21 this year can be read as follows: Local avalanche warnings after the avalanche incident on the 19th.
157462.subtitle_en: “My conclusion is: Put avalanche protection in place this summer.”

157473.excerpt_en: In 1969, we realized that a total ban on polar-bear hunting was imminent. Together with Arild Strand and Svein Ytreland, I went trapping on Edgeøya in the autumn of 1969.
157473.subtitle_en: “I hailed a taxi, and when I told the driver CFP Forasol, he waved away any further explanation of my dreadful school French. We sped off into the traffic.”
157473.title_en: From Trapping to Oil on Edgeøya

157486.excerpt_en: “Look how beautiful it is. It looks like a little polar bear,” says Astrid B.
157486.subtitle_en: Third grade from Longyearbyen enjoyed a wonderful day visiting our Russian neighbors.

157489.excerpt_en: It is past 10 o’clock, and the starting gun for Gruverennet should have gone off.
157489.subtitle_en: “It’s not the biggest mistake I’ve made,” said former Store Norske director Robert Hermansen, 78, when he finally reached the starting line. See the race photo gallery here!

157516.excerpt_en: A couple of days after Daniel Husdal struggled his way through the 45-kilometer Gruverennet, he is back on skis. This time at the head of Adventdalen, on an outing with his class.
157516.subtitle_en: Daniel Husdal, 14, does not really think a half marathon is anything to brag about.

157519.excerpt_en: “This will be an aircraft that is not part of the regular service, but will fly to Svalbard in emergencies,” says Oddvar Larsen, head of emergency preparedness at Helse Nord. Initially, the jet will be operational during the winter half of the year.
157519.subtitle_en: Helse Nord wants an air ambulance jet stationed in Tromsø to fly exclusively to Svalbard during the winter season.
157519.title_en: Could Arrive by Jet This Autumn

157539.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten reported in its previous issue that in May, Helse Nord will review the staffing arrangements at Longyearbyen Hospital, with a view to improving preparedness—particularly the physician staffing situation.
157539.subtitle_en: Nurses at Longyearbyen Hospital believe having an anesthesiologist on the rescue helicopters would significantly strengthen emergency preparedness.

157553.excerpt_en: The avalanche report for the cabin areas was supposed to be finished by Easter. It is still not ready, but Multiconsult has sent preliminary avalanche hazard maps to Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) and Store Norske.
157553.subtitle_en: Owners of cabins in avalanche-prone areas are being offered new plots, but will not be allowed to move before next winter. By then, more plots for new construction should also be ready.

157572.excerpt_en: This week’s historic image was, believe it or not, taken in June 1966 by Kjell Onarheim. The fjord is full of ice, and the caption to the more-than-50-year-old photograph reads: “Nordvarg, icebreaker, as the first boat in 1966.”
157572.subtitle_en: “Nordvarg” Breaks Through the Fjord Ice in June 1966.
157572.tags_en: historic image, life in Svalbard, history

157582.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Public Library will soon be ready to move. After 31 years at Lompen Shopping Centre, the library will move into newly refurbished premises in the Næringsbygget.
157582.subtitle_en: If you are going to borrow books from the library, the local council would prefer you to do it now.
157582.tags_en: news, Næringsbygget, library, Longyearbyen Public Library
157582.title_en: New Library Ready to Be Filled

157612.excerpt_en: On Thursday evening, four people were rescued from the water after falling through the ice on Tempelfjorden. One is critically injured and unstable; another has moderate injuries.
157612.subtitle_en: Life-saving equipment did not reach Longyearbyen on Thursday because it was not possible to send it on regular air ambulances.
157612.title_en: “The Accident Shows the Need for a Jet”

157624.excerpt_en: Although the Svalbard Ski Marathon was postponed by two hours to get somewhat better weather, things did not turn out quite as hoped. There was little sunshine and rather a lot of wind.
157624.subtitle_en: Emil Iversen finished almost 20 minutes ahead of second place in the marathon class, with a time of 2 hours and 10 minutes.
157624.title_en: Iversen Wins by a Wide Margin

157636.excerpt_en: The road reopened at around 2 p.m. on Sunday after being closed since Saturday. “We have reopened the road,” confirms Kjersti Olsen Ingerø, head of the technical sector at Longyearbyen Local Council.
157636.subtitle_en: Road 300 between Museumsveien and Huset has reopened after being closed because of avalanche danger.

157638.excerpt_en: A man on a snowmobile and a man who drove off the road in a car are suspected of driving under the influence. The Governor’s Office received a report of a car leaving the road at around midnight.
157638.subtitle_en: Two men are suspected of driving under the influence during the night. Otherwise, it was a quiet 24 hours.

article_keywords_en: senior police officer at the Governor’s Office
157642.excerpt_en: A reindeer went over a cliff and broke its front leg near Burmaveien. It was so badly injured that it had to be euthanized.
157642.subtitle_en: An injured reindeer has been euthanized.

157663.excerpt_en: Anna Marie Sandal Strømseng, 5, was one of 97 registered skiers preparing in the starting area outside Svalbardhallen on Sunday morning. She has attended almost all of Telenor’s ski-training events this winter and was well prepared.
157663.subtitle_en: The children enjoyed sunshine and excellent conditions at this year’s ski festival.
157663.title_en: Ski Festival in Glorious Sunshine for the Youngest

157680.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Bureau for the Investigation of Police Affairs is examining whether a criminal offence occurred before the 2015 avalanche, and, if so, who was responsible. “It could be individuals or companies. It is too early to draw any conclusions now,” says Halvor Hjelm-Hansen, who is leading the investigation.
157680.subtitle_en: Halvor Hjelm-Hansen and the Norwegian Bureau for the Investigation of Police Affairs were in Longyearbyen last week to conduct interviews.

157718.excerpt_en: Maya Lunde, Jørn Lier Horst, Lars Saabye Christensen and Annie Proulx are probably just some of the well-known authors who will be the main attractions at the Longyearbyen Literature Festival from 4 to 8 [date incomplete].
157718.subtitle_en: The new library is getting a spectacular start.

157741.excerpt_en: “This time, we have broken all records,” says Morten Ruud, chair of the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund. The fund, which is built up through the environmental fee on airline tickets to Svalbard, makes allocations twice a year.
157741.subtitle_en: In a record-sized allocation from the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund, Trust Arktikugol received the largest individual grant.
157741.title_en: Pyramiden Wins Big from Environmental Protection Fund

157752.excerpt_en: Once again, we show a “summer picture” from a time when summer looked rather different. Kjell Onarheim’s photograph is titled “Nordsel, June 1963” and shows conditions very different from those we have in June today.

157755.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten has to wait its turn when we visit Einar, the operations engineer at Longyearbyen Local Council (LL). In his office, Einar is discussing inspections of the elevated reservoir, both by phone and with a colleague. “If I remember correctly, there was a fault there in the autumn.”
157755.subtitle_en: Einar Olsen, 34, probably should not be smiling so much. But he cannot help it.
157755.tags_en: people, life in Svalbard, back page

157769.excerpt_en: On Friday afternoon, Statsbygg was informed by the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation that it had been awarded the plot in Gruvedalen, where Store Norske began work on new housing this winter. “Our homes were affected by the avalanches, and we have kept the ministry continuously informed about the housing situation.”
157769.title_en: Construction Halted on Store Norske Housing

157780.excerpt_en: Because of the severe housing shortage following the latest avalanche, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) initially asked to develop the plot in Gruvedalen and lead the project there. Store Norske, which manages the land on behalf of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, said no.
157780.subtitle_en: Store Norske has unexpectedly been stripped of the task of developing Gruvedalen. On Friday, the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation (KMD) asked Statsbygg to take on the entire development. What does this complete about-face really mean?

157805.excerpt_en: The poor weather forecasts did not dampen the number of entries. This year’s race had 933 registered participants.
157805.subtitle_en: Despite brisk weather and difficult waxing conditions, the Ulvang family thought taking part in the Svalbard Ski Marathon was a great experience.

157850.excerpt_en: The revised national budget will be presented this coming Thursday. According to Nordlys, it includes a proposal to allocate NOK 48 million for avalanche protection and housing construction in Longyearbyen.
157850.subtitle_en: The government is proposing NOK 48 million for avalanche protection in the revised national budget.
157850.title_en: Avalanche Protection and New Construction for NOK 48 Million

157864.excerpt_en: The woman rolled her snowmobile near Fritham at around 11 a.m. on Sunday. “She had back pain and needed assistance getting to hospital,” says senior police officer Anders Haugerud at the Governor’s Office. The woman was flown to the airport, and an ambulance transported her from there to Longyearbyen Hospital.
157864.subtitle_en: A female resident was flown to Longyearbyen Hospital on Sunday morning after a snowmobile rollover.

157881.excerpt_en: Tomorrow, Tuesday, Climate and Environment Minister Vidar Helgesen (H) will give the opening address at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly conference in Longyearbyen. He will speak about the global consequences of climate change and related security policy issues.
157881.subtitle_en: Climate and Environment Minister Vidar Helgesen (H) is one of several speakers at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly meeting in Longyearbyen on Tuesday.
157881.title_en: To Open NATO Meeting on Tuesday

157884.excerpt_en: The service building is the very heart of the research community in Ny-Ålesund. It contains a shared cafeteria, reception and offices.
157884.subtitle_en: Environment Minister Vidar Helgesen brought NOK 12 million for upgrading the service building when he visited Ny-Ålesund on Monday.

157889.excerpt_en: Norway’s liberation was commemorated at the grave of the “forgotten” war hero Trond Astrup Vigtel on Monday. On 8 May 1954, the German occupation was over and Norway could celebrate its freedom.
157889.subtitle_en: Norway’s liberation was commemorated at the grave of the “forgotten” war hero Trond Astrup Vigtel.

157896.excerpt_en: Digital Balke is a digital exhibition focusing on the northern Norwegian landscape motifs of Romantic painter Peder Balke. An electronic sound work composed by musician Gaute Barlindhaug has been created for the presentation.
157896.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, the Northern Norway Art Museum opened the Digital Balke exhibition at Kunsthall Svalbard. On 17 May, glass art will be shown at Galleri Svalbard.
157896.title_en: Digital and glass art on display

157911.excerpt_en: The government is proposing to give Statsbygg NOK 28 million for planning and ground surveys to prepare for housing construction in Gruvedalen and Nedre Skjæringa, where it will also draw up a zoning plan.
157911.subtitle_en: As is well known, Svalbard is receiving money for avalanche protection, new homes and securing the service building in Ny-Ålesund. Today, the revised national budget was presented.

157923.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries (NFD) is introducing a loan guarantee scheme for housing and business purposes.
157923.subtitle_en: The long-awaited loan guarantee scheme intended to ensure that the bank provides loans for business purposes was presented in the revised budget. The bank is not satisfied.
157923.title_en: The bank is not changing its practices

157934.excerpt_en: Technology company ABB has estimated that a subsea cable to Svalbard would cost NOK 3–5 billion, depending on whether a backup cable is installed. But the government does not consider a cable a satisfactory solution for the archipelago.
157934.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Petroleum and Energy has been tasked with investigating Svalbard’s future energy supply. And it is to be local.

157964.excerpt_en: Svalbard is an attractive tourist market. More and more people are discovering the fantastic nature and the truly unique experiences available here.
157964.subtitle_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard is showing great confidence in the future and in tourism on Svalbard by investing NOK 200 million in Longyearbyen. This will almost certainly also bring many contracts for local businesses and create more jobs in the long term.

157972.excerpt_en: Minister Helgesen was also in Ny-Ålesund in October, when the government allocated NOK 20.5 million for a new shared research building. “This is a special occasion. I am pleased to be here again to unveil the foundation stone for the new building.”
157972.subtitle_en: Climate and Environment Minister Vidar Helgesen unveiled the foundation stone for the new research building in Ny-Ålesund on Monday.

157975.excerpt_en: Before the weekend, it was leaked that the government is proposing to allocate NOK 48 million for housing construction and avalanche protection in Longyearbyen. The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) will have NOK 20 million at its disposal for avalanche protection, while Statsbygg will receive NOK 28 million for ground surveys and planning for new homes in Longyearbyen.
157975.subtitle_en: NOK 28 million for housing construction in the revised national budget means Statsbygg is moving ahead at full speed.
157975.tags_en: avalanche protection, news, Statsbygg, avalanche-prone areas

157996.excerpt_en: Climate and Environment Minister Vidar Helgesen brought NOK 12 million for upgrading the service building when he visited Ny-Ålesund on Monday. The service building is the very heart of the research community in Ny-Ålesund.
157996.subtitle_en: Lunch ended with good news for Kings Bay director Ole Øiseth.

158001.excerpt_en: “It won’t be a graduation celebration like those on the mainland. But we have planned a few antics,” says Vilde Klausen Markussen, president of this year’s Svalbard graduating class.
158001.subtitle_en: This year’s graduating class consists of just five people, but they still plan to make their mark.

158018.excerpt_en: The big move is about to begin. Nineteen thousand books will be moved from the top-floor premises at Lompensenteret to the newly built library in Næringsbygget.
158018.subtitle_en: After 31 years of library operations at Lompensenteret, the service ended with a twist for every book borrowed.

158034.excerpt_en: This week’s historic photograph was taken just four years ago, but it is nevertheless historical in every sense. Last week, Svalbardposten received an email forwarded by Thorvald Ianssen, which he had sent to article author Per Johnsson.

158040.excerpt_en: Not all of the museum’s objects are on display or packed away in storage. A few, such as the Berzelius rig, stand fully visible outdoors.

158064.excerpt_en: Consul General Vjatjeslav Nikolajev welcomed Governor Kjerstin Askholt and around a dozen Norwegian guests from Longyearbyen. In his speech, he emphasized the efforts made by the soldiers during the war and also commemorated all those who sacrificed their lives.
158064.subtitle_en: On Friday, 5 May, Restaurant Krasnij Medved in Barentsburg hosted celebrations marking the 72nd anniversary of victory after the Second World War.

158082.excerpt_en: In recent years, there has been a very positive focus on the tourism industry in Svalbard, and Longyearbyen is well on its way to becoming one of the world’s most exclusive and rugged destinations, with many positive forces at work.
158082.subtitle_en: Can we become even better? ask two of the men behind Svalbard Adventure Group.
158082.title_en: Longyearbyen: From company town to world-class tourist destination

158083.excerpt_en: Nature on Svalbard is often described in terms of glaciers, snow and barren mountains, but this is far from the reality. As many as 180 vascular plant species and several hundred species of mosses and lichens grow on Svalbard.
158083.subtitle_en: Vascular plants, mosses and lichens perform a vital function in the tundra ecosystem. Without them, there would be neither reindeer, ptarmigan nor geese, permafrost would thaw faster and erosion could increase.
158083.tags_en: feature articles, news, nature and the environment
158083.title_en: The green Arctic in a changing climate

158091.excerpt_en: “We are here to work together with Longyearbyen Hospital, see how they work and act as discussion partners on what can be done differently to provide an even better service,” says Lars Røsli, head of the Emergency Medicine Clinic in Tromsø, which the local hospital has now become part of…
158091.subtitle_en: This week, the clinic director and five others from UNN were in Longyearbyen to discuss the hospital of the future.
158091.title_en: Finding new solutions for the future

158111.excerpt_en: “It’s the architect calling,” says Knut Harald Holst-Hansen, silencing the ringing. Hurtigruten Svalbard has long had plans for further expansion and upgrades.
158111.subtitle_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard is starting work now. New IGP facilities will be ready by autumn, and Funken will reopen in a new-old guise next season.

158122.excerpt_en: “I am leaving for personal reasons. I will work until the end of August and leave in September.”
158122.subtitle_en: As NOK 200 million is being poured into Hurtigruten Svalbard, the company is searching for a new chief executive.

158156.excerpt_en: The salute at seven o’clock marked the start of a wonderful day in Longyearbyen. Sunshine through partly clear skies and temperatures of around four degrees below zero created a great atmosphere in the parade.
158156.subtitle_en: Constitution Day was celebrated on 17 May in partly sunny weather and only a few degrees below freezing. Some even wore traditional national costume shoes in the parade.

158163.excerpt_en: “Longyearbyen has been important to me. It is about developing as a person, and I have been given the opportunity to do that.”
158163.subtitle_en: Sveinung Lystrup Thesen (41) was happy and humble as he accepted Longyearbyen’s Culture and Community Prize for 2017.
158163.title_en: The Culture Prize Went to Sveinung

158169.excerpt_en: Marit Karlsen Brandal has been the course leader for this year’s humanist confirmation candidates. Saturday, 13 May.
158169.subtitle_en: On Saturday, 13 May, five young people were confirmed at the cultural centre.

158194.excerpt_en: When the snow melts, the sins are revealed: bottles, plastic bags, straws, and a cardboard box that blew away last year.
158194.subtitle_en: Aktiv i friluft has received NOK 1.3 million for beach clean-ups in Isfjorden this summer. But before we tackle the beaches, we will clean up around our own homes.

158215.excerpt_en: This year, the shop’s shelves have repeatedly been empty. Minced meat, smoked salmon, unseasoned canned tomatoes, noodles, coffee beans, different types of flour, infant formula and toilet paper, to name just a few.
158215.subtitle_en: Two new employees will help ensure that Svalbardbutikken keeps toilet paper and coffee on its shelves.

158229.excerpt_en: The work of assessing Svalbard’s future energy supply will finally get properly under way. Following the presentation of the revised national budget, the government is assigning the task to the Ministry of Petroleum and Energy.
158229.subtitle_en: It is high time to prepare Svalbard for the day when coal will eventually run out, and developing other renewable energy sources is urgent.

158257.excerpt_en: The school’s principal, Yana Kudryavtseva, gives us a tour of the 30-year-old building in perfect English. She has lived both in the United States and London.
158257.subtitle_en: The school in Barentsburg is being renovated. It is due to be ready in September.

158318.excerpt_en: Last weekend, he went on a solo cabin trip to Derten in Engelskbukta. The cabin is a 12-kilometre snowmobile ride from Ny-Ålesund.
158318.subtitle_en: Leif Arild Håhjem (61) has spent a total of twelve years in Ny-Ålesund. He has even become part of the museum collection.

158348.excerpt_en: Statsbygg once again has to take measures to protect the seed vault from water intrusion. “Higher temperatures and more rain are a major challenge for us. The permafrost has not re-established itself as expected.”
158348.subtitle_en: Statsbygg is now beginning work to dig trenches to divert water away from the entrance. They are on high alert when the snowmelt begins.
158348.title_en: More Protection Needed for the Seed Vault

158351.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) received NOK 20 million in the revised national budget to implement the first measure to protect against avalanches. The plan is to install snow-support structures to lock the snow in place, combined with snow fences on the plateau above the pointed-roof houses, the lowest part of Lia.
158351.subtitle_en: The detailed design for the first protective measure in Lia is due to be completed in mid-July. The work will then be put out to tender.

158354.excerpt_en: In her speech of remembrance, Ravlo said that on this day, people’s thoughts especially turn to those who gave their lives during the Second World War.
158354.subtitle_en: In her speech on 17 May, Store Norske CEO Wenche Ravlo paid special tribute to the 26 people commemorated by the memorial at Skjæringa.

158393.excerpt_en: The satirical English-language newspaper is called “The Ny-Ålesund Herald” and has been published twice so far, three weeks apart. The latest issue ran to two A4 pages.
158393.subtitle_en: Sally Hovelsø (26) has launched her own summer newspaper in Ny-Ålesund. It has been well received.

158395.excerpt_en: On May 31, Svalbard Cruise Network is inviting all residents of Longyearbyen to breakfast on Burma Road.

158408.excerpt_en: In June last year, a female bear with a cub was shot at Austfjordnes. The autopsy showed that she had pellets in her body.
158408.subtitle_en: Both female bears killed last summer had previously been shot at with a shotgun.
158408.title_en: Old shotgun pellets found in bears

158438.excerpt_en: The absence of a fire safety officer, fire drills and instructions for employees, as well as procedures for hot work, were among the measures Svalbard Adventure Group had not put in place when the fire service carried out an inspection last month. They visited Svalbard Hotell 1 and 2, Svalbar Lodge and Svalbar. “We see the need for inspections, particularly at accommodation establishments.”
158438.subtitle_en: Svalbard Adventure Group was reprimanded after a fire inspection last month.

158459.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten previously reported that 14 cabins lie in the 100-year hazard zone for various types of avalanches or landslides in the Bjørndalen–Vestpynten, Vindodden and Todalen areas.
158459.subtitle_en: The final avalanche reports for the cabin areas show that 30 cabins lie within the 100-year hazard zone. Many are also in the orange zone, which imposes restrictions.

158462.excerpt_en: Last month, Store Norske appealed the Governor of Svalbard’s decision at the end of March that tourist and research activities in Svea must stop because they violate the land-use plan. Store Norske appealed the decision, and this week the response came from the Ministry of Climate and the Environment.
158462.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Climate and the Environment agrees with the Governor of Svalbard that Store Norske may not accommodate tourists and researchers in Svea.

158477.excerpt_en: Climate science has been an empirical science. Its foundation is observation—empirical evidence.
158477.subtitle_en: A previous issue of Svalbardposten referred to Professor Ole Humlum’s conclusion that today’s warming falls within “nature’s” fluctuations. Nothing to worry about, he believes. He argues that climate models are unscientific because forecasts cannot be tested over a long period.

158516.excerpt_en: The mean temperature was 0.2 degrees higher than normal at the end of May: −3.9 degrees compared with the normal average of −4.1 degrees. This means there have been 78 consecutive months with a mean temperature above normal at the measuring station at Svalbard Airport.
158516.subtitle_en: High temperatures during the final two days of May resulted in yet another month with a mean temperature above normal.
158516.title_en: A Cold May, but Still Warmer Than Average

158532.excerpt_en: Eight-year-olds Ingeborg Hoem and Astrid Andersen were far from alone in admiring the first cruise ships to arrive in Longyearbyen on Wednesday. As the “Aidaluna” maneuvered into the quay, around 50 people in attendance cheered a welcome and waved flags.
158532.subtitle_en: “The cruise ships are the coolest of all because they have swimming pools on deck.”
158532.tags_en: news, cruise, Svalbard Cruise Network, cruise tourism
158532.title_en: A Warm Welcome for the Guests

158536.excerpt_en: Thorvald Ianssen sent us this photograph, taken at the head of Grønfjorden in the summer of 1967. According to Ianssen, it is the MS “Skule” in the background.

158547.excerpt_en: The seed vault was established so that the world’s genebanks could store backup copies of their seed collections and ensure that individual food or useful plant species are not wiped out by local or global disasters such as war, terrorism or natural disasters. The genebank has already demonstrated that it is extremely important.
158547.subtitle_en: Next year marks ten years since the Svalbard Global Seed Vault celebrated its opening. Since then, the seed storage facility, with its distinctive concrete entrance portal, has received a great deal of international attention.

158559.excerpt_en: Initially, NOK 14 million has been allocated solely to investigation and design work on the seed storage facility. The aim is to strengthen the vault’s security from a long-term perspective.
158559.subtitle_en: Consulting firm Dr. Techn. Olav Olsen has been tasked with proposing further improvement measures to secure the access tunnel to the seed vault.
158559.title_en: NOK 37 million in improvements to seed storage facility

158564.excerpt_en: On 1 April, German Katja Baum set out from Longyearbyen on skis towards the southernmost point of Spitsbergen.
158564.subtitle_en: Katja Baum (29) spent 49 days skiing the length of Spitsbergen. First from Longyearbyen to Sørneset at the southern tip, then north to Verlegenhuken at the far north. Then back again.

158570.excerpt_en: On Saturday, an open day was held at Svalsat with barbecues, tours, lectures, quizzes and drawing for the youngest visitors, in brilliant sunshine, as KSAT celebrated its 20th anniversary. “It’s exciting to come up here and see.”
158570.subtitle_en: Station manager Ole Petter Storstad was pleased to be able to show Svalsat to the town’s residents.

158613.excerpt_en: It undoubtedly took considerable thought, time and money to organise the open day at Svalsat, which has been operating for 20 years already. For the second time—most recently in May 2015—children and adults were invited in glorious weather.
158613.subtitle_en: Reinhard Mook hopes KSAT will repeat the success of its open day at Svalsat.

158620.excerpt_en: Staff reductions in the mining industry in recent years have affected employment figures more than can be seen in population trends. Employment statistics, based on figures from Statistics Norway, show a total decline of 150 in the number of employed people from 2015 to 2016, equivalent to 12 per cent of the total workforce.
158620.subtitle_en: Terje Aunevik, head of the Svalbard Business Association, believes it is worrying that employment has fallen noticeably.

158634.excerpt_en: Students who can demonstrate ten years of ties to Northern Norway may gain easier admission to medicine, law, dentistry, pharmacy and other sought-after programmes, either through reserved places or with a few fewer points than other students.
158634.subtitle_en: A whole lifetime on Svalbard is not enough to apply for the northern Norwegian student quota at UiT The Arctic University of Norway. “Unfair,” says the russepresident.

158639.excerpt_en: Backer first encountered Svalbard in 1987 and was immediately bitten by the Svalbard bug. Since then, she has visited many times and drawn a great deal of inspiration from Ny-Ålesund.
158639.subtitle_en: Mosaic artist Harriet Backer (83) believes more people should make use of the artists’ cabin in Ny-Ålesund.

158658.excerpt_en: “If we do not gain access to housing soon, particularly for holiday replacements and other seasonal employees, we will be unable to let people take their holidays. This applies to kindergartens, Energiverket and other municipal employees.”
158658.subtitle_en: On Monday, Longyearbyen Local Council decided to use its housing in the area where the Governor has imposed a standing ban on staying and travelling.
158658.tags_en: avalanche, housing shortage, avalanche danger, news

158671.excerpt_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard applied to Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) for a licence to serve beer and wine to guests taking snowcat tours. The tours, with something nice in the glass, were to travel into Adventdalen on one side of the valley and return on the other.

158703.excerpt_en: “The dream was to win, and my tactic was simply to give it everything I had from the start,” says Swede Andreas Nygren after winning the Spitsbergen Marathon in 2:58:06. It was also a new personal best.
158703.subtitle_en: Andreas Nygren set a new personal best and won his first marathon.
158703.title_en: Swede first across the finish line

158720.excerpt_en: It has taken a long time to finish the fast-food section of the Mix kiosk, but today it is finally opening. “Initially, we will stay open until 3 a.m. on Thursdays, and until 4:30 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays,” says general manager Leif-Arne Plahter.
158720.subtitle_en: Sausages, hamburgers, kebabs and buffalo wings until 4:30 in the morning.

158743.excerpt_en: With the exception of Svea, all Telenor’s base stations on Svalbard have been upgraded to 4G, and most have gone a little further and can now boast that they are 4G+ stations. For those less interested in technology, 4G can be explained as the fourth generation of mobile services.
158743.subtitle_en: 20 years since the first base station was built.

158752.excerpt_en: Assistant Governor Berit Sagfossen confirms that the case against the German has been suspended under Section 250 of the Criminal Procedure Act: “If the prosecuting authority finds that there are grounds for bringing charges, but that the accused cannot be convicted because his whereabouts are unknown or because he is abroad, the case is provisionally…”
158752.subtitle_en: The German who was arrested and charged last summer with tagging several buildings in Longyearbyen will probably get away with it.

158759.excerpt_en: Ten-year-olds Mathilde Hagebø, Dana Sofie Myhrvang Jacobsen and Embla Therese Abild were seated in front of two of the computer screens at the back of the library on opening day. They were unanimous in their verdict on the new library. “It’s good.”
158759.subtitle_en: The new library is much better than the old one. It is bigger, too, says Mathilde Hagebø (10).
158759.title_en: Cake and a warm welcome for the city’s new landmark

158761.excerpt_en: “It must have been a little exciting to be a whaler, but I think it was cold.”
158761.subtitle_en: Last Thursday, fifth- and sixth-graders at Longyearbyen School went down to the shore to learn how whalers boiled oil in the 1600s and 1700s.

158791.excerpt_en: “We are delighted with the new participation record and a great event,” says Silje M. Hagen, head of Svalbard Turn, which organises Spitsbergen Marathon.
158791.subtitle_en: Spitsbergen Marathon set a new participation record in glorious sunshine. A total of 374 runners took part in this year’s event.

158794.excerpt_en: “There’s quite a lot of rubbish, and that’s pretty silly. I think people are not very good at throwing things in the bin,” says Vetle Antoni Lutnæs, 7.
158794.subtitle_en: A community clean-up was held in Longyearbyen on Tuesday afternoon. Many people came out to help remove rubbish from the streets, something that was clearly needed.
158794.title_en: Invited the Town to a Community Clean-Up

158839.excerpt_en: The mean temperature was 0.2 degrees higher than normal at the end of May: −3.9 degrees compared with the normal average temperature of −4.1 degrees. This means there have been 78 consecutive months with a higher-than-normal mean temperature at the weather station at Svalbard Airport.
158839.subtitle_en: The high temperatures during the last two days of May resulted in yet another month with a higher mean temperature than normal.
158839.title_en: Cold May, but Still Above Average Temperature

158857.subtitle_en: This summer there will be two weeks without a print edition of Svalbardposten. Instead, the online newspaper will be opened free of charge to everyone, and articles will be published continuously there during the two paper-free weeks.
158857.title_en: Two weeks without a paper newspaper

158863.excerpt_en: He first encountered the archipelago in 1976, on an assignment for Tromsø Museum, when the Governor of Svalbard asked them to establish cultural heritage protection on Svalbard through documentation and outreach.
158863.subtitle_en: “My grandfather and I used to visit the old museum in Tromsø on Sundays. Ever since then, I have known that I wanted to work with history and archaeology,” says Per Kyrre Reymert, 72.

158871.excerpt_en: While researchers from many countries study ice, fish, polar bears, seals, marine life, the atmosphere, birds and the climate, Professor Paul Wenzel Geissler studies the researchers. What do they do?
158871.subtitle_en: One of the most important qualities of a good researcher is listening to their doubts and other emotions. You have to wonder and ask questions, says the social anthropologist.

158883.excerpt_en: Even in the High Arctic, we are close to our Nordic neighbours. It is only a two-hour flight with Lufttransport’s aircraft from Longyearbyen at 78°N to Villum Research Station, Station Nord (VRS), in northernmost Greenland at 81°N 36’N.
158883.subtitle_en: Nordic Arctic cooperation on research and higher education in the High Arctic.

158900.excerpt_en: Physical geographer Ole Humlum writes in SP issue 21, page 19: “Meteorology and climatology are traditionally subdisciplines of physical geography.”
158900.subtitle_en: Physical geographer Humlum examines weather statistics from the past and present without finding any alarming signs so far.

158910.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, 13 kindergarten children from Barentsburg visited the children at Kullungen and Polarflokken kindergartens in Longyearbyen. The parent councils at the two kindergartens had applied for travel funding, making it possible to hire a boat for the journey. “The children have been really looking forward to having visitors.”
158910.subtitle_en: “The children are culturally different, but children are children, and they play together,” says the head of the kindergarten.

158924.excerpt_en: We continue with Thorvald Ianssen’s striking photographs from the summer of 1967. Bodil Randers was employed as a cook, but proved that she could do more than prepare food.

158927.excerpt_en: Around 70 children lined up at the start when Sparebank1 organised the Labb and Line race on Saturday. “It was really fun, but also very tiring, because I didn’t take a break and ran the longest course,” says Astrid Andersen (7).
158927.subtitle_en: Perhaps this year’s Labb and Line race featured the next generation of marathon runners. At any rate, they had fun.

158930.excerpt_en: A total of 54 housing units had been evacuated ever since the latest avalanche struck in Lia on 21 February this year.
158930.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard lifted the evacuation of the area containing the 54 housing units in Lia.

158942.excerpt_en: A double-glazed window in the kitchen/office area had a huge hole in it when the staff at Kroa arrived at work early this morning. “No one has heard or seen anything.”
158942.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard wants to get in touch with any witnesses, if there are any.

158982.excerpt_en: At 6:30 p.m. on Wednesday, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre received a report that a sailboat had run aground at Cape Laila. It was travelling with two other boats, and one of the three had gone too close to shore.

159006.excerpt_en: On Thursday afternoon, the Administration Committee and Longyearbyen Local Council were due to meet to agree on a statement responding to a letter from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, asking for the politicians’ views on the way forward for Store Norske. Instead, the meeting was postponed until Friday the 23rd.
159006.subtitle_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen chose to postpone Thursday’s planned meetings at which politicians were to adopt their position on Store Norske’s future. Liberal Party leader Oddmund Rønning is pleased with the decision.

159009.excerpt_en: Over the weekend, the residents of Road 226-35 and 226-37—Jon Bautz and his family, and Morten Helliksen—moved back into their homes. They had been evacuated since the avalanche struck on the 21st.
159009.subtitle_en: There was a cheerful mood when the neighbours on Road 226 moved back home over the weekend after four months of evacuation.
159009.tags_en: news, evacuation, avalanche protection, the slope
159009.title_en: Finally Home Again After Four Months of Evacuation

159037.excerpt_en: “It’s great to celebrate an anniversary, and very fun that people show up,” says Morten Ruud, chair of Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund. The anniversary was marked with a range of activities in Longyearbyen last week, with the aim of showcasing some of the projects that have received support from the fund.
159037.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund celebrated its tenth anniversary this weekend with singing, cake and plenty of activities.
159037.title_en: Has Distributed NOK 110 Million in 10 Years

159053.excerpt_en: This week, all 72 students at the lower secondary school have worked on staging the play «Peter Pan», which will be performed for Longyearbyen’s residents at the cultural centre tonight. “The students are very excited. Hopefully, it will be one of the highlights they remember from lower secondary school,” says project manager André Balterzen.
159053.subtitle_en: The lower secondary school students will perform «Peter Pan» at the cultural centre on Friday.

159072.excerpt_en: The audience responded with a standing ovation after Store Norske Mandskor performed 17 songs, led by conductor Jovna Zacharias Dunfjell, during a two-hour concert at the Cableway Central on Saturday evening.
159072.subtitle_en: Store Norske Mandskor’s annual concert offered both humour and serious pieces in a packed Cableway Central on Saturday evening.
159072.title_en: Great Success for Store Norske Mandskor

159077.excerpt_en: “We are waiting for the final decision on the revised national budget, and then we will follow up the matter with Health Minister Bent Høie. At least, we are optimistic.”
159077.subtitle_en: Kjetil Figenschou and Merete Nordheim of Svalbard Høyre believe Longyearbyen will get a permanent psychology service.

159089.excerpt_en: In the summer of 2015, I took part in archaeological excavations at Nordhamna on Bear Island. The excavations were carried out under the auspices of the Governor of Svalbard, and the assignment was to conduct an emergency excavation of a Russian trapper’s grave that was about to collapse into the sea because of erosion.
159089.subtitle_en: The icon turns out to have been cast in copper and was probably produced in Russia, perhaps at a Russian Orthodox monastery by the White Sea, in the 1700s or 1800s.
159089.title_en: The Russian Icon from Bear Island

159109.excerpt_en: There was an introduction to the Longyearbyen Dog Club, and Mali Strømsvåg held an obedience course at the town dog yard. Visitors also had the opportunity to greet the dogs and go dog sledding. “It was great fun, because the weather is so lovely.”
159109.subtitle_en: An open day was held at the dog yard on Sunday as part of the programme celebrating the tenth anniversary of Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund.
159109.title_en: Open Day at the Dog Yard

159153.excerpt_en: Local bird enthusiast and amateur photographer Bjørn Frantzen (pictured) is sharing some of his photographs with Svalbardposten’s readers. In the largest image, Frantzen has captured three of the world’s four eider species.
159153.subtitle_en: Local birdwatchers believe Steller’s eiders are nesting near Longyearbyen. If nesting is confirmed, it would be the first time in Europe.
159153.tags_en: eider, walrus, Arctic fox, news, loff, Svalbard reindeer, rock ptarmigan
159153.title_en: Waiting for a Possible Wildlife Sensation Nearby

159157.excerpt_en: It has been almost five months since the man from Nesodden took on his latest new challenges at work. Bjørn Torjus is the events coordinator at Visit Svalbard.
159157.subtitle_en: Smak Svalbard is the newcomer, and Bjørn Torjus Hanssen (42) will coordinate it.

159182.excerpt_en: At 2:50 a.m. on Saturday, the fire service and police had to respond to a cooking incident in Road 232. “It was a drunk man who decided it would be a good idea to make himself some food, but then he fell asleep on the floor.”
159182.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard and the other emergency services in Longyearbyen had plenty to do during the night before Saturday.
159182.title_en: A hectic night for the police

159186.excerpt_en: Here you can view a picture gallery from Peter Pan. Read more about the performance in the next issue of Svalbardposten.
159186.subtitle_en: The lower secondary students performed Peter Pan at the cultural centre on Friday.

159208.excerpt_en: An enthusiastic tourism manager is there to welcome visitors in Barentsburg.
159208.subtitle_en: The number of tourists travelling to Barentsburg is increasing. Tourism manager Timofey Rogozhin has many plans.

159229.excerpt_en: Naturally, he finds it interesting and important that John Kerry, Ban Ki-moon, and a number of Norwegian and foreign politicians and bureaucrats have dropped by over the years. This is because climate issues make the greatest impact when people see them for themselves and experience some of the researchers’ work.
159229.subtitle_en: When Ole Øiseth leaves Ny-Ålesund in July, it is his colleagues he will miss the most.

159234.excerpt_en: This was the third time the scout group had taken part in this camp. This year, we brought 16 excited scouts who had never been to a scout camp before.
159234.subtitle_en: Over the weekend of 9–11 June, the pathfinders—fourth-grade scouts—from Svalbard Church’s scout group took part in a cub scout camp at Hamnvåg in Malangen, 1.5 hours south of Tromsø.

159246.excerpt_en: Apartments 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 at the top of Road 228 were first when demolition work began last Friday. An application was initially submitted for demolition of the first three apartments, followed by the last three.
159246.subtitle_en: Demolition work began on Friday on the houses hit by the avalanche in Road 228. More houses will eventually be demolished.

159276.excerpt_en: Statsbygg has now begun improvements to the Svalbard Global Seed Vault. Drainage ditches in the mountainside will carry away meltwater and any rainwater, while a watertight wall is being installed inside the tunnel.
159276.subtitle_en: “We have had people there to stop tourists from entering the construction site, but they have simply been ignored,” says Statsbygg communications director Hege Njaa Aschim.

159319.excerpt_en: They are divided into teams of two and will be based in Isfjorden, Kongsfjorden near Ny-Ålesund, and Magdalenefjorden. Each team consists of one person with a natural-sciences background and one police officer.
159319.subtitle_en: Today, six field inspectors are heading out to serve as the Governor of Svalbard’s extended arm in the field until 18 August.

159324.excerpt_en: “I had to shed a little tear at the end,” director Gerd Brox said when the performance was over. She had spent the entire previous week with the lower secondary students rehearsing for the premiere.
159324.subtitle_en: “Peter Pan” was warmly received by a full house at the cultural centre when the lower secondary students performed the play last Friday.

159333.excerpt_en: Ole Petter Løbben of Arba Follum proposed replacing coal with biochar and creating a CO2-neutral energy solution. The slogan was borrowed from Donald Trump: “Make Longyearbyen green again!” The proposal to replace Svalbard coal with biochar is appealing, not least because it is based on using the existing power plant.
159333.subtitle_en: An opinion piece about future energy solutions.
159333.title_en: A green energy solution for Longyearbyen?

159346.excerpt_en: The Norwegian authorities want to increase tourism investment in Svalbard. They have also stated that this should not result in increased motor traffic, and that tourism services should therefore be strengthened in and around the settlements.
159346.subtitle_en: The Norwegian authorities want to increase tourism investment in Svalbard. However, Svalbard’s strict environmental regulations place major restrictions on both the harvesting and marketing of local produce such as game and fish in the archipelago.
159346.title_en: Svalbard’s environmental regulations are blocking the desired tourism development

159360.excerpt_en: Ole Humlum’s response in SP on 16 June 2017 confirms agreement that the interactions that “control” the climate are extremely complex, are not fully understood, and that it is simply impossible to observe the relevant conditions adequately in time and space.

159389.excerpt_en: July is just around the corner, and it is once again time to invite readers to the summer’s big competition. For those unfamiliar with the phenomenon, Stetten is a snow formation that appears on Operafjellet every year.
159389.subtitle_en: It took a long time for the champagne glass on Operafjellet to appear this year. Will this affect the result of this year’s competition?

159426.excerpt_en: In the previous issue of Svalbardposten, Trude Borch of Akvaplan-niva wrote an opinion piece titled “Svalbard’s environmental regulations are blocking the desired tourism development.” Discussions about local food and tourism development must be based on facts; above all, it is important to make clear who is responsible for what.

159436.excerpt_en: When my parents realized, in the winter of 1954–55, that I intended to go to sea, despite ignoring their warnings, my father did his best to prepare me for a life abroad. For instance, he told me that there was a police force operating across national borders—long before the EU.
159436.subtitle_en: Freia on the tagging of listed buildings in L0ongyearbyen

159442.excerpt_en: On Monday, a unanimous local council voted to purchase 20 new three-room apartments from Statsbygg, which is leading the development project in Gruvedalen. The price tag is up to NOK 55 million.
159442.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen Community Council is buying 20 apartments to replace homes in Lia and offer employees something larger than bedsits in Blåmyra.

159469.excerpt_en: “But then we’ll have to move fast. It’s a combination of work and formalities that needs to be put in place,” says Hege Njaa Aschim, communications director at Statsbygg.
159469.subtitle_en: Statsbygg hopes the new homes can be completed during the course of next year.

159475.excerpt_en: On Monday, the Governor of Svalbard announced that a new land-use plan for Svea had been adopted.
159475.subtitle_en: Store Norske accepts the Governor of Svalbard’s requirements for time and numerical limits on tourist and research activities in Svea.

159504.excerpt_en: Researchers from many countries are constantly carrying out a range of projects in Greenland. Much of the focus is on the Greenland ice sheet: how much it is melting, and what this means for sea levels and marine life.
159504.subtitle_en: Greenland has little overview of who is researching what on the enormous island. Now it would like to learn how Svalbard has gained an overview and established control.
159504.title_en: Greenland wants to learn from Svalbard

159514.excerpt_en: A total of 30 children took part. They enjoyed a range of activities designed to give them positive experiences in nature and help them get to know their local surroundings.
159514.subtitle_en: This week, Svalbard Turn, through Aktiv i Friluft, has organized Activity Week for children aged 10 to 13.
159514.title_en: A great start to the summer holidays

159538.excerpt_en: She had heard everyone talking about how wonderful Svalbard was, but when Martine moved here in the summer two years ago, it was a difficult start to life. “Everything was just grey, overcast and sad. There was no midnight sun.”
159538.subtitle_en: “When I first came to Svalbard, I cried for a whole week,” says Martine Eidem (27) from Ulsteinvik.

159563.excerpt_en: Roofing work has recently been underway on some of Longyearbyen Boligeiendom’s apartment blocks at Vei 232. Several people have reacted to the way the scaffolding was built.
159563.subtitle_en: The company roofing Longyearbyen Boligeiendom AS’s buildings at Vei 232 must stop work until safety has been improved.
159563.tags_en: scaffolding, Longyearbyen Boligeiendom, WEM AS, news

159587.excerpt_en: There was a touch of drama at the coal quay on Saturday when this nest was discovered in the stacker, by the feeder at the loading facility, just before the ship “Zapolyaye” was loaded to transport the coal onwards to Rotterdam. “It quickly became clear that we had to move the nest.”
159587.subtitle_en: They saved a nest of snow bunting chicks.
159587.tags_en: news, snow bunting, coal quay, LNS Spitsbergen

159597.excerpt_en: Another wonderful historic photograph from Thorvald Ianssen’s collection, from the time Norsk Polarnavigasjon conducted oil exploration in Grønfjorden. The year is 1967, and workers are pulling up drill pipes.
159597.subtitle_en: Oil exploration with pipes to lift.

159610.excerpt_en: “I would have liked to see us build more road. And we’ll try again over the summer to see what we can achieve,” says Tommy Anderssen, one of the initiators of the volunteer project.
159610.subtitle_en: Bjørndalsveien has now been improved as far as the barbecue area. But the campaign group hopes to lay gravel much farther.

159614.excerpt_en: The debate over the division of roles in Longyearbyen has been heated in recent months, culminating recently in local council politicians’ input to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries on what Store Norske’s role in Svalbard and Longyearbyen should be, in their view. I am pleased that at the local council meeting on 23…
159614.subtitle_en: “Store Norske is at a crossroads, with the company’s continued mining operations entering a decisive period.”

159634.excerpt_en: Ole Humlum responds to Svalbardposten’s readers (SP 30 June 2017), as previously mentioned by me: The climate is the result of fluctuating systems linked together. The absorption of terrestrial radiation by “greenhouse gases” is not the only process governing the flow of energy through Earth’s systems.
159634.subtitle_en: A new response to Ole Humlum.
159634.tags_en: Ole Humlum, opinion, letters to the editor, Reinard Mook
159634.title_en: The Climate, the “Greenhouse” and Ole Humlum

159650.excerpt_en: The Longyearbyen Community Council plans to begin work on avalanche protection for the pointed-roof houses as early as November and December. This emerged when the “overall plan for avalanche protection in Longyearbyen 2018–2020” was presented by the Longyearbyen Community Council on the 30th.
159650.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen Community Council aims to have avalanche protection in place before the end of the year.

159662.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Polar Institute has been conducting reindeer counts in Bjørndalen, Adventdalen and the side valleys of these areas since 1979.
159662.subtitle_en: Many calves and few carcasses indicate that the reindeer have had a good year.

159688.excerpt_en: Floating cities dock with enough shelter for thousands of temporary residents. Earlier this week, “Aida Luna” was at the quay with beds for 2,100 passengers.
159688.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen is overflowing with plans and plans for plans.

159691.excerpt_en: Duurrrrrrrrrrr, tsch, tsch, duurrrrrr. Can after can moves along the conveyor belt and is filled with beer this Friday.
159691.subtitle_en: Pilsner, weissbier and ale are flying out of Svalbard Brewery’s production facilities. This week, they ordered two new large tanks to double production.

159695.excerpt_en: On 21 June, the Storting adopted a revised national budget stating that UNN can apply for a grant for a psychologist in Longyearbyen.
159695.subtitle_en: It is now possible to apply for funding for a psychologist position in Longyearbyen. But what such a psychologist can do is not entirely clear.

159719.excerpt_en: Metallic jewelry jingles against the African dress she is wearing in honor of the photographer. Jet-black hair threaded with red is pulled tightly over Agnes Nankoyian Kiilena’s head.
159719.subtitle_en: Her mother left Agnes Nankoyian Kiilena’s father so that she could go to school.

159732.excerpt_en: At 8 p.m. on Monday, the Governor’s Office was notified about a privately owned sled dog that had run away in Adventdalen. According to senior police officer Anders Haugerud, it had escaped through a hole in a fence at a kennel where it was staying at “summer camp” while its owner was on holiday.

159755.excerpt_en: Construction machinery from LNS Spitsbergen is now excavating pipes in Hilmar Rekstens Vei. “There are a number of pipe crossings there with settlement damage that creates bumps. We have now designed a more technical solution with geotextile, better fill material and insulation beneath the pipes.”
159755.subtitle_en: The bumps on Hilmar Rekstens Vei will be removed, and the road will get entirely new asphalt. Several other roads will also become less bumpy.

159760.excerpt_en: “One person sustained minor injuries and has gone off the road while coming down from Mine 7,” says senior police officer Espen Olsen at the Governor’s Office. The person was part of a guided tour group and was riding a quad bike, also known as an ATV.
159760.subtitle_en: A foreign national has been taken to Longyearbyen Hospital after leaving the road.

159765.excerpt_en: The reason the bridge over Melkeveien is being closed is that the culvert’s structural safety is inadequate. “It’s old, and if a hole develops in the pipe, the water could carry away material outside it,” says Marius Larsen, technical director of the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL).

159791.excerpt_en: In summer, Svalbard is visited by large cruise ships carrying far more passengers than the archipelago has residents. Sick passengers are transported to Longyearbyen Hospital. “This has become a very significant burden on local healthcare and emergency preparedness.”
159791.subtitle_en: Sick cruise tourists have become a major burden for Longyearbyen Hospital.

159794.excerpt_en: Jonathan Pedneault comes from Longueuil, just south of Montreal. But over the past ten years, he has travelled to most of the world’s conflict zones.
159794.subtitle_en: Canadian Jonathan Pedneault (27) works documenting war and misery. On Svalbard, he finds peace.

159801.excerpt_en: In a letter to Helse Nord, the University Hospital of North Norway writes that one measure that should be taken to strengthen local health preparedness on Svalbard is to staff the rescue helicopters with an anaesthetist.
159801.subtitle_en: University Hospital of North Norway wants anaesthetist coverage in Longyearbyen. A doctor could be in place by autumn.

159828.excerpt_en: On 1 June 2015, the state took over the landholding in Longyearbyen from Store Norske.
159828.subtitle_en: SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge has reached an agreement with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries and will now offer construction loans as usual.

159848.excerpt_en: This is the second consecutive year the expedition has been held, and this year’s focus was on the beaches between Vinodden and Fredheim. Last year, the beaches between Fredheim and Von Postbreen were cleaned.
159848.subtitle_en: Last weekend, 17 people from Longyearbyen took part in a rubbish-collecting expedition organised by Anders Magne Lindseth and the Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association.
159848.title_en: Set Out on a Rubbish-Collecting Expedition

159850.excerpt_en: “The administration building is becoming so poor that, in the near future, we will be in the same situation as with the Old Hospital. Serious subsidence damage means we must get started quickly,” says Guttorm Albrigt Hansen, director of Telenor Svalbard.
159850.subtitle_en: Subsidence damage means Telenor wants a new administration building to safeguard communications. The Directorate for Cultural Heritage demands better adaptation.

159865.excerpt_en: While the winter months are used to study the results and write publications, the short summer is used to collect data. With practised movements, Sveinn Are Hanssen swings the loop and catches the eider.
159865.subtitle_en: It is peak season for the researchers’ fieldwork. All across Svalbard, activity is in full swing as they collect new knowledge.

159891.excerpt_en: “It has been a long time since we carried out such an inspection at Longyearbyen Community Council. It is a key actor on Svalbard, and we want to examine how it looks after its employees,” says senior adviser Jon Helge Vaeng of the Labour Inspection Authority.
159891.subtitle_en: This autumn, the Labour Inspection Authority will examine the working environment of Longyearbyen Community Council.

159894.excerpt_en: “Svalbard is very interesting to us. It is interesting both politically and socially.”
159894.subtitle_en: The YMCA-YWCA owns the country’s largest folk high school. Now it wants to become the majority owner of Svalbard Folk High School AS.
159894.title_en: Folk High School Owner Wants Svalbard

159899.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Community Council is considering moving the climbing tower from the now-closed Longyearbyen kindergarten to Polarflokken. It has now received approval for the move from the Ministry of Culture, which provided NOK 300,000 for the tower.
159899.subtitle_en: The climbing tower could end up at Polarflokken.

159913.excerpt_en: “The dark polar night has descended over Svalbard and the north coast of Bellsund. The only sound is the wind whistling.”
159913.subtitle_en: The Svalbard Museum’s object of the month is traditional Russian footwear.

159927.excerpt_en: Svalbard’s residents are to choose a new energy supply. Advocates of renewable energy in the Arctic can point to Princess Elisabeth in Antarctica or Colville Lake in Canada as examples of wind and solar power.
159927.subtitle_en: Thorium should be included in the assessment of a new energy source for Svalbard.

159988.excerpt_en: A number of onlookers had come to see Norwegian land at Svalbard Airport with a Dreamliner on Monday evening. It was a 787-9, the larger of the two Dreamliner models in Norwegian’s fleet.
159988.subtitle_en: Five-day-old aircraft makes trip to Longyearbyen.

160000.subtitle_en: This summer, two 400-year-old whalers’ graves at Smeerenburg will be brought to the Svalbard Museum.
160000.title_en: Excavated Before the Sea Takes Them

160012.excerpt_en: Since 2008, the number of guest nights in Longyearbyen has risen from 92,000 to 142,300, according to Visit Svalbard. The hotel projects now being planned and built (see fact box) will increase the number of hotel rooms from 405 to 790.
160012.subtitle_en: New hotel projects will almost double room capacity, while cruise traffic is increasing. The tourism director wants a debate on how many tourists Longyearbyen should receive.

160054.excerpt_en: More and more ships are visiting Longyearbyen port. The large ocean-going cruise ships have continued to arrive, even though the heavy-fuel-oil ban now only allows them to sail in Isfjorden.
160054.subtitle_en: More and larger ships are arriving in Longyearbyen. Next year, the “big sister” of “Preziosa” is due to arrive, and several more ships will come as early as March.
160054.tags_en: ships, cruise, port, Longyearbyen port, news, boats
160054.title_en: Heading for a New Cruise Record

160060.excerpt_en: Håkon Sandvik is Svalbardposten’s cartoonist. Every week, he draws Polar Bears into the news.

160065.excerpt_en: “We have had positive meetings with Longyearbyen Community Council and Store Norske. We intend to phase out the housing in Nybyen and build new homes because we want to offer safe, good-quality accommodation,” says Hans Petter Kvaal, managing director of the student welfare organisation in Tromsø.
160065.subtitle_en: Po Lin Lee cannot build a hotel at Elvesletta. Now the student welfare organisation wants to move students there.
160065.tags_en: student welfare organisation, news, hotel, plots, Elvesletta, student housing

160083.excerpt_en: This week, the company received permission from Longyearbyen Community Council to build two blocks containing a total of 30 apartments. “We are pleased about that. We can now start designing and preparing sales and construction.”
160083.subtitle_en: Svalpro can put up two four-storey apartment blocks at Elvesletta.

160101.excerpt_en: At 10:30 a.m. on Sunday, the Governor received a report from someone who had observed a sled dog chasing a reindeer between Larsbreen and Longyearbreen above Nybyen. “We responded and arrived ten minutes later. By then, one of the town’s residents had already put the reindeer down.”
160101.subtitle_en: A reindeer had to be put down after being attacked by a sled dog.

160112.excerpt_en: The Governor has completed this year’s beach-cleaning expedition. The result was approximately 60 cubic metres of rubbish removed from the beaches. “That is slightly less than last year, when we collected 93 cubic metres, but ice and weather conditions meant we were unable to make full use of all the days,” says Knut Fossum, environmental protection officer with the Governor of Svalbard.
160112.subtitle_en: The Governor’s annual beach-cleaning expedition has now ended.

160132.excerpt_en: Suspicious traces have been observed in the area in front of Nordenskiöldbreen on Svalbard. Can glacier detective Lis Allaart solve the mystery?
160132.subtitle_en: Former UNIS student Lis Allaart investigated the retreat of Nordenskiöldbreen and won a science communication competition.

160145.excerpt_en: The sequence of events: In 2013, I found an old map of Nordenskiöldbreen (Adolfbukta, Billefjorden, Svalbard) in a book from 1910, showing two different glacier-front positions—1896 and 1910.
160145.subtitle_en: Suspicious traces have been observed in the area in front of Nordenskioldbreen on Svalbard. Can glacier detective Lis Allaart solve the mystery?

160156.excerpt_en: Longyearelva will be protected from Sjøområdet to Nybyen. Altogether, the project covers approximately 2,000 metres of riverbed.
160156.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council and the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate will begin work on permanent flood protection along Longyearelva this autumn.

160165.excerpt_en: Fifty-one windows have faithfully served through wind and weather along the façade of Longyearbyen School toward the ski slope since the 1970s, but now they are being replaced. “It is routine maintenance, as the windows have begun to age and have suffered some rot damage.”
160165.subtitle_en: Some offices and the library section at Longyearbyen School will receive new windows.

160178.excerpt_en: “This is like a photo album. We are trying to show what exists underwater right next to Longyearbyen,” says Piotr Balazy.
160178.subtitle_en: Two Polish marine biologists showcase the teeming life in Isfjorden.

160193.excerpt_en: “We have four people from the Governor’s Office who are now completing the investigation. The fire was larger than initially believed.”
160193.subtitle_en: The day-trip boat “Langøysund” was heading for Pyramiden when a fire broke out by the barbecue. “It felt dramatic when it was happening and people were frightened,” says one of the guests.

160217.excerpt_en: Yesterday, Svalbardposten reported that the fire aboard the day-trip boat started in connection with grilling on deck. “We will not confirm anything at all. We can only say that the investigation is ongoing.”
160217.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office is continuing interviews and investigations following the fire aboard “Langøysund”.

160241.excerpt_en: Police responded at 11:35 p.m. after receiving a report that two people in their 20s had been involved in an altercation outside the Svalbar pub late Friday night. “A man in his 20s punched another man in his 20s in the face twice without provocation.”
160241.subtitle_en: “This is something we take seriously,” says Governor’s Office officer Bjørn Gunnar Pedersen.

160243.excerpt_en: The Polar Row expedition, led by Icelandic sailor Fiann Paul, with Norwegian Tor Wigum, Welshman Jeff Willis, American Carlo Facchino and Indian Roy Tathagata as crew, arrived in Longyearbyen in the early hours of Sunday. They began rowing from Tromsø on the morning of Thursday the 21st.
160243.subtitle_en: Rowed from Tromsø to Svalbard in seven days.

160245.excerpt_en: At 3 a.m. on Sunday, the Governor’s Office received a report from staff at the Huset nightclub that they needed help removing a man who refused to leave. “He had been thrown out of Huset, but remained outside and allegedly refused to leave the area…”
160245.subtitle_en: The Governor’s Office had to respond.

160261.excerpt_en: “There was a break-in at Longyearbyen Kindergarten sometime between Friday evening and Monday morning. They broke in and stole computer equipment,” says senior police officer Marit Ellingsen of the Governor’s Office.

160266.excerpt_en: At 1 a.m. on Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard received a report that a very drunk man was attempting to take a car in the town centre. The man is a foreign tourist in his 50s.
160266.subtitle_en: A drunk foreign tourist attempted to drive a car from the town centre.

160279.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified at 11:37 p.m. that an emergency locator transmitter had been activated. Once they obtained a more precise position, it turned out that the distress signals were coming from Bjørndalen.
160279.subtitle_en: Two hikers activated an emergency locator transmitter.

160284.excerpt_en: While debate rages on the mainland over introducing a separate tourist tax for heavily burdened small municipalities receiving large numbers of tourists, the streets of Longyearbyen are filling with cruise passengers. Svalbard introduced its own visitor fee ten years ago to help safeguard the environment.
160284.subtitle_en: The environmental fee introduced ten years ago provides a unique opportunity to invest in various projects and environmental measures.
160284.tags_en: Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund, opinions, editorial, tourist tax
160284.title_en: Tourist Tax, Nature and the Environment

160287.excerpt_en: What was supposed to be a pleasant trip to Pyramiden became a minor nightmare for the group of friends vacationing on Svalbard.
160287.subtitle_en: “I said, ‘Now we’re going to die,’” says Benn Eidissen, who was among those who ended up in the bow of the “Langøysund” when the deck caught fire.
160287.title_en: Caught in a Sea of Flames

160303.excerpt_en: Earlier this summer, Svalbardposten reported that tourism chief Ronny Brunvoll wants a broad discussion about how much the tourism industry can grow and how large the cruise ships visiting Longyearbyen should be allowed to be. He believes this is something local politicians must decide.
160303.subtitle_en: More and more cruise tourists are visiting Longyearbyen. Since last year, traffic to the port has increased by 20 percent.
160303.title_en: Strong Growth Requires Good Logistics and Longer Berthing Times

160310.excerpt_en: Standing in the windswept landscape around Smeerenburg, in the far northwest of Spitsbergen, it is difficult to imagine what life must have been like for the Dutch people who travelled there in the 17th century.
160310.subtitle_en: The person in the coffin was buried approximately 400 years ago in Smeerenburg. Now the remains are on their way to the Svalbard Museum.

160314.excerpt_en: “It’s wonderful to arrive. Now I’m going to have a beer,” Tor Wigum said with a laugh as he stepped ashore in Longyearbyen on Sunday morning.
160314.subtitle_en: The “Polar Row” expedition spent seven days rowing from Tromsø to Svalbard.

160331.excerpt_en: Emma Hoette is wearing a white knitted collar. She ties off the end of the thread and walks round and round between two beams.

160372.excerpt_en: On Thursday morning last week, a fire broke out on the deck of the day-trip boat “Langøysund”, owned by Henningsen Transport & Guiding. Witnesses told Svalbardposten that the fire started in connection with the barbecue on deck.
160372.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard will not conclude what caused the fire until the investigation is complete.

160380.excerpt_en: For several years, parents and others have called for a walkway between Museumsveien and Polarflokken Kindergarten. In 2013, a pedestrian path was built from Melkeveien to Museumsveien, but it stops abruptly there.
160380.subtitle_en: It will finally become safe to walk and cycle from Museumsveien to Polarflokken Kindergarten and the school.

160427.excerpt_en: If stone steps are to be built, stone slabs require a stable foundation, and that is hard to find in the area around Longyearbyen. As permafrost melts and freezes, it causes most things to shift over time, as seen at the Old Hospital and Telenor’s administrative building.
160427.subtitle_en: It is difficult to understand how a Sherpa trail could be practical.
160427.title_en: Is a Sherpa Trail to Varden Feasible?

161331.excerpt_en: Knut Aune Hoseth, regional director for NVE’s Northern Region (the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate), confirms that they have faced greater challenges than expected. “Our work has been delayed because we have encountered greater challenges with permafrost and foundations than we initially anticipated.”
161331.subtitle_en: The detailed design for securing Lia, which was due to be completed in July and put out to tender, is still not finished.

161344.excerpt_en: Sushi Kita general manager Asuza Obo was unaware that the restaurant had to apply for an extension of its contract with Lompensenteret.
