She learned this—and that the centre would not renew their contract—in an email she received two weeks ago on Friday. “Right now, we are shocked by how things have unfolded.”
161344.subtitle_en: Sushi Kita has until the end of October to move out of Lompensenteret.
161344.tags_en: sushi kita, lompensenteret, classic pizza, taste of thai, news
161344.title_en: Sushi Kita shocked by eviction order

161352.excerpt_en: The paving work in Longyearbyen is over for now. During a few hectic days, the Finnish-owned company Lemminkäinen milled and laid new surfacing on most of Road 500, Hilmar Rekstens Vei and here and there at other locations where settlement damage had occurred.
161352.subtitle_en: Three hundred tonnes of asphalt turned out to be unusable when it arrived in Longyearbyen.

161359.excerpt_en: The term “exotic” can mean many things. On Svalbard, it is often used to describe the distinctive society at 78 degrees north.
161359.subtitle_en: Around 20 people got some exercise by dancing in the Sjøområdet district.

161387.excerpt_en: After nine years of data collection, the results are clear. Walruses are not disturbed by tourist visits.
161387.subtitle_en: After nine years of data collection, the results are clear. Walruses are not disturbed by tourist visits.
161387.title_en: Tourists don’t disturb walruses. Polar bears, on the other hand…

161410.excerpt_en: This is the story of Truls Teist, a small fledgling I came across the other day on my way from Svalbardhallen. This is the time of year when young black guillemots leave their sheltered nests somewhere high on the mountain slopes leading up towards Platået.
161410.subtitle_en: One of the wonderful things about living in Longyearbyen is being close to nature, even when you are out doing ordinary errands in town.
161410.title_en: “Truls Teist”: The Story of a Little Miracle

161439.excerpt_en: Jørn Dybdahl has to travel to Oslo for cancer treatment and had a ticket for today’s flight, which was cancelled yesterday. “There are no other ways for us to get away. No bus, no ferry, and Norwegian’s flights are full for several days ahead.”
161439.subtitle_en: SAS is prioritising flights from Longyearbyen to Oslo, among other things to bring cancer patient Jørn Dybdahl south.

161442.excerpt_en: The housing shortage is a consequence of the two avalanches in December 2015 and February 2017. Several homes were reduced to splinters, and a large number of housing units in Lia cannot be inhabited during the winter season until permanent protection is installed.
161442.subtitle_en: While local authorities talk about a housing crisis and struggle to find homes for newcomers, the number of Airbnb rental properties has increased.

161459.excerpt_en: Last week, the apartments comprising house numbers 15, 17, 19 and 21 on Vei 228 were demolished by LNS Spitsbergen on behalf of Statsbygg, which owned the properties. These homes had stood empty since the 2015 avalanche.
161459.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) and Longyearbyen Local Council reject claims that the houses would have served as avalanche protection.

161472.excerpt_en: “We have pursued policies that work, and I really believe in it. The atmosphere here is fantastic.”
161472.subtitle_en: The atmosphere was tense around the long table just before the first projection came at nine o’clock on Monday evening.
161472.title_en: Great Atmosphere at the Election Night Watch Party at Kroa

161492.excerpt_en: The road from the old museum to Huset will be closed when heavy rain is expected, because rain increases the likelihood of landslides.
161492.subtitle_en: The road from the old museum to Huset will be closed when heavy rain is expected, because rain increases the likelihood of landslides.
161492.title_en: Why There Is a Risk of Landslides

161503.excerpt_en: The fire service has noted an increase in the number of callouts to Airbnb properties over the past year and a half. “We in fire and rescue are deeply concerned about this development.”
161503.subtitle_en: Tourists can pick and choose between apartments, “polar bear dens” and cosy “fox dens” when visiting Svalbard. The fire chief is concerned about safety.

article_keywords_en: senior police officer at the Governor’s Office
161509.excerpt_en: The accident happened when the helicopter was transporting diesel to Avinor’s generator-powered base station at Torfjellet. A strap broke, and the diesel ended up in the river channel west of Pyramiden.
161509.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s helicopter lost around 1,600 litres of diesel just outside Pyramiden last Friday.

161523.excerpt_en: “We want to focus this week on making Longyearbyen even safer for children and young people,” says Vivian Dyb, head of the Children and Youth Unit at LL.
161523.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) wants to put children and young people in the spotlight for an entire week.
161523.title_en: Ready for Children and Youth Week

161534.excerpt_en: Brenner thought it was a great experience to talk to internationally renowned author David Grossman, and appreciated that he took the time to come to Svalbard.
161534.subtitle_en: A week featuring well-known visiting authors and books on the timetable was a success.

161553.excerpt_en: Among other things, the young people will serve as youth representatives on the local council’s various committees. Malin Nilssen Alexandersen, at the front in the middle, continues as council leader and youth representative on the local council.
161553.subtitle_en: A new youth council was elected in Longyearbyen on Tuesday.

161558.excerpt_en: The artists taking part are Pekka Kainulainen, Liina Kuittinen, Kurt Johannessen and Sophie Dupont. They are among the leading Nordic performance artists. “We give the artists the opportunity to create unique new works that can help preserve the powerful landscape they encounter,” says Stein Henningsen.
161558.subtitle_en: The Arctic Action performance festival opens this afternoon.

161561.excerpt_en: Henrik completed the final part of his bachelor’s degree in library and information science at Oslo and Akershus University College in Madrid. He interviewed for the job from Madrid and got his very first permanent position at Longyearbyen Public Library.
161561.subtitle_en: Henrik Holtvedt Andersen (25) came from his studies in Madrid to Longyearbyen a year ago. He has not regretted it.

161573.excerpt_en: At 5:30 p.m. on Thursday, the Governor received a report that a female polar bear with two cubs had been spotted close to Camp Barents in Adventdalen. “We had to use the helicopter again and moved the female and her cubs east of Innerhytta, towards Eskeerdalen,” says senior police officer Arnt Rennan. The operation ended at 9:20 p.m.
161573.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard had to respond to two separate incidents involving polar bear sightings on Thursday.
161573.title_en: Polar Bears Twice in One Day

161584.excerpt_en: Svenn Are Johansen and Emilie Våtvik set out for Kapp Laila in a 20-foot boat at 8:15 Friday morning to check on the cabin they use there, after being told that a polar bear had been in the area on Thursday evening. “We had planned to go out to the cabin…”
161584.subtitle_en: On Friday afternoon, a polar bear was sedated and flown by helicopter to Edgeøya after rampaging through several cabins at Kapp Laila.

161587.excerpt_en: At around 8 p.m. on Monday evening, a signal from a maritime emergency position-indicating beacon was picked up through the satellite systems at the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre of Northern Norway (HRS). The signal’s position was in Magdalenefjorden, northwest of Svalbard.
161587.subtitle_en: A major search operation was launched in Magdalenefjorden during the night before Tuesday.

161600.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, the Governor of Svalbard visited the station to provide assistance. “When we arrived, the polar bear jumped into the sea, and after that we saw nothing more of it.”
161600.subtitle_en: A polar bear has been causing problems for researchers in Hornsund for several weeks.

161615.excerpt_en: A long and tortuous bureaucratic process was crowned by final approval of the construction loan two weeks ago. Trond Håvelsrud, managing director of Svalbard Bygg, is pleased that they can finally begin work on their new commercial building in Sjøområdet. “It feels good to be under way.”
161615.subtitle_en: It took a year and a half from the first time Trond Håvelsrud was approved for a loan for a commercial building until the money reached his account.
161615.title_en: Finally, the Piles Are in the Ground

161629.excerpt_en: After wrecking several cabins at Kapp Laila last Friday, a male polar bear was sedated and transported to Nordaustlandet by the Governor of Svalbard. The bear comes from a family with many cabin break-ins on its conscience.
161629.subtitle_en: This is not the first time the male bear has been flown north by helicopter after breaking into cabins. The last time was in 2001.
161629.title_en: Second Helicopter Flight After Cabin Raid

161632.excerpt_en: The season for overseas cruise tourists is over. A total of 44,336 cruise passengers visited Longyearbyen during the period from 31.
161632.subtitle_en: Cruise passengers are very pleased with the hospitality in Longyearbyen. They believe the harbour area and access to the town could be improved.

161634.excerpt_en: A master’s thesis (pilot study) recently found antibiotic-resistant bacteria in faeces from Svalbard reindeer.
161634.subtitle_en: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria have been detected in Svalbard reindeer, but there is little reason for concern.
161634.title_en: No Cause for Concern over Resistance

161644.excerpt_en: Kings Bay Veterans’ Club chair Ellen Marie Ødegaard and the club’s board have been planning the trip since January this year. “I’m really looking forward to the trip amid Svalbard’s magnificent nature, beautiful Ny-Ålesund and MS ‘Nordstjernen,’ together with people who have strong memories and emotions—both good and bad—from…”
161644.subtitle_en: More than 100 people joined the Kings Bay Veterans’ Club aboard “Nordstjernen” to Ny-Ålesund this weekend.

161696.excerpt_en: They celebrated with birthday cake and balloons on Friday. Director Trine Berntsen has worked at the kindergarten since it opened.
161696.subtitle_en: Polarflokken Kindergarten celebrated its 10th anniversary this week.

161738.excerpt_en: It is Friday morning in Svea. Safety instructor Terje Blikfeldt has brought out blue visitor helmets for Bjørn Ivar Kruke, Abbas Barabadi and project manager Ann Christin Auestad from the Arctic Safety Centre at UNIS.
161738.subtitle_en: In 2019, UNIS may expand with a master’s degree programme in Arctic safety. The courses are now being developed.

161747.excerpt_en: Stein Henningsen (54) has set up a video camera and microphone beneath the Cableway Central. Below, a woman dressed in black stands while the town basks in golden autumn sunshine.
161747.subtitle_en: Stein Henningsen has carried crosses, dragged chains and bathed in red wine. In recent years, he has devoted himself to the Arctic and its changing climate.

161771.excerpt_en: Ptarmigan hunters are asked to submit one wing from each bird along with their hunting report. The wings indicate the proportion of chicks per adult bird in the population.
161771.subtitle_en: To understand the dynamics of Svalbard rock ptarmigan, we have counted ptarmigan in the hunting areas around Longyearbyen this autumn.
161771.title_en: Seeking the Link Between Ptarmigan Chicks and Wings

161803.excerpt_en: “It’s a real disadvantage running with the oxygen tank, but it looks tougher than the firefighters from Store Norske, who run around with their ‘schoolbags,’” says firefighter Thomas Nilsen, laughing after crossing the finish line in this year’s relay.
161803.subtitle_en: Saturday saw the start of this year’s TV campaign with a relay through Longyearbyen.

161812.excerpt_en: The Italian tourist who had become stranded on the mountain was brought down safely in the early hours of Sunday. “He was brought down between 5:00 and 5:30 a.m. He was fine, warm and comfortable, and did not complain of any pain.”
161812.subtitle_en: An Italian tourist had become stranded.

161842.excerpt_en: Ten-year-old Mats Lagergren is one of several enthusiastic young roller-skiers on Hilmar Rekstens Vei. The new asphalt is bringing entirely new users to the road.
161842.subtitle_en: “The new asphalt is great. Before, it was difficult both to roller-ski and ride a kick scooter.”

161861.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, Trym entered the classroom to cake, a trophy and cheers.
161861.subtitle_en: Trym Eide Aunevik (15) won six medals at the national swimming championships for people with intellectual disabilities. Now he is aiming higher.

161899.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Transport has decided to change Svalbard Airport’s status. Airport director Morten Ulsnes says work has been carried out at ministry level and that they contributed factual information to the process.
161899.subtitle_en: From Sunday 1 October, Svalbard Airport will change from an international to a domestic airport.

161913.excerpt_en: “The tour season is winding down, and there are many new people in town whom we want to get to know and show what we offer,” says Polar Puls coach Torill Brandal Berge.
161913.subtitle_en: On Saturday, Polar Puls held its kick-off for the autumn season.

161918.excerpt_en: “I visited both kindergartens, and a lot of good work is being done there. I was particularly impressed by the effective measures they have taken to promote inclusion and social skills,” says Lenning, who works full-time as the Anti-Bullying Ombud in Troms.
161918.subtitle_en: Anti-Bullying Ombud Jon-Halvdan Lenning met many children and young people during Childhood Week.

161943.excerpt_en: “It’s wonderful to see that the TV campaign has become part of people’s DNA and is passed on to newcomers arriving in Longyearbyen,” says Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik, head of the local TV campaign.
161943.subtitle_en: As tradition dictates, a relay was held in Longyearbyen on Saturday to raise money for this year’s TV campaign.

161960.excerpt_en: The attorney for Pia Sivertsen and Kim Rune Røkenes, who lost their two-year-old daughter Nikoline in the 2015 avalanche, has gained access to new information, interviews and documents. Based on this, he is once again submitting a claim to the Governor, through the Government Attorney, that liability for damages be acknowledged.
161960.subtitle_en: Attorney Christian Lundin has sent the Governor a new request to accept liability for damages following the avalanche in December 2015.

161964.excerpt_en: When the new land-use plan was approved, emphasis was placed, among other things, on transforming Sjøområdet. The politicians want industry and warehouse buildings there to be replaced by housing and light industry.
161964.subtitle_en: Before housing or light industry can be built here, all the plot leaseholders must agree on a detailed plan.

161978.excerpt_en: Many reindeer, for example, have been found dead with their antlers caught in the nets. To find out why these fishing nets end up on our shores and where they come from, Wouter Jan Strietman (Wageningen Economic Research) and Klaas-Jelle Koffeman (a former fisherman) conducted a study at the waste facility this summer.
161978.subtitle_en: Every year, fishing nets end up on Svalbard and pose a serious threat to wildlife.
161978.title_en: Why Fishing Nets End Up on Svalbard

161996.excerpt_en: The teenagers had set up camp at one of the cabin areas in Longyearbyen when they discovered shots being fired approximately 50 metres from where they were sitting at the bottom of a small hill.
161996.subtitle_en: The teenagers were frightened when they discovered shots being fired from a cabin near the tent camp. They are critical that the Governor did not come out to them.

164318.excerpt_en: Olsen tells High North News that it is highly reprehensible that the company first quoted a price for cleaning up mining operations in Svea, only to double it at the eleventh hour, just before the budget decision. “This has become a complete farce,” he says.
164318.subtitle_en: Local council leader Arild Olsen (Labour) says Store Norske’s management and board should resign. Managing Director Wenche Ravlo responds.

164356.excerpt_en: Turbine two at the Longyear power station has been temporarily taken out of service. During an inspection of the turbine, abnormal readings were recorded that may indicate incipient damage.
164356.subtitle_en: A diesel generator must replace one of the turbines.

164372.excerpt_en: Monday, 26 February, marks exactly ten years since the opening.
164372.subtitle_en: In February, it will be ten years since the Seed Vault opened. Representatives from gene banks around the world have been invited.

164384.excerpt_en: Store Norske CEO Wenche Ravlo is not surprised by the recommendation. “This was essentially as expected, given the debates in recent times. We stand by the profitable restart option we have presented, although there is of course some market risk.”
164384.subtitle_en: The Standing Committee on Business Affairs calls for mining at Svea and Lunckefjell to be wound up. Only the Centre Party opposes the proposal.

164395.excerpt_en: The two meteorologists Joanna Perchaluk (32) and Mateusz Mandat (27) first met at the Polish research station in Hornsund in 2015. This winter, they are overwintering there together as well.
164395.subtitle_en: This year’s very first Christmas trip was a little out of the ordinary.

164406.excerpt_en: On Monday, the book “Svalbard from the Air” was launched at Svalbard Museum. “We have worked hard to get the book ready before Christmas. This is this year’s Christmas gift for everyone who loves Svalbard,” says Yngve Melvær, head of the mapping section at the Norwegian Polar Institute.
164406.subtitle_en: Wondering how much Rosenthalbreen has shrunk, or how many thousand tonnes Austfonna weighs?

164423.excerpt_en: Marcela came from Chile to Svalbard at the age of 15. She started tenth grade there and then attended upper secondary school for two years.
164423.subtitle_en: Marcela Fuentes (23) is heading from the Christmas tree lighting to sunshine and summer in Chile.

164425.excerpt_en: The budget proposal adopted by politicians on the Administration Committee two weeks ago states that the costs of operating and maintaining the service residences exceed the revenue. Over the next four years, the service residences are budgeted to run at a deficit of around NOK 20 million.
164425.subtitle_en: Five years ago, rent for LL employees was increased to ensure that revenue would also cover necessary maintenance. The budgets are still running at a deficit.

164457.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, committee chair Kristin Furu Grøtting (V) welcomed everyone to this year’s “coziest meeting of the Committee for Education and Culture,” where the year’s NOK 2.9 million cork fund was to be distributed. Once questions of conflicts of interest had been settled, the politicians turned to the application list, which contained 51 applicants.
164457.subtitle_en: There was considerable debate when this year’s cork-fund money was to be allocated.
164457.title_en: Disagreement over the Use of Cork Money

164468.excerpt_en: Around 70 people lined up at the start across the three different course categories. “We had about the same number last year, which was double the number from before, so it was great that it happened again this year.”
164468.subtitle_en: The Christmas Mile was held on Saturday, organized by Svalbard Turn.
164468.title_en: A Run to Kick Off the Christmas Rush

164473.excerpt_en: After Svalbardposten published an article about a trip I made around Svalbard in 1967 (can it really be 50 years ago!), I have followed Svalbardposten regularly. Svalbard residents are naturally concerned that coal production appears to be coming to an end.
164473.subtitle_en: Svalbard residents are naturally concerned that coal production appears to be coming to an end.

164491.excerpt_en: I had a ticket for the night bus to Copenhagen, and I knew what time the bus would leave and from which platform. Now I was going to have something to eat.
164491.title_en: Going to the Toilet—Credit Card Only!

164537.excerpt_en: “Svalbard is following Troms and will also be switched off on 13 December,” says NRK distribution manager Bjarne André Myklebust.
164537.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, 13 December, the FM network will be switched off in Finnmark, Troms and Svalbard. This is the last region in the country to switch entirely to DAB broadcasts.

On the eastern side of Woodfjorden, in northern Spitsbergen, lies Mushamna, a trapping cabin now owned by the state that was previously leased by the Governor to trappers wishing to overwinter.

164580.excerpt_en: The children got ready early and sat excitedly waiting as their parents arrived to watch the Lucia procession and hear them sing the Lucia song “Santa Lucia” and the Christmas carol “A Child Is Born in Bethlehem.” “It was fun singing, and that so many people came to watch us,” says Marcus Roseth…
164580.subtitle_en: Wednesday saw Lucia Day celebrated at Kullungen kindergarten.

164605.excerpt_en: The Governor has decided to impose a total ban on staying in the following areas of Longyearbyen from Friday the 22nd onward.
164605.subtitle_en: The Governor is closing parts of Lia from Friday, 22 December.

164613.excerpt_en: Following a meeting with the Polar Department at the Ministry of Justice last week, the Community Council is proposing to raise electricity prices sharply for 2019 and 2020. The estimated annual electricity bill for a family in 2020 is NOK 20,000.
164613.subtitle_en: The Polar Department is asking the Community Council to budget for covering all costs of the power plant itself from 2019.

164634.excerpt_en: “We have reviewed the Christmas trips. The starting point for these trips to the trapping stations and remote outposts has been a Christmas service attended by the priest and the Governor,”
164634.subtitle_en: Private trappers will no longer have the priest, post, Governor and Christmas carols descending on them for the holidays.
164634.title_en: End of Christmas Trips to the Trapping Stations

164637.excerpt_en: Electricity, water, sewage and waste collection prices will rise sharply next year. This was decided on Monday, when the Community Council adopted the 2018 budget.
164637.subtitle_en: Municipal fees will rise, services will remain unchanged, and politicians will not receive iPads next year.

164649.excerpt_en: Last Thursday, Avinor Air Navigation Services marked the installation of new GPS-signal sensors on Svalbard, Bear Island and the mainland. The monitoring works by having aircraft transmit GPS data to ground-based sensors, which then send the position to Avinor’s systems.
164649.subtitle_en: Avinor Air Navigation Services has installed sensors for GPS signals that increase safety and make flight departures more efficient.

164663.excerpt_en: The second Sunday of Advent was marked with a Christmas concert at Svalbard Church. As tradition would have it—almost, at least—a packed church got to see the children of Polargospel sing their way down the aisle, Tundradundrene dust off last year’s Santa hats, and candles being lit.
164663.subtitle_en: Christmas was sung in at a packed Svalbard Church on Sunday, with performances by singers both young and old.
164663.title_en: Christmas concert for young and old

164667.excerpt_en: “I realized that I should start my own guiding business back home, focusing more deeply on local history. But I knew too little about tourism, so I decided to go to Svalbard to learn,” says Erlend.
164667.subtitle_en: Erlend Jensen Sandvoll (29) went to Svalbard to learn about tourism. Instead, he found a new calling.

164685.excerpt_en: A review of figures for the development of full-time equivalent jobs indicates that the local community has managed to adapt to the restructuring, with a sharp decline in the number of jobs in coal mining. This is shown by the 2017 analysis of social and business development, carried out by the Institute for Urban and Regional Research (NIBR) at Oslo and Akershus University College.
164685.subtitle_en: * Stable population * Stable employment * Decline in coal mining * Tourism expands

164704.excerpt_en: In its previous issue (8 December), Svalbardposten (SP) wrote about Longyearbyen Community Council’s (LL) terms for renting housing to its employees. The apparent message was that LL uses public funds to provide benefits for its own employees.
164704.subtitle_en: Espen Klungseth Rotevatn believes Svalbardposten should have written about the entire housing market in Longyearbyen, not just the housing scheme for Longyearbyen Community Council employees.
164704.title_en: A complete miss on housing costs

164738.excerpt_en: In late summer, two roads were closed. Melkeveien was closed because the Longyearelva River had eroded the foundations around the culvert.
164738.subtitle_en: Road 300, between Museumsveien and Huset, will not be reopened. This has little to do with avalanche danger.

164746.excerpt_en: The office, which has four employees, has already been operating for several weeks. Consumer Director Randi Flesland travelled north on Wednesday to lend some weight to the official opening. “The office in Longyearbyen will work on dispute resolution between sellers and buyers.”
164746.subtitle_en: The Consumer Council’s office in Longyearbyen will mediate between sellers and buyers throughout the country. The office was formally opened on Wednesday.

164754.excerpt_en: I am not entirely sure what is meant by “commercial festivals/events,” as mentioned in the article in the latest issue of Svalbardposten. In my mind, everything involving “commercial” activity is associated with goods or services for sale, which in turn should generate a contribution margin to cover fixed…
164754.subtitle_en: A letter to the editor about the cork-money distribution.

164794.excerpt_en: How many snow crab fishing licences in the Barents Sea has the EU decided to award in 2018? As the snow crab swarms towards Svalbard, it has become something of a sore point in cooperation between Norway and the EU.

164798.excerpt_en: At around 11 p.m. on Friday evening, the Governor was notified of a disturbance at Karlsberger Pub. Seven or eight people aged between 30 and 50 are said to have been involved, with a good mix of locals and visitors. “Two of them were more active than the others.”
164798.subtitle_en: A man was hit in the face with a glass.

164828.subtitle_en: The Governor has called a meeting of the emergency preparedness council after the Norwegian Meteorological Institute’s Northern Norway forecasting service issued an alert for Nordenskiöld Land on Monday afternoon.

164842.excerpt_en: On Monday afternoon, the Governor decided to evacuate homes and impose a travel ban in Lia and above the road in Nybyen (see map). The evacuation and travel ban apply from 10 p.m. Monday evening until further notice.
164842.subtitle_en: The Governor is imposing a travel ban across most of Lia and parts of Nybyen. NVE’s Markus Landrø says the situation resembles the conditions preceding the 2015 avalanche.

164860.excerpt_en: The Governor and Longyearbyen Community Council met with NVE at 10 a.m. this morning, and the forecasts for the severe weather remain unchanged. Gale-force to full-storm winds and 15–20 mm of precipitation are forecast for the Longyearbyen area.
164860.subtitle_en: Gale-force to full-storm winds are forecast, and the avalanche danger has been classified as considerable.
164860.tags_en: severe weather, news, winter storm, storm

164884.excerpt_en: “It has been a quiet night, and it appears that there was less weather than feared. Now that the weather has passed, we need to be a little patient and get an overview,” says Governor Kjerstin Askholt.
164884.subtitle_en: The Governor will hold another meeting with NVE on Wednesday morning. An assessment of whether the evacuation should continue will probably not be made until this afternoon.

164890.excerpt_en: This morning, NVE’s local avalanche observers are examining the mountain slopes on Sukkertoppen and above Nybyen on foot and by helicopter. “Based on these observations, new avalanche assessments will be made, along with a new decision regarding the evacuation,” Governor Kjerstin Askholt said in a press release. The Governor held another meeting with NVE at 9:30 a.m. today.
164890.subtitle_en: This became clear after a meeting with the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) on Wednesday morning.

164897.excerpt_en: Where can you find Villa Gjennomtrekk, and what is the area known as colloquially today? Local place names are usually created to describe an area simply, with the name-giver often taking something distinctive about the place as their starting point.

164920.excerpt_en: “People can therefore return home to their residences,” Governor Kjerstin Askholt said in a press release.
164920.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is lifting the evacuation order and travel ban in Lia and Nybyen with immediate effect.

164926.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Education and Research has asked the Norwegian Meteorological Institute (MET) to assess possible efficiency and cost-saving measures in the institute’s operations. “We note that the identified efficiency measures at Bjørnøya and Hopen are considered professionally sound from a meteorological perspective.”
164926.subtitle_en: Automation of the meteorological station at Hopen and staff cuts at Bjørnøya may result from cost-saving measures.

164943.excerpt_en: “I am just one of many people who are regularly evacuated. We have packed the essentials for a few days, and now we have to see how things develop,” says Local Council leader Arild Olsen.
164943.subtitle_en: Around 180 people were evacuated from Lia and Nybyen on Monday evening. Local Council leader Arild Olsen himself has been evacuated regularly with his family.

164945.excerpt_en: On Friday, Jovna Z. Dunfjell of Svalbard Church was ceremonially presented with St.
164945.subtitle_en: The Miners’ Association in Peissenberg, Germany, has given Longyearbyen St Barbara, the patron saint of protection against accidents and disasters.

164964.excerpt_en: “We have had two years of hell. We are saddled with several million kroner in bank debt and are paying rent as well.”
164964.subtitle_en: Brothers Sam and Avaz Ziaei are millions of kroner in debt over the ghost apartments at the Old Hospital. Now they are taking the former owner to court to get their money back.
164964.title_en: Taking Legal Action Against Former Owner

164975.excerpt_en: Four men are spending the winter at Hopen this year. They had been there for only ten days when the Christmas visitors came helicoptering in to the long, narrow island.
164975.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard, the priest and the rest of the party received a warm welcome when they arrived at Hopen meteorological station.

165001.excerpt_en: Store manager Karin Mella (65) sits at the meeting table at Svalbardbutikken, wearing glittering bracelets and a ring, with sparks in her eyes. On the table in front of her are several folders and a small notebook containing reminders for herself.
165001.subtitle_en: Karin Mella claims she can read the future and stop bleeding, and says she wishes she were a top executive. Now she is moving on to the biggest thing of all.
165001.title_en: “It’s Tough Being a Woman and a Leader”

165002.excerpt_en: The Svalbard Treaty of 9 February 1920 granted Norway “full and unrestricted sovereignty over the Spitsbergen archipelago”, but it took five years of legal work and a change of name before Norway gained sovereignty over Svalbard on the 14th.
165002.subtitle_en: When the sovereignty ceremony was cancelled, the polar community took matters into its own hands. A command ship, a hand-planed flagpole and “hospitable households” with wine ensured there was a celebration after all. Read the story here. Open access.
165002.title_en: When Svalbard Became Part of Norway

165013.excerpt_en: When Svalbardposten’s Christmas issue is published, Trym will be on holiday in Thailand. He has been allowed a sneak peek at the pages he was responsible for, pages 42 and 43 of the Christmas newspaper.
165013.subtitle_en: When Trym Aunevik (16) showed the editorial staff the Christmas newspaper he made last year, they asked whether he would create special Christmas pages for this year’s Christmas issue.

165026.excerpt_en: Once, in 2011, I was aboard the old and reliable «Nordsyssel». Oddleif Moen then asked me to translate the diary of a Russian who overwintered in Bjonahamna in 1923–1924.
165026.subtitle_en: Anastasia Gorter, a Russian-language adviser and interpreter for the Governor of Svalbard, has gained access to, among other things, the diary of Ivan Hochlin, who overwintered in Bjonahamna in the 1920s. Read the story here. Open access.
165026.title_en: A Russian on a Norwegian Overwintering Expedition in Bjonahamna

165064.excerpt_en: “Amundsen Villa was more or less as I had imagined it. Sitting in the living room, I felt proud.”
165064.subtitle_en: Beathe Holstad felt proud as she sat in the living room of her great-grandfather, Peter S. Brandal, one of the founders of Kings Bay Kull Company.
165064.title_en: A Rich History in His Great-Grandfather’s Footsteps

165129.excerpt_en: Fire attack leader Trond Håvelsrud has just lit a fire inside the flashover container at the fire-training ground above the airport. The temperature is steadily rising as Håvelsrud reports to the duty crew at the fire station that they must deploy.
165129.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen has 24 firefighters. Every week, they practise different scenarios they hope will never become reality.

165182.excerpt_en: What was the name of the newspaper Einar Sverdrup took the initiative to launch in 1922? Svalbardposten is an institution and has been delivering news to the island’s residents since 1948.

The person with the most correct answers wins; if several people tie, one lucky winner will be drawn from among them. 165205.excerpt_en: For 39 years, the Briton has spread humor and helped researchers in Ny-Ålesund. Several thousand researchers have benefited from his knowledge of getting around on land and water, as well as how to protect themselves from the dangers of nature.
165205.subtitle_en: No one who has met Nick Cox (64) forgets his smile, humor, thoughtfulness, good stories and the warm cup of English tea.

165226.excerpt_en: New Year’s Eve was celebrated almost as quietly and peacefully as the entire Christmas and post-Christmas period. The police had to deal with only one minor disturbance of the peace.
165226.subtitle_en: The new year was welcomed with a spectacular fireworks display in cold, clear weather and bright moonlight.

165237.excerpt_en: At around 9 p.m. on Monday evening, the Governor of Svalbard was called by a snowmobile driver who had seen a polar dog bite and injure a reindeer. “We went out and caught the dog,” says senior police officer Anders Haugerud. The reindeer was so badly injured that it had to be put down.
165237.subtitle_en: On Monday, the Governor of Svalbard had to put down an injured reindeer.

165251.excerpt_en: «Kronprins Haakon» is ice-strengthened and will meet both existing and emerging needs for presence, monitoring and data collection in ice-covered and open waters throughout the year. It will be owned by the Norwegian Polar Institute and operated by the Institute of Marine Research.
165251.subtitle_en: The research vessel «Kronprins Haakon» will be unveiled in Bergen on Tuesday.
165251.title_en: A New Era for Norwegian Polar Research

165267.excerpt_en: A 20-year-old from Troms has been convicted by Nord-Troms District Court of stealing a snowmobile and driving with a blood alcohol level of 2.06 in central Longyearbyen on April 30 last year.
165267.subtitle_en: Drove a stolen snowmobile with a blood alcohol level of 2.06 in central Longyearbyen.

165269.excerpt_en: A total of 191 snowmobiles and cars were handed in. In addition, around 25 deregistered vehicles will be collected at the owners’ expense.
165269.subtitle_en: Store Norske’s vehicle and snowmobile amnesty yielded a substantial haul.

165287.excerpt_en: At 21 and eager to work, my father Leif Langnes (75) travelled to Svalbard for the first time. It would become one of many trips to 78 degrees north.
165287.subtitle_en: Freelance journalist Rune Langnes interviewed his father, Leif Langnes, about his first visit to Svalbard. Read the story here. Open article.

165292.excerpt_en: On January 1, Bring merged A-mail and B-mail into a service with a two-day delivery time.
165292.subtitle_en: It will no longer be published on Fridays in Longyearbyen.

165302.excerpt_en: Last Thursday, the Icepeople editor turned 50. “I was up early, so it will be a quiet birthday,” Sabbatini told Svalbardposten when they met him that morning at his regular writing spot, Fruene in Longyearbyen. Ideally, he would have finished the next issue of the free English-language newspaper.
165302.subtitle_en: Icepeople’s 50-year-old editor Mark Sabbatini came to Longyearbyen to cover Polarjazz ten years ago. His dream is to stay here forever.
165302.title_en: “The Only Place That Has Ever Felt Like Home”

165314.excerpt_en: “The budget makes no provision for physical avalanche-protection measures, demolition or new buildings in safe areas.”
165314.subtitle_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen expresses deep concern about the follow-up, pace and funding related to avalanche protection.
165314.title_en: Urges Minister to Speed Things Up

165344.excerpt_en: In November, Rema 1000 presented plans to build out 1,159 square metres of floor area over two or three storeys in the parking lot next to Lompensenteret. Now Coop Svalbard has responded with a new planning proposal for the same area.
165344.subtitle_en: Coop Svalbard proposes turning the parking lot between Lompensenteret and Longyear 78 degrees into a shared public space.
165344.title_en: Wants a Town Arena with a Stage

165346.excerpt_en: The average temperature in December was 8.5 degrees higher than normal. For the year as a whole, it was 4.5 degrees above normal. “That is a lot.”
165346.subtitle_en: For 85 consecutive months, the monthly temperature at Svalbard Airport has been above normal. The annual average has now been higher than the normal temperature for 29 years in a row. “It’s extreme,” says Reidun Gangstø Skaland.
165346.title_en: This Development Frightens the Climate Scientist

165365.excerpt_en: It is Thursday and almost a full moon when the Governor’s chief police officers Anders Haugerud and Espen Olsen walk from the helicopter to a hangar at the Russian helicopter base at Kapp Heer. Shortly afterwards, an old burgundy Mercedes bearing the Governor’s logo on its side drives out.
165365.subtitle_en: Handcuffs, a bulletproof vest and a baton all came in handy when the Governor of Svalbard held an office day in Barentsburg.

165386.excerpt_en: A large box of poinsettias stands on the floor of the canteen in Barentsburg. Elin Amundsen unpacks the flowers and hands them to employees, who place them on saucers and set them on the tables. “I’m very happy about the flowers.”
165386.subtitle_en: Every year, Elin Amundsen brings Christmas cheer to Barentsburg. Tomorrow, Saturday, they will celebrate Christmas.

165412.excerpt_en: Door 1: When did the Sports Centre on Svalbard open? The correct answer is 1995. Door 2: When was the polar bear given full protection on Svalbard?
165412.subtitle_en: Once again this year, two people had the same number of correct answers. Inger Lise Næss and Leif Trønnes both had 23 correct, but in the draw it was Trønnes who took home the prize. Inger Lise Ness answered incorrectly on the question about organized flights to Svalbard, while Leif Trønnes answered incorrectly on the number of trappers stationed in 2017. Although it is true that Soleim has been in Longyearbyen since the summer, he is still stationed at Kapp Wijk, with a temporary stay due to illness.
165412.title_en: Leif Trønnes Wins the 2017 Advent Calendar

165414.excerpt_en: Police received a report of noise from a home on Road 228 at 2:10 a.m. “There were quite a few people present.”
165414.subtitle_en: Responded to a late-night party in the early hours of Sunday.

165437.excerpt_en: The seminar is held over five evenings and this year runs from the 16th to the 30th.
165437.subtitle_en: The 23rd edition of the Svalbard Seminar begins on Tuesday.
165437.title_en: Now You Can Learn More about Research, History and Safety

165443.excerpt_en: On Monday, UNIS Director Harald Ellingsen welcomed the students to Longyearbyen. This semester, 82 bachelor’s students will be here until summer, along with 25 master’s and doctoral students. “Our task is to educate tomorrow’s Arctic experts, and that means investing in you young people.”

165446.excerpt_en: A snowmobile carrying two people drove down a 15-metre-high slope in the area near Janssonhaugen in Adventdalen on Tuesday afternoon. “The two were injured.”
165446.subtitle_en: Two people have been sent to the University Hospital of North Norway in Tromsø for examination.

165460.excerpt_en: Are they hoping for a wider selection of goods? Many more retail jobs?
165460.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken’s proposal for a town stage and, not least, Svalbardposten’s latest Gallup poll have brought the question of Rema 1000 back into focus. Many seem to want two grocery stores in Longyearbyen. Why?

165471.excerpt_en: The University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) began work last spring on defining how Longyearbyen Hospital should be staffed and organised in the future. Four doctors are employed at Longyearbyen Hospital.
165471.subtitle_en: A general practitioner is being replaced by a surgeon at Longyearbyen Hospital.
165471.tags_en: Longyearbyen Hospital, emergency preparedness, news, surgery

165489.excerpt_en: Coop Svalbard proposes creating a town stage that could be used for major events in the town or as the start and finish area for sporting events. It also proposes more regulated parking, with options for lighting in the ground, a dedicated taxi rank, bus parking and a snow dump.
165489.subtitle_en: Coop Svalbard’s new plans for the parking area between Lompensenteret and Longyear 78, which Svalbardposten covered in its previous issue, have sparked considerable engagement.

165494.excerpt_en: In November, it became clear that Statsbygg had to launch a new detailed planning process in order to build homes in Gruvedalen. This was because they had to build a road making it possible to reach the new development site from both sides.
165494.subtitle_en: Fewer parking spaces make room for 20 new flats in Gruvedalen.

165504.excerpt_en: The letter to Visit Svalbard states: “The project is a significant intervention, and of a kind that has not previously been carried out on Svalbard.”
165504.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is asking Visit Svalbard to explain what kind of trail it wants built up to Varden.
165504.title_en: A Long Road to a Sherpa Trail

165535.excerpt_en: “We have emailed LNS Spitsbergen to get a cost estimate for the work that needs to be done. Then we have to start working on raising funds.”
165535.subtitle_en: Svalbard Turn has been given the green light to extend the ski trail by the school, but lacks the money.

165544.excerpt_en: It was a disturbing sight that greeted Anders Magne Lindseth when he returned home from celebrating New Year’s at the cabin.
165544.subtitle_en: “If it had landed on the roof, the house could have burned down,” says Anders Magne Lindseth.

165566.excerpt_en: On January 30, she will have been on Svalbard for a year.
165566.subtitle_en: Lisa Larsgaard (21) had a job and an apartment, but didn’t know anyone.

165577.excerpt_en: It will be a mild weekend on Svalbard. According to the Norwegian Meteorological Institute’s forecast, the weekend will begin with light rain or sleet on Friday.
165577.subtitle_en: See the forecast for the weekend weather.
165577.title_en: Svalbard Could Be the Warmest Place in the Country

165589.excerpt_en: The Norwegian flight from Oslo was unable to land at Svalbard Airport on Friday. The landing was aborted on the first attempt because of strong winds and an icy runway. “There was a little too much crosswind towards the end, and the runway conditions were only moderately good.”
165589.subtitle_en: The plane had to turn around and head to Tromsø instead.

165620.excerpt_en: Police responded to a road accident in Gruvedalen on Friday evening. A local man in his 30s had ended up off the road in the icy conditions and needed help getting out.
165620.subtitle_en: He needed help getting out of the ditch, but police suspected that something was not right.
165620.title_en: Drove off the Road While Drunk

165628.excerpt_en: On Monday, it became clear that biathlete Erlend Bjøntegaard (27) will represent Norway at the Olympics in Pyeongchang. Bjøntegaard won the final spot in competition with the greatest Winter Olympian of all time, Ole Einar Bjørndalen (43).
165628.subtitle_en: The son of the race director for the Svalbard Ski Marathon will represent Norway at the Olympics in Pyeongchang.

165636.excerpt_en: Between Saturday and Sunday, a full 65.5 millimetres of precipitation fell in Ny-Ålesund. “The monthly average for Ny-Ålesund in January is 30 millimetres. They received more than twice as much in a single day,” says meteorological consultant Torgeir Mørk at Svalbard Airport. “Ny-Ålesund lies on the coast and is more exposed to this kind of weather.”
165636.subtitle_en: There was more than enough precipitation over the weekend.
165636.title_en: Twice the Monthly Average in a Single Day

165644.excerpt_en: Early Wednesday morning, a local man in his early 40s had had far too much to drink. When he tried to walk home, he could not remember where he lived.
165644.subtitle_en: A local resident knocked on several doors in an attempt to find his way home early Wednesday morning.
165644.title_en: Helped Man Find His Way Home

165652.excerpt_en: At an extraordinary general meeting in December, the Norwegian YMCA-YWCA entered as majority owners of Svalbard Folk High School. A board election was also held.
165652.subtitle_en: Former minister Torild Skogsholm becomes chair of the board of Svalbard Folk High School.
165652.title_en: Folk High School Picks Up Speed

165660.excerpt_en: “We have obviously been anxious, because it will have a major impact on us, since we have had direct contact with the ministers who have visited Svalbard. I think we will have that with two of the new ministers as well, both the Minister of Trade, Industry and Fisheries and the Minister of Justice,” says Local Council leader Arild Olsen.
165660.subtitle_en: Sylvi Listhaug (Progress Party) becomes Minister of Justice and will thereby be responsible for Svalbard. “That could benefit us if we manage to make a good case for our issues,” says Local Council leader Arild Olsen.

165672.excerpt_en: “We are completely on schedule. These are hectic days, but that is always how it is during the final push.”
165672.subtitle_en: The hotel at Elvesletta will open its doors for Polarjazz.

165690.excerpt_en: The plane was unable to land as planned at Svalbard Airport. The landing was aborted on the first attempt because of strong winds and an icy runway. “We circled a little east of the airport while the runway was being prepared.”
165690.subtitle_en: It was a long journey for the Norwegian passengers travelling from Oslo to Svalbard last Friday.
165690.title_en: Had to Sit on Plane for Twelve Hours

165716.excerpt_en: The first large ship arrives on 30 May, and the last docks on the 29th.
165716.subtitle_en: More cruise passengers will experience Svalbard in 2018. The largest ship is called MSC “Meraviglia” and has a capacity of 4,500 passengers.

165729.excerpt_en: “It does not look as though this place will open in three weeks,” says Thomas Westergaard, executive vice president at Hurtigruten. He is standing in what will become Funken’s new restaurant.
165729.subtitle_en: Dark and mysterious. Funken reopens in a new guise on 1 February.

165743.excerpt_en: Store Norske wants to facilitate more cabin plots, among other things so that the 23 people with cabins in the red avalanche zone can have the opportunity to move their cabins to a safe location. Last week, the Technical Committee adopted the planning programme for the cabin areas.
165743.subtitle_en: The cabin plots at Vindodden are scheduled to be ready for consideration in February. Todalen and Foxdalen must wait for an environmental report.

165751.excerpt_en: In 2017, there were nine drunk-driving cases in Longyearbyen in total. Four of the cases were decided in December.
165751.subtitle_en: The verdicts from December last year are now in.

165777.excerpt_en: To be named a gazelle company, turnover must have doubled over four years (see fact box).
165777.subtitle_en: Mia Willman (30) and Audun Salte (26) are full of drive as they buy Svalbard Husky AS. It certainly does not hurt that the company ranks top among Svalbard’s six gazelle companies in 2017.
165777.tags_en: news, gazelle companies, Svalbard Husky, gazelles

165795.excerpt_en: In two weeks, Polarjazz 2018 gets under way, and this is the 21st year the festival has been held.
165795.subtitle_en: There are few pure jazz artists at this year’s Polarjazz. But the organiser is pleased with the lineup and expects good entertainment.
165795.tags_en: Svalbard life, culture, Unni Wilhelmsen, Circus Dos Mosquitos, Anneli Drecker, Polarjazz

165813.excerpt_en: At 5:40 p.m. on Sunday, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that a person had received an electric shock in Svea. “The man did not suffer serious injuries, but was picked up by helicopter,” says senior police officer Arve Johnsen at the Governor’s office.
165813.subtitle_en: Injured man picked up by helicopter on Sunday afternoon.

165821.excerpt_en: A heavily intoxicated woman in her 40s could not find her way home early Saturday morning. “She missed her apartment, couldn’t get all the way inside and lay down to sleep in the hallway,” says police superintendent Arve Johnsen of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
165821.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard got her home.
165821.title_en: Woman Fell Asleep in the Hallway

165829.excerpt_en: Sofia grew up with dog racing in Longyearbyen. She took part in Trappers Trail for the first time when she was just ten, together with her father, Johan.
165829.subtitle_en: Sofia Berger wasn’t sure she would manage to finish her first dog race on the mainland. She did so in style.
165829.title_en: Sofia (15) Beat the Boys on the Mainland

165861.excerpt_en: Last spring, the Governor of Svalbard established the assessment program for commercial cabins in the field, and applicants were given a deadline of August 1, 2017, to prepare and submit environmental impact assessments.
165861.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol has applied to have at least eight cabins approved as commercial cabins.
165861.title_en: Seeking Approval for Eight Commercial Cabins

165869.excerpt_en: The evening began with a performance by the young musicians of the Stavanger band “Strengeplukk.” The five band members are music students who demonstrated an impressive level of skill.
165869.subtitle_en: Saturday saw a concert by Blåmyra Bluegrass at Huset. As tradition dictates, people streamed into the venue, and before long the dance floor was filled with revelers.

165879.excerpt_en: Applications have been submitted to build several new commercial cabins in the area around Van Mijenfjorden, an important polar-bear denning area in recent years. The cabins are planned for tourism, in one of the polar bear’s last refuges.
165879.subtitle_en: Several times we have seen polar bears with cubs through binoculars from the cabin; they get up and run away, clearly stressed by groups of tourists driving across the ice toward Paulabreen.
165879.tags_en: news, reader’s letter, wildlife, commercial cabins, nature and environment

165889.excerpt_en: The Greek, who has been based in London for the past 18 years, has built up several popular nightclubs in the English capital. He also runs Moni on the Greek island of Mykonos, a venue frequented by celebrities such as Leonardo DiCaprio and Gerard Butler.
165889.subtitle_en: Every year, Greg Tsouloufris (35) spends two months in the Arctic to recharge.
165889.title_en: Greg Goes to the Arctic to Find Peace

165921.excerpt_en: Tommy Sandal first came to Svalbard in 1998 and has been a trapper for the past eleven years. In 2011, he took over the trapping area at Bellsund, and in 2013 he and his partner Elise Strømseng bought the main trapping station on Akseløya.
165921.subtitle_en: Trapper Tommy Sandal believes increasing traffic and human activity threaten Svalbard’s wilderness.

165942.excerpt_en: Frigg Jørgensen is managing director of the Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators (AECO), which has 70 international member companies in the expedition cruise industry. AECO aims to ensure sustainable tourism and has implemented many measures that members are required to follow or participate in.
165942.subtitle_en: Few places prohibit going ashore, but under AECO’s guidelines, no more than 100 passengers may go ashore at any one location.
165942.title_en: The Right of Public Access Applies

165950.excerpt_en: The growing number of cruise calls is overwhelming the port’s capacity in Longyearbyen. In September, Svalbardposten wrote that capacity had been stretched to breaking point and that the port had handled 75,000 passengers by the end of August—equivalent to all of 2016.
165950.subtitle_en: If everything goes according to plan, a new floating quay and associated building will be ready in Longyearbyen in 2020.

165959.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) and Store Norske have all been sent compensation claims totaling nearly NOK 4.4 million and are being held jointly and severally liable. “The claim is directed equally against all three, but the basis for the claim differs somewhat.”
165959.subtitle_en: Nikoline (2) died as a result of the landslide that hit her family’s home in 2015. Her parents have now quantified their compensation claims.

165980.excerpt_en: Children who have nothing to do during recess can sit there, and other children can come over and invite them to join in the play. “When you sit here, others can come over and ask whether you want to talk or play,” says pupil Joshua Biko Dahlstrøm-Haughton. “…”
165980.subtitle_en: The primary school’s student council has taken the initiative to build a buddy bench in the schoolyard.

165988.excerpt_en: Marcus & Martinus are regulars at Svalbardhallen. The twins from Trofors in Nordland are played frequently over the loudspeakers when the primary school holds its disco every Friday.
165988.subtitle_en: On Fridays, pupils can go to a disco during recess.

165996.subtitle_en: Norwegian is adding two weekly flights in February and March. At the same time, SAS is adjusting its schedules to better accommodate foreign tourists.

166004.excerpt_en: The Conservative Party, Progress Party and Liberal Party coalition announced the composition of the new government before the weekend. For Svalbard, the Minister of Justice is the most relevant, because the Polar Department falls under the Ministry of Justice.
166004.subtitle_en: The new Svalbard minister says she is deeply committed to Svalbard and the Arctic regions. “We know that the High North is important to Norway for a number of reasons,” she writes.
166004.tags_en: Svalbard minister, Sylvi Listhaug, Minister of Justice and Emergency Preparedness, news

166012.excerpt_en: “A few days ago, a child from Russia joined us who didn’t speak a single word of Norwegian. But meeting the other children went well, and it wasn’t long before play began and the first Norwegian words were spoken,” says Gunnhild Antonsen.
166012.subtitle_en: Sixty-four percent of the children at Kullungen Kindergarten have a first language other than Norwegian. It creates challenges, but above all benefits for both Norwegian and foreign children, says director Gunnhild Antonsen.

166050.excerpt_en: Fourth-grader Joanna Matea Rut Eriksson (9) is good at drawing cheerful suns. Competing against many other pupils at Longyearbyen School, she won last year.
166050.subtitle_en: “It’s very special to win again,” says Joanna Matea Rut Eriksson (9).

166058.excerpt_en: The fifth edition of the Bjørnøya Film Festival (BØFF) took place last weekend. “The festival was great. We set things up in the living room and showed films on a screen,” says meteorological assistant André Røsberg by phone from the Bjørnøya meteorological station.
166058.subtitle_en: The film festival on Bjørnøya was packed. The organizers received special treatment from Nordisk Film Distribution.
166058.title_en: “Fingern” Gives the Bjørnøya Cinema a Thumbs-Up

166076.excerpt_en: The football school was organized by Liverbirds Svalbard, while David Crist and Darren Carr from “5 Times” in Liverpool served as instructors. See photos from the football school in the gallery.
166076.subtitle_en: Thirty-nine children from Longyearbyen took part in a football school at Svalbardhallen over the weekend.
166076.title_en: See Photos from the Football School

166100.excerpt_en: “This is definitely a phenomenon worth seeing. For kindergartens and schools, it can be a great opportunity to show and then explain how celestial bodies move in relation to Earth,” says senior adviser Pål Brekke of the Norwegian Space Agency.
166100.subtitle_en: Lunar eclipses and supermoons are common, but on Wednesday we will see a supermoon eclipse. It is a rare phenomenon.
166100.title_en: The Moon Will Turn Red on Wednesday

166108.excerpt_en: “A great many things have gone wrong this year. The director had to withdraw, and we have not managed to find a replacement.”
166108.subtitle_en: A series of unfortunate circumstances has forced the revue group to change its plans.
166108.tags_en: Solfest Revue, Spitsbergen Revue Group, news, revue

166116.excerpt_en: The weather gods were on Longyearbyen’s side on Wednesday as the supermoon was slowly covered by shadow. The total eclipse lasted from 1:51 p.m. to 3:08 p.m.
166116.title_en: Perfect Conditions for the Dark Moon

166132.excerpt_en: We should be grateful that none of the 15 fires or incipient fires developed further, and that we have an effective direct-alarm system and a skilled fire brigade. The town centre is densely built up, and large parts consist of wooden buildings.
166132.subtitle_en: In little Longyearbyen, there was a fire callout slightly more often than every other day in 2017. A total of 187 callouts is a new record—but not one to be proud of this time.

166140.excerpt_en: Last year, the Longyearbyen fire service had a total of 187 callouts. Fifteen were to fires or incipient fires, 11 of them caused by unattended cooking.
166140.subtitle_en: “Without direct fire alarms, we would have had annual fire-related deaths,” says fire chief Jan Olav Sæter.
166140.tags_en: news, unattended cooking, fire, fire service

166162.excerpt_en: It was a mixed list. We carried out a selection process in which we assessed the candidates together with the clinic’s employee representatives.
166162.subtitle_en: Many familiar names appear on the list of applicants for the department head position at Longyearbyen Hospital.

166171.excerpt_en: In 2012 and 2013, Longyearbyen Boligeiendom bought several of Longyearbyen Local Council’s dormitory buildings, including the building at Vei 222-13. The building is in Lia, in the row closest to Sukkertoppen.
166171.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Boligeiendom is seeking more than NOK 8 million from Longyearbyen Local Council because the dormitory building it bought at Vei 222 is uninhabitable for part of the year.

166179.excerpt_en: In recent years, we have learned a great deal about life during the polar night. Just ten years ago, we viewed the polar night as a kind of biological desert where animals and algae simply waited for the light to return.
166179.subtitle_en: For organisms active in darkness, whether at night in southern latitudes or during the polar night farther north, artificial light can actually be a major disadvantage.

166191.excerpt_en: Inside the boss’s office, at the far end of the corridor in Store Norske’s office building, it is the standard poodle Molly who greets visitors. The director herself comes straight from the meeting room for the interview.
166191.subtitle_en: Wenche Ravlo (52) is soon ready to hand over the baton. Three years in the director’s chair at Store Norske and in Longyearbyen have brought many challenges, but also many good experiences.

166209.excerpt_en: It is art and crafts class in Year 10 at the school.
166209.subtitle_en: At Longyearbyen School, 40 per cent of the tenth-graders have parents who are not Norwegian. Several others have one non-Norwegian parent.
166209.tags_en: immigration, news, people from different cultural backgrounds
166209.title_en: Don’t Think About All the Nationalities

166217.excerpt_en: The school has no control over, or predictability regarding, when pupils turn up and need to be enrolled.
166217.subtitle_en: More and more foreign pupils arrive with no or very limited Norwegian skills. This creates challenges both for the pupils and Longyearbyen School.
166217.tags_en: Norwegian language education, news, immigration, Longyearbyen School

166233.excerpt_en: We present the latest picture from the collection lent to us by Per Sørflaten, or Hunde-Per, as everyone calls him. The picture was taken in the early 1960s and shows what is now the Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association cabin at Bjonahamna.

166241.excerpt_en: Visit Svalbard’s visitor figures show a much more modest development last year than in the preceding three or four years. The number of guests arriving at hotels and guesthouses in Longyearbyen rose by just over three per cent last year, while the increase in commercial guest nights was around four per cent.
166241.subtitle_en: Funken Lodge and The Vault open their doors today. “Welcome news,” says the tourism director after reviewing the 2017 visitor figures.

166265.excerpt_en: “The Norwegian market is rising slightly again after stagnating for several years and accounts for around 60 per cent of visitors. Germany, Sweden and the USA have performed well in recent years and are still going strong, as can also be said of France,” says Ronny Brunvoll.
166265.subtitle_en: Naturally, the countries visitors to Longyearbyen come from vary from year to year.
166265.title_en: Visitors from Liechtenstein Up 2,700 Per Cent

166273.excerpt_en: Three years ago, the two football coaches from Jamie Carragher’s football school visited Longyearbyen for the first time. It was an unusual visit. “We were told to bring a jacket, but we left it in the suitcase.”
166273.subtitle_en: The technique of Longyearbyen’s football players impresses English instructors Darren Carr and David Crist.

166281.excerpt_en: It was a particularly शानदार opening to this year’s Polarjazz on Wednesday evening. Did you miss the pre-party?
166281.subtitle_en: Want to relive the spectacular start to Polarjazz 2018? Here is a ten-minute video summary.

166292.excerpt_en: Polarjazz 2018 got off to a brilliant start with an opening show on Wednesday evening. See photos in the picture carousel.

166302.excerpt_en: Just minutes before Funken Lodge opened its doors on Thursday, the staff were working flat out. “It’s fun—this is when we see how everyone works together as a team, regardless of their usual jobs,” says hotel manager Mouawia Lababidi.
166302.subtitle_en: See photos of the hotel reopening today, Thursday. What do you think?

166311.excerpt_en: 35 hotel rooms, three floors, a reception, lobby and dining room. On Thursday, Svalbard Hotell The Vault opened its doors to its first overnight guests.
166311.subtitle_en: See photos and read why the new hotel is named after the seed vault.

166331.excerpt_en: Anneli Drecker was the first to take the stage at the cultural centre on Friday evening. “I could have lived in Asker,” Drecker said, referring to the song she wrote at 19 after her boyfriend broke her heart.
166331.subtitle_en: Friday was the women’s night at the cultural centre. See photos from the concerts.

166339.excerpt_en: The lunchtime concert with Unni Wilhelmsen, Ole Jørn Myklebust and Ronny Johnsen gave the audience a lovely, peaceful start to the day. Wilhelmsen sang several songs from “Hver gang vi møtes.”
166339.subtitle_en: The intimate concert at Kroa was a full house.

166347.excerpt_en: When Sondre Justad finally took the stage, the atmosphere was electric. Under-18s were also allowed to attend the concert on Saturday evening.
166347.subtitle_en: Sondre Justad was Polarjazz’s clear favourite among younger audiences.

166355.excerpt_en: The night before Sunday was hectic for the police and fire service. Around 10 p.m., firefighters were dispatched to a home where there was heavy smoke.
166355.subtitle_en: On the night before Sunday, a man was taken to hospital after a domestic disturbance. A woman drove off the road, and a drunk man needed help finding his way home.

166363.excerpt_en: The power was out across the town for only about ten minutes. Thawing weather, blowing snow and wind caused the short circuit. “Snow had accumulated on the line to Hotellneset.”
166363.subtitle_en: Shortly before 9 a.m. on Monday, the power went out throughout Longyearbyen. A short circuit in the lines to Hotellneset was the cause.
166363.title_en: The Weather Knocked Out the Power

166371.excerpt_en: A dog was hit in Sjøområdet at around 2 p.m. on Sunday. The driver reported the incident to the police, as well as the fact that the dog disappeared after being hit.
166371.subtitle_en: The husky puppy that was hit by a car on Sunday was found during the night before Monday.

166375.excerpt_en: Around 6 p.m. on Sunday, a woman in her 30s lost control while driving on Road 501, near the new bridge there.
166375.subtitle_en: The woman lost control near the bridge on Road 501.

166391.excerpt_en: “Poor visibility, strong crosswinds and slightly too little friction on the runway meant the aircraft could not land,” says airport manager Morten Ulsnes. The plane circled over Isfjorden four times before heading for Tromsø.
166391.subtitle_en: The SAS flight from Oslo, scheduled to land in Svalbard on Sunday evening, had to turn around and fly to Tromsø instead.
166391.title_en: This Flight Did Not Go Entirely as Planned

166413.excerpt_en: Over the past decade, Mark Sabbatini has been part of Longyearbyen. Through his free English-language newspaper, he has kept residents and visitors informed about events and issues in the local community.
166413.subtitle_en: For the second time in eight years, Mark Sabbatini (50) has broken his hip. A fundraiser has now been launched to pay for the Icepeople editor’s hospital stay.

166423.excerpt_en: Automatic weather stations were in use for at least 80 years, secretly deployed in places including Svalbard during the war. The stations were operated by mechanical clockworks, with data converted into radio signals and reflected off the ionosphere over long distances.
166423.subtitle_en: Automation will undermine safety, the contributor argues.
166423.tags_en: remote stations, meteorology, opinions, reader contribution, weather stations

166431.excerpt_en: Several people were dressed in beautiful, colourful gákti from different places. Parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen led the evening, which included interviews, Sámi singing and performances.
166431.subtitle_en: Many people took part in the celebration of Sámi National Day at Svalbard Church on Tuesday evening.

166439.excerpt_en: Normally, the flight carrying the print edition of Svalbardposten would arrive on Wednesday, after which it would be delivered to subscribers on Thursday morning. That will not happen this week.
166439.subtitle_en: Wednesday’s mail flight to Svalbard has been cancelled. This means the print edition of Svalbardposten will be delayed.

166443.excerpt_en: The light is returning, and with it the season’s tourism workers. This year, several people are finding it difficult to secure a place to live, including employees of Basecamp Spitsbergen and Better Moments. “If you post a housing request on Facebook, it’s completely dead.”
166443.subtitle_en: Companies cannot find housing for their employees. They say more people would rather rent to tourists through Airbnb.
166443.tags_en: housing shortage, news, Airbnb, housing crisis

166451.excerpt_en: Store Norske property manager Sveinung Lystrup Thesen says they have rented out everything they can. “We are trying to find solutions where we rent out homes that, strictly speaking, should have been renovated, but where we see that a company can rent and use them for its employees.”
166451.subtitle_en: The waiting list at Store Norske is so long that they have stopped adding people who need housing.
166451.tags_en: housing market, news, Airbnb, housing shortage

166467.excerpt_en: When Svalbardposten checked Airbnb on Tuesday, 56 rental properties were listed. Forty-two of them were entire homes.
166467.subtitle_en: The local council leader wants to wait for national regulations and learn from others’ experiences.

166485.excerpt_en: At the end of January, representatives from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE), main contractor Norsk Bergsikring and their subcontractors inspected the site to clarify all the technical details concerning the planned snow fences to be built above the gable-roof houses. All permits are now in place.
166485.subtitle_en: In about a week and a half, work will begin on installing snow fences in Lia.

166495.excerpt_en: Between 500 and 600 audience members visited the community centre on Saturday evening. On the other days, the major concerts averaged between 400 and 500 attendees. “Saturday is the main party day, and Sondre Justad appeals to many people of all ages.”
166495.subtitle_en: Only Saturday’s Polarjazz event was sold out.

166533.excerpt_en: “I’m probably less angry today than I was in 2006. Or perhaps I’ve transformed my anger into something more constructive.”
166533.subtitle_en: When Veronica Rønneberg Reitan (31) was 19, she had many answers. Today, she has far fewer.

166541.excerpt_en: For this week’s historic photograph, we present a 34-year-old picture of trapper Harald Soleim, taken by Kjell Onarheim in 1984. Soleim came to Svalbard as early as 1977 and established himself as a trapper.
166541.subtitle_en: Harald Soleim enjoying himself 34 years ago.

166549.excerpt_en: Polarjazz has a tradition of offering something for both young and old. On Saturday morning, Tonje Unstad held a family concert at Rabalder.

166567.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard, Lufttransport and the Red Cross are among those taking part in the avalanche exercise in Todalen on Saturday morning. The alarm was raised at 10:10, and a few minutes later the site was in full activity, with a helicopter and search crews.
166567.subtitle_en: Large numbers of personnel are taking part in an avalanche exercise in Todalen on Saturday morning.

166587.excerpt_en: The conference themes are “A Smarter Society,” “Sustainable Business Development” and “Svalbard as a Test Arena.” Minister of Trade and Industry Torbjørn Røe Isaksen will attend the conference. Local Council leader Arild Olsen, Svalbard Business Association chair Terje Aunevik and UNIS director Harald Ellingsen will open the seminar.
166587.subtitle_en: On Monday 19 and Tuesday 20 February, NHO Arktis, Innovation Norway, Svalbard Business Association, UNIS and Longyearbyen Local Council invite people to a business conference.
