170660.excerpt_en: At the beginning of March, Longyearbyen Boligeiendom AS announced that it was putting 84 studio apartments up for sale at a price of NOK 77 million. The units are spread across five buildings in town.
170660.subtitle_en: Short-term Airbnb rentals violate the zoning plan, Longyearbyen Local Council claims. The owner says he does not understand the objection.
170660.tags_en: Longyearbyen Boligeiendom, Airbnb, news, housing shortage
170660.title_en: Five rooms are being rented out on Airbnb. The local council wants it stopped

170701.excerpt_en: It was probably a rough Saturday for a local man who fell asleep outside the wrong home at Elvesletta. At around nine o’clock on Sunday morning, police were notified that a man was lying outside a door inside an apartment complex.
170701.subtitle_en: He fell asleep outside the wrong home.
170701.title_en: Drunk man had to be woken by police

170719.excerpt_en: Eighty-eight readers took part in the competition to predict when the stem of the champagne-glass-shaped snow formation on Operafjellet would break this year. The two most popular dates to bet on this year were the 29th.
170719.subtitle_en: The Stetten broke on Sunday. This year’s most popular prediction was correct.
170719.title_en: See who won the Stetten competition

170743.excerpt_en: “It is simply some planned maintenance work that we did not manage to complete last year. Work will be carried out beneath the road, so it will be partially closed,” says construction manager Reidar Tolsrød of Rambøll, hired by Longyearbyen Local Council (LL).
170743.subtitle_en: From Saturday, Road 400 by Isdammen will be partially or completely closed at intervals for one week.

170770.excerpt_en: On Saturday, 21 July, one of the newest and most modern ships in the German TUI shipping company’s fleet was docked in Longyearbyen for ten hours.
170770.subtitle_en: On the cruise ship Mein Schiff 5, environmental concerns are taken seriously. But they cannot prevent the vessel from emitting more than three times as much CO2 as Longyearbyen Energiverk while under way.
170770.title_en: Masters of almost everything—but not CO2 emissions

170781.excerpt_en: The cargo plane that was due to arrive with Svalbardposten on Thursday was unable to land in Svalbard. As a result, the newspaper will be delayed by one day this week.
170781.subtitle_en: This week’s issue of Svalbardposten will be delayed by one day.
170781.title_en: The plane never arrived, newspaper delayed

170786.excerpt_en: “We received word at six this morning that a motor sailboat was having trouble with both its sails and engine,” Governor’s Office chief officer Anders Haugerud told Svalbardposten. The boat was southwest of Sørkapp in Svalbard, with eight people on board.
170786.subtitle_en: Eight people in distress at sea were evacuated.
170786.title_en: Had to deploy a raft to rescue eight people in distress at sea

170810.excerpt_en: At the beginning of July, the feasibility study “Alternatives for Future Energy Supply to Svalbard” was published—an assessment commissioned by the Ministry of Petroleum and Energy from two consultancy firms. It is an attempt to gain a clearer understanding of what will power this community after coal.
170810.subtitle_en: In his editorial, Christopher Engås argues for a power supply to Svalbard.

170836.excerpt_en: “The boat was towed to Longyearbyen by KV Bergen,” says Governor’s Office officer Carina Søreng. On Thursday, the boat ran into trouble a little southwest of Sørkapp, at the southern tip of Svalbard.
170836.subtitle_en: Eight people had to be rescued by helicopter; now the disabled boat has arrived in Longyearbyen.

170838.excerpt_en: “Jone happened to spot the fox on Friday, while the whole family was walking the nine-hole golf course we have made for ourselves along the shore by our cabin,” says Kine Stiberg, referring to the fox her son Jone Stiberg-Hansen found at Vinodden.
170838.subtitle_en: Two foxes will be sent for testing next week.
170838.title_en: Family found a dead fox during cabin trip—now it is being tested for rabies

170842.excerpt_en: A couple of years ago, the Swedish adventurers set themselves the goal of rowing around Svalbard. After a year of preparations, they began the trip from Tromsø last summer.
170842.subtitle_en: Last year they crossed the Barents Sea, but were stopped by heavy ice and a broken finger. Now Sören Kjellkvist (44) and Glenn Mattsing (39) are continuing their journey around Svalbard.
170842.title_en: Sören (44) and Glenn (39) row around the clock

170860.excerpt_en: When the Governor was contacted by Karlsberger Pub (KB) about the theft of a bottle of whisky early Monday morning, it was difficult to prioritise the case. A visit by the royal yacht and a medical emergency meant the case was put on hold.
170860.subtitle_en: The man who stole a bottle of whisky from Karlsberger Pub early Monday morning was exposed with the help of the pub’s own “intelligence system”.
170860.title_en: Man stole a bottle of whisky from KB, but things did not go well

170876.excerpt_en: Tour operator Eyos Expeditions is exploring the possibility of using mini-submarines in Svalbard. “We have used submersibles in Antarctica.”
170876.subtitle_en: “There are no limits to creativity,” says the Governor.
170876.tags_en: expedition cruise, submarine, submarine tourism, news, tourism
170876.title_en: Tour operator now wants to take Svalbard tourists in a submarine

170889.excerpt_en: “Two earthquakes were recorded off Svalbard, but we believe our instruments underestimated their strength,” says Ben Dando, a senior geophysics researcher at NORSAR. Its instruments measured the largest quake, which occurred at 75.120 degrees north and 9.720 degrees east, at 4.5 on the Richter scale.
170889.subtitle_en: Two earthquakes were recorded in the sea off Bear Island yesterday.
170889.title_en: Earthquake measured at 5.8 on the Richter scale off Svalbard

170917.excerpt_en: Last Thursday, the sailboat “Meloria” ran into trouble off the southern tip of Svalbard. The engine stopped working and one of the sails was damaged.
170917.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Maritime Authority has declared the accident vessel “Meloria” unseaworthy.

170939.excerpt_en: Clearly nervous, Mikael Bergman, 9, adjusted his hat slightly as he stood outside Svalbard Museum, shivering a little in the chilly weather.
170939.subtitle_en: Long hours of waiting paid off for the nine- and twelve-year-old brothers.
170939.title_en: Mikael and Samuel met the King and gave him a homemade tie

170949.excerpt_en: People around the world have reacted in different ways after a cruise employee was attacked by a polar bear when they went ashore on Phippsøya in far northern Svalbard. Among the most vocal was world-famous comedian Ricky Gervais, who took to Twitter to speak out.
170949.subtitle_en: At the end of July, a man was attacked by a polar bear, which was killed in what is claimed to have been self-defence. The incident has prompted reactions.
170949.title_en: Fifteen polar bear shootings linked to tourism

170959.excerpt_en: Several respected Norwegian and international media outlets have devoted considerable attention to the incident, and people are highly engaged on social media. Almost all of this engagement shares a strong interest in the polar bear.
170959.subtitle_en: A highly unfortunate incident in Svalbard, in which a man from a cruise ship was attacked by a polar bear and the bear had to be killed to save the man’s life, has sparked strong engagement in Norway and abroad.

170983.excerpt_en: The polar bear attack on Phippsøya is one of the most serious incidents, and it has sparked an important debate about guides’ experience, local knowledge and vulnerability in nature. The incident should be thoroughly evaluated and considered in the context of increasing cruise traffic and the strain on the environment and local communities.
170983.subtitle_en: Events in recent weeks have shown that growing tourist pressure continues to create problems and, in some cases, dangerous situations.

170985.excerpt_en: “As far as I know, there are four boilers of this type left in the world. You have two here, there is one in South Africa, and one is on display in a museum in England,” says Henrik Hansen.
170985.subtitle_en: Full-scale maintenance is under way during the Power Station’s summer shutdown. Planning is also under way, as some parts must be ordered up to a year in advance.
170985.title_en: Busy at the Power Station, even when operations are halted

170992.excerpt_en: “My husband wasn’t home, so I went down to one of the snowmobile dealers. I got to try a used one for ten minutes, and then I tried a brand-new one.”
170992.subtitle_en: When she arrived, she was afraid of becoming lonely. Instead, Sølvi Hole has truly learned to appreciate Svalbard.
170992.title_en: When Sølvi retired, she moved to Svalbard and bought a snowmobile

171010.excerpt_en: Arne Gunhildsberget, construction manager at LNS Spitsbergen, nominated the young carpenter. “Andreas is a thoroughly exuberant person who carries out his work with enthusiasm and spreads good cheer around him,” Gunhildsberget says. Andreas has worked as a formwork carpenter at LNS Spitsbergen since 2013.
171010.subtitle_en: Andreas Grøtting Karlsen, 27, always has a smile ready. He has been nominated for the title of “the country’s nicest tradesperson.”
171010.title_en: Could win the title of “Norway’s nicest tradesperson”

171012.excerpt_en: The Governor states this on its website. Hunting season begins in Svalbard at midnight on Wednesday, and many have probably wondered what consequences the confirmed rabies outbreak would have.
171012.subtitle_en: Despite a rabies outbreak in Svalbard, the reindeer hunt will go ahead. However, there are some changes compared with previous years.
171012.tags_en: reindeer hunting, Svalbard reindeer, news, hunting, reindeer

171035.excerpt_en: The pictures we received were sent by Karine Hauan, operations engineer with Longyearbyen Local Council. She praises the effort made to improve the surroundings. “A full 56 young people turned up and cleaned when we held our clean-up day right at the end of June.”
171035.subtitle_en: More than 35 tonnes of waste have been cleared from urban areas over the summer.

171063.excerpt_en: “Suddenly a wave six or seven metres high came at us. It was like a house coming towards us.”
171063.subtitle_en: House-high waves destroyed the researchers’ sailboat. Now they are left without a vessel and acknowledge that the operation has gone down the drain.
171063.tags_en: distress at sea, boat, news, shipwreck
171063.title_en: Six- to seven-metre waves wrecked the boat and left Simone without a vessel

171066.excerpt_en: The Arctic fox found dead at Vindodden in early August has now been fully tested by the Norwegian Veterinary Institute. The samples showed that the fox did not have rabies, according to the Governor’s website.
171066.subtitle_en: Five foxes were recently tested for rabies after being found dead; none tested positive for the disease.
171066.title_en: Rabies test results back for dead Arctic fox

171081.excerpt_en: This winter, a rabid fox was put down on Hopen after attacking the dogs there. A new case was detected in a female reindeer in Ny-Ålesund this summer.
171081.subtitle_en: All alarm bells start ringing when rabies is detected in Svalbard once again.

171098.excerpt_en: “I have been interested in flowers since I was little. My mother was a gardener, and I trained as a landscape architect at the Ås Agricultural College,” says Olav Tveitnes, 67.
171098.subtitle_en: An interest in flowers and trips to Svalbard have resulted in a guide to 55 different species.

171129.excerpt_en: “We are really looking forward to getting started, but we are working night and day now,” says Kristofer Hedman, listed as general manager of Xarctic. The travel company was established last year and therefore has only one winter season behind it.
171129.subtitle_en: The company is launching boat tours to Svea with MS “Vargen”. Guests will be taken there for weekend trips.
171129.title_en: The boat caught fire and began taking on water—now it will carry mining tourists

171136.excerpt_en: For many, Svea will probably become more accessible in the future. That need not be a problem, but Morten Wedege, the Governor’s environmental chief, points out that this could lead more people to venture even farther from Longyearbyen.
171136.subtitle_en: The Governor’s environmental chief does not want people to use Svea as a starting point for travelling farther into Svalbard’s untouched wilderness.
171136.title_en: Environmental chief does not want Svea to become a “tourist hub”

171161.excerpt_en: He and his wife, Marianne Westby, felt it was time to do something different after living and working in the same district all their lives. “I was born and raised in Oslo and have barely been outside the district. The world is bigger than Ullern and Røa,” he says.
171161.subtitle_en: Frode Westby Thorstad (43) is the new principal of Longyearbyen School. Almost the entire leadership team is new this year as well.
171161.title_en: Almost an entirely new leadership team this autumn

171179.excerpt_en: Last year, the very first literature festival was launched in cooperation with NRK. Library director Elin Anita Olsrud was not entirely sure it would become an annual festival.
171179.subtitle_en: A substantial joint effort has made it possible to continue last year’s major literary initiative. This year’s guests include Erlend Loe and Jan Erik Vold.
171179.title_en: Ready to roll out the literary greats of the year

171200.excerpt_en: Siw did not attend kindergarten like most other children. She preferred the workshop, the garage and wherever the boys spent time. “We jumped from ice floe to ice floe during the spring thaw.”
171200.subtitle_en: Siw Landro (58) was born and raised in Svalbard. As a child, she preferred spending time with the boys.

171214.excerpt_en: The new homes Statsbygg is to erect in Gruvedalen will be assembled from prefabricated modular buildings from Skanska Husfabrikk in Steinkjer. The modules are now being shipped from the quay and will arrive in Longyearbyen during the first week of September, Statsbygg reports.
171214.subtitle_en: The steel frames for the new homes in Gruvedalen are ready to receive modules next week.

171221.excerpt_en: It was no ordinary mountain hike that awaited those who gathered in the square on Saturday morning. They had to cover 42 kilometres, along with plenty of elevation gain.
171221.subtitle_en: Despite the dreary weather, 14 people turned up for Svalbard Turn’s summit challenge.
171221.title_en: Peder (15) and Daniel (15) spent 12 hours on the mountain hike

171237.excerpt_en: On Tuesday evening, police stopped two young people on a moped. “It is not legal to ride together on that type of moped, and the moped was also deregistered,” chief inspector Kjell Arne Lundin of the Governor of Svalbard’s office told Svalbardposten. The passenger limit was not the only thing wrong with the moped.
171237.subtitle_en: Two teenagers were riding a moped illegally.
171237.title_en: Stopped two teenagers on one moped – police found several violations

171242.excerpt_en: It is Monday morning, and after a long, quiet summer everything is apparently back to normal. At around eight o’clock, the streets echo with children either cycling or walking to their first day of school.
171242.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten spoke to two third-graders and two second-graders. They were all looking forward to maths lessons in the new school year.
171242.tags_en: news, Longyearbyen School, first day of school
171242.title_en: Looking forward to a new school year and fun maths

171267.excerpt_en: The overseas cruise tourists no longer fill the streets. More and more permanent residents can be seen in the shops and cafés; summer is definitely coming to an end.
171267.subtitle_en: Little by little, calm is settling over the town again. Svalbard’s nature is donning its finest autumn colours, and the midnight sun is sending its final greeting over the town this week.

171296.excerpt_en: Ronny Brunvoll has headed Visit Svalbard for six years. He has now resigned and will work for Mimir AS from the New Year, a company that provides advisory services to private businesses, attractions and destinations.
171296.subtitle_en: The head of Visit Svalbard will have an office in Svolvær.

171315.excerpt_en: Rijpfjorden is a unique place. On the 4th.
171315.subtitle_en: Researchers have observed major changes in Rijpfjorden since 2006. During that period, winter ice cover has fallen from 200 to 20 days.
171315.title_en: A unique place of great importance to our understanding of the Arctic

171346.excerpt_en: People flock to famous galleries all over the world. What about a “House of Art in Svalbard”?
171346.subtitle_en: More “local tourism” is wanted in Svalbard. Longyearbyen’s Progress Party proposes building a House of Art!
171346.title_en: A house of art in Longyearbyen!

171379.excerpt_en: “I’ve been looking forward to this for a whole year. It was a wonderful way to celebrate my birthday,” says Trine Skogvang just after crossing the finish line at Svalsat.
171379.subtitle_en: When she turned 35, Trine Skogvang chose to run 8.5 kilometres with 400 metres of elevation gain.
171379.tags_en: Svalbard Spacerun, Spacerun, Svalbard Turn, news, sport
171379.title_en: Trine (35) chose a rather different birthday celebration

171396.excerpt_en: “We were trying to determine when Femmilsjøen became a separate lake rather than part of the fjord, when we discovered that the lake is 110 metres deep. It was very surprising how deep it was,” says PhD student and climate researcher Lis Allaart.
171396.subtitle_en: Glacier detective Lis Allaart has begun a new investigation in Svalbard. So far, one finding has been what is probably the deepest lake here.
171396.title_en: “Glacier detective” Lis (29) probably discovered Svalbard’s deepest lake

171403.excerpt_en: This autumn, he will leave both us and the great cathedral up here that nature is to him. Inside this “cathedral” stands Svalbard Church, his meeting place with us.
171403.subtitle_en: Waling Gorter thanks parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen for 12 years of service in Svalbard and wishes him luck in his new job as an itinerant priest in Southeast Asia.
171403.title_en: A monument to Leif Magne Helgesen!

171409.excerpt_en: Lene arrived here for the first time on 26 June and immediately started work as manager of the town’s only hair salon, Saxifraga.
171409.subtitle_en: Lene Koskamo-Kristiansen (34) put her cats in foster care and travelled to Longyearbyen straight from one of Oslo’s trendy hair salons in Grünerløkka.

171418.excerpt_en: This year’s Svalbard Spacerun was the third edition, and organiser Svalbard Turn was very pleased with how it went, even though conditions at the summit were two degrees and windy. “We’re very pleased, and delighted that KSAT is willing to let us organise this up here.”
171418.subtitle_en: Just under 60 participants lined up for the Svalbard Spacerun.
171418.title_en: See everyone who completed the “space race”

171422.excerpt_en: This week’s historical picture was taken in the summer of 1974 and was loaned by Pål Skaare. He says the background to the picture is that Store Norske hired Rover Scouts for a clean-up project in Longyearbyen.
171422.title_en: “Cruise” here was popular in the summer of 1974

171454.excerpt_en: The number of person-years worked in Svalbard is rising, despite a marked decline in mining, according to new figures from Statistics Norway (SSB). From 2016 to 2017, the number of person-years worked increased by four per cent.
171454.subtitle_en: Many believed that scaling down coal mining in Svalbard would mean fewer jobs. Statistics Norway figures show that did not happen.

171465.excerpt_en: “We believe 2018 will be even better than last year, so development has been solid,” says Vebjørn Andresen, acting destination manager at Hurtigruten Svalbard. Continued growth in tourism is clearly reflected in the figures of Longyearbyen’s major operators.
171465.subtitle_en: In 2014, Hurtigruten Svalbard had revenues of just under NOK 185 million; last year, the figure passed NOK 294 million.
171465.title_en: Rakes in hundreds of millions a year from tourism

171505.excerpt_en: “This evening’s last flight has been cancelled because there is standing water on the runway and heavy precipitation is expected,” says state meteorologist Ine-Therese Pedersen from Avinor’s control tower in Longyearbyen. She says an estimated five millimetres of precipitation has fallen so far today.
171505.subtitle_en: In Ny-Ålesund, the airport is closed due to precipitation, while a road in Longyearbyen is closed to all traffic.
171505.title_en: Flight cancelled – airport closed due to precipitation

171508.excerpt_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard is rapidly increasing its turnover in Longyearbyen and has become a major and important player in tourism. From 2014 to 2017, its turnover rose from NOK 185 million to NOK 294 million—more than NOK 100 million in four years.
171508.subtitle_en: We want to see more selfless contributions from Hurtigruten that do not generate money for the coffers, but can instead strengthen the community and solidarity in the town.

171511.excerpt_en: “This was hard,” says Einar Meland (11), sinking onto a bench in the satellite station at the top of Svalsat. He has just completed the third Svalbard Spacerun, admittedly in the untimed category.
171511.subtitle_en: The race director said yes, and so it was done. He powered ahead and was the first recreational runner across the finish line.
171511.title_en: Einar (11) Was Allowed to Race His Mum

171533.excerpt_en: Work has been under way on the mountainside above Lia for many weeks. The job involves laying the foundations for the five-metre-high support structures, which will be installed in three rows covering a total of 460 metres.
171533.subtitle_en: Five-metre-high support structures will be erected in Lia in September. The demolition of 140–150 housing units will take place next year.
171533.title_en: No Demolition of Buildings before Next Year

171553.excerpt_en: Technical director Kjersti Olsen Ingerø says there is currently no money in the budgets for a new bridge on Road 503, Melkeveien. “The main road plan includes a road connection there, but no money has been allocated in the budget,” she says.
171553.subtitle_en: The bridge on Melkeveien, from the town centre to Skjæringa, has been demolished. It may be a long time before a new solution is in place.
171553.title_en: It Will Be a Long Time without a Bridge

171574.excerpt_en: Svalbard Turn organises a fair every year to showcase the town’s organisations and activities. This makes it easier for newcomers to find out how to spend their free time.
171574.subtitle_en: Many stopped by Svalbardhallen to find out what activities are available.
171574.title_en: Several Hundred Visit the Activities Fair

171576.excerpt_en: “The kindergartens are generally full after admissions, and we want to create a buffer,” says Kristin Furu Grøtting, a Venstre politician and chair of the Local Council’s Committee for Education, Youth and Culture. She says the Local Council wants full kindergarten coverage in Longyearbyen.
171576.subtitle_en: Full kindergartens should not be a problem parents face when moving to Svalbard.
171576.title_en: They Will Not Leave Children without a Place—Propose a Five-Million-Krone Temporary Nursery

171582.excerpt_en: “It was more luck than good seamanship that got us safely away from the fire.”
171582.subtitle_en: Two members of the crew of the Langøysund have been fined following last year’s fire on 27 July.
171582.title_en: Protests Fines for Crew after Boat Fire

171598.excerpt_en: After two years at NTNU, the three students—Christian Paulsen, Martin Løvaas and Mathias Strand—have come to UNIS for their third year. They will study Arctic geology for two semesters alongside around 40 others in the same field. “We came here to experience something completely different.”
171598.subtitle_en: The three new bachelor’s students already have a clear impression of their new place of study after visiting Svalbardbutikken and the pub.
171598.title_en: “The Milk Is Expensive and the Beer Is Cheap Here”

171629.excerpt_en: Between one and two o’clock on Sunday morning, police went out after receiving a report of a heavily intoxicated person who had fallen asleep in the town centre.
171629.subtitle_en: A man in his 20s spent the night in custody after being arrested on suspicion of drunk driving.

171637.excerpt_en: She moved to Longyearbyen at the end of April. Her husband had got a job as property manager for Longyearbyen Local Council.
171637.subtitle_en: Lisbeth Espenes (65) followed her husband to Svalbard. It was not easy.
171637.title_en: With a Writer in Her Belly

171640.excerpt_en: Inside Vindbukta on the east coast of Rijpfjorden lies Torskevannet. The lake got its name after cod were found there in the 1990s.
171640.subtitle_en: Rijpfjorden holds a unique place not only in the history of how the Haudegen weather station housed the last armed German soldiers at the end of the Second World War. It is also home to a much older and at least equally important history—a story stretching back thousands of years that is still not fully told. This is a story that Torskevannet tells.

171663.excerpt_en: The Wednesday hike has become a familiar and much-loved concept for Longyearbyen residents, but last week it broke all records. “We knew it was a popular trip and thought quite a lot of people would come along.”
171663.subtitle_en: “We have never had numbers like this,” says tour organiser Mona Ada Andersen.
171663.title_en: They Have Never Seen Sign-Ups Like Those for This Trip

171669.excerpt_en: Autumn is here, and winter is approaching. This week’s historical photograph was actually not taken in winter, but in the middle of June 1969.
171669.subtitle_en: An icebound outing from Longyearbyen in June 1968.
171669.title_en: This Photograph Was Taken in June 1969

171686.excerpt_en: The former hospital, which was converted into an apartment complex, was closed in February 2016 after a consultant’s report found that the building was unsafe. The apartment owners have subsequently received nothing for their investments.
171686.subtitle_en: On Monday, 14 January, Nord-Troms District Court will hear a dispute concerning an apartment in the Old Hospital in Longyearbyen.
171686.title_en: First Court Case over the Old Hospital

171695.excerpt_en: The festival week opened on Monday with a literary cruise to Grumant. Authors, musicians, sponsors and guests took part in the trip. “After more than six months of planning, it is wonderful to finally get started.”
171695.subtitle_en: This week is devoted to literature in Longyearbyen. Several well-known authors have travelled to the Arctic.

171726.excerpt_en: Project manager Rainer-Helge Braun and communications director Hege Njaa Aschim, both from Statsbygg, inspected the work being carried out at the seed vault on Monday. “We are doing things we have never done before,” says Aschim. A gigantic freezing plant stands on the site.
171726.subtitle_en: A five-metre-thick plastic ice wall is keeping the ground in place while work in the construction pit proceeds at full speed. Twenty-six concrete elements will form a new watertight access tunnel.
171726.title_en: Massive Freezing Wall to Protect the Seeds

171749.excerpt_en: Although we have only had democracy since 2002, making us the country’s youngest municipality, it is time to adapt the legislation to modern times and, to a large extent, to the rules that apply on the mainland.
171749.subtitle_en: Alcohol legislation in Svalbard is unusual and a holdover from the time when Longyearbyen was a company town. It can produce many strange outcomes.
171749.title_en: It Does Not Have to Be a Banana Republic

171765.excerpt_en: “There has been quite a bit more rain than normal in August,” says state meteorologist Ine-Therese Pedersen, who is based in the control tower at Svalbard Airport. As has been the case every month in recent years, the average temperature was higher than normal for the two preceding months, but there has also been considerable precipitation.
171765.subtitle_en: Do you think it has been wet and grey over the past two months? You are probably right.
171765.title_en: Think It Has Been a Wet Summer?

171767.excerpt_en: “We are seeing more and more cruise tourists during the summer season. Many want to buy a few cans of beer as souvenirs, but they cannot buy them from us or at Nordpolet.”
171767.subtitle_en: Tourists arriving in Svalbard by plane can buy alcohol on land. Those arriving by boat cannot. Many want this changed.
171767.title_en: Only Air Passengers Can Buy Alcohol

171787.excerpt_en: Krisztina Uzonyi (35) from Hungary arrived in Svalbard on Monday and was introduced to the local business community on Thursday morning. Read also: Raking in hundreds of millions a year from tourism. Uzonyi was born in Hungary but moved abroad at an early age.
171787.subtitle_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard has hired a new destination director.

171824.excerpt_en: “We received the report at around seven today and went out by helicopter and boat,” Chief Inspector Irene Welle of the Governor’s Office tells Svalbardposten. In the area around Reveneset, three polar bears were trying to get into one of the cabins.
171824.subtitle_en: On Saturday morning, police went out by helicopter after receiving reports that polar bears were trying to get into a cabin.
171824.title_en: Polar Bear Chased from Cabin; Police Urge People to Stay Away

171839.excerpt_en: “We have confirmed that a power cable was dug through,” said Energy Manager Marianne Hegle. A power cable was severed during drilling for a foundation shortly after 4 p.m.
171839.subtitle_en: Many Longyearbyen residents were without electricity for several hours on Saturday afternoon after an accident at a housing construction site in Gruvedalen.
171839.title_en: Why Parts of Town Lost Power
