The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) has led the work of preparing safety alternatives, with assistance from Skred AS and Icelandic company HNIT.
175097.subtitle_en: The administration of Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) recommends the cheapest safety option for Lia and Vannledningsdalen. It will still be extremely expensive.
175097.title_en: Set to approve extensive safety measures

175099.excerpt_en: “We are very pleased that we can meet the demand for kindergarten places. There will be room for everyone who applied by the deadline for this spring’s main intake,” says Trine Berntsen, head of Polarflokken kindergarten.
175099.subtitle_en: The children at Polarflokken kindergarten will soon have more company. A new section will be ready for use at the end of February.
175099.tags_en: news, kindergarten places, Polarflokken kindergarten, kindergartens

175139.excerpt_en: On Saturday, people in Longyearbyen enjoyed a new performance by Sirkus Svalnardo. Children and young people presented the audience with an atmospheric show from an underwater world, put together by instructors Kaja Swensen and Sara Rønne.
175139.subtitle_en: “It struck me that it would be cool to put on a show with Svalbard underwater.”
175139.title_en: Dana Sofia (11) came up with the idea for the circus

175166.excerpt_en: During a debate on tourism and the future, Conservative politician Kjetil Figenschou called for yet another tourist fee.
175166.subtitle_en: At last week’s Friske fraspark tourism conference, a proposal was made to introduce a new tourist fee that would benefit visitors and residents alike.

175169.excerpt_en: “This is a wonderful tradition that we want to preserve,” says Torunn Sørensen of Svalbard Church. She herself has appeared at the front of the church on several occasions—for example, when she read the Christmas Gospel and sang with Tundradundrene.
175169.subtitle_en: As tradition dictates, Longyearbyen’s cultural community held a Christmas concert at Svalbard Church.
175169.title_en: “Now People Can Feel Christmas Drawing Near”

175184.excerpt_en: “Robert Plant is considered one of the greatest and most influential vocalists in rock history,” says the introduction to the artist’s English Wikipedia page. The 70-year-old is best known as the frontman of the British supergroup Led Zeppelin, which has sold between 200 and 300 million records worldwide.
175184.subtitle_en: Robert Plant is scheduled to give two concerts at the cultural centre in summer 2019.
175184.tags_en: news, Led Zeppelin, Robert Plant, Longyearbyen Cultural Centre
175184.title_en: Rock Legend to Perform in Longyearbyen

175203.excerpt_en: The matter was considered by the Technical Committee (TU) on 4 December and is listed last on the agenda for Monday’s local council meeting.
175203.subtitle_en: At the local council’s final meeting of the year, politicians will among other things choose a solution for avalanche protection in Lia and Vannledningsdalen.
175203.title_en: Interested in How Longyearbyen Will Be Secured?

175207.excerpt_en: “This shows that a major, established player believes in the project—and Longyearbyen Local Council also has great faith in it,” says Rune Bjerkestrand, chair of Arctic Memory.
175207.subtitle_en: The company Arctic Memory is receiving almost NOK 1.7 million for a feasibility study to develop a visitor centre with virtual experiences in Longyearbyen.

175222.excerpt_en: They were probably workers involved in transport. The photograph was taken by Erling J.
175222.subtitle_en: This photograph shows workers being picked up by the new bus in Nybyen in the spring of 1959.
175222.tags_en: Svalbard history, historical photograph, historical, history, Svalbard life
175222.title_en: Workers Picked Up by the New Bus in Nybyen

175241.excerpt_en: After consulting NVE, the Governor of Svalbard decided to evacuate one house in Sverdrupbyen.
175241.subtitle_en: Increased avalanche risk on the western side of Longyeardalen due to weather conditions.

175251.excerpt_en: On Tuesday evening, Sofia Berger (16) lost a team of eight dogs near Jernsenga in Adventdalen. Her father, Johan Berger, posted the following message on Facebook: “Lost an eight-dog team in Adventdalen by Jernsenga; they ran towards town.”
175251.subtitle_en: A team of eight sled dogs had gone missing in Adventdalen.
175251.title_en: The Sled Dogs Have Been Found Safe

175261.excerpt_en: “Since 2015, my political mantra has been that what we did before to protect ourselves against avalanches was not good enough. The protection option chosen by the local council has some obvious consequences, but I consider them acceptable,” local council leader Arild Olsen said from the podium at Monday’s council meeting.
175261.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council’s choice of protection measure for Lia and Vannledningsdalen will have dramatic consequences for the town.
175261.tags_en: avalanche protection, avalanche risk, avalanche, news, NVE, Longyearbyen Local Council, Vannledningsdalen
175261.title_en: Better Safety, but a Worsened Housing Situation

175277.excerpt_en: “If I had not known about it, I would have been surprised when we moved here,” says Ann-Lorin W.-Noor. This summer, she moved to Svalbard with her husband, Odd Rune Noor, and their children Emil, Leo and Prepple Walther-Noor.
175277.subtitle_en: Ann-Lorin W.-Noor and her family came to Svalbard this summer. Since then, their grocery budget has soared. “Fortunately, we were prepared for it.”
175277.title_en: Family’s Food Budget Almost Doubled After Moving to Svalbard

175281.excerpt_en: “Comparing our prices directly with those of a mainland shop is completely misleading,” says Ronny Strømnes, head of Coop Svalbard.
175281.subtitle_en: High freight costs, losses caused by the dry climate and emergency preparedness are cited as reasons why goods are more expensive in Svalbard.
175281.title_en: Transports Goods Worth 18 Million a Year

175294.excerpt_en: Low taxes and zero VAT can quickly be eaten up by high housing and living costs. Many have favourable rents and employer-provided support schemes, but not everyone does.
175294.subtitle_en: As Christmas approaches, people shop more than at other times of year. But filling your grocery basket at 78 degrees north is an expensive pleasure for most people.
175294.title_en: Low Taxes and Zero VAT Can Quickly Be Eaten Up by High Housing and Living Costs

175309.excerpt_en: Did you get a knot in your stomach when you saw all the emergency services rushing out at full speed on Thursday? First of all: You can breathe a sigh of relief.
175309.subtitle_en: It was meant to resemble a plane crash when Svalbard’s emergency crews practised responding to a crisis on Thursday.
175309.title_en: “We Are Still Short Around Twenty People”

175340.excerpt_en: “I don’t understand why so many large dog yards have to be built in such a small area,” says Martin Munck, shaking his head. He is sitting in a common room in one of the houses next to Green Dog’s largest yard in Bolterdalen.
175340.subtitle_en: With distances of as little as 25 metres between the dog yards, Martin Munck believes new yards in Bolterdalen could cause unnecessary problems.
175340.title_en: Fears a New Dog Yard Will Be Built Right Next to His Own

175343.excerpt_en: Under the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act, harvesting Svalbard reindeer must not significantly affect the population. This means hunting must not alter the population’s sex and age composition, size or development over time.
175343.subtitle_en: The former UNIS student leads a project group seeking to create an app to help the Governor of Svalbard allocate hunting permits.
175343.title_en: Bart (28) Wants to Adjust Hunting Permits with a New App

175351.excerpt_en: Svalbard Church was packed when Tine Westby Thorstad (14) stood up. She grabbed the microphone and sang powerfully throughout the hall.
175351.subtitle_en: But the 14-year-old did so with complete confidence at the Christmas concert.
175351.title_en: Tine (14) Had Never Sung a Solo on Stage Before Moving Here

175360.excerpt_en: Now the largest member companies, which own Visit Svalbard through the Svalbard Tourism Council, are taking action and ensuring that additional funds are provided next year. The companies are Coop Svalbard, Hurtigruten Svalbard and Svalbard Adventure Group.
175360.subtitle_en: It recently emerged that Visit Svalbard had to relinquish its Sustainable Destination certification because it failed to secure the necessary funding.
175360.title_en: Hopes Longyearbyen Will Remain a Sustainable Destination

175366.excerpt_en: In Svalbardposten’s Photo Magazine 2018/2019, Leif Magne Helgesen writes about “The Lady in the Ice” (Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik): “It is about bringing joy to others and caring…”. One could also put it this way on a deeply personal level: It is about forgetting oneself.
175366.subtitle_en: Reinhard Mook shares some of his thoughts and wishes for Christmas.

175378.excerpt_en: “We have not found an SMS alert system that is good enough and works in a way we consider satisfactory here in Longyearbyen, where there is a very high turnover.”
175378.subtitle_en: SMS alerts for evacuations in Longyearbyen have been considered, but have not yet been introduced.

175398.excerpt_en: This is done by checking all haul-out sites and photographing and counting the walruses at those currently in use.
175398.subtitle_en: As part of the Environmental Monitoring of Svalbard and Jan Mayen (MOSJ), the Norwegian Polar Institute attempts to estimate how many walruses there are in the Svalbard area every five years.
175398.title_en: Walrus Numbers Continue to Rise in the Svalbard Area

175399.excerpt_en: Local council leader Arild Olsen (Labour) supports the plans. “This could provide many profitable, year-round jobs in Longyearbyen,” he says. Last Monday, the project received almost NOK 1.7 million in funding from SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge through “Samfunnsløftet.”
175399.subtitle_en: The company Arctic Memory is planning a visitor center showcasing the seed vault, lizard finds and treasures from the digital archive in Mine 3.

175405.excerpt_en: Vegard started working as an AFIS officer in the control tower at Svalbard Airport in August. After several months of local training, he is now working a full roster.
175405.subtitle_en: Vegard By (42) is one of six people responsible for staffing the control tower around the clock.

175429.excerpt_en: All transport was by boat from approximately May until November or December. The rest of the year, people were isolated.
175429.subtitle_en: This photograph shows a Kjøde boat leaving Gamlekaia for Norway in 1959.
175429.tags_en: Svalbard history, historical photograph, historical, history, Svalbard life

175438.excerpt_en: “We think a lot about preparedness. We may have to train more here than on the mainland, because we have to allow for being left alone for a while,” says Espen Olsen, senior police officer with the Governor of Svalbard.
175438.subtitle_en: Last week, the emergency services practiced what to do when disaster strikes: a plane on fire and dozens of people missing.
175438.title_en: “We Have to Allow for Being Left Alone for a While”

175461.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) launched an upgraded version of its website. Political secretary Svein Olav Ween is the web editor and led the work on the new site. “The world has moved on since we launched the website a few years ago.”
175461.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) launched a new website on Tuesday.
175461.title_en: Longyearbyen Community Council Gets a New Online Look

175468.excerpt_en: Wednesday’s mail flight, which was due to land at Svalbard Airport this afternoon, has been canceled. Airport director Carl Einar Ianssen confirmed this to Svalbardposten.
175468.subtitle_en: They are counting on two mail flights Thursday to keep up with the Christmas traffic.
175468.title_en: Icy Runway Causes Trouble for Mail Plane

175472.excerpt_en: Although we are far removed from the usual Christmas rush on the mainland, we are entering the Christmas holidays here in Longyearbyen with a different kind of stress and anxiety: concern about the weather and whether there will be evacuations this Christmas.
175472.subtitle_en: “We share the joy of those who can look forward to a safe Christmas in secure homes.”
175472.title_en: “For Some, Snow Is More of a Threat Than a Welcome Sign That Christmas Is Coming”

175500.excerpt_en: After reviewing weather forecasts and consulting NVE, the Governor of Svalbard has lifted the evacuation of a holiday home in Sverdrupbyen. In addition, the Longyearbyen Community Council has lifted the ban on pedestrian traffic on the road between Huset and Museumsveien.
175500.subtitle_en: The avalanche danger has subsided, and people may travel on the road again.

175504.excerpt_en: The contract goes to Hæhre Entreprenør AS, the same company working on the seed vault. “It has been a thorough process, and we are very pleased with the strong interest in taking on the assignment,” says Jan Morten Ertsaas, managing director of Store Norske.
175504.subtitle_en: Store Norske has decided whom to offer the contract to clear the mine at Lunckefjell.
175504.title_en: They Have Decided Who Will Clear the Mine at Lunckefjell

175512.excerpt_en: The new crew on Bear Island arrived aboard KV Svalbard on December 2.
175512.subtitle_en: On Bear Island, the new winter crew has reopened the climbing wall.
175512.title_en: Reaching New Heights on Bear Island

175518.excerpt_en: “The store’s board has focused on prices for a long time, but I will give the issue extra attention at the next board meeting. What I have found so far is that general costs are probably a little too high,” says Arnt Vegar Jensen, chair of Coop Svalbardbutikken.
175518.subtitle_en: The chair of Svalbardbutikken believes prices are too high and says work is under way to lower them.
175518.title_en: Working at Board Level to Reduce Prices

175613.excerpt_en: “Warmly nestled in the night lies the town… Sheltered by high mountains. Row upon row like white temples, built by nature itself.” These are the lines of one of the finest songs ever written about Longyearbyen.
175613.subtitle_en: “It is important to come together around several more serious issues so that the town we care so deeply about can also benefit future generations,” writes Merethe Stiberg in this letter to the editor.
175613.title_en: Polar Nostalgia in the Winter Night

175616.excerpt_en: “Time goes quickly because the days are short,” says the Pole, who first visited Spitsbergen in 1995. He has been here 15 times since.
175616.subtitle_en: Piotr Zagórski has spent 15 summers in Hornsund, but the coming months will be something quite different for the head of the Polish research station.
175616.title_en: For the First Time, Piotr Will Spend the Winter at the Station on the Southern Tip of the Island—Almost Completely Isolated

175641.excerpt_en: “I am incredibly grateful to everyone who helped make this happen,” says Marit. The couple, who normally live in Skien, have been partners for 15 years and have a six-year-old daughter together.
175641.subtitle_en: Marit Ro (36) surprised her partner by joining him on a Christmas visit to Hopen to get married.
175641.title_en: Marit Finally Got Her Tom Erik

175675.excerpt_en: Stig Onarheim (51) was born in Longyearbyen and has lived on Svalbard for a total of 39 years. He has experienced more than most people.
175675.subtitle_en: As a young man, Stig Onarheim got a job as a polar bear guard at Haketangen alongside experienced trapper Odd Ivar Ruud.
175675.title_en: Stig Was a Polar Bear Guard During the Drilling Operation at Haketangen

175679.excerpt_en: We began looking for seals as soon as we arrived at Gråhuken. Although there was no ice in the fjord in July, it was expected that the seals would be sufficiently fat by this time, after a long spring, to float in the sea if we shot one.
175679.subtitle_en: Marit Brandal Karlsen and Steinulf Smith-Meyer got off to a flying start to the seal hunt at Gråhuken. Read more about the couple’s hunting experiences, written by Marit Karlsen Brandal.

175724.excerpt_en: To the sounds of familiar Christmas songs, young and old walked around the Christmas tree at Svalbard Church on Thursday. The mood was relaxed and cheerful, and energy levels were naturally high.
175724.subtitle_en: Christmas is not quite over for young and old. It was marked with a Christmas tree party at Svalbard Church on Thursday.
175724.title_en: “It Was Fun to Get a Present from Santa”

175753.excerpt_en: All fourteen people aboard the stricken vessel have been picked up by the Governor of Svalbard’s rescue helicopters—ten in the first and four in the second.
175753.subtitle_en: Fourteen people were rescued after getting into distress in Hinlopen Strait.
175753.title_en: The Last Crew Members Arrive in Longyearbyen After Rescue Operation

175777.excerpt_en: On Sunday, the Governor of Svalbard provided a helicopter so the Norwegian Coastal Administration could reach Hinlopen to inspect the “Northguider,” which ran aground on Friday. The accident triggered a rescue operation in which both of the Governor’s helicopters were used, and all 14 crew members were evacuated from the ship.
175777.subtitle_en: Watch video of the ship that ran aground in Hinlopen Strait. The video was produced by NRK.
175777.title_en: “The Weather Is the Wild Card in the Rescue Operation”

175818.excerpt_en: Yesterday, 2018 ended with a bang. Or, more precisely, many bangs.
175818.subtitle_en: Police had to respond to an incident at Huset.
175818.title_en: This Is How New Year’s Eve Was Celebrated on Svalbard

175843.excerpt_en: “It was a hectic Christmas this year. The weather gave us some challenges,” says Torunn Sørensen, who has taken a breather before the Christmas tree party when Svalbardposten meets her. “Christmas is busy, but it is busy in a good way.”
175843.subtitle_en: For 11 years, Torunn Sørensen has helped prepare for Christmas at Svalbard Church. In 2018, it became somewhat busier than usual.
175843.title_en: For Torunn, Christmas Is the Busiest Time of Year

175845.excerpt_en: “The Coast Guard arrived during the night, and the stricken vessel is in the same place and has the same list as before,” says Hans Petter Mortensholm of the Norwegian Coastal Administration to Svalbardposten.
175845.subtitle_en: The Coast Guard vessel KV “Svalbard” has reached the “Northguider” in Hinlopen Strait.
175845.title_en: They Have Reached the Stricken Vessel, but Weather Prevents Them from Boarding

175867.excerpt_en: “It was a demanding operation, but we did not experience it as dangerous,” says rescuer Tor Helge Edorsen. He was called out as the second rescue helicopter when the alarm went off at 1:34 p.m. on the fourth day of Christmas.
175867.subtitle_en: A demanding rescue operation was required when 14 people found themselves in distress at sea in Hinlopen Strait. Tor Helge Edorsen and the Lufttransport rescuers had to come to their aid.
175867.title_en: Tor Helge Had to Rescue Fishermen in Gale-Force Winds and Bitter Cold

175896.excerpt_en: Morten Wedege, the Governor of Svalbard’s environmental protection chief, hopes the Norwegian Coastal Administration can remove all the pollution as quickly and carefully as possible. The Coastal Administration is leading the salvage operation, with assistance from the Governor’s office.
175896.subtitle_en: The stricken fishing boat “Northguider” is located in a vulnerable area of Hinlopen Strait. A major diesel spill could cause extensive damage in the protected area.

175911.excerpt_en: This year’s Svalbard Seminar will be held for the 24th time from mid-January.
175911.subtitle_en: Are you new to town and need information about safety on trips, or are you interested in hearing about drone use or rabies? Then you should attend the Svalbard Seminar.
175911.title_en: Learn Something You Didn’t Know Before

175918.excerpt_en: On Friday, the fourth day of Christmas, the shrimp trawler “Northguider” ran aground in Hinlopen Strait in the far north of Svalbard. Fourteen people were rescued by rescue helicopter, and efforts to save the vessel are continuing.
175918.subtitle_en: The Coast Guard vessel KV “Svalbard” has completed the first part of the work in Hinlopen Strait.

175926.excerpt_en: On Christmas Day, the alarm went off at the Governor’s office. They received a report from a snowmobile group that a major avalanche had occurred in Gangskaret, between Gangdalen and Fritham.
175926.subtitle_en: A major avalanche between Fritham and Gangdalen meant that all the town’s emergency services had to respond.
175926.title_en: Picked Up from Christmas Trip by Helicopter

175935.excerpt_en: The ice on Woodfjorden had been unstable in February. One day it could fill the entire fjord, only to drift rapidly out of the fjord northwards the next.
175935.subtitle_en: Read Marit Karlsen Brandal’s story of how she and her husband spent the winter at Gråhuken.

175960.excerpt_en: Author Kari Holm has recently published the fourth edition of Svalbard’s Who’s Who, What’s What and Where. The first edition was published in 1990.
175960.subtitle_en: Kari Holm keeps track of most things that happen and have happened in Svalbard. She has also documented them diligently. Historical Guide is a useful reference work used by many.

175962.excerpt_en: There has been snowfall in recent days, and strong winds were forecast in Longyearbyen on Sunday. The Governor, the emergency preparedness council, the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate and Skred AS have therefore assessed the avalanche danger in the town.
175962.subtitle_en: For the time being, no one will be evacuated from Lia or Nybyen.

175970.excerpt_en: Bjørn Egil was 20 when he obtained his vocational certificate as an event manager. For many years he worked for the family business Pan Norway, which brought wealthy European clients to Norway. “I loved my job, but the pace was high and the responsibility for major contracts was considerable.”
175970.subtitle_en: Bjørn Egil Strathmann (34) gained an entirely new perspective on life after moving to Longyearbyen.
175970.title_en: The Simple Life Has Done Him Good

175985.excerpt_en: “The plaintiffs claim that the subsidence damage which led to the evacuation of the Old Hospital was already there before the transfer. We do not believe that.”
175985.subtitle_en: Counsel Miriam Fagerli Bors claims the subsidence damage for which her client is being sued occurred in recent years.
175985.title_en: Believes Building Damage Occurred in Recent Years

175987.excerpt_en: The trial began at nine o’clock on Monday morning in Tromsø. Brothers Sam and Avaz Ziaei, who own several of the apartments in the Old Hospital, are suing Roy Albrigtsen.
175987.subtitle_en: Lawyer Siri Barfod’s extract on the Old Hospital is around 600 pages long. In her opening statement, she referred, among other things, to a 1991 report from the Labour Inspection Authority ordering the building to be vacated because of its condition.
175987.title_en: “The Old Hospital Was Considered Unsafe as Early as 1991”

175999.excerpt_en: Everything we humans do involves the risk of not succeeding. That also applies to fishing in midwinter at 80 degrees north.
175999.subtitle_en: Reinhardt Mook on the shipwreck in Hinlopen Strait

176015.excerpt_en: Strong winds are forecast in Longyearbyen on Thursday, and the Governor has now warned the town’s residents. “The Norwegian Meteorological Institute has issued a warning of extreme gusts of 45 m/s for Nordenskiöld Land.”
176015.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard urges people to monitor the weather forecasts.
176015.title_en: Extreme Gusts Warned—May Reach 45 Metres per Second

176023.excerpt_en: Keeping the ground beneath the building cold was a prerequisite for ensuring its stability. Defendant Roy Albrigtsen finds it strange that the Ziaei brothers did not know about the cooling system. “Everyone knew—the Old Hospital stood solidly; there was no sign of subsidence or anything.”
176023.subtitle_en: Roy Albrigtsen is certain that the cooling system at the Old Hospital was working properly when he sold his stake in 2009.
176023.title_en: Roy: “The Cooling System Was in Order”

176028.excerpt_en: “I never heard anything about a cooling system at any point. Albrigtsen never said anything like that to me,” Ziaei began, responding to questions from his lawyer, Siri Barfod.
176028.subtitle_en: The District Court of Nord-Troms heard a heartbreaking testimony from plaintiff Sam Ziaei.

176042.excerpt_en: Severe weather is forecast for Longyearbyen on Thursday, and LL has now decided that the school, after-school programme and school of music and arts will remain closed from Thursday morning. They write that if the weather forecasts change significantly, the school will open as normal, and further information will be issued continuously.
176042.subtitle_en: This is reported by Longyearbyen Local Council on its website.
176042.title_en: Winds of 45 Metres per Second Expected—School to Close

176045.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has imposed a ban on travel and staying in Lia and Nybyen following a meeting of the emergency preparedness council this afternoon. “We ask people to find a safe place to stay and remain there until the weather has passed,” says Governor Kjerstin Askholt.
176045.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council is evacuating 29 housing units in Lia below Sukkertoppen and 81 students living in Nybyen.
176045.title_en: More Than 100 Evacuated After Storm Warning

176060.excerpt_en: Barfod spent three hours on her opening statement in court on Monday, presenting a wealth of information she had gathered from documents unearthed in the building’s history. With an extract of around 600 pages, there was a lot to leaf through.
176060.subtitle_en: Lawyer Siri Barfod is not sure whether the Old Hospital was completely renovated by Roy Albrigtsen and his associates in the late 1990s, as has been claimed.

176072.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has decided to evacuate homes at Vei 228 and the residential barracks on the upper side of the road in Nybyen. Travel and stay bans will also be introduced in these areas.
176072.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has imposed a travel and stay ban in Lia and Nybyen from Thursday morning.
176072.title_en: Parts of Lia and Nybyen closed to all traffic

176075.excerpt_en: In the wake of Northguider running aground far north in Hinlopen Strait during the Christmas holidays, debate about increased preparedness has flared up. This is partly because Polarsyssel, the Governor of Svalbard’s main vessel at sea, has only nine months of operational availability on Svalbard.
176075.subtitle_en: Several people are calling for increased winter preparedness. The Minister of Justice points out that preparedness has been strengthened in recent years.
176075.title_en: Calls for a boat to be on standby on Svalbard year-round

176078.excerpt_en: “We are a little worried about the weather, especially the strong gusts. It will be exciting to see whether the infrastructure holds,” says student Fredrik Olaussen, 23.
176078.subtitle_en: He and the other students are now in safe accommodation until the forecast severe storm has passed.
176078.title_en: Fredrik evacuated after three days on Svalbard

176097.excerpt_en: This is what Longyearbyen looks like right now. The storm is expected to strengthen throughout the day.
176097.subtitle_en: We are broadcasting live from the bad weather.
176097.title_en: The wind is picking up—and will continue to do so

176102.excerpt_en: Most of Svalbard has closed today following a storm warning. This applies to shops, eateries and other services.
176102.subtitle_en: So far, the worst weather has yet to arrive.
176102.title_en: Almost the entire town closed because of the storm

176137.excerpt_en: “We welcome everyone back to school, kindergarten, after-school care and the cultural school. Shortly after 8 p.m., the Norwegian Meteorological Institute reported that the worst of the wind had passed Longyearbyen.”
176137.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council announced Thursday evening that all its services will open at the usual time on Friday.
176137.title_en: School, kindergarten and after-school care operating as usual Friday

176139.excerpt_en: Today, the Governor of Svalbard met with the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) and Skred AS, which have examined the mountain slopes in the evacuation area.
176139.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is lifting the evacuation and travel ban from 3 p.m. Friday. The more than 100 people evacuated from their homes on Thursday can now return home.
176139.title_en: Can return home for the weekend

176143.excerpt_en: The energy situation in Longyearbyen and future energy solutions have been debated at length. The debate will not die down anytime soon.
176143.subtitle_en: Energy efficiency and ENØK measures have not been given priority so far.

176148.excerpt_en: “The first operation was successful. Preparations are now complete for emptying the boat of diesel,” says Rune Bergstrøm, duty officer with the Norwegian Coastal Administration.
176148.subtitle_en: The salvage operation for Northguider is, as expected, challenging in harsh Arctic conditions.
176148.title_en: Expects a lengthy operation to remove 300,000 litres of diesel

176159.excerpt_en: “We are trying to be innovative and environmentally friendly. So we wanted a different solution from district heating,” says Trond Håvelsrud, owner of Svalbard Bygg, to Svalbardposten.
176159.subtitle_en: Svalbard Bygg sought environmentally friendly solutions for its new premises. Nevertheless, it must connect to the district-heating system. That will not stop the company.
176159.tags_en: energy, Svalbard Bygg, power, energy supply, news
176159.title_en: Self-sufficient for heat, yet still has to pay 150,000 for district heating

176186.excerpt_en: Norway’s emergency preparedness system is responsible for extremely demanding maritime and land areas in the north. This was highlighted by two major rescue operations over the past week: one in Hinlopen Strait on Svalbard and the other in inner Troms.
176186.subtitle_en: Professor Odd Jarl Borch of Nord University and UiT The Arctic University of Norway raises several questions about preparedness in the north in light of recent events in Troms and on Svalbard.
176186.title_en: Norway—a preparedness superpower in the north?

176215.excerpt_en: When the trawler Northguider ran aground in Hinlopen Strait, the crew fortunately escaped unharmed. This was largely thanks to the efforts of the crews aboard our two rescue helicopters.
176215.subtitle_en: Activity in the north is increasing, making Longyearbyen a necessary hub for search and rescue. But the margin between success and failure is small.
176215.title_en: The local council leader on preparedness, security and society in the Arctic

176223.excerpt_en: “The first thing I noticed when I arrived on Svalbard was how warm the community here is. No one frowned upon me being Syrian or Muslim.”
176223.subtitle_en: Mouawia Lababidi was the first Syrian at the North Pole. Now the hotel manager is leaving Svalbard and moving to the mainland.
176223.title_en: “Mimo” becomes the first Syrian at the North Pole: “It was a fantastic feeling”

176245.excerpt_en: “It is unique to do this under such extreme conditions. As far as I know, nothing similar has ever been done,” says Rune Bergstrøm, senior adviser in the Norwegian Coastal Administration’s emergency preparedness department.
176245.subtitle_en: The Northguider has been emptied of everything that could harm the environment. The Norwegian Coastal Administration praises the rescue operation carried out.
176245.title_en: “A completely unique operation in extreme conditions”

176254.excerpt_en: We will see more extreme weather in the future, along with more precipitation. Much has changed since the avalanche in Lia in 2015 claimed two lives.
176254.subtitle_en: Was it all much ado about nothing?
176254.title_en: “19 December 2015 is, and will remain, a watershed”

176269.excerpt_en: The prestigious award was presented to Svalbard Fangst and Tank Design last Thursday afternoon at DOGA Day 2019 in Oslo. “The DOGA Award highlights the best projects where design and architecture have contributed to innovation and value creation.”
176269.subtitle_en: Svalbard Fangst has received the DOGA Award for excellent design.
176269.title_en: The family behind Svalbard Fangst wins design award

176275.excerpt_en: “I got a call telling me I should return to Svalbard because things at the shop did not add up,” says Stig Kristiansen, owner and general manager of Sportscenteret in Longyearbyen, one of the town’s five sports shops.
176275.subtitle_en: Stig Kristiansen has run a sports shop in Longyearbyen since 1995. Seven years ago, the whole business nearly collapsed.
176275.title_en: Three weeks from bankruptcy after fraud—now they have millions in revenue

176289.excerpt_en: “Tourists are absolutely crucial to our shops,” says Gry Sneltvedt, owner and general manager of Sport1 Svalbard. She has worked in retail on Svalbard for many years and has seen how tourism affects the shop.
176289.subtitle_en: All five of Svalbard’s sports shops are making healthy profits. They can probably thank tourism for a large part of that.

176303.excerpt_en: Polarjazz 2019 is just weeks away. It is 22.
176303.subtitle_en: Polarjazz is back at the end of January. This year, several concerts will offer a choice between standing and seated tickets.
176303.title_en: Now you can get a seat at standing concerts

176309.excerpt_en: But on Tuesday, 8 January, the children in Polargospel finally got to celebrate Russian Orthodox Christmas with the children in Barentsburg.
176309.subtitle_en: Svalbard Church and Polargospel had to postpone their trip to Barentsburg because of bad weather.

176313.excerpt_en: As the Governor of Svalbard’s helicopter operator, we are somewhat surprised to note that Professor Odd Jarl Borch claims, quote: “It also revealed capacity limitations in the existing search-and-rescue and oil-spill preparedness on Svalbard.” End quote.
176313.subtitle_en: Comment on Odd Jarle Borch’s opinion piece in Svalbardposten on 12 January 2019: Norway—a preparedness superpower in the north.
176313.title_en: Geir-Arne Sørensen responds to Odd Jarle Borch

176329.excerpt_en: On 28 December, the trawler Northguider ran aground at Sperreneset in Hinlopenstretet.
176329.subtitle_en: The shipowner and crew of Northguider thank Longyearbyen.

176342.excerpt_en: Seventy-eight people took part with the Coast Guard, 55 of them members of KV Svalbard’s own crew. On Friday they unloaded all the equipment used to empty the vessel of environmentally hazardous waste.
176342.subtitle_en: KV Svalbard arrived in Longyearbyen on Friday morning after a successful operation in Hinlopenstretet, where it emptied the wrecked vessel of oil, diesel and other equipment.
176342.title_en: Unloaded diesel from KV Svalbard in Longyearbyen

176350.excerpt_en: On the evening of Wednesday, 16 January, police received a report of an injured reindeer between Vei 226 and Hilmar Rekstens vei.
176350.subtitle_en: An injured reindeer had to be euthanized.
176350.title_en: Had to put down reindeer in the middle of town

176363.excerpt_en: But rockfalls and avalanches, gales and cold can pose threats on the mainland too, as can other natural hazards in other parts of the world. Acting in relation to nature entails risk.
176363.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s Arctic nature demands respect from its people.

176377.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Justice and Public Security will have two ministers. Minister Ingvil Smines Tybring-Gjedde becomes Minister of Civil Security and will be responsible for societal and ICT security and emergency preparedness, including crisis management and security governance in the justice sector.
176377.subtitle_en: Tybring-Gjedde becomes Minister of Civil Security in the Ministry of Justice and Public Security.
176377.title_en: Ingvill Smines Tybring-Gjedde becomes the new Svalbard minister

176379.excerpt_en: The signing took place in the boardroom at Funken Lodge. “We are very pleased that Store Norske chose us for this job,” says Gudmund Roen, managing director of Hæhre Entreprenør.
176379.subtitle_en: On Monday evening, Store Norske and contractor Hæhre signed an NOK 85 million contract to decommission and restore Lunckefjell.
176379.title_en: Signed a contract worth NOK 85 million

176385.excerpt_en: On Friday they received permission to start work, and by Saturday they had already begun driving piles for the lift. Within a few weeks, the 140-metre-long ski slope should be ready for use.
176385.subtitle_en: After seven years of waiting, there will be an alpine ski slope behind the pointed-roof houses this winter.
176385.title_en: Finally, an alpine ski slope again after a major volunteer effort

176393.excerpt_en: Five women and six men have applied for the position of parish priest in Svalbard. Leif Magne Helgesen left the post after 12 years in October last year.
176393.subtitle_en: Gitte Bergstuen, 51, is one of the applicants for the priest’s position in Svalbard. She has served as a substitute at the church for two summers.
176393.title_en: Eleven apply to become parish priest in Svalbard

176415.excerpt_en: “This has worked incredibly well. It has been a great collaboration between everyone involved in the operation, and we have had a shipowner who truly stepped up.”
176415.subtitle_en: Governor Kjerstin Askholt is deeply impressed following the emergency offloading operation involving the shrimp trawler Northguider, which ran aground in Hinlopenstretet on 28 December.

176425.excerpt_en: Less sea ice and warmer seas are changing life in the ocean. This is also causing the fishing fleet to move farther north.
176425.subtitle_en: The grounding of the shrimp trawler Northguider in the Hinlopenstretet nature reserve raises several questions.

176435.excerpt_en: Svalbard Turn, which organizes the Svalbard Ski Marathon, has not reached a final decision. But everything suggests this year’s ski race will not start from Todalen, as it has in recent years.
176435.subtitle_en: Heidi Harviken is taking over as race director for the Svalbard Ski Marathon from Sigvart Bjøntegård.
176435.title_en: Experienced skier takes over as race director

176440.excerpt_en: The company is taking over the warning contract for the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE). Skred AS’s very first assignment came during a start-up meeting with Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) and NVE.
176440.subtitle_en: The consultancy Skred AS took over the avalanche-warning contract for Longyearbyen Local Council at the beginning of January.
176440.title_en: Skred AS takes over avalanche observations

176471.excerpt_en: The civil case was heard in Nord-Troms District Court on 7–8 January.
176471.subtitle_en: Roy Albrigtsen was acquitted in Nord-Troms District Court following a lawsuit brought by brothers Sam and Avaz Ziai. The brothers must pay Albrigtsen nearly NOK 400,000 in legal costs.
176471.title_en: The brothers lost the lawsuit over the Old Hospital

176477.excerpt_en: Following the grounding of the Northguider in Hinlopenstretet just before New Year, emergency preparedness in the northern regions has been debated. Preparedness was also a topic a year ago.
176477.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Meteorological Institute proposes joint operations with other parties to retain personnel on Hopen and Bjørnøya. The matter is still with the ministry.
176477.title_en: Should Hopen and Bjørnøya be staffed?

176491.excerpt_en: While the children run back and forth and some have taken refuge on their mothers’ or fathers’ laps, conversation flows around the tables. Mostly in Norwegian, but also in English.
176491.subtitle_en: Parents, children and staff enjoyed food and conversation from many countries at Kullungen kindergarten on Thursday afternoon.

176513.excerpt_en: We have collected hydrographic and plankton samples here as often as once a week since December 2011.
176513.subtitle_en: UNIS takes the temperature of Isfjorden—more specifically, Adventfjorden—every month throughout the year.
176513.title_en: There probably won’t be ice on Isfjorden this year either

176542.excerpt_en: The Russian Consulate General informs Svalbardposten in an email. Gushchin takes over as Russia’s highest-ranking representative in Svalbard from Viacheslav G.
176542.subtitle_en: Sergei Sergeievich Gushchin has been appointed Russia’s new consul general in Barentsburg.
176542.title_en: Sergei is the new consul general in Barentsburg

176544.excerpt_en: While preparing a new research strategy for Ny-Ålesund, the Research Council has received surprisingly harsh criticism from China. The world’s most populous country is present in Ny-Ålesund and is one of several countries that have submitted comments on the new strategy.
176544.tags_en: Ny-Ålesund, Research Council, research, news, Norwegian Polar Institute
176544.title_en: Chinese criticism of the Research Council

176580.excerpt_en: Solberg received a call from some parents on Tuesday this week. The school then sent a message to all parents and guardians.
176580.subtitle_en: “It’s actually been a while now,” says the school secretary, Karina Solberg.
176580.tags_en: school, health, children, parents of young children, news
176580.title_en: A tiny bug sparks a major community effort

176598.excerpt_en: Five women and six men have applied for the position of parish priest in Svalbard. Leif Magne Helgesen left the position after 12 years in October last year.
176598.subtitle_en: Bjørn Christian Hagen, head of personnel in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland, says few priest positions attract as many applicants as Svalbard Church.

176617.excerpt_en: Sam and Avaz Ziaei were pleased but nervous when they left the courtroom in Tromsø a couple of weeks ago.
176617.subtitle_en: The Ziaei brothers were flatly rejected by the district court when they tried to rescind the purchase of four apartments in the Old Hospital in 2009. But they are not giving up and have announced an appeal.
176617.title_en: Appeals crushing verdict over poor housing purchase

176620.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority in Northern Norway, the Svalbard Tax Office and the Governor of Svalbard conducted a joint inspection this week of Hurtigruten Svalbard’s renovation project at the Radisson hotel in Longyearbyen. A series of violations was uncovered during the inspection.
176620.subtitle_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard’s renovation project at the Polar Hotel comes under criticism.
176620.tags_en: Polar Hotel, Radisson, Labour Inspection Authority, news

176636.excerpt_en: Coop Svalbard could lose its daily fresh produce, as well as its fresh fish offering on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Posten is reducing weekly postal flights from five to four and is also moving the flights to later in the afternoon.
176636.subtitle_en: Coop Svalbard has been in dialogue with Posten throughout 2018 about changes to air transport to Longyearbyen. They were not heard.
176636.title_en: “They are depriving people in town of fresh daily produce”

176663.excerpt_en: Slowly but surely, the town is beginning to wake up again after a long, dark night. Along with Polarjazz comes the blue light.
176663.subtitle_en: Reducing mail delivery would lead to poorer healthcare and thereby weaken part of the emergency preparedness.

176669.excerpt_en: “There are 110 applicants for the various positions. Those are very good numbers, we think.”
176669.subtitle_en: Espen Klungseth Rotevatn, principal of Svalbard Folk High School, is very pleased with the number of applicants for positions at the new folk high school.
176669.title_en: 110 want to work at the folk high school

176675.excerpt_en: Many chose to spend Friday evening curled up on a sofa or sitting in an armchair watching a French film. The film shown was Jean-Luc Godard’s “Breathless.”
176675.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Film Club has acquired a film screen. On Friday, a film screening was held at Huset.
176675.title_en: French film on a Friday evening

176677.excerpt_en: When Pål Remen and Linda Vassdal declined to spend a second year at the Austfjordnes trapping station a year ago, the Governor of Svalbard decided to take a year off to assess the station’s condition.
176677.subtitle_en: There will be no trapping at Austfjordnes next season, as the summer and autumn will be devoted to repairs.
176677.title_en: Austfjordnes on hold for another year

176685.excerpt_en: The statistics show that the number of fire call-outs has risen sharply since 2008. The fewest call-outs during the ten-year period occurred in 2012, with 131.
176685.subtitle_en: There were 191 fire call-outs in 2018, four more than the previous year. Boiling pans dry overnight are once again among the worst offenders.

176699.excerpt_en: Eleven years ago, the Governor of Svalbard gave Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) permission to discharge untreated wastewater into Adventfjorden. The condition was that the water would not pollute the sea or seabed.
176699.subtitle_en: Today, sewage, food waste, Q-tips and microplastics flow directly from homes in Longyearbyen into the fjord. That must stop.

176713.excerpt_en: After Q-tips were discovered in Hiorthhamn, LL made a humorous information video about waste disposal. In it, local council leader Arild Olsen is stopped from throwing Q-tips down the toilet.
176713.subtitle_en: Plumbers find underwear, socks and sanitary pads, among other things.
176713.title_en: All sorts of things in the toilet

176730.excerpt_en: “We expected this, since the environment is such a high priority here, but we need to look at the issue as a whole,” says technical director Kjersti Olsen Ingerø. LL has drawn up a new master plan for water and sewage for the period 2019 to 2029.
176730.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council is prepared for treatment requirements, but food waste grinders pose challenges.

176767.excerpt_en: A local resident was airlifted after a snowmobile accident at the bottom of Slakbreen while travelling from Svea to Longyearbyen on Monday evening. Police were notified of the accident at around 10:30 p.m. “The man had chest pain and was taken to hospital for a check-up,” says Governor of Svalbard senior police officer Irene Welle.
176767.subtitle_en: He was picked up after a snowmobile accident.

176790.excerpt_en: Vide Brandt and Anika Paust bought apartment number 22 in the Old Hospital from Arne Oddvar Bergdal on April 30, 2013.
176790.subtitle_en: The damage occurred long after the purchase was completed, Nord-Troms District Court finds.
176790.title_en: Another court defeat for owners of the Old Hospital

176818.excerpt_en: “When I saw the advertisement in Svalbardposten in May 2008, I thought it would be possible to get a cabin plot within two or three years. I was wrong about that, I’ll say,” says a frustrated Sølvi Jacobsen.
176818.subtitle_en: Would you have believed it possible to obtain a cabin plot within a couple of years if you had read the advertisement below? Sølvi Jacobsen, 58, did. Nearly 11 years later, she still has no cabin plot. And the cabin is in storage.
176818.tags_en: Store Norske, cabin plots, Foxdalen cabin area, Vindodden cabin area, Bjørndalen cabin area, news
176818.title_en: “SNSK gave people false hopes of getting a cabin plot”

176835.excerpt_en: Property manager Sveinung Lystrup Thesen agrees that, if he had read the advertisement published in Svalbardposten in May 2008, he would have thought a call for cabin plots would be issued within a couple of years. “It created expectations, including among us at Store Norske.”
176835.subtitle_en: Advertising new cabin plots has taken far longer than Store Norske itself expected when it began in 2008. Nevertheless, the company believes it has acted properly.

176842.excerpt_en: Ingeborg is in fifth grade at Longyearbyen School. She has entered the competition to draw the finest sun for the annual Sun Festival since she started first grade.
176842.subtitle_en: Ingeborg Andersen, 11, does not consider herself talented at drawing, but she won this year’s competition to draw the finest sun.
176842.title_en: Wins this year’s sun drawing competition

176855.excerpt_en: Marie-Louise Bendiktsen was found dead in a burned-out house in Sjøvegan, Troms. The 38-year-old man is charged with killing her with a knife-like object.
176855.subtitle_en: A 38-year-old man has been charged with the 1998 Sjøvegan murder.
176855.title_en: Charges filed in the Sjøvegan murder

176866.excerpt_en: “We’ve always had strong advance ticket sales. This year, those sales were absolutely terrible.”
176866.subtitle_en: Polarjazz 2019 looked set to be a financial disaster for a long time.

176873.excerpt_en: Svalbard veterinarian Astrid Vikaune of Svalbard Vet is pleased that more funding is now on the way. “It’s positive, and it looks like things are changing. It could mean a better service for the animals here.”
176873.subtitle_en: Svalbard Vet may receive NOK 750,000 in operating support for the animal clinic. This would significantly strengthen local veterinary services.

176897.excerpt_en: Lampe has several guides who cannot find somewhere to live because prices are so high. “It is a very desperate situation.”
176897.subtitle_en: Despite 60 new homes now being built, it does not appear to be making it easier for businesses to find accommodation. For Doreen Lampe of Spitzbergen Adventures, the situation is becoming untenable.
176897.tags_en: Gruvedalen, housing market, housing construction, news, Elvesletta
176897.title_en: “Someone has to do something about this—and it has to happen now”

176902.excerpt_en: Without saying a single word, Morten Barrikmo and Ole Jørn Myklebust managed to delight the children at Rabalder on Saturday. Through the precise use of music and mime, the two told the story of misunderstandings that can arise in a friendship.

176917.excerpt_en: Two polar bears decided to pay the Polish research station a visit on Friday morning. The two bears appeared to be in no hurry as they wandered past.
176917.subtitle_en: Researchers in Hornsund got a surprise on Friday morning.

176920.excerpt_en: “We urge people to be very aware that their dogs are secured against running away. They can potentially cause serious harm,” says senior police officer Vidar Arnesen.
176920.subtitle_en: Recently, the Governor of Svalbard’s office has had to put down one reindeer a week because loose dogs have either bitten them or chased them to their deaths.
176920.tags_en: news, Governor of Svalbard, Svalbard reindeer
176920.title_en: Reindeer suffer because of loose dogs

176921.excerpt_en: Some people even had to make do with standing room. Actress Juni Dahr’s powerful voice was accompanied by jazz musicians Tore Brunborg and Per Oddvar Johansen.
176921.subtitle_en: The venue was packed when Polarjazz held its first concert in Mine 3 on Sunday.

176941.excerpt_en: Last week, Svalbardposten reported that Svalbardbutikken would no longer have fresh fish after Posten changed its scheduled flights to Longyearbyen. The mail plane will first land at Svalbard Airport at around 4:15 p.m., meaning most people will already have eaten dinner before the fish reaches the shop.
176941.subtitle_en: It will still be possible to buy fresh fish at Svalbardbutikken on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

176975.excerpt_en: Last year, a discussion arose after some visitors came close to a pair of polar bears mating on the ice in Tempelfjorden. This year, the Governor’s office wants to be prepared and warns that the ice on several fjords may be closed if necessary.
176975.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s office wants to protect vulnerable wildlife.

176978.excerpt_en: A couple of kilometres into Todalen, activity was frantic on Saturday. In Longyearbyen, people noticed that something was happening, with a helicopter shuttling back and forth in and out of town.
176978.subtitle_en: “A group of ten snowmobiles has been hit by an avalanche in Todalen,” the message read. All agencies then responded—on exercise—on Saturday.
176978.title_en: Avalanche preparedness put to the test

176982.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) announced this on its Facebook page on Monday morning. Road 300, between Huset and Road 501, has repeatedly been hit by avalanches, both snow and earth slides.
176982.subtitle_en: That is what LL’s technical committee has decided.

176996.excerpt_en: Saturday saw the first sports exchange of the year with Barentsburg. Svalbard Turn hosted the first of four such exchanges this year.
176996.subtitle_en: When you look at the results, you might perhaps think that the cultural exchange is what matters most.
176996.tags_en: Svalbardhallen, life in Svalbard, sport, culture, sports exchange, athletics, Barentsburg, Svalbard Turn

176998.excerpt_en: Nikoline Røkenes (2) lost her life in the major avalanche that came down from Sukkertoppen on 19 December 2015.
176998.subtitle_en: But Longyearbyen Local Council does not acknowledge liability for the fatal 2015 avalanche.

177015.excerpt_en: At the end of January, the Governor of Svalbard’s office expelled a man who had arrived in Svalbard without a return ticket. He had neither a job, accommodation nor money to stay in the archipelago.
177015.subtitle_en: The man who arrived penniless and without an agreement for work or accommodation was deported the day he arrived.
177015.title_en: Arrived without money or a job, deported the same day

177035.excerpt_en: An electrical fault in the freezer-room fan caused smoke to develop. “The fire service responded after the report came in shortly after six. They brought the situation under control before it could develop further,” says senior police officer Arnt Rennan of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
177035.subtitle_en: Firefighters had to respond on Tuesday evening after a fire started.

177038.excerpt_en: Every year, avalanche preparedness is tested outside Longyearbyen. A couple of kilometres into Todalen, activity was frantic last Saturday.
177038.subtitle_en: “The exercise is absolutely essential,” says Atle Rokkan of the Governor of Svalbard’s office. For both the Governor’s office and everyone heading out into the terrain, the exercise provided the answers they were looking for.
177038.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, news, Norwegian rescue dogs, air transport, Longyearbyen Red Cross, Todalen, avalanche exercise

177052.excerpt_en: Romano Juric from Croatia has lived in Longyearbyen for four years. He has his network here and currently works at Stationen.
177052.subtitle_en: Ivano (9) moved to Longyearbyen on 15 August with his mother and older sister. He has not attended school since.

177057.excerpt_en: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child states that all children have the right to attend school and receive an education, and that primary education shall be free. Ivano Catufa is nine years old and lives in Longyearbyen.
177057.subtitle_en: The County Governor of Troms and Finnmark is asking Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) to provide Ivano (9), who is autistic, with schooling. LL says it lacks the ability and resources to do so. The Ministry of Education and Research will launch a broader review of the right to education on Svalbard. In the meantime, Ivano and his family are left without any provision.

177072.excerpt_en: “I have spent time realizing that I am closer to the Labour Party than Venstre. It is the social-democratic idea that has won me over, and in order to serve another term on the local council, I had to switch parties,” says Kristin Furu Grøtting.
177072.subtitle_en: Kristin Furu Grøtting (57) has long felt that she represented the wrong party on the local council.
177072.title_en: Kristin switches from Venstre to Labour

177085.excerpt_en: Saturday saw the first sports exchange of the year with Barentsburg. Svalbard Turn hosted the first of four such exchanges this year.
177085.subtitle_en: Without the students from UNIS, some of the teams would have been rather thin on the ground. “Their involvement is exactly what we want,” says Nina Lines of Svalbard Turn.
177085.tags_en: Svalbard Turn, culture, life in Svalbard, sports exchange, sports games, sport
177085.title_en: UNIS students made their mark on sports exchange

177087.excerpt_en: The population has grown slowly but steadily in the Norwegian settlements on Svalbard over the past ten years. The tax office in Longyearbyen keeps statistics on the number of residents in Longyearbyen, Ny-Ålesund, Svea, Hopen, Bjørnøya and Hornsund.
177087.subtitle_en: From 2008 to 2017, the share of non-Norwegians on Svalbard doubled. The minister is taking note of changes in the population makeup.
177087.title_en: Svalbard minister keeping a close eye on population figures

177092.excerpt_en: “I needed to throw myself into something new,” says Varisa Phothisat (17). So she became the press officer for Ung Kultur Møtes (UKM), the youth cultural festival taking place from the 18th to the 22nd.
177092.subtitle_en: This group is in charge when UKM kicks off next week.
177092.tags_en: UKM, Longyearbyen Culture House, culture, young people, library, life in Svalbard
177092.title_en: Creating cultural fun for young people

177111.excerpt_en: Yesterday, the Governor of Svalbard flew with Lufttransport over much of southern Nordenskiöld Land. When they reached Ulvebreen on the east coast, they discovered that a crevasse in the glacier is now larger than ever before.
177111.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard warns snowmobile riders about a large crevasse in Ulvebreen.
177111.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, news, glaciers, east coast, glacier crevasse, safety

177145.excerpt_en: At 10:30 on Saturday morning, police had to respond by helicopter after a concern was reported. A local resident who had driven a snowmobile to Kapp Sshoultz on Friday had not reported that he had arrived, as agreed.
177145.subtitle_en: A helicopter search was carried out on Saturday morning. No one is missing or injured.

177155.excerpt_en: This photograph shows the departure of the “Jacob Kjøde” for Norway from Gamlekaia in 1959. From roughly May until November or December, all transport to and from Longyearbyen was by boat.
177155.subtitle_en: A look back at 1959, when the boat was the link to the outside world.
177155.title_en: When the boat was bound for the mainland

177185.excerpt_en: “Based on the witness statements cited, the court finds it most likely that the cooling system was out of service before the claimants bought the apartment,” District Court Judge Møyfrid Eggebø writes in the judgment.
177185.subtitle_en: Nord-Troms District Court believes all indications are that the damage to the Old Hospital occurred long after the claimants bought the apartment.

177207.excerpt_en: Karianne Tangen Dypedahl (17), Truls Kløfsrud Jauert (17) and Mari Andersen Buch (18) are this year’s three “mainland pupils” at Longyearbyen School.
177207.subtitle_en: While many spend a school year abroad as exchange students, three pupils at Longyearbyen School have done the same — in Norway.

177212.excerpt_en: A snowmobile party travelling from Longyearbyen to Svea was involved in a crash. The Governor’s personnel flew by helicopter to the site.
177212.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard received the report at 10:30 on Monday.
177212.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, accident, snowmobile, news, Svea

177231.excerpt_en: Two polar bears decided to pay the Polish research station a visit on Friday a week and a half ago. The two bears appeared to have plenty of time as they wandered past.

177377.excerpt_en: The Zeppelin Observatory on the mountain above Ny-Ålesund proved more important than anyone had imagined when it opened in 1989. 177395.subtitle_en: Vannledningsdalen: are avalanche barriers a remedy that should have been avoided?

177407.excerpt_en: What are two lightly dressed Englishmen doing on the steps outside Svalbardhallen—in temperatures of minus 20? They were not dragged out there by the local newspaper, but are getting some fresh air after ten hours at a football school.

Now, thankfully, the population is increasing.
