181572.excerpt_en: “We’ve brought a mixture of very old and some new songs. And some hybrids—old songs in new packaging,” Robert Plant told the audience.
181572.subtitle_en: Robert Plant’s concerts along the Norwegian coast have received top marks. Svalbardposten is tempted to raise the score to seven.
181572.tags_en: culture, concert, Longyearbyen Culture Centre, rock, life in Svalbard, Robert Plant
181572.title_en: A Fireworks Display of a Concert

181625.excerpt_en: Around 60 local young people aged 13–17 picked up litter as a summer job. Longyearbyen Local Council was their employer, and the young workers collected rubbish throughout the town over two days this week.
181625.subtitle_en: Young people cleaned up the town this week.

181631.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen is a special place, and current circumstances have prompted the architects to put forward, on their own initiative, what they call an “ambitious vision.” “We want Longyearbyen to lead the way and become a circular capital,” says Ingvild Sæbu Vatn at LPO’s local office.
181631.subtitle_en: LPO Architects in Longyearbyen have an ambitious vision that everyone agrees makes sense.
181631.tags_en: Svea, news, LPO Architects, reuse, buildings, economy
181631.title_en: “We Have an Enormous Resource Bank for Reuse”

181643.excerpt_en: At Vei 222 5, residents have been told by the building’s owner, Longbo, that they must find somewhere else to live by July 1.
181643.subtitle_en: Although the demolition in Lia is taking longer than expected, residents must move out by July 1. LL hopes to make up some of the lost time in the project.
181643.tags_en: demolition, Lia, housing, avalanche protection, news
181643.title_en: Emptied of Residents Despite FrP’s Efforts to Prevent It

181660.excerpt_en: Babcock is continuing to operate the seven bases Lufttransport has had in Norway. They are located in Kirkenes, Alta, Tromsø, Bodø, Brønnøysund, Ålesund and Gardermoen.
181660.subtitle_en: As of today, 1 July, Babcock is flying air ambulances to Svalbard. It is taking over from Lufttransport, which lost the contract.
181660.title_en: Jets Can Land in Worse Weather with More Equipment

181683.excerpt_en: Last Saturday, Aktiv i friluft organized the summer’s first litter-collection expedition. Daudmannsodden, at the far west of Isfjorden, was on the litter-picking itinerary.
181683.subtitle_en: But you do not get to choose to hear only one of the pieces of news.
181683.tags_en: news, marine litter, isfjorden, aktiv i friluft, litter expedition, litter
181683.title_en: This Is Both Good News and Bad News at the Same Time

181689.excerpt_en: “There were many lovely souvenir shops in Switzerland. I have met many tourists here who say they miss having a wider selection of Svalbard souvenirs, so I decided to start designing,” she says.
181689.subtitle_en: A holiday trip to Switzerland inspired Manatsanan Kosanthia, who has now opened a souvenir shop at Lompen Shopping Center.

181703.excerpt_en: Many people deserve credit for making the town tidier. Store Norske, the Governor of Svalbard, Longyearbyen Community Council and countless volunteers, who through various initiatives give Longyearbyen, its surrounding area and all of Svalbard an extra clean-up.
181703.subtitle_en: Thanks to Svalbardposten for highlighting an unfortunately familiar problem: a disorderly town. That said, things have improved. And this is an important point in itself, because, although some always claim the opposite, things were worse before.
181703.title_en: A Rich Man by Spring and the Natural Flow of Materials

181721.excerpt_en: Earlier this month, Arctic Workshop held its first opening day. Dyngeland runs handicraft workshops here several days a week for people of all ages.
181721.subtitle_en: Lene Jeanette Dyngeland missed activities for gray-weather days in Longyearbyen. She decided to do something about it.
181721.title_en: “It Became Bigger Than I Had Expected”

181728.excerpt_en: The cruise ship «MSC Preziosa» is docked in the harbor. Five expedition cruise ships are anchored outside in the harbor basin.
181728.subtitle_en: “This is what we are going to make a living from,” many say. But Longyearbyen residents strongly disagree about whether mass tourism is good for the community.
181728.tags_en: cruise, visit svalbard, business, news, tourism

181732.excerpt_en: When Svalbardposten meets him at Fruene café on Friday, he has his plans ready. “I’m going to pack my things. Give away or throw out almost everything except a few necessities.”
181732.subtitle_en: Mark Sabbatini, known for the free newspaper Icepeople, can no longer afford his rent. This week, he moved into a tent.
181732.tags_en: mark sabbatini, ice people, news, icepeople

181759.excerpt_en: When Sølvi Jacobsen posted a picture on Facebook, it sparked a debate. This offers a glimpse into what the parties think about mass tourism, although many believe it is a complex issue that cannot be summed up briefly.
181759.subtitle_en: Here are statements from leading politicians in Longyearbyen.
181759.tags_en: cruise tourism, tourism industry, transition, politics, news
181759.title_en: What They Say About Mass Tourism

181763.excerpt_en: As for the water temperature, there is not much to boast about. The sea will probably still be quite cold.
181763.subtitle_en: Temperatures of up to 20°C are forecast in Longyearbyen this weekend. Time to get out the skirts and shorts and enjoy the fine weather.

181782.excerpt_en: At the end of June, the Norwegian Coastal Administration and the Governor of Svalbard were given a presentation on how the wreck of the shrimp trawler «Northguider» will be removed from the site of the accident in Hinlopen.
181782.subtitle_en: The plan is ready, but much depends on the weather in the area.
181782.tags_en: rescue operations, governor of svalbard, northguider, norwegian coastal administration, hinlopen, news
181782.title_en: It Will Be Towed Away, Then Broken Up

181784.excerpt_en: Summer is well and truly here again, and the peak tourist season is already in full swing. After a long, quiet polar night, the town comes back to life in February and March when the snowmobile season begins.
181784.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen depends on tourism revenue, but how can the industry and local residents live well together in the future?
181784.title_en: The Tourist Season Poses a Challenge

181792.excerpt_en: Roger Solheim, communications officer for Babcock Scandinavian AirAmbulance (BSAA), tells Svalbardposten that they are ready and well prepared to take over the air ambulance service from Lufttransport, which lost the contract. The transfer of operations has attracted considerable controversy, particularly from the pilots.
181792.subtitle_en: From 1 July, Babcock took over the air ambulance service to and from Svalbard. Emergency preparedness was also strengthened with an ambulance jet.
181792.title_en: Strengthening Emergency Preparedness with a Jet

181807.excerpt_en: “The facility is due for replacement; it is so old that obtaining spare parts would be difficult if something happened. We can let it keep running until it breaks down, take it down, or upgrade it and replace it with a new transmitter,” says Gunnar Garfors, NRK’s radio distribution adviser.
181807.subtitle_en: The medium-wave facility in Longyearbyen is more than 40 years old. NRK is considering what to do with it.

181819.excerpt_en: Three more people have been awarded Norges Vel medals for 30 years of dedicated work. They are Geir Hekne, Odd Jostein Sylte (back row, from left) and Gunnhild Antonsen (No.
181819.subtitle_en: They were presented with Norges Vel medals at a recent event at Funken Lodge.

181824.excerpt_en: British rock icon Robert Plant had never been to Svalbard before. Here, he had the experience of a lifetime, both on and off stage. “I’m hugely impressed by how well everything worked here,” Plant tells Svalbardposten.
181824.subtitle_en: The organiser, the artist’s own production team and Robert Plant himself are all full of praise for Svalbard and its audience.

181833.excerpt_en: The shipping company itself considers the accident to have been caused by human error.
181833.subtitle_en: Last July, “Aurora Explorer” crashed into the quay in Barentsburg, injuring 37 people. The case has now been concluded by the Norwegian Safety Investigation Authority (SHT).

181904.excerpt_en: At the top of the slope, a cyclist is waiting. Now they pedal as hard as they can, with plans to launch into the air over a jump after 100 metres.
181904.tags_en: summer, school, outdoor activities, swimming, children, news, cycling
181904.title_en: Children kick off the summer holidays in active style

181908.excerpt_en: Svalbard’s only carnivorous plant is also found in Ringhorndalen, a sheltered little side valley on the eastern side of Wijdefjorden, which lies within the national park.
181908.subtitle_en: In one place on Svalbard, temperatures can reach 40°C, and butterflies and rare plants can be found that are seen only here.

181911.excerpt_en: She had neither a place to live nor a job when she arrived. Nor did she know how long she would stay.
181911.subtitle_en: Ariella Madsen (20) had finished upper secondary school and wanted to try something new. So she booked a one-way ticket to Longyearbyen.

181913.excerpt_en: There are those who played in Longyearbyen, worked as adults and still work in the town, and also know that everything that begins eventually comes to an end. Retirement age is rising towards the horizon.
181913.subtitle_en: “It is still uncertain whether, or when, a solution may be found,” writes Reinhard Mook.
181913.tags_en: reader’s letter, cabins, opinion, cabin plots

181952.excerpt_en: Rapid snowmelt and high water flow caused several challenges over the weekend. In Endalen, the road was closed because of large volumes of water. “We closed the road on Saturday afternoon when the water began to run over it.”
181952.subtitle_en: Store Norske is closing Endalsveien until further notice because of subsidence damage to the road.

181969.excerpt_en: Choose who you want to be. How do you think that person will live and make a home on Svalbard in a hundred years?
181969.subtitle_en: Architecture students showed how they believe Longyearbyen could look in the future.
181969.title_en: Exhibiting the Svalbard of the future

181985.excerpt_en: UNIS writes in a press release: “Due to differing expectations regarding UNIS’s future direction, the board and Managing Director Harald Ellingsen have agreed that Ellingsen will step down as director of UNIS effective 1 January 2020.”
181985.subtitle_en: Harald Ellingsen (65) will leave his position as UNIS director at New Year after disagreeing with the board over the institution’s future direction.
181985.title_en: Ellingsen steps down as UNIS director

181998.excerpt_en: On 28 December, at about 1:15 in the afternoon, what should never have happened occurs.
181998.subtitle_en: One wrong choice could have been fatal. Fortunately, another decision was made, the report on the rescue operation in Hinlopen during the Christmas holidays shows. Here you can read how the rescue operation unfolded, minute by minute.
181998.tags_en: shipwreck, rescue operation, news, Northguider, air transport, Norwegian Coastal Administration, Governor of Svalbard, helicopter preparedness, emergency preparedness, rescue capacity
181998.title_en: The rescuers did not know what awaited them

182000.excerpt_en: “The weather situation indicated that it could get very warm because large masses of warm air were arriving with easterly winds, but unfortunately it did not quite turn out that way,” says meteorologist Ine-Therese Pedersen at Svalbard Airport. Even so, temperatures in the higher cloud layers reached nearly 20°C.
182000.subtitle_en: Temperatures of up to 20°C were forecast for the weekend. At its warmest, 16.1°C was recorded at Svalbard Airport.
182000.title_en: This is how warm it got over the weekend

182005.excerpt_en: The rescue operation in Hinlopen Strait during the Christmas holidays fortunately went well. Fourteen people were rescued after the boat ran aground.
182005.subtitle_en: We will be surprised if the ministry and the shipping companies have not learned from the accident.

182022.excerpt_en: The deadline for guessing when Stetten will appear has passed, and Svalbardposten has counted 299 entries in this year’s contest. The earliest date guessed is yesterday, the 10th.
182022.subtitle_en: Almost 300 guesses were submitted for Svalbardposten’s annual guessing contest.

182050.excerpt_en: Bilicz misses a support system for passengers who become patients at the hospital. If one of the employees on board falls ill, the agent takes care of all the related administration.
182050.subtitle_en: John Aksel Bilicz, chief nurse and acting department head at Longyearbyen Hospital, is concerned about the heavy administrative workload caused by cruise tourism.
182050.tags_en: Longyearbyen Hospital, cruise ships, news, cruise tourism
182050.title_en: “No one takes responsibility for the sick”

article_keywords_en: Convention on the Rights of the Child
182060.excerpt_en: In its previous issue, Svalbardposten wrote about the Governor’s decision concluding that Ivano Cafuta (9) is entitled to a place at Longyearbyen School and to primary education there, even though he has special needs and requires accommodations.
182060.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council strongly disagrees with the Governor’s decision in the Ivano case and therefore asked the Ministry of Education and Research to overturn it. The appeal has been rejected.

182072.excerpt_en: “This is absolutely fantastic. The flat is very nice and has a good layout,” says Tale Høgemark.
182072.subtitle_en: The minister who attended this week’s “housewarming party” did not bring any government plans for new housing in the immediate future. But she did receive a fine cardboard key.
182072.tags_en: news, Gruvedalen, building permit, housing policy, housing market, homes, housing construction, Statsbygg, ministerial visit
182072.title_en: “It’s great to see it finished already”

182078.excerpt_en: Ivar Smedsrød is the substitute priest at Svalbard Church this summer. He is joined by Jan Haugan, who will provide musical accompaniment at services and make sure church coffee and waffles are served as usual.
182078.subtitle_en: While the permanent church staff are on holiday, substitute priest Ivar Smedsrød and Jan Haugan will lead services and evening worship throughout the summer.
182078.title_en: These are Svalbard Church’s summer substitutes

182090.excerpt_en: I am more concerned about the environmental aspects of the cruise industry than the number of tourists it brings to town. The numbers can be managed well if tourists are enabled to be responsible visitors.
182090.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten week 27 ran a feature on mass tourism and cruise tourism. My main point about the issue was not included.
182090.title_en: Proposes tourist tax and heavy fuel oil ban

182106.excerpt_en: The service building, which will operate alongside the seed vault, will not officially open until October. But Minister of Local Government and Modernisation Monica Mæland (Conservative), accompanied by the political leadership, was given a quick tour and information about both the work carried out around the seed vault entrance and the functions the service building will have in the future.
182106.subtitle_en: The minister saw the Svalbard Global Seed Vault’s new service building. It is not intended to be a visitor centre.
182106.title_en: Minister gets a sneak preview of service building

182109.excerpt_en: A local resident was arrested after drunken disorder at Svalbar in the early hours of Sunday. “It eventually developed into an assault, and a man was arrested. He was released after a few hours when he was feeling better,” says Senior Police Officer Atle Rokkan, of the Governor of Svalbard.
182109.subtitle_en: Police had to respond to an assault at a nightlife venue on Saturday night.

182120.excerpt_en: The new modular harbour building and toilet facilities are now in place in the harbour area. The buildings are due to open officially later this summer.
182120.subtitle_en: The public building and toilet facilities have been fully installed.
182120.title_en: Public facilities building is in place

182141.excerpt_en: At the end of a road between Endalen and Todalen, a group of people is gathered. They are planning the day’s work of counting reindeer.
182141.subtitle_en: “We found a great many carcasses this year,” says reindeer researcher Åshild Ønvik Pedersen. It was probably caused by heavy rain on 21 December.
182141.tags_en: reindeer hunting, reindeer, rain, news, Norwegian Polar Institute, climate, research, winter
182141.title_en: One rainy day before Christmas killed a great many

182149.excerpt_en: Fannar Theyr Gudmundson and Guus Wellesen found the distinctive species. They spotted the bird in northern Bear Island among the “local” puffins in Nordhamna.
182149.subtitle_en: A tufted puffin was observed by a Norwegian Polar Institute field team on Bear Island on Saturday, 13 July. It is Norway’s first documented record of this bird.

182169.excerpt_en: More nature is to be protected. That is the decision of the Ministry of Climate and Environment.
182169.subtitle_en: The lower parts of Adventdalen may be protected. But first, a management plan must be drawn up, and Van Mijenfjorden will be incorporated into Nordenskiöld Land National Park.
182169.tags_en: protection, Van Mijenfjorden, Adventdalen, national park, nature conservation, news, Governor of Svalbard
182169.title_en: Conservation work begins for Van Mijenfjorden and Adventdalen

182192.excerpt_en: German Franka Leiterer came to Longyearbyen to study at UNIS three years ago and saw an announcement about a newly established cycling club. She had always been passionate about bicycles, so she signed up.
182192.subtitle_en: Fresh waffles, coffee, cake and bicycle repairs. Svalbard Resykkelerings workshop turns old junk into new treasures.

182194.excerpt_en: The red-throated loon chicks hatched a few days ago. The nest is in a small pool on the north side, just before the main pond, alongside a couple of other nests.
182194.subtitle_en: A red-throated loon family has chosen a highly exposed nesting site, just two metres from the road in Adventdalen.
182194.title_en: Please show consideration for this family

182224.excerpt_en: “Saying everything will be ready for the opening would be stretching it a little. But the programme for the opening weekend itself is ready,” he says.
182224.subtitle_en: The students who will attend Svalbard Folk High School arrive in town on 3 September. Preparations at the school will continue right up to the final deadline, says principal Espen Klungseth Rotevatn.
182224.title_en: “We’ll be polishing the trim on the last night before opening”

182229.excerpt_en: Opilio AS has only one vessel still operating after the “Northguider” ran aground in the Hinlopen Strait during the Christmas holidays. The “Northeastern” is currently fishing for crab south of the Barents Sea, east of Hopen.
182229.subtitle_en: The operations manager of the shipping company that owns the “Northguider” says they will consider shrimp trawling in the Hinlopen Strait again.
182229.title_en: Not deterred by the Hinlopen Strait accident

182248.excerpt_en: The Planning and Development Department of LL is now warning the LL property department of a fine; the latter is the developer responsible for the work. Planning and Development follows up all actors in Longyearbyen, while the property department acts as building owner and manager carrying out assignments for LL.
182248.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council is warning of a NOK 50,000 penalty for work started prematurely outside Næringsbygget.

182254.excerpt_en: TUI’s Mein Schiff 5 was docked in Longyearbyen on Wednesday, July 17.
182254.subtitle_en: The cruise ship Mein Schiff visited Longyearbyen yesterday.
182254.title_en: See Photos from Mein Schiff’s Arrival

182258.excerpt_en: Ekstedt formally takes over as station manager on September 1. “This is one of the most exciting places one can work.”
182258.subtitle_en: Maja-Stina Ekstedt has been appointed as the new station manager at Svalsat.
182258.title_en: She Will Be Svalsat’s New Station Manager

182273.excerpt_en: Two sailboats in June, two in July, a Danish TV crew, people from the Governor’s Office and Svalbard Museum, a representative from Kings Bay, several researchers and the Coast Guard. Normally, only nine people live on Bear Island, but this summer they have been busy.
182273.subtitle_en: The nine-person crew has had plenty of visitors to the island this summer. At most, 18 people sat down to dinner.
182273.title_en: A Rush of Visitors to Bear Island

182287.excerpt_en: It turned out to be a fire in car tires lying at the shooting range, and personnel from the Governor’s Office and the fire service responded. The extinguishing operation is still ongoing, but the situation is reportedly under control.
182287.subtitle_en: During the early hours of Saturday, from 12:30 a.m., the Governor’s Office received several reports of smoke from the shooting-range area.

182304.excerpt_en: Timofey Rogozhin, general manager of Grumant Arctic Travel Company, says the number of people working in tourism-related activities has risen from around 20 to 100 since the travel company was launched in 2016. Every year, they have developed new tourism products.
182304.subtitle_en: More and more of Barentsburg’s 450 residents work in the tourism industry. Visits to the active mine are the most popular attraction.

182310.excerpt_en: Ellingsen and his wife Anne are moving to Trondheim at New Year. He will work from there until his original fixed-term appointment expires in October 2020.
182310.subtitle_en: Last week, UNIS announced that Managing Director Harald Ellingsen will step down at New Year.
182310.title_en: Casting a Wide Net for New Director

182313.excerpt_en: Nina Lines will remain general manager of Svalbard Turn for a few more months before Silje Hagen takes over the reins. The work will be done from the mainland in the coming months, but first there is a little holiday.
182313.subtitle_en: Nina Lines and Ole Petter Storstad are heading back to the mainland. The moving container leaves for Jessheim on Tuesday.
182313.tags_en: news, Svalbard Turn, magazine, moving, SvalSat
182313.title_en: Packing Up After Nearly Five Years

182325.excerpt_en: “We have been conducting archaeological work in Svalbard for more than ten years, and have now completed the VR presentation of what Advent City looked like in 1908.”
182325.subtitle_en: In August, researcher Frigga Kruse and her team will come to Longyearbyen to showcase Advent City in VR (virtual reality).

182342.excerpt_en: “The cat population was already in Barentsburg before the ban was introduced, so they had to be allowed to live. The population has declined considerably, and we hope they do not have any more litters,” says Harald Os of the Norwegian Food Safety Authority.
182342.subtitle_en: The 1992 regulation banning the import of animals to Svalbard states that permission is not granted to bring cats to Svalbard. Nevertheless, several cats live in Barentsburg.

182371.excerpt_en: “Almost none of the 1,400 passengers went onto the tundra, nobody took pictures of those of us who live here, and if they did, they politely asked for permission first. The visit was very pleasant for both us and them.”
182371.subtitle_en: New guidelines for cruise tourists visiting Ny-Ålesund were introduced last week. The first experience has been very positive.

182406.excerpt_en: The coal-fired power plant in Longyearbyen has been quieter than usual in recent days. “We have to carry out a maintenance shutdown once a year. During that time, we perform essential maintenance that can only be done when the plant is not operating.”
182406.subtitle_en: The power plant has been shut down for maintenance since Monday. That means black smoke when it starts up again on Wednesday.
182406.title_en: The Power Plant Will Produce Plenty of Smoke Today

182427.excerpt_en: This week, a large excavator from LNS Spitsbergen began removing the topsoil at Blåmyra. Before long, trucks began shuttling back and forth to haul away the material.
182427.subtitle_en: There will be some hassle and detours over the next few months. After that, the road to Gruvedalen will be better for both pedestrians and motorists.

182429.excerpt_en: “I can confirm that we have gained access to camera footage from the shooting range. On the basis of this, we have opened a case,” says Senior Police Officer Kjell Arne Lundin at the Governor’s Office.
182429.subtitle_en: When a fire broke out at the shooting range over the weekend, the police did not know what caused it. They have now received help from camera footage.
182429.tags_en: Longyearbyen Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association, news
182429.title_en: Camera Images Reveal Cause of Fire

182434.excerpt_en: “I am bisexual and my brother is gay, so this is something that has always been relevant in my family.”
182434.subtitle_en: For the first time, Longyearbyen is getting its own Pride celebration. The driving force behind it is Lene Dyngeland.

182449.excerpt_en: State meteorologist Anita Ager-Wick, however, confirms that we cannot expect any heatwave on the island. “There will be no heatwave in Svalbard, and the low-pressure systems will not affect you at all in any way.”
182449.subtitle_en: “The heatwave is heading for Svalbard,” VG wrote yesterday, July 26.

182455.excerpt_en: “That’s right. Over the past few days, we have been testing the use of card terminals in Pyramiden.”
182455.subtitle_en: There is no longer any need to remember to bring cash when visiting Pyramiden. They now have card terminals as well.
182455.title_en: Card Payments Finally Available in Pyramiden

182484.excerpt_en: The fire aboard the sailboat overnight Saturday has made headlines in The Tennessean newspaper in the United States. It turns out that prominent Americans were aboard, including former Nashville mayor Karl Dean.
182484.subtitle_en: The former mayor of Nashville, Tennessee, was aboard the sailboat reported to have caught fire last weekend. It made headlines “over there.”
182484.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, The Tennessean, news

182490.excerpt_en: We take a brief look back at 2012 and show the pictures taken at the time by former editor Birger Amundsen. Much has happened over the past seven years.
182490.subtitle_en: There is no more coal to be seen in Svea. The clean-up is now in full swing.

182496.excerpt_en: They published their own photo story on their website, and Svalbardposten has been allowed to show the pictures. The photos were taken when four of Bear Island’s residents went to Nordhavna to clean up the beach.
182496.subtitle_en: Whenever the crew on Bear Island has the opportunity, they try to tackle the island’s major plastic problem on its beaches.

182506.excerpt_en: “The two men had been in the sea for an estimated couple of hours. It took us a little while to find them,” says Vidar Arnesen, Chief Superintendent of the Governor’s Office.
182506.subtitle_en: Two kayakers are in hospital after ending up in the sea last night. The Governor’s Office took time to locate them.
182506.tags_en: news, Diabasodden, Governor of Svalbard, kayak
182506.title_en: Saved the lives of two kayakers

182519.excerpt_en: For a long time, the snow lay thick on Operafjellet. Many actually thought the Stetten would not appear at all this year.
182519.subtitle_en: It was a late spring, and there was a lot of snow on Operafjellet for a long time. But on 28 July, the Stetten appeared.

182540.excerpt_en: In a press release, they write that hiking is also about observing the animal and plant life around us, and that the shelter is intended as a place where hikers can sit down and take a break on the walk from Hotellneset to Bjørndalen.
182540.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Field Biology Association (LoFF) has installed a wind shelter by Laguna at Hotellneset.

182594.excerpt_en: “I was absolutely delighted. It’s a milestone for us and absolutely essential for running a good veterinary clinic,” says Vikaune.
182594.subtitle_en: Veterinarian Astrid Vikaune has fought for an on-call service since arriving in Svalbard six years ago. Before summer, she finally received the news she had been waiting for.

182597.excerpt_en: The most observant residents noticed it long ago, and the keenest hikers have already started using the northern section of the “river promenade”, which is complete. “It makes me very happy to see people walking along the river there.”
182597.subtitle_en: The first serious attempt to “tame” the Longyear River is due to be completed in October. Then walkers will have much more space to enjoy.
182597.tags_en: Longyear River, LNS Spitsbergen, news, Longyearbyen Community Council
182597.title_en: Creating 3.6 kilometres more car-free road for you

182602.excerpt_en: “It was great fun, especially as it was on my birthday,” she says. She lives in Oslo, while her daughter, Cathinka Tønsberg, has lived in Longyearbyen for more than seven years.
182602.subtitle_en: Torill Tønsberg won this year’s Stetten competition. She guessed the correct date—28 July, which is also her birthday.

182611.excerpt_en: A French hiking group contacted the Governor shortly after midnight on Friday. “A polar bear had entered the tent camp in Gipsvika and started tearing tents apart. Those at the site were unable to scare the bear away,” says Chief Superintendent Atle Rokkan of the Governor’s Office.
182611.subtitle_en: The group of hikers was unable to scare away a polar bear that entered a tent camp in Gipsvika.
182611.tags_en: polar bear, Gipsvika, news, Governor of Svalbard
182611.title_en: Close-approaching polar bear forces evacuation of ten people

182637.excerpt_en: It has been a long time since Albert I of Monaco was among us. He was born in 1848 and died on 26.
182637.subtitle_en: Did you know that part of Svalbard is named after this man? In 2022, it will be 100 years since Albert I of Monaco died. This will be commemorated, if possible here as well.

182644.excerpt_en: They allegedly drove in the Todalen area. “We went out to speak to the people afterward and have begun investigating. We need to talk to witnesses, and the investigation will show whether they did it or not,” says Chief Superintendent Atle Rokkan of the Governor’s Office.
182644.subtitle_en: The Governor was notified last night about people who allegedly drove ATVs off-road and is opening a case.
182644.title_en: ATV driving off-road: police open investigation

182666.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration writes this. On Thursday this week, Smit Salvage, the company commissioned to remove the wreck, sailed toward Hinlopen with a crane vessel.
182666.subtitle_en: The salvage operation for the wrecked vessel “Northguider” begins this week, and a traffic ban will be introduced in parts of Hinlopen Strait from 4 August to 15 September.

182674.excerpt_en: The Governor was notified at around 3:30 p.m. about three people who had reached terrain where they saw no way to continue or get back down. “It’s steep, with a lot of loose rock.”
182674.subtitle_en: Three people had to be picked up by the Governor this afternoon while on their way to Sarkofagen.

182687.excerpt_en: “You develop a special sense of togetherness by playing in a band, and that’s something I miss. But I’ve never regretted that we chose to move up here,” he says.
182687.subtitle_en: What Fredrik Scott Oswold (27) misses most about the mainland is the rock band he is still part of. Otherwise, he has no regrets about leaving.
182687.tags_en: people, life in Svalbard, back page

182701.excerpt_en: “We’re going to produce sparkling water and get Ramlösa off the island,” says Robert Johansen, brewery manager at Svalbard Brewery, laughing. Invested several hundred thousand: If everything goes according to plan, the equipment will be installed and the first samples sent down during this week.
182701.subtitle_en: Svalbard Vann will most likely be available in shops during the month.

182730.excerpt_en: Norway’s municipal and county council elections are approaching. In Longyearbyen, residents will use their ballots to put together a new local council.
182730.subtitle_en: “Svalbard Høyre wants to know what you think they should think before they think anything themselves.”
182730.title_en: Changing one’s tune with the wind

182745.excerpt_en: Last Thursday, a crane vessel and two tugboats set course for the wrecked “Northguider” in Hinlopen Strait. When Svalbardposten spoke to insurance company Gard on Monday this week, which is responsible for removing the shrimp trawler, they said they had arrived at the wreck site.
182745.subtitle_en: All the sea ice has disappeared from the wreck site, and the salvage operation is proceeding as planned. This is what “Northguider” looks like now.
182745.tags_en: news, wreck, salvage operations, insurance, Hinlopen
182745.title_en: See photos of the wreck in Hinlopen

182761.excerpt_en: There are many of them, but they are the people most visible to visiting tourists. Svalbardposten met some of them to hear about their everyday lives.
182761.subtitle_en: What is it like working as a guide in Longyearbyen, and what do they think about tourism?
182761.title_en: “We must take care of nature—that’s what we’re actually selling”

182795.excerpt_en: From Monday to Thursday he works in Svea, Friday is office day in Longyearbyen, and he has the weekends off. His working day starts at seven. “There’s a lot going on right now.”
182795.subtitle_en: Store Norske’s Morten Johansen is the manager in Svea. He coordinates all the projects under way and everyone involved in them in various ways. The clean-up will probably take three to five years.
182795.title_en: New housing base at Cape Amsterdam

182822.excerpt_en: Researcher Frigga Kruse and her team—master’s student Rosanne van Bodegom and self-proclaimed “3D guy” Mathias Lang—are showing Svalbard residents this week what Advent City looked like, using VR at the library.
182822.subtitle_en: “It was absolutely fantastic. The background sounds and everything were so well done,” says Marianne Mulders-Zonneveld.

182827.excerpt_en: After heading Telenor Svalbard since January 1, 2015, Guttorm A.’s tenure is coming to an end.
182827.subtitle_en: “My ambition is to carry out the important tasks Telenor has in Svalbard, while also giving the company a voice in the public debate,” says Christian Skottum (51).

182837.excerpt_en: Overall, Arctic ice melt has been record-breaking so far this summer. The Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) reported 1.
182837.subtitle_en: There is a record-low amount of sea ice in the Arctic this summer. The record for the absolute minimum ice extent, set in 2012, looks likely to be broken this year.
182837.title_en: Warmth puts sea ice on course for a record

182856.excerpt_en: In recent years, work has been under way to establish a national park centre in Longyearbyen. In 2017 and 2018, a preliminary project was carried out after Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund and the Ministry of Climate and Environment allocated a total of NOK 955,000.
182856.subtitle_en: LL is receiving funding to hire someone to work on a new nature information centre. At the same time, the ministry is asking LL to scale down the centre.
182856.tags_en: money, tourism, national park, museum, Longyearbyen local council, news
182856.title_en: More than one million kroner spent on project—now they get funding to hire

182870.excerpt_en: Temperatures in Longyearbyen were three to four degrees above zero in the morning. Early in the day, when the clouds receded a little, several mountain peaks could be seen covered in a thin layer of snow.
182870.subtitle_en: Early Wednesday morning brought the season’s first snowfall to the peaks around Longyearbyen. “There may also be sleet down in Longyearbyen at night,” the duty meteorologist says.

182873.excerpt_en: “There are stereotypes in Bærum too, like everywhere else. But I’m not exactly ‘typically Bærum’ either,” she says.
182873.subtitle_en: Nelia Dahle (32) moved to Svalbard a year ago. She has lived in Bærum for most of her life, but she is not exactly a city girl.

182890.excerpt_en: The Svalbard Treaty was signed in Paris on February 9, 1920.
182890.subtitle_en: Today, August 14, marks 94 years since Norway gained full sovereignty over Svalbard. The Svalbard Treaty is the reason. “All countries agree on the treaty itself. But they do not agree on how it should be interpreted,” says Per Arne Totland.
182890.tags_en: politics, news, Svalbard Day, Svalbard Treaty, anniversary
182890.title_en: Nearly 100-year-old treaty still governs life here

182910.excerpt_en: At 7 p.m. on Wednesday, the three vessels—“Bear,” “Cormorant” and “Multratug 18”—passed the northern tip of Prins Karls Forland. Online traffic maps showed the three travelling together in convoy.
182910.subtitle_en: The vessels that were supposed to remove “Northguider” from Hinlopenstretet are now heading back to Longyearbyen, a few weeks earlier than planned.
182910.tags_en: Northguider, pilot, Longyearbyen port, Hinlopen, shipwreck, insurance, news

182918.excerpt_en: Svalbard Høyre took a fair amount of criticism in this column in the previous issue. We thought it was rather strange that the local branch had submitted its election platform as a consultation draft two months before the local elections.
182918.subtitle_en: Svalbard Høyre is actually best in class.
182918.tags_en: Svalbard Labour Party, opinions, Longyearbyen Progress Party, local elections, editorial, Svalbard Greens, Svalbard Liberals, Svalbard Conservatives

182940.excerpt_en: A couple of years ago, the supports beneath the covered conveyor belt to Mine 6 in Adventdalen failed. The structure eventually came to rest down the mountainside and now poses a safety risk.
182940.subtitle_en: Store Norske has been granted permission to use a helicopter to remove the conveyor belt from the mountainside.

182943.excerpt_en: “The plan for the next few days is to get these people to gel and put the final framework for the school in place. We are going to become the world’s best folk high school, after all,” principal Espen Klungseth Rotevatn says with a smile.
182943.subtitle_en: The entire staff of Svalbard Folk High School is in town, ready to develop a strategy for becoming the best in their field.

182959.excerpt_en: Some think it is too early. Others like the sight of the fresh snow lying on the ground.
182959.subtitle_en: The town awoke to a thin layer of fresh snow—and it is only August 16. You would have to have lived here for more than 30 years to have experienced anything similar on this date.
182959.title_en: More than 30 years since this last happened

182981.excerpt_en: The bear had been in the area around Hiorthhamn, on the opposite side of Adventfjorden, for several hours. The Governor of Svalbard stayed nearby in a boat for a long time to keep an eye on the bear, which is not believed to have caused any damage. “It hasn’t bothered anyone or damaged anything.”
182981.subtitle_en: On Saturday morning, the Governor of Svalbard went out by helicopter to drive a polar bear away from Hiorthhamn.
182981.title_en: Chased polar bear away from Hiorthhamn

182991.excerpt_en: After Eva-Britt Kornfeldt of Visit Svalbard welcomed them aboard, she went through some of the organization’s strategies for cruise tourism. Stay longer in town One of them is for ships to stay even longer in Svalbard, so tourists can see more of the archipelago.
182991.subtitle_en: Local business leaders were invited aboard the cruise ship Aidaluna. How best to manage tourism was one of the topics discussed.
182991.title_en: “It’s important that permanent residents are happy”

183016.excerpt_en: Lene Jeanette Dyngeland took it upon herself to organize Pride in Longyearbyen. In a short time, she managed to put the event together, without knowing how it would turn out.
183016.subtitle_en: The first Pride celebration in Longyearbyen drew several hundred people.

183024.excerpt_en: First, a helicopter from Lufttransport was spotted flying into Longyeardalen. Then it returned over Sukkertoppen.
183024.subtitle_en: Everyone in Gruvedalen noticed that something was happening around 10 p.m. on Saturday evening.
183024.tags_en: Sukkertoppen, Governor of Svalbard, news, Lufttransport, Gruvedalen, rescue operations

183039.excerpt_en: Aidaluna also has an anesthesiologist on board, unlike Longyearbyen Hospital, which has an anesthesiologist available in connection with the air ambulance service.
183039.subtitle_en: Aidaluna has its own hospital with 14 beds. By comparison, Longyearbyen Hospital has seven beds.
183039.title_en: In dialogue with the ship’s hospital

183061.excerpt_en: Normally, it is a real boost for Svalbardposten when Christopher Engås fills in as editor, and normally I do not spend time campaigning against the local newspaper either.
183061.subtitle_en: “The most important thing a local politician can do is listen to the public; that is why what matters most to us is what matters to you,” writes Kjetil Figenschou, leader of Svalbard Høyre.
183061.tags_en: Svalbard Høyre, local elections, letter to the editor, Kjetil Figenschou, Christopher Engås, opinions
183061.title_en: Real solutions to real problems for real people!

183070.excerpt_en: On Saturday, MSC “Preziosa” docked in Longyearbyen, marking the end of the season for ocean-going cruise ships.
183070.subtitle_en: Eva-Britt Kornfeldt, head of the Svalbard Cruise Network, is pleased that cruise tourists are making a better impression. She has now moved to Oslo but will continue working with Longyearbyen as a destination.
183070.tags_en: Svalbard community guidelines, news, Eva-Britt Kornfeldt, Visit Svalbard, Svalbard Cruise Network

183085.excerpt_en: For a long time, buying larger goods from the mainland has meant that the Governor of Svalbard must visit each individual at home to document the purchase. The Governor’s Office then certifies a document entitling you to a VAT refund.
183085.subtitle_en: Buying larger items online? Soon, mainland online retailers—or you yourself—will have to ensure that VAT is deducted before large goods arrive in Svalbard.
183085.tags_en: tax, online shopping, VAT, duties, Governor of Svalbard, news
183085.title_en: Mainland shops may soon take full responsibility

183096.excerpt_en: “I can probably be a little too open and honest about myself sometimes. If you ask me about something concerning me, I can answer anything; it doesn’t bother me,” she says with a laugh.
183096.subtitle_en: Kristine Austin (28) works as an accountant, but eventually plans to change careers and become a sexologist. She believes too much in today’s society is taboo.
183096.title_en: “Probably a little too open and honest”

183106.excerpt_en: A repentant sinner gave evidence when the Nord-Troms District Court convened in Longyearbyen on Tuesday.
183106.subtitle_en: “I realize I have made a fool of myself. Now I just have to accept whatever sentence I receive,” a male resident in his late 20s told the Nord-Troms District Court.
183106.tags_en: news, Governor of Svalbard, Nord-Troms District Court

183111.excerpt_en: 14 August is known as Svalbard Day.
183111.subtitle_en: On Svalbard Day, 14 August, the KV “Svalbard” headed north from Longyearbyen, reaching the pole on Wednesday morning. A Russia expert believes the Russians will not pay much attention to this.
183111.tags_en: news, politics, Coast Guard, research, North Pole
183111.title_en: Coast Guard at the North Pole

183127.excerpt_en: A full 42 people took part in the Peak Challenge, in which participants are to climb ten mountain peaks in twelve hours. Unfortunately, the weather proved challenging, with rain and fog.
183127.subtitle_en: Bad weather meant that only a handful managed to climb ten peaks in one day.
183127.title_en: Fit peak hikers faced bad weather

183142.excerpt_en: Sixth-graders Astrid, Madelin, Sigrid, Lina, Kjersti and Ada are not entirely positive about the first day of school, although they think it is perfectly fine to get started again. Better than holidays. Before the school day began, they waited outside for their new classmate Malin, who had moved to Longyearbyen from Stavanger.
183142.subtitle_en: Tuesday was the first day back at Longyearbyen School after the holidays. Although Lina Engås Vikaune admits it was nice to have time off, she says it will be good to get back into a routine.
183142.title_en: “It’s Great to See the Others Again”

183145.excerpt_en: “A polar bear has been at a cabin in Hiorthhamn. It damaged a door,” said Senior Police Officer Espen Olsen at 10:45 p.m. on Wednesday.
183145.subtitle_en: Police believe the same bear that was in Hiorthhamn on Saturday has returned. On Wednesday evening, the Governor of Svalbard chased the bear away by helicopter.
183145.title_en: Polar bear damaged cabin in Hiorthhamn and had to be chased away

183150.excerpt_en: When Pride is celebrated in larger towns on the mainland, there are often objections. That is not the case in Longyearbyen.
183150.subtitle_en: Lene Jeanette Dyngeland’s “crazy idea” to mark Pride in Longyearbyen was a success.

183160.excerpt_en: The ice has forced the boats away from Hinlopen Strait, where they are supposed to remove the wrecked shrimp trawler Northguider. The fact that there is ice there in August should come as no surprise.
183160.subtitle_en: “It now looks as though the chances are being squandered.”

183196.excerpt_en: A week ago on Thursday, the three vessels Bear, Cormorant and Multratug 18 returned from Hinlopen, just over a week after they had begun work at the wreck site at Sparreneset. The plan there was to remove the wrecked shrimp trawler Northguider.
183196.subtitle_en: Vulnerable birdlife is cited as the reason the operation in Hinlopen did not begin until August. The Governor of Svalbard’s office says it did not impose such deadlines. Now the operation has lost another week.
183196.tags_en: shipwreck, Nordaustlandet, environmental protection, Hinlopen, birdlife, management, emergency preparedness, news
183196.title_en: Losing Valuable Time Removing the Wreck in Hinlopen

183198.excerpt_en: “They are welding now, so everything should be up and running again by 9 p.m. at the latest, according to our plans,” says Torfinn Larsgaard, project manager for Longyearbyen Local Council. “Moisture got in from outside and into a joint, and then it corroded…”
183198.subtitle_en: Several roads will be without hot water and heating for the rest of the day.

183204.excerpt_en: Earlier today, the Governor of Svalbard’s office wrote on Facebook: “The polar bear sow that has visited cabins at Hiorthhamn twice in the past week is now heading back toward the area.”
183204.subtitle_en: The polar bear sow that has damaged cabins at Hiorthhamn recently is now heading east.

183208.excerpt_en: School started on Tuesday, but the approximately 50 employees had already been working for some time to prepare for the school year. When Svalbardposten asks to photograph all the new teachers, 11 people come outside with us.
183208.subtitle_en: They come from different parts of southern Norway and are looking forward to starting their new jobs at the school in the far north.
183208.title_en: Eleven New Teachers at the School

183247.excerpt_en: Linn Skåber is one of the authors appearing at the Longyearbyen Literature Festival from 2 to 6 September, together with Lisa Aisato, who illustrated her book.
183247.subtitle_en: Linn Skåber has big plans to see the inside of a Svalbard home and imagines forcing her way into an unfamiliar kitchen.
183247.title_en: “I Want to See How People Live”

183253.excerpt_en: He had four passengers in the car. His driving licence was seized, and the man was questioned today, Sunday. “We have not received the blood-test results yet, but the breathalyzer showed a high blood-alcohol level,” says Senior Police Officer Anders Haugerud of the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
183253.subtitle_en: At around 5 p.m. yesterday, Saturday, a man was caught driving under the influence.

183267.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen should be among the world leaders in environmental standards, cleanliness and waste management. Those of us who live and run businesses here should be the first to lead by example.
183267.subtitle_en: There should never be any doubt that Svalbard Venstre is the Green Party!

183271.excerpt_en: There is a wind farm in Finnmark with substantial spare capacity because of a lack of power cables (Raggovidda). It therefore already has a licence to produce power that is not being fully utilized.
183271.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen’s Progress Party wants the possibility of a hydrogen power plant to be investigated.
183271.title_en: Longyearbyen’s Energy Supply of the Future

183287.excerpt_en: For ten years, Loff House has been a haven for bird enthusiasts in Longyearbyen. Now it has had a facelift thanks to funding from the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund. “The house has always been open to anyone who wants to use it.”
183287.subtitle_en: Those who run the house would be delighted if you paused as you walked past.
183287.tags_en: news, coastal trail, bird, Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund, outdoor life, volunteer work, Loff

183305.excerpt_en: Researchers from several institutions have spent the summer on an expedition as far north as possible. The new research vessel Kronprins Haakon pushed through heavy ice and reached almost 85 degrees north.
183305.subtitle_en: Beneath the ice north of Svalbard live organisms with chemistry that could provide the raw material for the next generation of cancer medicines and new antibiotics.
183305.title_en: Searching for New Medicine Beneath the Polar Ice

183308.excerpt_en: Hans Normann (54) is originally from Malm in Trøndelag, but lives and works in Røyken Municipality in Buskerud. He works for Eltel Networks AS.
183308.subtitle_en: After the position of head of Energiverket had been vacant for a year, Longyearbyen Local Council has found its man.
183308.tags_en: Longyearbyen Energiverket, news, energy manager, Energiverket

183313.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration tells Svalbardposten. The cleanup vessels arrived at the wreck site last Wednesday.
183313.subtitle_en: Work to remove the wreck of the stricken vessel Northguider resumed a week ago and is proceeding at full speed in Hinlopen Strait.

183322.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has had to drive a female polar bear away from the cabin area at Hiorthhamn twice recently. It began on the morning of Saturday the 17th.
183322.subtitle_en: The female polar bear that has approached the settlement at Hiorthhamn twice is still being monitored.
183322.tags_en: news, Tempelfjord female bear, cabin bear, polar bear
183322.title_en: “We Have a Plan for the Polar Bear”

183337.excerpt_en: Five parties are standing in this year’s local elections on the 6th and 7th.
183337.subtitle_en: What matters to you when you vote in Svalbard’s local elections? Svalbardposten has asked questions of the candidates at the top of the parties’ election lists. Here you can see their views on everything from avalanche protection, social dumping, rescue preparedness and waste collection to much more.
183337.tags_en: news, local council chair, politics, local elections
183337.title_en: See What the Top Candidates Have to Say

183358.excerpt_en: The art of practising politics is, in many ways, a balancing act. On the one hand, local politics is in many ways a voluntary contribution to democracy.
183358.subtitle_en: “Use your right to vote! And if you are a politician, don’t be afraid to follow your inner voice and hold a truly unique opinion.”
183358.title_en: Separating the Wheat from the Chaff

183360.excerpt_en: Mushroom inspectors Reidun Bråthen and Even Woldstad are on Svalbard, along with retired biology professor Klaus Høiland.
183360.subtitle_en: Active Outdoors is holding several Svalbard mushroom-related events this week, and nearly 50 people took part in Sunday’s mushroom-picking trip in Adventdalen.

183380.excerpt_en: In addition to violating the Maritime Act’s alcohol provisions, the man is charged with violating the Police Act. He failed to comply with police orders to return to Longyearbyen after setting out with a total of eight passengers on the 15th.
183380.subtitle_en: Prosecutor Berit Sagfossen has requested an unconditional prison sentence for a local man in his 50s. He is charged with being under the influence of alcohol while sailing on Isfjorden with tourists last summer.
183380.tags_en: drink-driving, Maritime Act, news, Kapp Wijk, Polarsyssel
183380.title_en: Prosecutor Seeks Prison Sentence for Drunken Tourist Voyage

183396.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Coastal Administration and the Governor of Svalbard wish to stress that we have maintained close, ongoing dialogue about the cleanup effort since day one. The Norwegian Coastal Administration is leading the work on behalf of the authorities, while the Governor has contributed expertise in rescue and emergency preparedness as well as environmental matters.
183396.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten’s editorial and its 22 August article about Northguider leave the impression that the authorities are not cooperating well on the cleanup following the trawler accident that occurred during the Christmas holidays.
183396.tags_en: environment, reader’s letter, Governor of Svalbard, Norwegian Coastal Administration, Hinlopen, opinions

183411.excerpt_en: “This one is a good specimen—you should take a picture of it,” says Ims, holding up one of the dead mice. In what can only be called a “lab” in the Sea Area, the research team is dissecting the 52 mice caught and handed in by local residents during this winter’s trapping campaign.
183411.subtitle_en: Eva Fuglei, Rolf Anker Ims and Dominique Fauteux are in Longyearbyen to investigate the spread potential of eastern wood mice and parasites on Svalbard.
183411.title_en: Eastern Wood Mice Are Spreading on Svalbard

183414.excerpt_en: The new school year recently began, and the pupils have embarked on another year. Most are looking forward to it, but some are not looking forward to another year at school.
183414.subtitle_en: Not everyone is looking forward to starting school.
183414.tags_en: Svalbard Young Conservatives, politics, opinions, reader’s letter, Conservative Party, school

183428.excerpt_en: This week we are launching a new series of historical photographs. The images are on loan from Svalbard Museum, and the photographer is Hans Tollefsen.
183428.tags_en: Svalbard life, Svea, history, historical photograph

183434.excerpt_en: “This marks the start of the activity year, and offers Longyearbyen’s residents a chance to learn more about what is available here. It is also a great platform for meeting new people,” says Silje M., head of Svalbard Turn.
183434.subtitle_en: As is tradition, Svalbard Turn held an activities fair showcasing this year’s offerings.
183434.title_en: This Year’s Activities Get Under Way

183446.excerpt_en: In today’s society, kindergartens form an important part of the framework surrounding children’s upbringing, and for families more generally they are an important part of everyday life.
183446.subtitle_en: For us, it is not important who owns or runs the kindergarten. We care about what each child and family takes away from a day at kindergarten.
183446.tags_en: politics, local elections, reader’s letter, Conservative Party, kindergarten, opinions
183446.title_en: Choice and Flexibility for Families—A Value in Their Own Right

183453.excerpt_en: In mid-July, Svalbardposten ran the headline “LL Issues Fine to LL.” The story concerned work that LL’s Property Department had begun outside the Business Centre without a building application having been submitted.
183453.subtitle_en: In July, the Planning and Development Department of Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) issued a notice of a fine to LL’s Property Department. LL has now withdrawn the notice against itself.

183468.excerpt_en: “Our oldest started upper secondary school down south, and my mother’s heart told me that perhaps it wasn’t quite right for him to be there alone. So perhaps it was time to move south,” she says.
183468.subtitle_en: Last Tuesday, Kristin Bjellmo marked her 20th anniversary on Svalbard. A couple of days later, she and her family moved south.

183470.excerpt_en: On Tuesday morning, MS “Sjøveien” is being towed by the Governor’s vessel “Polarsyssel”. The destination is Longyearbyen, but it will be a while before they arrive. “It will be a long trip.”
183470.subtitle_en: All engine power was lost, and the passenger ship MS “Sjøveien” had to request assistance in Storfjorden on Monday evening.

183476.excerpt_en: On Monday, Coop Norge’s entire payment system was down. This meant that all payments at the tills had to be processed through a backup solution, with customers signing their names.
183476.subtitle_en: The queues at Svalbardbutikken were enormously long on Monday. “Today we’re hoping things will go much better,” says the store manager.
183476.tags_en: news, Svalbardbutikken, consumer, grocery retail, trade
183476.title_en: Hoping for a Better Day Today

183486.excerpt_en: “The strangest thing of all is that they think I’m the kind of guy who likes walking in the woods and mountains,” Kalvø said about being asked to take part in the celebrity version of 71 Degrees North.
183486.subtitle_en: Are Kalvø from Sunnmøre joked that he has not been on a mountain hike for more than 30 years. Nevertheless, he captivated a packed cultural centre with his skewed take on outdoor enthusiasts.
183486.title_en: Festival Opens with an Evening of Laughter

183491.excerpt_en: BREAKING: “They have now managed to get free of the ice, but for now they are not out of the area with heavy ice. KV “Andenes” will soon arrive.”
183491.subtitle_en: The Joint Rescue Coordination Centre Northern Norway is monitoring the situation involving M/S “Malmö” and maintaining continuous contact with the crew on board. It has taken longer than expected for the Coast Guard to reach the vessel.

183519.excerpt_en: On Saturday, the boat M/S “Malmö” left Longyearbyen for a tour of Svalbard. The original plan was to sail as far north as Kvitøya, but en route—due to weather and ice conditions—the course was changed toward Rossøya, north of Nordaustlandet.
183519.subtitle_en: “I think the situation was handled very well by the crew and the rescue helicopter team,” says Kjersti Holmang, who was aboard M/S “Malmö” when it was evacuated on Tuesday evening.
183519.tags_en: rescue operation, tourism, news, Coast Guard, Hinlopen, helicopter readiness, boat tourism, emergency preparedness, rescue operations
183519.title_en: To Longyearbyen with Only a Phone, Passport and Credit Card

183525.excerpt_en: “We are flying up the equipment needed to take core samples. A total of 27 samples will be drilled over the next three weeks,” says Longyearbyen Local Council project manager Øyvind Hellum.
183525.subtitle_en: The helicopter flying up and down Sukkertoppen on Wednesday morning is part of the safety project for Lia.

183527.excerpt_en: Because it was overweight, this week’s print edition of Svalbardposten was left behind in Tromsø. This means the newspaper will be delayed for everyone on the island.
183527.subtitle_en: The print edition of Svalbardposten could not go on the mail plane and will be delayed.
183527.title_en: Svalbardposten Too Heavy for the Mail Plane

183541.excerpt_en: For the past few years, we have been told repeatedly how important new businesses and business development are for our town. Innovation Norway has had both its own office here and earmarked funds for innovation and new initiatives.
183541.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council’s planning department has generated several major headlines in recent months.

183556.excerpt_en: Under the headline “Another boat with climate activists stuck in the ice: You just have to laugh,” the website document.no ridiculed MS “Malmö” and its passengers.
183556.subtitle_en: The right-wing website document.no mocked “the Swedish climate activists who got stuck in the ice” on Tuesday. “This is misinformation,” say Trygve Monsen and Tore Topp.
183556.tags_en: news, MS “Malmö”, Rønnbeckøyane, Ahlmann Expedition, Hinlopen Strait

183573.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was informed Wednesday afternoon that a workplace accident had occurred in Ny-Ålesund. “A man has been injured, and he was transported by air to Longyearbyen Hospital.”
183573.subtitle_en: A man was flown from Ny-Ålesund to the hospital in Longyearbyen.
183573.tags_en: ambulance mission, workplace mishap, news, Kings Bay, Ny-Ålesund, workplace accident

183575.excerpt_en: They will attend the budding researchers and outdoor life programs, respectively, and arrived in town on Monday morning. “My first impression was very good, with big mountains and beautiful scenery. It looks like a painting,” says Synne.
183575.subtitle_en: Gabrielle Kryvi Lund, Ann-Gaelle Korsmo and Synne Borøy are three of the 46 new folk high school students. The unique experience was what made them apply here.

183578.excerpt_en: “I think it may have been an advantage that I was already known, so I didn’t have to stand on a street corner luring young people in with pizza and soda,” Skåber says with a laugh.
183578.subtitle_en: At Wednesday evening’s festival event, Linn Skåber and Lisa Aisato talked about their work on the book “Til ungdommen,” written by Skåber and illustrated by Aisato.
183578.title_en: “Young People Have Been Given an Undeservedly Bad Reputation”

183590.excerpt_en: The local council has asked for an offering equivalent to 220 daycare places to be created in our town. It has not been said that all these places must be in the same building or organized as a single daycare center.
183590.subtitle_en: In its article in Svalbardposten on 29 August, Svalbard Conservative Party writes that the local council is now going to expand Polarflokken and create a large daycare center with 220 places. This is incorrect.
183590.title_en: The Labour Party’s Daycare Initiative in Longyearbyen

183597.excerpt_en: “The acts of violence were sudden and carried out with an implement capable of causing serious injury and endangering life,” Nord-Troms District Court writes in its judgment. Became heavily intoxicated. It was the night of 1…
183597.subtitle_en: A permanent resident has been sentenced to two and a half months in unconditional prison for a violent incident on New Year’s Day.
183597.tags_en: news, the house, violence, Nord-Troms District Court
183597.title_en: Permanent Resident Sent to Prison After Unprovoked Violence

183611.excerpt_en: “We can only keep our fingers crossed. My stomach hurts just thinking about the epidemic reaching here,” says Vikaune. Fatal consequences. In recent weeks, several veterinarians in the Oslo area have treated dogs with serious illnesses, and several of them have died.
183611.subtitle_en: Veterinarian Astrid Vikaune at Svalbard Vet fears that the disease epidemic spreading among dogs on the mainland will reach Svalbard.
183611.title_en: Worried About the Disease Epidemic on the Mainland

183624.excerpt_en: The Molloy Deep lies 160 kilometers west of Svalbard. It is the deepest point in the Arctic Ocean, and no human has ever been there before.
183624.subtitle_en: No matter where you have been in Svalbard, you can be sure you have not been to where this expedition is going.
183624.tags_en: news, research, expedition, diving, Arctic Ocean
183624.title_en: Heading Down to a Place Absolutely No One Has Been Before

183630.excerpt_en: It is also generally easy to deal with the local council and the Governor’s Office. At the Governor’s Office, you can get help with vehicle registration, a new passport, VAT refunds and other matters requiring an application.
183630.subtitle_en: Many people who live in Longyearbyen think it is a pleasant little settlement to live in. One reason is the short distance to work, daycare and school.

183633.excerpt_en: “It was a strange feeling to see the polar bear sitting in the boat. It was both beautiful and frightening at the same time,” says Dag Nilsen.
183633.subtitle_en: When Jon Kristian Bø (54) and Dag Nilsen (63) returned from their trip, they found that their boat had received a visitor.
183633.title_en: Polar Bear Climbed into the Boat

183638.excerpt_en: You may have seen it in the harbor—the large, dark-blue sailing boat that arrived in Longyearbyen at the end of August.
183638.subtitle_en: Filming of the BBC drama series “The North Water” begins in September. Svalbard will serve as a filming location for around a month, with Hollywood actors in the leading roles.
183638.title_en: Hollywood Actors Come to Svalbard to Film

183669.excerpt_en: In addition to experiencing Svalbard’s fantastic natural environment, we will work to ensure that you can become an active part of the local community here. Many describe folk high school as a year spent in a wonderful bubble.
183669.subtitle_en: It is truly wonderful to welcome the students and staff warmly to Longyearbyen.

183684.excerpt_en: Last week, we showed a picture from the seemingly chaotic construction work in Svea in the summer of 1959, which Svalbard Museum has lent to us. This week, we are showing a picture from the same area and period, taken by the same photographer, Hans Tollefsen.
183684.subtitle_en: Cableway to the mine in Svea in 1959.
183684.tags_en: historical picture, life in Svalbard, history

183696.excerpt_en: Exciting negotiations are in store after this year’s local elections have concluded on 7 October.
183696.subtitle_en: The Conservative Party wants to cooperate with the Liberals, while the Liberals are not thinking in terms of political blocs. Labour would also be happy to repeat its cooperation with the Liberals.
183696.tags_en: politics, local council leader, local elections, news, cooperation
183696.title_en: “The Strangest Models Could Be the Outcome”

183728.excerpt_en: I am genuinely saddened when my colleagues and friends say they feel like second-class citizens in our society because they are not Norwegian citizens. Like many Norwegians, they have found their paradise—and this is where they want to live.
183728.subtitle_en: Local politics in Longyearbyen can be challenging. One of the things I find most difficult is that there is almost an expectation that one should hold racist views.

183734.excerpt_en: In July 1873, some whalers set nets in Raudfjorden to obtain provisions. They expected to catch Arctic char, but ended up filling the nets with cod.
183734.subtitle_en: “The fjords of Svalbard are not a permanent home for cod. It may be physiologically easier for cod to migrate northward in a warmer climate, but perhaps climate is not what regulates its presence in Svalbard’s fjords—at least not directly,” write two researchers in this commentary.
183734.tags_en: polar cod, cod, commentaries, commentary, research, fish, opinions
183734.title_en: On Cod, Climate, Polar Cod and Benthic Animals

183751.excerpt_en: A few weeks ago, a polar bear broke into a cabin in Vindodden. It rummaged around and caused considerable damage before leaving again.
183751.subtitle_en: John-Einar Lockert is one of several cabin owners in Vindodden to have received a visit from a polar bear over the past week. An unusually large number of bear sightings have been reported around the town recently.
183751.tags_en: news, cabin bear, Vindodden, polar bear

183753.excerpt_en: We do not entirely recognize ourselves in this description. The matter was considered in two rounds by the Committee for Education and Culture (OKU), and a consultation was also held in which four weeks of complete summer closure for kindergartens was one proposal.
183753.subtitle_en: In the latest Svalbardposten, Stine Teigen of Høyre claims that Labour and Venstre are leading the push for a compulsory summer holiday period for families with children in kindergarten.
183753.tags_en: opinions, readers’ letter, Høyre, Venstre, local elections

183789.excerpt_en: Originally, the aim was to remove the wrecked shrimp trawler by mid-September. We are already there, but “Northguider” is still lying at Sparreneset in Hinlopen Strait.
183789.subtitle_en: After spending about a week in Woodfjorden, they are back in Hinlopen to work on removing “Northguider”. It will soon be October before they finish.
183789.tags_en: Northguider, news, Hinlopen, wreck, fishing industry, Hinlopen Strait
183789.title_en: Lost Another Working Week in Hinlopen Strait

183796.excerpt_en: To many residents, it may seem that there has been an unusually large amount of construction work in town this summer. But this is mainly due to the Gruvedalen project.
183796.subtitle_en: Several infrastructure measures have been carried out in Longyearbyen this summer.
183796.title_en: A Summer of Digging in Town

183799.excerpt_en: “I have just reported it to the insurance company. Someone broke into my boat, and I know who it was,” Jon-Kristian Bø (54) joked when Svalbardposten met him and his friend Dag Nilsen (63) at the small-boat harbour on Saturday.
183799.subtitle_en: Jon-Kristian Bø’s boat suffered tens of thousands of kroner in damage when the polar bear wrecked it. Nevertheless, he and his friend Dag Nilsen believe they had a wonderful day. The story has attracted considerable attention at home and abroad.
183799.title_en: “It Turned Out to Be a Great Day, After All”

183806.excerpt_en: Several polar bears have been causing trouble in the surrounding areas recently. The cabins at Vindodden have taken a beating, and UNIS has imposed restrictions on areas where it usually conducts fieldwork.
183806.subtitle_en: Increasing numbers of polar bears are staying close to the town and in the cabin areas.

183830.excerpt_en: Geir Hekne has lived in Longyearbyen for virtually his entire life. This Tuesday, he was awarded the Armed Forces Medal for International Operations.
183830.subtitle_en: Geir Hekne received the Armed Forces Medal for International Operations aboard KV “Svalbard”.

183832.excerpt_en: There have been numerous polar bear sightings in the areas around Longyearbyen over the past week. Three bears—a female and two larger cubs—have been seen around Vindodden.
183832.subtitle_en: “Nevertheless, exercise extra caution when going out and about now,” police urge.
183832.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, hiking, police, news, polar bear, safety equipment
183832.title_en: No New Polar Bear Sightings, But …

183838.excerpt_en: “I have never been as broke as I have been during this period,” says Mark Sabbatini when we meet him at a table in Fruene café. This is one of the places where he spends his days.
183838.subtitle_en: After two months in a tent, the town’s English-language journalist once again has a roof over his head. He admits it has been extremely difficult.

183876.excerpt_en: Prosecutor Berit Sagfossen was granted her full request in the case, which was heard in Longyearbyen at the end of August. In addition to 45 days’ unconditional imprisonment and losing the right to operate ships requiring certification for three years, the man must pay NOK 4,000 in legal costs.
183876.subtitle_en: The local man in his 50s has been sentenced to unconditional imprisonment and disqualified from operating ships for three years. Nord-Troms District Court found him guilty of sailing under the influence with tourists on board last summer.
183876.tags_en: Polarsyssel, Kapp Wijk, Maritime Code, news

183880.excerpt_en: The five leading candidates for the position of local council chair adorned Svalbardposten’s front page a couple of weeks ago. All five were men.
183880.subtitle_en: Only 36 percent of those standing for election to the local council are women, even though they make up a much larger share of the population.
183880.tags_en: news, local council, local politics, politics, gender equality, local elections
183880.title_en: Low Female Representation in the Local Council Election

183885.excerpt_en: “I am really looking forward to starting. I enjoy spending time in nature myself,” says Stiberg.
183885.subtitle_en: Merethe Stiberg (42) starts work as project manager for Aktiv i friluft on 1 October.
183885.title_en: New Head of Aktiv i friluft

183898.excerpt_en: The election campaign in Longyearbyen is picking up after a few quiet weeks immediately following the holiday. Local politicians still have time.
183898.subtitle_en: Will we get a centre-right coalition after the election?
183898.title_en: Is the Election Wind Blowing This Way?

183901.excerpt_en: “A polar bear was observed by Bjørndalselva this morning,” the Governor of Svalbard wrote on its Facebook pages late this morning. They were out by car, boat and helicopter to monitor the situation.
183901.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard observed polar bears in several places around town during the morning.
183901.title_en: More Polar Bear Sightings Around Town

183932.excerpt_en: We continue with a new photograph taken by Hans Tollefsen in the late 1950s, which we have borrowed from the Svalbard Museum. The photograph shows the Løwø Bridge, which ran from Mine 1b to Mine 4.

183935.excerpt_en: The BlimE dance has become a regular tradition at Norwegian schools. BlimE is NRK Super’s friendship campaign, whose aim is to promote friendship and caring for one another.
183935.subtitle_en: Within fifteen minutes, all the pupils at the school had performed the 2019 BlimE dance.
183935.tags_en: Longyearbyen School, dance, BlimE, Svalbard life, culture

183938.excerpt_en: “It is very exciting to go and check the fox traps after we have set them when we are tagging foxes. Sometimes fox cubs have gone into the trap, and then we cannot tag it.” “Why not?”
183938.subtitle_en: Anna Marie Sandal Strømseng (7) helped tag the fox that travelled from Svalbard to Canada. Her knowledge of the trapping life is extensive.

183945.excerpt_en: What would Longyearbyen be without choirs, big bands, brass bands on 1 and 17 May, Blåmyra Bluegrass, ukulele bands, jazz bands, blues bands, pop and rock bands, dance groups, cultural exchanges and the Polarjazz warm-up, to name just a few?
183945.subtitle_en: Alongside meaningful and secure jobs, cultural life is the “glue” that holds our community together. It is the very bedrock.
183945.title_en: See the Longyearbyen Community with Heart and Intellect

183992.excerpt_en: The fact is that Høyre put forward a proposal to reverse the change to the kindergarten regulations that introduced compulsory summer holidays.
183992.subtitle_en: The fact that Venstre’s Terje Aunevik and Andre Jenssen do not recognize themselves as having helped reduce flexibility for families with children in the town may be a sign that they are out of step with the society they live in and its residents.
183992.tags_en: opinions, local elections, readers’ letter, kindergartens, politics
183992.title_en: Labour + Venstre = Less Choice and More Bureaucracy

183995.excerpt_en: The young people ran the meeting place themselves for almost ten years, with strong support from the Community Council, their own guards and supervisors. It was open from 2 p.m. to 11 p.m. on weekdays and longer at weekends. A few unfortunate incidents led to the overly simple decision to restrict opening hours.
183995.subtitle_en: In March 2003, young people in Longyearbyen demonstrated for a place of their own. They were heard. Through broad cooperation, UHU was completed in 2004.

184009.excerpt_en: “I aimed my rifle at the polar bear, had it in my sights and was ready to shoot. But then I fired my revolver through the door to scare it off instead,” Reistad says.
184009.subtitle_en: Ole Reistad, 76, had several visits from a polar bear this week. Only a door separated him from one of the bears.
184009.title_en: “At one point I thought things were going to go badly”

184048.excerpt_en: The past four years have gone wonderfully. Except that we shut down all mining in Svea while local politicians were busy doing absolutely nothing.
184048.subtitle_en: The Labour Party, Liberals and Greens joined forces after the last election. Once they had allocated prestigious posts and well-paid office jobs among themselves, political everyday life could begin.
184048.title_en: The past four years in Longyearbyen

184051.excerpt_en: Dean Stig Lægdene conducted the installation. A packed Svalbard Church gave Siv Limstrand a warm welcome.
184051.subtitle_en: On Sunday, Svalbard Church’s first female parish priest was installed.
184051.title_en: “This is where I have been welcomed”

184068.excerpt_en: “Do you have the 19-millimetre socket?” Ørjan Isaksen is deeply focused on securing the antenna to the foundation.
184068.subtitle_en: A mast is being erected on a mountaintop in Forlandet that could save lives. It will help make boat traffic along Svalbard’s northwestern coast safer for many years to come. Next year, the east coast is next.
184068.tags_en: news, Joint Rescue Coordination Centre Northern Norway, boat traffic, rescue operations, boating, emergency preparedness, Norwegian Coastal Administration
184068.title_en: This will make it easier to save lives at sea

184070.excerpt_en: Over the past week, several polar bears have been active in the areas around Longyearbyen and in the cabin areas. Last week, we wrote about the polar bear that climbed into a recreational boat and caused extensive damage.
184070.subtitle_en: The chance of a confrontation and a serious accident is increasing. Safety measures must be considered.

184081.excerpt_en: “We have had capacity problems at Elvesletta. The area has been developed over the past ten years, but nothing has been done about the district heating,” says Torfinn Larsgaard.
184081.subtitle_en: At Elvesletta, Energiverket is replacing the district-heating pipes. While the work was under way on Thursday morning, black water sprayed from the pipes.
184081.tags_en: Longyear Energiverk, news, district heating, Elvesletta, housing, infrastructure
184081.title_en: Black water spilled from the district-heating pipes

184093.excerpt_en: “We are looking at ways to automate more at the Arctic weather stations,” says Roar Skålin, director of the Norwegian Meteorological Institute. The stations he refers to are Bjørnøya, Hopen and Jan Mayen.
184093.subtitle_en: Staffing at Bjørnøya may be reduced from 2020 or 2021. But Hopen will not have fewer staff than it does today.
184093.tags_en: meteorological stations, Norwegian Meteorological Institute, Hopen, Bjørnøya, emergency preparedness, staffing, news
184093.title_en: Fewer people may be stationed at Bjørnøya—Hopen is safe

184104.excerpt_en: State Secretary Magnus Thue (Conservative Party) of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries will present the government’s business and innovation strategy for Svalbard in Longyearbyen. The event is open to everyone. “Svalbard should have an exciting, high-quality business community.”
184104.subtitle_en: On Thursday 3 October, the government will present its vision for Longyearbyen’s future business community.
184104.title_en: Government to present Svalbard’s business strategy

184125.excerpt_en: The three vessels working on salvaging Northguider are now by Nordvestøyane, around 130 kilometres as the crow flies from Sparreneset, where the stricken vessel lies.
