190416.excerpt_en: LL writes this in a press release. Today’s sun café at Huset has also been cancelled.
190416.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) is cancelling all remaining Solfest Week events.

190425.excerpt_en: “A number of trips to conferences and meetings have been cancelled by the organizers. We have minimized travel overall,” says Kim Holmén, international director at the Norwegian Polar Institute in Svalbard, in an email.
190425.subtitle_en: Activity at the Norwegian Polar Institute in Svalbard has been reduced as a result of preventive measures against coronavirus infection.
190425.tags_en: infection control, news, Norwegian Polar Institute, coronavirus crisis, health, public health, working life, illness
190425.title_en: Travel and meetings cancelled for the Polar Institute

190433.excerpt_en: Ronny Strømnes, board chair and acting managing director of Visit Svalbard, describes widespread fear in the tourism industry about the impact of the coronavirus outbreak. Among the organization’s 75 members, 30 of them tour operators, every coronavirus-related news report is showing up in their systems.
190433.subtitle_en: Fear of the coronavirus is already having a major impact on Svalbard’s tourism industry. Fewer bookings and cancellations have so far resulted in a 20 percent decline compared with the same period last year, according to Visit Svalbard.
190433.tags_en: public health, illness, infection control, infection, Ronny Strømnes, tourism, news, coronavirus crisis, Visit Svalbard, preparedness

190441.excerpt_en: This means this week’s newspaper will be delayed. Kenneth Tjønndal, communications adviser at Posten Norge, says the plane had to return on Wednesday because of a technical fault. “A plane is planned to be sent up during the day, as well as tomorrow.”
190441.subtitle_en: The mail plane that was due to arrive in Longyearbyen on Wednesday was unable to land, according to information obtained by Svalbardposten.

190449.excerpt_en: Elsewhere in the region, the figure is 25 percent. The figure comes from a member survey conducted by NHO.
190449.subtitle_en: Businesses in Svalbard are being hit hardest in Norway by the consequences of the coronavirus: 38 percent of companies here have experienced lower demand or cancellations as a result of the virus. That is the highest figure in the country, NHO writes in a press release.
190449.tags_en: infection control, illness, coronavirus crisis, public health, news
190449.title_en: NHO: Svalbard hardest hit in Norway

190465.excerpt_en: As of Thursday morning, the doors of SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge’s Longyearbyen branch are locked.
190465.subtitle_en: Svalbard residents cannot enter the bank without an appointment. For tourists, it is completely closed.
190465.tags_en: illness, SpareBank 1, infection control, news, coronavirus crisis, public health, tourism
190465.title_en: Tourists face a closed bank door

190481.excerpt_en: A society shutting down, bit by bit. That is Norway today, Thursday.
190481.subtitle_en: The school in Longyearbyen is not closing, but that has not been ruled out. What will happen to the confirmation ceremony at Easter is uncertain. Whether the sports facilities will close is to be discussed today, Thursday.
190481.tags_en: Svalbardhallen, Svalbard Church, illness, infection control, news, Longyearbyen Local Council, coronavirus crisis, public health, Svalbard Turn
190481.title_en: Closing or staying open—that is the question

190490.excerpt_en: The sports club’s board spoke by phone on Thursday morning. They unanimously agreed that, given how the coronavirus situation has developed, cancelling the ski marathon was the best course of action.
190490.subtitle_en: The Svalbard Ski Marathon has been cancelled. In addition, all activities organized by Svalbard Turn are suspended through March. “This is of course very sad,” says board chair Per Nilssen.
190490.tags_en: Svalbard Ski Marathon, infection control, news, coronavirus crisis, public health, illness
190490.title_en: No one will be seen on this trail this year

190498.excerpt_en: With some excitement at seeing something so rare, parts of the Svalbardposten staff got up from the lunch table when a flock of ptarmigans came in to land outside. There may have been 15–20 birds in the group.
190498.subtitle_en: A flock of ptarmigans landed in central Longyearbyen around noon on Thursday.
190498.title_en: Ptarmigan flock in the town centre

190508.excerpt_en: “We have no surplus of air ambulance doctors. In the short term, people can work extra shifts, but in the event of illness, we are already struggling.”
190508.subtitle_en: Ole Magnus Filseth is the on-call anesthesiologist in Svalbard this week. In the event of illness or quarantine within the rescue service, staffing will become a challenge.
190508.title_en: Preparing procedures for the rescue service

190520.excerpt_en: At a press conference on Thursday afternoon, Prime Minister Erna Solberg said they were implementing what she called “drastic measures.” The measures will remain in place until further notice, through the 26th.
190520.subtitle_en: All schools, kindergartens and colleges in the country are closing, Prime Minister Erna Solberg says. Local Council leader Arild Olsen (Labour) believes the measures are long overdue.
190520.tags_en: infection control, news, illness, coronavirus crisis, public health, shops, society

190529.excerpt_en: In recent years, tourism has developed into a major and important industry in Svalbard. The number of cruise tourists is increasing, as is the number of expedition cruises to the archipelago in the far north.
190529.subtitle_en: This situation could have serious consequences. The government must consider measures.
190529.title_en: Tourism industry could be hit very hard

190537.excerpt_en: “A little extra, yes. Things like milk and toilet paper,” Brit Enoksen tells Svalbardposten.
190537.subtitle_en: Several people are buying a little extra from the grocery store, just in case. Coop manager Ronny Strømnes says it is unnecessary. They will ensure supplies.

190549.excerpt_en: From 6 p.m. on Thursday, businesses offering hairdressing and skincare services, among others, were prohibited from operating. The government announced this and a long list of other stringent measures to prevent the spread of the coronavirus on Thursday afternoon.
190549.subtitle_en: The owner of a spa in Longyearbyen is concerned about the consequences of the infection-control measures and hopes for schemes that can compensate for some of the lost income.
190549.tags_en: Polar Spa, Lompensenteret, coronavirus crisis, infection control, news

190569.excerpt_en: On Thursday afternoon, many people visited the shop and filled their shopping carts with goods. Some shelves were emptied. “We do not want people to stockpile; there is no reason to.”
190569.subtitle_en: There is no reason to buy extra food, assures Ronny Strømnes, managing director of Svalbardbutikken.
190569.tags_en: infection control, coronavirus crisis, public health, illness, news

190618.excerpt_en: “Generally, we are considering reduced opening hours. As far as I know, there are no plans to reduce opening hours at Lompensenteret in Longyearbyen as a result of the infection-control measures,” Ola Stavnsborg, security director at Olav Thon Gruppen (OTG), tells Svalbardposten.
190618.subtitle_en: Infection-control measures are affecting traffic at Longyearbyen’s only shopping centre, but there are no plans to reduce opening hours or close.
190618.tags_en: infection control, news, Lompensenteret, coronavirus crisis, retail, public health, illness

190626.excerpt_en: Senior officers from the Governor’s Office checked arriving passengers when they reached Svalbard Airport. Svalbardposten understands that the checks were carried out thoroughly in Tromsø and at Gardermoen, and that consequently no one was sent straight back after today’s inspection.
190626.subtitle_en: All passengers who flew to Svalbard today were checked on arrival.
190626.tags_en: infection control, illness, coronavirus crisis, public health, news
190626.title_en: This is what arriving air passengers faced

190634.excerpt_en: Since Thursday evening, the Kroa restaurant in Longyearbyen has reduced the number of guests it accepts, in line with the guidelines from the infection-control authorities. “This is a catastrophe. The employees have received temporary-layoff notices.”
190634.subtitle_en: Food and drink establishments in Longyearbyen are making major changes to meet infection-control requirements. Some employees have received temporary-layoff notices, one pub is closed and others are focusing more on food deliveries.
190634.tags_en: infection control, coronavirus crisis, nightlife industry, news

190656.excerpt_en: The fjord was steaming heavily, and there was no doubt that the sea was undergoing substantial cooling. The day was 3.
190656.subtitle_en: UNIS was out again, this time with Polarsyssel and the students on the marine biology course AB-202.
190656.title_en: New update on sea temperatures in Isfjorden

190668.excerpt_en: Svalbard residents who have been abroad, except in Sweden and Finland, must quarantine on the mainland for 14 days before travelling onwards.
190668.subtitle_en: People returning home to Svalbard after being abroad must first spend two weeks in quarantine on the mainland. This is stipulated in a new regulation.
190668.title_en: New regulation stops people returning home to Svalbard

190676.excerpt_en: There are few customers and plenty of space in the Skinnboden shops in Longyearbyen. Only a couple of residents and a handful of domestic tourists stop by.
190676.subtitle_en: The virus measures have laid the high season waste. The head of Skinnboden fears for the future of Svalbard’s entire tourism industry.
190676.tags_en: infection control, tourism, coronavirus crisis, retail, news
190676.title_en: “All of Svalbard is grinding to a halt”

190688.excerpt_en: The government’s decision to close all of Norway’s airports from 8 a.m. Monday does not apply to domestic flights.
190688.subtitle_en: Air traffic to and from Longyearbyen will operate more or less as normal from Monday as well, according to Avinor.
190688.tags_en: news, infection control, air traffic, coronavirus crisis
190688.title_en: Svalbard flights to operate as normal

190696.excerpt_en: Many workplaces in Svalbard are being affected by the infection-control measures. Employers and employees whom Svalbardposten has spoken to in recent days are expected to be hit by temporary layoffs.
190696.subtitle_en: Many people affected by the coronavirus crisis are entitled to unemployment benefits from NAV, subject to certain conditions depending on nationality and employment contract.

190712.excerpt_en: Just hours after the announcement, the evacuation of foreign tourists from Longyearbyen was a reality. Those who had arrived here from other countries after the 27th.
190712.subtitle_en: On Sunday evening, around 130 tourists who had been in coronavirus quarantine in Longyearbyen were put on a flight to Oslo.
190712.tags_en: illness, news, coronavirus crisis, public health, tourism, infection control

190724.excerpt_en: “Svalbard is being hit especially hard by the virus crisis. We depend largely on tourism, which is now disappearing entirely.”
190724.subtitle_en: Local businesses depend on financial assistance to survive the virus crisis. “We are being hit harder than elsewhere,” warns Terje Aunevik, head of the Svalbard Business Association.
190724.tags_en: Svalbard Business Association, infection control, news, coronavirus crisis, retail, public health, illness

190732.excerpt_en: The hospital, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) and the Governor of Svalbard will consider that question on Tuesday.
190732.subtitle_en: “When Tromsø has barred people from Dovre and southwards, it is natural to ask whether Svalbard should do the same,” says Knut Selmer, chief medical officer for communicable-disease control at Longyearbyen Hospital.
190732.title_en: Further restrictions to be considered on Tuesday

190740.excerpt_en: The bear was spotted shortly before five o’clock on Monday afternoon. “I can confirm that we have a polar bear situation and that we are working on a plan to get the bear under control. We have people out both in the air and on the ground,” says senior police officer Atle Rokkan at the Governor’s Office.
190740.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is monitoring the situation involving the polar bear in Bjørndalen. They will try to drive the bear farther away early tomorrow morning. The Governor urges people to be especially vigilant.
190740.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, news, Isfjorden, polar bear, Bjørndalen, Vestpynten

190756.excerpt_en: Svalbard businesses have been given very little time to comment on proposed tightening of Svalbard’s environmental regulations (see fact box). Many in the industry have reacted to this.
190756.subtitle_en: “While we are flat on our backs and trying to salvage what we can, the authorities continue with business as usual,” says Frigg Jørgensen of Aeco.
190756.tags_en: regulation, news, Norwegian Environment Agency, tourism, coronavirus crisis, Aeco, business
190756.title_en: Tourism industry on its knees—with government deadlines still tight

190766.excerpt_en: “A polar bear was spotted at Vestpynten at around 6:30 this morning.”
190766.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has posted information about a polar bear that has taken to the water and is swimming north in Isfjorden.
190766.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, Isfjorden, polar bear, Vestpynten, Bjørndalen, news

190776.excerpt_en: “We are retaining a basic staffing level and are trying, among other things, to keep the Radisson BLU Polar Hotel in Longyearbyen open, along with Barentzpub, IGP and Longyear78. They will operate with limited opening hours to serve the local population during a period with no tourism for the foreseeable future,” Andresen says.
190776.subtitle_en: Around 100 employees at Hurtigruten Svalbard have been temporarily laid off as a result of the coronavirus crisis. Many of those laid off will be left with no income at all. Hurtigruten management is calling for government support schemes to be introduced quickly.
190776.tags_en: coronavirus crisis, working life, news, Hurtigruten Svalbard

190792.excerpt_en: Olav Thon Gruppen (OTG) writes this in a press release. Lompensenteret is part of the Amfi shopping-centre chain, which is owned by OTG. “We consider the situation surrounding the coronavirus crisis to be dramatic for Norwegian retail.”
190792.subtitle_en: All the tenants at Lompensenteret in Longyearbyen are being granted a deferral on their rent payments.
190792.tags_en: infection control, illness, coronavirus crisis, public health, news

190800.excerpt_en: This emerges from a press release issued by LL on Tuesday evening. “This is a highly intrusive measure for those affected, both for individuals and for businesses.”
190800.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) decided this evening that everyone arriving in Longyearbyen from the mainland must quarantine at home for 14 days after arrival.
190800.tags_en: infection control, illness, Longyearbyen Community Council, coronavirus crisis, public health, news
190800.title_en: Imposes home quarantine on all arrivals

190808.excerpt_en: “It’s terribly sad. One side of the matter is, of course, what happens to the company and its income.”
190808.subtitle_en: A week ago, furloughs were being considered. Now 85 percent of the company he leads has been furloughed. “The mood is not good,” says John-Einar Lockert.
190808.tags_en: employment, tourism, business, news, coronavirus crisis, employment rights, economy
190808.title_en: Thinking about the fate of furloughed workers

190816.excerpt_en: Fortunately, we have svalbardposten.no, where we can continuously publish updated news. As I write this, Longyearbyen is quiet.
190816.subtitle_en: The past week has been like sitting in the middle of an unreal “science-fiction film” where we have no idea what will happen in the next few minutes.
190816.tags_en: illness, opinions, editorial, coronavirus crisis, public health, infection control

190832.excerpt_en: Svalbard is outside the Schengen Area, and special rules therefore apply. There are no forms of social assistance; for example, the Social Services Act does not apply to people living on Svalbard.
190832.subtitle_en: Many furloughed workers on Svalbard will be left entirely without income. Parliament is being asked to resolve this.
190832.tags_en: Parliament, NAV, coronavirus crisis, tourism, news

190866.excerpt_en: Over the past week, between five and 20 passengers have been aboard the flights arriving at Svalbard Airport. Following the Community Council’s decision on Tuesday evening requiring everyone arriving from the mainland to self-quarantine at home for 14 days, there will be even fewer.
190866.subtitle_en: How often flights to and from Svalbard will operate in the time ahead is currently uncertain.
190866.tags_en: transport, Svalbard Airport, coronavirus crisis, air traffic, news

190874.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) points out that parts of the national crisis package do not work on Svalbard. “...reductions or deferrals of taxes and charges would, because of Svalbard legislation, have no effect,” it says.
190874.subtitle_en: Unemployment benefits costing NOK 4.5 million a month. Millions in cuts to municipal fees. That is the price tag for ensuring the Svalbard community survives, Longyearbyen Community Council wrote in a letter to all parliamentary party groups on Wednesday afternoon.
190874.title_en: Svalbard unemployment benefits cost NOK 4.5 million a month

190907.excerpt_en: Store Norske went through its stockpiles in Svea and Gruve 7 to see whether it had equipment that could be used during the coronavirus pandemic.
190907.subtitle_en: Store Norske is sending 100 protective suits and 12,000 dust masks to the University Hospital of North Norway in Tromsø.
190907.tags_en: infection control, coronavirus crisis, public health, illness, news
190907.title_en: Sends protective equipment to UNN in Tromsø

190919.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten’s newest additions have spent a winter’s night outdoors before. Just not here.
190919.subtitle_en: The organiser and designer are hatching new ideas in a cosy living room at Vestpynten. 2019 was a good year. Now Jim Johansen and Kanerva Karpo are pressing ahead with their respective companies.

190929.excerpt_en: Astrup is a co-owner and board chairman of Svalbard Adventures and has helped build up the company over many years. Speaking by phone from Switzerland, he says he is working extremely hard to do what is needed to save the business. “In this situation, it’s frustrating to be sitting down here.”
190929.subtitle_en: “As an investor in Svalbard, I don’t take this lightly,” says Morten Astrup.
190929.tags_en: business, tourism, coronavirus crisis, working life, news
190929.title_en: Business owner frustrated by the situation

190945.excerpt_en: “The dogs are like my children; I can’t start putting them down. In the worst case, we’ll have to fly them south or ask whether people can keep them at home,” says Audun Salte of Svalbard Husky.
190945.subtitle_en: The dog kennels, like all tourism-oriented businesses, have been hit hard by the coronavirus pandemic.

190971.excerpt_en: She has set herself up at a desk at home. Unlike at school, she has the company of her dog, Kasper.
190971.subtitle_en: “It was pretty boring at first, but then I started getting used to it,” says sixth-grader Ada Feiner-Endresen after several days of home schooling.
190971.tags_en: school, children, coronavirus crisis, Longyearbyen School, news, education
190971.title_en: Home schooling brings out creativity—with just one pupil at school

191008.excerpt_en: On Thursday, Parliament decided that crisis measures should be introduced specifically for Svalbard. A special unemployment-benefit solution has been proposed for furloughed workers who are now without income because of the Svalbard rules, along with grants allowing Longyearbyen Community Council to cut the price of electricity and other services.
191008.subtitle_en: It will be weeks or days before furloughed people without income can receive emergency unemployment benefits, says Community Council leader Arild Olsen.
191008.tags_en: news, economy, coronavirus crisis, employment rights, crisis

191016.excerpt_en: “With each day and each week that passes, we in healthcare will have to think about problems other than infection control. The more time passes, the more real the problem becomes,” he says.
191016.subtitle_en: Being in quarantine or working from home can be taxing. Knut Selmer, the infection-control doctor at Longyearbyen Hospital, says one of the most important things now is not to become inactive.
191016.title_en: “Get outside and go for a walk”

191024.excerpt_en: In recent days, there have been intensive meetings between the Ministry of Transport and the airlines Norwegian and SAS. On Thursday, the government presented a crisis package for the two airlines.
191024.subtitle_en: “This is more than we had almost dared hope for,” says the head of Svalbard Airport.
191024.tags_en: Parliament, Svalbard Airport, news, coronavirus crisis, flights, government
191024.title_en: Good news for those who need to fly

191032.excerpt_en: Managing director Ronny Strømnes expects major consequences for the store’s turnover without tourists and students in town. Several permanent residents have also chosen to travel to the mainland while furloughed. “So far, turnover at the store has fallen by 30 to 40 percent.”
191032.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken has so far furloughed 18 employees. Further furloughs are being considered on an ongoing basis.
191032.tags_en: Svalbardbutikken, news, coronavirus crisis, illness, infection control
191032.title_en: Furloughs staff and reduces opening hours

191042.excerpt_en: This is stated in a press release from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security. The move follows a proposal from Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) to introduce emergency unemployment benefits for an estimated 300 furloughed foreign workers who, because of the rules applying to Svalbard, receive no income while furloughed. “We are now creating a temporary benefit scheme for Longyearbyen.”
191042.subtitle_en: The government is introducing a benefit scheme for people left without income after being furloughed on Svalbard. (English version at the end of the article)
191042.tags_en: news, government, working life, coronavirus crisis
191042.title_en: Government to secure income for foreign furloughed workers

191050.excerpt_en: She runs one of Longyearbyen’s many small tourism businesses. As a result of the coronavirus, she has had to furlough everyone.
191050.subtitle_en: Doreen Lampe, managing director of Spitzbergen Adventures, is one of many now desperately searching for some good news.
191050.tags_en: tourism, economy, news, coronavirus crisis, business

191058.excerpt_en: On their blog, they write that the annual film festival is under way, although some of the programme had to be moved because of hysterically clear and fine weather. The small crew, living in complete isolation until the summer changeover, are certainly in high spirits.
191058.subtitle_en: The nine people stationed at the meteorological station on Bear Island this season have enjoyed a film festival over the past week, while the coronavirus rages almost everywhere else in Norway.

191068.excerpt_en: The snowmobile driver drove straight into the wall at Polarsenteret. “We have spoken to the person involved, who explained that the snowmobile went straight from the parking lot at 232, across the road and into the wall. The throttle probably got stuck,” says senior police officer Kjell Arne Lundin at the Governor’s Office.
191068.subtitle_en: The Governor was notified of the snowmobile accident at around six o’clock.

191084.excerpt_en: Olav had never been to Svalbard before, but had seen the archipelago on maps and learned at school that there was activity up here. “I applied for a job with Store Norske when I was 16, but was told I was too young. Eventually, the dream was forgotten,” he says.
191084.subtitle_en: Olav Iversen (55) works as chief mate aboard the Polarsyssel. He has felt drawn to Svalbard ever since he was 16.

191092.excerpt_en: I lived in Longyearbyen in the winter of 1992/93, commissioned to draw up plans for an information centre for culture and nature, later renamed “Svalbardporten”.
191092.subtitle_en: In these sunny days, here is a small reminder that “the old hospital staircase” is not quite as old as some may think.
191092.title_en: How Old Is the Old Hospital Staircase?

191100.excerpt_en: All civilisations have always been exposed to dangers from nature. Ingenuity has created bounded spaces in which human beings, under conditions and at risk, are able to exercise control.
191100.subtitle_en: A virus is forcing the entire world to change its everyday life. Perhaps its way of living for good.
191100.tags_en: illness, opinion, reader contribution, coronavirus crisis, public health, infection control

191120.excerpt_en: The adventure begins at the end of May and will last six months: Ingvill Engdal got a job as an assistant meteorologist on Bjørnøya and is looking forward to her six-month stay. Her employer will be the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, which operates the station on the island.
191120.subtitle_en: Ingvill Engdal is taking a break from her shop job in Longyearbyen to experience Bjørnøya.
191120.tags_en: meteorology, news, Bjørnøya, working life, people

191128.excerpt_en: The rearmost residential buildings at Elvesletta Nord are shifting as a result of deep foundation piling, as well as water and ice in the ground. This has led to perforated wind barriers and problems with pipes and other building components.
191128.subtitle_en: Store Norske plans to demolish, reuse and build more housing at Elvesletta Nord.
191128.tags_en: news, Store Norske housing, Elvesletta Nord
191128.title_en: Working on a Major New Housing Project

191138.excerpt_en: A hotel at the airport? It sounds completely unreal given the situation Svalbard now finds itself in.
191138.subtitle_en: Now, of course, everything has been put on hold.
191138.tags_en: tourism, Hurtigruten Svalbard, Svalbard Airport, hotel, airport, Avinor, news

191148.excerpt_en: The man was from Tromsø and part of a larger tour group that lost a snowmobile in a lead in Van Mijenfjorden on 12 April last year.
191148.subtitle_en: The man first tested the ice by jumping on it, then carefully drove across the lead. The ice broke, the snowmobile sank, and its owner was fined NOK 15,000 for environmental damage.

191156.excerpt_en: There has been much speculation about how many planes will now fly between Longyearbyen and the mainland. The number of tourists does not appear likely to increase significantly in the coming weeks, but Avinor and the airlines want to keep the important route to and from the archipelago operating.
191156.subtitle_en: There will be flights to and from Svalbard every day except Saturdays in the period ahead.
191156.tags_en: news, Svalbard Airport, airport, flights, coronavirus crisis
191156.title_en: Almost Normal Number of Flights from 30 March

191164.excerpt_en: It was the Working Committee of Longyearbyen Community Council that approved the postponement at a meeting before the weekend. Originally, the school was due to reopen this coming Friday, 27 March.
191164.subtitle_en: The planned return to school after the coronavirus closure has been postponed until after Easter.

191184.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard received a report from a snowmobile convoy shortly before five o’clock on Monday afternoon.
191184.subtitle_en: A snowmobile convoy returning to Longyearbyen from Barentsburg had to be picked up by the Governor of Svalbard’s helicopter.
191184.title_en: Got Stuck and Had to Be Rescued

191200.excerpt_en: Local authorities’ crisis assistance to the local business community came in the form of two decisions at a recent extraordinary meeting of the Working Committee (AU). Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) is launching an initiative to help local businesses as much as possible.
191200.subtitle_en: The local council has drawn up a list of assignments that local businesses are to receive quickly.
191200.tags_en: news, coronavirus crisis, business, Longyearbyen Community Council

191208.excerpt_en: “Are there many sick people in town?” “A great many people are at home with colds. In such cases, we provide a lot of advice by phone,” says Selmer.
191208.subtitle_en: On Tuesday afternoon, four coronavirus test results were still pending. The results will most likely be available by Thursday, according to Knut Selmer, chief infection-control physician at Longyearbyen Hospital.

191216.excerpt_en: The payment deferral was approved by the Administration Committee (AU) at an extraordinary meeting on Friday. In practice, this means that the road-fee bills arriving these days will have their payment deadline postponed until 1 September.
191216.subtitle_en: The deadline for paying the 2020 road fee has been postponed to 1 September.
191216.title_en: Road Fee Payment Deadline Postponed Until Autumn

191224.excerpt_en: The annual clean-up cruises organised by the Governor of Svalbard are a popular activity. They give you the chance to see parts of Svalbard that you rarely get to visit, while making a useful contribution to the environment.
191224.subtitle_en: Twenty-four people have been selected to take part in two clean-up cruises aboard Polarsyssel this summer. Whether the cruises will actually go ahead is for the Governor of Svalbard to decide later.
191224.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, beach litter, Polarsyssel, news, environmental protection, marine litter, coronavirus crisis, clean-up cruise, rubbish, clean-up
191224.title_en: Are You Among the Lucky Ones Going on a Multi-Day Clean-Up Cruise This Summer?

191232.excerpt_en: In a press release, it writes: “Due to the situation related to Covid-19, with travel and quarantine restrictions, the NFD land administrators will not be physically present in Longyearbyen from the first day.”
191232.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries (NFD) has postponed the opening of its local office with two land administrators in Longyearbyen. The office was due to open on 1 April.

191248.excerpt_en: A couple of weeks ago it became clear that the coronavirus had put a stop to this spring’s ski marathon. Together with the running marathon in June, the ski race is the sports club’s two most important sources of external income.
191248.subtitle_en: Svalbard Turn is taking a loss on the ski marathon. “Fortunately, most of those who registered are transferring their entry fees to next year,” says Silje M. Hagen.
191248.title_en: Running Marathon in the Danger Zone

191283.excerpt_en: That is shown by the autopsy report, which is now complete. The Governor of Svalbard will now, in cooperation with the Norwegian Polar Institute, review procedures for pursuing and anaesthetising polar bears to prevent similar cases in the future.
191283.subtitle_en: The polar bear that died during helicopter transport suffered circulatory failure/shock as a result of prolonged pursuit, stress and drug-induced anaesthesia.
191283.tags_en: news, polar bear, Governor of Svalbard, Norwegian Polar Institute
191283.title_en: Female Polar Bear Died of Shock

191299.excerpt_en: There will be no regular allocation from the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund this spring because of the coronavirus crisis. The reason is simple: without traffic to Svalbard, the fund has no income.
191299.subtitle_en: Visit Svalbard is receiving support from the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund. Everyone else will have to wait until autumn.
191299.tags_en: Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund, Visit Svalbard, culture, coronavirus crisis, news
191299.title_en: Environmental Funds for Visit Svalbard Project

191307.excerpt_en: “We want to offer something extra in these times. Many people have asked for library services, which we are happy about, and this is entirely possible in little Longyearbyen,” says library director Elin Anita Olsrud.
191307.subtitle_en: The car is decorated and ready, and from today you can have books delivered to your door.

191323.excerpt_en: Friday will be the final opening day for Skinnboden at Lompen Shopping Centre in Longyearbyen. The local store management has no further comment, referring questions to Skinnboden Lompen AS owner and chairman Terje Sørgulen.
191323.subtitle_en: After Friday, Skinnboden will have just one shop on Svalbard: the store at Lompen Shopping Centre is closing its doors.
191323.tags_en: news, coronavirus crisis, business, Lompen Shopping Centre

191331.excerpt_en: It is quiet, and people are mostly staying at home. A few cafés and restaurants are still open, as are most shops.
191331.subtitle_en: Although the coronavirus has not yet settled in Longyearbyen at the time of writing, it has brought most normal activity to a standstill.

191339.excerpt_en: Espen Rotevatn, principal of Svalbard Folk High School, says these are strange days after the school was closed and 46 students sent home because of the coronavirus crisis. The father of four is now running the school from his home office. “It is extremely challenging, but people are capable and creative.”
191339.subtitle_en: The first upper-secondary folk high school class in history was sent home from Longyearbyen. Creative solutions are keeping teaching going until they meet again.
191339.tags_en: news, Svalbard Folk High School, coronavirus crisis

191347.excerpt_en: Earlier this week, news was presented about unemployment on the mainland. There has not been higher unemployment in the kingdom since the Second World War.
191347.subtitle_en: Unemployment has exploded on Svalbard. Two weeks ago, nine people were registered as completely unemployed. On Monday this week, there were 261. That equals more than 14 percent of the workforce.
191347.tags_en: news, downsizing, NAV, coronavirus crisis, jobs, working life, Tax Administration, travel industry, employment

191371.excerpt_en: “As I understand it, our costs or lost income will be covered. That is very good—and only right—when the authorities have ordered us to close the business,” says John-Einar Lockert, co-owner of the Saxifraga hair salon in Longyearbyen.
191371.subtitle_en: “When the authorities order us to close, it is very good—and only right—that the costs are covered too,” says the owner of a hair salon.
191371.title_en: Hair Salon on the Government’s Crisis Package:

191379.excerpt_en: Those laid off because of the coronavirus crisis who, because they come from countries outside the EU/EEA, are not entitled to income protection or subsistence support will receive their own support scheme. Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) requested this, and the government’s proposal follows a parliamentary request passed by the Storting on the 19th.
191379.subtitle_en: The government proposes allocating NOK 7 million in crisis assistance to third-country nationals on Svalbard who have been laid off.
191379.title_en: NOK 7 Million in Crisis Aid for Foreigners on Svalbard

191387.excerpt_en: As of March 27, the month’s mean temperature was 0.4 degrees below normal—that is, the average temperature between 1961 and 1990.
191387.subtitle_en: Since November 2010, Svalbard has averaged warmer-than-normal temperatures. March appears set to break the “new normal.”

191395.excerpt_en: NHO asked member companies across the country the same question. Nationally, one in three companies says the risk of bankruptcy is real.
191395.subtitle_en: NHO has taken the pulse of its member companies. On Svalbard, there is barely a pulse left to measure. Half of the Svalbard businesses surveyed by the association say there is a real risk they will go bankrupt.
191395.tags_en: travel industry, economy, news, coronavirus crisis, business
191395.title_en: Half Say Risk of Bankruptcy Is Real

191403.excerpt_en: Svalbard residents from countries outside the EU/EEA are being hit particularly hard by the coronavirus crisis when they are laid off. This group is referred to as third-country nationals and is not covered by unemployment benefit schemes.
191403.subtitle_en: The government proposes that so-called third-country nationals on Svalbard receive social assistance when their jobs and incomes disappear.
191403.tags_en: politics, Svalbard business association, coronavirus crisis, working life, news

191411.excerpt_en: Dear Kjerstin Askholt and Morten Wedege! I have great respect for much of the work you do, but now it is probably time to adapt the map to the terrain.
191411.subtitle_en: “Dear Kjerstin, bring out the ice chart of Svalbard—and measure what percentage of the ice lies in the areas you have now closed, compared with the fact that you have removed the tourism industry’s core product,” writes Morten E. Astrup in this contribution.
191411.tags_en: Tempelfjorden, Governor of Svalbard, travel industry, opinion, reader letter, polar bear, traffic ban, Billefjorden, tourism
191411.title_en: How Much Ice Must There Be Around Svalbard Before Closing the Fjords Is No Longer Necessary?

191429.excerpt_en: Measured in kroner, 2019 was the best year yet for Longyearbyen-based Wildphoto Travel. The travel company, established in 2012, had revenue of more than NOK 24 million last year and a solid profit of NOK 6 million.
191429.subtitle_en: All 19 nature photography expeditions planned for this year could be cancelled, putting the company’s future at risk. The government’s new crisis package gives Wildphoto Travel hope of surviving the coronavirus crisis.
191429.title_en: From Record Year to Crisis Mood

191455.excerpt_en: It is in times of crisis that we test whether the principles of the democratic rule of law hold. Many have compared the fight against the coronavirus to a war.
191455.subtitle_en: Never have editor-led media been more important. Let us hope they survive.
191455.title_en: Journalism in a Time of Crisis

191465.excerpt_en: “Today we said goodbye to one of the strongest women we have ever known—Mary-Ann. The woman who had indescribable energy and determination to create her own world, remain positive and make it through every difficulty along the way.”
191465.subtitle_en: Mary-Ann’s Polarrigg – Svalbard posted news of the death on its Facebook page. Dahle had battled cancer for a long time.
191465.title_en: Polarriggen Invites People to Light Candles

191483.excerpt_en: Parliament is currently working on a new white paper on cooperation to improve maritime safety.
191483.subtitle_en: “Work to strengthen Longyearbyen as the northernmost main base for Norway’s rescue service is continuing,” says Member of Parliament Steinar Reiten (Christian Democratic Party).
191483.tags_en: politics, news, Northguider, High North policy, emergency preparedness, Parliament, rescue operations, shipping
191483.title_en: Will Strengthen Longyearbyen as the Northernmost Rescue Base

191491.excerpt_en: This is from one of the lesser-known mineral extraction projects on Svalbard. The workers in the photograph are working at the zinc blende deposit.
191491.subtitle_en: This week’s historical photograph is from Sinkholmen in Bellsund in the early 1920s.

191499.excerpt_en: Svalbard reindeer are the largest herbivores in Svalbard’s tundra ecosystem. Since several important factors affecting population development, such as predation, disease and parasites, are effectively absent, weather and climate play a greater role here than among other subspecies of wild reindeer.
191499.subtitle_en: Svalbard reindeer are experiencing the fastest temperature increases on land. More than forty years of reindeer counts and weather data now show that local differences in climate trends in summer and winter contribute to major differences in population development among reindeer living along the coast and inland.
191499.title_en: Climate Warming Creates Local Contrasts in Svalbard Reindeer Population Trends

191513.excerpt_en: The owner of forcibly closed Polar Spa believes the government’s latest crisis support scheme looks promising. In the meantime, Camilla Flygel Granstrøm is selling her spa products online.
191513.subtitle_en: Polar Spa is selling its products through an online store after the salon was forced to close because of the coronavirus.
191513.tags_en: business, Polar Spa, Lompensenteret, coronavirus crisis, news
191513.title_en: Runs Online Store After Salon Closure

191521.excerpt_en: A new art gallery on a previously undeveloped plot in Sjøområdet could become a new meeting place for people and art.
191521.subtitle_en: He has worked on the Svalbard Art Center project since 2016. Now a neighbor notification has been sent out. “I want to create a new cultural industry from old industry,” says Stein Henningsen.
191521.tags_en: news, culture, gallery, Sjøområdet, land-use plan, art
191521.title_en: From Welding Hall in Svea to Art Gallery in Sjøområdet

191531.excerpt_en: Following a letter from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security a few days ago, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) has submitted proposals for inclusion in the revised national budget for 2020. The list sent to the ministry was considered by the Administration Committee before the weekend and contains several measures intended to “maintain economic activity in Longyearbyen.”
191531.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) is requesting a total of NOK 178.5 million from the government in a coronavirus crisis package.
191531.tags_en: news, coronavirus crisis, state budget, Longyearbyen Local Council
191531.title_en: Asks State for NOK 180 Million in Crisis Aid

191539.excerpt_en: The tender competition had been announced and companies had submitted bids in March. Now the tender has been cancelled and the project postponed. “The plan was to start both this project and construction of an avalanche barrier this summer.”
191539.subtitle_en: The coronavirus situation is forcing NVE to postpone construction of snow fences on Sukkertoppen until next year.
191539.tags_en: avalanche protection, Sukkertoppen, news, NVE, tender, demolition on the slope

191561.excerpt_en: “It seems many are waiting in town to see whether there will be work this summer. If the summer season does not happen, many of them will probably move away,” says Leiterer.
191561.subtitle_en: Franka Leiterer of the guides’ association is concerned about the knowledge that could be lost if many guides choose to move away from town.

191583.excerpt_en: These are strange times, including for the parish priest. Siv Limstrand has now completed her quarantine. “Not being able to move around as one is used to is an experience I think many of us find challenging and new.”
191583.subtitle_en: Holy Thursday’s music service will be the only chance to experience the inside of Svalbard Church for some time—but only via a screen.
191583.tags_en: Easter, culture, coronavirus crisis, Svalbard Church, people, news

191593.excerpt_en: The student welfare organisation, which houses UNIS students, receives NOK 129 million to build the 180 student homes included in the project presented earlier this year. Seven student welfare organisations and one housing foundation will receive a total of NOK 726 million to build 2,000 new student housing units.
191593.subtitle_en: The Arctic Student Welfare Organisation of Norway receives the most funding to build the planned student housing in the financial package from the Ministry of Education.
191593.title_en: Receives NOK 129 Million to Build 180 Student Homes

191609.excerpt_en: According to climate researcher Ketil Isaksen of the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, the average temperature was half a degree below normal as of March 31.
191609.subtitle_en: For the first time in 111 months, Svalbard recorded an average temperature below normal.

191627.excerpt_en: Norway’s most important task now and in the time ahead remains unchanged: We will protect the most vulnerable among us. That is why we are doing everything we can to limit the spread of the coronavirus.
191627.subtitle_en: The government is in continuous dialogue with the Governor of Svalbard and Longyearbyen Local Council and is closely monitoring the situation on Svalbard. The island’s healthcare system is vulnerable, and the community is being hit hard by the crisis we are now experiencing. Monica Mæland, Minister for Svalbard (Conservative Party)
191627.title_en: Closely Monitoring the Situation on Svalbard

191661.excerpt_en: A resident of Barentsburg helped arrange the repatriation of the two cats from Moscow. The Norwegian Food Safety Authority later sent the person a great thank-you for taking on interpreting assignments.
191661.subtitle_en: Two cats were denied entry to Svalbard. They arrived by plane from Moscow with a traveler bound for Barentsburg. The cats were sent back.
191661.tags_en: Norwegian Food Safety Authority, news, animal keeping, Barentsburg, airline passengers

191669.excerpt_en: “The official figure probably only reflects part of the reality on Svalbard for now. The number has risen sharply since last Wednesday,” says Anne-Margrethe Krogseth.
191669.subtitle_en: Unemployment has exploded on Svalbard. Over two weeks in March, it went from nearly nonexistent to above 14 percent. And the increase has not stopped yet.
191669.title_en: “The Number of Completely Unemployed Is Rising Sharply”

191677.excerpt_en: Approximately 300 people on Svalbard are believed to be without income as a result of the coronavirus crisis. This applies to people who are neither citizens of nor hold residence permits in an EU/EEA country.
191677.subtitle_en: From Thursday, temporarily laid-off third-country nationals can apply for grants to cover living expenses on Svalbard. But strict rules govern who can receive support.
191677.tags_en: Longyearbyen Local Council, unemployment, news, coronavirus crisis

191686.excerpt_en: Nationwide, 300,000 people have been made unemployed, most of them during the past two weeks. The coronavirus pandemic has plunged the entire world into an extremely difficult and uncertain situation.
191686.subtitle_en: From being a community with no unemployment, Longyearbyen now has the highest unemployment rate in the country. This clearly shows how vulnerable the community is.
191686.title_en: Money for Businesses Must Come Quickly

191694.excerpt_en: On Sunday evening, Arnt Vegar Jensen launched a fundraiser for two families. The families arrived in Svalbard less than six months ago and will therefore receive social assistance for no more than 20 days under the government’s latest crisis package for Svalbard. “Now they have nothing.”
191694.subtitle_en: He sees that friends who are not entitled to unemployment benefits are struggling badly. So he is collecting money.

191728.excerpt_en: Hans Kristian Mjelde has been hired as the new general manager of the veterinary clinic and will most likely be in place during the spring. The long-term plan is for Mjelde, together with Hope and Diinhoff, to buy into the business and continue running it.
191728.subtitle_en: After more than seven years in Longyearbyen, veterinarian Astrid Vikaune is heading home to Helgeland. Veterinarians Stine Diinhoff and Kristina Hope will eventually buy into the business together with the new general manager.

191736.excerpt_en: On Thursday, Longyearbyen Local Council opened applications for grants for third-country nationals left without income after being temporarily laid off. “We have received a number of applications and phone calls,” says project manager Karina Løvås Bakken.
191736.subtitle_en: Several third-country nationals applied to Longyearbyen Local Council for emergency support on the very first day. They have been promised a quick response.
191736.title_en: More People Apply for Emergency Aid

191744.excerpt_en: “So we didn’t come here for an interest-rate increase after all,” Espen Olsen says with a laugh. Together with Timon Brüggemann, he met Svenn Are Johansen at the bank to accept the gift.
191744.subtitle_en: Earlier this year, Spitsbergen Makerspace submitted an application to the Sparebank Foundation. On Thursday, they received the grant.

191752.excerpt_en: The coronavirus crisis has led to exceptionally high unemployment, including on Svalbard. Over the past week, the number of registered unemployed people has risen by 69, to a total of 330.
191752.subtitle_en: Over the past week, the number of unemployed people on Svalbard has increased by 69, from 261 to 330.

191760.excerpt_en: “A broken back” is how Ronny Strømnes describes the situation in Svalbard’s tourism industry. Visit Svalbard’s member businesses have minimal or no activity.
191760.subtitle_en: One day the coronavirus crisis will be over, and Svalbard will once again depend on tourism. Visit Svalbard is keeping people’s travel dreams alive.
191760.tags_en: tourism, coronavirus crisis, Visit Svalbard, news
191760.title_en: “We’re Keeping the Dream of Travel Alive”

191770.excerpt_en: Together with Tom Backe of Kaldnes Media, the former principal of Longyearbyen School has made 29 short films about Svalbard’s history. The films are funded by Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund and are freely available for everyone to use.
191770.subtitle_en: We are revisiting this film, which we first published in March 2018. Hear Svalbard veteran Hallvard Holm talk about the old hospital steps.
191770.tags_en: history, life on Svalbard, Svalbard history, Sun Festival Week, Sun Festival, Longyearbyen Hospital, historical documentary, historical picture, historical, hospital steps, old hospital
191770.title_en: Rebuilt the Hospital Steps for the 1993 Sun Festival

191787.excerpt_en: The patrol vessel Fridtjof Nansen was built at the Norwegian Navy’s Main Shipyard in Horten in 1930–31 and was the first ship in the Norwegian Navy to be built as a patrol vessel. From 1932, she was part of the fisheries inspection service in Northern Norway.
191787.subtitle_en: What was the patrol vessel Fridtjof Nansen doing in Adventfjorden?
191787.title_en: Can Any Readers Provide More Information?

191795.excerpt_en: He brought his sons and sons-in-law with him: Leonard Johan, Hjalmar, Sverre, Johannes, Lyder Jr., Jon Jonson and Hjalmar Arnø.
191795.subtitle_en: My great-grandfather, Lyder Andreas Olsen, ran the Kings Bay workshop for several seasons from around 1921 to 1929.
191795.tags_en: history, life on Svalbard, the locomotive, Kings Bay
191795.title_en: Working Men at Kings Bay in the 1920s

191837.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard received a tip from the public about the fox, which showed signs of problems with its central nervous system. They therefore went out with a snowmobile patrol. “We are unsure whether it may have rabies, but it was put down and has now been sent for testing.”
191837.subtitle_en: A polar fox was put down in Bjonehamna in Tempelfjorden on Sunday morning after displaying suspicious behavior.

191863.excerpt_en: She posted the film on Facebook, and at the time of writing it has nearly 14,000 views. Both TV 2 and NRK picked it up, and Harviken never expected so much attention around the “stunt.” “I never imagined it would become this big.”
191863.subtitle_en: Teacher Heidi Harviken and colleague Karine Jørgensen decided to get a little creative when assigning their students a physical education task. It became popular—not just among the students.
191863.title_en: Became an Internet Celebrity with a School Video

191875.excerpt_en: “We cannot accept having things this way,” says Arild Olsen. Longyearbyen’s chief ombudsman is referring to the fact that third-country nationals do not receive unemployment benefits when they are temporarily laid off on Svalbard.
191875.subtitle_en: Businesses on Svalbard should in future be required to provide welfare insurance for employees from countries outside the EU and EEA, local council leader Arild Olsen proposes.
191875.title_en: Proposes Mandatory Employee Insurance on Svalbard

191883.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) chief administrative officer Hege Walør Fagertun told politicians on the Administration Committee on Tuesday. “This is the biggest additional task imposed on us as a result of the coronavirus situation. The system we have created appears to be working well, and the processing of applications has begun,” Fagertun said.
191883.subtitle_en: So far, 130 third-country nationals have applied to Longyearbyen Local Council for emergency support.

191899.excerpt_en: Temperatures will fall from Wednesday, and the sun will come out. “Easter looks fairly good, with little or no precipitation. There will also be little wind, mostly a northeasterly and easterly breeze.”
191899.subtitle_en: If you are planning to spend Easter outdoors, fine days await you. The Easter weather will be marked by long periods of sunshine, the meteorologist promises.
191899.title_en: This Is What the Easter Weather Will Be Like

191907.excerpt_en: “Store Norske is sending 100 protective suits and 12,000 dust masks to the University Hospital of North Norway in Tromsø,” Svalbardposten wrote three weeks ago.
191907.subtitle_en: Between 150 and 200 employees at the University Hospital of North Norway in Tromsø are being tested for coronavirus because they used masks that were not approved for use. The masks were sent to Tromsø from Longyearbyen.

191919.excerpt_en: Of the almost 3,000 officially registered residents of the Svalbard archipelago, according to figures from Statistics Norway (SSB), 2,428 live in Longyearbyen and Ny-Ålesund. Another 10 are registered in Hornsund, and exactly 501 in Barentsburg and Pyramiden.
191919.subtitle_en: Officially, there are almost 3,000 residents in the Svalbard archipelago.

191927.excerpt_en: One of the people is said to have suffered frostbite to the face. Chief constable Lisbeth Hansen does not wish to say where they were when they requested assistance, but they are said to have been skiing north on Spitsbergen.
191927.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, the Governor of Svalbard had to rescue two cross-country skiers who had headed north.

191935.excerpt_en: More than 100 kindergarten children in Longyearbyen will return to kindergarten on Monday 20 April, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) announces.
191935.subtitle_en: Local kindergartens reopen on 20 April. A week later, pupils in grades 1 to 4 can return to school.

191943.excerpt_en: “If people are sitting at home wishing they had booked an appointment, we now encourage them to call,” says Knut Selmer, infection-control physician at Longyearbyen Hospital. Restrictions The hospital will still have some restrictions, such as ensuring that the waiting room does not become crowded.
191943.subtitle_en: After Easter, Longyearbyen Hospital will once again offer regular medical appointments and counselling.

191951.excerpt_en: “This is very good news for our research students, those doing master’s degrees, PhDs and postdocs. They are building their careers and depend on being able to do fieldwork and work in the laboratory at UNIS.”
191951.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, the government announced at a press conference that universities and colleges could gradually reopen from Monday 27 April.

191959.excerpt_en: We go around saying that these are challenging times. We go around saying that these are strange times.
191959.subtitle_en: Parish priest Siv Limstrand’s Easter greeting to Longyearbyen.
191959.tags_en: Easter, magazine, reader letter, Svalbard Church, news

191971.excerpt_en: Kine Bjelland, who normally works for Hurtigruten Svalbard, and Martine Nyhagen, who has worked as a guide for Svalbard Husky, were originally supposed to be field assistants for researcher Eva Fuglei.
191971.subtitle_en: Martine Nyhagen and Kine H. Bjelland feel lucky to have been given the job of counting ptarmigan for the Norwegian Polar Institute while the researcher is stranded in Tromsø because of corona.
191971.tags_en: corona crisis, news, Norwegian Polar Institute
191971.title_en: Laid Off from Their Jobs, Now Counting Ptarmigan

191983.excerpt_en: Kings Bay AS operates all infrastructure in Ny-Ålesund. The company’s director, Per Erik Hanevold, says there are now 40 people in Ny-Ålesund.
191983.subtitle_en: May and June are usually peak season in the research settlement at 79 degrees north as well. Now most of it has been cancelled.
191983.title_en: Reduced Activity Cuts Revenue in Ny-Ålesund

191994.excerpt_en: Svalbard couple Romano Juric and Zeljka Novokmet started Svalbard Delivery Service just before New Year. When the coronavirus pandemic triggered strict infection-control measures, the number of assignments skyrocketed. “We had been thinking about it for a long time.”
191994.subtitle_en: “People say I’m the only one making money now,” says Romano Juric. The newly launched courier company has received two to three times as many assignments because of the corona crisis.

192012.excerpt_en: The cabin residents had raised the flag, and as the clock approached one, more and more people arrived. Many had also taken a snowmobile ride to attend the service.
192012.subtitle_en: The traditional Easter service at Vindodden was a wonderful experience for those who attended.

192020.excerpt_en: No one mentioned, no one forgotten—but thank you to every single person. But what can we do to minimize the consequences for each individual?
192020.subtitle_en: A national effort is currently under way to limit the spread of COVID-19, and I have to say I am impressed by how the entire country is contributing.
192020.title_en: A Community Effort to Preserve Local Jobs

192036.excerpt_en: In recent Saturdays, the bell at Svalbard Church has rung in the weekend in Longyearbyen. In the years after the war, Longyearbyen had no church; this was the bell that summoned people to services held at Huset.
192036.subtitle_en: On Easter Eve, Saturday 11 April, the old bell at Skjæringa will be used to ring in the Easter celebrations.
192036.title_en: Ringing in Easter Weekend with the Bell at Skjæringa

192044.excerpt_en: More than 80 Russian trapping stations have been registered, well distributed throughout the archipelago. Most survive only as foundations, but some still have Russian trapping stations or cabins dating from the late 18th to the early 19th century. These are Svalbard’s oldest trapping stations and cabins.

192062.excerpt_en: The novel “Longyearbyen” is set in 1957, just before flights to Svalbard began.

192092.excerpt_en: The first-ever service at the church cabin in Todalen was “just right,” parish priest Siv Limstrand thought. Traditionally, the service is held in the church on this important religious holiday, but infection-control measures introduced because of the coronavirus pandemic are forcing everyone to find new solutions.

196001.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen’s new floating quay was back on the agenda for the Longyearbyen Port Authority before Easter. After spending about a year on ice, funding for the preliminary project is back in the national budget. “A framework of up to NOK 15 million has been allocated.”

196012.excerpt_en: So far, 150 Svalbard residents have applied for coronavirus crisis support. That is 20 more than just before Easter.
