212793.subtitle_en: Whether you want to eat there or cook at home, Isbjørnbutikken will provide the goods.

212810.excerpt_en: “We do not agree internally in the Conservative Party,” confirms Stein-Ove Johannessen. There is therefore still some suspense about the contents of the new square to be built between the post office and bank building and Svalbardbutikken this summer.
212810.subtitle_en: Timber from the Svea mines will become a meeting place in the pedestrian street. A free lizard will become a playground for the youngest children—even though the politicians do not entirely agree on where the ramp should stand.
212810.title_en: Mining History in the Town Centre

212820.excerpt_en: Hooray! We are also pleased to see debate and engagement around a new energy solution in LYB—both through reader letters such as Reinhard Mook’s and in other media, including TU and DN, since our last contribution.
212820.subtitle_en: During the summer half of the year, the entire town could be supplied with energy produced by rooftop solar panels, the contributors write, among other things.
212820.title_en: On Wind, Subsidies and Energy Storage in Svalbard

212837.excerpt_en: The bureaucracy is often criticised for working too slowly and laboriously. Impatient people and businesses often wait a long time for answers—but the Public Administration Act imposes strict requirements on the drafting of rules and regulations.
212837.tags_en: Svalbard package, Longyearbyen Local Council, editorial, bureaucracy, opinion

SNN closed its Longyearbyen branch before the New Year.
212839.subtitle_en: Foreign nationals opening an account with a Norwegian bank must still meet a customer adviser to verify their identity. An EU ruling has temporarily made the planned postal solution impossible.

212842.excerpt_en: One of the first to cross the finish line at Huset on Sunday was Alexander Hovland with his eight dogs. All in all, he concludes that he is very pleased. “But Fardalsbakken is just as brutal as ever.”
212842.subtitle_en: More than 50 people and just under 100 dogs took part, and the organisers of this year’s Trappers Trail are very pleased with Longyearbyen’s biggest event of the year for the dog community.
212842.title_en: “Fardalsbakken Is Just as Brutal as Ever”

212854.excerpt_en: She is trained as a child welfare officer and has, among other things, worked in the municipal child welfare service, as a manager and educational supervisor in kindergartens, and for the past 20 years as a department head at Buskerud Child and Family Centre, where she also led a family unit providing treatment, assessment and treatment in the home.
212854.subtitle_en: Nina Normann raises many questions about the new consultation proposals on education in Longyearbyen.

The position is now being advertised and should be filled by the start of the academic year on 1
212883.subtitle_en: When the new student housing is ready, the student welfare organisation will also have an executive in Svalbard.

212910.excerpt_en: The notice of a fine, or administrative penalty, was sent to Coop Svalbard as early as the day after the reopening on March 22.
212910.subtitle_en: When Svalbardbutikken opened in new premises, the local authorities had not granted permission. That could cost NOK 10,000 in fines.

212917.subtitle_en: Limited time can be a desirable driver of innovation. But haste also increases the risk of making the wrong investment, the contributor believes.

212925.excerpt_en: According to Ronny Strømnes, the project began as early as 2018. Like many others, Svalbard should have its own artist wine, several people agreed.
212925.subtitle_en: Local lithographs adorn the labels of Svalbard’s first two artist wines. They are released on Wednesday to mark Nordpolet’s reopening.

212928.excerpt_en: What is Statsbygg’s plan for Longyearbyen? “(He laughs.) Statsbygg has been in Longyearbyen for a long time.”
212928.subtitle_en: Harald Vaagaasar Nikolaisen, CEO of Statsbygg, admits that the housing situation in Longyearbyen is difficult—not only because of the shortage of homes, but also because of their quality.
212928.tags_en: news, Statsbygg, housing construction, housing shortage

212938.excerpt_en: This is stated in a press release from Minister of Trade and Industry Iselin Nybø (V). The money comes from the government’s grant scheme for restructuring projects in the tourism industry, administered by Innovation Norway.
212938.subtitle_en: The government is allocating NOK 11 million to 13 different event and tourism businesses in Svalbard.

212950.excerpt_en: Exterior construction work is still under way and the sign is missing, but inside everything is in perfect order. Nordpolet officially reopened on Wednesday.
212950.subtitle_en: The town’s alcohol outlet has officially risen again in new, modern premises.

212979.excerpt_en: Telenor’s construction and relocation project at Skjæringa enters a critical phase this coming Monday, May 3.
212979.subtitle_en: Over the next six weeks, Telenor will move technical solutions from the old building to the new one. “We are making a major investment in security and quality in Svalbard. During the transition, internet and mobile coverage may be somewhat unstable,” says general manager Christian Skottun.

212983.excerpt_en: I am saddened to read the proposal for new regulations on primary education in Longyearbyen. I am at least equally saddened, and quite exasperated, by the comments from people in leading administrative positions at Longyearbyen Local Council (LL).
212983.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council is trying to justify filtering out children who do not meet a desired standard, the author writes.
212983.tags_en: school, opinion, reader letter, special education
212983.title_en: Who Is Good Enough for Longyearbyen?

212985.excerpt_en: There is still a risk that the snow cornices at the top of Gruvefjellet could break loose and fall. As recently as Wednesday evening, an avalanche ran towards the buildings, the duty chief superintendent tells Svalbardposten.
212985.subtitle_en: The evacuation and the ban on staying and travelling in Nybyen remain in place. The Governor of Svalbard writes this in a press release today, Thursday.

212991.excerpt_en: On April 8, the consultation letter on how education is to be provided in Longyearbyen was published.
212991.subtitle_en: The consultation letter on how education is to be provided in Longyearbyen has a bad smell about it.
212991.title_en: The Road to a Sorting Society

213003.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard wrote this in a press release today, Friday. “The check was carried out as a preventive measure before the visitors were due to drive, and the blood-alcohol readings therefore have no consequences for those who blew red,” it said. The field team conducted the breathalyser check.
213003.subtitle_en: Two people failed breathalyser tests at Isfjord Radio on Thursday—and had to leave their snowmobiles standing until they could drive legally.
213003.title_en: Two Blew Red at Isfjord Radio

213022.excerpt_en: “We want people to contact us if they find birds with no visible cause of death and bring them to the Governor of Svalbard for testing,” says Hilde Haug, section head at the Norwegian Food Safety Authority’s Northern Region, Troms and Svalbard division. Svalbard is considered a risk area for avian flu because of its large breeding population.
213022.subtitle_en: Norway’s first case of avian flu was detected last autumn. Now the birds are heading towards Svalbard, and the Governor of Svalbard and the Norwegian Food Safety Authority are asking people to report suspicious bird deaths.

213027.excerpt_en: “All my guiding jobs had been cancelled, the town was shut down and the pandemic affected everyone’s everyday life. But then I realised for the first time how many people were actually walking around town with my products.”
213027.subtitle_en: Yann Rashid received a wake-up call when he returned to Longyearbyen in March 2020 after losing his guiding assignments. Now he is going all in on his company, Arctic Edge.

213044.excerpt_en: “Every time I walk past the miners’ statue, I think ‘respect’. And then I have wondered what it would be like to have more statues—perhaps a guide, or a cleaner.”
213044.subtitle_en: The weather arrived as ordered for this year’s 1 May celebration. Social anthropologist and Norwegian People’s Aid representative Zdenka Sokolickova issued an appeal for the day: that Longyearbyen’s population stand together for rights on more than one day a year.

213050.excerpt_en: “It is a little strange to miss something you had never really noticed. But we missed seeing mountains.”
213050.subtitle_en: After eight years in Oslo, Marius Felde Isaksen, 38, and his partner chose Svalbard—for more time with their children. And to see proper mountains.

213069.excerpt_en: Siri M. Kalvig presents her views in an opinion piece in *Stavanger Aftenblad* on 20.
213069.subtitle_en: Siri M. Kalvig is unrealistic about a new energy supply for Longyearbyen.
213069.tags_en: reader letter, energy, opinions, energy supply
213069.title_en: A Pipe Dream About the Green Transition in Longyearbyen

213083.excerpt_en: American author Jeanne Bender’s series of books about the puppy Lindie Lou is used by teachers around the world. In the fifth book, published this spring, the story is set on Svalbard.
213083.subtitle_en: American children’s author taught herself about Svalbard remotely in order to write a new children’s book.
213083.title_en: Don’t Put the Book Plans on Ice

213088.excerpt_en: “We are only at the very beginning of the work. But we know mild weather can arrive suddenly, and that skiing conditions around the town centre can disappear within a few days.”
213088.subtitle_en: Svalbard Turn has been granted permission to groom ski trails at Breinosa. But clarifications are still needed before it can happen.
213088.title_en: Gets Permission to Groom Ski Trails at Breinosa

213094.excerpt_en: This year also brings a new committee chair, 18-year-old Liv-Anna Ringheim. “Kristin Furu Grøtting from the Education and Culture Committee asked whether I would like to join the committee, and at the first meeting I was proposed as chair. Because 17.”
213094.subtitle_en: Despite restrictions again this year, the 17 May committee is nearly ready with this year’s programme.
213094.title_en: Ready for the Biggest Celebration of the Year

213109.excerpt_en: Two of the cases are still under investigation, while two were dismissed for lack of evidence. “There is a jungle out there that is difficult to navigate; it is often hard to find the perpetrator.”
213109.subtitle_en: Senior police officer Anders Haugerud of the Governor of Svalbard’s office has dealt with four online abuse cases over the past year.

213112.excerpt_en: You have probably seen it speeding around Longyearbyen on a snowmobile sled. The flamingo is one of the leading characters in Visit Svalbard’s new summer campaign.
213112.subtitle_en: What does it have to do with Svalbard?

213125.excerpt_en: During Monday’s mass vaccination at Svalbardhallen, 507 people were vaccinated. Six registered people did not show up. “But no vaccines were thrown away; we administered what we were supposed to, and then some.”
213125.subtitle_en: A total of 1,405 people on Svalbard have received a vaccine. Up to 90 of them are fully vaccinated.
213125.title_en: “Everyone Who Wants a Vaccine Must Sign Up Now”

213161.excerpt_en: The population of the Longyearbyen and Ny-Ålesund settlements increased by 31 people during 2020. As of 1 January 2021, 2,459 people live here.
213161.subtitle_en: Men are still in the majority, but the proportion of women is increasing.

213166.excerpt_en: The administration’s proposed regulations were otherwise adopted, against the votes of the Liberal Party and the Greens. The two opposition parties put forward their own proposal based on several of Visit Svalbard’s submissions during the consultation.
213166.subtitle_en: The biggest change in Svalbard Package 2, adopted by the local council on Tuesday, was increasing compensation from 50 to 75 percent of companies’ losses. But another matter was strange.
213166.tags_en: tourism, Svalbard package, local council, news
213166.title_en: “Strange That We Should Think About What Isn’t Being Used”

213187.excerpt_en: Researchers now know for certain that reindeer hunting is not uncommon among polar bears on Svalbard. “We think it is due to several factors. There are many more reindeer, polar bears are spending more time on land, and some of them are becoming specialists at hunting reindeer.”
213187.subtitle_en: Despite poor weather and a shortened season, researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute handled 39 polar bears this year. More and more polar bears are eating reindeer, something previously thought not to happen.
213187.title_en: “They Eat More Reindeer Than We Thought”

213190.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has decided to maintain the evacuation and the ban on staying and travelling in Nybyen. There is still a risk that the snow cornices at the top of Gruvefjellet may break loose and fall.
213190.subtitle_en: Evacuation in Nybyen is being maintained.

213197.excerpt_en: The agenda included approval of the 2020 annual accounts, payment of outstanding member rebates and the election of new board members. In March last year, the board of Svalbardbutikken chose to reduce the pre-guaranteed shopping rebate from four to one percent from 1.
213197.subtitle_en: Last year, you received a smaller shopping rebate from Svalbardbutikken. The general manager and the board as a whole received more.
213197.title_en: Board Fees and Executive Pay Up, Member Rebates Down

213207.excerpt_en: “I am pleased that we are now getting a new building for Svalbard Folk High School. The folk high school on Svalbard has been a pet project for the Liberal Party and the government since the idea was first proposed.”
213207.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries will contribute up to NOK 200 million so that Store Norske can begin construction of new premises for Svalbard Folk High School.
213207.title_en: Store Norske Receives Funding to Build New Folk High School

213212.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) and the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) will begin constructing support structures from the top of Sukkertoppen in week 21, starting on 25 May.
213212.subtitle_en: Avalanche-protection work in Lia will resume for the season in a couple of weeks.

213224.excerpt_en: Alcohol consumption on Svalbard has always been a delicate subject, writes Birger Amundsen in the book *Black and White*. In the 1950s, Longyearbyen was a mining community with many young, unmarried men and very limited leisure activities, combined with a culture in which binge drinking was the norm.
213224.subtitle_en: There is something nostalgic about the alcohol card. Nostalgia belongs to memory, and the card belongs in a museum.
213224.title_en: Send the Alcohol Card to a Museum

213238.excerpt_en: “It had been forgotten for many years, but after someone contacted us, we chose to revive the tradition. His family allowed him to be buried here because the people of Longyearbyen wanted to look after the grave, which is why we feel this commemoration is important.”
213238.subtitle_en: Four years ago, the Governor of Svalbard revived the tradition of laying a wreath at Captain Trond Astrup Vigtel’s grave in Longyearbyen.

213252.excerpt_en: Troset is now well underway in the kitchen and preparing his first menu. It premieres on the 25th.
213252.subtitle_en: Stationen’s new head chef, Martin Guin Troset (30), knows Svalbard well—even though he arrived here for the first time two weeks ago.
213252.title_en: Small Kitchen for a Big Chef

213269.excerpt_en: “I called the municipality and explained that I was supposed to get it for free, but I had no say in the matter. I was referred to the vaccination clinic, which is a private clinic,” she says.
213269.subtitle_en: Berit Ulvang has travelled south three times since the testing regime was introduced, in connection with routine hospital visits. When she needs a coronavirus test before returning home to Longyearbyen, she is referred to a private clinic in Bodø, which charges NOK 800 for a rapid test.

213290.excerpt_en: Because of travel restrictions, Svalbard is effectively closed to foreign researchers. The proportion of researchers present in Ny-Ålesund has fallen drastically, and the revenues of Kings Bay AS, which provides research infrastructure, have declined correspondingly.
213290.subtitle_en: It is not only tourism and business that have been hit by the coronavirus pandemic. Research activity is suffering, and the Research Council is now expanding its support.

213310.excerpt_en: This is stated in a press release. “Svalbard is a completely unique place in terms of nature, culture and history. A new certification scheme for Svalbard guides will increase tourist safety while safeguarding natural and cultural treasures.”
213310.subtitle_en: As part of its work on revised tourism regulations for Svalbard, the government is inviting input on the announced certification of tourist guides.
213310.title_en: Reviewing Competency Requirements for Guide Certification

213314.excerpt_en: And how can our elected representatives support the proposal without listening to those who live here and run businesses? Sometimes you cannot believe what you read.

213329.excerpt_en: “This is a serious attack on the rights of children and young people that belongs many decades in the past. We believe the proposal should be rejected and the current provision retained.”
213329.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Federation of Organizations of Disabled People (FFO) does not usually comment on local consultation proposals. But it considers the draft on education in Longyearbyen so serious that it is preparing a formal submission.

213332.excerpt_en: And perhaps that is not so strange when you know that just over NOK 20 million of the NOK 25 million from support package 1 has so far been distributed.
213332.subtitle_en: During last week’s community council meeting, opposition members found it odd that council leader Arild Olsen was so concerned with what to do with the money left over from support package 2.

213345.excerpt_en: They received the award for the project “Svalbard, at the Intersection of East and West.” The students take a closer look at Norwegian-Russian relations by comparing the relationship between Norway and Russia and examining the ties between the local communities of Longyearbyen and Barentsburg.
213345.subtitle_en: Marte Nilssen Alexandersen and Liv-Anna Ringheim of Longyearbyen School won third place in the Holberg Prize for Schools.

213365.subtitle_en: Teodor has lived in Longyearbyen all his life. Because he has Down syndrome and therefore receives special education at school, he could risk losing his place.
213365.title_en: Now He Could Lose His Place at School

213382.excerpt_en: Schütz wants paragraph 5A of the regulations governing the compensation scheme abolished. He wants the entire paragraph removed and has now filed complaints with the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
213382.subtitle_en: Marcel Schütz believes the compensation scheme in Svalbard Package 2 is discriminatory and is filing complaints with several ministries.

213386.excerpt_en: There is still a risk that the cornices at the top of Gruvefjellet could break loose and fall. The Governor’s Office writes this in a press release.
213386.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has once again decided to maintain the evacuation and the ban on staying and travelling in Nybyen.
213386.title_en: “It Doesn’t Seem That People Understand the Seriousness”

213397.excerpt_en: In terms of both cloud cover and sunshine, Longyearbyen is the big winner on the year’s biggest celebratory day. And the good weather is set to last. “Sunday looks fine around Longyearbyen, but there may be some clouds in the far north and along the coast.”
213397.subtitle_en: “Spitsbergen will have the nicest weather on May 17. Not in terms of temperature, admittedly, but surely one can cope with that. I would rather have been there than in the south, with its rain,” says state meteorologist Charalampos Sarchosidis.
213397.title_en: “I Wish I Could Have Been on Svalbard”

213410.subtitle_en: Earthquake recorded 300 kilometers west of Svalbard.

213414.excerpt_en: 442 points out of a possible 800 may seem merely average, but that puts Longyearbyen Community Council at the top of the Norwegian rankings in its category. Of all Norwegian municipalities with fewer than 5,000 inhabitants, only one scored higher in the Municipal Compass survey.
213414.subtitle_en: Our “municipality” is the country’s second-best in its category.

213455.excerpt_en: A substantial avalanche came down toward Longyear Glacier on Sunday afternoon. “The Governor of Svalbard has personnel out investigating the avalanche. There is no indication that anyone was caught in it.”
213455.subtitle_en: No tracks lead into the avalanche area.

213461.excerpt_en: A snowmobile driver was taken to hospital with minor injuries after an accident on Saturday evening. The Governor’s Office was notified at about 7:30 p.m. “It happened in Adventdalen between SSU and Hiorthhamn.”
213461.subtitle_en: A bruised snowmobile driver was taken to hospital on Saturday evening.

213465.excerpt_en: “I think the discussions we have to hold could be uncomfortable,” she says. On Wednesday, Grøtting attended an international meeting about the consultation proposals—“simply to listen,” she says.
213465.subtitle_en: Kristin Furu Grøtting, chair of the Education and Culture Committee, is clear that the consultation proposal will be difficult to process.

213488.excerpt_en: National Day celebrations began with a salute at 7 a.m. on Monday. An hour later, the scouts kicked off the 17…
213488.subtitle_en: The national day’s first speakers thanked the local healthcare service for keeping the infection off Svalbard.
213488.title_en: “Everything Will Be Fine—and Happy Constitution Day!”

213504.excerpt_en: A dog owner has been reported to the Governor of Svalbard after a dog got loose and chased a reindeer in Bjørndalen on Sunday morning. This was stated by senior police officer Magnar Silseth of the Governor’s Office.
213504.subtitle_en: A loose dog chased a reindeer, which had to be put down because of a broken leg.
213504.title_en: Reindeer Had to Be Put Down

213513.excerpt_en: Follow the celebrations on our website. (All photos: Audun Bårdseth)
213513.subtitle_en: National Day was celebrated in glorious weather in Longyearbyen this year.

213527.excerpt_en: “I was extremely shocked. When I called Marte to tell her, she didn’t believe me,” Liv-Anna says of her reaction when they learned they had won third place.
213527.subtitle_en: Marte Nilssen Alexandersen and Liv-Anna Ringeim took the prestigious third place in the 2021 Holberg Prize for Schools.

213528.excerpt_en: In his May 17 speech, Russia’s consul general in Svalbard, Sergey Gushchin, looked ahead to brighter times. “Thanks to strict measures and vaccination, we can once again enjoy people-to-people contact between our two towns,” he said.
213528.subtitle_en: The difficult COVID era is coming to an end. In Barentsburg, Russia’s consul general is looking forward to cultural exchanges starting again.
213528.title_en: Looking Forward to New Cultural Visits

213558.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) has notified Coop Svalbard of a possible fine for opening the new store premises without the necessary permit on March 22 this year. “We believe this is unjustified,” writes general manager Ronny Strømnes.
213558.subtitle_en: Svalbardbutikken denies opening new store premises without permission.

213575.excerpt_en: “The April figures for accommodation providers in Longyearbyen still reflect the pandemic and strict travel restrictions,” Visit Svalbard reports. The number of guest nights remains almost 70 percent below normal, according to the latest statistics.
213575.subtitle_en: The tourism figures still make for grim reading. Without the construction workers in town, things would have been even worse.
213575.title_en: One in Four Hotel Guests Is a Construction Worker

213578.excerpt_en: I was in Svalbard from April 29 to May 3.
213578.subtitle_en: It is challenging to speak about climate, the environment and tourism at the same time. One might argue that these things are entirely incompatible. Going on holiday to Svalbard to see the ice melt is such a huge paradox that it is tempting to say nothing about it. I will nevertheless try, because it feels too important not to.
213578.title_en: Coming to Terms with Svalbard’s Gigantic Paradox: Climate, Environment and Tourism

213598.excerpt_en: The chain is prepared and secured beneath the roof, where new pipes will be suspended. What is special about this job is that the pipes will not be buried—they will be hung up.
213598.subtitle_en: Large parts of Mine 7 were flooded last year. Now a completely new pump and pipe system will remove the water if it happens again.
213598.title_en: The Pipes That Will Prevent a New Crisis

213666.excerpt_en: “I’m so happy that a Svalbard project received support again this year. Especially during the pandemic, we have seen how important summer activities are for children and young people,” says Trine Vekseth, regional manager for the Gjensidige Foundation.
213666.subtitle_en: The Gjensidige Foundation has once again chosen to support Svalbard Turn’s event Activity Week.

213670.excerpt_en: Skred AS presented the new recommendation to local council politicians recently. The experts previously believed that a so-called deflection berm would be the best solution.
213670.subtitle_en: The experts have changed their minds: Steel mesh will protect Vannledningsdalen at least as well as the huge berm previously planned.
213670.title_en: Steel Mesh to Eliminate the Risk of Slush Avalanches

213676.excerpt_en: Two weeks ago, the local council adopted the administration’s proposed regulations for Aid Package 2, which has a framework of NOK 40 million. The Liberals and the Greens voted against the proposal.
213676.subtitle_en: It is incomprehensible why LL does not use industry codes that would include more businesses when drawing up the requirements for the aid package.
213676.title_en: The Regulations for Aid Package 2 Should Be Changed

213689.excerpt_en: “The situation remains such that the large snow cornices above the buildings in Nybyen pose a threat.”
213689.subtitle_en: Since April 9, the buildings on the eastern side of Nybyen have stood empty. It is the longest-lasting evacuation since monitoring began after the avalanche in 2015.

213692.excerpt_en: The focus these days is on the NOK 40 million in Svalbard Package 2 intended to save Norwegian investments and jobs in Svalbard’s tourism industry. As usual, the local focus is mainly on the negative.
213692.subtitle_en: “As a local politician, you apparently have to learn to live with the fact that whatever you achieve is never good enough,” the local Progress Party leader writes in this article.
213692.title_en: Progress Party on Svalbard Package 2: “It’s Far from Certain the Final Word Has Been Said”

213725.excerpt_en: “Almost a quarter of Visit Svalbard’s businesses are excluded. This could easily be solved without leaving money unspent by allowing as many as possible to apply,” says Olivia Ericson of the Green Party (MDG).
213725.subtitle_en: Opposition parties on the local council are reacting strongly to the restrictions on applying for the second aid package, which has a framework of NOK 40 million.

213736.excerpt_en: MP and former cabinet minister Ola Elvestuen of the governing Liberal Party says he is surprised by the local council majority’s decision on which businesses can apply for support from Svalbard Package 2. Elvestuen took part in negotiations on the crisis package in Parliament.
213736.subtitle_en: Liberal Party MP Ola Elvestuen believes the local council should broaden the criteria for which industries can receive support from Svalbard Package 2.

213744.excerpt_en: In his history of Svalbard, Thor B. calls
213744.subtitle_en: Some thoughts on what is happening in Longyearbyen and “the bigger picture.”

213754.excerpt_en: The chief administrative officer is recommending that the politicians on the Administration Committee (AU), which meets on June 2, take more money from the discretionary reserve to complete the conversion of the youth center into a nursery.
213754.subtitle_en: NOK 3.5 million is not enough for the planned conversion of the youth center into a nursery.

213778.excerpt_en: “We’ve only just begun,” says Iris Dahle Bjørkmann. Mary-Ann’s Polarrigg has been awarded just under NOK 800,000 in government support through Svalbard Package 1.
213778.subtitle_en: Several government-funded projects are preparing Polarriggen for the future. Among other things, they will build a private bathroom for every room. The restaurant will also produce less waste.

213791.excerpt_en: In a comment on criticism from the Liberals and the Greens locally, and from Member of Parliament Ola Elvestuen, Local Council leader Arild Olsen writes: “I completely agree that several businesses in Longyearbyen need support beyond the established national schemes.”
213791.subtitle_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen believes changes can easily be made to the resolution on Svalbard Package 2. He rejects criticism from the Liberals on the local council and in Parliament. Olsen believes the Liberals have done a poor job in both places.

214125.subtitle_en: The print newspaper has been delayed on its way to Svalbard because of the wind.

214133.excerpt_en: It feels like a claw clamping around your throat every time a cabinet minister takes the stage at a press conference in Oslo to announce good news about reopening society. Because there is no good news for this community.

214143.excerpt_en: We are grateful for the strong political efforts made by local politicians to secure the approval by the Storting of Svalbard Package 1 and Svalbard Package 2, worth a total of NOK 65 million. On behalf of our member companies and their employees: THANK YOU.
214143.subtitle_en: A response to the Polar Expedition Cooperation regarding Svalbard Package 2.

214150.excerpt_en: The newsroom was quiet late one Tuesday afternoon when someone knocked on the door at Svalbardposten. Standing there were Iben Nikoline Abild (11) and Gaute Søreide Jordbrudal (11), asking whether they could get a free advertisement in Svalbardposten.
214150.subtitle_en: “Could we get a free advertisement in Svalbardposten for our stop-motion videos?”

214806.subtitle_en: An already hard-pressed local population has been given another burden without being consulted first, says our highest elected representative.

214848.excerpt_en: State Secretary Lars Jacob Hiim of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security hopes, he writes in an email to Svalbardposten, to have “contact and dialogue” with the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) going forward. LL was not informed before the proposal to change the rules on voting rights and eligibility for foreign citizens in Svalbard was announced.
214848.subtitle_en: The Longyearbyen Community Council should have been informed in advance about the proposal to change voting rights, the Ministry of Justice admits.

214860.title_en: Fears Fewer Tourists Will Come if Testing Regime Is Scrapped

214869.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Justice is managing on its own to destroy trust in the public administration.
214869.tags_en: foreigners, politics, opinion, local elections, editorial, voting rights

214895.excerpt_en: He may not have taken Svalbard by storm, but Stig Bareksten has certainly made an impression over the past week. He has a style all his own.
214895.subtitle_en: The man behind one of the world’s finest spirits believes Svalbard deserves its own distillery.

214898.excerpt_en: A sailing trip around Spitsbergen in 2018 captivated her so much that she applied for a job in Longyearbyen. The following year, she was hired by Spitsbergen Sport and has worked both behind and in front of the counter ever since. “I had never been here before I came up in 2018.”
214898.subtitle_en: “You have to learn to be a normal dog,” Cathrine Fausk Christensen (31) tells the unruly Baloo (4). He will go with Cathrine when she moves to the mainland.
214898.tags_en: the dog yard, life on Svalbard, people, dog

214901.excerpt_en: Every year, Svalbardposten holds the Stem Competition. It involves guessing when the stem on the champagne-shaped snow remnants on Operafjellet will split in two.
214901.subtitle_en: When the stem on Operafjellet breaks, we know summer has officially begun. For now, there is still plenty of snow on the mountain.
214901.title_en: Will we get summer this year?

214949.excerpt_en: The state is saving NOK 700 million on the clean-up. “The work to clear up Svea and Lunckefjell is one of Norway’s most ambitious environmental projects. Store Norske is cleaning up after more than a century of mining in Svea and restoring the area to its natural state.”
214949.subtitle_en: As the clean-up of Lunckefjell and the Svea mines nears completion, it is becoming clear that it will cost far less than expected.
214949.title_en: Clean-up in Svea will be far cheaper

214955.excerpt_en: In my view, the government’s proposal is forward-looking and a consequence of social development. It is in line with one of the main objectives of Norwegian Svalbard policy: maintaining Norwegian communities on the archipelago.
214955.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Justice is destroying trust in the administration, Svalbardposten argued in an editorial on 25 June, referring to the government’s proposal to require non-Norwegian citizens to have lived for three years in a Norwegian municipality in order to vote and stand for election to Longyearbyen Local Council.
214955.tags_en: right to vote, opinions, reader’s letter, minister of justice and public security, politics

214959.excerpt_en: Last Friday, the government eased several infection-control measures applying to tourism activities on Svalbard. 214959.subtitle_en: The 2021 summer season is ruined regardless.

214959.title_en: Easing of restrictions: good, but too late

214981.excerpt_en: Especially when you have travelled abroad and seen how things are done elsewhere. Just under three weeks ago, I travelled to my home country, Germany, for the first time since October 2019.

214981.title_en: A fee for travelling to Svalbard, but free travel to Europe?

214996.title_en: Isfjord Radio now runs on batteries

215010.excerpt_en: First, however, the minister and his entourage were given a tour of the area in Svea that is to be returned to nature, where the rare transformation of a former mining community into part of a national park is taking place. “It is not every day that a climate and environment minister gets to open a national park, nor every…”

215038.title_en: New governor and a new name

215086.title_en: Satellite launch to secure coverage of the North Pole

215093.excerpt_en: It is cold, and their skis glide across the snow as they cross the glacier. Down on the sea ice, a polar bear peers into a breathing hole in the ice.
215093.subtitle_en: After four years on Svalbard and many experiences in nature, Dagmara Wojtanowicz (35) is moving on.

215145.excerpt_en: The minister visited Ny-Ålesund, Longyearbyen and Svea this week, where he officially opened the new Van Mijenfjorden National Park, among other things. His ministry’s zeal for protection has often caused frustration among Longyearbyen residents.

There is every reason for more people to start thinking that way, because as technology advances, outer space is playing an increasingly central role in global technological development.
215148.subtitle_en: Along the Svalbard–Tromsø–Narvik–Andøya axis, a national value chain with world-leading industry, high-tech infrastructure and outstanding space research operates every day, the contributor writes.

The surveys provide answers about the fjord’s condition and pollution from wastewater.
215174.subtitle_en: Have you ever flushed a wet wipe down the toilet? Then it ended up in Adventfjorden. Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) is now taking some action, but has no plans to clean it up.

215299.excerpt_en: The representatives of the Centre Party landed on Saturday. Since arriving in Longyearbyen, they have visited and spoken with several agencies and residents.
215299.subtitle_en: The Centre Party visited Svalbard and felt it was particularly important to gain insight into everyday life on the island.
215299.title_en: “It is important to talk to people”

215304.excerpt_en: Eider ducks have a large colony by the town kennel in Longyearbyen. Senior researcher at NINA, Børge Moe, says the birds are attracted to the kennel for protection from other animals. “Eiders have predators such as glaucous gulls and Arctic foxes.”
215304.subtitle_en: Have you seen the little ducklings swimming around in the ponds by the town kennel? Now is your last chance to see them hatch and set off on their journey.

215337.excerpt_en: Svalbard’s southernmost island, Bjørnøya, is considered a paradise for seabirds. Thousands of birds nest here on the steep cliffs plunging into the depths of the sea.

215337.title_en: Southern bird species nesting in the north

215381.title_en: Students move in in two weeks

215412.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Food Safety Authority has changed its interpretation of the rules for certification in pet passports on Svalbard. This will lead to changes for people travelling with dogs.

215430.subtitle_en: During a recent reindeer census, two dead reindeer were found entangled in steel cable.

It’s absolutely wonderful; you can’t get more locally sourced than this.”

215540.subtitle_en: In June, the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) adopted the zoning plan for the new cemetery.

A new assessment of whether we can move to step four will take place in mid-August.”

216096.excerpt_en: On 24 June, the Norwegian Directorate of Health completed a solution for people who cannot use a smartphone, PC or tablet and who are fully vaccinated or immune to COVID-19.
216096.subtitle_en: The COVID certificate can be sent by post.

Contractor LNS has received the necessary materials on the island and is ready to start, according to email correspondence obtained by Svalbardposten.
216097.subtitle_en: A bus bay will make the area by the Polar Hotel safer.

216124.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Meteorological Institute has measured temperature and precipitation at Svalbard Airport since 1976. The figures it presents for the past three years show a significantly colder July in 2021. “The last time an average temperature of 6.2 degrees was recorded was in 2008,” says climate researcher Helga Therese Tilley Tajet of the Norwegian Meteorological Institute.
216124.subtitle_en: Summer in Longyearbyen is usually colder than on the mainland. But July has not been this cold since 2008.

216129.excerpt_en: “No, we’ll sit outside. Do you have an ashtray?” he asks first.
216129.subtitle_en: He regularly celebrates milestone birthdays on Svalbard and remembers the time when Lompen was not a shopping centre.

216145.subtitle_en: NOK 1.8 million from the Longyearbyen Community Council means a great deal to cruise organisation Aeco. It fell outside all other support schemes.

216169.subtitle_en: The students moved into the new accommodation at Elvesletta in July, but say they are living in unfinished housing.

216177.subtitle_en: The year of COVID-19 was no time for big ventures. But a little of this and a little of that worked exceptionally well for one of the shops at Lompen.

216240.subtitle_en: Photo and video artists have traveled across Svalbard. The result could be an exhibition at the new Galleri Svalbard.

216414.subtitle_en: The truck damaged the guardrail more than the vehicle.

218480.title_en: Svalbard reindeer parasites under the microscope

218501.subtitle_en: In connection with the relocation of Mea Lux, UNIS commissioned an expert assessment of the boat’s condition.

218540.excerpt_en: “It is legendary. This is where it all started,” says Morten Søberg.
218540.subtitle_en: The money disappears into the machines. The world’s only banknote from Grumant helps people everywhere understand how. “It is a source of deep reflection.”

218544.excerpt_en: Venstre politician Oddmund Rønning accused the political leadership (Labour, the Conservatives and the Progress Party) of breaking the law from the podium at the local council on Tuesday evening. “Parts of the process involving the Childhood and Culture Committee (OKU) in its consideration of the consultation response on proposed new regulations for kindergartens and education have most likely been illegal under the Local Government Act’s provisions on…”
218544.subtitle_en: Venstre rebukes politicians and bureaucrats over questionable meeting practices. “Debates on important issues must take place in public, not behind closed doors,” says Oddmund Rønning.

218553.excerpt_en: The Nybyen venue was packed when Stein Henningsen conducted the official opening of the Arctic Action art festival on Monday evening. The venue was Spitsbergen Artists’ Centre, formerly Galleri Svalbard.
218553.subtitle_en: Ready for performance action over the next few days? Here is a taste of what we can expect.

218556.excerpt_en: Chief infection-control physician Knut Selmer stresses in a press release from the Governor of Svalbard that there is no reason for concern among Longyearbyen’s residents after a male resident tested positive for coronavirus. “Longyearbyen Hospital received a positive result from his PCR test on Tuesday afternoon.”
218556.subtitle_en: A man in Longyearbyen has tested positive for coronavirus.

218568.excerpt_en: The project “People on Longyearbyen as a Physical Framework” won second prize at the “Why the World Needs Anthropologists Apply Awards” (WWNA Apply Awards). This is a network for anthropologists in Europe, and this was the first time the awards were held.
218568.subtitle_en: Svalbard Social Science Initiative and LPO Arkitekter won second prize when the best anthropological research projects were selected in Prague this autumn.
218568.title_en: Research project in Longyearbyen wins award

218605.excerpt_en: Among those attending the local council’s debate on the voting-rights proposal on Tuesday was social anthropologist and Svalbard researcher Zdenka Sokolickova. She wished more people had followed the debate. “Everyone who will vote in the next election in Longyearbyen, Norwegian or not, should have watched it.”
218605.subtitle_en: If foreigners lose the right to vote, it will create a dangerous divide in Longyearbyen, a social scientist warns. She is disappointed that some local politicians nevertheless support the move.

218620.excerpt_en: The lizard is both long-awaited and, to some extent, controversial, but now it is standing there. For the time being, behind construction fences, but as soon as possible the town’s new meeting place—the square—will open for play and socialising.
218620.subtitle_en: The lizard figure is almost ready for use in the new town square.

218625.excerpt_en: The so-called Blackout Challenge has become popular among children and young people via the TikTok app. The trend has also found its way to Svalbard, police with the Governor of Svalbard warn in a press release.
218625.subtitle_en: A choking trend from social media has also reached Svalbard. Police are warning people.

218636.excerpt_en: He asks: “What other society in the world can a foreigner turn up in—even without a visa—and demand a say in the administration of the country’s tax revenues?” There is one society where people from all the states that signed the treaty can settle without a visa.
218636.subtitle_en: In Arnstein Skaare’s letter to the editor in issue 34 of Svalbardposten, he raises a question I would like to answer.
218636.title_en: “Contrary to the spirit of the treaty”

218644.excerpt_en: Knut Selmer, chief infection-control physician at Longyearbyen Hospital, says this in light of the many events taking place this weekend. “As I understand it, this means a record number of visitors to Longyearbyen. The likelihood that some will be infected with coronavirus will be higher than ever since the pandemic began,” he reasons.
218644.subtitle_en: “It would not be a bombshell if some of this weekend’s visitors were infected with coronavirus.”
218644.title_en: Higher infection risk—but no cause for alarm

218649.excerpt_en: Dark Season Blues was officially opened on Thursday evening before a packed Culture House and an enthusiastic audience. Neither the audience nor the musicians could praise the event enough, and Danish musician Mike Andersen felt that the only right thing is for music to be played from a stage in front of people.
218649.subtitle_en: Audiences and musicians alike have been starved of good musical experiences. They will get one this weekend in Longyearbyen.
218649.tags_en: Dark Season Blues, culture, music, Svalbard life
218649.title_en: “Music should be played on a stage in front of people”

218658.excerpt_en: Amid a high-Arctic panorama, Trygve Vågseter Jakobsen’s welding torch crackles. He flips up his visor, symbolically blows on the weld and happily knocks on the steel beam.
218658.subtitle_en: The road to Svalsat on Platåfjellet is being protected against avalanches with half a kilometre of fencing.
218658.tags_en: news, avalanche protection, LNS Spitsbergen, Svalsat

218667.excerpt_en: Her plan after upper secondary school was not really to attend a folk high school; she only knew that she wanted to go to Svalbard. Somehow.
218667.subtitle_en: Herborg Skjelle, 20, has always been interested in Svalbard. Last year, she decided to attend the folk high school here. One year suddenly became two.

218688.excerpt_en: Local council leader Arild Olsen (Labour) lashes out at Venstre and Oddmund Rønning after Rønning criticised the political leadership for closed-door processes from the podium at the local council’s latest meeting. He accuses Rønning of political games, distorting facts and outright lies. “He is dragging local democracy through the mud,” Olsen rages.
218688.subtitle_en: “Venstre actively took part in all the processes it is now criticising as illegal. The party is playing political games that drag democracy through the mud,” says local council leader Arild Olsen.

218699.excerpt_en: To make the project a success, municipalities need local blood donors, and recruitment of emergency donors has already begun on Svalbard.
218699.subtitle_en: A new project will strengthen blood preparedness in municipalities across the country. People are now being urged to register as emergency blood donors. On Svalbard, many have already expressed interest in becoming “walking blood banks.”

218707.excerpt_en: Adam Douglas broke through when he won Stjernekamp in 2017. He is here for the third time this year, but 2017 was a very special experience. “It was because of this crowd up here that things worked out in Stjernekamp,” Douglas said.
218707.subtitle_en: Adam Douglas won Stjernekamp in the middle of Dark Season Blues four years ago. “It would never have happened without you,” he said in an onstage interview.
218707.tags_en: blues, Dark Season Blues, music, Svalbard life, culture
218707.title_en: “It would never have happened without you”

218728.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, 19 October, the folk high school students held a house concert to raise money for this year’s TV fundraiser. The concert opened with “Vem Vet” by Lisa Ekdahl, performed by Amanda Leonara Holme and Marie Lindbo.
218728.subtitle_en: The students at Svalbard Folk High School have come up with many creative ideas to raise money for this year’s TV fundraiser. A house concert is one of them.
218728.title_en: Going all out for this year’s TV fundraiser

218761.excerpt_en: Statistics from Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) show that voter turnout has increased in each of the past three local elections. Sixty-two percent of eligible voters cast a ballot in the most recent election, in 2019.
218761.subtitle_en: Increasing numbers have exercised their right to vote in Longyearbyen’s local elections. But turnout remains lower than on the mainland.

218774.excerpt_en: The Kulturhuset was packed when the annual auction in aid of the TV campaign took place. The first auction item was a bouquet of flowers.
218774.subtitle_en: This year’s TV charity auction took place last night, with Anne Lise Sandvik, Governor of Svalbard Lars Fause and Sveinung Lystrup Thesen as hosts, making it an evening filled with good cheer.
218774.title_en: TV Charity Auction Raises More Than NOK 500,000

218792.excerpt_en: “Congratulations, students, on a new, safe home close to the town center,” local council leader Arild Olsen said when the Norwegian Arctic Student Welfare Organization held the official opening of the new student housing at Elvesletta on Sunday.
218792.subtitle_en: With celebratory speeches and a ribbon-cutting ceremony, the new student housing was officially opened.

218810.excerpt_en: When the world shut down, Tommy needed something to do. He borrowed his father’s Nikon and started taking photographs.

218810.tags_en: culture, Svalbard life, Dark Season Blues, photography

218859.excerpt_en: There were ribbon-cutting scissors, waffles, bubbles in champagne flutes and words of praise when Longyearbyen’s frisbee golf course opened recently. Per Nilssen, chair of Svalbard Turn, cut the ribbon before the first users headed out onto the course, which has nine baskets along a route near the school.
218859.subtitle_en: Subzero temperatures and darkness are no obstacle to a round on the frisbee golf course. Mari Torgersen, 11, was first out.

218868.excerpt_en: Lennarth Kvernmo, head of business development for Longyearbyen Local Council (LL), has so far received no answer as to what happened to the grant money awarded to the bankrupt company Polar Permaculture Solutions. The company received just under NOK 600,000 of an approved NOK 800,000 grant from Svalbard Package 1.
218868.subtitle_en: The local council is considering filing a police report to trace grant money following a business bankruptcy. The head of business development is also urging people not to prejudge those involved.

218926.subtitle_en: The head of tourism is optimistic. Tourists will return quickly.

218928.subtitle_en: Visit Svalbard is asking the new government for increased funding.

218932.excerpt_en: The final delivery of bricks for the avalanche barrier being built between Sukkertoppen and the homes in Lia will be delayed.
218932.subtitle_en: The avalanche barrier below Sukkertoppen is delayed, but is due to be completed before Christmas.

218954.excerpt_en: The company Arctic Travel Concepts is bankrupt. The tourism company targeted tourists from Asia and had a turnover of more than NOK 6 million in 2019. “There has been virtually no activity in the company since the COVID-19 pandemic broke out in March 2020.”
218954.subtitle_en: Waiting for Chinese tourists to return proved too long. Olivia Ericson had to file for bankruptcy for her business.

218958.excerpt_en: Sebastian Bach stands in a bright red outdoor jacket in front of Mary Ann’s Polarrigg. He is now heading back to Stavanger after spending two weeks inspecting his new local community.
218958.subtitle_en: In January, Gruvelageret will get a new restaurant manager. His name is Sebastian Bach—not a German composer, but a spontaneous, outdoor-loving 31-year-old from Poland.

218977.excerpt_en: The calculation is as follows: 42 businesses applied for grants from Svalbard Package 1. The package amounted to NOK 25 million.
218977.subtitle_en: If the Svalbard packages totaling NOK 65 million are not fully used, businesses and politicians should agree on proposals for how the remaining money should be spent, the head of business development urges.
218977.title_en: Wants to Keep Unused Crisis Millions—If There Are Any

218979.excerpt_en: “It comes as no surprise,” says Store Norske director Jan Morten Ertsaas about the Governor’s recommendation to the Directorate for Cultural Heritage to preserve Isfjord Radio. Store Norske will continue its pilot project for the site’s energy transition, he assures us, while the Directorate for Cultural Heritage puts the preservation regulations in place.
218979.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard recommends that the Directorate for Cultural Heritage preserve Isfjord Radio. Store Norske will switch to green energy during the process.

219005.excerpt_en: Construction work began on Sunday below the recycling station at Sjøskrenten. The reason is that water and ice are causing problems in the area.
219005.subtitle_en: A ditch is to protect buildings and equipment from water and ice.

219018.excerpt_en: Cooperation, and organizations’ understanding of one another, is largely built before and after the exercise itself—and organizing exercises is also a valuable exercise in its own right. Friday, 8.

219030.subtitle_en: Exploring the possibility of reusing Svea’s control tower at Sjøskrenten in Longyearbyen.

219049.excerpt_en: “We ask the new government to withdraw the far-reaching regulatory proposals put forward by the previous government. 219049.subtitle_en: The proposals for field safety regulations and new, stricter environmental rules must go back to the drawing board, Svalbard’s business community says.

219055.excerpt_en: Minister of Research and Higher Education Ola Borten Moe (Centre Party) opened the Svalbard Conference on Tuesday morning. The conference is organized by the Research Council of Norway and is the third to be held.
219055.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s many researchers are important in finding tomorrow’s green energy solutions, says the minister.

219070.excerpt_en: That there are also undetected cases would not surprise infectious-disease control physician Knut Selmer. “We know there have probably been infected people at events, nightlife venues and cafés. Travel and testing are now normal, so this is simply something we have to expect,” says Selmer.

219081.excerpt_en: Hege Leithe, head of Polarflokken Nursery, says the panel must have fallen sometime during the night, but they do not know exactly when. They noticed what had happened when they arrived at work on Wednesday morning.

219081.title_en: Ceiling panel falls from roof at nursery

219086.excerpt_en: Chief administrative officer Morten Dyrstad recommends that the Administration Committee (AU), at an extraordinary meeting on Tuesday, allow Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) to borrow an additional NOK 3.5 million to complete the conversion of the former youth centre into a new nursery department. That is NOK 1.5 million less than at the previous stage and is due to less uncertainty in the calculations.
219086.subtitle_en: Converting a youth centre into a nursery will cost less than initially thought.

219099.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Environment Agency says no to filming birds in a nature reserve. The planned Netflix series is considered neither scientific research nor a “particularly compelling reason” to grant permission.

219167.excerpt_en: “It turns out that feedback from parts of the business community, including Svalbard Turn, has been very positive.”

219215.subtitle_en: The government must listen to local residents and businesses. Put Svalbard’s regulatory drive on hold.

219247.subtitle_en: Six people in total have tested positive for coronavirus in Longyearbyen. Knut Selmer, the infection-control physician at Longyearbyen Hospital, believes the virus has now truly taken hold in Longyearbyen.

219514.subtitle_en: The 200 torches were snatched up almost before the event had begun. Several hundred people demonstrated today against consultation proposals that would affect Svalbard.
