219516.excerpt_en: At a hymn evening at Huset, people sang through the hymns that have represented Svalbard over the past hundred years. Finally, they heard the new hymn, performed by the winners themselves. Wallin Larsen says she is fascinated by Svalbard, especially its nature and the northern lights.
219516.subtitle_en: The winners of the hymn competition, Angela Wallin Larsen and John Vegard Schow, performed the new Svalbard Hymn for the first time at Huset.

219529.excerpt_en: The rose-colored starling has been seen on Bear Island for the first time. A lone male spent the summer around researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute, they write on their website. “For much of the fieldwork, the rose-colored starling stayed near us,” says seabird researcher Hallvard Strøm.
219529.subtitle_en: A pink-feathered bird was blown off course and became the first of its kind recorded on Bear Island.

219541.excerpt_en: On the morning and late morning of Friday, November 19, 2021, a partial lunar eclipse will occur, with almost the entire lunar disk entering shadow.
219541.subtitle_en: On Friday, November 19, when the Moon is full, a partial lunar eclipse will occur. It will be best viewed from Svalbard.

219567.excerpt_en: The protection proposals lack legal harmonization and face opposition. Norwegian authorities are investing heavily in further protecting Svalbard. The argument for protection is linked to the future of the archipelago’s vulnerable natural environment and Norway’s responsibility to manage it on behalf of the international community.
219567.subtitle_en: The protection proposals lack legal harmonization and face opposition, write Arnstein Skaare and Bjørn Fjukstad.
219567.tags_en: opinion, Svalbard Treaty, mining, readers’ letter
219567.title_en: Credible Assertion of Sovereignty Through Protection?

219571.excerpt_en: Fossum says he is not surprised that the changes to the environmental regulations prompted reactions, but notes that engagement with this and several other issues is strong.
219571.subtitle_en: The section chief has lived in Svalbard for two periods and knows the environmental regulations well, having worked as the Governor’s chief environmental officer. He hopes to receive more specific feedback during the consultation.
219571.title_en: “Made Out to Be More Extensive Than It Is”

219621.excerpt_en: In February, the Polarjazz Spitsbergen board welcomes everyone to the 24th edition of Polarjazz.
219621.subtitle_en: Bugge Wesseltoft and Lars Lillo Stenberg will open the jazz festival at Svalbard Church.

219628.excerpt_en: The distribution station for COVID self-tests opens Monday, the Governor of Svalbard writes in a press release. Longyearbyen Community Council is opening the station in the car park by Longyear 78°.
219628.subtitle_en: From 11 a.m. Monday, people can collect free COVID tests from a dedicated station in central Longyearbyen.
219628.title_en: Free COVID Tests Distributed Here from Monday

219663.excerpt_en: “A year has now passed without us hearing anything. They said they would get this under way before Christmas last year.”
219663.subtitle_en: Since veterinarian Hans Kristian Mjelde came to Longyearbyen, he has repeatedly contacted the authorities about veterinary regulations in Svalbard.
219663.title_en: “At risk of allowing animals to suffer”

219671.excerpt_en: Dear Knut Fossum. Thank you for taking the time to listen to the opinions and knowledge of Longyearbyen’s residents in the important work you and your agency are currently carrying out.
219671.subtitle_en: Are we to understand the Norwegian Environment Agency section head’s statement correctly—that he believes we have not familiarised ourselves sufficiently with the consultation because we disagree with the agency’s proposal? If so, it is a dirty trick, the writer argues.
219671.title_en: A dirty trick by the Norwegian Environment Agency

219676.excerpt_en: As someone interested in environmental issues and a former employee at the power plant, I have followed the discussion about a new power plant for Longyearbyen closely.
219676.subtitle_en: Could small nuclear power plants be the energy solution for Svalbard?
219676.tags_en: letter to the editor, energy solution, energy supply, opinions

219686.excerpt_en: Disappointed by refusal to restart process. Disappointed Svalbard businesses are demanding major changes to, and investigations into, the proposed new rules. Otherwise, the dispute will continue.
219686.subtitle_en: Disappointed Svalbard businesses are demanding major changes to, and investigations into, the proposed new rules. Otherwise, the dispute will continue.
219686.title_en: Disappointed by refusal to restart process

219729.excerpt_en: “We’re not good enough. The biggest problem is electrical waste in general waste.”
219729.subtitle_en: Climate, the environment and sustainability are issues most people care about these days. But how good are Longyearbyen’s residents really at sorting their waste?

219734.excerpt_en: Patrick Bossart of Longyearbyen Community Council, Aktiv i friluft and Avinor worked together to get the rink ready this year. They have also arranged for various equipment to be available for loan.
219734.subtitle_en: At last, Svalbard’s skating enthusiasts can use the ice rink below Polarflokken kindergarten.
219734.title_en: The ice rink is ready for use

219762.excerpt_en: In 2010, Hurtigruten Svalbard took over operation of Rabalder at the Cultural Centre. Now the contract has expired, and Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) has been looking for new tenants able to run the popular café in Longyearbyen.
219762.subtitle_en: Not many people are able to run Rabalder when you consider the qualifications required.
219762.tags_en: Rabalder, leader, café contract, café, opinions

219765.excerpt_en: “It isn’t sustainable to be white in winter when it has become warmer,” says Kim Holmén of the Norwegian Polar Institute. He shows a picture of an Arctic fox trying to hide on a rocky beach.
219765.subtitle_en: Decades upon decades of research have not provided the answer to climate change. The solution lies in sharing knowledge and continuing to work together for a better future, says a polar veteran.
219765.tags_en: Norwegian Polar Institute, research, news, climate

219770.excerpt_en: At precisely 5:27 a.m., the power went out in Longyearbyen. The outage lasted half an hour, says Hans Normann, energy manager at Longyearbyen Community Council (LL). “Both turbines stopped.”
219770.subtitle_en: The town is running on backup power after both turbines at the coal-fired power plant stopped early Wednesday morning.

219785.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) reported this in a press release at 5:30 p.m. A shutdown of both turbines at the power plant caused a half-hour power outage at around 5:30 Wednesday morning. “The coal-fired power plant in Longyearbyen is producing electricity again.”
219785.subtitle_en: The coal-fired power plant was back in operation Wednesday evening. District heating, however, was still running on a backup solution.

219787.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, 16 November, around 240 people heard and watched the Norwegian Environment Agency present proposals for tighter environmental regulations in Svalbard.
219787.subtitle_en: The authorities have so far failed to take sufficient action on the challenges posed by a growing number of unorganised operators with small boats, writes Frigg Jørgensen.

219797.excerpt_en: No one else has tested positive at the hospital since the seventh case in Longyearbyen was confirmed.
219797.subtitle_en: The likelihood that there is coronavirus infection in Longyearbyen is greater than the likelihood that there is not, says Knut Selmer, infection-control physician at Longyearbyen Hospital.
219797.title_en: “We must expect coronavirus infections in town”

219799.excerpt_en: As the world’s northernmost diving club, Longyearbyen Diving Club are obvious participants. Some may think that diving into the dark Adventfjorden, with the sea barely above freezing and the air well below freezing, does not rank among the “top 10” things to do in life.
219799.subtitle_en: Every year, on the first Saturday in November at the same time, more than a thousand divers enter the water around the world. Perhaps the world’s most famous night dive: “Diversnight.”
219799.title_en: In deep water with the world’s northernmost diving club

219811.excerpt_en: Torgeir Prytz of LJFF gives his views in a letter to the editor of Svalbardposten on some of my statements to the same newspaper following the consultation meeting on the environmental regulations.
219811.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Environment Agency welcomes all input on the local consequences of its specific proposals for new environmental regulations in Svalbard.
219811.tags_en: Svalbard Environmental Protection Act, opinions, letter to the editor, torchlight procession, Norwegian Environment Agency

219823.excerpt_en: Following the power outage at Longyearbyen’s coal-fired power plant on Wednesday morning, there were problems with the fuel supply for the backup power system. This emerged in a press release from the Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) on Wednesday evening. “We had problems getting diesel into the backup power system.”
219823.subtitle_en: The fuel for the backup power plant was the wrong type and had to be heated before it could be used.
219823.title_en: Diesel had to be heated before use

219837.excerpt_en: The 40 paintings in the Kåre Tveter Collection in Svalbard are being presented in a book due to be published next year to mark the artist’s 100th anniversary. The project is a collaboration between two foundations—the Kåre Tveter Collection Foundation in Svalbard and the Lyshuset Picture Collection Foundation in the artist’s home municipality of Sør-Odal—as well as the latter municipality.
219837.subtitle_en: Korkpenger will provide English text for a lavish book marking the 100th anniversary of a Svalbard artist.

219870.excerpt_en: One of them was Casper Kjøren (7), who has taken part in the race since he was three. “I actually like it. It was a bit cold, but I’m glad it wasn’t too warm.”
219870.subtitle_en: Twenty-two children and adults braved the weather to take part in Svalbard Turn’s annual Christmas Mile.
219870.title_en: “It’s a good thing it wasn’t too warm”

219888.excerpt_en: The helicopter takes off from the helibase in Longyearbyen. On board are a cellist, three representatives from the Governor of Svalbard’s office and a journalist.
219888.subtitle_en: Meetings are not always equally exciting, but a cello concert drew residents of Barentsburg to the community centre for this year’s public meeting.

219896.excerpt_en: The 25-year-old from Nesodden has not regretted for a second moving up here. She works as a bartender at Svalbar, a job she greatly enjoys. “I’m a very sociable person, so I like working in the bar and talking to people,” Johansen says.
219896.subtitle_en: For the past six years, Rasa Cassandra Johansen lived in Perth, Australia. When she grew tired of the heat, she wanted to try something completely new and applied for a job in the far north.

219922.excerpt_en: Local Council leader Arild Olsen took the opportunity to highlight the positive aspects of Longyearbyen—and pointed out that he feels the focus has at times been too negative. “There are, of course, many serious issues that affect us all and challenge us, both as individuals and as a society.”
219922.subtitle_en: As tradition dictates, the first Sunday of Advent was marked on Sunday. The new square was also officially opened.

219936.excerpt_en: Last week, people held a torchlight procession before the public meeting on the new environmental legislation in Longyearbyen. It is not only the tourism industry that is feeling the impact of tighter environmental laws.
219936.subtitle_en: When we talk about the elephant in the room, we mean an obvious truth that no one wants to discuss. And elephants can quickly cause uproar and destruction.
219936.tags_en: opinion, Svalbard Environmental Protection Act, torchlight procession, editorial

219957.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council reported the matter to the police. The vandalism is alleged to have taken place while the school was using the hall.
219957.subtitle_en: Last Wednesday, what police describe as major vandalism was carried out at Svalbardhallen.

219969.excerpt_en: One of the incidents involved a polar bear that was euthanized during the night of 1 January 2020.
219969.subtitle_en: Two polar bears died after being handled by the Governor of Svalbard’s Office in January 2020. The Norwegian Bureau for the Investigation of Police Affairs investigated the incidents.
219969.title_en: Special Unit Investigated Polar Bear Handling

219979.excerpt_en: Today, Tuesday, the hospital is vaccinating people over 65, those receiving their first or second dose, and people with underlying conditions.
219979.subtitle_en: This week, an unvaccinated permanent resident tested positive for coronavirus. The chief infection-control physician’s message is clear: People who are not vaccinated must do so today.

219996.excerpt_en: The lorry that crashed into the guardrail while crossing the bridge over the Longyearelva early this autumn will hopefully be moved this week. This is according to an employee of Brekke Maskinstasjon, the company that owns the lorry.
219996.subtitle_en: The lorry standing in the ditch by Eventyrbrua may be moved this week.

220028.excerpt_en: They neither jingle nor weigh anything, but digital Svalbard coins do sell. So much so that the partners in SpareBank1 Group’s “svalbard.money” project are planning to produce more.
220028.subtitle_en: More digital coins are to be issued as part of the Svalbard project before Christmas. The first were sold at auction for up to NOK 12,000.

220037.excerpt_en: NKOM is now requesting further information, writing in a letter that it wants “concrete examples showing that the ‘Svalbard surcharge’ cannot be considered affordable for residents and businesses in Svalbard.” “Sounds strange.” Stein-Ove Johannessen, chair of the Local Council’s Environment and Business Committee, finds this an odd characterization. “…”
220037.subtitle_en: In April this year, Longyearbyen Local Council filed a complaint with the Norwegian Communications Authority (NKOM) concerning the Svalbard surcharge on postage.
220037.title_en: Asks for Examples Showing It Is Unaffordable

220042.excerpt_en: We reach the author by phone in Oslo. He has never been to Svalbard.
220042.subtitle_en: Didrik Magnus-Andresen is making his book debut with the graphic novel “Ultima Thule,” which is set in Svalbard.

220055.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Health and Care Services announced this in a press release on Thursday afternoon. “A major virus outbreak in Svalbard could, as a result of reduced health preparedness, challenge critical societal functions and lead to evacuations to the mainland, which in turn would place a strain on the air ambulance service,” the ministry writes.
220055.subtitle_en: From midnight on 2 December, travellers entering Svalbard must once again present a negative coronavirus test.

220072.excerpt_en: Just after 5 p.m. on Thursday, he had just finished a meeting with Longyearbyen Hospital and Longyearbyen Local Council.
220072.subtitle_en: Governor of Svalbard Lars Fause learned about the discussion concerning the reintroduction of a testing regime on Thursday morning. The emergency preparedness council will now meet Friday morning.

220074.excerpt_en: Residents can also use Dr. Dropin’s testing centre at Gardermoen, the company writes on its website. “Anyone who needs a valid certificate or proof on the Helsenorge website can come to us and get one.”
220074.subtitle_en: At Fredrik Langes gate in Tromsø, Svalbard travellers can take a free rapid test.
220074.title_en: Svalbard Travellers Can Get Tested Here

220078.excerpt_en: “I’m a man who grew up in Gausdal and has lived in Lier for 25 years. I’m married and have three grown-up daughters.”
220078.subtitle_en: The new senior police superintendent at the Governor’s Office, Stein Olav Bredli (52), is deeply fascinated by Svalbard.
220078.tags_en: police, Governor of Svalbard, appointment, news
220078.title_en: “I Completely Fell in Love with Svalbard”

220090.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has filed a police report and opened a case. This is according to senior police officer Kjell Arne Lundin at the Governor’s Office.
220090.subtitle_en: Someone hit this car on Wednesday morning—and drove away.

220099.excerpt_en: The person who has now tested positive on a rapid test is a visitor. According to Selmer, there is therefore good reason to believe the infection was brought from the mainland. “The hospital will therefore take a PCR test, but we cannot send it off until Monday.”
220099.subtitle_en: A new person tested positive on a rapid test Friday, Longyearbyen Hospital reports. At the same time, the emergency preparedness council has concluded that it will follow the national measures.

220130.excerpt_en: When the Polar Institute went through the submissions to count who had handed in the most mice, they had a good laugh. Someone named Luremus had submitted the most—fourteen in all.
220130.subtitle_en: A total of 72 mice were handed in by 28 people to the Norwegian Polar Institute’s mouse-catching campaign in Longyearbyen last year, but one name stood out. The best mouse catchers are now being rewarded for their efforts.

220132.excerpt_en: Former Foreign Minister Ine Eriksen Søreide stated from the Storting’s rostrum, in response to a question from our current Minister of Justice Emilie Enger Mehl on 16 December 2020, that Svalbard’s environmental legislation in practice takes precedence over the mining regulations.
220132.subtitle_en: The country’s previous government pursued policies that weaken the sovereignty the Svalbard Treaty grants Norway, particularly by undermining the mining regulations directly authorized and established under the treaty.
220132.tags_en: opinion, industry, mining, Austre Adventfjord, reader letter
220132.title_en: Has the Svalbard Treaty Ceased to Apply?

220146.excerpt_en: The latest update is that skier Heidi Weng has signed up for the event, Svalbard Turn writes in a press release. “Talented and likeable.” Managing director Elisabeth Leinan Johannessen of Svalbard Turn is pleased that Weng is heading north. “She is a talented and likeable skier whom it will be wonderful to have…”
220146.subtitle_en: Nearly two years after the last Svalbard Ski Marathon, plans are under way for a ski race this spring.
220146.title_en: Heidi Weng to Compete in the Svalbard Ski Marathon

220166.excerpt_en: How serious were last week’s events at the power plant? We know that the electricity went out briefly on Wednesday morning.
220166.subtitle_en: Last week’s events at the power plant show that we need a completely different pace in the work to establish a new energy supply for Longyearbyen.
220166.tags_en: opinion, renewable energy, energy supply, diesel, editorial
220166.title_en: Poor Diesel and Uncertain Energy Decision

220171.excerpt_en: She is leaving her job as a manual therapist to become the hospital’s top manager in Longyearbyen, after more than 25 years in her current position. “I applied for the job three years ago as well, when Bente (Brataas, editor’s note) got it.”
220171.subtitle_en: From the New Year, Kristin Furu Grøtting will take up the position of head of department at Longyearbyen Hospital.

220183.excerpt_en: A perfect ten. Rån AS and managing director Alexia Spencer received that score in two of the three criteria in the competition to run Rabalder.
220183.subtitle_en: Alexia Spencer won the competition to run Rabalder. The contract was ready to be signed when politicians halted the process. This week, the political do-over began—a process that could end with a new tender. “Unprofessional,” says Spencer.

220193.excerpt_en: In 2022, Mine 7 will deliver 30,000 tonnes of coal to the power plant, while between 90,000 and 100,000 tonnes will be exported to the one customer Store Norske has had for the past 40 years: Germany’s Clariant, Arbeidsmanden writes. Clariant has factories in the Munich area and in Bilbao.
220193.subtitle_en: The special properties of Svalbard coal make it ideal for moulds used in the metal industry.

220196.excerpt_en: This became clear on Monday, December 6, during the weekly meeting between Longyearbyen Local Council, the hospital and the Governor of Svalbard.
220196.subtitle_en: The town’s 16- and 17-year-olds will receive their second dose, while the remaining adult population will receive a third dose before Christmas.

220211.excerpt_en: Kåre Willoch died yesterday, aged 93. He was a prominent Conservative politician who also managed to become widely popular.
220211.subtitle_en: That was 36 years ago. Since then, no one has seen a prime minister at an anniversary celebration.
220211.title_en: He was the last prime minister to mark a treaty anniversary

220216.excerpt_en: In the effort to persuade the authorities to restart work on new rules for environmental protection and traffic on Svalbard, Svalbard’s tourism businesses have invested in legal assistance. This adds further weight to arguments from Visit Svalbard and others that the consultation proposals should be discarded and the process begun anew.
220216.subtitle_en: Legal assistance is lending fresh strength to demands that the proposed new environmental and traffic regulations for Svalbard be scrapped.

220219.excerpt_en: “We have considered it back and forth, but concluded that we need to take certain steps regardless of what the government decides,” says principal Frode Westby Thorstad. The government has announced a press conference and stricter measures on Tuesday evening.
220219.subtitle_en: All joint gatherings at Longyearbyen School have been cancelled or reorganised as a result of quarantine regulations.

220239.excerpt_en: Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said this during today’s press conference. The measures take effect overnight into Thursday, December 9.
220239.subtitle_en: The one-metre rule, table service and a ban on alcohol service are among the new measures.

220242.excerpt_en: Jan Eggum sings that, but he is not singing about coronavirus, Omicron, COVID or the pandemic. He sings about raw love, betrayal, new women, family and realism.
220242.subtitle_en: This government has learned nothing about planning and information flow when implementing coronavirus measures aimed at Svalbard.

220268.excerpt_en: “At last,” the local politicians say; they now have a business fund to draw on. Starting next year, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) will set aside NOK 1.5 million.
220268.subtitle_en: From next year, LL will allocate NOK 1.5 million to good business projects. The new business fund is intended to shake loose more money from the state.
220268.title_en: “Hello, central government: It’s your turn now”

220271.excerpt_en: “Notice is hereby given that compensation will be demanded (...) up to a maximum of NOK 2,500,000 if Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) maintains its breach of contract,” states a letter from Rån AS’s lawyer, Ahmed Lindov, a copy of which Svalbardposten has received.
220271.subtitle_en: If Rån AS is not allowed to operate Café Rabalder, the company warns that it will seek up to NOK 2.5 million in compensation.
220271.title_en: Million-kroner compensation claim over café contract

220290.excerpt_en: This will improve safety in the popular area, while data is updated hourly and available to everyone here. It is one of only a few meteorological stations inland in central Svalbard, and is located at approximately 400 metres above sea level, UNIS writes in a press release.
220290.subtitle_en: UNIS has installed yet another weather station. This time at Fritham.

220294.excerpt_en: “The cremation furnace for dead animals has been operating for about a week,” says Karine Hauan, professional manager for waste management and the environment at Longyearbyen Local Council (LL). This brings an end to burying carcasses at the landfill, as has been done until now.
220294.subtitle_en: From now on, dead animals will be cremated on Svalbard. Owners can have the ashes returned in an urn.
220294.title_en: A better solution when animals die

220312.excerpt_en: This interview came about in a somewhat unusual way, because private individuals do not usually call to ask to be featured in the newspaper, as Erik Eikenes Bassermann did. But he had a reason.
220312.subtitle_en: He was dropped off downtown without food or money. About a day later, Erik Eikenes Bassermann (18) is sitting in Svalbardposten’s meeting room. How did he end up here?

220333.excerpt_en: Svalbard Folk High School is expanding its programme with a new course next school year: dog sledding. The school has entered into an agreement with Arctic Husky Travellers, and Anja Wiid has been hired as the course teacher.
220333.subtitle_en: The folk high school is expanding its offerings with a dog-sledding programme in cooperation with Arctic Husky Travellers.
220333.tags_en: Svalbard Folk High School, dog sledding, Tommy Jordbrudal, news

220344.excerpt_en: Hanne and Anders Wiik Mittet are sitting in the café, waiting for the doors to the concert to open. They have never attended a Mollkameratene concert before, but Anders works with two of the group’s members.
220344.subtitle_en: Mollkameratene’s alternative Christmas concert went ahead despite new restrictions. Face masks, a maximum number of guests per table and two concerts could not stop an evening of humour, good cheer and music.

220368.excerpt_en: 2021 was the year of paving stones. Longyearbyen’s pedestrian street was relaid, expanded and improved.
220368.subtitle_en: The local council is building a new pedestrian street for NOK 27 million. The neighbours will pay back most of it. In the long run.
220368.title_en: What businesses will pay for the new pedestrian street

220376.excerpt_en: On October 25, 2021, I bought a flight ticket online for the Longyearbyen–Tromsø route on the 14th.
220376.subtitle_en: “My experience with you has been marked by unserious, shoddy and highly unprofessional handling of this matter,” the contributor writes.
220376.tags_en: opinion, reader’s letter, air passengers, SAS
220376.title_en: Dear SAS, you can’t be serious

220382.excerpt_en: “We received a report of a heavily intoxicated woman who had fallen asleep in a ditch,” the duty chief constable told reporters Monday morning. When the Governor’s Office went to the place where the woman had supposedly fallen asleep, passers-by had apparently already helped her, but the police still considered it necessary to escort her home.
220382.subtitle_en: After a damp night out, most people can feel Ole Lukøye—old Mr Sandman—slowly but surely arriving. That was also the case for a woman in Longyearbyen on Saturday evening, the Governor of Svalbard reported Monday.

220385.excerpt_en: “I am very pleased with the testing regime introduced last time—that all travellers must present a negative coronavirus test before departing for Svalbard. We have discussed its importance before, but with the new Omicron variant, I am absolutely delighted about it.”
220385.subtitle_en: On Monday morning, the government announced a press conference on the coronavirus situation that evening at 8 p.m. Chief medical officer Knut Selmer is pleased with the restrictions already introduced for Svalbard.

220397.subtitle_en: Over the next few weeks, Mine 3’s heated warehouse will be converted into a restaurant. After New Year, eight different chefs will create different menus over eight weeks in the pop-up restaurant.

220411.excerpt_en: “Today will be our last day open. There will be layoffs across the board,” Steve Daldorff Torgersen said Tuesday.
220411.subtitle_en: As during the previous ban on alcohol service, Karlsberger Pub will close its doors.

220424.excerpt_en: “For the industry we represent, temporary layoffs may become necessary, and we are receiving reports that many are now considering this measure.”
220424.subtitle_en: According to managing director Ronny Brunvoll, temporary layoffs are not currently an option for Visit Svalbard. They consider it very important to remain fully operational in the period ahead.

220429.excerpt_en: “It is a bittersweet day for us. It will be the final day in an eleven-year run,” says Kjell Olav Pettersen, hotel manager at Hurtigruten Svalbard.
220429.subtitle_en: The much-discussed contract for Hurtigruten Svalbard’s operation of Rabalder expires at the turn of the year, as many know. The café is now inviting people to one final gathering.
220429.tags_en: news, Rabalder, local council leader, Local Council
220429.title_en: “Who knows what the future will bring”

220438.excerpt_en: This also accords with the chief administrative officer’s recommendation. The matter was also discussed at the previous Local Council meeting, but it was then decided to postpone it on the advice of a lawyer.
220438.subtitle_en: A unanimous Longyearbyen Local Council voted on Tuesday evening to report Polar Permaculture AS to the police.
220438.title_en: Local Council votes to report company to police

220452.excerpt_en: The interior of Longyearbyen Hospital has been decorated for Christmas: a Christmas tree, baubles and angels.
220452.subtitle_en: If you have visited the hospital in recent months, you have certainly met them. Hege Heimdal Lamo, 53, and Rebekka Heimdal Pettersen, 20, have settled well into their jobs as medical secretaries—and into Longyearbyen in general.

220471.excerpt_en: Initially, there was nothing to indicate that an evacuation was necessary, but early on Wednesday morning they were asked to come to Bear Island to carry out a closer check of the crew. Evacuated to Bear Island. The leak is believed to have been substantial, according to the Governor’s Office.
220471.subtitle_en: On Tuesday evening, around midnight, the Governor of Svalbard was notified of a boat north of Bear Island that had suffered an ammonia leak.

220482.excerpt_en: At the start of the new year, he will return to his “old” job as head of the technical sector before starting his new position in Lofoten on 1 March. “At first, I had no plans to move.”
220482.subtitle_en: Morten Dyrstad, acting chief administrative officer of Longyearbyen Local Council, has been appointed municipal chief executive of Vestvågøy Municipality.
220482.title_en: Becomes municipal chief executive in Lofoten

220484.excerpt_en: The trapping station at Austfjorden has a long tradition of offering overwintering positions. This is usually advertised during the autumn, but that has not been done this year.
220484.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has not advertised an overwintering position at Austfjordnes for next year. Kristin Heggelund, head of environmental protection at the Governor’s Office, says it is not among the tasks being prioritised.
