220484.title_en: “Not at the top of the priority list”

220495.excerpt_en: People arriving in Svalbard must test for SARS-CoV-2 within 24 hours of arrival. The test must be an antigen rapid test (self-test).
220495.subtitle_en: If you are travelling to Svalbard, a test before departure is not enough. You must now also take a rapid test within 24 hours of arrival.
220495.tags_en: coronavirus test, news, coronavirus, coronavirus crisis
220495.title_en: You must now also test after arrival

220508.excerpt_en: The aim of the Arctic Safety Conference, organised by the Arctic Safety Center in the autumn, is to focus attention on safety in the Arctic. One of the topics discussed at the conference was the safety of women in Arctic fieldwork, an area that has been little researched.
220508.subtitle_en: Poorly adapted equipment and clothing, inadequate toilet facilities and sexual harassment in the field are challenges faced by women in Arctic fieldwork. They are now calling for greater adaptation and better solutions in the field.

220510.excerpt_en: Some time ago, a post was made on Facebook claiming that there was too much complaining and whining in Longyearbyen. There is good reason to whine and complain when you see how the authorities are wreaking havoc on people and lives up here.
220510.subtitle_en: It was easier than I thought.

220545.excerpt_en: Both the accused, a man in his 20s, and the injured party are permanent residents of Longyearbyen.
220545.subtitle_en: On the day before Christmas Eve last year, a man was punched in the face, causing him to fall and suffer neck fractures and loss of consciousness. A man has now been charged and must appear before the Nord-Troms and Senja District Court.

220564.excerpt_en: It was chef Fredrik Lund who recorded this video of the polar bear that visited on 19 December. “He stayed around here for about 10 minutes.”
220564.subtitle_en: Since 5 December, the crew at Hopen have been visited by 15 polar bears.
220564.title_en: Another bear visit at the station

220577.excerpt_en: Here is the updated Christmas programme: Christmas Eve at 2 p.m. and 3 p.m.: Christmas services outdoors on the church grounds by Svalbard Church. Christmas worship services outdoors by the church.
220577.subtitle_en: “The new restrictions mean changes to the church’s Christmas programme,” says parish priest Siv Limstrand.
220577.title_en: Church forced to change its programme

220598.excerpt_en: “Lufttransport saw the damage and polar bear tracks on Sunday while conducting a training flight. They did not see a bear when they were there,” says Chief Superintendent Taina Maria Bjørkås of the Governor’s Office.
220598.subtitle_en: A polar bear broke through a door at Totakteren’s cabin in Bjonahamna. The Governor’s Office repaired the damage on Monday.

220641.excerpt_en: The injuries to the reindeer and tracks in the area indicate that the injuries were caused by one or more dogs. “We do not know which dog or dogs injured them, so we urge dog owners to double-check that their dogs have not escaped,” says Chief Superintendent Arnfinn Ree of the Governor’s Office.
220641.subtitle_en: Just after 3 p.m. on Tuesday afternoon, the Governor of Svalbard was notified of two injured reindeer in Adventdalen.

220644.excerpt_en: “On two occasions, we have uncovered shoplifting through random checks linked to the self-service checkouts,” says Ronny Strømnes, managing director of Coop Svalbard. Strømnes says the thefts mainly involve various types of energy drinks.
220644.subtitle_en: In recent weeks, Svalbardbutikken has caught young people aged 13 to 15 attempting to steal through the self-service checkouts. The store now wants to tighten procedures to stop the trend.
220644.title_en: “Some young people think it’s okay to steal”

220648.excerpt_en: The two projects will receive a total of NOK 657,000. Hearts In The Ice will use the money for teaching about plastic pollution, while the folk high school will continue cleaning up Isfjorden.
220648.subtitle_en: Hearts In the Ice and Svalbard Folk High School receive funding from the Handelens Miljøfond environmental fund.
220648.title_en: Two Svalbard projects receive environmental funding

220674.excerpt_en: “Earlier this year, I was Santa Claus for a kindergarten where my mother used to work. So when I came here on holiday, she asked whether I would consider a Santa job that was a little outside my comfort zone.”
220674.subtitle_en: This far north, one might think Santa Claus would come here himself on Christmas Eve, but this year he has had to call in a substitute. Andreas Moberget, 17, is taking on the job.
220674.title_en: “I didn’t think there would be so much interest”

220683.excerpt_en: “This will be the biggest full-scale change for the entire archipelago ever,” says Sergey Gushchin, the consul general in Barentsburg. “Administrative Area 10 will no longer be an unrestricted area to move around in. If you are not registered as a permanent resident, your ability to move outside the settlements will be severely restricted.”
220683.subtitle_en: The new field safety regulations and proposed new environmental regulations will be highly negative for Russian research and tourism operations in Svalbard.

220689.excerpt_en: “We have noticed a slight increase since the ban on serving alcohol was introduced, but nothing dramatic,” says Nils Harald Schrøen of Nordpolet.
220689.subtitle_en: Christmas food, rice cream, Christmas cookies and Christmas beer—a mountain of rich, heavy food that often calls for five or even ten minutes on the sofa after it has been consumed. Nils Harald Schrøen of Nordpolet therefore recommends a slightly lighter drink option for those who feel that too much of a good thing can be a bit much.
220689.title_en: “Both white and sparkling wine can go well with rich food”

220697.excerpt_en: “The people one generally worries about at Christmas are the so-called vulnerable members of society. We have very few of them up here,” says Selmer.
220697.subtitle_en: Every year, page after page is written about people who experience Christmas as a particularly lonely time. Infectious-disease control physician Knut Selmer at Longyearbyen Hospital, however, believes the situation looks somewhat different here in the north, despite the infection-control measures.
220697.tags_en: school, infectious-disease control physician, Christmas, news
220697.title_en: “It Would Be Foolish to Organize a Large Gathering Now”

220726.excerpt_en: For Longyearbyen, it is important to keep watch in these times. It is important not to remain passive.
220726.subtitle_en: Taking a picture like this may be impossible in two years.
220726.tags_en: opinions, coal, Mine 7, jobs, reader’s letter
220726.title_en: The Foundation Stone Has Come Loose and Is Adrift

220771.excerpt_en: One person in a snowmobile group consisting of a guide and three guests crashed into a post near SSU. “The man was dazed and bruised and was taken to the hospital for a check-up,” says Chief Superintendent Ragnar Schjølset of the Governor’s office.
220771.subtitle_en: A man in his fifties was taken for a medical examination after a snowmobile accident yesterday evening.

220847.excerpt_en: All three tested negative before leaving the mainland, but tested positive on the test they were given after arrival. One immediately after arrival, one after three or four days and one about a week after arrival, according to the doctor.
220847.subtitle_en: Three people have tested positive for coronavirus since 23 December. Infectious-disease control physician Knut Selmer believes we must prepare for more infections in the time ahead.

220868.excerpt_en: Øystå comes from the Drøbak newspaper Amta, where she has been both editor and journalist. “My husband Alf and I have been looking for a new reality for a little while. We’re from the seaside town of Drøbak, so when I saw the job advertisement, I had no doubts.”
220868.subtitle_en: Journalists Felicia Øystå (52) and Marcus Røseth Isachsen (20) have joined Svalbardposten.
220868.title_en: Felicia and Marcus Are Svalbardposten’s New Journalists

220879.excerpt_en: In darkness and light snowfall, three women walk down the steps of the Aeroflot plane at Svalbard Airport. At home in Hovseter, Oslo, Foreign Minister Knut Frydenlund has just finished decorating the Christmas tree.
220879.subtitle_en: At 8:30 p.m. on 23 December 1975, a diplomatic crisis steps off the Aeroflot flight from Moscow.
220879.tags_en: history, Svalbard Airport, aircraft in Svalbard, life in Svalbard

220905.excerpt_en: The artist from New Hampshire has spent the past few months as an artist-in-residence at Artica and is very pleased with her stay here on Svalbard. In the project Time Line, she used a laser to point in the exact direction in which the solar system is moving through the galaxy.
220905.subtitle_en: Have you seen a green laser in the sky in recent weeks? Then you probably saw Jessica MacMillan’s (34) project, Time Line. MacMillan had set realistic expectations because she knew the project could still fail. But she was surprised by the result.

220917.excerpt_en: “I wanted to get out here because it was a project the three of us were going to do together. And then there was the matter of planning a trip for a long time, from what we needed to bring to how it would work.”
220917.subtitle_en: Kristin (25), Mads (25) and Jeppe (32) usually work as guides in Longyearbyen. This autumn, they did something few people have the opportunity to do: spend three months at the trapping station in Farmhamna.
220917.title_en: “We Wanted to Get Far Away—That’s How It All Started”

220923.excerpt_en: The day before he was due to travel, Blomli received a call from an airport employee who had noticed that he had applied to the Norwegian Food Safety Authority for an inspection of Mitra at the airport before departure. But there was nothing on the flight booking indicating that he was travelling with a dog. “I booked the ticket on the 14th.”
220923.subtitle_en: Jan Ole Blomli and his dog Mitra were ready for a Christmas holiday on the mainland and had tickets for 22 December. Or so he thought.
220923.title_en: SAS Procedural Failure Led to Christmas in Longyearbyen

220936.excerpt_en: After the government imposed a complete ban on alcohol service for four weeks from 14 December, the industry called for wage-support funding.
220936.subtitle_en: Many chose takeaway from the town’s restaurants on New Year’s Eve. Several of the restaurants are also fully booked.
220936.title_en: “Everyone We Spoke to Wanted to Keep Their Reservations”

220961.excerpt_en: If you had to pinpoint what interests Svalbardposten’s readers most, it is clearly stories about polar bears. The story about the polar bear attack in Mohnbukta has been particularly widely read.
220961.subtitle_en: It will soon be time to wave goodbye to 2021 and welcome a new year. For that reason, we want to take a brief look back at the year that has passed and all the stories that have been published.
220961.tags_en: Mohnbukta, polar bear, 2021, news, Mark Sabbatini
220961.title_en: “We Can Feel the Government and Administration Tightening Their Grip on Svalbard”

221000.excerpt_en: When I met High North News editor Arne O. Holm at an event at UNIS earlier this winter, he asked, as he normally does, “How are things?” I replied that the government, the state and the administration are currently wreaking havoc on Svalbard.
221000.subtitle_en: 2022 will quickly become like 2021—and like most of the years before it.
221000.tags_en: Norwegian Environment Agency, opinions, editorial, voting rights
221000.title_en: “Oh, Right. Then Everything’s Normal Up Here.”

221020.excerpt_en: It can be difficult to give an overall answer to what the weather was like on Svalbard in 2021, but meteorologist Ine-Therese Pedersen at Svalbard Airport has given it a try. “In 2021, we mostly had mild temperatures, with all monthly averages 2–4 degrees above normal.”
221020.subtitle_en: If this year’s weather is summed up as briefly as possible, one could say it has been slightly warmer than normal, even though many may remember a cold summer.
221020.title_en: “The Past Few Summers Have Been Getting Warmer and Warmer”

221028.excerpt_en: Jovna is not known for being someone who takes up much space, despite often being at the center of cultural and musical events in Longyearbyen. It is clear that what he says is carefully considered, and he does not come across as someone who speaks off the cuff.
221028.subtitle_en: Jovna Zakharias Dunfjell (38) boarded a plane to Svalbard for the first time on 28 August 2015 to begin work as a church musician at Svalbard Church. The year would, in its final weeks, become part of history.
221028.title_en: “I Thought a Lot About What Would Have Happened If I Had Stayed”

221043.excerpt_en: Governor Lars Fause previously said that establishing a public prosecutor position had been discussed for two or three years.
221043.subtitle_en: A long-awaited position at the Governor’s office has now been filled, and the new public prosecutor begins in March.

221058.excerpt_en: As many people now return to Longyearbyen after the Christmas holidays on the mainland, there is naturally concern about whether they will bring coronavirus infection to the island. A large proportion of those returning are also school students.
221058.subtitle_en: At Longyearbyen School, they will take active steps to prevent a possible outbreak after school resumes on Tuesday. Principal Frode Westby Thorstad says they are always apprehensive about the infection situation after holidays, but are now especially alert because infections have been recorded in town.
221058.title_en: “Dependent on Students and Parents Taking It Seriously”

221085.excerpt_en: Fifteen men sailed from Tromsø in early August 1912 aboard the motor cutter “Herzog Ernst”, bound for the northern coast of Svalbard. The leader was the young German lieutenant Herbert Schröder-Stranz.
221085.subtitle_en: A poorly planned summer expedition would cost eight men their lives, while seven others endured months of hardship in cold and darkness with inadequate equipment.
221085.tags_en: history, Svalbard history, life in Svalbard

221089.excerpt_en: The visit has been in the planning for more than two years, and the formal request has now been sent to the Governor. The reason is that Albert I organized and financed four expeditions to Svalbard that contributed to the development of Norwegian Svalbard research and the establishment of what would later become the Norwegian Polar Institute.
221089.subtitle_en: This year marks 100 years since Prince Albert I died. It could mean a distinguished visit to Svalbard by his great-great-grandson, Prince Albert of Monaco.
221089.title_en: “He Loves Norway Very Much, Just as His Great-Great-Grandfather Did”

221120.excerpt_en: Several positive Covid-19 cases were recorded on Svalbard over the Christmas period. Two permanent residents were infected while travelling, and one permanent resident was infected here in town.
221120.subtitle_en: Knut Selmer, the infectious-disease control physician at Longyearbyen Hospital, confirms that three permanent residents have tested positive for Covid-19 in Longyearbyen. One of the cases is not linked to travel.
221120.tags_en: infectious-disease control physician, vaccination, coronavirus, news

221126.excerpt_en: Rüdiger was largely forced to remain still, while Rave gathered driftwood along the shores, collected snow for melting and took care of the cooking. He was also busy tending Rüdiger’s frostbitten foot and changing the dressings every third day at first.
221126.subtitle_en: Time dragged for Hermann Rüdiger and Christopher Rave in the cabin at Elvetangen.
221126.tags_en: Svalbard history, history, life in Svalbard

221131.excerpt_en: Both permanent residents and tourists travelling to Svalbard must take a rapid test within 24 hours before departure and are told that it can be taken at Dr. Dropin at Gardermoen.
221131.subtitle_en: Many travellers have experienced long queues and delays on their journey to Svalbard. A request has now been sent to the Ministry of Justice.
221131.title_en: “We Have Asked for Testing to Be Free”

221163.excerpt_en: Public health officer Knut Selmer writes in a press release that it has now been confirmed that the infections recently detected in Longyearbyen are the Omicron variant. “Omicron has also been detected in a person in Longyearbyen whose source of infection is unknown.”
221163.subtitle_en: Public health officer Knut Selmer at Longyearbyen Hospital says we must now prepare for an infection situation more like the one on the mainland.
221163.tags_en: news, public health officer, coronavirus, Longyearbyen Hospital

221166.excerpt_en: Of the 34 applications, 13 have been rejected for various reasons, and next week the politicians will decide whether to approve the recommendation. Three million kroner has been set aside for distribution, but the summary shows that the chief administrative officer’s proposal would distribute only NOK 2.5 million.
221166.subtitle_en: Next week, NOK 2.5 million in cork funds will be distributed among various applicants. And not everyone is equally happy with the administration’s recommendation.
221166.title_en: “I Hope the Politicians See the Value of the Work We Do”

221174.excerpt_en: When their Christmas plans did not turn out as they had imagined, the idea of going away arose. The journalist’s mother visited Svalbard in the 1990s and apparently never stopped boasting about all the experiences she had there.
221174.subtitle_en: When TV 2 journalist Karima Elisabeth Magnussen and her mother decided to spend Christmas on Svalbard and in Longyearbyen, it proved far more complicated than they had initially expected.
221174.title_en: “I Was the Only Infected Person on All of Svalbard”

221186.excerpt_en: Poor ice conditions on Isfjorden meant that the local relief expedition, consisting of four of the mining town’s finest dog mushers, did not set off across the fjord ice toward Kapp Thordsen and onward into Nordfjorden and Dicksonfjorden until 24 January.
221186.subtitle_en: What the six men in Sorgfjorden did not know was that Alfred Ritscher had managed to reach Longyear City, triggering international efforts to come to their rescue.

221207.excerpt_en: When politicians were to decide who would operate the Rabalder cultural centre café for the next five years, they decided to send the matter back to the chief administrative officer.
221207.subtitle_en: Next week, politicians will decide whether the new agreement is more palatable.
221207.tags_en: politics, news, Longyearbyen Cultural Centre, Rabalder, business
221207.title_en: The New Operating Agreement for Rabalder Is Ready

221221.excerpt_en: At the start of the year, Ellen Øseth became the new deputy director and director of the Administration Department at the Norwegian Polar Institute. Øseth has worked at the institute since 2009, first as a climate adviser and later as a senior adviser.
221221.subtitle_en: Ellen Øseth is joining the senior management of the Norwegian Polar Institute. Director Ola Arve Misund believes this will strengthen the institute’s management team.
221221.title_en: “I’m Really Looking Forward to Playing a Larger Role in the Strategic Leadership of the Norwegian Polar Institute”

221245.excerpt_en: After the government introduced stricter infection-control measures in mid-December last year, it became difficult for many Svalbard businesses to operate normally. For some, it became impossible.
221245.subtitle_en: Community Council leader Arild Olsen has never feared more for local jobs than he does now.
221245.tags_en: government, Community Council, coronavirus, Svalbard package, news
221245.title_en: “I’m More Concerned Now Than I’ve Ever Been Before”

221260.excerpt_en: This was reported by Space Norway AS, which owns and is responsible for the fibre connection between the mainland and Svalbard. Communications to and from Svalbard are nevertheless operating normally.
221260.subtitle_en: One of the two connections in the Svalbard fibre-optic system is out of service.
221260.tags_en: news, Governor, emergency preparedness council, internet
221260.title_en: “The Emergency Preparedness Council Has Been Called to a Meeting Today”

221281.excerpt_en: Mia and Audun Salte, who run Svalbard Husky together, are not short on determination. Their new operations building is now in place, and the two have many plans for this year as well. “We have received funding both from the Community Council and from Innovation Norway.”
221281.subtitle_en: Svalbard Husky is now seeing a surge in bookings and is also making plans for local residents.
221281.title_en: “We Want to Create an Activity Park for Permanent Residents”

221286.excerpt_en: On Sunday morning it became clear that one of the two connections in the Svalbard fibre-optic system was out of service. It was then decided to convene the emergency preparedness council at noon.
221286.subtitle_en: On Sunday, the emergency preparedness council met to map the possible consequences if a technical fault were also to occur on the other fibre-optic cable between Svalbard and the mainland.
221286.tags_en: Space Norway, Governor, fibre-optic cable, news
221286.title_en: “We Are Mapping the Consequences and Assessing Emergency Measures”

221296.excerpt_en: In December last year, Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) decided to report the company to the police, partly on the basis of the trustee’s report, which described both improper business practices and evidence that operations had been conducted at creditors’ expense.
221296.subtitle_en: The final report following Polar Permaculture’s bankruptcy shows that, after everything has been sold, claims against the estate exceed NOK 2.2 million.
221296.tags_en: Polar Permaculture, news, crime, Governor, business
221296.title_en: “The Case Has Been Sent to the Director of Public Prosecutions”

221332.excerpt_en: Organized by Aktiv i friluft, Lene Jeanette Dyngeland had to deliver the sad news that there would be no Christmas-tree bonfire after all.
221332.subtitle_en: The bonfire of old Christmas trees was postponed because of the wind.
221332.tags_en: Aktiv i friluft, Christmas tree, news
221332.title_en: “It’s Lovely to See Such a Large Turnout”

221347.excerpt_en: “We no longer have control over the chains of transmission for each individual positive case,” public health officer Knut Selmer said about the infection situation in Longyearbyen on Tuesday. Thirteen coronavirus cases have now been registered in Svalbard so far this January.
221347.subtitle_en: Thirteen new coronavirus cases have been registered in Longyearbyen. Four of them have been confirmed as Omicron.
221347.tags_en: infection, public health officer, coronavirus, news
221347.title_en: “Now We Have to Do What We’ve Practised”

221366.excerpt_en: The supervisory committee has asked the administration for answers about liquor-control inspections in Longyearbyen. The committee now wants an account of the procedures used when such inspections are carried out.
221366.subtitle_en: The supervisory committee has asked the administration for answers about liquor-control inspections in Longyearbyen.
221366.title_en: “The Same People Come Every Time—and at the Same Time”

221373.excerpt_en: As the pandemic continues to rage around the world and new cases of infection are constantly being reported on Svalbard, people understandably feel a need to test for coronavirus. In Longyearbyen, the testing booth distributes rapid tests, but only according to certain criteria.
221373.subtitle_en: Why doesn’t everyone who asks for a rapid test get access to one?
221373.tags_en: Longyearbyen Hospital, rapid test, news, coronavirus

221389.excerpt_en: Including Statsbygg, the state owns around 60 percent of the housing stock in Longyearbyen. “We are interested in housing portfolios, but we are not interested in vacuuming up the market, and generally do not buy individual apartments put up for sale.”
221389.subtitle_en: Store Norske is expanding its housing portfolio with 76 new apartments. The company now controls 40 percent of all housing in Longyearbyen.
221389.tags_en: news, Store Norske, housing, housing market
221389.title_en: Store Norske Now Controls 40 Percent of the Housing Market

221400.excerpt_en: In previous years, both the tourism industry and local associations have expressed strong opinions about what they see as restrictions on travel opportunities in Svalbard.
221400.subtitle_en: The Governor has once again submitted proposed regulations on travel over sea ice for public consultation.
221400.title_en: “There Have Been Many Opinions on Social Media”

221415.excerpt_en: “With all the forces of good on our side,” we said before setting off—and we had not counted on the authorities. My wife thought we needed some encouragement this winter; she had received an irresistible offer to celebrate Christmas on Svalbard.
221415.subtitle_en: What is it like to be stopped when you are on your way to the promised land of Svalbard?
221415.tags_en: letter to the editor, coronavirus test, coronavirus crisis, opinions
221415.title_en: North and Down – The Story of Not Making It to Svalbard

221428.excerpt_en: Some received more, while others received less after the meeting of the Education and Culture Committee. Committee chair Kristin Furu Grøtting opened the meeting by asking whether any members had comments on the administration’s recommendation.
221428.subtitle_en: Several important changes were made when the cork funds were allocated.
221428.tags_en: Education and Culture Committee, cork funds, politics, news
221428.title_en: “This is an investment that will last for decades to come”

221433.excerpt_en: There had been considerable suspense surrounding the government’s decision on the ban on serving alcohol introduced a month ago. Restaurants in Longyearbyen have had many empty seats, but there is now reason for optimism again.
221433.subtitle_en: The taps reopen on Friday, but the government announced that there would be no changes to the practice of testing for Svalbard.
221433.title_en: Taps open—but testing on entry remains

221463.excerpt_en: In NRK’s regional final of Klassequizen, Longyearbyen School came joint first with Lavangen School. The school’s representatives competed against pupils from Lavangen School, Finnsnes School and Skånland School.
221463.subtitle_en: There was a fierce battle for first place when Longyearbyen School competed in the regional final of Klassequizen.
221463.title_en: “We hope we can show that there’s some brainpower up here”

221470.excerpt_en: At the government’s press conference on Thursday evening, it became clear that the measures introduced a month ago had been eased. Minister of Health and Care Services Ingvild Kjerkol gave a hesitant answer to Svalbardposten’s questions about the practice of testing upon entry.
221470.subtitle_en: Residents and business operators in Longyearbyen are furious after it became clear that there would be no changes to the entry measures.
221470.tags_en: tourism, news, coronavirus test, Minister of Health and Care Services, tourism

221481.excerpt_en: The discussion became heated at AMU’s meeting as members tried to determine what the new agreement should emphasise when the contract is put out to tender again. The premises have stood empty and dark since December, after Hurtigruten’s eleven-year contract expired.
221481.subtitle_en: The politicians on the Administration Committee (AMU) have now agreed on how the various criteria in the agreement for operating Rabalder should be weighted.
221481.title_en: “The agreement has been perceived as subsidised”

article_keywords_en: Minister of Health and Care Services
221499.excerpt_en: At Thursday’s press conference, Minister of Health and Care Services Ingvild Kjerkol (Labour) revealed her lack of knowledge about Svalbard when answering questions from Svalbardposten: “Erm, I don’t have a complete overview of that, but it’s the same as on entry to Norway.”
221499.subtitle_en: The government’s press conference once again demonstrated its poor knowledge of Svalbard.
221499.tags_en: testing regime, opinions, editorial, coronavirus, government
221499.title_en: Trusts everyone except those of us in Svalbard

221502.excerpt_en: Earlier this week, Minister of Trade and Industry Jan Christian Vestre visited Svalbard and injected plenty of enthusiasm into the Store Norske team working on energy development. “The political leadership in our ministry supports and is ambitious about the energy transition that is to take place.” After meeting all the parties, he is willing to open the toolbox.
221502.subtitle_en: 2022 is the most important year for Store Norske. But work on a new energy plan for Longyearbyen must gather pace.
221502.tags_en: news, energy supply, Store Norske, renewable energy
221502.title_en: Store Norske is itching to get started

221505.excerpt_en: “I thrive in the cold,” she says. Sarlote Ludborza, 36, has lived in Longyearbyen since October.
221505.subtitle_en: She is originally from Latvia, but has lived in Greece, Denmark, Lofoten, Stavanger and Bergen. When she needed peace in her life, she headed north to the cold.
221505.title_en: “I cried with joy when I arrived”

221520.excerpt_en: With only one internet connection, Svalbard is vulnerable, and if the other one fails, satellite communications are the alternative. Deputy Governor Sølvi Elvedahl says parts of the emergency preparedness council met on Friday. “We have outlined the consequences and measures; the preliminary conclusion is that this is an unlikely scenario.”
221520.subtitle_en: Last Friday, a failure was discovered in one of the two internet connections to and from Svalbard.
221520.tags_en: police, news, internet, fibre-optic cable, governor
221520.title_en: “We are working on contingency plans for the scenario”

221528.excerpt_en: Although Markusson started his job as museum director on Tuesday, 4 January, this is far from the first time he has set foot on Svalbard. “The first time I came up here was in 2000.”
221528.subtitle_en: Eystein Markusson is the new museum director at Svalbard Museum.
221528.title_en: “We are, after all, society’s most important memory”

221537.excerpt_en: The proportion of infected people has increased throughout January. According to Longyearbyen Hospital, 15 new infections were expected during the previous week.
221537.subtitle_en: Infections continue to rise in Longyearbyen. A case has now also been confirmed at Longyearbyen School.
221537.tags_en: news, coronavirus, infectious disease control officer, Longyearbyen School

221548.excerpt_en: The surcharge was introduced in 2004. Today, it costs NOK 499 to send a package to or from Svalbard, and many people have worked over the years to end this practice.
221548.subtitle_en: The local council is now asking Svalbard residents for specific input on how the Svalbard surcharge on packages affects them.
221548.title_en: “In practice, it’s cheaper to buy a plane ticket”

221573.excerpt_en: The company faces several complaints, including from Longyearbyen Local Council. The bankruptcy administrator reported both improper business conduct and evidence that operations may have been conducted at the creditors’ expense.
221573.subtitle_en: The Public Prosecutor’s Office for Troms and Finnmark Police District has now examined the bankruptcy of Polar Permaculture, and the Governor is continuing to work on the case.
221573.title_en: The Governor wants to investigate the bankruptcy further

221579.excerpt_en: The consultation published about a week ago has sparked local engagement, and Longyearbyen’s Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association (LJFF) is now proposing that there be no temporary closure of the affected areas to residents.
221579.subtitle_en: The Governor proposes changes to access on sea ice, but faces opposition from Longyearbyen’s Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association.
221579.tags_en: sea ice, governor, traffic ban, news

221590.excerpt_en: Throughout the pandemic, measures have been stricter and more extensive for Svalbard. And the unequal treatment continues.
221590.subtitle_en: The special COVID-19 testing regime for travellers to Svalbard worsens and prolongs the crisis for businesses and makes everyday life in the local community more difficult.
221590.tags_en: testing regime, reader letter, coronavirus test, coronavirus crisis, opinions
221590.title_en: Is Svalbard not part of Norway after all?

article_keywords_en: Ministry of Health and Care Services
221593.excerpt_en: The Governor has responded to inquiries from residents who have been on the mainland but cannot obtain a negative test result and therefore cannot return home to Longyearbyen. Chief medical officer for infectious disease control at Longyearbyen Hospital, Knut Selmer, confirms the issue. “It is well known that PCR tests can remain positive for longer than rapid tests,” he says.
221593.subtitle_en: People who have had COVID-19 may test positive on a PCR test long after the infection has passed. This could cause problems for Svalbard residents.
221593.title_en: Residents risk having their journey home delayed

221606.excerpt_en: On Monday, we wrote that the hospital expected 15 new infections during the second week of the year. The figure turned out to be 20—five more than the hospital and infectious disease control officer Knut Selmer had expected.
221606.subtitle_en: Infectious disease control officer Knut Selmer believes it would be strange to remove the testing regime, but is open to a solution involving vaccine passports.
221606.tags_en: infectious disease control officer, testing regime, coronavirus, news
221606.title_en: “I don’t want you to come to Svalbard unvaccinated”

221610.excerpt_en: “We have established the company Svalbard Bivrost Distillery AS. By the end of the month, we’ll be ready.”
221610.subtitle_en: Svalbard Bryggeri and Bivrost are starting production of vodka, gin and aquavit in Svalbard.

221617.excerpt_en: Rasmus Hansson of the Green Party believes it is entirely legitimate to link government funding to freedom of expression, and threatens to punish Visit Svalbard if it does not keep quiet (SP 18 January 2022). Longyearbyen’s Hunters’ and Anglers’ Association is not keeping quiet, but says it is not being heard when it provides input in administrative processes (SP 19 January 2022).
221617.subtitle_en: Relations are becoming increasingly strained between, on the one hand, Svalbard’s local population and business community and, on the other, parts of the administration and the central political establishment.
221617.tags_en: environmental protection, opinions, reader letter, tourism
221617.title_en: Administrative responsibility—more than the environment and safety

221631.excerpt_en: The snowmobile season is in full swing, and those who do not already have a snowmobile parked outside are probably interested in getting one. In Longyearbyen, there are two ways to buy one.
221631.subtitle_en: The used market is busier than ever and dealers are completely sold out. Where can you buy a snowmobile?
221631.tags_en: snowmobile, Svalbard Snowmobile Rental, IGP, news

221651.excerpt_en: The ministry has so far not answered the questions, but both letters on the public correspondence list and Governor Lars Fause confirm that a process has been initiated. The testing regime means that both residents and tourists travelling to Svalbard must take a rapid test within 24 hours before departure, and tourists must pay for the test.
221651.subtitle_en: A week on, the Ministry of Health and Care Services has still not answered important questions about the testing regime.
221651.title_en: “I can confirm that a process is underway”

221655.excerpt_en: Some politicians pointed out that they felt the process of finding a new operator for the Rabalder cultural café in the previous round had been poorly handled. As a result, they have now changed the procedure.
221655.subtitle_en: There was heated debate over the Rabalder process, but in the end the majority agreed.
221655.title_en: “The guidelines should have been more precise”

221666.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, 2 February, the police, fire service and ambulance service will conduct a so-called PLIVO exercise.
221666.subtitle_en: How should the emergency services respond if someone launched a firearms attack in town? Now Longyearbyen’s emergency services will practise precisely that.
221666.tags_en: police exercise, police, news, fire service, UNIS
221666.title_en: “That sounds very serious, but it is important that we practise for it”

221679.excerpt_en: In April last year, Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) filed a complaint with the Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom) concerning the Svalbard surcharge on parcels. Today, it costs NOK 499 to send a parcel to or from Svalbard.
221679.subtitle_en: Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre stated emphatically at the coronavirus press conference two weeks ago that Svalbard is part of Norway. This does not apply when the mail has to get through.
221679.title_en: The mail must get through—even when it costs more than you want to pay

221698.excerpt_en: In Svalbardposten on 18 January, we read your statements in the matter of Rasmus Hansson of MDG wanting to punish Visit Svalbard financially.
221698.subtitle_en: Trine Krystad of Visit Svalbard responds to MDG’s Olivia Ericson in the case concerning government support.
221698.tags_en: Visit Svalbard, politics, opinions, reader letter, tourism
221698.title_en: “The tourism industry does much of what you are calling for—shall we talk?”

221704.excerpt_en: The partial plan was considered by the local council last week. None of the politicians had any comments, and the result was unanimous. The background to the case is the relocation of cabins located in the so-called red zone—areas where an avalanche is considered likely to occur once every 100 years.
221704.subtitle_en: A partial plan concerning the relocation of existing cabins due to avalanche risk creates the opportunity to establish 18 new cabins.
221704.tags_en: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, politics, cabin plots, news
221704.title_en: “There are many good suggestions for how the cabin plots can be allocated”

221707.excerpt_en: Space Norway reported this this week, explaining that it was restored by supplying power from Longyearbyen to the fibre-optic cable.
221707.subtitle_en: Repairs to the fibre-optic cable that is one of Svalbard’s two internet connections are still ongoing, but reserve capacity has now been restored.
221707.tags_en: news, Space Norway, fibre-optic cable, internet
221707.title_en: Cause still unknown—but capacity has been restored

221733.excerpt_en: Although she has only been a permanent resident here since last September, she talks about Svalbard as if she had lived here all her life. With love and respect. “I visited Svalbard last April and worked from home here for a month.”
221733.subtitle_en: It was love at first visit when Michelle Le Gal Hermandsen visited Svalbard last spring.
221733.title_en: “Eating a packed lunch on Sukkertoppen and seeing the polar bear through binoculars was absolutely unique”

221750.excerpt_en: Money is distributed from: the Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund; cork money; the local council’s business fund; Innovation Norway; Svalbard Package 1 & 2. The allocations finance local environmental and climate measures, research, most cultural and sporting activities, innovation linked to new business activity, restructuring of the business sector and crisis packages. Applications and allocations under the grant schemes MUST be trustworthy.
221750.subtitle_en: Grant administration is a central part of Longyearbyen’s social structure.
221750.tags_en: grants, opinions, reader letter, bankruptcy, politics
221750.title_en: The credibility of Svalbard’s grant administration is at stake

221753.excerpt_en: A leak at the junction by UNIS is causing significant water accumulation in the area, the local council reports on its website. District heating operations engineer Harald Berre tells Svalbardposten that it is a fault in a domestic hot-water heat exchanger. “People are on it now.”
221753.subtitle_en: The local council is urging people to stay away from the area.

221774.excerpt_en: Speaking by phone from Tromsø, Emil describes what happened. The journey back to school went nothing like planned, and he is now left with extra expenses and experiences he could have done without. “I took a test at Gardermoen, as the rules require.”
221774.subtitle_en: When Emil Aga Løvdal (19) was due to return to Svalbard Folk High School after the holidays, he ran into major problems because of the testing regime.
221774.tags_en: Svalbard Folk High School, testing regime, news
221774.title_en: “I was thrown off the plane while my luggage continued on”

221780.excerpt_en: I own and run the Norwegian company Arctic Wildlife Tours AS. The company was founded on the basic idea of promoting environmental awareness and understanding of nature by giving our customers close encounters with nature.
221780.subtitle_en: In my eyes, MDG and Rasmus Hansson were once a source of hope for the environment. That hope has gradually faded, and after the parliamentarian’s latest contribution to Svalbardposten, it is clear that Hansson has understood neither as a politician nor as a biologist what sound environmental protection should and must be in the future.
221780.tags_en: environmental protection, MDG, reader letter, tourism, opinions

221784.excerpt_en: The Governor’s Office says that someone hit a car during the night. “We received a report this morning when the owner was going to work, so it may have happened during the night. The car’s lamp is smashed, so someone has hit it,” says senior police officer Lisbeth Hansen.
221784.subtitle_en: A car was hit during the night.
221784.title_en: Found that someone had crashed into the car

221806.excerpt_en: “We were supposed to get more fruit and vegetables, as well as some minced meat,” says Ronny Strømnes, managing director of Coop Svalbard. He has been informed that problems with the postal aircraft from Oslo are why mail and orders have not reached Svalbard over the past 24 hours.
221806.subtitle_en: Due to technical problems with the postal aircraft, yesterday’s mail shipment has not arrived in Svalbard.
221806.tags_en: Posten, postal aircraft, Coop Svalbard, news
221806.title_en: “We were supposed to get more fruit and vegetables”

221814.excerpt_en: Knut Selmer, the communicable disease control physician at Longyearbyen Hospital, can also report an upward trend in infections in Svalbard this week. “These are infections we don’t have an overview of. There are positive tests every day in Longyearbyen now,” he says.
221814.subtitle_en: If many people in Longyearbyen are kept away from work because of quarantine rules, it could create challenges for general preparedness. Communicable disease control physician Knut Selmer is concerned about this.

221832.excerpt_en: Research in Svalbard is one of the Government’s main priorities for Svalbard. Three actors play important roles in implementing Norwegian research strategies.
221832.subtitle_en: We are good at research infrastructure, but we can improve in other areas.
221832.tags_en: Ny-Ålesund, leader, Climate and Environment Minister, research, opinions

221849.excerpt_en: Barth Eide spent Thursday in Ny-Ålesund, where he was briefed on the research station, visited the Zeppelin Observatory and met with Kings Bay. The schedule was packed, and back in Longyearbyen on Friday he had clear views on climate change, both globally and locally for Longyearbyen.
221849.subtitle_en: Climate and Environment Minister Espen Barth Eide (Labour) says he is unaware that Norwegian researchers in Ny-Ålesund publish less than researchers from other countries.
221849.tags_en: Climate and Environment Minister, research, news, climate
221849.title_en: “I don’t think I would have criticized the government if I hadn’t been published”

221863.excerpt_en: As many people are now being, or have been, vaccinated with a third dose of the coronavirus vaccine, a so-called booster dose, it is also possible to test one’s way out of quarantine.
221863.subtitle_en: The latest changes to the quarantine rules make it easier to avoid long periods in quarantine.
221863.tags_en: news, communicable disease control physician, rapid test, coronavirus
221863.title_en: “We are monitoring developments day by day”

221871.excerpt_en: Visit Svalbard has taken criticism from none other than Rasmus Hansson—and the fact that we in the local MDG branch partly support that criticism—rather badly. Has Visit Svalbard inherited the confidence Store Norske used to have, as a kind of untouchable industry?
221871.subtitle_en: Visit Svalbard has taken criticism from none other than Rasmus Hansson—and the fact that we in the local MDG branch partly support that criticism—rather badly.
221871.tags_en: Svalbard Environmental Protection Act, politics, opinions, MDG, reader letter, tourism

221874.excerpt_en: It was in the early hours of Saturday that police were called out after receiving a tip about a car parked unusually. “We went to the scene and found the car. We then managed to track down the vehicle’s owner,” says Governor’s Office senior police officer Taina Maria Bjørkås.
221874.subtitle_en: Someone noticed a car parked strangely and called the police.
221874.title_en: Police called out after suspected drink-driving

221886.excerpt_en: “I’m going to finish writing a book, and I’ve been given a writing residency by the Artica Foundation. This suited me very well, because it’s incredibly difficult to find the time to write properly.”
221886.subtitle_en: Vibeke Koehler (41) has a job, leads an organization, has three children and a passion for writing. To do more of the latter, she sought out the darkness of Svalbard.
221886.tags_en: literature, author, people, Artica Svalbard, life in Svalbard
221886.title_en: The fantasy writer found peace in the darkness

221896.excerpt_en: Since July last year, Arnesen has held the position of chief superintendent with the Governor of Svalbard and spent much of his time in the office. But office work was not what drew him to Svalbard the first time in 2011. “I was on a weekend trip in May, in fantastic weather, with the best snowmobile experience you could imagine.”
221896.subtitle_en: Vidar Arnesen began his many years on Svalbard as a field inspector eleven years ago. But now it is over.
221896.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, news, accidents, police
221896.title_en: “Svalbard has fantastic nature, but it can also be brutal”

221897.excerpt_en: To minimise the damage caused by climate change and impacts on nature, we should ideally move towards zero emissions and continue towards powering our society with fuels of higher energy density. The world has systematically been paralysed when it comes to taking action.
221897.subtitle_en: In the election, politicians have shouted, debated and written op-eds, but as usual they omit the energy source that could take humanity to the next level, both economically and in terms of emissions.
221897.title_en: What about nuclear power on Svalbard?

221912.excerpt_en: Police described a quiet night, apart from a disturbance of the peace in the town centre. “We were called by witnesses who reported a person causing a disturbance,” says senior police officer Taina Maria Bjørkås with the Governor of Svalbard. They went to the area near the hospital. “We found the man and spoke to him.”
221912.subtitle_en: A man was removed due to a disturbance of the peace early Sunday morning.
221912.tags_en: disturbances of the peace, police, news

221937.excerpt_en: There was, however, an outbreak on board, and Hurtigruten has now been given a corporate fine of NOK 1 million. Both the captain and one of the ship’s doctors have also been fined. “The prosecution considers it right to fine Hurtigruten for this, and based on the nature and seriousness of the violation considers that 1…”
221937.subtitle_en: In August 2020, MS “Roald Amundsen” made two voyages from Tromsø and around Svalbard.

221961.excerpt_en: The defendant, a man in his 50s, was fined NOK 8,000 for violating Section 181 of the Penal Code. The section concerns fighting, noise or other improper behaviour that disturbs the public peace and order.
221961.subtitle_en: The explanations varied when witnesses were to describe what happened at Kroa one December evening in 2020.
221961.title_en: “It was a reaction in a moment of weakness”

221980.excerpt_en: Fur lice were first discovered on Arctic foxes in Svalbard in 2020. The lice were also observed in foxes trapped in 2021.
221980.subtitle_en: For the third time in a short period, fur lice have been discovered on foxes in Svalbard.
221980.tags_en: Norwegian Polar Institute, Arctic fox, news
221980.title_en: Fur lice discovered on Svalbard foxes

221985.excerpt_en: The changes mean that permanent residents, fully vaccinated people and people who have recovered from COVID-19 no longer have to be tested before departing for Svalbard.
221985.subtitle_en: The government is now easing the rules for travel to Svalbard, the Ministry of Health and Care Services writes in a press release.
221985.title_en: Relaxed rules on testing before departure to Svalbard

222004.excerpt_en: Several tourism businesses on Svalbard have written letters to the Ministry of Health and Care Services, expressed their views in newspaper columns and tried to convince the authorities of the unfairness they have experienced.
222004.subtitle_en: The testing regime is finally a thing of the past after many businesses fought a courageous battle.
222004.title_en: Testing regime ends—and venues can serve alcohol for longer

222018.excerpt_en: During the minister’s visit, Barth Eide also met the tourism industry to discuss both the environmental protection regulations and the field-safety regulations.
222018.subtitle_en: Ronny Brunvoll of Visit Svalbard says he is not unreservedly optimistic after meeting Climate and Environment Minister Espen Barth Eide.
222018.tags_en: tourism, Visit Svalbard, Minister of Climate and Environment, news

222031.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, the government presented significant changes to the national coronavirus measures. These largely also apply to the measures that have affected the nightlife industry for a long period.
222031.subtitle_en: Several local businesses are deeply dissatisfied that the government did not remove the one-metre distancing requirement when easing the remaining coronavirus measures.
222031.title_en: “Once again, our industry is taking the hardest hit”

222046.excerpt_en: As part of the decommissioning and clean-up following mining operations in Sveagruva, four archaeologists will work on monitoring, documentation and locating or uncovering covered cultural heritage sites. The archaeologists will work on Svalbard for around four months between May and September. “Svea is a major project that began in 2019.”
222046.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard sought four archaeologists for fieldwork in Sveagruva and received many applications.
222046.tags_en: Svea, news, Governor of Svalbard, summer job
222046.title_en: “It’s incredible that so many people are interested”

222049.excerpt_en: “Walruses have a somewhat similar history on Svalbard to polar bears. They were once widespread, but were hunted almost to extinction,” says Karoline Andaour, Secretary-General of WWF-Norway.
222049.subtitle_en: WWF is seeking “walrus detectives” to investigate how climate change is affecting walruses.
222049.title_en: “I hope future generations can have the same experience”

222055.excerpt_en: A so-called PLIVO exercise was held at UNIS on Wednesday afternoon. PLIVO stands for ongoing life-threatening violence, previously referred to as an active-shooter situation.
222055.subtitle_en: A PLIVO exercise was held at UNIS on Wednesday evening.
222055.tags_en: ambulance callouts, news, exercise, police, police exercise
222055.title_en: “We don’t get help from anyone else”

222088.excerpt_en: Polarjazz 2022 is under way, and Thursday’s opening filled the cultural centre to capacity. Polarjazz’s Vorspiel is described as the festival’s most popular concert.
222088.subtitle_en: This year’s Polarjazz got off to a start with the traditional Vorspielet.

222098.excerpt_en: On Tuesday it became clear that the testing regime in force on Svalbard would end. The consultation response submitted by the Governor of Svalbard has now been made public.
222098.subtitle_en: Submissions concerning the assessment of the testing regime have so far been confidential. But no longer.
222098.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, coronavirus, testing regime, news
222098.title_en: Proposed an exemption from the testing requirement

222133.excerpt_en: This year’s Polarjazz continues, and Friday’s programme offered rhythmic sounds and Norwegian folk songs. We heard both Trio de Janeiro and Jan Eggum.
222133.subtitle_en: Friday’s Polarjazz programme featured both folk songs and South American sounds.
222133.tags_en: life in Svalbard, Polarjazz, culture, concert
222133.title_en: From bossa nova to melancholy in Bergen dialect

222148.excerpt_en: They are extremely popular, often relatively cheap and only available to those of us who live permanently on Svalbard. Of course, we are talking about residents’ trips.
222148.subtitle_en: The concept of trips for permanent residents has exploded in popularity. That is perhaps not surprising when it gives you a trip at a fraction of the original price.
222148.tags_en: snowmobile, Svalbard Adventures, news, permanent residents
222148.title_en: “People who know how much the right clothing matters”

222172.excerpt_en: Following the adoption of the road-safety plan last November, the way is now open for Longyearbyen’s first roundabout—possibly the first in all of Svalbard.
222172.subtitle_en: High vehicle speeds entering the intersection, poor visibility and problems for vulnerable road users could lead to changes in the town centre.
222172.title_en: This could become Longyearbyen’s first roundabout

222205.excerpt_en: “The concert went very well, but it was all a bit spontaneous on my part. I said yes to working with three musicians who already had assignments.”
222205.subtitle_en: Jan Eggum played to a packed cultural centre during Friday’s Polarjazz, but this was not the first time the Bergen native has set foot on Svalbard. Despite the fact that he can’t stand cold weather.
222205.tags_en: Polarjazz, culture, life in Svalbard, music
222205.title_en: “I’m quite a wimp when it comes to cold weather”

222223.excerpt_en: The café at the cultural centre, Rabalder, has been empty since December. The tender documents have now been prepared, and next week politicians will provide their input.
222223.subtitle_en: Politicians will now provide input on the tender and the lease agreement.
222223.tags_en: politics, rabalder, Longyearbyen Cultural Centre, news
222223.title_en: The tender for operating Rabalder is now ready

222226.excerpt_en: The local council reported on Facebook that a fault occurred in the high-voltage grid at around 5:45 this morning. At 8:30, power had returned to most places.
222226.subtitle_en: Because of a fault in the high-voltage grid, large parts of the town were without power in the early morning hours.

222239.excerpt_en: We meet author Ellinor Rafaelsen at Fruene. Alert eyes and an enthusiasm that could be mistaken for infatuation.
222239.subtitle_en: Her first encounter with Svalbard was a chapter of sorrow. Fortunately, she went on to write new chapters.
222239.title_en: “In the End, I Got Tired of Listening to Myself”

222249.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard had to use a helicopter to carry out a medical evacuation on Monday. “We had to evacuate a man from a ship. He had dislocated his shoulder the day before and had to be picked up today,” says Governor’s officer Taina Maria Bjørkås.
222249.subtitle_en: A man had to be picked up by helicopter from a trawler east of Hopen.

222254.excerpt_en: Saturday’s Polarjazz opened with familiar hits by former deLillos vocalist Lars Lillo Stenberg, followed by acclaimed jazz artist Bugge Wesseltoft with the trio Rymden.
222254.subtitle_en: The final days of Polarjazz 2022 were filled with both familiar music and a completely new lineup of artists.

222280.excerpt_en: Large parts of Longyearbyen were plunged into darkness on Monday morning after a power outage lasting two to three hours. Many also remember the incident in November, when there was a power cut after problems getting diesel into the backup power system.
222280.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council leader Arild Olsen says Monday’s power outage provided new lessons for emergency preparedness.
222280.tags_en: news, power outage, emergency preparedness, local council
222280.title_en: “We Recommend Being Prepared, with Particular Attention to the Cold”

222287.excerpt_en: It was during the night before Sunday, 3 October, that a man was attacked from behind outside Karlsberger Pub in the town centre.
222287.subtitle_en: A man was knocked unconscious in the town centre, and the case is now going to trial.
222287.title_en: Attacked from Behind—Suffered Broken Nose and Concussion

222299.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten’s editorial of 28 January 2022—“World-Class Research, or…”—raises important questions about research infrastructure on Svalbard, Norwegian and international research on Svalbard, and the opportunities Svalbard offers for research into green energy. What constitutes good research?
222299.subtitle_en: “The number of publications from Norwegian polar research almost doubled from 2005 to 2014,” writes the Norwegian Polar Institute.

222315.excerpt_en: Pandemic monitoring was changed in January, which means that figures after 25 January are not comparable with those from before.
222315.subtitle_en: In Longyearbyen too, the infection figures show that cases are no longer being recorded as they were before.
222315.title_en: “We Would Like to Hear from Everyone Who Tests Positive”

222318.excerpt_en: Sofie is in the fourth grade at Longyearbyen School.
222318.subtitle_en: This year’s Sun Festival drawing has been selected, and fourth-grader Sofie Maudal came out on top.
222318.title_en: “I Try to Draw Better When There’s Competition”

222320.excerpt_en: At the same time as downsizing and the closure of coal mining, the Norwegian authorities chose, through the most recent Svalbard White Paper (Report No. 32 2015–2016), to facilitate a significant increase in the volume of tourism on Svalbard, well supported by input from the tourism industry itself (Masterplan Svalbard 2015).
222320.subtitle_en: Tommy Sandal writes about preserving Svalbard’s wilderness.
222320.title_en: Svalbard Is No Longer Wilderness as It Once Was

222335.excerpt_en: The judgment states that the court considers it proven beyond reasonable doubt that the sequence of events is correct. The man in his twenties confessed and explained that he had lost control.
222335.subtitle_en: On Christmas Eve 2020, a man in his sixties was knocked down and suffered long-term injuries. Now the defendant, a man in his twenties, has been convicted.
222335.title_en: Sentenced to Six Months in Prison for Unprovoked Assault

222356.excerpt_en: The matter was raised in the local council on the basis of the action programme, in which improved road safety is one of the objectives.

222356.title_en: “It Makes Sense to Take the Step Towards a Car-Free Centre”

222359.excerpt_en: We in the Norwegian Nature Guide Association—NNGF—hope that the entire tourism industry on Svalbard will join in developing good, clear field-safety regulations instead of working against them.

222359.tags_en: tourism, reader’s letter, guide, Arctic nature guide, opinions
222359.title_en: We Are Creating Svalbard’s Future Nature-Based Tourism

222370.excerpt_en: The police investigation so far indicates that it is doubtful that the break was caused by natural circumstances, NRK reports. Troms Police District and Space Norway used Polarsyssel and an underwater robot to examine the break site, located along a section 130 to 230 kilometres from Longyearbyen.
222370.subtitle_en: Police do not believe the break in the fibre-optic cable to Svalbard was caused by natural circumstances.

222389.excerpt_en: On Monday, 14 February, the two cabinet ministers will place seeds from two gene banks in Germany, Sudan and Slovakia, as well as from the international research centre ICARDA and NordGen, in the Global Seed Vault on Svalbard.
222389.subtitle_en: Minister of Agriculture Sandra Borch and Minister of International Development Anne Beathe Tvinnereim are coming to Svalbard to carry out this year’s first seed deposit at the Global Seed Vault.

222397.excerpt_en: “We had a similar project this summer at Otternes, which was Popup Norway’s first baby. We used the same concept, inviting 11 chefs to prepare their specialities using our local ingredients.”
222397.subtitle_en: Local ingredients, cooperation with the local community and eight different concepts. That is how Popup Svalbard suddenly came into being.
222397.title_en: A Little Piece of Norway Gathered on Svalbard

222402.excerpt_en: For most people, everyday life will become easier, including for people on Svalbard. But requirements for travelling to Svalbard remain in place.
222402.subtitle_en: The government is removing most measures, but is continuing those that apply specifically to Svalbard.
222402.title_en: Most Restrictions Lifted, but Svalbard Measures Remain

222431.excerpt_en: First of all: I have a car, and I use it a lot. I like driving; it is warm and comfortable, with four-wheel drive and good ground clearance.
222431.subtitle_en: A roundabout can quickly spark debate both in the local council and out on the street.
222431.tags_en: traffic, opinions, editorial, cars, road safety

222435.excerpt_en: Head of Culture Are Nundal opened the long-standing sports exchange. But he also had the pleasure of welcoming more than just athletes. “Welcome.”
222435.subtitle_en: Sport at a friendly level is the best way to describe the sports exchange between Longyearbyen and Barentsburg at Svalbardhallen on Saturday. See the photos.

223603.excerpt_en: “We cannot close Barentsburg to visitors. We are a free settlement in a free country where everyone can visit us.”
223603.subtitle_en: The conflict in Ukraine has led to local sanctions against Barentsburg. Life has become more difficult for most people. Nevertheless, Consul General Sergey Gushchin welcomes everyone to the town in the west.

223632.excerpt_en: Since 1998—the same year Lasse moved north—Polarjazz has warmed audiences in Longyearbyen. Lasse has led it since 2005. “It’s because I’m committed and want to do things that make a difference to people.”
223632.subtitle_en: Klovner i Kamp paid tribute from the stage last Thursday to Mr Polarjazz, Lasse S. Hansen. He has run the festival since 2005. Now it is over.

223645.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten reported at the beginning of March that someone had placed an extra iron bed beside the landmark, turning two beds into three. The third bed has now been removed again.
223645.subtitle_en: There are at least two different stories about the origins of the Iron Bed.
223645.title_en: A new version of the mystery of the Iron Bed

223652.excerpt_en: From 13 to 15 May, Svalbard Turn plans to stage a major swimming meet for the first time since 2004.
223652.subtitle_en: For the first time in many years, Svalbard Turn will stage a major swimming meet. But to make it happen, they are seeking help from local residents.
223652.title_en: Taking place for the first time in 19 years

223654.excerpt_en: Galleri Svalbard’s new premises are on the second floor of the Coop building, with an area of nearly 1,000 square metres. Last autumn, LL worked to renew the brand and wanted to tailor an operating model that would give the gallery stable income and strengthen Longyearbyen’s reputation.
223654.subtitle_en: A great deal of money has been spent preparing new premises for Galleri Svalbard. Now the gallery’s director is to be appointed.
223654.title_en: “We had hoped for and wanted a broader pool of applicants”

223667.excerpt_en: The Governor has dealt with several incidents over the past 24 hours, says Senior Police Officer Ragnar Schjølset. “We received a report of vandalism involving a snowmobile. For now, we will not say anything more because the case is under investigation.”
223667.subtitle_en: The Governor had to set out to pick up a snowmobile group.
223667.tags_en: rescue operation, the Governor, helicopter, news

223679.excerpt_en: As many people know, the historic Huset was sold by Spitsbergen Eiendom to Store Norske in February. Hurtigruten Svalbard took over its operations from Svalbard Adventures.
223679.subtitle_en: Huset is currently closed and will not reopen until May, if everything goes according to plan.
223679.title_en: Hopes to open Huset in May – kitchen to be renovated

223693.excerpt_en: If someone becomes acutely ill in Svalbard, help may take time to arrive. Figures from 2020 to the present show that in some cases it has taken as long as eight hours from notification to the medical coordination center for air ambulances until the final crew carrying out the mission was alerted.
223693.subtitle_en: It takes an average of eight hours for an air ambulance to reach an emergency patient in Longyearbyen, statistics from the past two years show. One response took more than 16 hours.
223693.tags_en: Longyearbyen Hospital, news, air ambulance, emergency preparedness
223693.title_en: If you become acutely ill, it takes an average of eight hours to get help

223703.excerpt_en: At the beginning of January, damage was discovered to one of the two internet connections to Svalbard. A case was opened by Troms Police District, and the investigation has now been completed.
223703.subtitle_en: A lack of evidence means the case concerning damage to one of the fiber-optic cables to Svalbard has been dropped.
223703.title_en: “Questioned the skipper of a Russian trawler”

223707.excerpt_en: In the spring semester of 2021, UNIS introduced strict measures and rules for students because of the pandemic. The student representative at the time, Elizabeth Jean McMaster, spoke with many worried and lonely students. “There is definitely a need for a mental-health expert in town, especially during COVID,” she says.
223707.subtitle_en: During COVID, several students experienced strict rules and loneliness. A former student representative is dissatisfied with the psychological services available in Longyearbyen.

223731.excerpt_en: Engagement ranges from torchlight processions, private sanctions and financial support for international aid organizations to information efforts aimed at Russian citizens with limited access to media coverage of the war in Ukraine. The debate over how best to conduct ourselves is heated both on social media and in Svalbardposten.
223731.subtitle_en: There is considerable engagement over the war between Russia and Ukraine and our relationship with our neighbors.

223735.excerpt_en: The Ukraine conflict is one that has built up slowly but surely since the fall of the Berlin Wall. The EU, USA, NATO and Russia are countries and organizations that have been deeply involved, and we are seeing the symptoms now.
223735.subtitle_en: Seen in today’s light, we are living in 2022—a year in which no one thought we could once again have a war right on our doorstep, or rather, in Europe.

223760.excerpt_en: The war in Ukraine is still raging and is something most people follow closely, including tourists traveling to Svalbard. Some time ago, the Svalbard Tourism Council issued a highly controversial request to stop buying goods and services from Russian companies in Svalbard.
223760.subtitle_en: Despite the tense situation in Europe, many tourists still want to travel to the Russian settlements.
223760.title_en: “We’re taking our lunch out into nature”

223764.subtitle_en: It was only fitting that Per Kyrre Reymert should also be honored in Svalbard. After all, this is where his heart is.

224211.excerpt_en: The Customs Act does not currently apply to Svalbard, and the Norwegian Customs Administration therefore does not inspect goods brought into or taken out of Svalbard. 224655.excerpt_en: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries recently advertised six of the 19 cabin plots in Todalen, Foxdalen and Vindodden. Longyearbyen Local Council now wants two of the plots in Todalen, to establish sites that the nurseries can use.
224655.subtitle_en: The local council wants two cabin plots that parents of children in the nurseries can use.
224655.title_en: Wants Two Cabin Plots for Parents of Young Children

224660.excerpt_en: On Thursday afternoon, several residents and prominent figures in Longyearbyen gathered at Svalbard Museum to spend the evening with the Crown Prince and Crown Princess. Åse Jensen performed a poem, while Mia Ekeblad Eggenfellner, Sigri Klausen Markussen and Niva Stiberg Hansen provided the musical entertainment.
224660.subtitle_en: On Thursday afternoon, the Crown Prince and Crown Princess gave a speech about their relationship with Svalbard.

224670.excerpt_en: “It’s absolutely fantastic here today, with perfect weather and sunshine,” says race director Heidi Harviken, wearing perhaps the biggest smile to be seen in Todalen.

224670.title_en: “We Couldn’t Have Asked for Anything Better”

224691.excerpt_en: For nearly six months, Lance drifted with the ice north of Svalbard, from anchoring beside an ice floe at 83° north in January until she docked in Longyearbyen in early summer.
224691.subtitle_en: In the winter of 2015, the research vessel Lance froze into the pack ice north of Svalbard. For months, the ship drifted with the ice while researchers and technicians worked flat out with one goal in mind: to study the effects of climate change in the Arctic Ocean.
224691.tags_en: magazine, Norwegian Polar Institute, news, Lance, research
224691.title_en: When the Research Ship Lance Froze into the Pack Ice

224712.excerpt_en: “Everything was really very random. I was going to Denmark to study graphic design, but I thought I needed a backup plan.”
224712.subtitle_en: Andrea Aasbø Diedrichson, 19, was originally going to Denmark to study, but instead she went in the exact opposite direction.
224712.tags_en: people, news, Svalbard Folk High School
224712.title_en: “The Best Thing I Could Have Done”

224722.excerpt_en: The background to the case is the discovery of fluorinated toxic substances called PFAS and PFOS in the area. They originate from the former fire-training site by the road to the airport. The hazardous fluorinated substances were previously used in firefighting foam until the training site was closed in 2000.

224722.title_en: Toxic Substances Are Not Being Removed—the Plan Is Delayed

224734.excerpt_en: I strongly recommended to you that the arts centre should remain together, including both studios and any artists’ flats, since these three units naturally belong together and complement one another.
224734.subtitle_en: On Svalbardposten.no, I read on March 20, 2022, that no one knows when the gallery will reopen. You should have had an answer to this instead of closing it down before you had somewhere new to move it.

224749.excerpt_en: According to the Governor of Svalbard, the incident took place on April 9.
224749.subtitle_en: During Easter, a snowmobile convoy allegedly drove on the sea ice in Petuniabukta. They have now been reported for illegally travelling on sea ice.
224749.tags_en: news, law violations, Governor of Svalbard, Motor Traffic Regulations

224764.excerpt_en: The survey figures show that 88 percent believe tourism contributes to good services in Longyearbyen, while 74 percent of respondents were negative towards conventional cruise ships. “I understand that people react both out of concern for the environment and because of tourism’s general impact on the town.”
224764.subtitle_en: A survey showed that Longyearbyen residents are negative towards cruise tourism. Local council leader Arild Olsen says they are working on improvements.
224764.tags_en: tourism, news, Longyearbyen Local Council, cruise ships, Visit Svalbard
224764.title_en: “We Have a Duty to Receive Ships and Cannot Refuse Them Port Calls”

230704.excerpt_en: “It was first tested in eastern Norway, but then we wanted to give it a proper trial and sent it to Tromsø over Saltfjellet. The biggest test, however, had to be testing it on Svalbard.”
230704.subtitle_en: With its latest addition to the vehicle fleet, Posten on Svalbard will use electricity exclusively as fuel. The company believes this should inspire others to do the same.
230704.title_en: “There Is No Excuse Not to Do It”

230722.excerpt_en: The agenda includes a case headed “Transfer of Longyearbyen Local Council’s Homes to Statsbygg.” However, the case is exempt from public disclosure, so few details are available for now.

230722.tags_en: Longyearbyen Local Council, homes, Statsbygg, news
230722.title_en: Statsbygg to Buy 177 Homes from the Local Council

230738.excerpt_en: Commissioned by Store Norske Boliger, Statsbygg and Longyearbyen Local Council, Sweco has carried out several condition assessments of public and state-owned homes in Longyearbyen. The work is scheduled to continue until August 2022 and is intended to map the condition of the homes and their rehabilitation needs.
230738.subtitle_en: A survey of a home at Vei 216 uncovered major defects in the building’s foundations. The residents therefore had to move out with immediate effect.
230738.title_en: “We Don’t Want to Take Any Chances”

230754.excerpt_en: The revue was originally scheduled to take place on March 4, as the opening event of this year’s Solfest Week.
230754.subtitle_en: They were originally meant to mark the start of this year’s Solfest Week, but had to postpone because of illness. This weekend, however, audiences will get to see the revue “Written in Coal.”
230754.title_en: “We Have Some Elements That Will Surprise You”

230772.excerpt_en: One question is whether the new regulatory proposals from the Norwegian Environment Agency will hamper tourism’s contribution to beach clean-ups on Svalbard. If adopted, the proposal could mark a decisive turning point in efforts to combat plastic pollution on Svalbard.
230772.subtitle_en: For nearly two decades, expedition tourists have taken part in beach clean-ups on Svalbard. After two years of the pandemic, a new and long-awaited season is about to begin, with expedition leaders and guests ready to continue the fight against marine litter on Svalbard.
230772.tags_en: opinions, reader’s letter, expedition cruises, cruise tourism, travel industry
230772.title_en: Expedition Tourists Clean Up Svalbard’s Beaches

230781.excerpt_en: “Jason Roberts alerted us to the discovery of the polar bears. We were there ourselves on 1.”
230781.subtitle_en: Polar-bear researcher Jon Aars of the Norwegian Polar Institute believes the female and cub found in Mohnbukta in March were unlucky and were caught in an avalanche after heavy rainfall.

230783.excerpt_en: And Sam Dwinnell knows more about that. She is conducting her PhD research on Svalbard, focusing on reindeer and climate change. “I am trying to find out how reindeer respond to climate change, both in their behaviour and their physical condition.”
230783.subtitle_en: Are you among those who feel sorry for reindeer scraping for food when the ground is covered in ice and snow? If so, there is something you need to learn. Svalbard reindeer are among the fattest ungulates in existence.
230783.title_en: “They Are the Fattest Ungulates I Have Seen”

230797.excerpt_en: This weekend, Jason Roberts and PolarX will screen the film “Polar Bear” at Longyearbyen Kulturhus. Produced on behalf of DisneyNature, the film is, according to Roberts, the result of a dream more than ten years in the making. “We have wanted to make a full-scale feature film about polar bears for a long time.”
230797.subtitle_en: After ten years of planning, filming and post-production, PolarX’s film “Polar Bear” is finally ready to be shown. Now they want feedback from local residents.
230797.tags_en: news, documentary film, PolarX, polar bear

230810.excerpt_en: “The idea is that we provide the dogs and coffee, and people can come and cuddle them,” says Iris Dahle Bjørkmann, one of five owners who have joined forces to open a café offering Longyearbyen residents something completely new.
230810.subtitle_en: Huskies Café/Shop opened its doors on Friday. From now on, coffee, cakes and canine cuddles will be served at Elvesletta north.

230815.excerpt_en: May 1 is Workers’ Day, and for Svein Jonny Albrigtsen, leader of Svalbard’s Labour Party and LO Svalbard, the day is probably especially important.
230815.subtitle_en: Safety inspector Svein Jonny Albrigtsen has not given up hope of avoiding the closure of Mine 7. He believes the disappearance of the mine would affect the Longyearbyen community.

230840.tags_en: opinions, reader’s letter, air passengers, SAS
230840.title_en: Dear SAS, You Are NOT Serious!

230881.excerpt_en: “There was a russe celebration in the square last night,” says Senior Police Officer to the Governor Ragnar Schjølset. Schjølset says the russ are believed to have played loud music and partied in the area.

230895.excerpt_en: This weekend, it was finally time to head to Huset and exercise our laughter muscles. After a two-year coronavirus hiatus, Spitsbergen Revylag returned with the revue “Written in Coal Script.”

266339.excerpt_en: The front line is called the Polar Front, the area where cold water masses from the north meet the (relatively) warmer waters from the south. The invading forces from the south include cod, haddock, mackerel, blue mussels and snow crab, while the defending forces in the north include polar cod, shrimp and Calanus glacialis.
266339.subtitle_en: Far north in the Barents Sea, a tough and merciless battle is being fought between invading forces from the south and defending forces in the north.

Now Sigmund Andersen, head of the Arctic nature guide programme, believes such requirements must be introduced. “The guide has an important role, and tourists pay a high price to go on excursions.”
266450.subtitle_en: “Guests should know what they are getting,” says Sigmund Andersen, head of the nature guide programme.

266479.excerpt_en: In January, 18 people applied for the position of department manager. None was hired. “We had a candidate who could have been a good successor in the leadership role.”

266497.subtitle_en: In 2017, Rabalder exceeded NOK 4 million in turnover for the first time. Cultural affairs director Roger Zahl Ødegård is delighted.

266593.excerpt_en: Tourism in Svalbard has grown in recent years, in line with the ambitions of the government, local authorities and the member companies of the Tourism Council. When the crisis at Store Norske struck in 2014, the industry was tasked with doubling the number of tourism jobs in Longyearbyen—from 300 at the time to 600 by 2025.

266602.excerpt_en: In the previous issue, Svalbardposten wrote that politicians had decided to retain the youth club UHU because of the great uncertainty surrounding the need for nursery places. 266602.subtitle_en: Full nurseries are making parental leave complicated for Øyvind Kolbu.
