266627.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Maritime Authority is fining Unis for this trip with eight students in temperatures of minus 20 degrees.

308429.title_en: The Biggest Gift Weighs Nine Tonnes

308548.excerpt_en: This week’s historical photo was given to Svalbardposten by Roald Westerbotten. He titled the image “Christmas Celebration at the New Church,” and it was taken in 1958.

308562.excerpt_en: “The boat leaves at 6 p.m. Anyone who wishes can come to Bykaia to say goodbye,” says senior police officer Arve Johnsen, the Governor of Svalbard’s office.
308562.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s vessel Polarsyssel is heading for Tromsø on Monday evening.
308562.title_en: Setting Sail After the Season Ends

308574.excerpt_en: “We will present the results of the avalanche hazard assessment that has now been carried out. It provides an updated assessment of the avalanche risk for different types of avalanches in built-up areas of Longyearbyen,” says acting regional director of NVE Region North, Knut Hoseth.
308574.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) has completed its avalanche hazard assessment for Longyearbyen. On Thursday, it will present the report at a public meeting at UNIS.

308609.excerpt_en: An unusually large crowd had turned up to receive the SAS flight at Svalbard Airport today. Many parents wanted to see the rather unusual Lucia procession organized by the first-graders at Longyearbyen School.
308609.subtitle_en: All the new arrivals were charmed by the first-graders who walked in a Lucia procession when the plane arrived at Svalbard Airport.
308609.tags_en: news, Lucia, Longyearbyen School, Svalbard Airport
308609.title_en: Delighted by Lucia Procession at the Airport

308675.excerpt_en: The researcher was part of a group of Russian researchers camping at Selvågen on Prins Karls Forland. The bear was shot as it approached the camp late on Tuesday evening, the 9th.
308675.subtitle_en: The Russian researcher who shot and killed a polar bear on Prins Karls Forland in August has been issued a NOK 15,000 fine by the Director of Public Prosecutions for Troms and Finnmark.

308679.excerpt_en: The avalanche assessment shows that the upper settlements in Lia and Nybyen face a one-percent annual probability of being hit by an avalanche. The same applies to one of the Power Station’s buildings and the elevated reservoir for the town’s water supply, both located in Gruvedalen.
308679.subtitle_en: Large parts of Longyeardalen are marked red, orange and yellow on the NVE’s new avalanche map. Avalanches there could claim lives and damage buildings.

308694.excerpt_en: At a public meeting at UNIS on Thursday evening, Local Council Chair Arild Olsen (Labour) received the Longyearbyen avalanche report from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE). The report shows which areas of the town are exposed to avalanches.
308694.subtitle_en: The political goal is to move the population out of a situation in which they risk being evacuated because of avalanche danger. But this may take a long time.
308694.title_en: Evacuations Will Become Part of Life

308713.excerpt_en: And without this unique research village, we would not know that sunscreens used by people in Longyearbyen contain pollutants that are now set to be banned. Kings Bay AS, the company that facilitates international climate research in Ny-Ålesund, is celebrating its centenary these days.
308713.subtitle_en: Without the Cold War, today’s Ny-Ålesund would probably not exist.
308713.title_en: Research Village Ny-Ålesund Celebrates an Anniversary

308739.excerpt_en: “It is good to be able to mark the day. My thoughts go first and foremost to those who were hardest hit and everyone who was affected,” says local council leader Arild Olsen.
308739.subtitle_en: Today marks one year since the major avalanche struck Lia. It will be commemorated in a simple and dignified manner.
308739.title_en: Marks One Year with Simple Ceremony and Torchlight Procession

308761.excerpt_en: After the memorial ceremony, anyone who wishes can go up to the church. Parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen will welcome people for a gathering.
308761.subtitle_en: Anniversaries can stir up many memories and strong emotions. Svalbard Church will remain open into the evening.

308776.excerpt_en: A major and extensive task now lies ahead for Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) to secure the areas identified as hazardous. The report from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) will be an important tool in determining how the town will be developed in the future.
308776.subtitle_en: The wider community must now step up and ensure public safety and security for the town’s population.
308776.title_en: Securing the Area Will Take Time and Money

308794.excerpt_en: “If we were North Korea or Cuba, this would be acceptable practice. But given the world we live in, it is not acceptable for politicians to appoint people to the board of a newspaper.”
308794.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council will no longer appoint board members to Svalbardposten AS.
308794.title_en: LL Will No Longer Appoint Board Members

308816.excerpt_en: Svalbard Airport’s two electric cars are not the first on the island. Pole Position has driven its electric car for two summer seasons; it is exactly the same type as the newly purchased vehicles.
308816.subtitle_en: Pole Position AS has had an electric car for two seasons.
308816.tags_en: Pole Position, Svalbard Airport, electric car, news
308816.title_en: “An Electric Car Is Ideal for Use in Longyearbyen”

308826.excerpt_en: “The fact that electric cars are now being put to use in business, including in Svalbard, is excellent,” says Rotevatn as he takes Pole Position’s Nissan Evalia NV200 for a test drive with the journalist.
308826.subtitle_en: An electric-car trip with MDG frontman Espen Klungseth Rotevatn turned out to be just an ordinary drive.

308839.excerpt_en: “Through the Svalbard white paper, the state has said that tourism in Area 10 is to be prioritised. Temporary installations are part of this initiative.”
308839.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has approved five of six applications to place temporary installations in the field during the winter season.

308866.excerpt_en: This week’s historical photo comes from the collection of Kjell Onarheim, who came to Svalbard in 1963. His son, Stig Onarheim, has loaned the photographs to Svalbardposten.
308866.tags_en: historical photo, life in Svalbard, history

308880.excerpt_en: “The bear was shot with the intention of scaring it away, according to the information the police have received,” says senior police officer Bjørn Georg Pedersen, the Governor of Svalbard’s office. Statements, traces at the scene and police investigations show that the two-year-old female was hit by a ricochet.
308880.subtitle_en: The polar bear shot on Forlandet in August was injured by a ricochet, took to the water and drowned. The Russian researcher who fired the shot must pay a NOK 15,000 fine. Updated article.

308893.excerpt_en: On 8 January, the mail plane operated by West Atlantic Sweden crashed while travelling from Oslo to Longyearbyen via Tromsø.
308893.subtitle_en: The Swedish Accident Investigation Authority’s report concludes that the mail plane received an incorrect display from its artificial horizon before it crashed.

308912.excerpt_en: Just before the commemoration began, the wind and blowing snow died down. Around 400 people gathered for the event at the Cultural Centre.
308912.subtitle_en: A heartfelt and powerful commemoration moved those who took part in the torchlight procession up to Lia, where the avalanche struck on December 19 last year.

308942.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen will never be quite the same. The catastrophic avalanche that destroyed eleven houses on the 19th.
308942.subtitle_en: Take care of our solidarity, be there for one another, see one another and give each other hugs, just as we did last year.

308952.excerpt_en: A small group ended up at Atle Husby’s, 42, after a night at the pub. By Saturday morning, Atle was alone in the house.
308952.subtitle_en: Parish priest Leif Magne Helgesen lost one of his close friends in the avalanche. He allowed himself to grieve alongside the entire Longyearbyen community.
308952.title_en: Priest and Friend at the Heart of the Disaster

308991.excerpt_en: “He was insanely funny. He used to put his glasses on the wrong way round, upside down.”
308991.subtitle_en: It has been a year since Bendik, 13, Mali, 11, and Rasmus, nine, lost their father, Atle Husby, 42. When they talk about him, there are both tears and laughter.

309012.excerpt_en: “A magical place,” said board chair Unni Steinsmo, and none of the guests disagreed. Few centenarians have experienced as much excitement or played roles as important as Kings Bay AS.
309012.subtitle_en: Little Sigri Oline, four months old, and Kåre Willoch, 88 years her senior, had a wonderful time at the Kings Bay party, along with just over a hundred other friends of Ny-Ålesund.
309012.title_en: Big Celebration for a Vibrant Centenarian

309026.excerpt_en: Inside, it is warm and welcoming, and the nine people who live on Bear Island offer a warm welcome. Their main task is to make weather observations.
309026.subtitle_en: Station manager Ragnar Sønstebø welcomes the Christmas visitors from Longyearbyen outside the helicopter. The Christmas tree stands on the steps and the star shines in the window.
309026.title_en: Nearly Ready for Christmas on Bear Island

309079.excerpt_en: Elke Morgner sleeps late with her daughter Svala, eight weeks old, that morning. Her eldest daughter, Elida, two, has got up early with her father, Malte Jochmann.
309079.subtitle_en: The storm leaves Longyearbyen white and silent on the morning of December 19. Soon, ten people will be buried in snow. Eight survive.
309079.tags_en: rescue work, natural disaster, avalanche, survival, Svalbard, news

309157.excerpt_en: My interest in the Arctic began early. When my father read stories to us children, he usually chose Nansen and Johansen’s wintering in the stone hut on Franz Josef Land rather than Bambi and the Seven Dwarfs.
309157.subtitle_en: Per Johnson was a dog driver on an expedition with Torstein Raaby, who was the radio operator on the Kon-Tiki voyage. There, he heard stories that had never been told before.

309172.excerpt_en: “We are pleased that the report from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate is now available. It is an important report that will provide a vital basis for further work, both locally and on the authorities’ side, to further develop Longyearbyen,” says Gjermund Hagesæter (Progress Party) of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security.
309172.subtitle_en: The government will work to ensure that people feel safe living in Longyearbyen.
309172.title_en: Important Avalanche Report, Including for the Government

309180.excerpt_en: Sixty children of different ages took part in a short but good performance by Svalnardo Circus this week. Rehearsals began on Monday, and in the end they put on a show with a clear storyline.
309180.subtitle_en: Mining was the recurring theme in this year’s performance by Svalnardo Circus.

309194.excerpt_en: In 1964, I took part in Bjørn Staib’s North Pole expedition, which ended in failure. We got a little farther north than Nansen, but there was hardly much to boast about.
309194.subtitle_en: In 1964, I took part in Bjørn Staib’s North Pole expedition, which ended in failure. Some of us wanted to make another attempt.
309194.title_en: The Dream of the North Pole

309240.excerpt_en: In the Christmas issue, we feature a photograph from Stig Onarheim’s collection. It was taken in 1965 and is titled “Departure.”
309240.subtitle_en: A classic 1960s snowmobile as a means of transport.
309240.tags_en: historical photo, life in Svalbard, history

309288.excerpt_en: The monument at Huset tells the story in condensed form: “Director Einar Sverdrup. For his efforts in Svalbard, 1922–1942.”
309288.subtitle_en: Coal mining in Longyearbyen between the wars was an achievement that shines in Norwegian industrial history. The drama that unfolded in the town during the war is unparalleled in military history. The central figure in both mining and the war was Einar Sverdrup, “The King of Spitsbergen.”

309316.excerpt_en: Harstad native Per-Willy Amundsen of the Progress Party took over as Minister of Justice and Public Security on Tuesday, succeeding fellow party member Anders Anundsen. Anundsen had served as a cabinet minister since October 2013.
309316.subtitle_en: The new “Svalbard minister” is Per-Willy Amundsen.
309316.tags_en: Polar Committee, Polar Department, Per-Willy Amundsen, news, Anders Anundsen, Svalbard minister

309349.excerpt_en: “Everyone in Longyearbyen knows Jørn, and when I read about his fight against cancer in VG, I thought about what I could do. So I set up a private Facebook group and invited my Svalbard acquaintances to join,” says Sidsel Mellerud Svarstad, the initiator of the fundraiser for Jørn Dybdahl and a former chief inspector with the Governor of Svalbard.
309349.subtitle_en: Jørn Dybdahl has spent his savings on cancer medication not covered by the public health service. Now the Svalbard community has rallied to provide financial help.
309349.title_en: More Than Half a Million Raised for Jørn’s Fight

309359.excerpt_en: Reports indicate a peaceful Christmas celebration in Svalbard. While much of mainland Norway has been badly hit by severe weather, snow has fallen gently over Longyearbyen without a single incident.
309359.subtitle_en: Celebrated Christmas in an old hunting cabin.

309371.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Meteorological Institute reports an increase to a southeasterly full storm in Longyearbyen from Wednesday afternoon. Storm expected on #Svalbard late Wednesday, see https://t.co/zTwZMe7i5U – NVE has warned of considerable avalanche danger – see https://t.co/GihnK8ygCy pic.twitter.com/b0CQi0udX2—The Meteorologists (@Meteorologene) 27.
309371.subtitle_en: On Wednesday afternoon, meteorologists warned of severe weather reminiscent of last December’s storm.

309383.excerpt_en: “There are no major changes from yesterday’s forecast. We note that the warning for Spitsbergen has been upgraded from full to severe storm in exposed areas.”
309383.subtitle_en: The Northern Norway Weather Forecasting Service is maintaining the storm warning for Spitsbergen. The wind is picking up.

309401.excerpt_en: “Both decisions were made on the basis of avalanche assessments by NVE. We are monitoring weather developments closely and remain in continuous contact with NVE,” Governor Kjerstin Askholt states on the Governor’s Office website.
309401.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has decided to evacuate Nybyen, while people in Lia may remain in their homes. Following a meeting of the emergency preparedness council at 5 p.m., the situation is unchanged.

309418.excerpt_en: “We are facing a weather situation similar to last December. A lot of wind from the east, a full storm, and then some snow.”
309418.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate has checked the snow above Lia and Nybyen and advised the Governor of Svalbard to evacuate Nybyen in case more snow arrives than forecast.
309418.title_en: Wants to err on the side of caution

309428.excerpt_en: Indians Aayush Anchal (27) and Vaibhav Sharma (30) meet Svalbardposten as they leave one of the huts at Coal Miners’ Cabins in Nybyen with their luggage. They have been told to pack their belongings and report to reception as quickly as they can.
309428.subtitle_en: “We are disappointed to be evacuated and not get to experience what we had planned,” says Aayush Anchal (27) from India.
309428.title_en: Disappointed, but understand why they have to evacuate

309442.excerpt_en: “We have raised the level of preparedness among the police, Longyearbyen Local Council and the fire service. At 11 p.m., a new weather forecast will be issued, which NVE will relay to the police duty officer.”
309442.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard and local avalanche experts will assess conditions in Longyearbyen during the night.

309475.excerpt_en: “The evacuation in Nybyen remains in effect until further notice. NVE wants to examine the mountainsides there more closely before making a new assessment.”
309475.subtitle_en: On Thursday morning, the Governor of Svalbard decided that Nybyen would remain evacuated. There is no need to evacuate people from Lia.

309490.excerpt_en: “We reached a full storm here at the airport, and at Platåberget there were hurricane-force winds in the mean wind,” says meteorological assistant Torgeir Mørk at Svalbard Airport. He says the strongest mean wind recorded was 33 metres per second at Platåberget, with gusts of 40 metres per second.
309490.subtitle_en: There was plenty of weather in Longyearbyen overnight Wednesday. Meteorological consultant Torgeir Mørk at Svalbard Airport has the storm under full control.

309506.excerpt_en: Today, snow conditions were examined beneath Sukkertoppen and above Nybyen. “On the basis of these examinations, NVE believes avalanches cannot reach the buildings, including those in Nybyen,” says communications adviser Terje Carlsen at the Governor’s Office.
309506.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is now allowing tourists and residents to move back to Nybyen.

309536.excerpt_en: “A caller in Adventdalen reported seeing a white flare in the direction of Trollsteinen,” says senior police officer with the Governor of Svalbard Trond Olsen.
309536.subtitle_en: A signal flare fired from the area around Trollsteinen prompted the Governor of Svalbard to fly up by helicopter on Wednesday morning. They were unable to determine where it came from.

309561.excerpt_en: January: Many questions remain unanswered after the avalanche disaster on December 19, 2015.
309561.subtitle_en: All of 2016 was marked by the tragic avalanche. We discussed responsibility, vulnerability and how we are to live with avalanche danger. At the same time, the population of the world’s northernmost urban community continued to grow.

309636.excerpt_en: Poor flying conditions, with wind and extremely limited visibility on Thursday, meant that the plane carrying Svalbardposten’s print edition could not land. This means the newspaper will be delayed in reaching subscribers and outlets on Friday.
309636.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten’s first print edition of 2017 will be delayed.

309693.excerpt_en: The archipelago’s two major museums have completely different views on who arrived here first. In Barentsburg, the story is told of Pomors hunting and trapping on Svalbard around 1550.
309693.subtitle_en: “The history must be rewritten. Norway and Russia should have the same history book when it comes to Svalbard,” says archaeologist Victor Derzhavin.
309693.title_en: Still divided over who arrived first

309729.excerpt_en: I agree with tourism director Ronny Brunvoll (SP, November 18, 2016) that the guides I have met in Longyearbyen over several years are cheerful, helpful, welcoming and eloquent. Some are even very charming.
309729.subtitle_en: Letter to the editor: “Like a skilled journalist, [a guide] should know at least ten times more than he or she would normally have any use for. Only then should the tourism director and the rest of Visit Svalbard be satisfied.”
309729.title_en: Guides without a sense of history

309750.excerpt_en: Next Tuesday, Svalbard Seminar 2017 begins, a series of lectures open to everyone in Longyearbyen. This year, the programme includes a new section. “It will be an artistic evening, combining Kunsthall Svalbard with the Northern Norwegian Opera and Symphony Orchestra,” says Inger Lise Næss of UNIS, one of the organisers.
309750.subtitle_en: This year’s Svalbard Seminar combines historical mysteries, new research and a dedicated arts section that is new this year.
309750.title_en: Offering mysteries and the sound of the Arctic

309766.excerpt_en: “I think about NOK 630,000 has come in. Now I expect things to level off a little,” says Jørn Dybdahl by phone from a hospital in Oslo.
309766.subtitle_en: Jørn Dybdahl, 55, believes he has received enough help to get by until the medicine he needs is approved by the Norwegian Medicines Agency.

309787.excerpt_en: Just before Christmas, the Ministry of Climate and Environment adopted the new regulations governing motor traffic in Svalbard. They allow visitors travelling with permanent residents or taking part in organised tours to drive snowmobiles across glaciers in an area between Longyearbyen and Pyramiden.
309787.subtitle_en: Updated regulations allow tourists to drive across glaciers to Pyramiden, while the Governor of Svalbard can close fjords to protect wildlife.
309787.title_en: Glaciers open—the ice may be closed

309804.excerpt_en: Last week, 35 guests had to be evacuated from Guesthouse 102 in Nybyen, along with five people from a private apartment. A storm had been forecast, and there was a risk that avalanches could threaten the building.
309804.subtitle_en: Evacuating guests from Nybyen Guesthouse comes at a cost. Arne Kristoffersen of Guesthouse 102 believes Nybyen should instead be permanently secured.

309812.excerpt_en: “I would say the same about Nybyen as I would about Lia. It is a political goal to move beyond the evacuation situation.”
309812.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council has asked the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate to propose safety measures, but it will probably take many years before the evacuation procedure can be replaced by something else.
309812.title_en: Examining safeguards in Nybyen and Lia

309820.excerpt_en: Isbjørnar is set to become a regular companion in Svalbardposten in the period ahead. The simple polar bear with the sharp punchlines comes from Haakon Sandvik’s pen, and was created by chance in his shop last spring. “It was 1.”
309820.subtitle_en: Much of Longyearbyen’s development is driven by tourists’ wishes. The drawings by Haakon Sandvik, 35, are no exception.

309830.excerpt_en: Even before avalanche danger became an issue, the student welfare organisation had thought it would be more practical to house students closer to UNIS. “When avalanche danger is identified, the issue becomes more pressing and we have to address it more quickly,” says Ellen Appelbom, campus manager for the student welfare organisation in Tromsø and Longyearbyen.
309830.subtitle_en: The Arctic Student Welfare Organisation of Norway is in dialogue with Longyearbyen Local Council about moving the student housing from Nybyen.

309848.excerpt_en: In the report “This Is Svalbard 2016”, published this week, Statistics Norway (SSB) writes that 1,650 person-years were worked in Longyearbyen, Ny-Ålesund and Svea in 2015. That is almost twice as many as in 1993, when the figure was 750.
309848.subtitle_en: Statistics Norway confirms the trends in Svalbard society.

309858.excerpt_en: From Wednesday afternoon, December 28, a full to severe storm was forecast for Spitsbergen.
309858.subtitle_en: One year after the storm that claimed two lives in Lia, a similar storm was forecast. This time, the avalanche warning system was in place and Nybyen was evacuated.

309875.excerpt_en: This week’s historic picture comes from Stig Onarheim’s collection and was taken in 1985. It shows the area in Lia with the relatively newly built pointed-roof houses.
309875.subtitle_en: The picture was taken in the spring of 1985.
309875.tags_en: historic picture, life in Svalbard, history

309886.excerpt_en: So far, 2017 has not got off to a very good start for Svalbardposten’s print edition. Because of poor flying weather on Thursday, the newspaper was delayed in reaching Svalbard.
309886.subtitle_en: Some copies of Svalbardposten’s print edition have blank pages, while content is missing from others.
309886.title_en: Printing error in the paper edition

309897.excerpt_en: “We responded after a resident reported reckless snowmobile riding. Four teenagers were out on their snowmobiles,” says the police.
309897.subtitle_en: Shortly before 11 p.m. on Friday, police received a report of reckless snowmobile riding on Hilmar Rekstens vei.

309917.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, the Governor of Svalbard flew to Diabas to pick up two people staying in a cabin without firewood to keep warm. They were part of a party of four who had set out on two snowmobiles a couple of days earlier.
309917.subtitle_en: The party of four that travelled to Diabas on Monday ran into problems with snowmobiles and a shortage of firewood.

309958.excerpt_en: “The only reason I’m still here is that I’ve received mixed signals from the authorities all year,” sighs German national Philipp Bergau. He has applied to establish a kennel in Bolterdalen, but the sequencing provisions in the old land-use plan have effectively stopped his plans.
309958.subtitle_en: Showing up with dogs first and then trying to establish a kennel is difficult. Philipp Bergau, 31, has learned that the hard way.
309958.title_en: German man not allowed to pull a Spanish one

309973.excerpt_en: “A doctor friend of mine in Sweden knows Yussuf Jabir, who started a school in his home in Tanzania several years ago. The project grew and has received support from around the world, mainly from medical communities,” says Strøm.
309973.subtitle_en: A school in Zanzibar, Tanzania, will inherit eleven computers from Longyearbyen School. Last week, Hilde Fålun Strøm packed them for shipment.

309986.excerpt_en: This week’s historical picture comes from Stig Onarheim’s collection and shows a well-known event in Longyearbyen’s history. Sverdrupbyen was established before the Second World War and escaped destruction when the Germans attacked in 1943.
309986.subtitle_en: Sverdrupbyen was burned down in 1985 and 1986.

309996.excerpt_en: Next week’s meeting of the Education and Culture Committee will consider the 2016 cork-fund allocations. The administration has proposed distributing just over NOK 2.7 million from the NOK 2.9 million fund.
309996.subtitle_en: The English-language free newspaper Icepeople has increased its readership. That is reflected in the proposed distribution of cork funds for 2016.

310021.excerpt_en: Today, Longyearbyen has only one grocery store: Coop Svalbard’s Svalbardbutikken.
310021.subtitle_en: The grocery chain wants to open a store in Longyearbyen and is asking to build on the car park in front of Svalbardbutikken.
310021.title_en: Rema 1000 wants to build new store

310038.excerpt_en: “Although we are positive in principle, we are not prepared to let ourselves be held hostage to someone else’s terms. We need the matter to be discussed politically.”
310038.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen politicians want competition in groceries, but are not wholly positive about building on the car park.
310038.title_en: Yes to food, maybe to parking

310051.excerpt_en: The Svalbard Tourism Council is asking the Governor of Svalbard to remove the requirement for rescue insurance and a bank guarantee for the tourism industry on Svalbard. “If the requirement had been introduced for all industries throughout the country, that would be one thing, but it seems unreasonable that it applies only to the tourism industry on Svalbard,” says tourism director Ronny Brunvoll.
310051.subtitle_en: The tourism industry in Longyearbyen believes it is unreasonable that it alone must have rescue insurance.

310062.excerpt_en: “There have been different practices in recent years, and for a period it was not customary for the Governor of Svalbard to invoice rescue costs. We feel the need to examine the matter more closely, since several people here at the office have not dealt with it before,” says tourism adviser Aud Andersen at the Governor’s office.
310062.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is waiting to charge for tourism rescues until it has clarified what its future practice will be.

310070.excerpt_en: “The basis for applying to the environmental protection fund was that we had expenses related to the project. It has now been clarified that we will receive salvage payments for snowmobiles and cars.”
310070.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council is turning down NOK 250,000 for a rubbish amnesty because it received salvage payments on the mainland. The fee for delivering wrecks to the waste facility has now been reduced.

310084.excerpt_en: On 6 January, the Russian population of Barentsburg celebrated Orthodox Christmas Eve.
310084.subtitle_en: When children from Longyearbyen met children in Barentsburg, they used Google Translate.
310084.title_en: A warm meeting filled with laughter and a few choice Google words

310107.excerpt_en: It is the Governor’s environmental protection department that has initiated a centre to communicate Svalbard’s cultural and natural values. The “Svalbard National Park Centre” project has received NOK 675,000 from Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund and NOK 280,000 from the Ministry of Climate and Environment for a one-year preliminary study.
310107.subtitle_en: The authorities want a centre that can spread more knowledge about the national parks and Svalbard’s special flora, fauna and cultural heritage.
310107.title_en: National park centre in the making

310120.excerpt_en: The sea holds many secrets, especially in the north, where darkness, cold and ice have effectively kept a protective hand over the Arctic Ocean, preventing researchers and other curious minds from looking in.
310120.subtitle_en: “The sea holds many secrets, especially in the north, where darkness, cold and ice have effectively kept a protective hand over the Arctic Ocean, preventing researchers and other curious minds from looking in.”
310120.title_en: On bamboo, ghost crabs and an Arctic in change

310155.excerpt_en: While Mack Brewery is openly battling Rema 1000 because it has removed their beer from its stores across much of mainland Norway, the grocery giant is exploring the possibility of establishing itself in Longyearbyen. Svalbardbutikken is the sole player in the grocery market.
310155.subtitle_en: “A competing grocery store would be good for consumers”

310164.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard reports on its website that new polar-bear tracks have been observed at Passhytta. The tracks are probably from a mother bear with a cub.
310164.subtitle_en: Fresh tracks from a mother bear with a cub have been observed at Passhytta in Eskerdalen. The Governor of Svalbard is asking people out in the terrain to take precautions.

310178.excerpt_en: “They reacted both to the helicopter and snowmobiles and to the deterrents we used. When we left them, they were continuing farther into the valley,” reports acting chief superintendent Trond Olsen.
310178.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard located the polar bears around 1 a.m. on Saturday and managed to drive them farther into Foxdalen using a helicopter and snowmobiles.
310178.title_en: Mother Bear with Two Cubs Driven into Foxdalen

310182.excerpt_en: The three bears were spotted in Adventdalen, on the road by Gruve 6, at 7 a.m. on Sunday. “We are driving the bears eastward through Adventdalen by helicopter and snowmobiles, and we have the situation under control,” says acting chief superintendent Thor-Arild Hansen.
310182.subtitle_en: The mother polar bear and her two cubs, which were spotted just outside Longyearbyen on Sunday morning, have now been driven eastward and away from town. The Governor of Svalbard ended the operation on Sunday afternoon.

310255.excerpt_en: The mother polar bear is at Gruve 7 mountain just outside Longyearbyen, after the Governor of Svalbard repeatedly tried to chase them away from the area around Longyearbyen by snowmobile. “The bears are lying still, and we are keeping them under observation,” says acting chief superintendent Vidar Arnesen.
310255.subtitle_en: The mother polar bear and her two cubs are approaching Longyearbyen again. The Governor of Svalbard is using considerable resources to keep the bears away from town.

310271.excerpt_en: Neither visitors nor residents can get to Longyearbyen with SAS today. The flight that was due to leave Tromsø at 12:20 was cancelled because of bad weather in Longyearbyen.
310271.subtitle_en: Today’s SAS flight has been cancelled, and the postal flight had to turn back. Norwegian also had to cancel its flight.

310281.excerpt_en: The mother polar bear and her two cubs have returned to the area around Longyearbyen twice after the Governor of Svalbard tried to chase them eastward and away from town. “We have concluded that it is not wise to try to chase the mother bear farther into Adventdalen yet again.”
310281.subtitle_en: Following a meeting with the Norwegian Polar Institute, the Governor of Svalbard has decided to guide the mother polar bear and her two cubs toward Revneset.
310281.title_en: Plans to Drive the Mother Bear Past Longyearbyen

310296.excerpt_en: This evening, the mother bear and her two cubs were driven a considerable distance toward Revneset. “They have now settled down. In consultation with the Norwegian Polar Institute, we are ending today’s operation,” says Governor of Svalbard Kjerstin Askholt.
310296.subtitle_en: The polar bears have now been driven past Longyearbyen and toward Revneset with the help of the Governor’s helicopter, assisted by polar-bear researcher Jon Aars.

310306.excerpt_en: Footprints from the mother polar bear and her two cubs were observed at UNIS early this morning. “We then saw tracks at Kuhaugen and Isdammen, indicating that the bears are heading out of town again,” says Governor of Svalbard Kjerstin Askholt.
310306.subtitle_en: Early this morning, tracks belonging to the mother polar bear and her two cubs were observed at UNIS, right in town. At 6:15 a.m., they were spotted at Endalen, just outside the built-up area.
310306.title_en: The Bears Have Been in Town

310310.excerpt_en: Berit Våtvik has lived in Longyearbyen since the mid-1970s and has encountered polar bears many times before. She and her husband run Svalbard Wilderness Centre and live just outside town by the municipal dog kennel.
310310.subtitle_en: Berit Våtvik was woken by the dogs in the kennel shortly after 5 a.m. on Tuesday. When she went outside, the mother bear and her cubs were outside the house where she lives.
310310.title_en: Came Face to Face with the Mother Bear

310335.excerpt_en: “Our most important task now is to keep the bear away from town. We urge people to be careful and take precautions,” says Governor of Svalbard Kjerstin Askholt.
310335.subtitle_en: The mother bear and her two cubs were last seen in the middle of the day in Endalen. The Governor of Svalbard is asking people to be especially vigilant.

310349.excerpt_en: Empty mail and fresh-produce shelves in Longyearbyen were due to be restocked today. The first postal flight landed as scheduled and returned to Tromsø to pick up another load.
310349.subtitle_en: A postal flight arrived in Longyearbyen on Thursday, the first since Friday. Thursday’s extra flight was cancelled, which, among other things, affects Svalbardposten.

310357.excerpt_en: Hurtigruten has a long history, including on Svalbard. As early as 1896, Vesteraalens Dampskibsselskap, led by Captain Richard With, transported a prefabricated tourist hotel from the mainland, which was assembled at Hotellneset.
310357.subtitle_en: As of January 1, 2017, Spitsbergen Travel changed its name to Hurtigruten Svalbard.

310377.excerpt_en: The ocean is an almost inexhaustible source of fascinating organisms with distinctive adaptations, life histories, and appearances. One of the strangest may be nature’s own super-communist: siphonophores.
310377.subtitle_en: Unlike most other organisms, these creatures have a division of labor and social organization that even Karl Marx would have been impressed by. (External article)

310399.excerpt_en: Svalbard Turn’s swimming group took part in Ishavssvøm in Tromsø at the weekend. Twenty-four swimmers aged 9 to 16 participated, and for ten of them it was their first competition. “For the youngest ones, there is one competition a year, and it is Ishavssvøm.”
310399.subtitle_en: 24 swimmers, 102 starts and 60 personal records. The swimmers from Longyearbyen deliver when they get to compete.

310409.excerpt_en: Pictures, crates and sculptures are strewn haphazardly around Kunsthall Svalbard’s rooms at Svalbard Museum this Tuesday.
310409.subtitle_en: The Nordnorsk Kunstmuseum has brought some of its greatest works to Svalbard. Tomorrow, an exhibition tracing the Arctic from the 19th century to the present day opens.

310417.excerpt_en: At the start of every semester, UNIS organizes a six-day safety course primarily for students. They receive training in polar-bear safety, avalanche hazards, first aid, and what to do when working in the field under difficult conditions.
310417.subtitle_en: Students who began the semester just after New Year were drilled in how to travel through the Arctic wilderness.
310417.title_en: Preparing Students for Polar Bears and Avalanches

310438.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten is now presenting a collection of historical photographs lent to us by Stig Onarheim, who is now a helicopter pilot with Lufttransport. His father was a fire chief, and Stig says he was told by Store Norske management to burn down the buildings in Sverdrupbyen because they were standing empty and deteriorating.
310438.subtitle_en: The burning down of Sverdrupbyen was controversial.

310449.excerpt_en: Experiments are under way in Kongsfjorden involving four unique underwater vehicles and an advanced kayak that records everything from tiny algae to the seabed, fish, and temperatures. Biologists are working closely with technologists, and robots are answering questions researchers have long asked.
310449.subtitle_en: Brand-new technology is being used to learn more about life in the ocean during the polar night.

310465.excerpt_en: The mother polar bear and her two cubs, which have roamed the area and even entered town over the past week, may have received far more attention than she herself would have wanted. The bears have made news well beyond Svalbardposten’s coverage area.
310465.subtitle_en: In retrospect, we must be very grateful that the mother bear and her two cubs encountered an experienced bear expert who dealt with the situation himself and chased the bears out of the residential area.

310475.excerpt_en: In total, funding was sought for 50 different projects. The application for funding for the youth film project Sons of Svalbard sparked the most debate.
310475.subtitle_en: Sons of Svalbard applied for NOK 310,595 for a snowmobile film. In the end, they received NOK 40,000.
310475.tags_en: news, Sons of Svalbard, grant funds

310501.excerpt_en: This autumn, the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate commissioned a report from Almaviva AS on which protective measures may be relevant for Longyearbyen. “It contains proposals for specific protective measures in Longyearbyen. We will examine them more closely.”
310501.subtitle_en: NVE will recommend what kind of avalanche protection Longyearbyen should have. The conclusion may not be permanent measures.

310524.excerpt_en: Avalanches posing a danger to buildings and human life can occur in Lia, from Road 230 to Road 222, in Nybyen and in the area above Longyearbyen kindergarten. This is shown in the report Multiconsult prepared for the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate last year.
310524.subtitle_en: It is entirely possible to permanently protect the avalanche-prone areas of Longyearbyen, but it will be costly. Protecting the town from avalanches could come with a price tag of more than NOK 180 million.
310524.title_en: How the Town Can Be Protected from Avalanches

310551.excerpt_en: Rema wants to build a store on the parking lot in front of the town’s only grocery store, Coop Svalbard’s Svalbardbutikken.
310551.subtitle_en: If Svalbardbutikken loses its parking lot to Rema, the board will have to reassess its investments and operations, says board chair Frigg Jørgensen.

310570.excerpt_en: For almost 100 years, the coal cars have stood outdoors. They have survived winter storms and torrential rain, salt spray from the sea, and thousands of tonnes of black coal.
310570.subtitle_en: Five old workhorses from the coal-mining era will shine beautifully when the boss returns.

310584.excerpt_en: To be sure, all employees in the world’s northernmost community play important roles. But much would grind to a halt without Sunnmøre native Frode Flaate. The 59-year-old is Kings Bay’s only mechanic, responsible for around 50 vehicles, from snowmobiles and heavy excavators to electric cars and sand spreaders.
310584.subtitle_en: “Of course I can” could have been the motto of Ny-Ålesund’s most important man.

310623.excerpt_en: Many curious onlookers are visiting the avalanche site. The Governor of Svalbard fears something could happen and urges people to be careful.
310623.subtitle_en: Road 300 between Huset and Museumsveien is closed after an avalanche reached the ski trail on Saturday morning. That same afternoon, the road up to Gruvelageret was also closed.

article_keywords_en: chief superintendent of the Governor’s Office
310666.excerpt_en: A visiting tourist will be fined after behaving poorly at Huset on Friday evening. The man had consumed more alcohol than was safe.
310666.subtitle_en: A tourist was fined. Three other tourists thought they had seen a polar bear. In both cases, the police responded.

310670.excerpt_en: The deep-sea jellyfish is known by the Latin name “Periphylla periphylla”, and two specimens slowly swam into the harbour at Ny-Ålesund. The jellyfish lives in the deep ocean but rises to the surface at night.
310670.subtitle_en: The crown jellyfish, which causes problems in many Norwegian fjords, has been discovered in Svalbard for the first time.

310681.excerpt_en: Last Saturday, Road 300 was closed from the junction with Road 501 all the way up to Gruvelageret. By then, four or five smaller avalanches had occurred on the mountainside, one of which had stopped against the ski trail.
310681.subtitle_en: Road 300 from Melkeveien up to Huset has reopened after being closed since Saturday. The road up to Gruvelageret has also reopened.

310719.excerpt_en: This year’s friends-and-friends football tournament had everything: technical tricks, powerful shots, hopeless passes and plenty of laughter. Seven teams took part, several combining women and men, younger and slightly older players.
310719.subtitle_en: Police Squad dominated the students, but in the final the hard men pleaded desperately to be allowed to quit.

310758.excerpt_en: Last week, researchers and students from the University of Tromsø (UiT) and UNIS, together with partners from Scotland (SAMS) and the United States, completed a 14-day polar-night expedition aboard UiT’s research vessel Helmer Hanssen. During the expedition, they carried out a range of physical and biological surveys in Van Mijenfjorden, Isfjorden, Kongsfjorden and Rijpfjorden.
310758.subtitle_en: A group of researchers provides the answer here.
310758.title_en: Can the Town Bears Expect Ice in Van Mijenfjorden This Year?

317432.excerpt_en: No one could match UNIS’s mixed team in Saturday’s TV Action relay in the town centre, organised by Svalbard Turn.
317432.subtitle_en: When Ola Bakke crossed the finish line in a new course record, the month-long fundraising campaign for the TV Action was officially launched.
317432.title_en: Fundraising Campaign Opens with Course Record

317444.excerpt_en: “I was moved. The children showed tremendous effort and an impressive range of cultural forms.”
317444.subtitle_en: “It was absolutely fantastic,” says Store Norske CEO Wenche Ravlo about Longyearbyen School of Culture’s tribute to the centenarian that built the town. Click the main image to view 27 pictures in the gallery.
317444.tags_en: news, Store Norske, School of Culture
317444.title_en: Impressed by magnificent Store Norske performance

317473.excerpt_en: There are no newspapers that follow daily life on Svalbard day by day and week by week, except Svalbardposten. Nor are there any newspapers that cover the High Arctic from the High Arctic, except this one.
317473.subtitle_en: In 2014, Svalbardposten took the step of beginning to publish English-language news stories and features alongside its Norwegian content. We also published the Top of the World magazine for the first time. The aim is to reach as many people as possible with news and information about Svalbard.
317473.title_en: About the Arctic in the Arctic

317482.excerpt_en: “No, that is very kind to hear,” says dentist Johansen about the good review from the people of Longyearbyen. No fewer than 93 percent of those who have sat in his dental chair are either “satisfied” or “very satisfied” with the service.
317482.subtitle_en: Dentist Rolf Johansen (60) is Longyearbyen’s most popular service provider.
317482.title_en: He Cured Our Fear of the Dentist

317492.excerpt_en: Sofia Berger was, as last year, the youngest participant in Trappers Trail. This year she competed in the eight-dog class, with seven dogs. “I drive because I enjoy competing with my dogs, and because I generally love spending time with dogs,” says the 13-year-old.
317492.subtitle_en: Just six minutes behind her personal best.
317492.title_en: Sofia, 13, Has Become an Experienced Dog Musher

317500.excerpt_en: There is no shortage of interest in local politics and who will govern Longyearbyen for the next four years. Monday’s panel debate was standing room only at Kroa.
317500.subtitle_en: ELECTION 2015: Or the one with the most—or least—hair. It probably makes no difference.
317500.tags_en: politics, reader contribution, election campaign, opinions
317500.title_en: Choose the best-looking of these politicians

317516.excerpt_en: “Do you have access to a plane or helicopter? Or would you simply like to set fire to some old junk lying behind the cabin?”
317516.subtitle_en: This is how the major TV auction unfolded.

317523.excerpt_en: The open hearing on the Svalbard White Paper began at nine o’clock Thursday morning at the Storting.
317523.subtitle_en: Members of Parliament had many questions for the representatives from Svalbard.

317525.excerpt_en: “No, paddling isn’t my thing. There, it’s all about willpower,” Christian Svarstad said after winning the men’s class in the annual quadrathlon competition on Saturday.
317525.subtitle_en: Christian Svarstad had to work hard after “paddling like a crow.”
317525.title_en: Ran and cycled to build a big lead

317570.excerpt_en: “12 February is very early, but at the same time it is something we have seen in recent years.”
317570.subtitle_en: On Monday, three common eiders were spotted in the small-boat harbour—one male and two females.

317578.excerpt_en: “The exhibition has been well attended, and we have received a lot of positive feedback,” gallery manager Jan Martin Berg said when Svalbardposten visited the exhibition on Sunday. Read more: Vandalizing Himself
317578.subtitle_en: Artist Martin Whatson held a pop-up exhibition at Galleri Svalbard from Thursday to Sunday last week.

317592.excerpt_en: The house was purchased in 2017 for NOK 5 million. It consists of two residential units, the larger measuring 175 square metres.
317592.subtitle_en: At its meeting on 11 February, the local council decided to sell the house it owns at Vei 232.523. The proceeds will be used to buy new homes.
317592.title_en: Selling house to buy new homes

318578.excerpt_en: “It has been a long process, but we have finally launched a new website and new login system. We are thrilled to be able to offer our readers an even better service and reading experience,” says editor Børre Haugli.
318578.subtitle_en: Svalbardposten is back in a new guise, with a new website provider. We hope the entire website experience will be as much of a delight for our readers as it is for us.
318578.title_en: Look, We Have a New Website!

318663.excerpt_en: If you are travelling to or from Svalbard, flying is the only option.
318663.subtitle_en: When she was 23, Marit Brekke said her dream was to work for an airline. “Svalbard Airport and Widerøe have been my home in recent years.”

320509.excerpt_en: Lønø was an experienced trapper, with three previous overwintering stays on the east coast of Svalbard. The reason he asked me was probably that I had spent several summer seasons in Svalbard.
320509.subtitle_en: I was 20 years old in the summer of 1964. I worked on a tunnel project in Røldal. Then I received a letter from my former high-school teacher, Odd Lønø. He asked whether I would join him on a planned overwintering expedition in Tjuvfjorden on Edgeøya that autumn.
320509.tags_en: Edgeøya, news, magazine, trappers, trapping life
320509.title_en: “The Bear Sprang Up and Charged at Us at an Unbelievable Speed. It Was a Terrifying Sight.”

324020.excerpt_en: Equipment is being set up in the sitting room on the second floor of the mess hall in Ny-Ålesund. A couple of hundred metres away, the airship mast towers above the town, while the airship “Norge” floats across the black-and-white photographs on the walls inside the concert venue.
324020.subtitle_en: The concerts attracted nearly 2,500 guests. The Polarjazz director is confident this year’s festival will not end in the red.

325798.excerpt_en: “Good choreography, strong technical skills, originality, creativity, and good teamwork.”
325798.subtitle_en: These participants advance in the Youth Cultural Showcase (UKM).
325798.tags_en: UKM, Youth Cultural Showcase, magazine, news

352497.excerpt_en: “There is little snow, but enough for there to be a risk of avalanches,” says Acting Chief Constable Arve Johnsen. That is the conclusion after a hiker triggered an avalanche at the weekend and reported it to the Governor of Svalbard. “It happened on Larsbreen.”
352497.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard urges people to be alert to the risk of avalanches.

352596.excerpt_en: “It’s another mouse year,” announces Eva Fuglei of the Norwegian Polar Institute (NPI). The last one was in 2018, and as then, she is mobilizing people with free traps and prizes for those willing to help.
352596.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s mouse population has enjoyed favorable conditions. Now residents are joining forces to limit the spread.
352596.tags_en: news, eastern vole, Norwegian Polar Institute

352629.excerpt_en: It became clear on Monday that the government will not provide further support to help the company through the coronavirus crisis. The consequences of extensive travel restrictions are severe.
352629.subtitle_en: Norwegian is making deep cuts to its route network and furloughing 1,600 employees. But it will continue operating the route between Longyearbyen and Tromsø.

352635.excerpt_en: Since yesterday, Monday, it has moved a couple of hundred metres east. The Governor of Svalbard went out by helicopter this morning and located the bear, which is probably a large male. “It is important to say that people must be alert to this, especially now during the polar night.”
352635.subtitle_en: The polar bear that has been in Adventdalen since Sunday is still in the area.

352657.excerpt_en: There are an average of 90 guests per day at Longyearbyen’s accommodation establishments this week, according to figures from Visit Svalbard. This is the lowest number since registration began in the summer, immediately after the coronavirus entry restrictions were lifted.
352657.subtitle_en: There are 90 daily visitors in Longyearbyen this week—the lowest figure since tourists returned.

357137.excerpt_en: Three creative hosts guided the audience through ten performances in a fun way, dressed for every scene change. Two bands, a number of soloists and musicians, circus and acrobatics, and art took the stage in turn.
357137.subtitle_en: Creative young people presented a wide range of cultural performances at the local UKM showcase at the cultural centre on Friday.

362193.excerpt_en: Where it all began This is Nanny Glerup. Nanny is the founder of Glerups footwear, and as a young newlywed she decided to felt a pair of slippers from wool for her husband, Ove.
362193.subtitle_en: It should be specified here that no form of Arctic farming is planned anytime soon, but one can easily become inspired after receiving a few Gotland sheep. Or what do you say, Nanny?

363603.excerpt_en: “The rest is up to you now. I recommend kitesurfing,” said pilot Robert Johansen after landing in Svea.
363603.subtitle_en: Strong winds, snow and canceled flights on Friday evening were not ideal for the organizers of Gruveløpet. But the race went ahead—and so did the sunshine.

368869.excerpt_en: The polar bear is Svalbard’s symbol and brand. Even so, few tourists are lucky enough to see one in the wild.
368869.subtitle_en: The typical Svalbard tourist learns about Svalbard’s history from Longyearbyen’s many stuffed polar bears. We have 17 of them.
368869.tags_en: news, tourism, polar bear, history, Svalbard Museum

371265.excerpt_en: There were only smiles, only joy, only beautiful trails, only brilliant weather—and only Svalbard at its best. “We came here to ski the Svalbard Ski Marathon, but we came anyway when it was cancelled. And then we got to take part in this.”
371265.subtitle_en: Why have a ski marathon when we have the Longyearbyen Ski Festival?
371265.title_en: Almost Better Than a Ski Marathon

375787.excerpt_en: “I have to do some laundry before I head back to civilisation. It’s not exactly drying weather at the moment,” says Harald A.
375787.subtitle_en: Harald A. Soleim has spent 40 winters on Svalbard. Now he has moved into a room in Longyearbyen, at least for a while.

381034.excerpt_en: John-Einar Lockert, Bård Heio, Tollef Svenkerud and Morten E. Astrup own large parts of Longyearbyen’s restaurant and tourism businesses.
381034.subtitle_en: Huset, Svalbard Snowmobile Rental, bars, hotels and housing. Four men pull the strings.
381034.tags_en: news, business, tourism, company, restaurant, hotel

386815.excerpt_en: “I love being here; we’re having such a good time. The parents are happy, we’re happy, and the children are having a wonderful time,” she says.
386815.subtitle_en: Camilla Rød Ellingsen, an educator at Kullungen Kindergarten, is delighted that an outdoor kindergarten has finally become a reality.

387785.excerpt_en: Fire attack leader Trond Håvelsrud has just lit a fire inside the flashover container at the fire-training ground above the airport. The temperature is steadily rising as Håvelsrud reports to the duty crew at the fire station that they must deploy.
387785.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen has 24 firefighters. Every week, they practise different scenarios they hope will never become reality.

388031.excerpt_en: Once, in 2011, I was aboard the old and reliable «Nordsyssel». Oddleif Moen then asked me to translate the diary of a Russian who overwintered in Bjonahamna in 1923–1924.
388031.subtitle_en: Anastasia Gorter, a Russian-language adviser and interpreter for the Governor of Svalbard, has gained access to, among other things, the diary of Ivan Hochlin, who overwintered in Bjonahamna in the 1920s. Read the story here. Open access.
388031.title_en: A Russian on a Norwegian Overwintering Expedition in Bjonahamna

399788.excerpt_en: Saturday’s Polarjazz opened with familiar hits by former deLillos vocalist Lars Lillo Stenberg, followed by acclaimed jazz artist Bugge Wesseltoft with the trio Rymden.
399788.subtitle_en: The final days of Polarjazz 2022 were filled with both familiar music and a completely new lineup of artists.

400306.excerpt_en: Head of Culture Are Nundal opened the traditional sporting exchange. But he was pleased to welcome more than just sport. “Welcome.”
400306.subtitle_en: Sport at a friendly level best describes the sporting exchange between Longyearbyen and Barentsburg in Svalbardhallen on Saturday. See the pictures.
400306.title_en: In the shadow of the Olympics

407929.excerpt_en: It is old news that mining in Svea and Lunckefjell is to cease. The Svea settlement will be cleared away, and the area restored to the way it was before mining began.
407929.subtitle_en: Store Norske, the Governor’s Office and Svalbard Museum agree that the mining history must be preserved.
407929.tags_en: Governor’s environmental protection department, Svalbard history, Governor’s Office, Svalbard Museum, news, museum, environmental protection chief, history, mining museum, mine, Svea

415393.excerpt_en: Former Svalbardposten journalist Kent Roar Nybø got a surprise on Monday. He received an invoice from Gruvelageret for his wedding.
415393.subtitle_en: Kent Roar Nybø received a surprising bill from Gruvelageret.

415711.excerpt_en: This week’s historical photo shows the D/S “Ingerfem” at the quay at Hotellneset in 1960. “Ingerfem” was one of six “Inger” vessels belonging to Kjøde’s shipping company in Bergen (Ingeren, Ingerto, Ingertre, etc.).
415711.subtitle_en: Coal, cargo and passenger vessel at the quay in 1960.

415989.excerpt_en: Others can decide whether I’m wise or foolish, but I certainly understand what you mean when you write: “I’m tired of hearing about bad things! I’d much rather hear about all the cool things happening here in town!”
415989.subtitle_en: Thank you so much for a thoughtful and relevant letter to the editor—you’re a wise 11-year-old.
415989.title_en: Hi Freja, I’m taking that to heart too!

416647.excerpt_en: Sunday was the first day of competition at the Special Olympics for Trym Eide Aunevik from Longyearbyen. He set a personal best by nearly four seconds in the 200-metre freestyle, then lowered his personal record in the 100-metre butterfly by an impressive 11 seconds.
416647.subtitle_en: Trym Eide Aunevik, 17, set personal records in both freestyle and butterfly at the Special Olympics in Abu Dhabi.
416647.tags_en: Special Olympics, news, swimming, Trym Eide Aunevik
416647.title_en: Great start for Trym in Abu Dhabi

417322.excerpt_en: “Being present by the hospital steps where everyone sang and shouted for the sun was almost magical,” says Ingeborg Widerøe, 26.
417322.subtitle_en: She arrived on the day the sun returned, had never been north of the Arctic Circle and has already become a Svalbard resident.

417463.excerpt_en: Earlier in the championships, the 17-year-old swimmer from Longyearbyen swam to fourth and fifth place.
417463.subtitle_en: Trym Eide Aunevik swam to sixth place in his final event at the Special Olympics in Abu Dhabi.
417463.tags_en: Svalbard Turn, news, Trym Eide Aunevik, Special Olympics

417627.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, Jonny Haugen of Applied Autonomy was in Longyearbyen to drive the route and program a self-driving bus. The project is led by Arctic Memory in cooperation with Svalbard Buss og Taxi and Kongsberg Gruppen.
417627.subtitle_en: On Thursday, you can take the self-driving bus for a test ride.

417906.excerpt_en: Latest: Svalbardposten arrived on the SAS flight on Thursday afternoon. Newspaper retailers received it at around 4 p.m.
417906.subtitle_en: Due to technical problems with the mail plane.
417906.tags_en: Svalbardbutikken, Svalbardposten, news, food, newspaper, mail plane

417980.excerpt_en: Large parts of Lompensenteret were flooded when a pipe burst during the morning. It has now emerged that the leak occurred when a pipe leading to a fire hose suddenly burst. “Now we must investigate and try to determine why the pipe burst.”
417980.subtitle_en: The major water leak at Lompensenteret on Tuesday, March 12, caused less damage than feared.

418334.excerpt_en: “We need to take a broader view. There are increasingly more tourists and increasingly more rental snowmobiles.”
418334.subtitle_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard has recently been granted permission to use the area by Forskningsparken to park its snowmobiles. The neighbours are far from pleased.
418334.tags_en: news, Longyearbyen land-use plan, snowmobile parking, Hurtigruten Svalbard

418376.excerpt_en: “I understand that the neighbours are complaining, and I understand that those affected see this as a major change to the land-use plan,” says Arild Olsen.
418376.subtitle_en: Community Council leader Arild Olsen (Labour) has great understanding for the concerns of residents in Road 238.
418376.tags_en: news, Arild Olsen, snowmobile parking, Longyearbyen Community Council

418433.excerpt_en: “Today’s travellers have high expectations, particularly when they come to Svalbard,” says Krisztina Uzonyi, manager of the Polar Hotel. Earthy natural colours greet you as you enter the newly renovated hotel, which Uzonyi is happy to show off.
418433.subtitle_en: The Polar Hotel was renovated over three months. Here is the result.
418433.tags_en: Polar Hotel, news, Hurtigruten Svalbard, hotel industry, construction industry, architecture, renovation
418433.title_en: “The colours were important when we renovated”

418488.excerpt_en: “We have already lost two human lives because of climate change. Enough is enough,” he said, referring to the 2015 avalanche.

When the sun is insufficient, they will operate their own power plant using LNG (liquefied natural gas).

429196.excerpt_en: Oddgeir Sagerup of BirdLife Svalbard contacted the newspaper to say that it is now possible to follow the snow bunting via a webcam on YouTube. “We would like to give our only breeding songbird a little extra attention.”
429196.subtitle_en: You have probably heard the chirping of our regular spring visitor, the snow bunting.
429196.title_en: You Can Now Watch the Snow Bunting Live

429232.excerpt_en: This year’s russe president in Longyearbyen is Ronja Hermansen (19). She is now approaching the russe celebrations with slightly more responsibility than the other red-clad graduating students.
429232.subtitle_en: Ronja Hermansen (19) is this year’s russe president in Longyearbyen.
429232.tags_en: Longyearbyen School, 17 May, russe celebrations, news

429235.excerpt_en: This became clear when she met representatives from the folk high school at Fruene café in Longyearbyen on Friday morning. There are several reasons why the extra millions are now being allocated. “This will be an important school for Norwegian Svalbard policy.”
429235.subtitle_en: The folk high school first received NOK 7.1 million through the national budget. Today, Minister of Research and Higher Education Iselin Nybø (V) announced that it would receive another five million.
429235.tags_en: students, national budget, government, politics, news, Svalbard Folk High School
429235.title_en: More Money for the Folk High School

429276.excerpt_en: By presenting proposals to amend the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act and its associated regulations, as well as a proposal for new regulations on safety in the field and more in Svalbard, the Norwegian authorities have put forward plans for powerful new regulations governing travel and tourism in the archipelago.
429276.subtitle_en: “There is a need to put a ceiling on parts of tourism development in Svalbard,” writes Ulf Prytz.
429276.title_en: The Elephant in the Room – Changes to Tourism and Environmental Laws and Regulations

429294.excerpt_en: “We are now standing at the grave of Captain Trond Astrup Vigtel. He lost his life fighting German occupiers in Svalbard in 1943.”
429294.subtitle_en: It is a well-established tradition for the Governor of Svalbard to lay a wreath at the grave of Captain Trond Astrup Vigtel on Liberation Day. This year, it was done with a thought for those who do not enjoy the same freedom as we do.
429294.tags_en: news, Governor of Svalbard, Liberation Day, cemetery
429294.title_en: “I Hope Ukrainians Will Also Get a Day Like This”

429306.excerpt_en: The draft currently shows that applications could be made for up to NOK 400,000 for business development. If approved, Longyearbyen Community Council will ask the state for funding.
429306.subtitle_en: Politicians will now consider a proposal to establish a business development fund in May.
429306.tags_en: news, Longyearbyen Community Council, politics, business
429306.title_en: Final Push for Business Fund – Counting on State Funding

429334.excerpt_en: We speak to Roger Frank by phone from Sweden. He was one of the participants in this year’s ski marathon, together with his daughter and her partner.
429334.subtitle_en: A very special friendship blossomed during this year’s ski marathon.
429334.tags_en: Svalbard Ski Marathon, tourism, news, volunteers
429334.title_en: “I’ve Gained a Friend for Life in Sølvi”

429391.excerpt_en: As is well known, fluorinated toxic substances called PFAS and PFOS were detected in the area in 2012. They originated from the former firefighting training site by the road to the airport. The hazardous fluorinated substances were previously used in firefighting foam until the training site was closed in 2000.
429391.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Geotechnical Institute will research whether it is possible to isolate the toxic material at the airport.
429391.tags_en: news, Norwegian Environment Agency, PFOS, environmental contaminants
429391.title_en: “We Want to See Whether It Is Possible to Limit the Risk”

429424.excerpt_en: The Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund received 77 applications totalling NOK 36 million. Grants have been awarded in all different amounts.
429424.subtitle_en: Thirty-one applicants can head into the weekend celebrating. On Friday, Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund distributed NOK 9 million for various environmental measures.

429466.excerpt_en: “We’re standing here wondering what we’re handing out the most of: bananas or chocolate,” say Mona Dahl and Ida Johannessen. They are at the food station 12 kilometres into the course, smiling and laughing.
429466.subtitle_en: The ski marathon’s polar-bear patrols, food stations, race-number distribution and banquet: none of it would have happened without the volunteers’ efforts.
429466.tags_en: volunteers, Svalbard Ski Marathon, skiing, news, cross-country skiing, volunteering, Svalbard Turn
429466.title_en: Infectious Smiles on the Ski Trail

429629.excerpt_en: After the Viking Sky incident off Hustadvika a month ago, emergency rescue preparedness is once again being discussed. MP Arne Nævra (SV), also known as an NRK nature-film producer, has therefore submitted a proposal to the Storting.
429629.subtitle_en: MP Arne Nævra (SV) has spent many years on Svalbard. Now he wants the Storting to examine the emergency preparedness situation as cruise traffic increases in Norwegian waters.
429629.tags_en: politics, news, cruise, emergency preparedness, AECO, rescue capacity
429629.title_en: They Believe Size Restrictions Must Be Discussed

429753.excerpt_en: Here are some of the new teachers at Svalbard Folk High School. From left: Christine Tilley (outdoor activities teacher), Eike Stübner (research-track teacher), Rico Behlke (research-track teacher), Pål Berg (head of administration), Mari Eiken (outdoor activities teacher), Ronny L.
429753.subtitle_en: Svalbard Folk High School will begin operating in Longyearbyen this autumn.
429753.title_en: The Folk High School Teachers Are Ready

429900.excerpt_en: The tragic incident in Lia in December 2015 shook all of us in Longyearbyen, as well as many people on the mainland. Then, completely unexpectedly, another avalanche came from Sukkertoppen in February 2017.
429900.subtitle_en: Ole Reistad points to what he believes are discrepancies between the Norwegian Meteorological Institute’s climate report and the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate’s assessments of climate change.

430027.excerpt_en: In June last year, a man in his 30s drove under the influence in Longyearbyen without a driving licence, while asking random people on the street where he could obtain drugs. After the man was arrested, police found drugs he had with him in the car.
430027.subtitle_en: Prison, permanent revocation of his driving licence and a hefty fine. That was the outcome of a somewhat unusual drug case by Svalbard standards.

430149.excerpt_en: Ellen is Swedish and has worked in Norway’s tourism and service industries for several years. Seasonal jobs take her to different parts of the world.
430149.subtitle_en: Ellen Simberg (27) had a summer job at Karlsberger pub (KB) in 2017. Now she is back in a new job.

430256.excerpt_en: For a long time, it was a “forgotten” tradition, but a few years ago the Governor revived the practice of laying a wreath at the grave of Captain Trond Astrup Vigtel. He was commander of the Norwegian forces in Longyearbyen, but was killed when a German warship bombed the town in September 1943.
430256.subtitle_en: Four girls from Longyearbyen School read poems, and Minister Tybring-Gjedde laid a wreath.

430394.excerpt_en: Our routine is to collect the week’s edition of Svalbardposten from the postal service on Thursday morning. The bundles are then driven out to the various sales outlets.
430394.subtitle_en: Help us solve the mystery of the missing newspaper.

430401.excerpt_en: The newspaper is being delivered to the city’s shops and hotels as you read this. Working for Svalbardposten involves tasks one would not normally encounter at newspapers on the mainland.
430401.subtitle_en: The mystery of the missing newspaper was solved after more than an hour of intense detective work.

430605.excerpt_en: This week, the Greens finalized their list for this autumn’s local elections. It was clear early on that Pål Berg would become the party’s top candidate and thus its candidate for local council chair.
430605.subtitle_en: Benjamin Vidmar is the only person standing for re-election for the Green Party (MDG). Everyone else on the list is new.

430621.excerpt_en: Venstre is fielding a list of 21 names. Eirik Berger of the nomination committee is very pleased. “We are very proud of the list we have put together.”
430621.subtitle_en: Venstre has its list ready for the autumn election. Over the weekend, they held their first campaign stall to gather input.
430621.title_en: See Who Is Standing for Venstre

430863.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen has a long history as an industrial community. Now other industries are gradually taking over from mining.
430863.subtitle_en: Workers’ rights were put on the agenda on 1 May, both in the banners carried in the parade and at the evening event at the cultural centre afterwards.
430863.title_en: Celebrated Workers’ Day in Strong, Cold Headwinds

431106.excerpt_en: On Sunday, the Svalbard Labour Party adopted its final list for October’s local election. There had been long-standing speculation that the new leader, Elise Strømseng, would take the top spot on the list.
431106.subtitle_en: Arild Olsen (Labour) hopes to continue as local council chair in Longyearbyen.
431106.tags_en: news, local council chair, Svalbard Labour Party, local election

431295.excerpt_en: It is not every day that you get the chance to suggest a name for an area—and perhaps even be allowed to name a mountain peak or glacier. Some of the maps to be printed later this year are missing place names in certain areas.
431295.subtitle_en: Every year, the Norwegian Polar Institute publishes new maps. This time, they are missing names for several large glaciers, headlands, bays and mountain peaks.
431295.title_en: Name a Glacier or Mountain Peak

431367.excerpt_en: “This is very positive for us,” was Per Erik Hanevold’s first reaction when he heard the news. The government has just published its proposal for a revised national budget.
431367.subtitle_en: The government proposes allocating an additional two million kroner to Kings Bay. The money will go towards upgrading buildings in Ny-Ålesund.
431367.tags_en: national budget, Svalbard Folk High School, politics, Polarsyssel, news, Ny-Ålesund, seed vault, emergency preparedness, government

431486.excerpt_en: Ole Reistad’s letter to the editor, published on 5 May, rightly points to the discrepancy between the report “Climate in Svalbard 2100” and the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate’s assessments.

431613.excerpt_en: Few have more years of experience as a miner than Anita Johansen. In April 1988, at the age of 21, she began her first shift at Mine 3. “We crawled and crawled, and walked and walked.”
431613.subtitle_en: After 26 years with Store Norske, Anita Johansen (53) has become leader of the Norwegian Union of General Workers.
431613.tags_en: Longyearbyen Workers’ Association, Anita Johansen, news, Norwegian Union of General Workers

431757.excerpt_en: Wednesday this week was the final deadline for local parties to submit their lists for this autumn’s local election. In Longyearbyen, five parties are running lists.
431757.title_en: Parties gear up for local battle for your vote

431759.excerpt_en: The Progress Party has the “youngest” local branch in Svalbard and is running eight candidates on its list.
431759.subtitle_en: The Progress Party’s list for this year’s election was finalized on Monday this week.

431817.excerpt_en: Whether you celebrate Constitution Day by marching in a parade, standing on a mountain peak or staying at home in your living room, we wish you a wonderful day. According to the forecast, the weather will be splendid, with temperatures from zero to minus one degree, sunshine and only a light breeze.
431817.subtitle_en: We hope May 17 brings wonderful experiences for all our readers.
431817.tags_en: Constitution Day, Constitution Day, party, celebration, May 17, news

431964.excerpt_en: Games, cakes, soda and ice cream. And entertainment.
431964.subtitle_en: For many people, May 17 simply isn’t complete without a trip to Svalbardhallen.

431994.excerpt_en: “This came completely unexpectedly. I perhaps prefer having a small supporting role,” Ottar Svensen said when he received the award at a packed cultural center on May 17.
431994.subtitle_en: This year’s recipient of the Tyfus statuette has been involved in almost every aspect of the town’s cultural life during the 15 years he has lived here.

432031.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen’s resident mood-booster, Trym Aunevik, suddenly became the center of attention when his name was read out. He has made his mark in many fields, and over the past six months he has truly distinguished himself on the international swimming scene.
432031.subtitle_en: There was great cheering in the hall when this year’s recipient of the Youth Culture Grant was announced.
432031.tags_en: news, youth, culture, May 17, culture grant

432060.excerpt_en: The new public facility is scheduled to be ready on June 14 and will replace the tent that has housed the tourist information office in recent years.
432060.subtitle_en: The modules that will become a new public facility and a sanitary building are ready on the boat in the harbor. Piling work will begin shortly.
432060.title_en: Building a public facility and sanitary facilities

432174.excerpt_en: There has long been a desire to do something about the town’s pedestrian street.
432174.subtitle_en: The skate ramp may disappear, and Bruktikken may be relocated. Large lizards from the past are coming in. Plans for Gågata are beginning to take shape.
432174.title_en: New paving stones, new lawn—and lizards

432379.excerpt_en: When Svalbard Minister Ingvil Smines Tybring-Gjedde visited the power plant last Wednesday, both boilers stopped and the entire plant shut down. The town was switched to backup power and heating plants.
432379.subtitle_en: The power plant came to a complete stop during the minister’s visit.
432379.title_en: “It was rather fitting that the minister was here”

432463.excerpt_en: The station manager at Hornsund was in Poland when the avalanche accident occurred. Now he wants to get to Svalbard as quickly as possible to assist and support his colleagues.
432463.subtitle_en: “This is a difficult situation for all of us,” says station manager Wlodek Sielski. The names of the two people killed in the avalanche have now been released.
432463.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, avalanche accident, avalanche, news, Hornsund, summit tour
432463.title_en: Releasing the Names and More Details About the Accident

432496.excerpt_en: It was on 10 December last year that the local council asked the administration to draw up a plan for establishing a project position focused on energy.
432496.subtitle_en: “If we are going to have an opinion on the energy transition, we need the capacity to work on it,” says operations engineer Rasmus Bøckmann.
432496.tags_en: energy efficiency, news, energy transition, power station

432554.excerpt_en: March 2019 was the 100th consecutive month with above-normal temperatures in Svalbard.
432554.subtitle_en: Svalbard is a powerful symbol of a changing climate. Norwegian politicians often bring international guests here to illustrate the dramatic changes. With good reason: climate change is clearly visible in the vulnerable Arctic landscape.
432554.title_en: Svalbard—from Coal Dependence to Renewable Role Model

432592.excerpt_en: Frantz Vangen, chief union representative at Hurtigruten Svalbard, believes the process has been orderly. The employees were informed about the transfer of operations at a meeting on Monday the 6th.
432592.subtitle_en: From 1 June, all 23 cleaning workers currently employed by Hurtigruten Svalbard are scheduled to move to new contracts with ISS.
432592.title_en: ISS to Take Over Cleaning for Hurtigruten Svalbard

432652.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Environment Agency has previously rejected the establishment of monitoring stations in the Nordenskiöld Land and Sassen-Bünsow Land national parks. The Polar Institute appealed the decision.
432652.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Polar Institute has applied to set up weather stations at various locations on Spitsbergen.
432652.tags_en: protected area, news, Norwegian Polar Institute, Norwegian Environment Agency, climate, research, weather observations
432652.title_en: When Researchers Wanted to Set Up Stations in Protected Areas, the Directorate Put Its Foot Down

432787.excerpt_en: This year’s 17 May celebration on Bjørnøya was a crowded affair.
432787.subtitle_en: While Bjørnøya had an exceptionally large 17 May parade this year, the people’s parade on Hopen consisted of four people.
432787.title_en: Mixed 17 May Turnout on Bjørnøya and Hopen

432969.excerpt_en: “There appears to be a problem in the uppermost soil and rock layers at Sukkertoppen. It will be difficult to properly anchor the planned support structures,” says Øyvind Hellum, project manager for avalanche protection at Longyearbyen Local Council (LL).
432969.subtitle_en: In the worst-case scenario, it may become necessary to demolish 41 homes in Vei 228. They come in addition to the 139 housing units already slated for demolition.
