506451.subtitle_en: Hurtigruten Svalbard is taking over operation of Bakehuset Nord-Norge’s bakery, but initially only to meet its own needs.

article_keywords_en: Senior Police Officer to the Governor
506498.excerpt_en: It all began with a ski party on Lomonosovfonna. “We had to go and pick them up by helicopter late yesterday evening. They are said to have suffered frostbite,” says Senior Police Officer to the Governor Kjell Arne Lundin.
506498.subtitle_en: Over the past 24 hours, the Governor of Svalbard has had to respond to drunken tourists, pick up a ski group and issue an order over forgotten firearms paperwork.
506498.tags_en: drunken disturbance, news, accident, the Governor of Svalbard
506498.title_en: Responded to drunkenness, frostbite and forgotten firearms paperwork

506507.excerpt_en: Every time you or a tourist travels to Svalbard, NOK 150 is added to the plane or cruise ticket as an environmental fee. Over the course of a year, that adds up to quite a lot of money.
506507.subtitle_en: Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund is awarding NOK 9 million to 27 projects. Even so, the board wishes it had received more applications.
506507.tags_en: Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund, Kings Bay, news, cultural heritage
506507.title_en: “I wish there had been more applications”

506515.excerpt_en: Last year, the May 17 committee in Longyearbyen announced that it had chosen to invite children from Barentsburg to celebrate Constitution Day with us in Longyearbyen.
506515.subtitle_en: This year, too, the May 17 committee has invited children from Barentsburg to celebrate Norway’s Constitution Day in Longyearbyen. This time, the Russian settlement has accepted the invitation.
506515.tags_en: news, Longyearbyen Community Council, Barentsburg, May 17
506515.title_en: “Children must not be caught in the crossfire of a war that is not their fault”

506528.excerpt_en: The post was first published on Rossi’s Facebook page. “Why don’t people want to stay?” asks Line Nagell Ylvisåker in this week’s Svalbardposten editorial. But we do!
506528.subtitle_en: Came for the mountains, stayed for the people
506528.tags_en: opinion, debate, reader contribution, quality of life
506528.title_en: Came for the mountains, stayed for the people

article_keywords_en: Senior Police Officer to the Governor
506553.excerpt_en: A snowmobile caught fire at Revneset on Friday evening. “There was no drama, apart from the fact that the driver had to jump off the snowmobile,” says Senior Police Officer to the Governor Kjell Arne Lundin.

506569.excerpt_en: On Sunday, students from Svalbard Folk High School had set up the finish area above Huset. There, 16 teams and just under 100 dogs would finally cross the finish line after two days in the field.
506569.subtitle_en: With brilliant sunshine at their backs, participants in this year’s Trappers Trail crossed the finish line at Huset on Sunday.
506569.tags_en: dog sledding, Trappers Trail, news, sport
506569.title_en: “The weather hasn’t been this good in many years”

506573.excerpt_en: At around 5 p.m. on Saturday, the Governor of Svalbard was notified by the Northern Norway Joint Rescue Coordination Centre that an InReach transmitter had been activated. Someone then called via an Iridium phone and said they were a snowmobile party of three.

506672.excerpt_en: For the first time ever, the Lytring debate forum is coming to Longyearbyen. Together with a panel comprising senior researcher Siri Veland of Nordland Research Institute and High North News editor Arne O.
506672.subtitle_en: In cooperation with Svalbardposten, the Lytring debate forum brings Arne O. Holm, Trine Krystad, Terje Aunevik and researcher Siri Veland together to discuss Longyearbyen’s transition to a low-emission society.
506672.tags_en: tourism industry, debate, coal mining, news, research
506672.title_en: Tuesday debate to focus on coal mining, tourism and security policy

506676.excerpt_en: “It was very surprising, of course, but it means a lot to me. I really love my job.”
506676.subtitle_en: Teacher Troels Ørsted Yttredal was leading a regular lesson with his fifth-grade students. Suddenly, NRK was in the classroom.

506696.excerpt_en: During Easter, a female polar bear was found dead in the fjord near Vindodden. Jason Roberts had followed the bear, tagged “N23992,” since she was a cub.
506696.subtitle_en: Jason Roberts believes the Governor’s wildlife management policy must take the blame for fatal encounters between polar bears and people.
506696.tags_en: Governor’s Office, news, Jason Roberts, environment, management, polar bear

506711.excerpt_en: A certification exercise was held at Longyearbyen Hospital on Tuesday morning. From the alarm being raised until the blood had been drawn and a nurse was ready with the bag took 48 minutes.
506711.subtitle_en: The volunteer blood-response team managed to be ready with fresh blood in 48 minutes. Health Minister Ingvild Kjerkol (Labour) was impressed.
506711.title_en: Blood preparedness in place in Longyearbyen

506738.excerpt_en: Senior officer Ingunn Iversen of the Governor’s Office says the night began when they had to respond to one of the town’s bars. “They had a difficult customer. He indicated that he wanted to fight,” she says.
506738.subtitle_en: In the early hours of Tuesday, senior officers from the Governor’s Office had to respond to several incidents linked to partying and intoxication.
506738.title_en: “He indicated that he wanted to fight”

506775.excerpt_en: It is a relatively quiet Tuesday for Svalsat station manager Maja-Stina Ekstedt when we meet her for a chat. The normally busy top executive at one of Longyearbyen’s largest companies has a small opening in her schedule that day.
506775.subtitle_en: Maja-Stina Ekstedt took up the leadership position in 2019. Although she had other plans that year, she has never regretted becoming Svalsat’s public face.
506775.title_en: “I feel enormously privileged to have been station manager”

506796.excerpt_en: According to NRK, Chemerilo is from Blagoveshchensk, on the border with China in Russia’s far east. He became consul general in Barentsburg in July last year and, according to NRK, has previously served as a diplomat in Oslo and Stockholm.
506796.subtitle_en: NRK reported on Wednesday that Russian consul general in Barentsburg Andrei Chemerilo has links to Russia’s military intelligence service, the GRU.
506796.title_en: Consul general in Barentsburg is an agent

506807.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, NRK reported that Russian consul general in Barentsburg Andrei Chemerilo has links to the GRU, Russia’s military intelligence service. Chemerilo denied to NRK the allegation that he is connected to Russian intelligence or special services.
506807.subtitle_en: Community Council leader Arild Olsen (Labour) is not surprised by the revelations about the consul general’s links to Russian intelligence.
506807.tags_en: intelligence, news, Longyearbyen Community Council, Barentsburg
506807.title_en: “The Kremlin’s long arm is reaching out from Barentsburg”

506861.excerpt_en: Last year, the cruise ship Ocean Atlantic was banned from sailing after an accident in Hinlopen Strait. When the Norwegian Maritime Authority inspected the vessel, it found more than 20 serious deficiencies.
506861.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Maritime Authority is extending the Svalbard season. Last year, it issued a total of 150 orders. Three boats were banned from sailing.
506861.tags_en: ships, safety, Norwegian Maritime Authority, news
506861.title_en: Warns of more inspections of ships

506875.excerpt_en: In the School of Culture production *An Arctic Adventure! Our Village and Our Pack!*, we follow the character Aurora, who suddenly ends up in Svalbard.
506875.subtitle_en: The School of Culture presented this year’s production to students at Longyearbyen School. The performers themselves admit there were a few butterflies in their stomachs.
506875.tags_en: culture, School of Culture, children and young people, news
506875.title_en: “I was nervous until I walked onto the stage”

506936.excerpt_en: It is through NRK’s documentary series *The Shadow War* that Andrei Chemerilo, consul general in Barentsburg, is linked to the GRU military intelligence service as a Russian intelligence agent in Svalbard. NRK has mapped a large number of embassy employees in the Nordic countries and documented that 39 of them have links to the GRU.
506936.subtitle_en: Consul General Andrei Chemerilo denies being affiliated with Russia’s military intelligence service, the GRU, and calls NRK’s article a pure provocation.
506936.title_en: “The main aim is to discredit me personally”

506940.excerpt_en: “This is the result of a very broad consultation process involving the town’s residents. We went out and asked people what they wanted us to use it for.”
506940.subtitle_en: The plans for Longyearbyen’s new landmark venue are ready. If politicians give the project the go-ahead, it could be completed as early as next winter.
506940.tags_en: Longyearbyen Community Council, news, recycling station, Fønix
506940.title_en: “If politicians respond positively, we’ll start building fairly quickly”

506951.excerpt_en: Antirasistisk Front is complaining about several place names in Svalbard to the Norwegian Polar Institute’s naming committee. They now want the use of names such as Negerpynten, Negerfjellet and Negerodden to end.
506951.subtitle_en: Antirasistisk Front has now submitted a formal complaint about several place names to the Norwegian Polar Institute.
506951.tags_en: place names, news, Norwegian Polar Institute

506961.excerpt_en: Jørn Dybdahl passed away peacefully on Thursday, April 27.
506961.subtitle_en: A longtime Svalbard resident and one of Longyearbyen’s most distinctive voices died on Thursday evening.
506961.title_en: “I will miss all the wonderful conversations with him”

506976.excerpt_en: When Svalbardposten visited Longyearbyen Public Library on Wednesday, a huge group of students from near and far had taken over the entire library. In various corners, the young people sat either deeply concentrated or engrossed in conversation.
506976.subtitle_en: How can games be used for learning at school? Students from Longyearbyen School, together with students from Wales, Denmark and Portugal, have taken a closer look at that question.
506976.tags_en: games, news, Longyearbyen School, Erasmus, Longyearbyen Public Library

507019.excerpt_en: This week, teacher Troels Ørsted Yttredal of Longyearbyen School was nominated as one of three candidates for the title of Norway’s best teacher in Supernytt’s awards. A wonderful recognition for him and the school.
507019.subtitle_en: It is a big job for children who see friends leave and new ones arrive, while classroom dynamics are constantly changing. That is worth its weight in gold: having teachers who see everyone and stretch out their octopus arms to include them all.

507062.excerpt_en: The unregistered weapon was discovered during a check carried out at around 8 p.m. on Saturday. The incident is said to have occurred outside town, and the person concerned was not a permanent resident. “Yesterday, an investigation was opened into a person with an unregistered weapon.”
507062.subtitle_en: A person is under investigation after police discovered an unregistered weapon. “The weapon had also not been stored in accordance with regulations,” says Senior Police Officer Ragnar Schjølset of the Governor’s Office.
507062.tags_en: news, weapons, Governor’s Office, checks, accidental discharge

507090.excerpt_en: Since around 9 a.m. on Monday, the Governor’s Office has carried out several checks around town. These included breathalyser tests, checks of weapons and documents, and checks of driving logs, including at SSU.
507090.subtitle_en: Both alcohol levels and documents were checked.
507090.title_en: Carried out several checks in town

507094.excerpt_en: Several people gathered by the church in Longyearbyen to take part in both a service and a march marking Workers’ Day. Although the march may not have been the longest, several important issues were highlighted on the banners.
507094.subtitle_en: Quality of life, energy prices and social dumping were among this year’s slogans marking Workers’ Day in Longyearbyen.
507094.title_en: Marked Workers’ Day with miners’ buses and speeches

507168.excerpt_en: The Lytring debate forum invited people to a debate in the cultural hall on Tuesday evening. Among other things, they debated whether tourism is more environmentally friendly than coal mining.
507168.subtitle_en: Ahead of the debate, senior researcher Siri Veland from Nordland Research Institute will also give a presentation on the research project.
507168.tags_en: news, debate, tourism, coal mining, environment
507168.title_en: Watch the recording of Tuesday’s Lytring debate here

507174.excerpt_en: Like Store Norske, Statsbygg faces a major task with its 220 homes in Longyearbyen. Longyearbyen Community Council’s energy plan places considerable emphasis on the town’s housing stock undergoing several types of energy-saving measures.
507174.subtitle_en: To improve both quality and energy efficiency in its homes, Statsbygg will invest substantial sums. Tenants will notice the impact as well.
507174.title_en: “It Will当然 Be Reflected in the Rent”

507213.excerpt_en: Last year, Eva Fuglei, an Arctic fox researcher at the Norwegian Polar Institute, reported an explosive increase in fur lice among Svalbard’s Arctic foxes. The lice, first discovered in 2019, had appeared in just over ten per cent of the fox population during the years 2019 to 2021.
507213.subtitle_en: Last year, fur lice prevalence in Arctic foxes exploded. This year, prevalence was surprisingly low, but researchers will monitor the lice closely. “We are cautiously optimistic,” the researchers say.
507213.tags_en: fur lice, news, Arctic fox, Norwegian Polar Institute

507237.excerpt_en: The county showcase in Finnsnes brought together young people from across Troms and Finnmark to compete in all kinds of performing arts. From Longyearbyen came Mikael Bergman (piano), Hanna Lindland Ree (vocals), Åse Jenssen (piano), Dana Sofia Myhrvang Jakobsen (vocals), and the aforementioned Mia Ekeblad Eggenfellner and Aurora Aurora Nordtømme Uhlen (acrobatics/aerial tissue).
507237.subtitle_en: At UKM’s county showcase in Finnsnes, Mia and Aurora came out on top.

507249.excerpt_en: It was not exactly planned. She had held her youth council position for quite some time, but the other two roles practically fell into her lap. “We had a russe meeting at my home last December, and I ended up as russe president,” she says with a laugh.
507249.subtitle_en: Sarine Masterbakk, 19, is both this year’s russe president, head of the 17 May committee and deputy chair of the youth council. She admits she does not mind taking up a little space.
507249.title_en: “Things Will Probably Get a Little Livelier in Town”

507262.excerpt_en: This week, Svalbardposten writes about Phoenix, the old waste facility that could eventually become a new community hub. It would contain many of the facilities people in Longyearbyen feel are lacking today: a climbing wall, workshop, new premises for the second-hand shop, a communal workshop, artists’ studios, co-working space, kitchen, classrooms and facilities for metalworking.
507262.subtitle_en: Is it time for a construction pause?
507262.tags_en: Svalbardhallen, Longyearbyen Community Council, opinion, Phoenix
507262.title_en: Is It Time for a Construction Pause?

507273.excerpt_en: Vilde Ferah Molven, 31, will intern at Svalbardposten until June, followed by a summer job. She comes from the Nynorsk Newspaper Centre and has previously interned at Firda in Førde.
507273.subtitle_en: “I really wanted to combine the internship with an adventure. I’m curious about Svalbard as a society and look forward to getting to know the place and the people here,” says Vilde Ferah Molven.

507292.excerpt_en: The final of the “World Championship” in the board game Risk was held in Longyearbyen at the end of April.
507292.subtitle_en: Newly crowned “world champion” Roar Sivertsen is very pleased with this year’s competition.
507292.title_en: Held “World Championship” in Risk in Longyearbyen

507304.excerpt_en: The film “Storm’s World Is Melting – The Arctic and the Climate” has been nominated at Germany’s largest children’s film festival, Goldener Spatz, and at the Nature Vision Film Festival. The main subject learned about the nomination last week. “I think that’s fun—I had completely forgotten about the documentary,” says Storm Bernlow.
507304.subtitle_en: Storm Bernlow, 14, had actually forgotten that he appeared in the documentary about Svalbard. Now he and the production company could win two awards for it.

507312.excerpt_en: At around 5 a.m. on Thursday, police received a concern report about the skier. The man, who had put on his skis to climb Varden after a boozy night out, was spotted making his way back down the mountain.
507312.subtitle_en: The person is said to have decided to climb Varden on skis after a night out in town.
507312.title_en: Drunk Skier Needed Assistance After Going Up and Then Down Varden

507343.excerpt_en: After several difficult years for the jazz festival, with the pandemic and restrictions, it was wonderful to finally be able to stage it on a full scale again this year.
507343.subtitle_en: “It’s a pleasure to run a festival here,” says festival director Trond Strugstad.

507399.excerpt_en: A tourist in an organised tour group had an accident on his snowmobile on Thursday.
507399.subtitle_en: He is believed to have had an accident on his snowmobile while travelling to the Russian settlement.
507399.title_en: Injured Snowmobile Rider Retrieved from Pyramiden

507405.excerpt_en: “I wouldn’t have dared if it weren’t for Wenche,” says Anne Jahre. The others chime in.
507405.subtitle_en: “I’ll always think of you when I use it,” says Wenche Løpsmark, who is teaching three colleagues and friends to sew Svalbard folk costumes.
507405.title_en: Together, They Have Lived in Svalbard for 75 Years—Now It Was Time

507441.excerpt_en: “Visit Spitsbergen”, “Barentsburg” and “Pyramiden” are written in large letters on the façade of Russki Dom, Trust Arktikugol’s building at Sjøskrenten. A Russian flag was also flying on the entrance side on Friday morning.
507441.subtitle_en: The signs are a natural consequence of Trust Arktikugol being excluded from Visit Svalbard, says tourism director Ronny Brunvoll.
507441.tags_en: Russki Dom, signs, news, Longyearbyen Community Council
507441.title_en: New Signs Installed Without an Application

507463.excerpt_en: Sports and athletics were always a major part of Jørn’s life. First orienteering and cross-country skiing, then windsurfing, before his passion for surfing truly took hold and became a lifelong companion.
507463.subtitle_en: Eventually, he took off on his final wave and rode it into the sunset. After ten years of cancer, even Jørn Dybdahl—the strongest of us all—had to give in.

507483.excerpt_en: On the night of Saturday, a person was removed from Karlsberger Pub. The police ordered him by phone to leave the premises, and he did so.
507483.subtitle_en: One person was removed from a pub, while another struggled through the snow.

507497.excerpt_en: At 2:45 a.m., the Governor was contacted about noise from a party at a private address in Longyearbyen. “It was neighbours who complained about loud music.”
507497.subtitle_en: The Governor broke up a party early Sunday morning.

507512.excerpt_en: According to political secretary Svein Olav Ween of Longyearbyen Local Council, the lists are expected to arrive during the week. But it is not unusual for them to receive the lists on the very last day.
507512.subtitle_en: Monday is the deadline for political parties in Longyearbyen to submit lists for this year’s local election.
507512.tags_en: politics, Longyearbyen Local Council, news, local election
507512.title_en: “12:00 on 15 May Is the Absolute Final Deadline”

507516.excerpt_en: In total, Longyearbyen Fire and Rescue responded 207 times to false or unnecessary alarms, while there were seven callouts for building fires or potential fires. “We clearly see a connection between the number of assignments and visitor activity in the archipelago.”
507516.subtitle_en: There have not been this many callouts since 2016, according to Longyearbyen Fire and Rescue.
507516.tags_en: Longyearbyen Fire and Rescue, statistics, news, fire service
507516.title_en: Responded to More Than 200 False or Unnecessary Alarms

507520.excerpt_en: Until now, the engine-room technicians at Longyearbyen Energiverk have been responsible for the emergency dispatch centre receiving reports of fires or potential fires across much of the town. When an alarm comes in, they call out fire and rescue crews via VHF radio.
507520.subtitle_en: According to Longyearbyen Fire and Rescue, time is now becoming critical to clarify the future of the 110 emergency dispatch centre.
507520.tags_en: news, fire service, Longyearbyen Fire and Rescue
507520.title_en: May Have to Move 110 Emergency Dispatch to Tromsø

507524.excerpt_en: Police prosecutor Magnus Rindal Fredriksen confirms that the Governor received the Veterinary Institute’s report last week. “Unfortunately, I cannot provide any further details about it or other parts of the investigation at this time,” Fredriksen writes in an email to Svalbardposten.
507524.subtitle_en: Last week, the Governor received the Veterinary Institute’s report on the polar bear that died at Vindodden during Easter.
507524.title_en: Polar Bear Death Still Under Investigation

507537.excerpt_en: The editorial in Svalbardposten issue 16/2023 confirms through examples that Longyearbyen Community Council is on the defensive when it comes to maintaining infrastructure and buildings. The tooth of time gnaws at everything, including the mountains.
507537.subtitle_en: “The tooth of time gnaws at everything, including the mountains. The backlog itself proves that society is already living beyond its means.”
507537.title_en: Phoenix and Living Beyond Our Means

507541.excerpt_en: This year marks 80 years since the attack on Longyearbyen. Both the ninth-grade speakers and Governor Lars Fause told those gathered about Captain Trond Astrup Vigtel.
507541.subtitle_en: Ninth-grade pupils at Longyearbyen School marked Liberation Day on Monday morning at the grave of Captain Trond Astrup Vigtel.
507541.tags_en: the Governor, cemetery, news, Liberation Day
507541.title_en: “We Don’t Take Our Peace for Granted”

507557.excerpt_en: Hans Normann is leaving his position as managing director of Svalbard Energi AS, the company said in a press release on Monday. Guttorm Nygård will take over the company’s management on an interim basis from Tuesday morning. “We are pleased to have a new leader in place already.”
507557.subtitle_en: Hans Normann has resigned as managing director of Svalbard Energi AS. Guttorm Nygård will take over on an interim basis.
507557.title_en: Steps Down as Managing Director of Svalbard Energi

507579.excerpt_en: “It’s going very well, but there are also some challenges,” says Martine Eidem when asked how the plastic-bag initiative is progressing. She is HR and administration manager at Coop Svalbard.
507579.subtitle_en: “I have to admit that I’ve forgotten to bring a reusable bag a few times,” says Gry Elise Barlund. The result is a large stockpile of Coop’s reusable bags at home.
507579.title_en: Coop Svalbard Takes Further Measures to Reduce Plastic Bag Use

507607.excerpt_en: Earlier this year, it became known that the Governor had issued tender documents for the purchase of a new service vessel. 8.
507607.subtitle_en: As the Governor now seeks a new vessel, it is being criticised for not giving greater weight to environmental considerations.
507607.tags_en: environment, Polarsyssel, Governor of Svalbard, news
507607.title_en: Criticised for Lack of Focus on the Environment

507626.excerpt_en: No representatives from Svalbard Energi attended Tuesday evening’s Local Council meeting, where the matter was to be discussed by the politicians.
507626.subtitle_en: The report from Svalbard Energi, intended to inform the Local Council about the transition to diesel, was just over 300 words long.
507626.tags_en: power station, news, energy transition, Svalbard Energi
507626.title_en: Submitted a Report on a Single A4 Page

507637.excerpt_en: Acting fire chief at Longyearbyen Fire and Rescue, Geir Hekne, says there is a rising trend of unattended cooking in town. There were seven incidents in 2021, followed by a slight decline last year, while there have already been four incidents this year.
507637.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen fire chief Geir Hekne urges people to avoid cooking at night.
507637.tags_en: news, unattended cooking, Longyearbyen Fire and Rescue, fire safety
507637.title_en: “The Goal Is for No One to End Up in the Death Statistics”

507653.excerpt_en: The University of Tromsø announced the discovery in a press release on Tuesday. The feature discovered by researchers from UiT in collaboration with REV Ocean is thus the second mud volcano ever found in Norwegian waters.
507653.subtitle_en: The volcano lies approximately 70 nautical miles south of Bear Island, at a depth of 400 metres.
507653.title_en: New Volcano Discovered in the Sea Between Svalbard and Mainland Norway

507657.excerpt_en: Timofey Rogozhin, formerly Barentsburg’s head of tourism, says he has never seen such a parade in Barentsburg on 9 May before. “Victory Day has never previously been celebrated so deliberately and loudly, with so much propagandistic noise and pathos,” he wrote to Svalbardposten.
507657.subtitle_en: Vehicles, flags, a helicopter and snowmobiles were used in Tuesday’s 9 May parade along Barentsburg’s main street.
507657.title_en: “I’ve Never Known Victory Day to Have Been Marked with So Much Propaganda”

507707.excerpt_en: At Janssonhaugen, there is a hole extending 102 metres underground. For the past 25 years, this borehole in Svalbard has been highly important both nationally and internationally.
507707.subtitle_en: “It has been extremely exciting to be part of the journey from the beginning,” says Ketil Isaksen, a climate researcher at the Norwegian Meteorological Institute. He says it is thought-provoking to monitor how quickly the permafrost is thawing.
507707.tags_en: permafrost, climate, Norwegian Meteorological Institute, news
507707.title_en: “The Measurements Taken Here Are Completely Unique”

507749.excerpt_en: Although only five of the 12 people attending Svalbard Conservative’s nomination meeting could vote on the list, it was a united group that launched Celine Anderssen as Svalbard Conservative’s top candidate for this year’s local election on Thursday evening.
507749.subtitle_en: Sandefjord native Celine Anderssen (28) becomes Svalbard Conservative’s top candidate.
507749.tags_en: news, Svalbard Conservatives, local election, election campaign

507763.excerpt_en: On 1 January 2023, a total of 2,897 residents were registered in Svalbard, according to Statistics Norway (SSB).
507763.subtitle_en: At the same time, Longyearbyen and Ny-Ålesund saw record-high in-migration.
507763.title_en: Never Have So Few People Lived in the Russian Settlements

507804.excerpt_en: In January this year, the Støre government announced a new white paper on Svalbard. The reason is that the government believes a comprehensive review of the framework for Svalbard policy is needed, so that the development of Svalbard and Longyearbyen aligns with climate change, increased activity and a new security situation in Europe.
507804.subtitle_en: The Key Lies at the National Level
507804.tags_en: innovation, value creation, business, head of business development, opinions
507804.title_en: The Key Lies at the National Level

507808.excerpt_en: When a person robbed the bank, the Governor mounted a major emergency response. But if someone misappropriates a couple of million kroner from public grant schemes in Svalbard, the Governor has neither the time nor the expertise to follow it up.
507808.tags_en: Longyearbyen Local Council, grants, opinions, Svalbardposten, Governor of Svalbard, business

507814.excerpt_en: Fingers hold the blue fabric. Small, firm stitches are sewn.
507814.subtitle_en: Fingers hold the blue fabric. Small, firm stitches are sewn. On Wednesday, four women from Longyearbyen will wear self-sewn Svalbard folk costumes. They will no doubt wave flags in red, white and blue.

507824.excerpt_en: Gustav Halsvik, general manager of ISS Renhold, has lived in Longyearbyen for 40 years. For just as long, he has campaigned for good working conditions for employees in the cleaning industry.
507824.subtitle_en: Gustav Halsvik, general manager of ISS Renhold, does not believe the companies in town operating illegally will change their practices unless forced to. There is simply too much money to be made, he says.
507824.tags_en: workers’ rights, General Application Act, news, business, working life

507839.excerpt_en: A full alarm was raised on Wednesday morning when a fire alarm went off in Nybyen after smoke developed in one of the buildings. According to acting fire chief Geir Hekne, it initially looked dramatic.
507839.subtitle_en: The fire service initially feared the smoke came from a fire that had started in one of the buildings, and responded with a full team of 18 people.
507839.title_en: Responded to Smoke Development in Nybyen

507843.excerpt_en: On 6 March this year, Trust Arktikugol once again applied to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for an exemption allowing goods to be sent from Russia to Barentsburg.
507843.subtitle_en: Trust Arktikugol received another exemption in March to import supplies to Barentsburg.
507843.tags_en: Barentsburg, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, brief
507843.title_en: Granted Another Exemption to Import Goods from Russia

507850.excerpt_en: “It’s really fun!” says Emmett De Alvarenga Våtvik (10) about the extra-creative days the pupils at Longyearbyen School have enjoyed.
507850.subtitle_en: For three days, fifth-, sixth- and seventh-graders have worked on various projects putting climate and the environment on the agenda.

511010.excerpt_en: BirdLife Svalbard contacted Svalbardposten as Svalbard is being cleared of rubbish and scrap. They have a clear request for the town’s residents: take an extra look before cleaning up. “Longyearbyen offers many different nesting sites for snow buntings.”
511010.subtitle_en: According to BirdLife Svalbard, snow buntings often build their nests in the most ingenious places. They are therefore urging people to pay extra attention when clearing their surroundings.
511010.tags_en: nesting season, BirdLife Svalbard, snow bunting, snowmobile, news
511010.title_en: “Snow buntings can build nests in some pretty crazy places”

511026.excerpt_en: “We’re really looking forward to it. We’ve finished everything that needed organising, so now only the fun part remains,” smiles library director Lars Holt.
511026.subtitle_en: On 3 September, the seventh edition of the six-day festival gets under way. The programme will feature music, film and debate—and, of course, plenty of literature.
511026.tags_en: news, Longyearbyen Public Library, Longyearbyen Literature Festival, literature festival, culture
511026.title_en: “Now we can look forward to it”

511049.excerpt_en: Lene Jeanette Dyngeland, general manager of Aktiv i friluft, was able to breathe a sigh of relief and smile a little more last week.
511049.subtitle_en: When time was running out to move the course, Aktiv i friluft urgently needed help. Assemblin was happy to oblige.
511049.tags_en: news, weather stations, Aktiv i friluft, frisbee, Assemblin
511049.title_en: Frisbee golf course gets a new location

511061.excerpt_en: This summer, the Norwegian Polar Institute was granted permission to ring and collect blood samples from 50 ivory gulls as part of population monitoring in the Arctic. They began the work in Longyearbyen on the 26th.
511061.subtitle_en: Ole Arve Misund, director of the Norwegian Polar Institute, believes Norwegian marine researchers do not have genuine access to Russian waters. At the same time, they are carrying out population monitoring of ivory gulls with a Russian research institute.
511061.tags_en: news, research, Barentsøya, Norwegian Polar Institute
511061.title_en: “We will maintain some contact with Russian researchers”

511065.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Maritime Authority informs Svalbardposten that the vessel Isbjørn 2, which ran aground in Borebukta on 22 May, is no longer being detained by the authority.
511065.subtitle_en: The vessel that ran aground in Borebukta on 22 May is now cleared to sail again.
511065.tags_en: news, Norwegian Maritime Authority, Borebukta, grounding

511092.excerpt_en: Svalbardposten speaks to two tired but happy young women on Wednesday morning after the weekend’s national festival of Ung Kultur Møtes, also known as UKM. Mia Ekeblad Eggenfellner and Aurora Nordtømme Uhlen are sitting at Oslo Airport, Gardermoen, waiting for their next flight north to Svalbard when we call.
511092.subtitle_en: Because of problems with baggage delivery, Mia Ekeblad Eggenfellner (17) and Aurora Nordtømme Uhlen’s (17) performance at UKM’s national final nearly became a one-woman show.
511092.tags_en: UKM, concert, Ung Kultur Møtes, national festival, news
511092.title_en: Luggage trouble nearly derailed UKM performance

511107.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard announced this on its website on Wednesday. Until now, employers or educational institutions have contacted the Governor of Svalbard about new residents who need an alcohol card.
511107.subtitle_en: From 1 July, newcomers must take responsibility for obtaining an alcohol card themselves. The Governor of Svalbard believes this will make things easier for everyone.
511107.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, alcohol, news, alcohol card

511133.excerpt_en: The German cruise ship Mein Schiff 4 arrived at Longyearbyen harbour on Thursday. A total of 2,384 guests arrived, and once the ship had docked and the gangway was down, it did not take long for a steady stream of German tourists to emerge.
511133.subtitle_en: With its 2,384 passengers, the Thursday call by Mein Schiff 4 was one of the biggest this summer. We were there when the ship docked.
511133.tags_en: Visit Svalbard, cruise tourism, Svalbard Cruise Forum, Svalbard Cruise Network, news, Longyearbyen harbour

511139.excerpt_en: During the night of 7 January last year, damage was discovered on one of the two fibre-optic cables from Svalbard to the mainland.
511139.subtitle_en: Last winter, a break in the power supply from one of the fibre-optic cables between Svalbard and the mainland was discovered. It will soon be fully repaired.

511146.excerpt_en: It was in mid-May that Svalbardposten first reported on Katharina Rise. At the time, she had just accepted the position as the new environmental protection chief with the Governor of Svalbard.
511146.subtitle_en: Katharina Rise was originally due to start as the new environmental protection chief in September. Instead, she will become the new deputy governor.
511146.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, deputy governor, news

511155.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard has announced that Katharina Rise will become the new deputy governor. She takes over from Sølvi Elvedahl, whose fixed-term appointment has now ended.
511155.subtitle_en: Rise was originally due to take up the position of environmental protection chief in September, but will instead become Lars Fause’s new deputy.
511155.title_en: Katharina Rise becomes new deputy governor

511227.excerpt_en: “We’re almost finished now!” says Krista Wright when Svalbardposten visits on Thursday afternoon.
511227.subtitle_en: Today, an exhibition about polar bears opens in the igloo just outside UNIS and the museum. Here, you can learn more about polar bears—and ask researchers questions as well.
511227.title_en: “We need to talk about the polar bear”

511244.excerpt_en: Senior police officer Carina Søreng of the Governor of Svalbard tells Svalbardposten that they received a report at 10:53 p.m. on Thursday about a person aboard the German cruise ship Mein Schiff 4 who needed to go to hospital. “It’s a woman who has fallen and injured herself.”
511244.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s helicopter had to be dispatched to Mein Schiff 4 on Thursday evening.
511244.tags_en: Longyearbyen Hospital, cruise, news, Governor of Svalbard

511256.excerpt_en: The three tourists were stopped at around 11:30 p.m. on Wednesday, says senior police officer Ingunn Iversen of the Governor of Svalbard. The tourists—all adult men—were standing near the centre of Longyearbyen, each flying a recreational drone.
511256.subtitle_en: Three tourists were stopped on Wednesday evening after flying their drones inside the no-fly zone. A criminal case has now been opened.

511260.excerpt_en: “A British tourist has already stopped by and tried them out, and it went very well.” Ragnhild Kommisrud, airport manager at Svalbard Airport, Longyear, says this as she stands in front of two brand-new check-in machines at Svalbardbutikken on Friday morning.
511260.subtitle_en: You no longer have to go to the airport to check in your luggage, but the airport manager is still worried that people will forget one important thing.
511260.title_en: You can now do this at the shop

511301.excerpt_en: According to the press release, the centre aims to bring together the world’s leading researchers on ice melt and carbon emissions, with the goal of filling knowledge gaps about how melting glaciers and ice caps affect the planet’s carbon budget and climate change.
511301.subtitle_en: In cooperation with the Norwegian Polar Institute and NORCE, UiT The Arctic University of Norway will establish a new research centre to study glaciers and ice caps.
511301.tags_en: news, ice, Norwegian Polar Institute, research
511301.title_en: Launching new research centre based in Tromsø

511323.excerpt_en: In March, Svalbardposten reported that Kristin Furu Grøtting, department head at Longyearbyen Hospital, was concerned about the hospital’s capacity this summer, when a large number of tourists were expected. The summer season is now well underway—so how is it going?
511323.subtitle_en: Older cruise tourists with health problems are causing considerable frustration at the hospital. Senior consultant Ole Tveiten says they have already had cases this summer in which patients barely survived.
511323.tags_en: health, tourism, Longyearbyen Hospital, news, cruise tourism
511323.title_en: Says cruise industry should require medical certificates

511326.excerpt_en: There has been considerable excitement about when the Stett would fall this year. After a weekend with what could reasonably be called summer temperatures on Svalbard, it was clear that the Svalbardposten newsroom had to watch the chute on Operafjellet more closely on Monday.
511326.subtitle_en: At 2 p.m. on Monday, it was confirmed that the Stett had officially come loose from the champagne glass—and summer had finally arrived.

511330.excerpt_en: There is not much left after Longyearbyen’s fire service burned down large parts of Sverdrupbyen in 1985. A few memories do remain, however.
511330.subtitle_en: According to the owner, the old Trafokiosken in Sverdrupbyen is too grey and boring. Now he wants to do something about it, provided Longyearbyen Local Council approves.
511330.tags_en: planning and building matters, Sverdrupbyen, news

511372.excerpt_en: The antenna, owned by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, was installed in the 1990s and put into use in 1994. It was used for VLBI measurements—that is, to map movements in the Earth’s crust.
511372.subtitle_en: A 20-metre-high parabolic dish has stood at Hamnerabben, the airport in Ny-Ålesund, since the 1990s. It will now be dismantled and removed.
511372.tags_en: Hamnerabben, news, Norwegian Mapping Authority, Ny-Ålesund, Earth observatory
511372.title_en: Antenna at Ny-Ålesund airport to be removed

511395.excerpt_en: On Monday evening, a very special delivery arrived at Statens hus in Longyearbyen. A parcel locker had arrived in the cargo hold of Posten’s fully electric lorry.
511395.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen’s latest addition to the post office has 14 compartments and is available 24/7.
511395.tags_en: Posten Norge, Posten, Longyearbyen Post Office, parcels, news
511395.title_en: Svalbard gets its very first parcel locker

511418.excerpt_en: Olise sounded somewhat surprised when she answered the phone as Svalbardposten called. “Huh, are you kidding?”
511418.subtitle_en: That was Olise Haugan’s reaction when she was told she had won this year’s Stetten competition.
511418.title_en: “Huh, are you kidding? Is it true?”

511439.excerpt_en: It has been discussed in the Facebook group “Ros og info i Longyearbyen” and internally in the Svalbardposten newsroom: Doesn’t the water taste a little strange these days?
511439.subtitle_en: Recently, tap water has had an almost earthy taste—and there is a good reason for it.
511439.tags_en: drinking water, Longyearbyen Local Council, news
511439.title_en: Why your water tastes so strange right now

511448.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard is now investigating breaches of the traffic ban at several nature reserves. These include Lovénøyane in Kongsfjorden and Gåsøyane in Billefjorden.
511448.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is investigating several breaches of the traffic ban at various bird reserves around Svalbard.
511448.tags_en: traffic ban, birdlife, Governor of Svalbard, news
511448.title_en: Investigating several breaches of the traffic ban

511458.excerpt_en: “The population is high this year,” says Åshild Ønvik Pedersen. She is a researcher at the Norwegian Polar Institute and responsible for the reindeer counts on Svalbard.
511458.subtitle_en: This summer’s reindeer count in Adventdalen is now complete. They found 1,694 animals—just seven fewer than the 2018 record.
511458.tags_en: Åshild Ønvik Pedersen, news, research, reindeer, Norwegian Polar Institute
511458.title_en: Almost a new record this year

511478.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard announced that several breaches of traffic bans in nature reserves on Svalbard were being investigated. The breaches allegedly occurred, among other places, near Lovénøyane in Kongsfjorden and Gåsøyane in Billefjorden, where the ban covers an area extending 300 metres out to sea.
511478.subtitle_en: From late May to early July, several vessels breached the traffic ban in various places across the archipelago. The chief of staff at the Governor’s Office says some of the incidents were connected to cruise traffic.
511478.tags_en: birds, Governor of Svalbard, news, traffic ban, nature reserves
511478.title_en: “Vessels linked to cruising, tourism and research”

511489.excerpt_en: While temperatures on Svalbard reached 14.5°C on Wednesday morning, Paris recorded 13.5°C—at least at 8 a.m. today.
511489.subtitle_en: At 8 a.m. on Wednesday, the temperature on Svalbard was measured at 14.5°C.
511489.title_en: Today it is warmer here than in Paris

511492.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, the Governor of Svalbard conducted traffic checks in Longyearbyen. At around 1 p.m., officers stopped a car near the airport, where a child was sitting on a passenger’s lap in the back seat.
511492.subtitle_en: Yesterday, the Governor of Svalbard discovered a car in which a small child was unsecured while the vehicle was moving.
511492.tags_en: road safety, news, Governor of Svalbard

511558.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council says that, if everything goes according to plan, the company will come up in August to lay asphalt in Longyearbyen.
511558.subtitle_en: Veidekke AS will arrive on August 15 to lay new asphalt and repair potholes.
511558.tags_en: Veidekke, road, news, Longyearbyen Local Council, paving
511558.title_en: Plans to pave roads in August

511632.excerpt_en: A preliminary report from the Norwegian Board of Health Supervision concludes that specialist health services connected to Svalbard are operating with an unacceptably high risk of failure.
511632.subtitle_en: Before Ottar Svensen died at Longyearbyen Hospital, warnings were issued several times that the air ambulance service could face resource shortages. His son, Remi Svensen, finds it infuriating that this proved decisive for his father.
511632.tags_en: Norwegian Board of Health Supervision, Longyearbyen Hospital, news, air ambulance service, Health North, air ambulance, emergency preparedness
511632.title_en: “To put it mildly, it makes me furious”

511670.excerpt_en: “It is important to study the area as it is now, while it is covered in ice. If the ice disappears, this will be particularly important for biology, because the area is very interesting biologically.”
511670.subtitle_en: The GoNorth research expedition is being carried out in the Arctic Ocean for the second time. This time, the team has brought a Norwegian ROV.
511670.tags_en: Molloy Deep, Kronprins Haakon, GoNorth, Gakkel Ridge, research vessel, research, ROV, news, expedition, Arctic Ocean
511670.title_en: Will send «Ægir» down to the Gakkel Ridge

511749.excerpt_en: A woman in her 20s has been convicted of violating the Road Traffic Act after, in the early hours of 30 December last year, causing a car to roll into a bench and then the window of Skinnboden, shattering it.
511749.subtitle_en: A woman in her 20s was convicted by Nord-Troms and Senja District Court of driving while impaired, despite being seated in the passenger seat.
511749.tags_en: traffic accident, court case, Governor of Svalbard, news
511749.title_en: Car rolled into shop window – convicted of careless driving

511765.excerpt_en: The daily update from the GoNorth expedition reports that a positioning instrument was damaged during an operation near the Molloy Deep on Sunday. Although the ship was built to conduct research in sea ice, the steel pipe carrying the instruments could not withstand colliding with a large chunk of ice.
511765.subtitle_en: The positioning equipment on «Kronprins Haakon» was damaged during the dive at the Molloy Deep. The research vessel must now head to Tromsø for repairs before the expedition can continue.
511765.tags_en: research vessel, Gakkel Ridge, news, SINTEF, Kronprins Haakon, expedition, GoNorth

511788.excerpt_en: “For a long time, I wanted to become a sign-language interpreter,” says Celine Ueland Anderssen, the leading candidate for Longyearbyen’s Conservative Party. She leans forward in her chair and demonstrates with her hands how to communicate with a person who is both deaf and blind.
511788.subtitle_en: The Yes Person Who Wants to Say No More Often
511788.tags_en: Svalbard Conservative Party, politics, news, 2023 local government elections, Community Council, election campaign, profile
511788.title_en: The Yes Person Who Wants to Say No More Often

511796.excerpt_en: For several years, regular METAR and TAF reports have been produced for Bjørnøya. While METAR provides observations of the actual weather at an airport or helicopter landing site, TAF is a forecast for the weather at the site itself, over a specific period and adapted to aviation and airport operations.
511796.subtitle_en: Since 2014, the meteorological station on Bjørnøya has provided direct weather observations for use in aviation. Now the service is being discontinued.
511796.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, news, weather forecasting, Bjørnøya, Norwegian Meteorological Institute
511796.title_en: Governor concerned about reduced weather forecasting

511813.excerpt_en: On Monday, Svalbardposten wrote about the supervisory case following the air ambulance incident, in which more than eight hours passed from the air ambulance being requested until it landed in Longyearbyen. In its preliminary report, the Norwegian Board of Health Supervision concludes that specialist health services in Svalbard operate with too great a risk of failure.
511813.subtitle_en: Governor of Svalbard Lars Fause makes clear that there can be no guarantees that people will receive necessary medical care. Nevertheless, he believes it is important to once again raise the challenges of onward transport to the mainland.
511813.tags_en: news, emergency preparedness, air ambulance, Helse Nord, Governor of Svalbard, Norwegian Board of Health Supervision, Longyearbyen Hospital
511813.title_en: “There is no guarantee we can get an air ambulance here”

511831.excerpt_en: “Longyearbyen Local Council has investigated whether this could affect children in Longyearbyen.”
511831.subtitle_en: Several concern reports sent by the police through the Altinn service have not reached the municipalities and child welfare services on the mainland. So far, this does not appear to apply to Svalbard.
511831.tags_en: child welfare, Governor of Svalbard, news, Norwegian Police Directorate, Longyearbyen Local Council, police
511831.title_en: Governor: “We have a good overview of the reports we forward”

511842.excerpt_en: This article expresses the writer’s personal views. Endless landscapes of snow, ice and rock, fjords with calving glaciers and the occasional polar bear. Svalbard’s natural environment has a powerful attraction for many of us, but it is now under pressure.
511842.subtitle_en: Tourism in Svalbard is booming, but rapid climate change and stricter rules on travel to protect nature loom on the horizon. The latter may make it harder for the tourism industry to adapt.

511872.excerpt_en: “Being a guide is no easy job. It is challenging both mentally and physically, and you are responsible for people’s lives, especially here in Svalbard.”
511872.subtitle_en: Franka Leiterer of the Svalbard Guide Association hopes the work to develop guide certification is done thoroughly enough—and that the guide association’s views are heard.
511872.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, field safety regulations, news, guides, guide certification

511913.excerpt_en: The resident man in his 60s is now charged with making threats against a younger woman inside Karlsberger Pub. The incident allegedly took place on the premises in the early hours of Saturday, the 28th.
511913.subtitle_en: The man in his 60s must now appear before the district court after threatening a woman and borrowing firearms requiring registration without permission.
511913.tags_en: weapons, court case, news, Nord-Troms and Senja District Court, Governor of Svalbard, threats
511913.title_en: Shouted “I’m going to kill you” at woman in bar

511927.excerpt_en: Last Thursday, Joachim Buerskog and his girlfriend travelled back to Norway from a holiday in Italy. That was when a situation arose that they had not entirely anticipated.
511927.subtitle_en: When Joachim Buerskog, 25, returned from holiday, his luggage failed to appear. This created unexpected problems with his insurance company.

511950.excerpt_en: “It’s difficult to make an issue of this, because these are valuable customers of the shopping centre, and we want to give them the best possible experience of Longyearbyen. But we now feel that the burden and costs this places on us have become too great.”
511950.subtitle_en: Lompensenteret has to spend large sums cleaning toilets when the town fills with tourists. Now the shopping-centre manager is calling for better solutions in the town centre.
511950.tags_en: news, Longyearbyen Local Council, cruise, Lompensenteret
511950.title_en: “1,500 people use the toilets in a day”

512040.excerpt_en: On Tuesday morning, the Governor of Svalbard’s office issued a press release announcing that it had appointed a new head of environmental protection. This follows Katharina Rise taking up the position earlier this spring, before accepting a job as deputy governor shortly afterwards.
512040.subtitle_en: “I’m looking forward to finding out how we will tackle the challenges,” says Bente Rønning, the Governor of Svalbard’s new head of environmental protection.
512040.tags_en: climate, news, Governor of Svalbard, head of environmental protection, environmental protection
512040.title_en: Governor of Svalbard appoints new head of environmental protection

article_keywords_en: senior police officer with the Governor of Svalbard
512050.excerpt_en: It was around 3 a.m. on Tuesday that the Governor’s office was notified that a party had become a little too loud. It was at an address in Elvesletta.
512050.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard’s office had to respond to a party that became a little too lively early Tuesday morning.
512050.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, news, disorderly conduct
512050.title_en: Responded to noise complaint at party

512135.excerpt_en: In March, the Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority visited Kongsberg Satellite Services (KSAT), Svalbard branch (Svalsat). This resulted in seven orders being issued to the company – all related to health, safety and environmental work (HSE).
512135.subtitle_en: Earlier this year, the Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority carried out an inspection at Svalsat that resulted in several orders. Outgoing station manager Maja-Stina Ekstedt says they were prepared for deviations to be found.
512135.tags_en: KSAT, Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority, news, Svalsat
512135.title_en: Multiple violations of the Working Environment Act at Svalsat

512145.excerpt_en: See the extensive photo series at the bottom of the article. Two weeks.
512145.subtitle_en: For two weeks, the three friends have embarked on a particularly creative journey.
512145.title_en: “Fascinating to experience nature between winter and summer”

512195.excerpt_en: At 2 p.m. on Saturday, an official memorial ceremony for 22 July was held outside the church, with speeches and singing.
512195.subtitle_en: Today marks twelve years since the terrorist attacks in Oslo and on Utøya. The anniversary was commemorated at the memorial outside the church.

512317.excerpt_en: So far this summer, bird flu has been confirmed in four dead birds. They were found in connection with fieldwork.
512317.subtitle_en: Last year, bird flu was detected in Svalbard for the first time. This summer, dead birds carrying the virus have also been found.
512317.tags_en: Norwegian Polar Institute, birds, birdlife, news, bird flu, Kongsfjorden
512317.title_en: Bird flu confirmed in Svalbard again this year

512331.excerpt_en: For several years, it has been known that the ground at the old fire-training site is contaminated by several different fluorinated substances, known as PFAS. In February this year, the Norwegian Environment Agency decided that Avinor should be made responsible for the cleanup.
512331.subtitle_en: “There will be increased heavy traffic on the roads in connection with the work,” says airport director Ragnhild Kommisrud.
512331.title_en: Cleanup begins at old fire-training site

512403.excerpt_en: “It looks like you’ve had a lovely, warm summer,” says Hanne Heiberg, climate duty officer in the Climate Services Department at the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, when Svalbardposten calls to talk about, yes, the weather.
512403.subtitle_en: It has been an exceptionally dry July so far this year. There have not been so few clouds over the town since 1976. But that may be about to change – just before the end of the month.
512403.tags_en: news, weather, Norwegian Meteorological Institute, climate
512403.title_en: So far, the driest July since 1998

512539.excerpt_en: “The airport is like an ecosystem,” says airport director Ragnhild Kommisrud, continuing: “We are completely dependent on everyone who works here.” She is referring to those who work in the control tower.
512539.tags_en: news, Avinor, Svalbard Airport, airport, summer job, airport director

512598.excerpt_en: The Alien Species List provides an overview of species that are not naturally native to Norway and the risk they pose to biodiversity. The aim of the list is to support knowledge-based management of nature.
512598.subtitle_en: Every five years, the Norwegian Biodiversity Information Centre publishes a new Alien Species List. The previous list was released in 2018—and a new one is now in place.
512598.title_en: “More species will establish themselves in Svalbard as the climate warms”

512700.excerpt_en: “We received the report at 6:40 p.m.,” says senior police officer Bjørn Inge Knudsen of the Governor of Svalbard’s office. He says a tourist was standing on the walkway by the Radisson and flying a drone at an altitude of 465 metres on Saturday evening.
512700.subtitle_en: On Saturday evening, yet another tourist was caught flying a drone inside the no-fly zone. This time, it happened while a plane was approaching to land.
512700.title_en: Flew drone as plane was approaching – fined NOK 18,000

512724.excerpt_en: On July 24, six scouts from Longyearbyen traveled to South Korea to attend the international Jamboree scout camp, held every four years in a selected country.
512724.subtitle_en: Six scouts from Longyearbyen have traveled to South Korea to attend an international scout camp.
512724.title_en: Scouts from Longyearbyen travel to South Korea

512746.excerpt_en: In a letter to the Russian mining company Trust Arktikugol, the Governor of Svalbard writes that it has learned the company has put up signs or notices on buildings in Nordenskiöld Land incorporating the Governor of Svalbard’s emblem or seal.
512746.subtitle_en: It may not use the Governor of Svalbard’s emblem.

512761.excerpt_en: At the end of May, Karoline Bælum and Rico Behlke announced in a Facebook post that they were considering selling the trapping station Farmhamna in Forlandsundet. The post states, among other things, that the buyer must be approved by the Governor of Svalbard and that the station must operate as a trapping station.
512761.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard will not pre-approve potential buyers, but refers to the requirement for overwintering trapping.
512761.tags_en: Governor of Svalbard, trapping life, trapping station, Farmhamna, overwintering trapping, news

512779.excerpt_en: On Wednesday last week, climate watch officer Hanne Heiberg of the Norwegian Meteorological Institute told Svalbardposten that temperatures so far in July had been 3.4 degrees above normal—and that the average July temperature was currently 10.3 degrees.
512779.subtitle_en: Last week, meteorologists reported that it had so far been the warmest July since 2000. Now the record has been broken.
512779.title_en: Svalbard set a July temperature record

512787.excerpt_en: Five small boats took part as Russian officials honored the country’s navy on July 30, The Independent Barents Observer reports.
512787.subtitle_en: On Sunday, Russian Consul General Andrei Chemerilo led a naval parade in the waters off Barentsburg.

512802.excerpt_en: The dissolution of the Soviet Union brought geopolitical changes that had major consequences for marine research communities in the north. From the late 1980s, several major research programs were developed involving Polish and Russian institutions and researchers.
512802.subtitle_en: Cooperation between the Polish Institute of Oceanography and research communities in Tromsø and Svalbard.
512802.tags_en: research, research vessel, oceanography, cooperation, Norwegian Polar Institute, UNIS, opinions

512826.excerpt_en: Robin was first married to Torun, and they both worked for SNSK. Together with his second wife, Nina, he built up Arctic Wilderness Experience in Bolterdalen.
512826.subtitle_en: Robin Buzza was passionately concerned with nature and the environment—almost a wild man who fled civilization and modernity.

512846.excerpt_en: It was Longyearbyen Local Council that alerted the Governor of Svalbard shortly after 2:30 p.m. Wednesday, says chief inspector Silje Høysæter. Considering closing road. The Governor of Svalbard now asks people to exercise caution.
512846.subtitle_en: At around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday, the Governor of Svalbard was alerted that two large rocks had fallen near the cemetery.
512846.tags_en: avalanche risk, weather, Governor of Svalbard, landslide, rain, news
512846.title_en: Two large rocks have fallen near the cemetery

512882.excerpt_en: On Wednesday morning, the Governor of Svalbard contacted the captain of a large cruise ship after it sailed inside the restricted zone at the southern tip of Bear Island Nature Reserve. Chief inspector Taina Maria Schogster Bjørkås of the Governor of Svalbard’s office says so.
512882.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, a cruise ship sailed inside the restricted zone at the southern tip of Bear Island Nature Reserve. The captain claims he did not know sailing in the area was prohibited.
512882.tags_en: Bear Island, Governor of Svalbard, news, nature reserve, traffic ban, cruise ship

512893.excerpt_en: On Wednesday afternoon, the Governor of Svalbard reported that two large rocks had fallen near the cemetery. Because heavy rain had been forecast, chief inspector Silje Høysæter said they would assess today, Thursday, whether to close the road and the area above it.
512893.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard is taking no further action after yesterday’s rockfall.
