530868.excerpt_en: Abandoning coal as an energy source on Svalbard was driven by political idealism. The gain in reduced carbon dioxide emissions will probably be less than 25 percent.

530899.excerpt_en: On Friday and Saturday, 15 films are lined up for screenings on the big screen at both Nordover Cinema and the cultural centre. That is when this year’s Arctic Film Festival in Longyearbyen gets under way.
530899.subtitle_en: Fifteen independent films will be shown at this year’s Arctic Film Festival. Several of them are set in or inspired by Svalbard.
530899.tags_en: film festival, Arctic Film Festival, Longyearbyen, independent cinema, climate change, news

530907.excerpt_en: On Tuesday afternoon, they set off up Todalen in their respective large grooming machines. They will be working almost around the clock until Saturday to create “tram tracks” for this year’s most beautiful skiing adventure. “Now we’re grooming the course and removing bumps and hollows.”
530907.subtitle_en: The grooming machines are at work. Before the start on Saturday morning, Knut Fastvold and Ove Hagen guarantee that the course for this year’s ski marathon will be in top shape.
530907.tags_en: Svalbard Turn, grooming machines, volunteers, skiing adventure, news, ski marathon
530907.title_en: This is where the ski tracks will go

530956.excerpt_en: On Friday, 15 March, one of the engines at our backup power plant blew up.

530988.excerpt_en: On social media and in conversations around town, it has been strongly insinuated that the Governor of Svalbard dropped the case to prevent the actual cause of death from emerging. “We have nothing to hide.”
530988.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard has listened to input and reactions from several quarters, but will not reopen the investigation into how the polar bear sow “Frost” died.
530988.tags_en: news, Governor of Svalbard, investigation, Svalbard, polar bear, cause of death

530992.excerpt_en: In December, the Community Council decided that residents would be shielded from higher energy costs, while the four largest consumers would foot the bill for everyone. The Ministry of Justice decided on 7.
530992.subtitle_en: Next week, the Community Council will decide what residents must pay for the electricity they have used so far this year. Overall prices have risen by at least 75 percent. “Challenging,” says Community Council leader Terje Aunevik.

531010.excerpt_en: During the Community Council meeting, the three appeals concerning the cork money were considered, after the Local Community, Childhood and Culture Committee (LOKU) rejected them in March (see fact box). When Fred Skancke Hansen of the Liberal Party briefed the Community Council on the matter, he said a meeting had been held with the appellants.
531010.subtitle_en: Those waiting for a final answer on what will happen to the cork money will have to wait a little longer.
531010.tags_en: news, politics, community council, cork money, appeals, Culture Committee

531014.excerpt_en: The project to establish a maintenance hall and warehouse at the port is now moving forward, after politicians temporarily halted it last autumn.
531014.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, Community Council politicians approved an expansion of the port. If all goes according to plan, the building could be ready by next winter.
531014.title_en: Gets approval to build maintenance hall and warehouse at the port

531108.excerpt_en: Next week, Liv Gulbrandsen will come to Longyearbyen with Riksteatret. The play “Shut Up, It’s Ibsen!”, normally performed at the National Theatre, will now be staged at the cultural centre.
531108.subtitle_en: Liv Gulbrandsen has never been to Svalbard before and is terrified of polar bears. On Thursday, she is coming to Longyearbyen to talk about Ibsen.
531108.title_en: “I can talk people’s ears off, but I don’t know if that will work against a polar bear”

531149.excerpt_en: In March this year, Longyearbyen had 6,373 arriving guests who generated 17,064 guest nights, compared with 6,196 guests in March last year, who generated 16,515 guest nights. The industry’s latest first-quarter figures also show that the number of tourists from Norway visiting the archipelago is falling.
531149.subtitle_en: The number of tourists so far this year is slightly up on last year. But what pleases the tourism industry most is that each tourist is staying in town longer. And profitability in the industry is significantly better than on the mainland.
531149.tags_en: Longyearbyen, guest nights, tourism, Svalbard, news, travel industry

531165.excerpt_en: “We are proud, happy and a little surprised. I think it’s fantastic.”
531165.subtitle_en: Svalbard Museum is one of three museums in the country that could be named Museum of the Year.
531165.title_en: “We are proud, happy and a little surprised”

531199.excerpt_en: It is a decidedly cheerful group who stop for a chat just after boarding the train from Lillehammer, following this year’s Amandus Festival.
531199.subtitle_en: Agnes Zadewasser received both the Youth Jury Award and the prestigious Audience Award for the short film “Amanda” at this year’s festival.
531199.title_en: Svalbard resident wins two awards at the Amandus Festival

531203.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, politicians will decide what residents and businesses in Longyearbyen will pay for electricity in 2024. The administration of the Longyearbyen Community Council recommends the new energy-fee scheme proposed by Svalbard Energi.
531203.subtitle_en: The biggest increase will be for private residents, and a smaller one for large business customers. This is one consequence of the proposal that the Longyearbyen Community Council’s administration is recommending to politicians.

531236.excerpt_en: The Svalbard Ski Marathon has been postponed by one hour on Saturday, from 9 to 10 a.m. The reason is safety assessments.
531236.subtitle_en: Wind and drifting snow are increasing the avalanche danger. The organisers have a Plan B ready.
531236.tags_en: Svalbard Ski Marathon, course changes, news, safety assessments, ski race, avalanche danger
531236.title_en: Ski marathon postponed—avalanche assessment Saturday morning

531249.excerpt_en: “We had personnel from UNIS conduct an inspection from a helicopter. In addition, we carried out an assessment by snowmobile.”
531249.subtitle_en: Following this morning’s avalanche assessments, Svalbard Turn has deemed the marathon course safe.

531256.excerpt_en: A fresh wind blew through the starting area below Todalen, and the advertising pennants fluttered incessantly. Sales of cold drinks in front of the lavvu were rather poor, but inside, in the warmth, it was popular to be. “This is absolutely fantastic.”
531256.subtitle_en: Biting wind and temperatures of minus 12 did not dampen this year’s ski marathon. “A great experience,” says Olympic champion Olaf Tufte, who started in position one.

531276.excerpt_en: “We have a tour group on Flatbreen, where one person has run into difficulties and cannot continue. We tried to retrieve the person yesterday evening, but the weather was simply too poor,” says Governor’s first constable Thomas Antonsen.
531276.subtitle_en: The group has been waiting for assistance from the Governor of Svalbard since Friday evening because one person is unable to continue under their own power. It is not considered an emergency.
531276.title_en: Tour group stranded by weather on Flatbreen

531288.excerpt_en: In brilliant sunshine and a slight headwind, this year’s participants raced across the finish line in Todalen. Despite the race starting with a biting wind in their faces, several ski-marathon participants said that was no longer the case once they rounded the first bend. “I’m absolutely delighted with today’s race.”
531288.subtitle_en: There was both biting wind and brilliant sunshine for participants in this year’s ski marathon. But that did not stop most of them from flying into the home straight with the wind at their backs.
531288.title_en: Soleng Skinstad races to marathon victory

531388.excerpt_en: “The person who was unable to continue the trip independently was transported to Longyearbyen this morning,” says duty Governor’s first constable Thomas Antonsen. He says the helicopter landed in Longyearbyen just before 9 a.m., after the weather had improved enough for them to retrieve the man.
531388.subtitle_en: The man had been waiting for assistance from the Governor of Svalbard at Flatbreen since Friday evening, together with the organised tour group. He was back in Longyearbyen on Sunday morning.
531388.title_en: Ski tourist rescued in the early morning

531414.excerpt_en: The sixth-graders have barely started their lesson when we interrupt them for a chat.
531414.subtitle_en: Just before Easter, a major leak was discovered at Longyearbyen School. As a result, the sixth-graders have temporarily become high-school students.
531414.tags_en: leak, repairs, school, teaching, Longyearbyen, news
531414.title_en: Sewage water seeped into classroom walls and floors

531450.excerpt_en: So far this year, the Governor of Svalbard’s rescue service has responded to 22 missions. Last year, the rescue service had 86 assignments, while there were 69 callouts in 2022.
531450.subtitle_en: The rescue service wants people to use it. They say it is better to respond once too often than to lose lives. Even saving a frozen hand can be extremely important.
531450.title_en: “Ask for Help Rather Than Suffer Permanent Injury”

531462.excerpt_en: State Secretary Sindre Lysø (Labour) is leading the Norwegian delegation. In a press release from the Norwegian Polar Institute, he says the purpose of the visit is to examine how cooperation between the countries can be developed and strengthened.
531462.subtitle_en: The Ministry of Education and Research has invited the French and German ministers responsible for higher education and research to Ny-Ålesund to discuss closer cooperation on polar research.
531462.title_en: German and French ministers visit Ny-Ålesund

531471.excerpt_en: “It turned out that the school was not in such bad shape at all, considering its age. Much better than we may have feared,” says principal Frode Westby Thorstad.
531471.subtitle_en: Last year, Rambøll conducted a major survey to assess the school’s technical condition. The foundations still need to be inspected.
531471.tags_en: maintenance, school, renovation, building inspection, news, infrastructure

531534.excerpt_en: During Easter, Svalbardposten told the story of Svalbard’s first snowmobile. Miner Martin Barlund was a jack-of-all-trades who assembled parts from a Tempo moped, a drive wheel, some tracks and much more.
531534.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s first snowmobile could have been the beginning of an industrial success story. Mine worker Martin Barlund’s counterparts in Canada founded BRP, now the world’s largest snowmobile manufacturer.
531534.tags_en: Svalbard, innovation, industrial history, snowmobile, news, mechanics
531534.title_en: “It Could Have Become an Industrial Success Story”

531538.excerpt_en: Svein Jonny Albrigtsen, leader of Svalbard Labour, elaborates that he and the party’s members now believe the process moved too quickly. “When we decided last autumn to switch to operating on diesel, we should have put a stop to it and let the coal-fired power plant run until everything was in place…”
531538.subtitle_en: A week before the extraordinary fee meeting, Svein Jonny Albrigtsen took the floor and apologised for the Labour Party voting to switch off the coal-fired power plant. “I can only apologise on behalf of our party for having helped decide on this transition too quickly.”
531538.title_en: “We should have put a stop to it”

531547.excerpt_en: For ptarmigan researcher Eva Fuglei of the Norwegian Polar Institute, what is happening is encouraging. She has followed the ptarmigan’s development for many years, and the population is now more robust than it has been in a very long time. “The population is growing, and the most important reason is that winter temperatures in Svalbard are rising.”
531547.subtitle_en: Slightly milder winters and slightly less hunting are creating a brighter future for the Svalbard ptarmigan. These days, males and females are gathering for courtship.

531555.excerpt_en: On Saturday, a total of 107 dogs will be harnessed in front of sleds and skis before the starting gun goes for this year’s longest sled-dog race, Trappers Trail. The route is approximately 70 kilometers long, and the race takes place over two days. “We are pleasantly surprised by the high number of participants this year and are looking forward to the weekend!”
531555.subtitle_en: Among the goals and strategies of those standing at the back of the sleds are avoiding unauthorized mating on the trail and reaching the finish before the sun goes down.
531555.title_en: 20 Teams Line Up at the Start

531564.excerpt_en: Following this weekend’s Norwegian Youth and Junior Championships, Svalbard resident Sander Higraff, aged 16, can now call himself the Norwegian youth champion.
531564.subtitle_en: Sander Higraff, 16, set two new Norwegian records in his weight class while earning the title of Norway’s best at this weekend’s Norwegian Youth and Junior Powerlifting Championships. Two other Svalbard residents also celebrated strong placements at the championships.

531595.excerpt_en: The live broadcast is streamed via Longyearbyen Local Council’s municipal TV service. Svalbardposten therefore has no control over the technical aspects of the broadcast.
531595.subtitle_en: On Wednesday, politicians held their extraordinary meeting to set new energy tariffs.
531595.title_en: Watch a Recording of the Meeting on Energy Fees Here

531605.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Meteorological Institute issued its warning about the expected bad weather through the messaging service X, formerly Twitter.
531605.subtitle_en: “Batten down the hatches,” the Norwegian Meteorological Institute wrote on X. A low-pressure system is expected to move in from the west on Thursday, followed by strong winds on Friday.
531605.title_en: Could Be a Gale—or a Full-Blown Storm—on Friday

531618.excerpt_en: On Wednesday, the Local Council met to adopt new energy fees after the December decision was declared invalid by the Ministry of Justice. Energy costs for Longyearbyen have roughly doubled, from NOK 130 million when the town operated on coal in 2023 to NOK 269 million this year.
531618.subtitle_en: Politicians are prioritizing households over businesses. For larger customers, the electricity price will rise by 82 percent.
531618.title_en: Chooses Energy Fees That Shield Households Most

531628.excerpt_en: Longyearbyen Local Council wrote this on its website on Wednesday. The water will be shut off between 8 and 10 a.m. Thursday while components in the drinking-water network are being replaced.
531628.subtitle_en: On Thursday, Longyearbyen Local Council will shut off the water for two hours.
531628.title_en: Water to Be Shut Off Thursday in Haugen and Several Areas of Lia

531641.excerpt_en: Years of planning, testing, trial and error, and investment have now been rewarded. Competing against solar parks from across the country, Isfjord Radio won the Solar Energy Cluster industry association’s top award and was named installation of the year.
531641.subtitle_en: The green energy solution at Isfjord Radio has won a national award. The experience from the solar-cell installation will now be used to create green energy for SvalSat on Platåberget.

531729.excerpt_en: In January, the organizations NOAH and OneWhale applied to move the beluga whale to Svalbard and introduce him to others of his species. The Norwegian Environment Agency says no, partly following advice from the Norwegian Polar Institute.
531729.subtitle_en: The Norwegian Environment Agency believes it would be too dangerous to introduce “Hvaldimir” to the Svalbard population. It is concerned about infectious diseases.

531740.excerpt_en: The intense itching also means the foxes do not prioritize feeding. In 2019, the previously unknown fur louse was discovered on the first foxes in Svalbard.
531740.subtitle_en: The unusual louse attacking Arctic foxes in Svalbard is having serious consequences. The foxes scratch their necks and backs so much that they may lose their crucial winter insulation.
531740.tags_en: Arctic fox, wildlife, Svalbard, Norwegian Polar Institute, polar fox, fur louse, fur, occurrence
531740.title_en: Blood-Sucking Lice Cause Itching and Problems for Arctic Foxes

531758.excerpt_en: The airport in Longyearbyen is getting a new energy solution. In the future, the airport will use liquefied biogas as its energy carrier.
531758.subtitle_en: Svalbard Airport, Longyear, will temporarily be operated on liquefied biogas.

531767.excerpt_en: The fund’s board also believes it is high time to increase the environmental fee paid by people traveling to Svalbard. Since its launch in 2007, NOK 150 has been collected from air and cruise passengers through their tickets, allowing the fund to distribute nearly NOK 20 million annually.
531767.subtitle_en: Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund is distributing almost NOK 20 million this year. Chair Pål Prestrud hopes for an increase in the environmental fee and more applications from individuals and groups with good ideas.
531767.title_en: “Time to Raise the Environmental Fee to at Least NOK 250”

531775.excerpt_en: Recently, the sea ice has come and gone. At times it has been almost thick and solid; at others, nearly transparently thin. “On Wednesday, we were tipped off that a man was walking on the ice.”
531775.subtitle_en: Police remind people that the ice on the fjord is in no way safe. They advise against such risky walking.
531775.tags_en: dangers of walking on ice, sea ice, safety, news, Chief of Police First Sergeant Magnar Silseth, police

531833.excerpt_en: Dear Longyearbyen, all over the world there are children and young people with different challenges that mean they need special-needs education at school. Our small Longyearbyen is no exception.
531833.subtitle_en: How can the Longyearbyen Local Council be proud of its diversity and use it as a resource when it denies some of its most vulnerable members access to schooling? asks the Longyearbyen Youth Council.
531833.tags_en: Local Council, special-needs education, diversity, Longyearbyen, opinions, school

531837.excerpt_en: “At 8:48 a.m., my manager called and told me that Store Norske had to send 1 megawatt of power to the town from then on and at least until Monday evening.”
531837.subtitle_en: On Friday morning, Mine 7 was asked to help supply electricity to Longyearbyen. The reason is reportedly that yet another one of Svalbard Energi’s engines has stopped.
531837.title_en: Mine 7 Supplies Power to the Town

531842.excerpt_en: “It is not too late. There is still time to take the right steps, but they must be taken quickly,” says Franziska Hasenburg, one of the driving forces behind the event and an active participant in the Arctic Climate Action Svalbard project.
531842.subtitle_en: Today, climate strikes are taking place in numerous countries. In Longyearbyen, there will be a protest march this afternoon, along with professional talks on how we can save the planet together.
531842.title_en: Striking Today to Save the Planet

531883.excerpt_en: The latest figures from Statistics Norway show that the authorities’ goal of strengthening the Norwegian presence is not reflected in the population statistics. The proportion of Norwegian citizens in Longyearbyen is now 64.0 percent, and according to Statistics Norway, a lower Norwegian share has never previously been recorded.
531883.subtitle_en: Over the past ten years, Longyearbyen and Ny-Ålesund have gained 500 residents. Foreign nationals account for 96 percent of the increase. There are now 2,617 people in the Norwegian settlements—a record high.
531883.title_en: Longyearbyen Has Never Had So Many Residents

531917.excerpt_en: In February, Svalbard Labour Party was due to travel to Oslo to try to secure electricity support. By then, the administration of Longyearbyen Local Council had sent a letter to the Ministry of Justice with input for the revised national budget. “We said we would very much like to see what costs were involved.”
531917.subtitle_en: Local politicians are responsible for running Longyearbyen. Nevertheless, they were not informed about increases in energy costs or what must be done to ensure an adequate backup supply.
531917.title_en: “As Long as We Have Overall Responsibility, We Should Be Told What’s Going On”

531943.excerpt_en: Because of the weather and avalanche danger, Trappers Trail is postponing the start until Saturday afternoon and changing the race route.
531943.subtitle_en: Trappers Trail participants will not tackle the feared Fardalsbakken hill this year.
531943.tags_en: Svalbard, sled-dog race, dog team, news, avalanche danger, Trappers Trail, weather conditions, dog sledding

article_keywords_en: senior police officer at the Governor’s Office
532006.excerpt_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified of the incident at 2:30 p.m. Saturday.
532006.subtitle_en: “Polarfront” has run aground near Diabas with 12 passengers and a crew of 13.

532020.excerpt_en: Saturday featured howling, happy dogs, sleds, pulks, race numbers and many spectators on the flat ground beyond the town kennel. A total of 18 teams set off on Trappers Trail—the year’s longest dog-sled race.
532020.subtitle_en: The first teams are expected to reach the finish around 11 a.m. Sunday.

532069.excerpt_en: On Sunday morning, the Governor of Svalbard was notified that there were people on the ice in Adventfjorden who appeared to be having trouble finding a route back to shore. This is according to Governor’s Office officer Bjørn Inge Knutsen. “This is not the time to go out on the ice.”
532069.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard was notified that people on the sea ice were having trouble getting back to shore.
532069.title_en: “This is not the time to go out on the ice”

532075.excerpt_en: Embla Abild, 16, and the dogs were the first team across the finish line. When she set the anchor and walked over to cuddle the lead dogs, the tears came.
532075.subtitle_en: Embla Abild, 16, thought for a long time that she would not be able to compete. On Sunday, she sped across the finish line in Trappers Trail.

532109.excerpt_en: “I was lucky there,” says Tommy Jordbrudal after the results were announced on Sunday evening. His wife Janne Søreide and the eight dogs of Husky Travellers completed the first leg and had the fastest time on Saturday.
532109.subtitle_en: Tommy Jordbrudal feared he would have to sleep on the sofa because he was unable to match the strong time his wife Janne Søreide posted on the first leg. Now he can breathe a sigh of relief.
532109.title_en: Didn’t have to sleep on the sofa after all

532127.excerpt_en: The Joint Rescue Coordination Centre for Northern Norway received word of the Danish sailing ship “Linden” at 8:17 a.m. Monday. They report that there was a minor fire onboard and that the vessel began taking on water in connection with the fire. “The fire has been extinguished and the situation is reportedly under control.”
532127.subtitle_en: According to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre, the sailing ship is now heading for Longyearbyen. The vessel is being escorted by KV “Svalbard” after a fire broke out onboard Monday morning and it began taking on water.
532127.title_en: Danish sailing ship takes on water after onboard fire

532141.excerpt_en: Just over 3,000 tonnes of waste from the coal-fired power plant have been deposited here every year since 2018. The possible environmentally harmful chemicals contained in the material remain somewhat uncertain.
532141.subtitle_en: There are strong indications that the landfill for slag and ash from the coal-fired power plant is leaking. The Norwegian Environment Agency is taking the matter seriously and has requested measurements of the contents and an explanation of what is happening.
532141.title_en: Suspects landfill is leaking environmental toxins

532170.excerpt_en: On Tuesday, Tio Monchos’ liquor licence will once again be considered by the Technical, Environment and Business Committee. The background is that the company’s general manager and owner, Andreas Styrsell, has terminated the contract to operate the café at the cultural centre.
532170.subtitle_en: Tio Monchos has terminated its contract at the cultural centre but may consider continuing if granted an extended liquor licence.
532170.title_en: Will close down unless liquor licence is extended

532174.excerpt_en: On Monday, it became clear that the Jektefart Museum in Bodø is Museum of the Year 2024, according to a press release from the Museums Association. Svalbard Museum had also been nominated for the award. “The Jektefart Museum greatly impressed the jury.”
532174.subtitle_en: Svalbard Museum was one of three nominees for Museum of the Year 2024.
532174.title_en: Fell just short of the top prize

532192.excerpt_en: A foreign national has been charged in Nord-Troms and Senja District Court with making threats and negligent handling of a firearm. According to the indictment, the tourist allegedly threatened the hosts at a tourist cabin on Monday last week.
532192.subtitle_en: The man is now charged in connection with two separate incidents last week.
532192.title_en: Man charged with threats and accidental discharge

532201.excerpt_en: There was no debate when the Technical, Environment and Business Committee considered Tio Monchos’ request for an extended liquor licence on Tuesday. They all agreed that the case presentation was sound.
532201.subtitle_en: The Technical, Environment and Business Committee believes Tio Monchos can point to good experience with alcohol service and unanimously sent the matter on to the Local Council for consideration.
532201.title_en: Gets first-round approval to serve more alcohol

532209.excerpt_en: Jon Aars, together with a veterinarian and other specialists, spent a month on an expedition examining the condition of polar bears. This is done regularly, allowing researchers to compare the condition of the same bears from year to year.
532209.subtitle_en: Unusually large amounts of sea ice are creating good conditions for polar bears. “The ones we have examined are doing well, and the area where they can now hunt seals is enormous,” says polar bear researcher Jon Aars.
532209.title_en: A good winter for polar bears

532216.excerpt_en: “It’s about a girl who has just started at a new school. She meets a boy during the ski holiday and finds out that she is going to start at the same school as him.”
532216.subtitle_en: There has been intensive rehearsal activity at the cultural centre both in the evenings and at weekends over the past week. On Wednesday, East High the Musical opens.
532216.title_en: The School of Music and Arts stages a musical

532225.excerpt_en: The Norwegian Maritime Authority says that “Polarfront” has been permitted to continue sailing after running aground between Deltaneset and Diabas on Saturday afternoon.
532225.subtitle_en: While “Polarfront” has been given the all-clear to continue sailing after running aground at the weekend, “Linden” is still waiting for its inspection to be completed.
532225.title_en: One cleared to sail on, the other awaits inspection

532285.excerpt_en: To-Takteren is one of Longyearbyen’s oldest associations, established in 1966 to bring people together around something new that had arrived: the snowmobile. Over time, however, the association’s interests shifted from valleys and mountains to fjords and the sea.
532285.subtitle_en: As soon as the first warm days of spring arrived, boating enthusiasts turned their gaze toward the fjord. The first preparations have begun in the marina.
532285.tags_en: To-Takteren, boating life, news, Svalbard, leisure activities, Longyearbyen
532285.title_en: Boating enthusiasts are itching to get out

532303.excerpt_en: In an article published in Svalbardposten on April 18, we read that the board of Svalbard’s Environmental Protection Fund believes it is high time to increase the environmental levy paid by those travelling to Svalbard by plane and cruise ship.
532303.subtitle_en: Increase in Svalbard environmental levy: An opportunity to fund public goods in Longyearbyen
532303.tags_en: environmental levy, visitor contribution, sustainable tourism, Svalbard Environmental Protection Fund, public-goods funding, opinions, Svalbard
532303.title_en: Increase in Svalbard environmental levy: An opportunity to fund public goods in Longyearbyen

532313.excerpt_en: The samples were taken from drinking water at various locations around town. Drinking water means all water coming from taps and showerheads in the town. “We’re doing this now to rule out legionella in our drinking water and to map the situation.”
532313.subtitle_en: Ten water samples were taken Wednesday morning to determine whether legionella may be present in several locations in Longyearbyen.
532313.title_en: “We are testing solely as a precaution”

532342.excerpt_en: During a briefing for politicians on Tuesday, property manager Lars Prestegård provided an update on the school building. It became clear that the students probably will not be able to move back into their classrooms until after the summer.
532342.subtitle_en: Students in fifth and sixth grade at Longyearbyen School will probably not move back into their classrooms until the summer holidays.
532342.tags_en: water leak, school building, news, Longyearbyen School, property manager Lars Prestegård, insurance claim

532356.excerpt_en: For twelve weeks, fifth grade at Longyearbyen School read more than 700 pages to get through the books by the five super-finalists in the Bokslukerprisen.
532356.subtitle_en: The jury class’s clear favorite, “Evighetsspillet,” won this year’s Bokslukerprisen. Fifth grade took part via video link from the library to present the award.
532356.title_en: Took part in the Bokslukerprisen award ceremony

532359.excerpt_en: On Wednesday morning, the Governor of Svalbard’s helicopter assisted a woman whose snowmobile overturned on her way to Isfjord Radio. Senior police officer Carina Søreng says they received word of the incident at 9:30 a.m.
532359.subtitle_en: Snowmobile overturns on way to Isfjord Radio
532359.title_en: Snowmobile overturns on way to Isfjord Radio

532369.excerpt_en: Svalbard Airport reports on Facebook that, due to a temporary fault at Oslo Control Centre, the airspace over southern Norway is closed. This will likely cause substantial delays to air traffic.

532439.excerpt_en: “Since we were unable to get rid of the problem, we wondered whether the source of infection could be outside the airport,” says Nils Lorentsen, operations manager at Svalbard Airport. Svalbard Airport discovered Legionella bacteria during a routine inspection in 2021.
532439.subtitle_en: Avinor at Svalbard Airport ordered new showerheads, flushed the pipes and installed a treatment system. Nevertheless, the infection returned.

532463.excerpt_en: According to the Governor of Svalbard, the visiting man went very close to the walrus lying on the ice and disturbed it, causing it to react to his presence. Several members of the public who observed the man contacted the Governor’s Office shortly before 9 p.m. Wednesday.
532463.subtitle_en: A tourist was fined on Wednesday after walking onto an ice floe in Advent Bay and approaching a walrus.
532463.title_en: Fined NOK 12,500 for getting too close to a walrus

532473.excerpt_en: This winter, the cultural school offered a musical, and its participants joined forces with the dance group to stage “East High the Musical.” “It went extremely well. Actually, beyond all expectations.”
532473.subtitle_en: The cultural school’s musical received a standing ovation. “It’s a shame there’s only one performance,” said an enthusiastic audience member, regretting that the whole town was not in the hall.

532491.excerpt_en: We meet road and local-environment operations engineer Lillian Risvaag and acting fire chief Ruben Johansen at Vei 232 in Gruvedalen. This is where they have asked to meet to discuss what they describe as problematic snowmobile parking in Longyearbyen.
532491.subtitle_en: Acting fire chief Ruben Johansen has no doubt that this type of snowmobile parking is unacceptable. If the fire service had needed to enter the substation, these vehicles would have obstructed the fire engine and crew.
532491.title_en: “In a critical situation, this could quickly become a time thief”

532511.excerpt_en: The amendment is being considered by the Storting’s Standing Committee on Energy and the Environment this week. Their conclusion is scheduled to be considered by the Storting on the 16th.
532511.subtitle_en: Both the Conservative Party and the Progress Party in the Storting want to send a proposal to amend the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act back to the government. They are asking the government to listen to input received, including from Longyearbyen.
532511.tags_en: consultation process, Svalbard, Storting, news, legislative amendment, polar bear protection

532519.excerpt_en: Rescue coordinator Jakob Carlsen at the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre of Northern Norway says they were alerted by the Governor of Svalbard shortly after 6 p.m. Thursday. “We eventually made contact with the boat ourselves, but communication was difficult because they were in Magdalenefjorden, where the terrain is extremely rugged.”
532519.subtitle_en: The boat M/V “Vikingfjord” ran aground in Magdalenefjorden on Thursday afternoon. The vessel remained there for half a day.
532519.title_en: Had to wait for high tide to get free

532539.excerpt_en: During the extraordinary local council meeting in April, Trond Olsen (Ap) was present to report on the status of the Audit Committee’s work on the energy matter. In December, the local council asked the committee to assess the energy cases from 2019 to September 2023.
532539.subtitle_en: In February, the committee requested additional funds to examine whether the transition from coal to diesel had been carried out properly. The matter was not forwarded for political consideration and stalled.

532550.excerpt_en: Governor Lars Fause will not comment on why the environmental protection chief is leaving. However, he does not hide the fact that criticism of the agency can sometimes be harsh and, unfortunately, personal.
532550.subtitle_en: After six months in the position, Bente Rønning is stepping down as environmental protection chief at the Governor’s Office. Lawyer Linda Karlstad is acting chief of the 14-person environmental protection department from today.

532569.excerpt_en: On Friday morning, the Governor’s police patrol received a report about a pair of trousers with no owner. According to senior police officer Robert Sørflaten, a man in his 20s had gone to sleep in the wrong place after a boozy night out.
532569.subtitle_en: The man in his 20s fell asleep in the wrong bed. He was not welcome there, and forgot both his phone and trousers when the homeowner chased him out.

532578.excerpt_en: His interest in history grew with age, and books about Svalbard caught his attention. Frank Jakobsen now has 7,819 different polar-book titles, each containing at least one paragraph about Svalbard.
532578.subtitle_en: If LNSS manager Frank Jakobsen were to display his collection of polar books, along with everything else the 63-year-old collects, one of the company’s larger warehouses might be just big enough.
532578.tags_en: collection, history, Svalbard, Frank Jakobsen, news, polar books

532625.excerpt_en: To keep operations within the available budget framework, the Norwegian Polar Institute has decided to reduce some activity in 2024.
532625.subtitle_en: Tight finances mean the Norwegian Polar Institute is laying the “Kronprins Haakon” up for a period.
532625.title_en: Cancels expedition to study water inflow into the Arctic Ocean

532644.excerpt_en: Last summer and autumn, the Governor of Svalbard and researchers at the Norwegian Polar Institute were notified of six or seven dead walruses in the Isfjorden, Forlandsundet and Kongsfjorden areas. There may also be dead animals elsewhere that were not observed.
532644.subtitle_en: The walrus found dead on Hopen last summer died of avian influenza. Researchers are now asking everyone traveling in Svalbard to report dead walruses and keep their distance.

532654.excerpt_en: The lifeline to and from the mainland, the container ship “Norbjørn,” runs on a regular route and was unable to attend. Apart from that, nearly 250 interested people turned up for a treasure hunt, a tour of an electric truck, grilled sausages, bags of sweets and pleasant conversation about logistics. “Norbjørn” calls every ten days.
532654.subtitle_en: Almost everything needed to operate the town comes in through Gammelkaia. On Saturday, the terminal hosted a party and open day with balloons and grilled sausages as Bring marked 30 years.

532664.excerpt_en: Warmer water has pushed into the fjords in recent years, and new species are following. There is less sea ice in the fjords, making it harder for the large seals to access food on the seafloor.
532664.subtitle_en: Bearded seals, one of the most common seals in Svalbard, may now see their daily lives changed and disrupted by climate change.
532664.tags_en: climate change, bearded seal, Svalbard, Norwegian Polar Institute, marine biology, news
532664.title_en: Climate Is Driving Bearded Seals Out

532702.excerpt_en: Police on duty were alerted at 2:30 a.m. Sunday about a fight at a nightclub, and that the bouncer needed assistance. “One man was injured in the face and had to go to hospital for stitches,” says Governor’s senior police officer Robert Sørflaten.
532702.subtitle_en: Three young, fit men from town must explain themselves to the police on Monday.

532731.excerpt_en: Wind and ocean currents have broken up the fast ice farther out and pushed thick chunks of ice into Isfjorden. Here, it piles up where nature dictates, including outside Gammelkaia and by the floating quay, where this year’s smaller cruise ships are now arriving. “It’s been 15–20 years since we’ve had anything similar.”
532731.subtitle_en: The entire harbor was full of ice in a short time. The Dutch schooner “Ocean Sherpa” struggled to reach the quay.
532731.title_en: Drift ice fills the harbor and causes trouble for smaller boats

532743.excerpt_en: “It will be incredibly exciting. Atle Skårdal has been working as part of the slope crew today.”
532743.subtitle_en: Nedover officially opens on Monday afternoon. The head of the alpine skiing group will compete against former world champion Atle Skårdal.
532743.title_en: Promising a party and fun on the slopes

532758.excerpt_en: “There is no suspicion of technical causes behind the grounding. The person responsible on the bridge at the time of the grounding has been questioned, and there is suspicion of negligent navigation,” prosecutor Magnus Rindal Fredriksen writes to Svalbardposten.
532758.subtitle_en: Last weekend, the tourist boat “Polarfront” ran aground at Diabas. The Governor of Svalbard does not suspect technical causes behind the grounding.
532758.tags_en: grounding, ship safety, Norwegian Maritime Authority, news, navigation error, polarfront

532781.excerpt_en: We meet Krystad and Eggenfellner the day before the christening. For the photograph, they have slipped into their russ outfits.
532781.subtitle_en: Russ president Ella Krystad (19) and fellow russ Frode Eggenfellner (19) say the plans are ready for this year’s russ celebrations.
532781.title_en: “The Goal Is to Empty the Russ Fund”

532800.excerpt_en: Initially, the work will involve preparations, before helicopter operations resume from 20 May, according to Longyearbyen Local Council.
532800.subtitle_en: Next week, work will resume on avalanche protection in the valley between Sukkertoppen and Gruvefjellet.

532887.excerpt_en: The cost of operating Svalbard’s energy supply has risen from NOK 130 million to NOK 269 million. Switching from coal to diesel has made electricity and heating twice as expensive.
532887.subtitle_en: Electricity bills doubled—but only for businesses.
532887.tags_en: energy supply, sustainability, opinion, Svalbard, business community, politics
532887.title_en: A Dagger Blow to Longyearbyen’s Business Community

532908.excerpt_en: On bare asphalt, in above-zero temperatures with only a slight draft in the air, LO Svalbard leader and Labour Party member Svein Jonny Albrigtsen handed out the slogans for this year’s May Day march.
532908.subtitle_en: Working conditions, the phase-out of mining, quality of life and the energy transition were topics at the 1 May rally. There was also good news for young people.

532935.excerpt_en: At least five people were in the room when a man was demonstrating partially loading a .308 rifle. The weapon turned out to be loaded, and the shot went into the floor.
532935.subtitle_en: At the beginning of April, a shot was fired indoors when a man was demonstrating loading a rifle halfway. The case has now been settled.

532978.excerpt_en: With a majority consisting of the Labour Party, Centre Party, Socialist Left Party, Red Party, Liberal Party and Green Party, the Standing Committee on Energy and the Environment backed changes to the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act to tighten the rules concerning polar bears. The committee published its recommendation on the bill on Tuesday.
532978.subtitle_en: On Tuesday, the Standing Committee on Energy and the Environment recommended that the Svalbard Environmental Protection Act be amended. It is therefore up to Parliament to decide whether distance requirements for polar bears should be introduced.

533002.excerpt_en: Legionella bacteria were detected in all ten water samples sent for analysis last week. Longyearbyen Local Council writes this on its website.
533002.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen Local Council is in close dialogue with the health authorities for advice and recommendations.
533002.title_en: Legionella Detected in All Water Samples

533025.excerpt_en: The man was on a work assignment in Svalbard. Together with a colleague, he went 11.
533025.subtitle_en: A foreign national must pay an NOK 8,000 fine after causing trouble at a venue in Longyearbyen.
533025.title_en: Refused to Leave Venue, Clung to the Wall

533029.excerpt_en: Three years after MS “Bard” made its maiden voyage in Longyearbyen, the catamaran operating a route for Hurtigruten Svalbard was ceremonially christened on Thursday.
533029.subtitle_en: It took three attempts before the bottle broke, but on Thursday the catamaran was finally christened.

533060.excerpt_en: The case is being updated. The two Norwegian skiers requested assistance themselves for medical reasons.
533060.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard evacuated two skiers from the area near Isbukta on Friday.

533078.excerpt_en: This photograph from 1 May 1955 comes from Erling Johan Nødtvedt’s collection.
533078.tags_en: Svalbard Museum, news, historical photograph, historical, photo archive

533089.excerpt_en: On Thursday, it became clear that Legionella was present in all ten water samples Longyearbyen Local Council collected from the drinking-water network the previous week. On Friday, Longyearbyen Local Council is taking new samples.
533089.subtitle_en: Chief Infection Control Officer Ole Tveiten at Longyearbyen Hospital says the risk of anyone contracting Legionnaires’ disease is low, but offers advice on what people in town should do—including when showering.

533145.excerpt_en: The man was evacuated by the Governor of Svalbard’s helicopter and taken directly to Longyearbyen Hospital. It landed outside the hospital at 5:30 p.m. Before the helicopter landed in the car park, Road 500 was closed to traffic so it could land just outside the hospital.
533145.subtitle_en: A foreign national is believed to have suffered a medical emergency in the terrain near Tellbreen on Friday afternoon.

533179.excerpt_en: Darren Carr says the coaching duo has now made several trips to Longyearbyen. The very first was eight years ago, in 2016.
533179.subtitle_en: This weekend, Darren Carr and David Crist are back on the island to contribute to the Liverbirds supporters’ club football school.
533179.title_en: Coaching Duo Darren and David Gave Players Helpful Tips and Tricks

533241.excerpt_en: After a winter filled with unforeseen energy expenses, it feels good to be wrapped in ice and cooled down a little. Shops, restaurants, service providers and the state and public sector itself will all face higher electricity prices.

533258.excerpt_en: It is minus ten and blowing a gale. The roads have been scraped smooth as glass.

533278.excerpt_en: Once again, elected representatives will decide whether Tio Monchos should be granted a permanent alcohol licence with extended serving hours at the cultural centre, at Wednesday’s local council meeting. If the concept is changed again, alcohol sales at the cultural centre could begin before noon.
533278.subtitle_en: The Youth Council says it is understandable that Tio Monchos wants an extended alcohol licence at the cultural centre. At the same time, it asks politicians and Rockhouse AS to explore solutions to ensure children and young people can be shielded.
533278.title_en: “Children and Young People Shouldn’t Feel Unsafe Going to the Library”

533297.excerpt_en: The two allegedly used the money for a range of private benefits. They are accused of using public funds for luxury trips to numerous destinations, including Svalbard.
533297.subtitle_en: Two men have been charged with aggravated fraud against the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Climate and Environment.

533301.excerpt_en: The energy bill following the switch from coal to diesel is rising by the hour. Demanding that businesses pay is just as utopian as it has been to decree that the largest electricity consumers were obliged to do so.
533301.subtitle_en: Fire Up the Coal-Fired Steam Boiler Again!
533301.title_en: Fire Up the Coal-Fired Steam Boiler Again!

533310.excerpt_en: Six children and one senior competed in a total of 36 events. They set 18 personal bests.
533310.subtitle_en: The Svalbard Turn swimming group took part in a swim meet in Harstad at the weekend. They were unable to train before leaving, but on Monday Longyearbyen local council will allow the oldest swimmers to use the pool in Longyearbyen again.

533324.excerpt_en: Hernes is regarded as a living legend in polar circles. As Minister of Church Affairs, Education and Research, he was central to the establishment of the University Centre in Svalbard (UNIS) in 1993.
533324.subtitle_en: Svalbard enthusiast Gudmund Hernes (83) has been appointed an honorary member of the Norwegian Academy of Polar Research.
533324.title_en: Honoured for his contribution to Svalbard

533356.excerpt_en: After four years of chopping and packing firewood and developing a successful enterprise, Trym Aunevik (22) has extra reason to smile. This week, he is visiting Longyearbyen again.
533356.subtitle_en: After four years of thorough work in the student enterprise “Bardufoss ITL – Ved og vel”, Trym Aunevik (22) was proud to show Longyearbyen to his fellow students.

533443.excerpt_en: Technical manager Tom Schaug announced this when he briefed the Longyearbyen local council (LL) on the Legionella situation on Wednesday morning. He said it was still unclear what had caused the outbreak.
533443.subtitle_en: Longyearbyen’s drinking water will be treated with chlorine to suppress the Legionella outbreak.

533478.excerpt_en: Birgitte Tautra Vegsund comes from the position of sales manager at the same company, a role she has held since 2018. “Birgitte has extensive knowledge of the organisation and is driven by creating unforgettable and sustainable experiences in the Arctic.”
533478.subtitle_en: Birgitte Tautra Vegsund will become the new destination manager for Basecamp Explorer Spitsbergen AS, succeeding Renate Pedersen.
533478.tags_en: Basecamp Explorer Spitsbergen AS, Birgitte Tautra Vegsund, Svalbard, sustainable tourism, tourism, leadership change, news

533482.excerpt_en: Alongside running the venue at the cultural centre, Andreas Styrsell followed the case online.
533482.subtitle_en: Tio Monchos managing director and owner Andreas Styrsell is relieved by Wednesday’s outcome in the local council.
533482.tags_en: Andreas Styrsell, news, alcohol licence, cultural centre, Youth Council, Tio Monchos
533482.title_en: “At least now we have the chance to try”

533486.excerpt_en: As tradition dictates, the Governor’s Office and Longyearbyen School jointly organised the event this year as well. Governor Lars Fause and Chief Superintendent Stein Olav Bredli took part together with pupils from Year 9.
533486.subtitle_en: Liberation and Veterans’ Day on 8 May was commemorated on Thursday with a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery.

533490.excerpt_en: The former editor of Jærbladet and consultant for the Association of Norwegian Local Newspapers has been elected as a new board representative of the Svalbardposten Foundation. Are Nundal will continue as chair and Cecilie Østlie as a board member, while Wenche Sørensen is the employee representative.
533490.subtitle_en: The former editor of Jærbladet and consultant for the Association of Norwegian Local Newspapers has been elected as a new board representative of the Svalbardposten Foundation. Are Nundal will continue as chair, and Cecilie Østlie as a board member.
533490.title_en: Kirsten Marie Myklebust joins the Svalbardposten board

533558.excerpt_en: Police went to Lompensenteret on the night before Thursday after receiving a report that people were arguing. “Both parties were intoxicated. By the time we arrived, they had gone their separate ways,” says Chief Superintendent Kjell Arne Lundin of the Governor’s Office.

article_keywords_en: chief superintendent of the Governor’s Office
533562.excerpt_en: “Someone has probably broken their ankle. It is not dramatic, but the person is in pain,” says Chief Superintendent Kjell Arne Lundin of the Governor’s Office.
533562.subtitle_en: On Thursday afternoon, the Governor’s Office received a report via the Emergency Medical Communications Centre about a person injured just below Varden.

533658.excerpt_en: This picture comes from Louis Torjusen’s collection and was taken during the evacuation of Svalbard in 1941. Torjusen worked in the warehouse and was an organist at the church, as well as conductor of the men’s choir for a period.
533658.tags_en: historical picture, Svalbard Museum, historical, photo archive, news

533662.excerpt_en: Legionella bacteria were recently detected in all ten water samples sent to Tromsø for analysis. The local council has said that it is not dangerous to drink tap water, and that there is no need to boil it before use.
533662.subtitle_en: Because of the Legionella situation in Longyearbyen, many people prefer to buy water.

533666.excerpt_en: There have been strong gusts over the past 24 hours. On Thursday evening at around 6 p.m., the Governor’s vessel Polarsyssel had to assist a sailboat experiencing difficulties in the wind.

533670.excerpt_en: The Governor’s helicopter was dispatched on Thursday evening to retrieve a sick passenger from the cruise ship Ultramarine. The vessel was just north of Kapp Mitra, not far from the entrance to Kongsfjorden.

533684.excerpt_en: “I have known for a long time that this would be my last Pride in Longyearbyen,” says Lene Jeanette Dyngeland, who started Longyearbyen Pride in 2019. Dyngeland says that although she is stepping down, this does not necessarily have to be the end of Pride in Longyearbyen.
533684.subtitle_en: This year’s Pride will be Lene Jeanette Dyngeland’s last. She has therefore brought Svalbard Vibe onto the team.

533705.excerpt_en: This week, Svalbardposten wrote about Tio Monchos, the restaurant that was awarded a contract to operate in the cultural centre, but not to serve alcohol. Ever since the cultural centre opened, young people in Longyearbyen have spoken out against alcohol service at a venue that is so important to them.
533705.subtitle_en: Keep commenting, but do it properly
533705.title_en: Keep commenting, but do it properly

533711.excerpt_en: Today, wastewater from Longyearbyen is discharged into the fjord. Every day, wash water, sewage and ground-up food waste from residents and visitors are pumped straight into the sea after being screened through a grate.
533711.subtitle_en: A new report concludes that better use of wastewater could provide Longyearbyen with cheaper energy and protect the environment in Adventfjorden.

533728.excerpt_en: On Saturday, a confirmation ceremony will be held at the cultural centre for four Humanist confirmation candidates. A fifth candidate from Svalbard will be confirmed on the mainland.
533728.subtitle_en: This weekend, there will be a Humanist confirmation ceremony in Longyearbyen.

533745.excerpt_en: A rubbish bin outside the sports shop 78 Longyear caught fire on Friday evening. “We received a message from 110 that a rubbish bin was on fire and waited until the fire service had been at the scene,” says Chief Superintendent Taina Maria Schogster Bjørkås of the Governor’s Office.
533745.tags_en: fire, 78 Longyear, police, brief, sports shop, rubbish bin

533808.excerpt_en: Some time ago, the Artica cultural foundation and Svalbardposten launched a writing competition for young people aged 14 to 20 living in Longyearbyen. It has now been announced that Huse has won.
533808.subtitle_en: Ruth Møllerplass Huse (20) won the writing competition for young people.
533808.title_en: Wrote about life beneath the polar sky

533933.excerpt_en: On Friday, it became clear that there is no Legionella in Isdammen, the town’s drinking-water source. Longyearbyen Local Council (LL) can therefore now be certain that the Legionella bacteria are inside the water network.
533933.subtitle_en: Notices have been posted at the harbour informing people that there is Legionella in Longyearbyen’s drinking water. For now, it has not been deemed necessary to send text messages to tourists.
533933.tags_en: drinking water, infection control, news, legionella, health, longyearbyen
533933.title_en: Uncertain when the water can be declared safe

533937.excerpt_en: In keeping with a long-standing tradition, Svalbardposten has checked the prospects for traditional-costume weather on the national day itself. And the answer we got was this: “It doesn’t look too bad at all.”
533937.subtitle_en: Partly cloudy, zero degrees and no precipitation. That is what the 17 May weather will be like in Longyearbyen.

533951.excerpt_en: In mid-April, two inspectors from the Civil Aviation Authority carried out a spot-check inspection at Svalbard Airport. They spent three days reviewing items that could affect aviation safety.
533951.subtitle_en: None of the discrepancies are classified as serious enough to pose a major risk, but the Civil Aviation Authority has ordered the airport to draw up an action plan by 7 June.
533951.title_en: Found eleven discrepancies at the airport

533966.excerpt_en: Imagination is needed to open our eyes to possible new paths. But before setting out, one must examine them carefully, rather than trust baseless rumours.

533989.excerpt_en: At 10:45, Finance Minister Trygve Slagsvold Vedum (Centre Party) presented the Støre government’s proposal for the revised national budget for 2024. Alongside the key figures for the Norwegian economy and the government’s view on implementing economic policy, the preliminary version of the government’s proposal was also released.
533989.subtitle_en: UNIS, the student housing in Nybyen, Store Norske and the Norwegian Polar Institute are among those the government proposes supporting, in addition to the announced electricity subsidy for Longyearbyen Local Council.
533989.title_en: Proposes funding for more recipients in the Svalbard budget

534015.excerpt_en: In January, SAS launched a trial project offering flight passes for travel to and from the mainland. Residents and businesses have long been frustrated by high ticket prices, and both Longyearbyen Local Council and the airport committee have worked for change.
534015.subtitle_en: The trial project selling flight passes was such a success that SAS will probably follow up with a new special offer for people on Svalbard.
534015.title_en: Considering another round of flight pass sales

534072.excerpt_en: The school year ended last week, and this year’s students went home. The dormitory now stands empty and locked despite a severe housing shortage in Longyearbyen.
534072.subtitle_en: Svalbard Folk High School wants to rent out its dormitory to generate income this summer. But the state says no.
534072.title_en: Has 60 vacant rooms but is not allowed to rent them out

534109.excerpt_en: Ruben Johansen took up the position as acting fire chief just before Easter and has now become fire chief on a permanent basis. “It’s incredibly exciting.”
534109.subtitle_en: Ruben Johansen moved to Longyearbyen nearly two years ago. Now he is the new fire chief.
534109.title_en: Ruben takes over as fire chief

534132.excerpt_en: The statuette is proof that someone has done something good and had a positive influence on the Longyearbyen community, showing a willingness to make “typhus” a little less “typhus”. The very first person to receive the award was William Viken, in 1974.
534132.subtitle_en: Together with Anne Lise Klungseth Sandvik, William Viken (pictured centre) had the honour of presenting award number 51. He received the very first one in 1974. But Anne Lise says the cultural award is what it is today thanks to William himself.
534132.title_en: “If William hadn’t had to accept the award, we probably would never have turned around”

534235.excerpt_en: Posten Norge press chief Kenneth Pettersen confirms that sales of Norgespakker increased in the first quarter of 2024.
534235.subtitle_en: Posten Norge reports that removing the much-discussed Svalbard surcharge has had an effect. More people are now sending Norgespakker to and from Svalbard.
534235.title_en: More people are sending parcels to Svalbard

534242.excerpt_en: Yesterday, Svalbardposten reported that the mayor’s chain of office had disappeared. On Thursday, the local council announced that the chain had been found.
534242.subtitle_en: “We broke into the Business Building on Monday evening—or, more precisely, we had an accomplice who gave us a key,” says russe president Ella Krystad (19).
534242.tags_en: russetide, news, local council leader, governor, svalbard, mayoral chain of office

534272.excerpt_en: Spring is delightful now, with summer just around the corner, and one of the most pleasant signs of spring is clearly visible—and, not least, audible—on Svalbard. As early as mid-April, snow buntings arrived in flocks, probably both hungry and exhausted after a long flight from the mainland.
534272.subtitle_en: People are wondering whether there are steadily fewer snow buntings on Svalbard. Experts are more relaxed.

534276.excerpt_en: At the local council meeting on 8 May, Chief Administrative Officer Arild Hammerhaug of Longyearbyen Local Council was asked to brief the politicians on what answers they had to the letter sent by the Ministry of Justice on the 9th.
534276.subtitle_en: A briefing by Chief Administrative Officer Arild Hammerhaug revealed that Svalbard Energi has had problems with its diesel this winter. However, it is not yet clear whether this caused the two engine failures at the eastern emergency power plant.

534334.excerpt_en: A deadline has now been set for concluding the wage settlement for Norwegian’s pilots. The date the parties must meet is the 31st.

534359.excerpt_en: SAS is stepping up its competition for passengers willing to pay for Arctic experiences such as the northern lights, dog sledding and spectacular, untouched nature. As Svalbardposten recently reported, Svalbard is good business for airlines.
534359.subtitle_en: SAS is expanding its network to Scandinavian winter destinations. This will affect Svalbard.

534369.excerpt_en: Last year, Longyearbyen Local Council identified water shortages as the town’s greatest emergency preparedness threat. It has now begun work on a preliminary project to improve water security. “Both energy and water supplies have become highly topical given the security policy situation we are facing.”
534369.subtitle_en: It is not only Longyearbyen’s energy situation that is vulnerable. Longyearbyen has no backup water source. The local council will now assess a new waterworks based on water from Isfjorden.
534369.tags_en: Longyearbyen, infrastructure, news, climate change, water supply, emergency preparedness
534369.title_en: Considering seawater as new main water source

534386.excerpt_en: Before this year’s 17 May committee leader, Linnea Mari Våtvik (16), heads home to prepare tomorrow’s 17 May speech, and after two long days of exams, she has a small opening in her schedule for a chat with Svalbardposten.
534386.subtitle_en: Linnea Mari Våtvik (16) is this year’s 17 May committee leader. She believes it is important that everyone is included and wants to be the voice of children and young people.
534386.title_en: Linnea (16) welcomes people to Longyearbyen celebrations: “It’s important that everyone is included”

534398.excerpt_en: Ingrid Kjerstad, research coordinator at the Norwegian Polar Institute in Ny-Ålesund, says the parade began at the traditional “balloon launch” hosted by AwiPev (editor’s note: Alfred Wegener Institute (AWI) and the French Polar Institute Paul Emile Victor (IPEV)), before heading down to Mellageret. A 17 May speech was held there, with this year’s speaker being Elias Aukan from…
534398.subtitle_en: Slag & Blæs led the 17 May parade through the streets of Ny-Ålesund at 79 degrees north.

534429.excerpt_en: In the morning, Longyearbyen’s 17 May celebrations began with the traditional laying of wreaths at the memorials.
534429.subtitle_en: Despite a chilly start to 17 May, it was a fine commemoration at the memorials.

534515.excerpt_en: Recently, the sun has been shining around the clock on Svalbard—literally. Most people had probably hoped it would be like that on 17 May.
534515.subtitle_en: The weather was not quite what one might have hoped for, but there was nothing wrong with the atmosphere in Longyearbyen on the national day.
534515.title_en: A little chilly, but very nice

534693.excerpt_en: To conclude this year’s 17 May celebrations, Longyearbyen Kulturhus opened its doors for a gala performance. The show featured a variety of acts, and the evening’s two award presentations were major highlights.
534693.subtitle_en: Dag Arne Husdal was awarded the 51st Typhus statuette, 50 years after the first one was presented. He received it for having been a bridge-building and creative force in Longyearbyen’s local community for many years.
534693.title_en: Dag Arne claims the statuette as the 51st recipient

534736.excerpt_en: On Norway’s Constitution Day, Storm Bernlow flew south to the capital for a week-long internship in one of Norway’s most exclusive kitchens. He just managed to catch 17.
534736.subtitle_en: Storm Bernlow is back in town after an internship in the palace kitchen. The 15-year-old can already look back on four years of work experience and is clear that commitment matters.

545060.excerpt_en: The community council has nine matters on its agenda to consider at Wednesday’s meeting. In addition, there are several information items.
545060.subtitle_en: These are the matters the community council will decide on Wednesday
545060.title_en: These Are the Matters the Community Council Will Decide on Wednesday

545148.excerpt_en: Eva Therese Jenssen from Longyearbyen proposed naming each of the islands, Polarhistorie.no reports. New names in Svalbard are adopted by the Norwegian Polar Institute’s Names Committee.
545148.subtitle_en: They were previously known collectively as Ryke Yseøyane. Now they have been given individual names.
545148.tags_en: place names, Norwegian Polar Institute, history, news

545185.excerpt_en: At around 2 p.m. on Friday, the Governor of Svalbard responded by helicopter to the area near Trollsteinen.
545185.subtitle_en: The Governor of Svalbard first responded by helicopter on Friday, before later having to go out in the patrol boat.
545185.title_en: Man Stranded on Mountain and Rubber Boat Adrift

545219.excerpt_en: On Saturday evening, performance art took over the former Galleri Svalbard when Stein Henningsen invited Longyearbyen to this year’s Arctic Action. Those attending experienced the first four artists taking part in the festival.
545219.subtitle_en: The seventh edition of Arctic Action opened at Spitsbergen Artists’ Center on Saturday. Four of the eight artists shared their first performances with Longyearbyen.
545219.title_en: “An Audience Puts Extra Pressure on the Artists”

545260.excerpt_en: At the end of last year, Longyearbyen Community Council (LL) was tasked with reviewing its cultural and sports services. The aim was to define which services the unit should provide and how they could be rationalized and made more efficient.
545260.subtitle_en: It is better to cut a service entirely than to shave a little off all of them, the administration has told politicians.
545260.title_en: Looking for Cuts in Culture and Sports

545267.excerpt_en: An excavator and staff from LNS Spitsbergen were at the Perleporten bridge on Monday morning. They have begun dismantling the well-used footbridge between Lia and Haugen.
545267.subtitle_en: On Monday, LNS Spitsbergen began removing the railing from the footbridge.
545267.title_en: Parts of Perleporten Now Being Removed

545297.excerpt_en: “Visitor figures are at an all-time high in terms of guest nights, and each guest stays a little longer.”
545297.subtitle_en: Tourists flocked to Svalbard this summer, and those who came stayed slightly longer than before.
545297.tags_en: tourism, business, news, travel industry, cruise

545325.excerpt_en: Svalbard Brewery now supplies both water and beer on reusable plastic trays. To ensure the trays are returned and enjoy a long life, the brewery has introduced a NOK 50 deposit per tray.

545386.excerpt_en: On Monday afternoon, the Governor of Svalbard received a report of an accidental discharge at the shooting range in Longyearbyen. The shot was fired during organized training.

545408.excerpt_en: “At a time when infrastructure in Europe is more exposed than before, and when Russia in particular is considered to pose a hybrid threat, we are focusing especially on how our own infrastructure is connected to other critical infrastructure,” Telenor wrote in the statement issued last week.
545408.subtitle_en: Arctic areas are more exposed to security-policy tensions. This calls for extra vigilance. Christian Skottun, head of Telenor Svalbard, urges people to turn off roaming and avoid using open networks.

545459.excerpt_en: Just before 5 p.m. on Tuesday afternoon, police responded to the recycling station. “We received a report of a fire at the recycling station,” police sergeant Håkon Finstad told Svalbardposten at 4:50 p.m. “Police are on the scene, and no one has been injured,” Finstad said.

545504.excerpt_en: “Someone disposed of residual waste, and among it was a battery that had not been sorted out,” says operations manager Hans Petter Lauritsen of Longyearbyen Community Council, after a fire started in the shredder inside the recycling station on Tuesday afternoon.
545504.subtitle_en: It was probably a lithium battery that caught fire at the recycling station on Tuesday.
545504.title_en: “Do Not Throw Batteries in Regular Waste”

545543.excerpt_en: The community council has decided to change the framework for annual allocations of bottle-deposit funds to clubs and associations. Thirty percent of Nordpolet AS’s profit, or a maximum of NOK 2.4 million, will now go to this purpose.
545543.subtitle_en: Community council chair Terje Aunevik (Liberal Party) made the request when politicians debated the bottle-deposit scheme at Wednesday’s meeting.
545543.tags_en: community council, bottle-deposit funds, news, politics, culture

545561.excerpt_en: This coming Friday, September 20, people around the world will demonstrate for stronger climate action, and Longyearbyen will join them.
545561.subtitle_en: “We want to send a strong signal to the world.”
545561.title_en: “We Want to Send a Strong Signal to the World”

545582.excerpt_en: Svalbard Conservative Party’s Jo Gytri said this from the podium during the review of the cultural and sports services. Politicians commissioned the review at the community council’s December meeting last year, and it was presented to them at the council’s first autumn meeting on Wednesday. “We have a great deal to be proud of in the town.”
545582.subtitle_en: “When running a gallery comes at the expense of what we call primary services, we have gone off track.”

545609.excerpt_en: Tommy Sandal has worked as a trapper on Svalbard since 2007. Akseløya is his main base, and these days he is out in the field to shoot the 40 reindeer for which he has a quota.
545609.subtitle_en: Tommy Sandal believes the overwintering requirement is outdated, but says the state must set requirements for trappers. “Those who believe it is impossible to make a living from this should not be allowed to own a trapping cabin,” he says.
545609.title_en: Year-Round Work Preferred to Staying Overwinter

545658.excerpt_en: At the start of Wednesday’s community council meeting, Gytri questioned the administration on behalf of the Venstre/Conservative Party list alliance. This follows up on last year’s budget meeting.
545658.subtitle_en: “Longyearbyen Community Council must thoroughly assess what it spends money on, and we want a broad review to gain a clear overview. That is what Jo Gytri of Svalbard Conservative Party emphasizes.”
